TitreApplicationTitle: Pathogenesis of viral myocarditis - role of intrinsic innate immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: CDNA MICROARRAYS; HEART FAILURE; INNATE IMMUNITY; MYOCARDITIS; TRANSGENIC MICE; VIRAL CULTURES
Abstract-Résumé: Congestive heart failure accounts for more than 1/2 of all the admission to hospital, and is the number one rising cardiovascular epidemic in the 21st century.  Congestive heart failure is the inability for the heart to pump adequate blood to the rest of the body, and is due to weakness of the heart muscle.  One of the causes of heart failure is virus infection of the heart muscle.  This is particularly important as this affects a younger population, and can have long term consequences with development of heart failure in the adult.         Currently, there is no specific treatment for the disease, and how the virus causes damage to the heart is only beginning to be unravelled.  We have been investigating the cause of this problem in several mouse models, where a specific component of the immune system can be removed through genetic engineering.  With these models, we now have identified the critical molecules that can make the disease totally disappear, or to make them extremely sick.  We now have found that an innate or intrinsic component of our defense system may pave the way for the virus to either be contained by the immune system, or be stimulated by the virus to attack the heart.  This understanding should also point towards new treatment strategies for this disease, and identify novel means to diagnose the disease earlier and more accurately.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dopamine, glutamate interactions in relapse to psychostimulant self-administration
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTION; ANIMAL MODELS OF DRUG SELF-ADMINISTRATION; BRAIN DIALYSIS; NEUROCHEMICAL ANALYSES; NEUROPHARMACOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Drug addiction is a brain disease in which repeated exposure to psychoactive drugs produces long-lasting changes in synaptic plasticity which in turn may underlie the development of compulsive behaviour and 'craving' for drugs of abuse.  Drug addiction is also characterized as a chronic relapsing disorder, and relapse to drug-seeking and self-administration is now recognized as the greatest challenge to the treatment of human drug addiction.  This research program focuses on preclinical experiments in which electrical stimulation of neurons that release glutamate can be used to reinstate drug-seeking behaviour.  This model will facilitate systematic pharmacological, electrophysiological and behavioural analyses of glutamate-dopamine interactions involved in relapse.  As such, these experiments may identify new pharmacological interventions for the control of relapse to addictive behaviour.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dopamine and incentive motivation: Links to depression
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTION; ANIMAL MODELS; BIPOLAR DISORDER; BRAIN DIALYSIS; DEPRESSION
Abstract-Résumé: The neurotransmitter dopamine has been implicated in a wide range of disorders including addiction, schizophrenia and depression but there is still uncertainty about the role of dopamine in the control of motivation, emotion and cognitive function.  This project will resolve this question by measuring the release of dopamine in the rat brain during sensitive behavioural tests of motivated behaviour.  A second objective is to gain further understanding of the detrimental effects that exposure to, and withdrawal from, psychostimulant drugs (amphetamine or cocaine) can have on the normal function of brain dopamine systems.  The final objective is to develop an animal model of bipolar depression, a psychiatric condition that affects 1% of the population and one with a high incidence of suicide.  The availability of a valid preclinical model of this disorder will facilitate research into the intracellular signalling pathways may underlie the symptoms and thereby aid in the development of new and more effective therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Drug resistance mechanisms in the human pathogen Leishmania
Keywords-MotsClés: ABC TRANSPORTERS; ANTIMONY; DNA MICROARRAY; DRUG RESISTANCE; LEISHMANIA; PROTEOMIC
Abstract-Résumé: The control of parasitic diseases is an important public health problem and the emergence of drug resistance is a major complication.  In the last years we have studied the mechanism of resistance to antimonials that are used in the treatment of parasites responsible for kala-azar and leishmaniasis.  These diseases are caused by the parasite Leishmania which is distributed worldwide and affects several million people including soldiers in Irak and Afghanistan.  Resistance to antimonials is a major problem in some part of the world and we are proposing to define the mechanisms of resistance using a state of the art technological approach. A better understanding of resistance  is important to circumvent or overcome this important clinical and public health problem.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms of oncogenic activation of the met RTK in human cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL TRANSFORMATION; CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; PROTEIN STRUCTURE; PROTEOMICS; RECEPTOR TRAFFICKING; RECEPTOR TYROSINE KINASE; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Our work in the past few years has uncovered an important regulator of invasive cell growth, the Met receptor. In normal cells, Met acts to relay signals from the cell surface that promote tissue organization. However when these pathways are altered in cancer cells, this acts to enhance cell invasion the first step of metastasis. We have identified multiple mechanisms present within the cell that act to tightly regulate the activity of the Met receptor. These include positive regulation by naturally occurring growth factors as well as negative regulation. We have recently identified a key player that acts to negatively regulate Met and other receptors, a protein called Cbl. We have shown that loss of negative regulation of the Met receptor by Cbl contributes to oncogenic activation of the Met receptor and possibly other receptors in human tumors. In this application we will identify the various molecular mechanisms that exert negative regulation on the Met receptor and the consequence of loss of these mechanisms to human cancer. A mechanistic understanding of this process will ultimately impact on therapeutic strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: The culture and context of adolescent marijuana use
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTIONS; ADOLESCENCE; ETHNOGRAPHIC; MARIJUANA; QUALITATIVE; SOCIO-CULTURAL CONTEXT; SUB-CULTURE
Abstract-Résumé: Over the past decade there has been a shift in the public discourse related to marijuana; it is a drug that is increasingly seen as socially acceptable. Research has demonstrated the harmful social and health effects of marijuana use and there is increasing evidence that some individuals become dependent on marijuana. Despite these consequences many youth continue to believe that marijuana is a ¿natural product¿ that is less harmful than cigarettes. This study is directed at increasing our understanding of marijuana use among youth, focusing particularly on the context and culture of use in three communities in British Columbia. The study also aims to understand how youth frame the health and social consequences of frequent marijuana use and understand marijuana dependence. The proposed study uses an ethnographic qualitative approach to describe the culture of regular marijuana use by youth  Data will be collected using three approaches: naturalistic observation, focused interviews with stakeholders (teachers, principals, community leaders), and in-depth interviews with youth. The first two strategies will be used to understand community norms and practices related to marijuana use among youth. The third strategy will be used to understand youth¿s perspectives on marijuana use and will rely heavily on narrative techniques. The findings will provide an empirical foundation for developing policies and prevention programming related to marijuana use among adolescents that that is sensitive to the actual lives and experiences of adolescents.

TitreApplicationTitle: A randomised controlled evaluation of HPV testing for cervical cancer screening
Keywords-MotsClés: CERVICAL CANCER PREVENTION; HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS; POPULATION SCREENING; RANDOMISED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: It has been conclusively established that infection with high-risk Human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is a necessary cause of cervical cancer. On the basis of these data, it has been proposed that testing for HR-HPV could enhance the performance of cervical screening programs and preliminary studies have shown that this has a higher sensitivity and negative predictive value than the Pap smear, albeit with lower specificity and positive predictive value. However, all of these studies suffered from methodological limitations that restrict their use for public health policy formulation and there is general agreement within the public health community that large scale randomised controlled trials (RCTs) are required for this purpose. This application proposes just such a RCT to establish the efficacy and cost-effectiveness of HPV testing as a stand-alone screening test when used within the context of an organised Canadian cervical cancer screening program. The study will recruit 33,000 women, aged 25-69 years, who are attending for routine screening within the organised cervical screening program of British Columbia. Women randomised to the control arm will be screened with cytology and managed according to provincial guidelines. Women randomised to the intervention arm will be screened with HPV testing and those with a positive result will be triaged with cytology. Both arms will exit at 48 months (2 screening rounds in the control arm, 1 round in the intervention arm) at which time they will both be screened using cytology and HPV testing with any women having a positive screening test being referred for intensive colposcopy. Histologically confirmed incident CIN3 or worse detected over 4 years post recruitment will be compared in the control arm and the intervention arm as a surrogate marker for eventual reductions in the incidence of cervical cancer that could be achieved by the respective screening methodologies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Expression profiling in antibiotic resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIBIOTICS; ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE; GENE INACTIVATION; PROTEOMIC; STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE; TRANSCRIPTOMIC
Abstract-Résumé: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the main bacterial pathogen of the respiratory tract (pneumonitis, bronchitis, and otitis media) in adults and children resulting in significant morbidity and mortality. Several antibiotics are available against this bacteria but unfortunately these antibiotics are not effective because S. pneumoniae is now resistant to multiple drugs. We propose a novel strategy to study resistance which consists in carrying state of the art genomic techniques. This work should reveal novel targets that could lead to the design of much needed novel antibiotics.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair on Emerging Viruses and Antiviral Resistance
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Viruses are a constant threat to mankind. In the recent years, we have witnessed the emergence of many new viral diseases including those caused by West Nile virus, SARS-associated coronavirus and avian influenza. Preventive and therapeutic modalities are unavailable for many viral infections whereas viral resistance is a growing concern for treatable viral diseases. In this Canada research chair, we first aim at identifying, characterizing as well as developing preventive (vaccines) and therapeutic (antivirals) strategies for emerging human viruses especially respiratory viruses. The second objective of this research program is to understand the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of antiviral drug resistance and to evaluate the clinical impact of drug-resistant viral mutants in different clinical settings. Our ultimate goal is to establish an international center in virology with expertise in conventional and molecular diagnosis, basic and clinical research, technology transfer and student training.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cardiac Regeneration
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Following a heart attack, the heart is injured and cells in the damaged area are replaced by scar tissue. This greatly increases the risk of heart failure. We have previously demonstrated that cell transplantation into the damaged region of the heart improves cardiac function. This research proposal will focus on identifying the optimal cell type and conditions for transplantation to regenerate the damaged myocardium and using cell and gene therapy to promote blood vessel formation and prevent the complications of heart injury. If successful, cell transplantation should significantly improve heart function and increase patient longevity and quality of life.

Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence of allergic and immune/inflammatory diseases has increased dramatically, affecting one third or more of the population. This research project will focus on (i) immunological mechanisms and immune tolerance in allergic and autoimmune diseases; (ii) development and clinical testing of curative synthetic vaccines, since current treatments are primarily symptomatic. The project will specifically investigate the role of the immune/inflammatory response in allergic asthma and autoimmune disease models, and then adapt and generalise this knowledge to establish a major research focus in development of vaccines to treat many established immunological diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: One carbon metabolism in the human parasite Leishmania
Keywords-MotsClés: DNA MICROARRAY; FOLATE; LEISHMANIA; MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS; METHIONINE; PROTEOMIC
Abstract-Résumé: Antifolates are widely used drugs during chemotherapeutic interventions.  In this third millenium, chemotherapy of infectious diseases is jeopardized by the emergence of drug resistance.  In this grant proposal we are proposing to pursue our studies on folate metabolism in the human parasite Leishmania.  Leishmania is more and more resistant to the chemothapeutic mainstays and alternatives are urgently needed. Leishmania is endemic in several countries including Afghanistan and Irak where Canadians are more and more present. These studies should pinpoint novel intracellular target for drug development and should suggest strategies to circumvent resistance.

TitreApplicationTitle: Translational control in eukaryotic development
Keywords-MotsClés: DEVELOPMENTAL GENETICS; DROSOPHILA; INTERCELLULAR SIGNALING; STARVATION RESPONSE; TRANSGENIC ORGANISMS
Abstract-Résumé: Translation is the process by which proteins are produced using  the information found in genes.  We are interested in how  translation of a gene is initiated, and have identified and studied  numerous factors required for this to occur in the fruitfly  Drosophila.  One of these factors, called eIF4E, is itself regulated  by a protein (4E-BP) which binds to it and inhibits its activity.  In  the most recent term of the grant, we have found that regulation  of translation by 4E-BP is necessary for an organism to resist  starvation and other stress conditions.  Under normal  conditions, Drosophila lacking 4E-BP have a higher fat content  that wild-type flies, indicating that 4E-BP has a function in  metabolic regulation.  As 4E-BP expression and activity increase  in response to insulin in both Drosophila and mammals, our  work has established a model system for understanding the  fundamental causes of diabetes.  The proposed work will  expand and extend this study to understand more about the  mechanisms by which 4E-BP activity is regulated, and to identify  and characterize critical target genes whose expression is  regulated by 4E-BP.

TitreApplicationTitle: Differences in uptake of cancer preventive options in Canadian women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation
Keywords-MotsClés: BRCA1; BRCA2; BREAST CANCER; CANCER PREVENTION; OVARIAN CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation have one of the highest known risks for the development of breast and ovarian cancers.  The average cumulative risks for BRCA1 carriers by age 70 years is 65% for breast cancer and 39% for ovarian cancer.  The corresponding risks for BRCA2 carriers are 45% and 11% [1].  Fortunately, there are options available for women to lower their risk of both breast and ovarian cancers.  Thus, the value of genetic testing for BRCA1 and BRCA2 is to identify high-risk women, and ultimately reduce the number of cancers occurring, and in-turn, reduce the number of women dying of the disease.  However, this goal can only be achieved if women do elect for a cancer prevention option.  In Canada, we have observed marked differences in uptake depending on where in the country a woman received her genetic counseling and testing.  The ranges in uptake of the options were quite substantial, ranging from 8 to 46% for prophylactic mastectomy, 39 to 67% for prophylactic oophorectomy, and 4 to 16% for tamoxifen. We do not currently understand why these differences exist.   The proposed study aims to determine the reasons for the differences in uptake of preventive options in Canadian women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.  By understanding the reasons for the differences, we can aim to address the differences to ensure that all Canadian women who undergo genetic testing for BRCA1 and BRCA2 receive consistent care.

TitreApplicationTitle: The development of pain distress regulation in infancy: A longitudinal analysis of infant, caregiver and interactional factors
Keywords-MotsClés: BEHAVIOUR CODING AND INTERVIEW; INFANT DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORY; INFANT PAIN RESPONSE AND EMOTION REGULATION; LONGITUDINAL GROWTH MODELING; MOTHER MENTAL HEALTH; MOTHER-INFANT INTERACTION
Abstract-Résumé: Learning how to manage distress is an important developmental skill that impacts biological, psychological and social dimensions of health . It is currently held that how caregivers modulate an infant's distress is crucial to later distress regulation abilities.  The current project aims to follow a group of mothers and infants through routine immunizations over the first year of life (2-, 6- and 12- month immunization). Researchers will videotape the mother-infant dyad during each immunization visit to the pediatrician. After each visit, mothers will participate in an interview that covers topics such as maternal mental health, current stressors and perceived social support.  By collecting behavioural and interview data over an infant's first year of life, we hope to better understand how both infant characteristics and maternal characteristics influence a child's ability to regulate distress at the end of the first year of life.  In addition to providing important descriptive data relevant to the health of all babies, these findings will help infant caregivers better understand and improve the developmental trajectories of vulnerable infants in greatest danger of detrimental long-term physical and psychosocial health outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding chronic pain following surgery in women
Keywords-MotsClés: ABDOMINAL SURGERY; ADOLESCENTS; BREAST SURGERY; CAESARIAN SECTION; CHILDREN; CHRONIC PAIN; HEALTH CARE UTILIZATION; HEALTH RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE; PROSPECTIVE COHORT; WOMEN
Abstract-Résumé: Pain directly impacts quality of life and function and a growing body of evidence suggests that women are experiencing chronic pain after fairly common surgical procedures. Pain after surgery is one of the most common complications associated with delayed recovery and discharge from hospital, further effecting women's lives. Varying levels of chronic postsurgical pain are reported with rates as high as 50% after abdominal surgery. However there is a paucity of information about the etiology and epidemiology of chronic postsurgical pain.  Prevention of chronic pain is important because it is difficult to manage once incurred, and is associated with high levels of disability and poor health related quality of life.  The purpose of this program of research is to identify factors associated with chronic postsurgical pain and decreased health related quality of life in women after gynecologic surgery, caesarian section and breast surgery. The study will also analyze type and amount of health care utilization related to this problem. The studies currently underway are the first phase of a line of enquiry to address chronic pain following necessary gynecological procedures. Findings will inform the next phase where a multi-intervention will be evaluated. Chronic pain is long lasting and difficult to manage, and predictors of chronic pain are necessary to aid in the development of improved prevention and management strategies specific to women. This research will have profound implications for pre-operative counselling, informed consent, and individually tailored pain treatment strategies for women.

TitreApplicationTitle: Maintaining women caregivers' health in palliative and end-of-life care
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; MEDICALLY UNDER-SERVED AREAS; MIXED METHODS; PALLIATIVE CARE; POLICY RESEARCH; WOMEN CAREGIVERS
Abstract-Résumé: Women are assuming the overwhelming majority of costs and responsibilities associated with palliative and end-of-life (P/EoL) caregiving.  P/EoL caregiving responsibilities are often more considerable than what women caregivers can manage, resulting in compromised physical, psychosocial and financial health.  Preventing morbidity and enhancing the health of women caregivers engaged in P/EoL care is a critically important issue in Canada due to population aging and increased pressure to provide care in the home.  The Research Program currently funded via CIHR involves two interrelated research streams addressing the health of women caregivers engaged in P/EoL care.  The first is focused on preventing WC morbidity and the second on improving P/EoL health care services in medically under-serviced areas for women caregivers.  This Research Program will build capacity on women¿s health through knowledge translation and dissemination, community-university research partnerships, and through the training of the next generation of researchers in women¿s health.  The highlighted project from the first research stream is the evaluation of the Compassionate Care Benefit, a caregiver policy recently introduced in Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR team in community genetics (ECOGENE-21)
Keywords-MotsClés: COMMUNITY GENETICS; CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE; GENOMICS; HEALTH SERVICES; LIPID DISORDERS; METABOLIC SYNDROME; POPULATION HEALTH; RARE RECESSIVE DISORDERS
Abstract-Résumé: When a large group of people lives in close geographical proximity, several resources, institutions, risks and exposure to a number of conditions are systematically shared. These include resources or conditions that contribute or influence the state of health. The concept of community genetics specifically relates to this aspect. Disease prevention and quality health care services in the community require integration of data on all determinants of health. Among health determinants, genetic information plays an important role, as do lifestyle habits and social environment. The CIHR Team in Community Genetics (ECOGENE-21) aims at understanding the role of genetic health determinants and new genetic technologies in global health issues as well as integrating this knowledge into a comprehensive framework to improve health and prevent disease at the community level. ECOGENE-21 is a cohesive, transdisciplinary initiative driven by the specific needs of communities: founder vs. diversified populations, urban vs. rural settings, ethnic and cultural backgrounds. ECOGENE-21 builds upon previous, ongoing and emerging national and international projects, platforms and networks of expertise, hence creating a unique continuum in community genetics: knowledge generation - validation - replication - integration into health programs, health services and health policies. Over a 5-year timeframe, we will conceive, deliver, evaluate and validate new cost-effective vanguard technologies, strategies and concepts for disease prevention. The team will obviously not be able to cover all dimensions of new knowledge and genomic technologies in all communities and for all health problems. Consequently, our action plan is developed around a matrix system approach which includes selected templates and "action zones" that delimitate action in an integrated design. We have selected these action zones on the basis of their likelihood of ensuring maximal dissemination of activities.

TitreApplicationTitle: Medical Annotation of the Human Genome Sequence
Keywords-MotsClés: COPY NUMBER VARIATION; GENOME-SCANNING; GENOMIC DISEASES; HUMAN GENOME ANALYSIS; PERSONALYZED GENOME; SEQUENCING; STRUCTUAL VARIATION
Abstract-Résumé: The human genome encodes the information sufficient to direct the development of a fertilized egg into a complex organism capable of decoding its own DNA instruction book. Variation in DNA forms the basis of human diversity and in some instances deleterious changes can occur resulting in disease. Recently, our group with others discovered that the human genome universally contains a previously unknown type of structural alteration of chromosomes that causes copy number variation (CNV) of genes. We have been working with an international consortium of scientists to generate public databases cataloguing the CNV content in genomes from worldwide populations. This data is now widely used by the clinical genetics, diagnostic, and biomedical research community. In this study, we will build on this fundamental knowledge and apply it towards understanding how CNVs cause or influence susceptibility to disease. Specifically, with doctors from across Canada we will collect DNA samples from individuals having undiagnosed disease, characterize their genomes using state-of-the-art technologies (including personalized genome sequencing), and assess if the CNVs found are pathogenic. Equally important will be to identify regions and features of the genome that when variable in copy number either have no clinical consequence, or are lethal. Our team will contextualize the information so it is comprehensible by clinicians, counselors, and families alike.

TitreApplicationTitle: Évaluation de l'adoption d'un guide de prise en charge interdisciplinaire de la douleur lombaire au Québec: impacts sur la pratique professionnelle.
Keywords-MotsClés: APPLICATION DES CONNAISSANCES; GUIDES DE PRATIQUE; INTERDISCIPLINARITE; LOMBALGIES; ORGANISATION DES SERVICES; PRATIQUES; PROFESSIONNELLES; PREVENTION; SANTE PUBLIQUE; EVALUATION
Abstract-Résumé: Le mal de dos amene des consequences nefastes pour l'individu qui en souffre, son entourage, et la societe dans laquelle il vit. Afin de mieux intervenir aupres des personnes qui presentent un mal de dos, les professionnels de la sante sont appeles a tenir compte des connaissances actuelles dans ce domaine. Cependant, des etudes indiquent qu'il y a un grand ecart entre les connaissances et les pratiques actuelles des professionnels. De plus, les differents professionnels n'ont pas une meme comprehension des meilleures facons d'intervenir pour le mal de dos, de telle sorte que les messages transmis a ceux qui en souffrent varient souvent. Le but de ce projet de recherche est d'evaluer les resultats de la diffusion d'un guide visant a ameliorer les interventions des professionnels de la sante aupres des personnes qui ont mal au dos. Ce projet de recherche visera a: 1) identifier et decrire la population de professionnels de la sante ayant pris connaissance du guide et celle n'en ayant pas pris connaissance, 2) decrire les connaissances et les pratiques des physiotherapeutes, des ergotherapeutes et des medecins du Quebec et les comparer avec le contenu du guide, et 3) identifier les perceptions des professionnels de la sante quant aux effets de l'utilisation du guide sur leur travail, sur la condition des personnes ayant mal au dos qui les consultent, ainsi que sur l'utilite du guide pour favoriser une meilleure collaboration entre les differents professionnels. Des questionnaires et des rencontres de groupe seront les moyens utilises afin de repondre aux objectifs. Les resultats de l'etude serviront a une meilleure application des connaissances issues de la recherche dans la pratique et aideront a harmoniser les connaissances et les pratiques des differents professionnels. Il en resultera une amelioration des services offerts aux personnes presentant un mal de dos, contribuant ainsi a l'amelioration de la sante et la qualite de vie des Canadiennes et des Canadiens.

TitreApplicationTitle: CABG off or on pump revascularization study (coronary)
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIO-PULMONARY BYPASS; COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION; CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE; COST EFFECTIVENESS; OFF-PUMP CABG; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: Coronary artery disease remains a major cause of death in Canada and consumes a significant portion of our health care budget.  Coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) is a well-recognized treatment of advanced coronary artery disease.  Conventional CABG is performed with the help of a cardiopulmonary bypass circuit (CPB), commonly called the pump. While cardiopulmonary bypass allows the surgeon to perform the delicate surgery it has been associated with significant complications such as cardiac ischemia, stroke, neuro-cognitive dysfunction and renal dysfunction.  In order to avoid these deleterious consequences, cardiac surgeons have designed new heart stabilizers to allow them to perform CABG on a beating heart without using cardiopulmonary bypass (off-pump CABG) and reduce costs of CABG surgery. The CORONARY trial is a prospective multi national randomized trial comparing the new off-pump CABG technique (beating heart surgery) vs. the conventional on-pump CABG surgery.  This trial will recruit 4700 patients from 100 cardiac surgery centers in North America, South America, Western Europe Eastern Europe Middle East and Asia.  The co-primary outcomes are a composite of total mortality, MI, stroke, renal failure and repeat revascularization at 30 days and 5 years.  The secondary outcome is a cost-effectiveness analysis.  We are confident to demonstrate an improvement in the safety of CABG surgery and reduce costs in the delivery of cardiac services.

TitreApplicationTitle: Activity-related adaptations in neuronal gene expression and functional properties in rat spinal cord
Keywords-MotsClés: EXERCISE; GENE EXPRESSION; LOCOMOTION; MOTONEURONES; SPINAL CORD; TRANSECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Recent evidence suggests that physical activity has an impact on the biochemistry and function of the nervous system.  We propose to examine this plasticity in the spinal cord.  Rats will be treated with increased or decreased chronic neuromuscular activity by allowing them to exercise on voluntary exercise wheels, to live in standard square cages, or treating them with a simulated weightless environment.  After 16 weeks, the rats will be decerebrated, and fictive locomotion will be generated by stimulating the mesencephalic locomotor region using a tungsten electrode.  We will measure the regularity and robustness of the locomotion from recordings taken from hindlmb flexor and extensor nerves, bilaterally.  We will also measure biophysical properties of alpha-motoneurones that innervate the hindlimb muscles, during locomotion and quiescence, and compare these properties among the activity groups.  In separate groups of rats, we will measure the effects of activity level on the expression of genes encoding for receptors thought to be important in locomotion, including receptors for glutamate and serotonin. Finally, in rats with transected spinal cords, we will measure these parameters 4 weeks following the injury, as well as in transected rats exposed to daily treatment with passive leg exercise.  This basic information is important for our understanding of the use of physical activity as a rehabilitative modality to improve function of the nervous system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Transcriptional regulation by estrogen and breast cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIESTROGENS; BREAST CANCER; ESTROGEN SIGNALING; HORMONAL THERAPY; REGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION
Abstract-Résumé: Estrogens play important roles in the normal development and function of the reproductive system, but also stimulate growth of about two thirds of breast tumors. Estrogens act via specific receptors, which modulate gene expression to effect the cellular response to these hormones. Selection of estrogen target genes is likely to play an important role in tumorigenesis. Here we propose to investigate the mechanisms controlling the choice of genes regulated by estrogen receptors, which determine the physiological or pathological consequences of estrogen exposure.  We will use estrogen receptor-positive breast and uterine cancer cell lines which express different networks of estrogen target genes to analyze the mechanisms governing the selectivity of gene regulation by estrogens. These studies will increase our understanding of the mechanisms of action of estrogen receptors and have the potential to shed light on the processes leading to changes in the mode of action of estrogens in tumorigenesis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude de cohorte observationnelle pour identifier les facteurs influençant l'observance des patients incidents sur les statines
Keywords-MotsClés: DOULEUR; MYOPATHIES; OBSERVANCE; PREVENTION CARDIOVASCULAIRE; QUESTIONNAIRES; STATINES
Abstract-Résumé: Quand un medicament est prescrit dans le but de prevenir des evenements nocifs, de nombreux patients cessent de le prendre avant d'avoir eu le temps d'en beneficier. C'est le cas des statines qui sont des medicaments tres efficaces pour baisser le cholesterol et  prevenir les maladies du coeur. Notre groupe a demontre qu'au Quebec, 60% des patients inities sur une statine l'ont cessee apres 2 ans. L'arret premature de ce medicament, que la plupart des patients devraient prendre durant toute leur vie, a des consequences desastreuses. L'effet protecteur du medicament contre les maladies cardiaques disparait  lorsque le patient  l'arrete. Par ailleurs, etant donne qu'une grande partie de la medication est financee par des fonds publics, un arret premature produit un gaspillage important. Bien que cette mauvaise observance soit  bien documentee, ses causes demeurent  mal connues. De ce fait, il est tres difficile d'elaborer et de deployer des interventions visant a ameliorer le probleme. Une des causes de cette mauvaise observance est que ces medicaments n'apportent aucun benefice immediat. De plus, les statines peuvent produire des effets secondaires indesirables au niveau musculaire ce qui peut amener a un arret du medicament. L'objectif principal de notre etude est d'identifier les differentes raisons qui amenent les patients a arreter leurs statines en portant une attention particuliere au role des effets secondaires musculaires. Les participants seront recrutes aupres d'omnipraticiens dans differentes regions du Quebec qui leur auront prescit une statine pour une premiere fois. Les patients interesses signeront un consentement informe autorisant les membres de notre equipe a les contacter par telephone pour repondre a des questionnaires periodiques. Nous pourrons ainsi determiner le pourcentage de patients qui cessent leur medicament, les raisons de cet arret, l'incidence et la severite des effets indesirables au niveau musculaire et leurs consequences.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development and function of C. elegans pharyngeal glands
Keywords-MotsClés: C. ELEGANS; FOREGUT; GENETICS; GLANDS; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: One of the key questions of developmental biology is how organs are formed and how genes control this process. To understand this complex process I am studying the development of a simple organ: the pharynx of the nematode C. elegans. C. elegans is a small (~1mm long), soil-dwelling worm and its pharynx is analogous to the human throat and stomach, functioning to pump in food and initiate digestion. What we learn about worm development often applies to other animals, including humans. For example, a gene that is critical for formation of the C. elegans pharynx is also critical for development of the human digestive tract.  My current interest is in how different types of cells in the pharynx function and how they are programmed, or specified, to carry out that function. Work in my lab has found that glands in the pharynx function much as our own salivary glands: correct development of glands in nematodes and mammals depends on the same gene, and in both animals the glands function to protect from bacterial infection and toxicity. Surprisingly, worms with abnormal glands die in response to their normal bacterial food source. This has significant implications for understanding host-bacterial interactions. In addition, because interference with gland function leads to death of the nematode, it may provide a new avenue for combatting parasitic nematodes, which are an enormous problem in both plants and animals worldwide.

TitreApplicationTitle: Combination pharmacotherapy for the management of pain
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALGESIC PHARMACOLOGY; ANTICONVULSANTS; ANTIDEPRESSANTS; CHRONIC PAIN; CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY; DIABETIC NEUROPATHY; DRUG COMBINATIONS; NEUROPATHIC PAIN; OPIOIDS; PAIN; PAIN MEASUREMENT; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS
Abstract-Résumé: Pain is a major public health problem affecting one-third of the population and costing $165 billion/year in North America alone. Individual pain-relievers provide incomplete relief and can often produce troubling side effects. It has been suggested that combining different kinds of pain-relievers may improve effectiveness and reduce side effects. Some drug combinations have been proven better than each of their components alone. However, it has also been shown that the ratio, or proportion, of drug doses in a combination is very important such that some ratios (e.g. more of one drug and less of the other) may perform much better than other ratios (e.g. equal amounts of both drugs). We have recently shown that a gabapentin-morphine combination is better than either drug alone. However, because of how that study was designed, we could only test one dose ratio of gabapentin to morphine (i.e. 50 mg gabapentin for every 1 mg morphine). The main objective of this grant proposal is to demonstrate that drug combinations relieve pain more effectively (and/or with fewer side effects) at some dose ratios compared to others. This objective will be met by conducting a clinical trial in diabetic patients with pain due to nerve disease. The research plan involves a double-blind, randomized crossover trial which studies the combination of a newer gabapentin-like drug (pregabalin) with morphine in four different milligram dose ratios (i.e. 60:1, 13:1, 3:1 and 0.6:1). During each of the 4 treatment periods, doses of the two drugs will be gradually increased to the highest possible dose, yet a dose which produces only minimal side effects. We expect to determine which dose ratio of these drugs provides the best pain relief and/or fewest side effects and establish new methods for studying pain-relieving drug combinations. Future research using these methods will allow for more comprehensive testing of other analgesic combinations for pain management.

TitreApplicationTitle: Osteoporosis, Falls, and Fracture Prevention
Keywords-MotsClés: APPROPRIATE PRESCRIBING; ELDERLY; FALLS; FRACTURES; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; OSTEOPOROSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Numerous studies indicate an osteoporosis caregap - only 30% of women and 10% of men with a fracture ever receive treatment, despite clear practice guidelines and a dramatic reduction in future fractures with treatment by 40-60%.  A fragmented approach to fracture prevention currently exists, particularly in the frail, elderly population. There is a lack of integration between management and treatment of osteoporosis and the assessment of falls. Development of elder-focused strategies and education of health care providers is critical. With a focus on improved delivery of health care and knowledge translation (KT) activities, this program of research will address two major areas for preventing osteoporosis/fractures in the elderly: 1) Improved mechanisms to identify patients who require treatment in acute care, primary care, and long-term care (LTC) 2) Developing and disseminating best practices for LTC for falls prevention, and osteoporosis management 3) Mentorship of an interdisciplinary team of young investigators. To address these objectives, the 5-year plan of research will build on my existing partnerships (community, hospital, and government), ongoing research, and KT activities, including i) 'Osteoporosis, Falls, and Fracture Prevention Strategy in LTC': Working with key partners (Ontario Ministry of Health, Osteoporosis Canada, College of Family Practice, LTC Association), I will lead a team to implement best practice protocols for osteoporosis management in LTC facilities; ii) Fracture? Think Osteoporosis (FTOP): Building on this disease management program, we will develop and pilot an integrated approach to fracture care in the elderly (overcoming falls 'silos' that currently exist); iii) Canadian Quality Circle National Project: This program promotes uptake of Osteoporosis guidelines with family physicians using multiple KT strategies. Chair funding will enable expansion of this program to include elder-focused fracture care and falls prevention.

The second major objective is to use this knowledge as the basis for the development of specific cell lineages for novel stem cell therapiesa central tenet of regenerative medicineto replace or regenerate cell populations and tissues destroyed by disease, accident or age.

Abstract-Résumé: Disturbances and complications of connective tissue matrix remodeling (e.g. arthritis, periodontal diseases) are high prevalence health care problems, particularly in tissues that are subjected to prolonged physical loading or chronic infections.  The impact on society as measured by morbidity, premature loss of function, quality of life and cost is enormous (e.g. $4.4 billion for arthritis alone in Canada). This great impact is because of the ubiquitous distribution of connective tissues throughout the body and their key roles in supporting, attaching and stabilizing tissues and organs. The proposed research program examines the fundamental mechanisms that regulate matrix remodeling. The applicant's research program will build upon his existing strengths and greatly improve understanding of how matrix remodeling is regulated by cell signals. This knowledege will provide new opportunities for therapies that prevent untimely and inappropriate matrix remodeling as is seen in fibrotic diseases of liver, kidney, heart and joints.

This will motivate patients to comply with the interventions, leading to achievement of desired outcomes and reduced need for additional and expensive treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Early Rheumatoid Arthritis Help-Seeking Experience (ERAHSE) Project
Keywords-MotsClés: EARLY INTERVENTION; HELP-SEEKING; MIXED METHODS APPROACH; RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS
Abstract-Résumé: Early treatment for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can prevent unnecessary joint damage and improve health outcomes; however, up to 38% of people waited longer than 3 months to initiate a consult with a family physician for joint symptoms. Current research has mainly focused on family physicians to improve referrals to rheumatologists, but little is known about the facilitators and barriers for patients to initiate medical consults for arthritis symptoms.   This project aims to improve the provision of treatment for people with early RA by understanding their help-seeking processes (i.e., the practice of information-seeking and treatment-seeking) in the context of their daily life. The objectives are to (1) identify factors influencing help-seeking from the symptom onset to diagnosis; (2) estimate the percent of people with early RA in a nation-wide arthritis registry who consulted a family physician within the first month of arthritis symptoms; and (3) test the relationships between facilitators/barriers and timely consultation with family physicians for early RA symptoms.  In Phase I of the study, we will interview 30-36 patients with early RA about their help-seeking experience and information needs. In Phase II, we will conduct a mail survey with 185 patients with early RA, in order to test whether certain barriers / facilitators are related to seeking treatment for joint symptoms.   Early treatment for RA can prevent unnecessary joint damage and improve patients' health outcomes. Our results will allow researchers and clinicians to develop targeted interventions to improve early diagnosis and DMARD use. Also, this research will inform health care administrators in the planning of health services and support resources (e.g., education programs, information technologies, transportation, and health human resources), leading to a patient-centred arthritis care strategy.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of histone modifications in adrenergic-stimulated gene expression in the rat pineal gland
Keywords-MotsClés: ADRENERGIC-REGULATED GENES; CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; HISTONE MODIFICATIONS; PINEAL; SIRNA
Abstract-Résumé: Abnormalities of rhythmic hormone secretion are increasingly being implicated in a number of common and serious medical conditions including obesity, depression, sleep apnea, jetlag, and fatigue in shift workers. Our research program is aimed at understanding the mechanisms controlling rhythmic hormone secretion.  Since we can identify factors that control the surge in the rhythmic production of melatonin every night, we use the rat pineal gland as a model for these studies.  In this application we propose to investigate the impact that neurotransmitter-induced alterations of histone, a structural protein of chromosome, has on this nightly surge of melatonin.  The findings from our study will increase our understanding of rhythmic hormone secretion and will be fundamentally important to the future development of treatment strategies for conditions linked to alterations of rhythmic hormone secretion.

TitreApplicationTitle: Factors that Influence the Production of and Responses to Intimate Partner Violence in the Sri Lankan Context
Keywords-MotsClés: CRITICAL ETHNOGRAPHY; FEMINIST RESEARCH; GLOBALIZATION; INTIMATE PARTNER VIOLENCE; POSTCOLONIZATION; WOMEN'S HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) is a worldwide public health issue with far-reaching impacts, yet most health research on IPV and its effects has been conducted in North America. In a recent WHO study (2006), rates of lifetime IPV across 10 countries varied widely, as did women responses to IPV, with many factors affecting the production of IPV and its effects. In Sri Lanka, a country steeped in civil war for more than 20 years and the homeland of more than 250,000 immigrants to Canada, leaders of NGOs suggest that IPV is pervasive but little research has been done to support this claim. Result of several recent studies in the Tamil community in Toronto suggest that stressors associated with immigration, such as loss of socioeconomic status, contribute to IPV and affect the ways in which women and communities respond to it. However, it is difficult to understand the complexity of IPV after immigration without understanding factors that contribute to its production in the country of origin. In this qualitative exploratory study, we will describe the ways in which gender, social, economic, geographic, and cultural factors influence the production of IPV among Tamils and Sinhalese, and influence their responses to IPV and their health. In collaboration with community leaders in Sri Lanka, in-depth interviews and focus groups will be conducted with key stakeholders, including health professionals, staff in NGOs, women and men from diverse socioeconomic and religious backgrounds, and women who have experienced IPV, to gain their perspectives about the production of IPV, its effects, and strategies for health promotion and violence prevention. Findings may be used to inform services and policies to reduce IPV and support women exposed to IPV in Sri Lanka, and will provide a basis for a larger study examining factors that shape the health of Tamil and Sinhalese women who have experienced IPV in both Canada and Sri Lanka.

ClasseRechercheFR: MALADIES INFECTIEUSES ET PARASITAIRES; AUTRES MALADIES VENERIENNES
TitreApplicationTitle: Microtubule proteins during phagocytosis and infection.
Keywords-MotsClés: CHLAMYDIA INFECTIONS; FLUORESCENT MICROSCOPY; INFLAMMATION; MICROTUBULE CYTOSKELETON; PHAGOCYTOSIS; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: The microtubule cytoskeleton is essential for cell division, cell polarity and cell secretion due its primary role in intracellular trafficking.  The aim of our research is to understand the microtubule cytoskeleton contributions to macrophage function.  Macrophages defend the body against invading microorganisms, comprising a key element of our innate immunity. Macrophages clear the body of pathogens by binding specifically to them and engulfing and destroying them in an intracellular compartment.   Macrophage killing mechanisms can be enhanced by inflammatory mediators however prolonged activation of macrophages can lead to serious inflammatory disorders.  While many pathogens are killed effectively by macrophages, some pathogens have evolved strategies to avoid degradation in macrophages.  A major bacterial strategy for host infection and evasion includes manipulation of the host cytoskeleton.         We have just completed an exhaustive screen of the major proteins associated with the microtubule cytoskeleton in macrophages.  Identification of these microtubule proteins will be used to tackle three major projects.  First, we will use sophisticated microscopy to examine the function of microtubule stabilization for secretion of matrix enzymes in activated macrophages. Secondly, we will examine the role of microtubules in modulating cell surface receptors and vesicle trafficking events during internalization of complement-opsonized particles.  Importantly, we will examine how pathogens like Chlamydia trachomatis, which contribute to worldwide health problems, modify the microtubule cytoskeleton to effect their host invasion and replication strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Interactions of aryl hydrocarbon receptor and estrogen receptor alpha
Keywords-MotsClés: ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR; BREAST CANCER; CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; ESTROGEN RECEPTOR; GENOMICS; TOXICOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) and estrogen receptor alpha (ERalpha) are two proteins that play key physiological roles in cells, but are also implicated in diseases such as breast cancer. AHR mediates most, if not all, of the toxic effects of chemicals called dioxins, whereas ERalpha is the key regulator of estrogen action. Previous studies have shown that these two proteins and their associated networks interact with each other. However, the mechanisms behind this interplay remain elusive. Recently, new insights into the function of AHR/ERalpha have been reported that have important implications on how they relay signals inside cells. Our studies have shown that molecules that activate AHR induce binding of ERalpha to genes targeted by AHR, and that this effect is enhanced by co-treatment with estrogen, but that estrogen alone has no effect. These data suggest that molecules that bind to AHR modulate ERalpha in a manner distinct from estrogen, suggesting new mechanisms of interaction between these two receptors. These interactions have important consequences on ERalpha activity and its regulation, but also highlight a new regulatory function for ERalpha. The general objective of this study is to elucidate the mechanisms of reciprocal interaction between AHR and ERalpha. To attain this objective, the researchers will use powerful molecular biological approaches, animal models, and genomics. This study should also identify the signals that induce interaction between ERalpha and AHR. A better understanding of the AHR/ERalpha interplay will enable better estimates of the health risks associated with the combined environmental and dietary exposure to modulators of AHR and ERalpha activity. In addition, the results should help clarify the complex mechanisms of AHR toxicity and its role in diseases such as breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Reducing social inequalities in smoking.
Keywords-MotsClés: INTERVENTION RESEARCH; PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH; REFLEXIVITY; SMOKING; SOCIAL INEQUALITIES IN HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: The period between February and June 2006 showed signs of relatively good news for population health in Canada; just over 4.5 million people, representing 18% of the population aged 15 years and older, were current smokers.  Despite this trend towards a decline in population-based smoking levels, two areas of tobacco control are particularly problematic: 1) smoking prevalence and incidence is following an increasingly steep social class gradient, across all age groups, and; 2) amongst younger smokers there has not been similar evidence of major reductions in tobacco use. The combined data on social inequalities in smoking among youth, along with the continuing high smoking rates among youth as an overall group, suggest a clear need to focus on youth, and particularly low SES youth, as a vulnerable population with regard to their tobacco use.  This research has two major objectives: 1) To understand some of the social reasons why lower SEP youth smokers are at continuing high risk of smoking; 2) To use the information collected regarding the social context of youth smoking to stimulate reflexive practice amongst tobacco control practitioners to improve intervention efforts. This is a comparative study involving Montreal and Vancouver. The first phase of this research explores the social context of smoking drawing on the perspectives of youth smokers themselves, as well as the perspectives of practitioners.  For Phase 2, we propose to use an adaptation of Labonte et al's (1999) "story/dialogue method" (S/D-M) to bring youth smokers and tobacco control practitioners together in a dialogue about the social context of smoking.  Phase 3 will enable us to judge the impact of the dialogical methods used during Phase 2 on practitioners' actual practice.

TitreApplicationTitle: Integration of Disconfirmatory Evidence in Schizophrenia: Cognitive and Neural Underpinnings
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNITION; HALLUCINATIONS & DELUSIONS; NEUROIMAGING; SCHIZOPHRENIA
Abstract-Résumé: A primary symptom of schizophrenia is delusions. Delusions are defined as fixed false beliefs. Evidence from our laboratory suggests that the fixedness aspect of fixed false beliefs is attributable, at least in part, to dysfunction of a brain system responsible for integrating disconfirmatory evidence for the purpose of revising thoughts. The current study is designed to determine the independence of this brain system from others that may be relevant to delusions, both in terms of measurement of behaviour and functional brain imaging, and to assess whether or not changes in this brain system correspond with changes in delusions over time. Awareness of strong evidence that impairment in integrating disconfirmatory evidence is the basis of delusions may prove helpful for consumers of mental health services, to the extent that consumers can recognize and counter the thinking patterns that lead to psychosis without the need to discuss personally relevant delusions. This work may also lead to new clinical targets for treatment responsiveness and prediction of relapse in schizophrenia patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular mechanisms orchestrating epithelial cell polarity
Keywords-MotsClés: COLON CANCER; EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY; EPITHELIAL POLARITY; INTESTINAL EPITHELIUM
Abstract-Résumé: Epithelia, composed of epithelial cells, delimit the frontier between the external environment and the inside of multicellular organisms. Therefore, epithelial cells cover the surface of the body (e.g. skin) and line internal cavities of the body (found in the intestine, lung, liver, etc). The main functions of epithelia are to protect against pathogen invasion and to selectively transport several molecules to adjust the chemical composition of different compartments of the body. The function and homeostasis of epithelial cells greatly depend on their polarity, meaning the asymmetrical distribution of cellular components. Indeed, loss of epithelial polarity is associated with progression of many cancers. Mechanisms linking the loss of cell polarity with cell division and invasion in the context of cancer are still poorly understood.  We have previously identified genes important for the establishment and maintenance of epithelial cell polarity. Mutations in these genes result in loss of tissue integrity similar to what occurs during cancer progression. The aim of this research program is to understand how these genes regulate the normal physiology and maintain homeostasis of epithelial cells.   Our study will bring a better understanding of the fundamental mechanisms underlying the establishment of epithelial cell polarity. Furthermore, this will provide further insight into diseases such as cancer which involve polarity defects.

TitreApplicationTitle: Rho-kinase inhibitor as therapy for chronic neonatal pulmonary hypertension
Keywords-MotsClés: ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY; PULMONARY HYPERTENSION; RHO-KINASE; VASCULAR REMODELING; Y-27632
Abstract-Résumé: Pulmonary hypertension is a commonly observed complication of critically ill newborn infants that causes considerable mortality and long-term morbidity.  An increased propensity to pulmonary hypertension in the newborn period is related to two factors: 1) a failure of normal dilation of blood vessels in the lung at birth, and 2) rapid thickening of the walls of blood vessels  (known as vascular remodeling), which may become chronic and irreversible.  Vascular remodeling may have especially serious consequences for the newborn, by causing long-term inhibition of lung growth and progression to fatal pulmonary hypertension in later life.  The therapies we currently have available to treat newborns with pulmonary hypertension, which act by dilating blood vessels, are often ineffective, have not been shown to decrease death or improve long term outcome, and may cause harm.  More effective therapies are urgently required.  A great deal of evidence has emerged implicating the signaling molecule, Rho-kinase (ROCK), as a central mediator of chronic pulmonary hypertension in adults.  In short-term studies, we showed that a single dose of a specific ROCK inhibitor drug (Y-27632) was dramatically effective at reversing pulmonary hypertension in infant rats with severe vascular remodeling.  This promising new drug therefore has the unique potential to both effectively prevent and treat chronic pulmonary hypertension.  Our proposed research in newborn rats will address two questions with important clinical implications: 1) whether treatment with Y-27632 from birth will prevent chronic pulmonary hypertension from developing, and 2) whether chronic treatment with Y-27632 can reverse the pathological changes of chronic pulmonary hypertension.  The proposed studies will help open the way for the testing of this therapy in human newborns.  ROCK inhibitors may well represent a breakthrough in our ability to treat this challenging, and often-devastating, disease of the newborn.

TitreApplicationTitle: The CHIPS trial (control of hypertension in pregnancy study)
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIHYPERTENSIVE THERAPY; DIFFERENTIAL CONTROL OF MATERNAL BLOOD PRESSURE; FETAL AND NEONATAL COMPLICATIONS; MATERNAL COMPLICATIONS; PREGNANCY HYPERTENSION; RANDOMISED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: Almost 10% of pregnancies are complicated by high blood pressure (hypertension). Experts agree that blood pressure medication should be given to pregnant women with severe hypertension to protect them from stroke. However, for pregnant women with non-severe hypertension, it is not known whether blood pressure medication benefits mothers or babies, and such medication may cause poorer growth of the baby. Such babies are at increased risk for problems as newborns (and thereafter). Guidelines for treatment have been based mainly on the opinions of experts, and based on a national survey, Canadian obstetricians are uncertain about what to do. We have designed CHIPS (Control of Hypertension In Pregnancy Study) to determine whether allowing the mother's blood pressure to be higher than normal during pregnancy results in better health of the baby after birth than does normalising blood pressure by prescribing blood pressure medication. Women with non-severe hypertension, who are between 14 and 33 weeks' pregnant and are carrying a live baby will be eligible to participate. Women will not be eligible if they have severe hypertension, proteinuria, are not eligible for either arm of the trial, are likely to deliver in the next week, and/or are carrying a multiple pregnancy or a baby with a serious abnormality. Women will carry a diary with them during the pregnancy; they will use this to record blood pressure values and tests used to monitor mother and baby. Women and babies will be followed until six weeks after birth or until hospital discharge, whichever is later. The results of CHIPS will be used by clinicians to choose the best treatment for mothers and their unborn babies, in Canada and internationally.

TitreApplicationTitle: A parallel study of methamphetamine psychosis on brain structure and neuronal integrity in humans and animals, with regards to cognitive impairment
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTION; ANIMAL/HUMAN; COGNITION; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; MAGNETIC RESONANCE SPECTROSCOPY; METHAMPHETAMINE
Abstract-Résumé: Methamphetamine abuse has risen dramatically in North America in the past decade, with levels reaching near epidemic proportions. High doses of this drug frequently result in a psychosis similar to that observed in schizophrenia. Our research group has recently been awarded a CIHR Operating Grant to characterize the nature of cognitive deficits that occur following methamphetamine induced psychosis. In order to extend the impact of this project, we propose to conduct a related series of structural MRI and Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy studies in a subgroup of this same population, to investigate potential changes in brain structure and neuronal integrity. Putative changes are predicted to correlate with cognitive impairment. In order to address various confounding issues raised by studying this clinical population, we shall also utilize a rodent model of exposure to multiple high doses of methamphetamine. With this paradigm, we shall examine comparable anatomical and metabolic changes to those noted in humans, assessed in vivo by an animal NMR scanner, as well as possible changes in cognition resulting from drug exposure. The results of both human and animal studies will offer important insights into the neurobiology of methamphetamine induced cognitive impairment, and may provide the basis for future treatment strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: The causes and consequences of genome reduction in eukaryotes
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; DNA SEQUENCING; GENOME REDUCTION; GENOMICS; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PROTEIN STRUCTURE
Abstract-Résumé: Genome size in eukaryotic (nucleus-containing) microorganisms varies more than 200,000 fold. At the lower end of this spectrum are the reduced genomes of microorganisms that have become symbionts or intracellular pathogens, such as apicomplexans (e.g., Plasmodium, the causative agent of malaria) and microsporidian parasites (e.g., Encephalitozoon, an opportunistic pathogen of AIDS patients). The most extreme examples of eukaryotic genome reduction are the "nucleomorph" genomes of cryptophytes and chlorarachniophytes. Nucleomorphs are the remnant nuclei of eukaryotic phototrophs that established themselves as endosymbionts inside a non-photosynthetic host cell¿at well under a megabase in size, nucleomorph genomes are the smallest and most compact nuclear genomes known. This research proposes to use the miniaturized nucleomorphs of cryptophytes and chlorarachniophytes as a model system with which to elucidate the process of genome reduction and quantify its impact on protein structure and function. These results will contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the universal principles governing genome size change in eukaryotes and provide insight into the genetic and biochemical changes that occur when free-living eukaryotic microorganisms become intracellular parasites.

TitreApplicationTitle: Examining labour market changes and their consequences on injury and illness in Canada: a focused examination of their effects on recent immigrants
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH BEHAVIOURS; IMMIGRANT HEALTH; LONGITUDINAL METHODS; OCCUPATIONAL ILLNESS AND INJURY; SOCIAL EPIDEMIOLOGY; SURVEY DATA
Abstract-Résumé: The last 25-years have seen many changes in Canadian workplaces.  Greater numbers of Canadians work in the service sector, work extra unpaid hours, or are self-employed, with labour force participants also being older and better educated. In addition, the majority of labour force growth in last 10-years, and all the growth in the near future, will result from immigrants to Canada.  Despite their importance to Canada, surprisingly little research has examined the labour market conditions of immigrants and the health impact of these experiences. Demographic and structural labour market changes have changed the nature of work-related injuries and illnesses in Canada. Trends in claims submitted to Canadian workers' compensation boards suggest, at the very least, that occupational injuries and illnesses are becoming less visible, less acutely traumatic, and more difficult to attribute to a specific cause. It is likely that recent immigrants to Canada may face specific challenges with the changing nature of occupational injury and illness; both in their recognition of when a work injury has occurred, and the consequences from these injuries.   Moreover, changes in the nature of work might be associated with various chronic health problems, with these changes possibly having differential health consequences for recent immigrants. For example, more sedentary employment, longer working hours, and decreased job autonomy may lead to decreases in physical activity, resulting in higher rates of obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular disease. These types of working conditions, combined with difficult cultural transitions, and higher financial and social stress may be particularly deleterious to particular groups of immigrants. The research undertaken as part of this award seeks address the paucity of research in these areas, helping to better understand the how changes in work impact on work-related injuries and illness, and chronic health conditions among immigrants to Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Heart outcomes prevention evaluation (HOPE-3) trial. A large simple randomized trial of combined cholesterol modification and blood pressure lowering in middle aged people at average risk
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD PRESSURE LOWERING; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE PREVENTION; CHOLESTEROL LOWERING; PRIMARY PREVENTION; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease and stroke are major causes of death and disability worldwide and are largely preventable. Cholesterol and blood pressure are major cardiovascular risk factors. Previous studies have shown that certain drugs can effectively and safely lower cholesterol and blood pressure and prevent heart attacks and strokes. Such studies have been conducted primarily in people who had already sustained a heart attack or a stroke, or in people with high cholesterol and blood pressure levels. However, most heart attacks and strokes occur in people with average ("normal") cholesterol and blood pressure. Therefore, in the HOPE-3 trial we will evaluate whether a cholesterol lowering drug, rosuvastatin, and a combination blood pressure lowering pill, candesartan/hydrochlorothiazide, used alone or together can reduce the risk of heart attacks, stroke and their sequelae in people without known heart disease and at average risk. The trial will enroll 11,000 women 65 years or older and men 55 years or older without known heart disease or prior stroke and without a clear indication or contraindication to any of the study medications. Eligible and consenting individuals will be randomized to receive either the real study medications or placebo (dummy pills) and will be monitored for an average of 5 years. The rates of heart attacks, strokes, deaths and other cardiovascular complications will be compared between subjects receiving the real drugs and those on placebo. The study will include people from at least eleven countries, will be monitored by an international group of scientists and physicians and will be coordinated by the Population Health Research Institute at McMaster University. The study is expected to demonstrate that combined lipid lowering and blood pressure lowering will substantially lower the risk for cardiovascular diseases and may substantially change our approach to cardiovascular prevention.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessing Care of Patients with Major Traumatic Injuries:  A Template for Developing Quality Indicators
Keywords-MotsClés: INJURY; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; QUALITY INDICATORS; QUALITY OF CARE; TRAUMA
Abstract-Résumé: Each year, injuries affect 700 million people around the world including 30 million North Americans and 2 million Canadians.  In Canada, injuries are the leading cause of death among those under the age of 45 years and account for more premature deaths than heart disease, lung disease or HIV infection.  In 2003, 13,906 Canadians died as a result of injury; 1 death every 38 minutes.  However, deaths are only the tip of the injury iceberg.  The human and societal burden is even greater with many survivors never returning to school, work or their "regular" lives.  Any Canadian can suffer an injury on any given day.  However, the risk of dying from injury varies amongst developed countries, provinces and Canadians of different ethnic background.  The underlying causes for these variations are unknown and remarkably little is known about the quality of care provided to patients with major injuries and the impact on patient outcomes.  We propose to begin a major work of research to measure and improve the quality of trauma care delivered in Canada.  Our first project will be to identify and evaluate all the tools that can be used to measure the quality of trauma care.  Next, we plan to survey national and international organizations with expertise in trauma care to determine how they measure the quality of trauma care and incorporate this information into performance improvement initiatives.  A sample of Canadian trauma care experts will then review the information we have collected and select the best tools for measuring the quality of trauma care.  Finally, we will test these tools in a group of injured Canadians to confirm that they are accurate and valid in measuring the quality of trauma care that patients receive.  This proposal is essential to improving outcomes for patients who suffer major traumatic injuries.  Health care providers, patients, researchers, funders and policy makers will be informed and enabled to improve patient outcomes following trauma.

TitreApplicationTitle: Ex-vivo Gene Repair of Injured Donor Lungs for transplantation
Keywords-MotsClés: CYTOKINES; EX-VIVO THERAPEUTIC GENE THERAPY; INHIBITION OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY FACTORS; LARGE ANIMAL MODELS, CLINICALLY REJECTED HUMAN DONOR LUNGS; LUNG TRANSPLANTATION
Abstract-Résumé: Over the last two decades, lung transplation has become the mainstay of therapy for selected patients suffering from many types of end-stage lung disease (e.g. emphysema, pulmonary fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension and cystic fibrosis) refractory to medical management.  Lung transplantation has enjoyed increasing success with better early and late survival rates.  However, the number of patients requiring lung transplantation has been increasing and largely exceeds the number of donors available.  As a result, the death rate on the waiting list is 20% to 30% in most lung transplant centers.  The best alternative will be to expand the number of donors.  Indeed, we currently are able to use only 15% to 25% of the lungs that are offered to us from brain dead donors; 75% to 85% of donors are rejected due to various forms of lung injury.  Hence, any stategy that would increase our utilization rate of lung donors from 15% to even 40-50% could potentially double and even triple the number of lung transplants rformed every year.  Our project, using a large animal model and human injured donor lungs will study a very novel concept:  ex-vivo (outside the body) repair of damaged lungs for transplantation.  After organ retrieval and ischemic storage we will treat the donor lungs ex-vivo for  6 to 12 hours in a special pump perfusion system while repairing the organ with gene therapy.  We will be able to evaluate the lung function in the perfusion system to document improved lung function and confirm that after transplantation.  The consequent improvement in the quality of donor lungs with ex-vivo repair will have a significant impact on the number of transplants performed each year and on the outcome after lung transplantation.

TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation of Tissue injury and Novel Approaches to Tolerance Induction to Promote Long Term Renal Transplant Survival
Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSIS; EPITHELIAL CELL; KIDNEY; TRANSPLANTATION
Abstract-Résumé: This proposal describes three major areas of research we are engaged in.  The first looks at mechanisms by which kidneys and likely ohter organs are injured following transplantation.  The very nature of transplantation is associated with organ injury, as all organs are at least temporarily removed from a blood supply with the procurement procedure.  While not preventable, the extent of injury may be modifiable by studies of the molecular pathways by which cells undergo injury.  Our hope is that these can be modified to minimize injury not only with organ procurement but also after transplantation, with rejection.  The second area is the development of genetically modified plants that express human proteins for applications in medicine.  Plant systems overcome many of the hurdles currently facing the production of biotherapeutics, including high cost, ability of produce abundant amounts, easy scale-up, and freedom from human pathogens and viruses.  Finally, we are developing protocols for human transplantation by testing those strategies most extensively tested in mouse models, to non-human primates.  It is our hope that we will define strategies that allow immune acceptance of transplant with limited or no ongoing immunosuppressive drugs.  Overall these projects are linked by a desire to utilize basic discoveries to strategies that will lead to human therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improved Methodological Approaches to Need-based Resource Allocation
Keywords-MotsClés: CAPITATION FORMULAE; HEALTH CARE RESOURCE ALLOCATION; NEED FOR HEALTH CARE; NEED-BASED
Abstract-Résumé: Growth in health expenditures and the desire to cover new services (e.g., drugs) continue to outpace our ability to fund health care. Thus, we cannot avoid the issue of how to allocate limited health care resources. It is generally accepted that equitable allocation of health resources and funding should be based on equal funding for equal need. Researchers and policy-makers have extensively worked towards this goal of equitable resource allocation in a number of areas. For example, most provinces in Canada and many industrialized countries, such as the United Kingdom and Australia, estimate expenditure need to allocate health funding between regions. In addition, similar methods and approaches are used to address other resource allocation problems in health planning and management. Despite extensive research on resource allocation methods, there remains a lack of consensus on appropriate indicators and methods. This proposed project aims to fill this gap by addressing fundamental methodological questions of resource allocation in estimating expenditure need for health care in Canadian provinces. This proposed project clearly addresses one of the most pressing health care issues in Canada, and it will have far-reaching impact in various resource allocation issues domestically and internationally. In particular, this project will contribute to informing debates on equitable federal transfers through equalization and the Canada Health Transfer.
