TitreApplicationTitle: Vitamin D intake, serum level of 25(OH)D alone and in association with bone metabolism biomarkers and their link to anthropometric values, cognitive status and functional capacity in veterans living in long-term care facilities.
Keywords-MotsClés: 25(OH)D; AGING; BIOELECTRICAL IMPEDANCE ANALYSIS; FUNCTIONAL ASSESSMENT; HEALTH; LONG-TERM CARE; MORTALITY; NUTRITION; RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL; VITAMIN D
Abstract-Résumé: Vitamin D is well known as an important nutrient for strong bones. Recently, vitamin D is also found to be important as an indicator of a person's ability to function. In Canada, vitamin is low in the senior population who live in their own homes, but less information is known about those who live in hospitals or long-term care facilities. Since improving vitamin D might be a possible and simple way to improve health and functioning in seniors, this study is designed to establish how many people have enough vitamin D and how many need to obtain more from their diet. The vitamin D will be linked with health outcomes and functioning. The data is needed to help design trials that test if taking more vitamin D improves health and functioning in seniors. The work will be conducted at Ste.Anne Hospital where the unique setting lends to the various measurements. Ultimately, finding the proper food carrier for vitamin D will provide us with the knowledge how much vitamin D can individuals eat, how much will it cost and how much more active will they be in their everyday life.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Women's Health & Immunobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: In any disease, specific target cells develop characteristics that determine severity and outcome.  Knowledge of these characteristics - disease biomarkers - provides targets for therapeutic intervention.  Dr. Fishs laboratory identifies these biomarkers, whether the  disease is viral (influenza, SARS) or autoimmune (rheumatoid arthritis, multiple sclerosis). Dr. Fishs strategy is to identify and correct any host defect, to eliminate disease, focusing on the host immune response, not the disease.  In particular, Dr. Fishs research focuses on sex-related biomarkers, investigating how distinct immune environments in males and females can underlie differences in susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases.  Dr. Fishs strategy of focusing on the host response to disease, rather than focusing on the disease, will lead to the development of novel therapeutics that will havewidespread clinical application. Specifically, the creation of small molecule drugs targeted to optimize immune responses.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Medical Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Aaron Fensters research spans two broad research programs: Vascular Imagingand Image Guidance in Oncology. He is committed to expediting the discovery, development and translation of advanced technological innovations that will transform the manner in which disease is diagnosed and treated. Specifically, his innovations include the development of 3D ultrasound imaging, which is used for prostate cancer diagnosis, minimally invasive therapy, and image guided biopsy; 3D ultrasound guided breast biopsy, which is used to increase the accuracy of guiding the biopsy needle to the suspicious target; and 3D carotid ultrasound imaging, which is used to identify and monitor vulnerable carotid plaque that may lead to stroke.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Bionanotechnology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Nanotechnology has the potential to touch almost every aspect of our lives from military applications to cosmetics. Bionanotechnology, specifically, is going to enable us to develop novel medical treatments, diagnostic methods and preventative approaches to health and wellness. The research program of the Chair will focus on the development of intelligent delivery systems and biomolecular devices. These delivery systems and devices will provide effective, non-invasive and targeted technologies for administering macromolecular therapeutic agents, such as proteins, DNA and vaccines, into the body. These technologies will be applied in dermatology, immunology, and neurosciences.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Ultrasound Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The overall goal of Dr. Fosters research program is to develop microimaging systems that allow scientists to study disease models in the living mouse.  Attaining this objective will improve our understanding of developmental biology, speed the development of new drugs and therapies, and provide unique tools for image guided bioresearch. Knowledge gained via preclinical applications of the new technology will ensure more effective and rapid translation of leading-edge therapeutics to human clinical trials. His research, which aligns well with the Strategic Research Plan of the University of Toronto, has a direct and far-reaching impact on the quality and availability of health care globally.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en neurobiologie des maladies mentales
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: La schizophrénie est une maladie grave du cerveau, qui atteint 1% de la population, indépendamment du contexte social et culturel. Aujourd'hui, on ne sait pas guérir cette maladie, on ne sait soigner que certains de ses symptômes avec les médicaments antipsychotiques. Au cur de la schizophrénie, et d'autres maladies psychiatriques, la dopamine est un neurotransmetteur  essentiel, mais son rôle exact n'est pas bien identifié. Notre projet de recherche, utilisant des techniques moléculaires et comportementales, veut tenter de mieux comprendre le rôle et les mécanismes intimes qui contrôlent ces processus de la transmission dopaminergique, pour développer des approches thérapeutiques originales.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Developmental Neurogenetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Developmental disorders of the brain, which have a large toll on the individual, family and society, can have a clear genetic basis (e.g., some forms of mental retardation) or a more complex cause arising from gene-environment interactions (e.g., autism and attention deficit disorder). As Tier 1 CRC in Developmental Neurogenetics, Dr Daniel Goldowitz studies both single gene and more complex developmental disorders using the integrated power of genomics, informatics, and the mouse as an experimental model system to drive discovery about normal and abnormal brain development and to inform new therapeutic interventions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Microbiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Bob Hancock is studying an important antibiotic resistant hospital pathogen, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, deciphering especially mechanisms of virulence, antibiotic uptake and antibiotic resistance. This information has assisted in the design of two separate broad strategies for treating infections. The first involves the rational and semi-random design and production of short cationic peptides with broad spectrum antibiotic activity, subsequently deciphering the mechanism of action and efficacy in model infections. The second, based on an understanding of the activities of cationic host defence peptides, represents an entirely novel approach to anti-infective therapy through the selective boosting of human innate immunity while suppressing potentially harmful inflammation.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Maternal and Fetal Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The Chairs research is focused on understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie low birth weight or fetal growth restriction (FGR). Growth restricted fetuses have higher perinatal mortality and morbidity, and adverse long-term outcomes. Preeclampsia (PE) may cause FGR, and placenta is the site of disease. Self-renewal and differentiation of placental stem cells are studied in relation to placental development. He is utilizing molecular, biochemical, genomic and proteomic tools on animal models and clinical materials from human subjects, to improve our understanding of FGR, its causes and the mechanisms of its long-term outcomes, and develop clinically relevant diagnostic tools.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Human Genetics and Molecular Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: This Canada Research Chair is retaining an individual who has made landmark discoveries in genetics and its application to medicine.  These discoveries have tremdendous significance for neurodegenerative diseases such as Huntington disease, lipid disorders leading to coronary artery disease and diabetes, and genetic determinants of responsiveness to drugs.  This research program is geared towards making additional discoveries which will have direct impact on new approaches to therapy for many disorders affecting million of people worldwide.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Human Genetics and Phenomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Robert Hegele is one of Canadas leading clinician scientists making fundamental contributions to understand the genetic basis of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.  He is internationally recognized for identifying the causative genes for 10 diseases, including pioneering work in patients with inherited diabetes.  His approach of studying rare subtypes of common diseases has revolutionized our understanding of the molecular basis of insulin resistance. The discoveries have been implemented worldwide as routine diagnostic tests and have led to improvements in patient care and outcomes.  He has published over 350 scientific articles and has received numerous national and international scientific awards and distinctions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Imaging Technologies in Human Diseases and Preclinical Model Cluster
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Now that both the human and mouse genome sequences have been completed, there is a real opportunity to understand the genetic bases of human diseases by working on mouse models. If we are going to study in detail human-like diseases in the mouse, we need to have access to the same kinds of technologies that are used to look for disease in the human population. It is very hard to imagine doing modern medicine without modern medical imaging. It is necessary to have the same kinds of imaging techniques adapted to the mouse. Dr. Henkelman has established the Mouse Imaging Centre (MICe) in Toronto to develop and use three-dimensional imaging technologies for characterizing changes in genetically-modified mice. This centre is a leader in the world and over the next seven years will show that imaging is absolutely essential for understanding human diseases from the perspective of mouse genetics.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Sleep and Respiratory Neurobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Sleep disorders are a major public health burden. Obstructive sleep apnea affects ~4% of adults and is caused by closure of the air passage in the throat due to sleep-related relaxation of those muscles (e.g., tongue) whose activity normally keeps this airway open. This project will determine the brain nerve cells and chemicals involved in control of these important breathing muscles and develop pharmacological treatments (not yet available) for sleep apnea. The research is important because of the adverse clinical, societal and economic costs of this common disorder, e.g. increased strokes, heart attacks, and debilitating daytime sleepiness causing traffic and work accidents.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuroethics
Keywords-MotsClés: Social medicine, NA
Abstract-Résumé: This application summarizes the vision for a new Canada Research Chair and the creation of National Core for Integrated Neuroethics in Canada (NCINC) located at UBC. The candidate and core will be dedicated to the ethical, legal and social implications (ELSI) of frontier neuroscience, broadly defined as neuroethics, and will bring leadership, innovation and sustainability to ELSI in both basic and translational neuroscience research and practice. The program will advance current priorities in neuroethics, be informed by and responsive to researchers, providers, patients and other stakeholders, and continuously update priorities in synch with other neuroethics programs on  global scale.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Nutrition, Metabolism and Vascular biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Nutrition and food hygiene, Health
Abstract-Résumé: CRC funding has allowed us to take a lead internationally in research on diets combining cholesterol-lowering food components in a single diet in order to maximize serum cholesterol reduction and reduce other heart disease risk factors. We have termed this approach a dietary portfolio and demonstrated that under metabolically controlled conditions the cholesterol lowering effect may be drug-like with 30% reductions in LDL-cholesterol.  Due to the pilot studies which were made possible by CRC funding, we are now funded for future studies by CIHR to improve this dietary approach further and by an additional CIHR grant to carry out a multicenter trial across Canada to determine the effectiveness of this approach in clinical practice. This study will be the first multicenter dietary trial in Canada and one of very few such dietary trials internationally aimed at cholesterol reduction.  We believe that sustained CRC funding will allow us to continue to explore new areas of importance related to heart disease and diabetes and maintain our leadership role.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur les maladies infectieuses et parasitaires
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: My laboratory is working on two major themes: AIDS and Cancer. A-   AIDS: We established a mouse model of AIDS by expressing the HIV-1 genes in transgenic (Tg) mice. We are using this unique model to study and rescue immune defects and to investigate the lung and kidney diseases induced by HIV-1. B-   CANCER: We recently discovered that Notch1 is involved in mammary cancer in mice. Epidemilogical studies also showed its involvement in human breast cancer. Our studies will focus on how Notch1 transforms a normal cell into a cancer one, with special emphasis on the mammary stem cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Proteomics, Bioinformatics and Functional Genomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Protein function derives from three-dimensional structure and how structure changes with time. Although very detailed static pictures of protein molecules have been produced, macromolecular function is, in many cases, intimately coupled to flexibility and knowledge of molecular motions is thus critical. The goal of this research is to develop new Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy based techniques for relating molecular dynamics to function. The methodology will be applied to the study of a number of important biological molecules, including the proteasome, the central molecular machine that regulates a large number of critical biological processes. The importance of this system is underscored by the fact that it is a target for anti-cancer and anti-inflammatory drugs. This research will provide a much clearer picture of how this essential molecular machine functions. In addition, protein folding, binding and catalysis will be probed in a number of systems to elucidate the general mechanisms of functional dynamic processes.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Leukocyte Recruitment in Inflammatory Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Insufficient or over-exuberant response by the immune system to infections accounts for the majority of world-wide suffering and death.  One example is sepsis, a systemic infection killing 500,000 North American people (young and old) per year, many of them otherwise healthy.  At the crux of this issue are white cells, which seem to be agitated to release many of their killing molecules but instead of targeting bacteria, they kill our own tissues.  We will continue to examine how white cells get to sites of infection and how they kill bacteria versus our own tissue in the laboratory setting, as well as in the clinical Intensive Care Unit setting.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair on "Pain, Sleep & Trauma"
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Our research program, for the next 7 years, is directed/focused toward the understanding of the relationship between pain (11-29% of population) and sleep disorders such as sleep bruxism (tooth grinding; 8% of population), sleep apnea (cessation of breathing; 2-4 % of population) and periodic limb movement during sleep (8-12% of population).  We are testing new ways to prevent consequences of pain on sleep and subsequent daytime sleepiness.  We are also developing original studies to: 1- understand placebo mechanism in relation of sleep; 2- identify genetic predisposition for chronic pain and poor sleep in patients victim of minor brain injuries.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular and Cellular Biology of Cystic Fibrosis and Other Conformational Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Plasma membrane proteins play a critical role in the normal physiology of individual cells and their interactions in the human organism. Perturbations of the structure, function and/or localization of membrane proteins by genetic mutations cause severe, so-called conformational diseases. Dr. Lukacss research aims at elucidating the molecular and cellular basis of these genetic diseases, with a particular focus on cystic fibrosis. This will be accomplished by testing a novel conceptual framework of membrane trafficking pathway of structurally impaired surface proteins in cystic fibrosis and other conformational diseases. Innovative biochemical, biophysical and morphological approaches are required to demonstrate how impaired conformation represents a critical signal for intracellular mislocalization and degradation. The results will promote the understanding the pathogenesis of genetic diseases and design targeted screening assays for drug development to alleviate their symptoms.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CRC in Molecular Cardiovascular Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Calcium is required for heart muscle to contract, and must be removed to allow relaxation. These changes in calcium are normally carefully coordinated to allow fluctuations in the speed and extent of contraction in response to changing demands. Unfortunately, this coordination can go awry, which results in serious cardiovascular disease. Work in the Lytton laboratory will investigate mechanisms that regulate the sodium/calcium-exchanger, a cell surface transporter whose function is critical in the control of calcium cycling. This information will provide a fundamental understanding of the coordinated control of calcium, with the potential to solve clinically important problems of calcium dysfunction.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Immunology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: I study two sets of proteins made by the immune system, antibodies and cytokines. Antibodies specifically recognize viruses or bacteria. My work has shown that we inherit genes that enable us to generate antibodies that target vulnerable spots on common microbes. Cytokines coordinate our defences by triggering biochemical signals that usually protect the body from microbes, but may damage it, leading to common diseases like arthritis, asthma and diabetes. I have discovered novel components of these signals. My findings may lead to new agents for the prevention or treatment of infectious diseases, and the treatment of cancer and arthritis.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Gastrointestinal Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Although the cause of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is not yet known, currentevidence indicates that, in a genetically predisposed host, healthy bacteria normally present in the intestine are altered causing injury. We have provided evidence regarding the anti-inflammatory effects of specific bacteria (referred to as probiotics) using complementary approaches with cells grown in culture and animal models of IBD. The purpose of this research is to improve current understanding of mechanisms underlying the effects of probiotics in gut injury. The proposed research will provide new findings that can be employed to develop novel strategies for the management of IBD.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Hormones, Brain and Cognition
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Proposed studies, focused on further elucidating effects of specific sex hormones on aspects of cognition, could ultimately lead to the development of intervention strategies to prevent cognitive aging in both women and men. Novel investigations of the optimal timing of hormone treatment in menopausal women, of the role of androgens in cognition in women, of the influence of hormones on mood and cognitive disturbances during pregnancy and postpartum, and of effects of estrogen on cognitive functioning in older men will further our understanding of the possible impact of decreasing levels of sex hormone production in older individuals on cognitive aging.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Brain Science
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Information is coded in the brain as electrical impulses which travel along nerve fibers to their terminals and trigger neurotransmitter release, activating or inhibiting the target cell.  The impulse admits calcium ions through calcium channel membrane pores.  These ions trigger the fusion of neurotransmitter-filled secretory vesicles with the membrane, discharging their contents.  We have demonstrated that the calcium channel is a component of the transmitter release apparatus.  Our objective is to analyze the structure and function of this apparatus and to test for defects that may contribute to severe psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in CNS Disorders
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: Parkinsons disease (PD) is estimated to affect 100,000 Canadians at a cost of at least $2.5 billion annually. Dr. Stoessl has assembled a team of clinical and basic scientists who will use a combination of neuroimaging, genetic and epidemiological approaches to address 3 overarching questions:1. What causes Parkinsons?2. What are the underlying mechanisms that contribute to complications of advanced disease and long-term treatment, including depression and cognitive impairment?3. How can we use PD as a model to better understand the role of dopamine and other monoaminergic systems in the brain, including placebo effects, reward and pathological gambling?

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Axo-glial Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord play the critical role of transmitting information to and from the nervous system.  Many devastating neurological disorders such as stroke, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injury and brain trauma cause major disability because of damage to these delicate fibers.  This research project will use the most advanced microscopy and imaging technology to study how nerve fibers and their critically important insulating sheaths (myelin) are damaged and which biochemical pathways are most responsible.  This information will guide the development of drugs that can be rapidly brought to the clinic for testing in humans.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Behavioural Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: My research addresses the psychological factors that influence how people respond to pain.  Candid observation reveals that some individuals seem to cope adequately with painful medical conditions while others seem unable to cope.  Similarly, some individuals who undergo major medical procedures seem to recover without complication while others follow a path of complicated recovery characterized by ongoing pain, disability and distress.  My research attempts to understand the basis of these differences.  Our research to date has shown that certain individuals seem to become particularly alarmed about their pain symptoms, they might focus more on their pain, and the strategies they attempt to use to cope with their pain are not effective.  These individuals appear to be a risk for problematic outcomes following injury, ilnness or medical intervention.  We hope that as we learn more about psychological influences on pain and recovery, we might be in a better position to develop more effective interventions to assist individuals who are at risk for problematic health outcomes.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chair in Inflammation Responses and Traumatic Injury
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer has now surpassed cardiovascular disease as the primary cause of death in Canada. Conventional therapies are unsatisfactory due to inherent toxicity or limited specificity, and surgery is not a comprehensive cure. Cancer is in fact a collection of heterogeneous diseases driven by a myriad of genetic mutations that allow tumour cells to divide in an uncontrolled manner, resist cell death, avoid differentiation, and metastasize to distant organs. We hope to design novel drugs that can precisely target metabolic adaptation in tumour cells, enabling us to specifically treat the cancer while sparing the normal tissue.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Vision and Macular Degeneration
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Inherited retinal degenerative diseases including retinitis pigmentosa and macular degeneration are a leading cause of blindness in Canada and the rest of the world.  They are characterized by progressive photoreceptor cell death resulting in partial or complete loss in vision. Currently there are no effective treatments for this set of diseases and as such they represent a serious health problem and a significant social and financial burden to both individuals and society. The CRCs research program is directed toward 1) identifying and characterizing novel proteins that play key roles in the structure, function and survival of photoreceptor cells; 2) evaluating mechanisms underlying retinal degenerative diseases including macular degeneration; and 3) designing and developing gene and drug based therapies that can slow or eliminate loss of vision due to inherited retinal degenerative diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Hematopoiesis and Immune Cell Differentiation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Blood stem cells that reside in the bone marrow have a life-long ability for self-renewal. During a differentiation process, called hematopoiesis, they give rise to effector cells, which mediate the bodys immune defense. This maturation process is controlled by transcription factors, which are regulators of gene activity. A number of diseases, in particular leukemia and lymphoma, can be caused by defects in this regulatory mechanism. My research program aims to understand how hematopoietic transcription factors work at the molecular level to provide the basis for new therapeutic strategies helping to fight infectious disease, immune disorders and blood cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: The Chair was instrumental in the development and implementation of new technologies for neuroscience research at Queen's University.  He developed a new facility to combine animal behavioural neurophysiology, human behavioural neuroscience, and functional brain imaging.  The chair uses the new infrastructure for new research that includes: 1) detailed neurophysiological investigation of eye movement control circuits in the brain; 2) analysis of eye movement abnormalities in a variety of neurological and psychiatric patients; 3) combining eye movement recording and brain imaging to investigate functional abnormalities in patients. These studies will lead to the development of new functional tools for clinical assessment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de Recherche du Canada de niveau 1 en Immuno-Rétrovirologie Humaine
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Lobjectif central du présent programme de recherche demeure létude des facteurs viraux et cellulaires pouvant affecter la réplication du VIH-1. Le titulaire de chaire poursuivra lanalyse du processus dincorporation de protéines de la cellule hôte dans le virion. Il propose aussi détudier les interactions entre le VIH-1 et les cellules dendritiques, de définir le parcours du virus dans les trophoblastes polarisés et de décortiquer les conséquences pathophysiologiques dune infection avec le VIH-1 et le parasite protozoaire Leishmania. Une meilleure compréhension des acteurs impliqués dans la pathogenèse de linfection par le VIH-1 est essentielle pour le développement de thérapies plus efficaces.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Stem Cells and Regeneration
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The Nagy laboratory brings together a unique world-class expertise in areas essential for breaking new horizons for stem cell research. Built on long experience, Dr. Nagy researches embryonic stem cells for both the creation of disease models and the development of future therapies.  Using sophisticated genome modification techniques, his research applies stem cell-based approaches to innovative new applications such as cutting-edge cancer research.  The potential benefits of using these new techniques is enormous, and as these new methods are refined, they will be key to the development of safer and more effective treatments in the fight against cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Signal Transduction and Human Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Neels research involves the protein Shp2 and other related molecules.  Shp2 is mutated in about half of patients with Noonan Syndrome, the most common single gene cause of congenital heart disease, which is also associated with a rare leukemia. Non-inherited mutations in Shp2 contribute to several types of childhood and adult leukemia, and rarely, to solid tumours.  By creating and analyzing animal models in which normal or mutant Shp2 is turned on or turned off at specific times or in specific tissues, he is defining the mechanisms of these diseases and providing the groundwork for more effective treatments.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Urologic Pain and Inflammation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic pelvic pain conditions afflict up to 10% of men and women, while approximately 50% of men will suffer from benign prostatic hyperplasia.  Dr. Nickel plans to identify biomarkers of disease and disease progression, continue his investigation into the relevance of inflammation in the pathogenesis of these conditions, evaluate novel therapies by designing and implementing pilot and then phase III randomized placebo controlled trials, expand his ongoing biopsychosocial and cognitive behavioral work, and further explore the important sexual functioning issues associated with these conditions.  The general health of our population will improve by providing a scientific evidence-based approach to management of these important medical conditions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cognitive Dimensions of Clinical Expertise
Keywords-MotsClés: Education, training, recurrent education and retraining, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research addresses a broad spectrum of issues in professional education from fundamental research on the cognitive psychology of clinical diagnostic reasoning to applied research examining the potential of simulation for learning. The basic research continues to explore the role of non-analytic reasoning (pattern recognition) in medical diagnosis, and extends the understanding of how various kinds of knowledge are coordinated. Proposed research will extend the study of expertise to elite physicians, and  will examine aspects of learning, particularly transfer  using prior knowledge to solve novel problems using methods of cognitive psychology.  Finally, this research is applied to the study of how skills acquired in high and low fidelity simulations transfer to real clinical settings.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Vascular Smooth Muscle Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Abnormalities of smooth muscle function contribute to numerous diseases, e.g. hypertension, coronary and cerebral vasospasm. Many important questions concerning the mechanisms controlling smooth muscle contraction remain to be answered. My work will shed important new light on the molecular mechanisms of regulation of smooth muscle contraction, which are likely to be defective in pathophysiological conditions, and will lead to the identification of novel drug targets. It is also relevant to understanding of smooth muscle cell migration during the development of atherosclerosis and non-muscle motile processes such as transcellular invasion of tumour cells and migration of cells of the immune system.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Prion Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Agriculture
Abstract-Résumé: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy has had devastating effects in Canada.  BSE is a prion disease, a class of neurodegenerative disorders with infectious, genetic and sporadic manifestations. We believe that sporadic manifestation is the most important and troubling variety of prion disease, as it is common, can emerge in clean livestock populations, can be associated with novel prion strains that can spread to new species, and because Alzheimers and Parkinsons Disease are also characterized by sporadic manifestation.  Sporadic Disease represents a new frontier in neurodegenerative disease research and we advocate a three-pronged strategy to demystify this troublesome, mysterious entity.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in The Early Determinants of  Adult Chronic Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic diseases including cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, and respiratory diseases, are the leading causes of death, disability, and illness in Canada. The aim of the Canada Research Chair in the Early Determinants of Adult Chronic Disease is to increase understanding of the early socio-demographic, psychosocial, behavioural and environmental determinants of adult chronic disease, and to assure incorporation of this new knowledge into public health programming and clinical practice. The research program proposed, which emphasizes the need for interdiscipinary research that is well grounded in public health, encompasses studies ranging from inquiry into the genetic origins of risk to evaluation of policies to prevent or reduce risk in youth.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Metalloproteinase Proteomics and Systems Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Proteases function as molecular switches in signalling circuits on the cell surface and in the extracellular milieu. In light of the many proteases that are encoded by the genome, and the even larger number of bioactive substrates, it is crucial to identify which proteases cleave a particular substrate and which substrates individual proteases cleave. We have developed innovative proteomic strategies to quantitate all components of proteolytic pathways: the proteases, inhibitors and substratesa field we term degradomics. Elucidating these degradomes will help us to understand the function of proteases in development and disease and to validate proteases as drug targets.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Biochemical Pharmacology & Therapeutics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The goal of this research is to elucidate the cellular and molecular mechanisms responsible for the initiation and maintenance of steroid firmation in the adrenal, gonads and brain, in health and disease. This includes understanding the regulation of steroid biosynthesis, intracellular compartmentalization and homeostasis by hormones, chemicals, drugs, and environmental factors. Our goal is to understand the pathophysiology of steroidogenesis and develop tools for the treatment of diseases due to elevated or low steroid levels or alter subcellular steroid compartmentalization to block disease acquisition/progression.  This research has applications in reproduction and development, stress-related disorders, aging and brain-related dysfunction and cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CRC in Antibiotic Chemical Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: We propose to continue our efforts to understand the molecular basis of resistance to antibiotics and apply this knowledge in the identification of leads for new drugs.  Our strategy is to use Chemical Biology approaches (research methods at the interface of chemistry, microbiology, genomics, and biochemistry) to discover the fundamental aspects of antibiotics and associated resistance.  By using a combination of genome scale and one at a time investigations, we will uncover essential characteristics of how antibiotics work and how resistance emerges that will inform our efforts to find the new antibiotics that are required to combat infectious disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cancer Genomics and Proteomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer occurs when several mutations to the human genome accumulate within a single cell.  These mutations unleash normal growth regulatory mechanisms and allow the cell to proliferate uncontrolled.  A common mutational target amongst the majority of human cancers results in the deregulation of the c-myc oncogene.  Myc is a master-regulator that binds to DNA to control the expression of many downstream genes.  We aim to better understand how Myc can play such a profound role in such a wide-spectrum of cancers.  With this knowledge our goal is to develop new anti-cancer therapeutics that target Myc function and destroy the tumour.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Fetal, Neonatal and Maternal Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Despite modern management, lung immaturity remains a leading cause of early mortality and long-term disability.  We are investigating normal lung development and how clinical interventions such as ventilation may negatively affect on this process.  The proposed research will provide new findings that can be employed to develop new strategies for the clinical management of premature infants.  Beyond childhood lung disease, our investigations could also translate to new approaches for improving lung healing and to regenerate new lung tissue for patients with end-stage lung disease.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CRC Tier 1 Childhood Disability Research, Dissemination and Mentoring
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Rosenbaums research addresses issues concerning childhood disability: how to describe and measure it; what services work; how to support families; how to inform practitioners, learners and policy people. Finding new evidence and translating research into practice and policy is Dr. Rosenbaums mission in childhood disability, a field still in its academic infancy.  Through McMaster Universitys CanChild Centre, he is collaborating with like-minded colleagues across the broad spectrum of health, social science and policy with the goal of improving the life quality of children and youth with developmental disabilities and their families in Canada and around the world.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair on the Spinal Cord
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: This chair is devoted to the study of spinal cord mechanisms involved in the recovery of locomotion after spinal cord injury. Major achievements include the identification of adaptive mechanisms within the spinal cord itself as well as the localization of crucial spinal segments for the generation of spinal locomotion in cats. Furthermore, classical electrophysiological and behavioural approaches have been complemented by imaging studies including Magnetic Resonance Imaging and cineradiography. The Chair was instrumental in obtaining a team (15 researchers) grant from the CIHR to study mechanisms of locomotor recovery in animal models and patients with spinal cord injury.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Chronic Disease Management
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Evidence is accumulating that persons with schizophrenia suffer from premature mortality losing over 25 years of life, as compared to the general population.  Cardiovascular disease (CVD) accounts for most of the excess mortality and adverse metabolic effects of antipsychotic medications partially account for the increased CVD and diabetes risk in schizophrenia.  The research proposed will address reducing the morbidity and mortality from CVD in schizophrenia by developing interventions to lower CVD risk factors such as obesity, high cholesterol, and glucose intolerance, in patients with established disease, and to prevent their development in individuals at the beginning of the illness.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Understanding the functions of genes that regulate the behavior of stem cells during muscle regeneration is the major focus of the Rudnicki laboratory. His team discovered that the factor Pax7 is an essential genetic switch required for muscle stem cell function, and that Wnt signaling regulates the repair process. In the next phase of his research, he is defining the regulatory genetic networks that regulate the growth and differentiation of stem cells. Dr. Rudnicki is the Scientific Director of the Stem Cell Network, the founding Director of the International Regulome Consortium, and a founding scientist in StemPath, Incorporated.

TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en oncogénétique
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Lutilisation de lhistoire familiale de cancer du sein facilite grandement lidentification des personnes à risque accru de cancer pouvant bénéficier des stratégies de prévention et de diagnostic précoce. Le programme interdisciplinaire de la CRC en oncogénétique a pour but didentifier les facteurs de risque génétiques et dévaluer leur impact afin daméliorer les méthodes de prédiction du risque de cancer du sein. Des études visent aussi à mieux comprendre les barrières et les mécanismes facilitant la communication du risque familial afin daccélérer le développement doutils favorisant lapplication des connaissances en clinique.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Visual-Motor Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: The purpose of the brain is to generate behaviour, and in humans this relies heavily on vision.  Therefore, much of the human brain is involved in transforming visual inputs from the eyes into behavioral commands.  By corollary, most diseases, injuries, and disorders of the human brain affect these transformations in debilitating ways.  Our invesitgations use computational models, behavioral testing in patients and healthy people,  brain imaging in humans, and direct neural recordings in animals to understand how the brain transforms vision into action, and why these transformations go awry in some patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Resistance and Susceptibility to Infections
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Plummer is a prominent Canadian physician scientist and a global leader in infectious disease research and training.  His work on understanding the HIV epidemic in Africa has led to interventions that prevent tens of thousands of HIV infections annually around the world.  The focus of his current work in understanding natural immunity to HIV  what protects some individuals from infection despite extensive exposure and what is different about such individuals that permits them to develop protective responses.  By understanding natural immunity, Dr. Plummer hopes to develop new approaches to HIV vaccines and microbicides.

TitreApplicationTitle: Immunological mechanisms of therapeutic peptide vaccines in allergic asthma
Keywords-MotsClés: ALLERGY; ASTHMA; IL-10; IMMUNOTHERAPY; T CELLS; THERAPEUTIC VACCINES
Abstract-Résumé: Allergic diseases result from an over-reaction of the immune system to normally harmless environmental proteins from house dust, grass pollens and pets. These proteins are called "allergens". The exagerated immune response is controlled by a particular kind of white blood cell called a T cell. T cells respond to small fragments of the allergen protein called "peptides".The applicant has been developing "peptide vaccines" which target the over-active T cells and switch them off. At the moment it is unclear how the peptide vaccines switch of the T cell response.Understanding this process will improve the design and delivery of the vaccines. The applicant has developed a model of allergic asthma to study how the vaccine peptides work. The model, which is established in an inbred strain of mice, is designed to closely mimic the human response to the vaccine peptides. The applicant has already shown that the peptides can switch off the T cell response that cause asthma in these mice by a mechanism that seems to involve creating a new population of "regulatory T cells" which suppress inflammation and disease. In the current application, a series of experiments are designed to understand how the peptide vaccines work and to study how the regulatory T cells are induced and how they block the allergic immune response. The research will have important implications for health as it will improve the design of the vaccines for human use and will help the scientific/medical community to understand how it is possible to re-balance an over-reacting immune system. This information will be of use in the fight against many chronic diseases in addition to allergies, such as autoimmune diseases like diabetes, multiple sclerosis and rheumatoid .

Abstract-Résumé: Coronary artery disease, leading to chest pain and heart attacks, is the leading cause of death in the developed world. The damaged heart muscle is replaced with scar tissue resulting in diminished ability to pump blood and culminating in heart failure in a third of all patients, even with all the treatments provided by modern medicine. Based on positive results in small animals, there is hope that cell-based therapies using transplants of progenitor cells, such as bone marrow derived in stem cells, will provide a means to reduce the incidence of heart failure by repairing the damaged heart tissue.  In research towards this goal, methods for following the location and studying the activity of these transplanted cells are of utmost importance. Magnetic resonance imaging has shown a great deal of promise for tracking the location of stem cells non-invasively. In the proposed research plan, a novel method for imaging stems cells such that the signal is bright (as opposed to dark with conventional methods) is developed towards application in the clinic.  In a second project component, MRI of hyperpolarized carbon-13, which enables the direct imaging of metabolism using an MRI machine, is studied.  This new method is proposed for studying cellular metabolism in and around damaged heart muscle to better plan and evaluate regenerative therapy.

Abstract-Résumé: Tobacco use remains a significant public health issue in Canada.  Gender differences that influence tobacco use are reflected in the different smoking rates and practices among women and men.  These differences demand targeted interventions aimed at tobacco reduction. However, few interventions take into account the empirical evidence concerning the intertwined nature of gender and tobacco.  This research program will broaden methodological approaches; build research capacity in an interdisciplinary team; and develop and mobilize an evidence base related to tobacco by taking into consideration gender to improve policy and tailor tobacco reduction interventions for women and men, and girls and boys.

Abstract-Résumé: This Emerging Team will improve the health of girls and women by enhancing the role of disease prevention and health promotion within health services. The team will examine existing practices of health promotion to determine their usefulness for girls and women. At the same time, we will conduct health promotion projects ourselves, both in the community and in a hospital, and develop suggestions from those practical experiences about the best ways to provide health promotion programs for girls and women. The projects will be about promoting heart health for girls and women; improving maternal health among Aboriginal girls and women; and improving counseling by health care and social services providers on alcohol and other substance use among pregnant women and mothers. Finally, we will examine how information about health promotion effectiveness is currently compiled and suggest better ways to develop and report that information. The findings from this work will improve program design, program evaluation, and program effectiveness, as well as policy intended to support the health of girls and women. We will also be better able to integrate health promotion within the hospital sector and link to hospital programs with community initiatives.

Abstract-Résumé: Although it is common knowledge that boys and girls, men and women are biologically different and that their experiences bring them into contact differently with their physical and social environments throughout their lifespan, research in environment and health has been slow to translate this knowledge into methodologically sound studies that adequately consider sex and gender. The paucity of information in this area has vital implications for health, health services and preventive intervention strategies for children, adolescents, family members involved in paid and non-paid work, and the elderly. The overall objective of this proposal is to integrate gender/sex considerations into research in health and environment throughout the lifespan. To achieve this goal, we propose to set up a pan-Canadian interdisciplinary research tem, building on recognized Canadian expertise in environment and health and in quantitative and qualitative methods to take account of gender and sex. The emerging team will (i) develop and refine interdisciplinary quantitative and qualitative methods for integrating gender/sex considerations in Canadian and international research in environment (including workplace and health; (ii) establish strong collaborations with community-based and public health partners working in environment and health, in order to come to a richer understanding of the real-life mechanisms linking environmental health to sex and gender; (iii) train and mentor young researchers; (iv)initiate multi-centre, multi-disciplinary research demonstrating the scientific importance of integrating gender/sex considerations into research and intervention in health and environment. We propose a participatory structure with partners working in the field of environment and health and a 5-year progressive research and activities plan grounded in on-going research in environment and health across Canada.

Abstract-Résumé: The most dangerous complication faced by premature infants is related to lung immaturity and include respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). The major cause of RDS is surfactant deficiency, which causes alveolar collapse. The surge of surfactant synthesis is delayed in boys compared to girls, and this depends to the presence of androgens in male lungs. As consequences, extreme premature boys are more likely than girls to develop RDS, to survive with severe sequels, and/or to die. An important question is how the fetal sex influences clinicians and the parental decision to begin and to maintain or to stop medical support in cases of extreme premature infant? There is no guideline in neonatal pulmonary practices concerning the implication for a premature baby to be a boy or a girl. This depends on the fact that our understanding of the biological impacts of the fetal sex on lung development is partial. To approach this question, we propose: 1) to use advanced biomedical technologies to document molecularly the effect of biological sex on lung development; 2) to use the Quebec cohort of extreme premature infants to document the relationship between fetal sex and associated neonatal complications and long term neurodevelopment outcomes; 3) to question the impact of the fetal sex on counselling provided by clinicians; and, 4) to translate existing and new research findings into realizations for premature infants to improve health and well-being for these infants. To do so, we will profit from a WEB-based discussion forum. Using precise questions, experts from several related disciplines, including health-oriented social scientists, and representative from a parents' association of premature infants will evaluate how knowledge gained from research and transdisciplinary analysis can be integrated to formulate new evidence-based clinical guidelines, programs and, public policy. This program will promote rapid knowledge transfer and use for the profit of premature infants.

Abstract-Résumé: Mental health problems during pregnancy and the postpartum period pose a significant public health concern for several reasons. They affect up to 20% of childbearing women, and can persist for up to a year, and place women at high risk for future episodes of psychiatric illness. However, these disorders are often unrecognized and untreated. The research program to be undertaken under the auspices of the proposed Emerging Team in Perinatal Mental Health will integrate the investigation of sociocultural, psychological and biological factors related to psychiatric illness in pregnancy and postpartum. Specific questions to be addressed include 1) the role of oxytocin in postpartum depression; 2) the role of fatigue and sleep disorders in perinatal mental illness; 3) sociocultural variation in the prevalence, course, and sequelae of perinatal mental illness; 4) health care services needs among women with perinatal mental illness; 5) delusions in postpartum psychosis. This innovative research program will permit the development of novel approaches for the assessment and treatment of psychiatric disorders in childbearing women, and will also inform broader theoretical questions about psychiatric disorders such as depression and psychosis.

Abstract-Résumé: Each year, approximately 1000 Canadians sustain an acute traumatic spinal cord injury and join close to 40,000 paralyzed individuals across our nation who endure one of the most physically and psychologically devastating of injuries.  We have recently shown that two novel populations of stem cells we have identified, one of which derives from the skin, and one from the brain, can promote anatomical and/or functional recovery when transplanted into the injured spinal cord.  While these studies were performed with rodent cells, we have shown that similar stem cells are present in humans.  In this proposal we will ask whether the human cells also promote recovery from spinal cord injury and, if so, will pursue preclinical and ethics studies with the ultimate goal of, if warranted, providing the basis for a human clinical trial to treat this devastating and currently untreatable condition.

Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; BIOLOGICAL VALIDATION; DRUG DEVELOPMENT; NANOSEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES; TOURETTE SYNDROME; VARIANT SCREENING AND VALIDATION
Abstract-Résumé: We propose to create a research Team to develop strategies towards the identification and validation of genes causing brain diseases. This Team will combine expertises in genomics and bioinformatics to develop analytical methods to deal with the massive sequence data-sets that will soon be generated by nanosequencing techniques, such as the sequencing of whole genomes of individuals. The Team will focus on the screening of genomes of patients affected with Tourette syndrome. The role of the gene variants identified will first be genetically validated, then functionally tested in model systems. The multidisciplinary nature and scope of this project render its completion by isolated research groups virtually impossible; rather, it requires the creation of a unique collaborative Team with expertise in the various aspects of this research. Ultimately, our objective is to set up a Team of researchers specialized in the identification and validation of genetic variants causing or predisposing to brain disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of a Multidisciplinary Stem-Cell Program To Fight Congestive Heart Failure
Keywords-MotsClés: ADIPOSE-DERIVED STEM CELLS; CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE; MAGNETIC FIELD-ASSISTED CARDIAC RETENTION OF IMPLANTED CELLS; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY; SUPERPARAMAGNETIC NANOPARTICLES
Abstract-Résumé: Cell transplantation holds great promise for treatment of heart failure. However, the majority of implanted cells usually end up in organs, other than heart. As a result, most studies have only shown a mild to moderate improvement in heart conditions following cell transplantation. Taking advantage of the strong magnetic attraction of iron particles, we hypothesize that an appropriate magnet positioned over the left chest can significantly increase the retention of iron particle-labeled cells in the heart, which may in turn lead to significant improvement in efficacy of cell transplantation for heart failure. The first objective of the proposal is to test this hypothesis. Magnetic resonance (MR) imaging is currently considered the most suitable imaging modality for tracking of implanted cells. However, results obtained with commercial MR contrast agents are far from satisfactory. We are confident that significantly better MR contrast agents can be developed. We believe that cells labeled with our new MR contrast agents can be tracked for a significantly longer period than cells labeled with commercial contrast agents. The second objective of the proposal is to develop stronger MR contrast agents for tracking of implanted cells. The optimal cell type for treatment of heart failure still remains to be defined. The subcutaneous fat tissue contains a group of adult stem cells, so called Adipose-derived Stem Cells (ASCs) that offer promise as a therapeutic agent. Therefore, the third objective of this program is to determine whether ASCs are able to repair injured hearts and prevent heart failure. To achieve the above objectives, a multidisciplinary team has been developed and a number of studies have been designed. We believe that the results of this team proposal have potential to revolutionize cell therapy for cardiovascular diseases as well as for other diseases. Therefore, this proposal has a great significance for Canadian Healthcare.

Abstract-Résumé: The team aims to promote mobility in aging by optimizing gait and balance (G&B). Our objectives are to: 1) develop innovative, cost-effective approaches to improve G&B and prevent falls; 2) test the efficacy of these new approaches; 3) transfer the new technologies and knowledge to consumers, health-care providers and policy makers. An advisory board representing these research users will oversee all phases of the work. The work will advance new G&B assessment and training methods, sensory aids, mobility aids, footwear, garments and handrail systems, and will address the complex demands of moving about safely in daily life by: 1) simulating real-life loss-of-balance situations in the lab; 2) using  wireless systems and computer vision to study G&B in real-life settings. To build a capacity for ongoing clinical testing and translation of the new knowledge, we will set up a network of "G&B optimization" clinics. These clinics will serve as a new model for delivery of mobility-related health-care services.

Keywords-MotsClés: BEHAVIORAL ANALYSIS; CELL CULTURE; CELL TRANSPLANTATION; CORNEA; ELECTRORETINOGRAM; GENE EXPRESSION; HUMAN RETINAL STEM CELLS; LENTIVIRUS; MOUSE MODELS; NANOPARTICLES; RETINA; TRANSGENESIS
Abstract-Résumé: The goal of this project is to bridge the gap between basic science and the clinic; developing new therapies for the treatment of corneal and retinal disease.  To meet this challenge, we have amassed a team of investigators with expertise in eye stem cells (SC), developmental neurobiology, tissue engineering and ophthalmic surgery. To date, members of our group have made instrumental advances in the field of regenerative medicine in the eye; developing biomaterial-based corneas for transplantation in human patients and identifying retinal stem cells (RSC) in the adult eye. We will now address additional key pre-clinical issues as a preamble to instituting new therapies for eye repair. Specifically, our goals are to: 1) improve the efficacy of obtaining pure populations of SC-derived photoreceptor neurons; 2) optimize the transplant of new photoreceptors to the retina using novel delivery methodologies, and 3) develop improved corneal substitutes that are viral-resistant and can be exploited for drug and SC delivery to infected corneas. Short term (3 year) deliverables include identification of the optimal SC source for cell transplantation, development of methodologies for the safe and efficient expansion and generation of photoreceptors, development and pre-clinical testing of novel approaches for SC and drug delivery to the retina and cornea.  Longer term (5years and beyond) deliverables include the application of these methodologies for the derivation and expansion of autologous RSC transplants, pre-clinical testing of novel SC delivery approaches to the retina and clinical trials of scaffold/drug and SC combinations in the cornea.

Keywords-MotsClés: CLSA; MOBILITY AND AGING; MULTIDISCIPLINARY; OUTCOMES; TRAJECTORIES
Abstract-Résumé: The Canadian Longitudinal Study of Aging (CLSA) Mobility Initiative (CLSA-MI) is a comprehensive program of research that proposes to describe and evaluate all aspects of mobility in adults aged 45 to 85 years.  This Mobility Initiative will consider the physical, psychological and social factors that contribute to one's level of mobility over time. In this Mobility Initiative, the emerging team (ET) can explore the relationships between these factors and how they contribute to a person's mobility status, as well as how one's mobility status impacts important health outcomes and even diseases. The CLSA-MI is designed to capture changes or trajectories over time and uniquely capture all relevant aspects of changes that can lead to diminished mobility. Moreover, the ET will be composed of an extensive network of multidisciplinary researchers and stakeholders across disciplines and sectors.  This CLSA-MI will also allow for the development of researchers new to the study of mobility. Overall, the CLSA-MI will provide comprehensive and cross-cutting understanding of one's mobility within middle aged and older Canadians; it will also provide important understanding of the transitions of one's mobility status over time.

Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHMA; CYSTIC FIBROSIS; EMBRYOID BODY FORMATION; EMPHYSEMA; ES CULTURE; ESC DIFFERENTIATION; HUMAN-MOUSE XENOGRAFTS; LUNG REGENERATION/REPAIR; TRANSPLANTATION
Abstract-Résumé: Thousands of Canadians suffer from tissue and organ degeneration caused by congenital abnormalities, tissue injury, or autoimmunity. Lung diseases such as asthma, cystic fibrosis,  and chronic lung disease resulting from premature birth are a major health issue for children and adults resulting in reduced quality of life, and death. Although interventional strategies to  improve outcomes are being developed for these diseases based on improved techniques to define and follow the evolution of abnormalities, as well as to better understand the underlying  pathophysiologic processes, new treatments are needed.  The promise of cell replacement therapy has lead to an emerging field in "regenerative medicine" and with it tremendous opportunities for the development of new treatments for the repair of damaged tissues and organs through regeneration of  specific tissue to regain overall physiological function. A new paradigm of treatment focused on stem cell regeneration and repair would likely transform the treatment of diseases where  airway epithelium is underdeveloped or defective. However, the existence of endogenous stem cells in the adult lung is controversial and largely unproven. We believe, that human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), with their pluripotent potential to  differentiate into any tissue, represent the best option for the achievement of durable cell replacement treatment in patients. To this end, our team will work together towards the development of lung progenitors differentiated from hESCs that possess the ability to engraft and regenerate lung epithelial tissue. We believe this will offer a new source of human cells and method to treat patients suffering from chronic lung degenerative conditions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Nanomedicine in Organ Transplantation:  Polysaccharide Structures as Immunologic Tolerogens for Infant Heart Transplantation
Keywords-MotsClés: ABO BLOOD GROUP ANTIGENS; BLOOD GROUP BARRIER; HEART TRANSPLANTATION; NANOPARTICLES; STENTS; TOLEROGENS
Abstract-Résumé: In organ transplants, ABO blood type compatibility between donor and recipient is needed to avoid organ loss or patient death. Recent studies by Dr. West showed that ABO-mismatched heart transplants are possible in infants because their immune systems are immature. Dr. West's protocol has now been adopted around the world and has allowed more infants to be transplanted. After transplant, exposure to the ABO-mismatched heart does not provoke an immune response; rather, as the child matures, the immune system becomes unreactive or 'tolerant' of the blood type of the donor heart. Despite the success of ABO-mismatched transplants, donor hearts for infants needing transplants are still scarce. A longer immune 'grace period' would allow ABO-mismatched transplantation at an older age when more donors are available. This project will test the idea that exposing the young immune system to very tiny synthetic ABO substances will induce tolerance during development, in similar fashion to infant heart transplant patients, thus expanding the window when a mismatched transplant can be performed safely. We have formed a Team of highly qualified scientists in medicine and chemistry to answer this question. Our Team is an integrated group of senior researchers and promising young scientists with diverse expertise, each bringing independent strengths. Chemists and nanoscientists will design and produce ABO substances and attach them to implantable devices (stents or particles). These implants will be modified to make them optimal to modify the immune system and allow tracking; finally they will be tested in a piglet heart transplant model. This is an exciting and entirely novel multidisciplinary project with enormous clinical potential. The work of this new Team will also include the training of young scientists who will build capacity in medical research for the future, and important networking opportunities in areas of science and medicine that will build innovative bridges.

TitreApplicationTitle: Novel Gene Therapy Approaches for the Treatment of Retinal Degenerative Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: GENE THERAPY; IMAGING TECHNIQUES; KNOCKOUT MICE; MACULAR DEGENERATION; RETINAL DEGENERATIVE DISEASES; VIRAL VECTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Inherited retinal degenerative diseases including retinitis pigmentosa and macular degeneration are a major cause of blindness in Canada and the rest of the developed world. Currently, there are no cures or effective treatments for this set of diseases.  This research program will develop novel gene therapy procedures that have the potential to restore vision in animal models for selected inherited retinal degenerative diseases for which the gene defect is known.  Three key diseases, for which animal models are either available or will be produced as part of this proposal, and targeted in this study are: Stargardt macular degeneration, Leber Congenital Amaurosis, and X-linked Retinitis Pigmentosa.  To achieve this goal, a viral vector will be developed that can deliver large, normal genes to photoreceptors of mice that are deficient in vision due to a defective gene. The rescue of photoreceptor cells and restoration of vision following gene replacement will be monitored by a range of biochemical, molecular, cellular, immunological, electrophysiological and ophthalmic techniques, some of which will be further developed and improved as part of this program.  The safety and persistence of this gene therapy approach will also be investigated. Demonstration of the 'proof of concept' that a single injection of the viral-gene construct can result in the recovery of vision in these animal models will serve as a basis for its application in human clinical trials.
