TitreApplicationTitle: Changes in motor system connectivity after stroke.
Keywords-MotsClés: DTI; FMRI; FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY; MOTOR AREAS; MOTOR SYSTEM; PLASTICITY; REHABILITATION; STROKE; TMS
Abstract-Résumé: Whenever we make a movement, our limbs are responding to a precise command sent by neurons located in the motor areas of our brain. After a stroke, the pathways that normally communicate these motor commands can be damaged, resulting in movement difficulties. The goal of this proposal is to study how the brain reorganizes itself to compensate for such damage and how to enhance recovery. We hope that the information gained by this research will help us to develop effective neurorehabilitation strategies.   Ongoing advances in our understanding of recovery-related brain changes raise the prospect of directly influencing brain activity to promote desired patterns of brain reorganization. This proposal aims to develop such therapies by targeting the human motor areas, regions shown to be critically involved in recovery of movement after stroke. Using a range of brain imaging and stimulation techniques, we propose to study the anatomy, physiology and functional connectivity of motor circuits in the healthy brain, to test for changes in these circuits in patients suffering from a stroke, and to assess the long-term effects of modulating the spared motor areas. Our hypothesis is that modulating activity in the motor areas based on the residual functional motor network of patients that suffered from a stoke, particularly the secondary motor areas, will increase the beneficial effects of rehabilitation in patients.   In conclusion, a better understanding of how brain reorganization influences recovery will help us to develop novel therapies for patients suffering from stroke.

TitreApplicationTitle: The functional role of a H2AX promoter polymorphism associated with non-Hodgkin lymphoma
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER GENETICS; COMMON GENETIC VARIANT; DISEASE SUSCEPTIBILITY; FUNCTIONAL GENETICS; HISTONE H2AX; NON-HODGKIN LYMPHOMA
Abstract-Résumé: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) is a specific type of cancer in which an abnormal growth of cells of the immune system produces a tumour. The cells in these tumours often have a type of chromosome damage called a translocation, where two chromosomes are incorrectly joined together. These translocations may occur when genes that are responsible for repairing damaged DNA are not functioning properly. Although most of the DNA sequence is similar between individuals, there are a number of DNA sequence differences, known as genetic variants. Previous studies in my lab looked at genetic variation in six DNA repair genes in patients with NHL and control (unaffected) individuals. They found that a common DNA sequence variant at one of these genes, called H2AX, was much more frequent among the patients than the controls. Individuals who carry this gene variant have twice the risk of NHL as those who do not have it. Since this DNA sequence feature is very common in the population, it is predicted that 23% of NHL could be caused by this gene variant. The goal of this project is to determine why individuals with the H2AX gene variant have increased risk of NHL. The DNA sequence variant is found at the part of the gene that controls how H2AX is regulated and may affect how this gene is turned on and off. Since H2AX is a gene involved in repairing damaged DNA, if it is not regulated correctly, damaged DNA may not be properly repaired, leading to the translocations found in NHL tumours. Using molecular techniques and cell culture assays, I will look at how this DNA sequence variant affects regulation of the gene and influences the ability of the cell to repair and survive DNA damage. Understanding how and why this specific gene variant increases risk for NHL will lead to a better knowledge of how this cancer develops. This information will eventually be useful for identifying new drug targets and therapies for NHL, and may provide insight into the development of other cancers as well.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health Impacts of Highly Skilled Participation: Development and Application of a Sensorimotor Test Battery
Keywords-MotsClés: ATHLETES; MUSICIANS; PAIN; PREVALENCE; PROPRIOCEPTION; RISK; SENSORY DISCRIMINATION; SKILLED PARTICIPATION; SURVEY; TEMPERATURE SENSATION
Abstract-Résumé: The experience of illness is individual, and depends in part on contextual factors such as financial circumstances and a supportive work environment. Researchers do not yet fully understand how these factors influence health. The differences between groups of people whose occupations require highly skilled participation, including musicians and athletes, can help us understand how contextual factors affect the health of all people. At any time, about 40% of professional musicians have injuries related to playing an instrument, mostly affecting arms and backs. These injuries are poorly defined in research and large-scale data has not been collected in North America since 1986. For comparison, tennis players have about the same number of injuries but they experience different contexts. Professional athletes tend to have high salaries; most professional orchestra members make between $20,000 and $30,000/year. Athletes have access to sports injuries clinics and team doctors, while many professional musicians don't even have extended health insurance. An injury might mean a musician can't work, and the resulting personal financial hardship can translate to an additional tax burden for Canadians. There are over 47,000 professional union musicians in Canada, and many more non-union or amateur musicians who might be affected by these injuries. The cost to taxpayers for our public healthcare system to treat these injuries is substantial.  The aim of this study is to determine how healthy professional musicians and athletes differ from each other and from other people in terms of their performance on tests of movement and sensation. These results will be used to design a survey to be administered to a large group of professional musicians in Canada and the US to update and improve our understanding of what health problems musicians experience, and how many are affected. This will help in developing better services that recognize the individual nature of health and illness.

Abstract-Résumé: My postmenopausal health research program examines novel pathways to prevent chronic diseases in postmenopausal women, such as osteoporosis, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease and cancers, and investigates innovative modalities for early diagnosis of these diseases.  It also addresses gender and sex differences in health care utilization and outcomes, and explores determinants of women's perception of and preferences for various health states.  My overall goal is to improve the health and well-being of postmenopausal women through disease prevention, early diagnosis, better access to treatment, and by reducing social, cultural and gender barriers to well-being.  This can be achieved through a cutting-edge program of research that involves expertise from multiple disciplines.  This program also offers unparalleled opportunities for the training of future researchers in postmenopausal health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Estrogen in the Prefrontal Cortex:  Implications for Cognitive Functioning and Mood in Women
Keywords-MotsClés: AFFECT; ANTEPARTUM; COGNITIVE EVALUATION; COGNITIVE FUNCTIONING; CYCLE; DEPRESSION; FUNCTIONAL IMAGING; GENETIC ANALYSIS; IMMUNOASSAYS; MENOPAUSE; MENSTRUAL; MENTAL HEALTH; NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT; POSTPARTUM; PREFRONTAL CORTEX
Abstract-Résumé: In women, high levels of estrogen are secreted from the ovaries during the reproductive years. Concentrations are not constant, but vary over the menstrual cycle and with significant reproductive events such as pregnancy, childbirth, or menopause. Animal studies have shown that estrogen has a wide range of effects in different parts of the brain, where it can modify local neurochemistry. It is important, therefore, to discover how estrogen's trophic actions in the brain might help to maintain optimal cognitive and mental health in women. Dr. Hampson investigates the effects of estrogen in a brain region not usually studied in this context - the prefrontal cortex (PFC). In humans, the PFC participates in several important memory processes, including a distinct type of short-term memory ('working memory') and in memory retrieval. The PFC is also involved in the regulation of mood, and is a basis for several higher-order cognitive functions that are not memory-related, but which influence everyday activities, including decision-making, cognitive flexibility, and reflectiveness. An OWHC/ IGH Senior Investigator Salary Award will enable Dr. Hampson to devote increased time to her research on estrogen's effects in the PFC. The work involves cognitive assessment techniques derived from clinical and experimental studies of the PFC, combined with functional MRI, a brain imaging technique that allows researchers to visualize areas of activity in the brain during cognitive processing. Developing a greater understanding of estrogen's effects, and how they vary in pathological conditions, could have important implications for women's mental health and quality of life. Dr. Hampson's projects include investigations of mood disturbance and cognitive functioning during pregnancy and the postpartum, perimenopause, and in women with healthy or atypical menstrual cycles. Genetic polymorphisms that enhance or diminish these effects will also be studied.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessing the Origins and Impacts of Conspiracy Beliefs on HIV Prevention Behavior in the Western Cape, South Africa.
Keywords-MotsClés: ADHERENCE; COMMUNITY; COMPLIANCE; CONSPIRACY; DISTRUST; HEALTH; HIV/AIDS; IN-DEPTH INTERVIEWS; MULTIVARIATE ANALYSIS; NARRATIVES
Abstract-Résumé: South Africa has the highest absolute number of people infected with HIV/AIDS in the world.  Although testing and treatment centres are available throughout the country, testing rates remain low, and treatment uptake is inconsistent.  HIV testing is an essential precursor to treatment, and treatment with antiretroviral drugs has been shown to lower the viral load in an individual, thus making them less infectious.  Both testing and consistent treatment form part of a comprehensive HIV prevention campaign.  Although there are various reasons for low rates of participation in testing and treatment programmes, an understudied factor is the effect of conspiracy beliefs.  A recent study (Bogart et al 2008) showed that people who endorsed a genocidal conspiracy belief (e.g."HIV was created by Whites to kill Blacks") were less likely to have an HIV test.  Ethnographic research by Steinberg (2007) suggests that conspiracy belief is also an important impediment to seeking treatment with antiretroviral medication.  The political and historical origins of such beliefs are persuasive: generations of an Apartheid government that actively researched biological and chemical weapons that could be used against ANC insurgents, as well as recent 'AIDS denialism' by the former President Mbeki and his colleagues has lent credibility to the notion that HIV/AIDS is man-made, and that health programmes may not be benevolent.  By understanding this phenomenon in more detail, and establishing the effects of conspiracy belief on health seeking behavior, this research will better inform interventions that are attempting to promote HIV prevention.  This study also seeks to develop our understanding of the role of conspiracy theories' influence on responses to HIV/AIDS as an exemplar for understanding this phenomena in infectious diseases more generally.

Abstract-Résumé: The objective of the proposed research is to study the process of implementation of a program of addiction/mental health intervention into primary health care settings. The research sites include three health clinics in Montreal administered by the Centre de Sante et de Services Sociaux (CSSS) de la Montagne.   The program entitled "Treating Substance Dependence and Mental Illness: Tools for the Front Line Practitioner" was designed by the staff of the Addictions Unit at the McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) to facilitate the screening, assessment and treatment of clients with addictions and comorbid mental illness by front line practitioners. Using both qualitative and quantitative methods, the research will determine the conditions that favor the process of knowledge translation from specialty to front line services and will involve an examination of the systemic barriers to knowledge uptake. In addition, the effectiveness of the intervention program as administered in primary care sites will be determined using a pre-post design with monitoring of outcomes in terms of the changes in health care service delivery and outcomes for patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: L-arginine metabolism in inflammation and fibrosis in inflammatory bowel disease
Keywords-MotsClés: FIBROSIS; INFLAMMATION; INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE; L-ARGININE METABOLISM; MACROPHAGES
Abstract-Résumé: Canada has the highest rate of inflammatory bowel disease in the world with 1 in 200 Canadians suffering with IBD.  Disease is characterized by unchecked inflammation that leads to a cycle of tissue damage and healing.  The repeated damage and healing process also leads to fibrosis causing stricture formation in patients that frequently requires surgey.  I study a specific type of immune cell called a macrophage.  Macrophages are key players in the inflammatory process.  In fact, they are the largest producer of TNFalpha in the gut and an anti-TNFalpha antibody, Remicaid, has proven to be a very effective treatment for IBD.  Normally when macrophages are finished their job in inflammation, they convert to a healer cell that assists in the resolution of inflammation.  A key switch that happens in macrophages is dictated by how they use the amino acid L-arginine.  L-arginine can be metabolized by two pathways, one that leads to inflammation and one that promotes healing.  I am proposing to manipulate the metabolism of L-arginine in macrophages during IBD to stop the inflammatory process and to stop the fibrosis that can lead to stricture formation.  If we can force L-arginine metabolism down the correct pathway, we may be able to use it to stop the inflammatory process that is the root of IBD.  In addition, we may be able to manipulate this pathway to prevent fibrosis and stricture formation and avoid the need for surgical intervention to correct these serious complications in patients with IBD.

TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR Team in transdisciplinary studies in DWI onset, persistence, prevention and treatment.
Keywords-MotsClés: DRIVING WHILE IMPAIRED; INTEGRATIVE KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; SUBSTANCE ABUSE; TEAM; TRANSDISCIPLINARY
Abstract-Résumé: This proposal describes the next steps in a pioneering integrative and transdisciplinary research program, initiated in 2002, to reduce driving while impaired by alcohol and other drugs (DWI). We extend the team's scope and membership, while maintaining the innovation and collaboration that have inspired us to date. We propose an interlocking, progressive DWI research program to pursue five main objectives: 1) clarification of causal factors; 2) development and evaluation of a first-time offender classification system; 3) evaluation of the deterrent effect of policies and programs; 4) study of offenders who fail to engage in remedial programs; 5) KTE. These issues are key to advancing DWI prevention and intervention. By its transdisciplinary logic, this  proposal is consistent with CIHR's "Blueprint" to "catalyze and encourage the convergence of disciplines that underlie the most exciting and important discoveries in health research, and to resolve evermore complex health problems". By its integrative approach, the team, involving Quebec's licensing authorities and other decision-makers, knowledge brokers, and researchers in traffic safety, addictions, psychology, criminology, behavioural neuroscience, psychiatry, medicine, biology, and epidemiology, fortifies its pursuit of a problem-based, user guided DWI research agenda, its capacity to create new knowledge, and to expedite knowledge translation into reducing the public health burden related to DWI-related crashes in Canada, and of course, immeasurable human loss and suffering.

ResearchClassEN: DRUGS- PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCE/CHEMISTRY & NON MEDICAL USE OF DRUGS; EPIDEMIOLOGY
ClasseRechercheFR: DROGUES - SCIENCES PHARMACEUTIQUES/CHIMIE ET UTILISATION NON MÉDICALE DES DROGUES; EPIDEMIOLOGIE
TitreApplicationTitle: Non-Medical Use of Prescription Opioid Analgesics in Canada: Epidemiology, Consequences and Interventions
Keywords-MotsClés: BRIEF INTERVENTIONS; DEPENDENCE; DIVERSION; GENERAL POPULATIONS; HEALTH CARE UTILIZATION; HEALTH SYSTEMS; MORBIDITY; MORTALITY; NON-MEDICAL DRUG USE; PAIN; POLICY; POLY-DRUG USE; PRESCRIPTION OPIOID ANALGESICS; PREVENTION; PUBLIC HEALTH; STREET DRUG USE; TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Several indicators-including relevant projections based on US data - are suggesting that the non-medical use of prescription opioids (POs), and related harms (e.g., morbidity and mortality) are a rapidly growing phenomenon in Canada. However, key empirical data to systematically analyze and understand the phenomenon, and inform evidence-based interventions (e.g., prevention, treatment and policy) are missing. This NET, consisting of investigators of multiple research disciplines/ pillars and institutions across Canada, proposes a program of inter-linked research projects to inform interventions development in the area of non-medical PO use. These include: Epidemiology of non-medical PO use in general and and street populations; mapping of medical PO availability/ dispensing across Canadian jurisdictions; sub-projects into non-medical PO sourcing routes and poly-drug use among street drug users; monitoring of PO related mortality (i.e., poisoning deaths); feasibility of brief interventions for problematic PO use. A knowledge translation (KT) group consisting of representatives from key governmental, non-governmental and professional stakeholders/ institutions will form the basis for systematic KT of research results into intervention domains.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Population Health and Human Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The human early learning partnership (HELP) is a collaborative, interdisciplinary research institute that contributes to new knowledge in early child development and enhances the quality of childrens early years. HELP links over 200 faculty, researchers, and graduate students from six BC universities and is the worlds first research network to bring a population-based perspective to early child development. Core research activities include provincial-level assessment of early child development, community mapping, linked and longitudinal database development, the Consortium for Health, Intervention Learning and Development (CHILD) Project, neurogenomics research, early learning and child care research, social care and social citizenship, early childhood screening evaluation, and international child development. HELPs research explores how different environments contribute to different developmental outcomes for children. In addition to grant funding, HELP receives core infrastructure funding from the BC Ministry of Children & Family Development.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Transplantation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Patients undergoing transplantation face serious side effects from the immunosuppressive drugs that prevent graft rejection but also non-specifically suppress the immune system. We are studying whether a type of white blood cell, known as T regulatory cells (Tregs), could be used to control undesired immune responses, without affecting other aspects of the normal immune system. This proposal aims to address questions about the molecular and cellular biology of Tregs and to develop new models to test their function. This research will lead to the use of Tregs as a "cellular therapy" to control undesired immune responses to transplanted tissues and organs.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neural Control in Decision Making
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The brain makes thousands of decisions every day. When doing so, it must combine variables such as the probability of receiving a reward, the magnitude of reward, and delay to reward. My research attempts to uncover how these important decision variables are represented in the brain to guide motor actions. The uniqueness of this research is that neural mechanisms are examined using sophisticated behavioural tasks with both brain imaging in humans and neurophysiological techniques in animals. Ultimately, the aim of this research is to improve diagnosis and treatment options for individuals, such as pathological gamblers, who routinely make poor decisions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Adverse Drug Reactions
Keywords-MotsClés: Pharmaceutical products, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Different people respond to medications differently.  A drug that is safe and effective for most people can lead to a serious adverse reaction in some patients.  Such adverse reactions are a significant cause of death and are a major contributor to health care costs and the uncertainty of drug development.  They are not well understood and are difficult to study but it appears that most of these adverse reactions are due to chemically reactive metabolites rather than the parent drug and are immune-mediated.  This research program targets the basic mechanisms of these adverse reactions by identification of reactive metabolites of drugs, determination of how these reactive metabolites can lead to an immune response and development of biomarkers to predict which drugs are likely to cause such adverse reactions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Microbiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Chris Whitfield directs a research program whose ultimate goal is to understand the processes involved in the assembly of complex polymers on the surfaces of bacterial cells. These polymers play crucial roles in the lifestyles of bacteria. In pathogens, they are essential contributors to the infection process. The ambitious fundamental objective of this research is an atomic-level view of the assembly components and determination of their mechanisms of action. In addition, Dr. Whitfield hopes to exploit this information to develop new targets for therapeutic intervention for treatment of bacterial infections.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Atlantic Studies
Keywords-MotsClés: Social change, social processes and social conflicts, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research will continue research initiated during the last two years of the current Canada Research Chair. Specifically, this research has focused on the ways in which contemporary health services are organized in a variety of settings. This research will continue to explore the changing environment of work practices and organizational structures within health care, paying particular attention to the introduction of new occupational groups, shifting professional boundaries, and responses to shortages of health care professionals in various Canadian settings. The project will provide an historical context to important debates within Canadas health care system concerning human resource issues.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Viral Hepatitis/Immunology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) are major blood-born human pathogens which cause liver diseases, including chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, liver failure and liver cancer.  An estimated 550-600 million people worldwide suffer from chronic hepatitis B or C, including ~500,000 Canadians.  These viruses also replicate in the immune system and, as we have found, frequently establish asymptomatic persistent infections, called occult infections, which are difficult to detect by current blood tests. My research investigates how these occult infections develop, to what degree they are important to human health, if treatment is require, and how the immune system is involved.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuropharmacology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Currently available drug therapy for muscle and joint pain is often associated with undesirable side effects.  Dr. Cairns continuing research focuses on the identification of targets within muscles and joints that may prove useful for the development of drugs to treat this pain with fewer serious side effects.  Since certain types of chronic muscle and joint pain conditions, such as temporomandibular disorders, fibromyalgia, migraine headache and arthritis, are more common in women than in men, this research also involves understanding sex-related differences in pain, with a particular emphasis on the role of muscle and joint nerves.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Blood Proteins
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Metalloproteins comprise one-third to one-half of all proteins found in nature, and they are involved in a wide range of normal and pathological processes in man. This CRC supports research that focuses on understanding metalloproteins that are (a) essential to human iron metabolism, (b) involved in iron metabolism in pathogenic bacteria, and (c) involved in tumor resistance to the normal immune response. Success of this research will promote or lead to new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of human diseases that affect a substantial fraction of the worlds population.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in HIV/AIDS and Urban Population Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: Inner city populations, particularly injection drug users, are at extremely high risk of many drug related harms including HIV, hepatitis C and overdose death.  Martin Schechter is studying these vulnerabilities, with a particular focus on young Aboriginal drug users, in order to help design prevention programs that stop these harms from occurring.  To improve the treatment of addiction, he and his team are conducting innovative clinical trials that are testing whether medically prescribed heroin and related treatments can benefit both people with the most severe cases of heroin addiction as well as their communities.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chairs in Statistics and Modeling of the Health Care System
Keywords-MotsClés: Hospital structure and organization of medical care, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Why is it so difficult to improve the timeliness of care? Waits, delays, and cancellations continue to have negative impacts on patients and their families, care providers, and hospital operations. A key contributing factor is our limited  understanding of how changes in the health system affect the delivery of healthcare services. Funding is requested to continue developing methods for assessment of the most probable impacts of changes in the organization of surgical care on patient and system outcomes. The overall objectives of the proposed research are:1)   to construct discrete-event simulation models for patient flow in surgical cardiac care;2)   to evaluate alternative methods for managing the care process using simulation experiments;3)   to position UBC as an international leader in simulation-based healthcare evaluation; 4)   to train the next generation of health services researchers; and5)   to translate results into beneficial changes in the surgical care received by Canadians.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Valvular Heart Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Dr Pibarot performs multidisciplinary research to elucidate the mechanisms underlying the development and progression of valvular heart diseases (VHD) and to develop and validate novel approaches to improve the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of these diseases. Over the past 10 years, he has established at Université Laval a research consortium of several laboratories and colleagues who share his vision and enthusiasm for research and innovation in the field of VHD. This consortium is now one of the most productive in the world in terms of valve disease research and knowledge translation in this field.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair of Research Transfer in Intensive Care
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Critically ill patients require life support and are at very high risk of death and disability. Venous blood clots and heart attacks are two potentially deadly but often unrecognized problems in this population.  Through international clinical trials, this award will focus on preventing blood clots (which occur in 10% of patients), and identifying and treating heart attacks (which occur in 20% of patients) in medical and surgical intensive care units.  This award will enhance research capacity, help to train highly qualified personnel, ensure that research results are applied at the bedside, and ultimately, decrease the burden of critical illness.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CRC in Neurodegenerative Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Alzheimers disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by a gradual loss of memory, followed by deterioration of higher cognitive functions. The neuropathological features associated with AD brains include selective loss of neurons, extracellular deposits of beta-amyloid (Ab) peptide and intracellular accumulation of phosphorylated tau protein. The basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and glutamatergic neurons of the hippocampus and neocortex are most severely affected in AD brains, but very little is currently known regarding the cause of vulnerability of these neurons. Results obtained from our lab lead us to hypothesize that Ab peptides by regulating phosphorylation of tau protein can mediate degeneration of the neurons. To address our hypothesis we are currently investigating not only the cellular mechanisms underlying the cause of neurodegeneration in AD pathology and but also how to protect them against toxicity. These findings will have major implications for our understanding of the etiology and pharmacotherapy of AD.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Autoimmunity and Tumor Immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: T lymphocytes or T cells play a key role in both normal immune responses and pathological immune responses (e.g. autoimmune disease). T cells recognize specific antigens using the T cell receptor, and important physiological processes are in place to ensure that tolerance to self antigens is maintained. Current models predict that the cell presenting the antigen to T cells is the key parameter that determines whether T cell tolerance or T cell activation occurs. Our objective is to manipulate the T cell response to promote anti-tumor immunity and apply this knowledge to development novel immunotherapeutic strategies for cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Fetal, Neonatal and Maternal Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Lyes research program investigates the mechanisms underlying pregnancy complications that impact not only maternal, fetal and neonatal health, but also the offsprings lifelong health.  Studies uniquely integrating genetic, molecular, physiologic and clinical elements will define 1) the mechanisms underlying preterm labour, as well as the development of new diagnostics/therapeutics to prevent preterm birth; 2) the mechanisms by which placental cells remodel the maternal uterine vasculature, an essential component supporting fetal growth and development; and 3) the genetic basis for developmental origins of health and disease, whereby a suboptimal environment during development increases an individual's risk of disease in adulthood.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Tumor Biology, Angiogenesis & Antiangiogenic Therapy
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Major advances are being made in the development of new anti-cancer drugs, especially molecular targeted therapies. These include antiangiogenic drugs designed to inhibit the formation of new blood vessels that provide the oxygen and nutrients tumors require for relentless growth. However these drugs cause only modest increases in prolonging survival, and are extremely expensive. Dr. Kerbels program is devoted to significantly improving the anti-cancer effects, cost efficacy, and toxicity profiles of antiangiogenic drugs, primarily by integrating them with a novel therapeutic strategy he is pioneering known as metronomic chemotherapy wherein patients are treated continuously with small, non-toxic doses of chemotherapy.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in International Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Existing understandings of international health are based on a centrifugal model whereby knowledge and practices are generated in industrialized metropoles and disseminated outwards.  My research, by contrast, examines the dynamics of international health from a Latin American perspective, an arena both under-explored and important for current global health policymaking.  I will pursue three interconnected historical studies, each focusing on non-central, yet influential, actors and ideas: the role of Latin American-European interchanges in the emergence of the international child health agenda; the part played, abroad and domestically, by US health professionals in international health movements; and Soviet-Latin American public health relations.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair for Physical Actitivty and Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity and physical inactivity represent two of Canadas most serious health challenges.  The proposed research will develop new treatment strategies for overweight older adults, whose rates of obesity are increasing faster than other Canadians.  Novel strategies to promote active lifestyles will be explored.  Health-related changes that take place after obesity surgery among seriously obese patients will be examined.  New pre- and post-surgery exercise programs will be developed to minimize post-surgical complications and optimize long-term outcomes.  Finally using national databases, trends will be monitored and recommendations made to increase population levels of physical activity and improve the health of all Canadians.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en génomique fonctionnelle / Canada Research Chair in Functional Genomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: La molécule d'ARN aide l'ADN des gènes à produire les protéines et c'est la synthèse de lARN messager (ARNm) qui intéresse la Chaire de recherche du Canada en génomique fonctionnelle. La CRC étudie l'épissage alternatif de l'ARN, un processus biologique crucial qui permet de créer différents types de molécules d'ARNm à partir de chaque gène. Ce processus est responsable de la diversité des structures et des fonctions de plus de 90% des protéines humaines. La CRC a pour but de consolider les réalisations du mandat précédent qui ont mis à jour plusieurs stratégies moléculaires qu'utilisent  les cellules pour contrôler lépissage alternatif. La CRC permettra aussi de comprendre et dexploîter la contribution inouïe de lépissage alternatif dans lévolution du génome humain depuis la séparation homme-singe jusquaux variations entre individus. Enfin, les mécanismes contrôlant lépissage alternatif et la diversité qui en résulte seront utilisés dans lélaboration de nouvelles approches pour détecter et combattre les maladies humaines dont le cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Global Health and Capacity Building
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: This unique community-based trans-disciplinary approach will address the burning question of how best to build the capacity of the health workforce worldwide. With a world shortage of health workers, this innovative, cross-cultural applied research will implement and evaluate interventions in Canada as well as in Africa and Latin America. Building on previous successful innovations, the new cross- cultural research program focuses more specifically on the growing challenges of HIV/AIDS, drug-resistant tuberculosis and other infectious diseases, taking a broad ecosystem health approach as well as answering specific questions of concern to policy makers regarding policies to reduce the burden of infectious diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cellular and molecular biomechanics
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The Canada Research Chair in molecular and cellular biomechanics is aimed at addressing specific muscle (skeletal and cardiac) and neuromuscular diseases using a unique mixture of femto-, nano-, and micro-technology approaches to help specific patient populations. Areas of focus include cerebral palsy, Duchennes and myotonic muscular dystrophies, osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, and dilatational cardiac myopathies. Structural changes on the molecular and cellular level associated with diseases are associated with functional implications for the patients. Particular emphasis is on the development of conservative treatment strategies to prevent disease, or to reverse, stop and slow down ongoing disease processes through an understanding of the molecular causes of the pathology.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Hemostasis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The inherited bleeding disorders, hemophilia  A and von Willebrand disease, result in significant chronic morbidity in tens of thousands of Canadians.  Their diagnosis and treatment is variably challenging and expensive.  This research program will focus on novel approaches to enhance our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying these conditions and innovations of treatment.  The experimental strategies to be utilized will involve methodologies ranging from basic molecular and cellular biology to human trial evaluation.  We propose that this research program will continue to make important contributions to our improved basic knowledge and clinical management of these common inherited bleeding diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cancer Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: MRP1 is a protein that makes tumour cells resistant to chemotherapy by pumping drugs out of cancer cells.  MRP1 also protects normal cells by impeding entry of drugs and other foreign chemicals.  The major objective of the proposed research is to learn exactly how MRP1 (and related MRP4) pumps drugs out of cells, and how variations in MRP1 and MRP4 affect individual responses to drugs and chemical toxins.  This research will advance our understanding of how MRP protein pumps can protect against chemically-induced toxicities, which has implications for the safety and efficacy of chemotherapy for cancer and other human diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Lipid Metabolism
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Canada is experiencing an epidemic of obesity that is contributing to diabetes, heart disease, and premature death. This proposal investigates why being obese causes the metabolic syndrome with a specific emphasis on insulin resistance  and atherosclerosis.  An improved understanding about how hormones regulates the body's storage and breakdown of fat and responsiveness to insulin will enable the development of new medicines for the treatment of obesity and the prevention of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en transduction du signal de stress cellulaire
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Une surcharge du système de contrôle de qualité des protéines est mise en cause dans un grand nombre de maladies dégénératives humaines et sa vulnérabilité représente une cible importante pour le traitement du cancer. Le laboratoire étudie la réponse cellulaire au stress protéotoxique. Il s'intéresse aux mécanismes de détection par les chaperons moléculaires de la famille des HSP des protéines altérées, ainsi qu'à la signalisation induite par  celles-ci et déterminant les différentes avenues de réponses cellulaires possibles comme l'augmentation de la capacité de repliement des protéines, l'induction de mécanismes spécifiques de dégradation, ou l'induction d'un programme de mort cellulaire.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Host Resistance to Respiratory Pathogens
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Infectious diseases are directly responsible for over 25% of all deaths and have gained added prominence in the 21st century. The complex host-pathogen interactions that lead to serious infection are poorly understood. Forward genetic analysis of inbred and chemically mutagenized mice will be used to to define host susceptibility to bacterial, viral, and fungal respiratory pathogens. Candidate genes that are identified will be studied among affected populations in order to establish their relevance to human infection. Precise identification of novel immunodeficiency genes will guide the development of innovative management strategies to diminish the extensive burden of microbial disease on human populations.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Developmental Genetics of the Urogenital System.
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Several developmental defects and tumor types are known to affect the urogenitalsystem, leading to severe health complications or even death. The cellularand molecular mechanisms underlying these urogenital diseases are unfortunatelystill very limited. In the past years, we have studied some of the most important genes for urogenital system development and cancer using the mouse as model system. By studying how these genes perform their normal function in the cell, we try to understand how the urogenital system develops. By modifying their function, we recreate urogenital disease models. The long-term objectives of this research program is to develop better diagnoses and treatments for this disease group.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Control of Synaptic Structure
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Biomedical research over the last decade has led to an important appreciation of the diversity of molecules that reside at synapses, the specialized contact points between neurons within our brain. However, the assembly of these molecules into signaling networks that confer complex physiological properties to synapses remains poorly understood. The proposed research program to understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms that allow our brains to process and store information through modification of synapses. Unique to this grant is its interest in defining how glial cells in the brain contribute to synapse structure and function. This propsal seeks to uncover synapse regulatory mechanisms that may become impaired in numerous brain diseases, especially those associated with mental retardation.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in the Genetics of Pain
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The research is fundamentally aimed at explaining interindividual differences in sensitivity to pain and pain inhibition, and susceptibility to developing chronic pain after injury.  Like any biological phenomenon, the sources of such variability encompass genetic factors (nature), environmental factors (nurture) and their interaction.  Much of the effort has been focused towards the identification of specific genes responsible for variability in these traits.  Along the way to this goal, however, we have discovered phenomenon that have become important parallel avenues of research:  sex differences in pain and analgesia, and environmental (especially social) determinants of pain sensitivity.

TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur le sommeil
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Les troubles du sommeil sont très fréquents dans la population générale et ont des conséquences graves sur la santé, la qualité de vie des canadiens et entraînent des coûts considérables, notamment ceux associés à labsentéisme au travail et aux accidents dus à linsomnie et la somnolence. Le programme de la Chaire étudie lensemble des troubles du sommeil comme les insomnies, le syndrome dapnées au cours du sommeil, la narcolepsie, les parasomnies comme le somnambulisme, les terreurs nocturnes, le bruxisme et enfin les conséquences dun mauvais sommeil en bas âge sur le développement intellectuel et lapparition dobésité à lâge scolaire.

TitreApplicationTitle: Gap Junction Regulation and Vascular Control
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Arteries adjust the flow of blood to active tissue.  For arteries to respond as a network, cells within this tissue must communicate with one another.  Cell-cell communication is controlled by tiny pores, or gap junctions, which allow chemical and electrical information to spread between cells.  Research has yet to provide clear insight into how these pores govern blood flow.  Using a range of experimental and theoretical approaches, the applicant will continue to explore the relationship between gap junctions and blood flow control.  Clinical targeting of gap junctions could limit the blood flow defects found with hypertension and diabetes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Human Retrovirology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: AIDS is a slow degenerative disease of the immune and nervous systems resulting from HIV infection. This disease represents an international health crisis that threatens to overwhelm even the best systems of health care delivery. The mission of the Research Chair in Human Retrovirology is to investigate how HIV interacts and exploits host cell factors to produce and transmit fully infectious viral particles. Ultimately, the elucidation of these mechanisms will lead to a heightened understanding of viral multiplication and pathogenesis and will reveal additional targets for antiviral strategies, more of which are urgently needed, in both developed and developing countries.

TitreApplicationTitle: Delineation of the Relationships Between Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) Use and the Development of Osteoporosis and Osteoporosis Related Fractures
Keywords-MotsClés: FRACTRURES; GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE (GERD); OSTEOPOROSIS; PROTON PUMP INHIBITORS
Abstract-Résumé: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are among the most commonly prescribed medications in clinical practice. PPIs are the most effective medications for reducing the production of stomach acid, and as a result are very effective for the treatment and prevention of upper gastrointestinal diseases, including gastroesophageal reflux (GERD) and peptic ulcer disease. These medications are generally believed to be safe, though recent studies have suggested that the use of these medications is associated with the development of osteoporosis related fractures, including those of the hip, spine, and wrist.  However it is unclear whether the relationship between PPIs and osteoporosis-related fractures is causative, nor has the mechanism by which PPIs may promote osteoporosis or fractures been elucidated.  PPIs are commonly used in the elderly, who are at the highest risk of developing osteoporosis and osteoporosis related fractures. Furthermore, osteoporosis related fractures, especially hip fractures, are associated with a high risk of death and disability, with up to 20% of people diagnosed with a hip fracture dying within six months, and a high proportion of survivors left with significant disability and loss of independence. Our determining that PPIs definitively contribute to the risk of osteoporosis and osteoporosis related fractures may therefore have a huge impact on patient care.    Therefore, we are seeking to perform a number of related studies in man and in animal models with the aim of providing further information on the possible cause-and-effect relationship between PPIs, osteoporosis, and osteoporosis related fractures.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluation of the Renin-Angiotensin System in Aboriginal People
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL; GLOMERULAR HEMODYNAMICS; GLOMERULAR HYPERFILTRATION; RENAL PHYSIOLOGY; RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN SYSTEM; SALT
Abstract-Résumé: There is a widespread recognition that Aboriginal people have a dramatically increased risk of kidney disease compared to the general population, though the reasons behind this discrepancy are unclear.  Despite this ever-increasing burden of kidney disease with its associated morbidity, mortality and cost to the Canadian health care system, the renal physiology, and specifically the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), of the Canadian Aboriginal people has never been studied.  The knowledge that the RAS is operative in this population could lead to rational treatments to delay progression, or even prevent initiation, of kidney disease.  It is the central hypothesis of this proposal that in the high-salt state (a state of maximal RAS suppression), healthy Aboriginal people will exhibit increased renal and systemic RAS activity, activation of which results in a predisposition to glomerulosclerosis and ultimately, kidney failure.  These experiments will be conducted in young, healthy Aboriginal and Caucasian subjects who are on a controlled sodium and protein diet.  Renal hemodynamic function will be assessed using classic inulin and para-aminohippurate (PAH) clearance techniques.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Birth Cohort: Indoor Air and the Development of Asthma and Allergy
Keywords-MotsClés: AIRWAY INFLAMMATION; ALLERGY; ASTHMA; BIRTH COHORT; ENVIRONMENTAL INFLUENCES ON HEALTH; EPIGENETICS; GENETICS; IMMUNOLOGY; INNATE IMMUNITY; LONGITUDINAL; LUNG FUNCTION; RESPIRATORY INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Environmental exposures, diet, physical activity, stress and epigenetic changes may underlie increased childhood allergy and asthma. This funded study has been designed as a multidisciplinary, longitudinal, Canada-wide population-based cohort study (n = 5,000), to examine the interaction of genetic & environmental factors in asthma development. Women will be recruited early in pregnancy and children will be studied at birth, at a home visit at 3 months, and at clinic visits at ages 1, 3 and 5 years with intervening telephone questionnaires.  In Toronto, a subgroup of the cohort will have detailed assessments of infant lung function and airway inflammation at 3 months then yearly as well as detailed virologic studies in the first year of life. Allergic asthma at age 5 is the primary outcome on which the study is powered. Atopy, recurrent wheeze, food allergy, and allergic eczema are secondary outcomes. Environmental exposures will be assessed by questionnaire, home inspections, dust sampling and modeling of outdoor exposures. Immunological studies, genetic and epigenetic testing of DNA will be performed. Nutrition, viral and bacterial infections will be studied with a focus in infancy. Pulmonary function, airway inflammation, acquired and innate immunity, psychosocial factors and stress will be assessed. Family-based genetic testing will test previously identified asthma- or allergy-related genes. Inflammatory cell gene expression will be related to gene sequence variation, environmental exposures, epigenetic phenomena and clinical outcomes. Environmental, genetic and biologic material will be assayed both in real time and stored for later analyses using cohort and nested case-control designs. Multiple investigators from diverse academic disciplines, and scientists from several Federal departments, together with scientific, ethical and legal advisors, are involved in this study. Recruitment has commenced this year, with follow-up to age 5 to be completed in 2014.

Keywords-MotsClés: APPLIED STATISTICS; DRUG UTILIZATION; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; LONG-TERM CARE HOMES; PROVIDER PROFILING; QUALITY OF CARE
Abstract-Résumé: The correct use of drug therapies in residents of long-term care homes (also known as nursing homes) is a challenge. These individuals are frail, have many clinical conditions which require multiple medications, and are treated by a number of different doctors, nurses and aides. All of these factors place nursing home residents at special risk for developing problems related to their drug treatments. This study will compare the prescribing patterns for different kinds of drugs across nursing homes in order to see if facilities with good (or bad) prescribing practices can be identified consistently. The results will be used to determine which drugs should be included in reports to the public on the quality of nursing homes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Individual, social and environmental barriers to HIV risk reduction among men who have sex with men and transgendered populations in India
Keywords-MotsClés: BEHAVIOUR CHANGE; HIV AND AIDS; MEN WHO HAVE SEX WITH MEN; PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: In South Asia, men who have sex with men (MSM) are highly vulnerable to HIV infection and because many also have females sexual partners, prevention programs targeting MSM are a critical part of an overall HIV control strategy. However, prevention programs and services for MSM are impeded by social and environmental factors such as stigma and discrimination that inhibit MSM from accessing these services. The objective of this study is to create new knowledge about the individual, social and environmental factors that lead to increased risk among MSM so that programs can be better designed. The study will be conducted in three diverse cities in south India and will involve the MSM community as researchers to gather in-depth information from MSM. Analysis will focus on differences in how MSM interact with each other and with the broader social environment to uncover how these interactions influence HIV risk and vulnerability. The results will be used to inform the MSM community and HIV prevention programs about how to promote behaviour change that will lead to lower HIV risk.

Keywords-MotsClés: CRITICAL HEALTH RESEARCH; HEALTH CARE; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; PLACE; TECHNOLOGY; TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENT
Abstract-Résumé: The Health Care, Technology & Place (HCTP) Program is the only graduate training program that tries to understand 21st century health care by examining the way that technologies, societies & space interact. HCTP provides an integrated, collaborative & interdisciplinary approach to research training. In its first 6 years, HCTP1 generated a group of scholars who built research capacity through scholarship that links many academic disciplines & examines the complex linkages between people, places, technologies & work in modern health care.   While HCTP1 focused on the setting (or places) where health care is sought, delivered or received, HCTP2 looks also at technology since increasingly, people who participate in care (patients, providers) & the technologies they use can be separated in space or time. In looking at technologies, HCTP continues to examine the people, places & work practices through which technologies are produced, understood, & have their effects. Also, HCTP2 works to encourage a broader approach to the highly practical & policy relevant domain of health technology assessment (HTA) in order to capture the wide-ranging & context-specific features of technologies in health systems & everyday life.  While funded in the first wave of CIHR training programs, HCTP has evolved. This application offers evidence of innovation & progress as: HCTP2 has the same name but an enhanced emphasis on the technological mediation of care; new mentors add disciplinary depth & complementary & distinguished records to the HCTP1 mentor team; the HCTP2 curriculum structure involves innovations in design & content to ensure greater integration & core shared content; knowledge translation across disciplines is augmented by knowledge transfer & exchange (KTE) with the fields of practice & policy; & research training has been transformed & supplemented through research placement opportunities with decision maker organizations at the local, national & international levels.

TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR Strategic Training Program in Vascular Research (STPVR)
Keywords-MotsClés: ATHEROSCLEROSIS; CARDIOVASCULAR; CEREBROVASCULAR; TRAINING PROGRAM; VASCULAR IMAGING
Abstract-Résumé: Our goal in developing our established transdisciplinary CIHR Strategic Training Program in Vascular Research (STPVR) was to integrate the expertise of well-established scientists at Robarts Research Institute, The University of Western Ontario, and the University of Waterloo, in the biological, physical, and engineering fields, to train the next generation of scientists by supplementing their specialized academic education with training in different aspects of vascular disease required for them to become leaders in their research fields. This new proposal for our training program will add some exciting new elements to our successful training program to teach students the critical professional skills required to make the transition from student to new investigator, and the translational skills required to move their discoveries and innovations into the clinical and private sectors. Our students fall into two major groups; those in disciplines urgently needed to help advance vascular research, such as physics, computer science, mathematics, and engineering, but who require extra training in the biological and genetic bases of vascular disease, and those students with strong backgrounds in medicine, genetics, cell, and molecular biology, who need the physics, engineering, and mathematical knowledge critical to advancing vascular research outcomes and discovery. Our overall goal is to develop top research scientists with the expertise to build their own transdisciplinary teams focused on the understanding, treatment, and prevention of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease. Only students who make a successful transition to professional scientist and who learn how to translate their discoveries into the clinic or industry will progress to become leaders of their own transdisciplinary teams. Our Strategic Training Program addresses these critical needs building on the success of our existing Program and with the introduction of new critical elements.

Keywords-MotsClés: ACADEMIA; CLINICAL TRIALS; DRUG DISCOVERY; EXPERIMENTAL THERAPEUTICS; INDUSTRY
Abstract-Résumé: Progress in biomedical research is driving an unprecedented pace of discovery in the understanding of the molecular mechanisms of disease. However, despite this progress, there is an enormous gap between the discovery of tools that improve our knowledge of disease processes and the numbers of new therapies "translated" to the bedside. This proposal for a Drug Development Training Program (DDTP) is based on the premise that introducing students to strategies designed to develop candidate molecules into useful drugs will accelerate translation and lead to a greater impact of basic research on disease management. This program brings together strong basic science and clinical research at McGill University and the McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) together with local Biopharmaceutical Industry partners to expose students to the process, successes and failures of state-of-the-art drug development efforts. It is our goal that DDTP will train the academic and industry leaders who will develop the next generation of therapies to benefit all Canadians.

Keywords-MotsClés: COMMUNITY CAPACITY BUILDING PRACTICES; HEALTH INEQUALITIES; MULTI-CENTERED TRAINING NETWORK; POPULATION HEALTH INTERVENTION RESEARCH; SCALING UP GRADUATE STUDENT TRAINING CAPACITY; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: This application is about equipping Canada for the "sea-change" that is coming in population health. We refer to the switch of attention from studying the causes and determinants of health problems, "to the science and practice of solving them", the field known as population health intervention research (PHIR). Seven universities are combining to construct a training program which (1) focuses on four main themes/priority areas in PHIR (methods; economic evaluation, ethics and research governance; and interventions addressing social health inequalities);(2) produces and delivers a shared curriculum around key competencies in PHIR; (3) develops web based resources for learning within and beyond the STIHR network; (4) recruits students and facilitates training pathways across the seven sites; (5) facilitates learning in both official languages; and (6) partners with the National Collaborating Centres for Public Health (NCC PH) in order to maximise contacts and relationships between producers of primary PHIR, those committed to synthesising this knowledge and end users (decision-makers and practitioners) With the demand and need for PHIR increasing in connection with the pressure to develop evidence-informed public health practices, our STIHR addresses how the supply of skilled researchers will be met.

TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR Strategic Training Program in Work Disability Prevention
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVANCED TRAINING PROGRAM; COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE; INTERNATIONAL PROGRAM; RETURN TO WORK; TRANSDISCIPLINARITY; WORK DISABILITY PREVENTION
Abstract-Résumé: Work disability, occurring when a worker is unable to remain at or resume work because of a health problem, is prevalent and imposes a heavy burden on Canadian society and abroad. In 2002, the CIHR acknowledged the need for developing capacity in the field of work disability prevention (WDP) by subsidizing the development and implementation of the WDP CIHR Strategic Training Program, a unique training program in the world. The main objective of this program is to help future researchers develop transdisciplinary knowledge, skills and attitudes regarding WDP. The WDP Training Program is an advanced diploma program which is superimposed onto the doctoral or post-doctoral studies taken by the trainees at their own universities. During the last 6 years, the Program has trained 54 high-quality trainees from 11 countries. This proposal pursues two objectives: (1) to continue to improve young researchers' training in WDP and (2) to develop an international community of practice in WDP. This proposal gathers a large team of 30 highly qualified mentors with various expertises and from 16 universities, 9 research centres, and 4 countries. Also, this application proposes the organisation of a community of practice that had spontaneously emerged from the experience of the Program participants. Not only will it be formally organized to foster year-round knowledge building among trainees, alumni and mentors, but it will also be extended for the benefit of stakeholders and allow for their participation. Over the past years, this training program has contributed to raise national training standards and reinforce Canada's international leadership role in building WDP capacity. Working toward the objectives of this proposal will allow the development of knowledge building, translation and exchange to help reduce the individual and societal burden of work disability. Continuation of the grant will allow excellence to be maintained as the training program moves toward full autonomy.

Keywords-MotsClés: GENE THERAPY; REGENERATIVE MEDICINE; STEM CELLS; TOLERANCE; TRANSPLANTATION
Abstract-Résumé: Organ failure is a pervasive medical problem that results in immense personal and economic costs, morbidity, and death.  At present, the only truly effective treatment for organ failure is transplantation.  The deficiencies of this option are increasingly apparent, and include a chronic shortage of donor organs, side effects from harsh immunosuppressive medications, and chronic rejection leading to the eventual loss of most transplanted organs.       The nascent field of regenerative medicine, defined as the practice of repair, regeneration, or replacement of tissues and organs that have failed, has enormous potential to revolutionize diagnostic and therapeutic alternatives to transplantation via the development of radical new therapies.        At present, there are few scientists and practitioners of regenerative medicine, and we have now developed the only comprehensive training program in this important field in Canada. It is essential that this program continue to be funded in partnership with industry to identify and train scientists who will lead this important new field in health research.

Keywords-MotsClés: DRUG DESIGN AND SYNTHESIS; DRUG DEVELOPMENT; DRUG EVALUATION; DRUG FORMULATION AND DELIVERY; DRUG SCREENING; DRUG TARGET IDENTIFICATION
Abstract-Résumé: The Multidisciplinary Training in Drug Development (M-TraDD) program is a Centre for Drug Research and Development (CDRD) initiative. CDRD is the first of its kind in Canada. Its mission is to take drug discoveries from the Universities and Teaching Hospitals of British Columbia and develop them into new medicines to treat diseases.  The process of drug discovery and development takes a long time and requires the expertise of many different disciplines such as chemistry, biology, etc. Therefore, researchers who are experts in one field often do not have the expertise or the access to the specialized equipment and personnel to move their discoveries from the laboratory to the clinic. This is where CDRD gets involved. CDRD offers both specialized equipment and personnel who are knowledgeable in drug discovery and development. CDRD assists with the identification of disease targets and the drugs that act on them, the development of new, more effective drugs, the formulation of drugs into medicines suitable for human use, and the testing of the medicines to ensure they are effective and safe. Because CDRD offers not only a variety of expertise, but also the latest in equipment and technology, it is an ideal environment to train talented individuals in drug discovery and development. The trainees will take specialized courses and modules. Further, they will become part of multidisciplinary teams working to develop new medicines. They will have a unique opportunity to work with different technologies and alongside colleagues with very different scientific backgrounds to their own. The trainees will not only develop a vast array of scientific skills but also communication and organizational skills. Such well-rounded individuals with an understanding of the entire drug development process are highly sought after. We expect M-TraDD graduates to become leaders in the drive to develop new and more effective medicines for the benefit of Canadians and patients worldwide.

Abstract-Résumé: This CIHR training program is offered through a partnership among several established areas of excellence in musculoskeletal health research in Southwestern Ontario.  Trainees will have the unique opportunity to participate in cutting-edge transdisciplinary research and knowledge translation, while gaining the leadership skills and experience that are essential for scientific progress in the 21st century.   By providing a vigorous transdisciplinary training environment, JuMP will increase research capacity and productivity in Canada and develop future leaders in musculoskeletal health research.  The importance of preventing and treating musculoskeletal disorders are widely recognized, especially with the emergence of an aging population.  JuMP will train the leaders who can meet the upcoming challenges in musculoskeletal health research and who will significantly improve the health, mobility and quality of life of Canadians.

Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CANCER; COMPLEX DISEASES; COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY; GENOMICS; IMAGING; MATHEMATICAL MODELLING; ORPHAN DISEASES; PROTEOMICS; QUANTITATIVE BIOLOGY; SYSTEMS BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: High-throughput (eg microarrays, sequencing) and high-content (eg single cell imaging, chemical screening) assays are now an integral part of biomedicine, and have produced successes that are now finding clinical utility. This is true for a range of human diseases including cancer, diabetes, fibrosis and many orphan/neglected diseases. A consequence of the use of these approaches is the need for inter-disciplinary teams that simultaneously provide the excellence to develop these technologies, to model the data quantitatively, and to extract from these models physiologically relevant knowledge that will have impact in the clinic. Such teams involve a broad range of researchers including clinicians, basic researchers, quantitative scientists and experts in technology. Since traditional training programs provide for depth in a single area of research, the current generation of students tends to understand only a small fraction of these systems or integrative biology projects. This ignorance represents an enormous conceptual and practical training challenge. Our program will provide students with a mature understanding of the biology by integrating the trainees into inter-disciplinary research teams. Workshops and courses will provide students from the quantitative sciences instruction in laboratory techniques, and students with biomedical or technological backgrounds instruction in statistics, modeling and computation. Through a seminar series, yearly retreats and special interest groups, the program will introduce students to ethical and translational issues related to their work. By the end of their studies, trainees will have both an in depth understanding of their specific research area and a broad overview of systems and integrative techniques used to study human disease, that the next generation of Canadian researchers will be primed to initiate and drive inter-disciplinary research programs.

Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; COMPUTER SCIENCE; EPIDEMIOLOGY; GENOMICS; PROTEOMICS; STATISTICS
Abstract-Résumé: The explosion of genetic information, such as the sequencing of the human genome, has created a demand for highly skilled scientists who have a combination of computational and biological training. The bioinformatics training program meets this need in Canada by training scientists to work in this specialized environment of using biomedical information to improve health research. This interdisciplinary program has been successful in bringing together leading biomedical and informatics scientists from key institutions in British Columbia. During its 6 years of development, the program has established a training platform of sufficient depth to produce scientists with exactly the right combination of skills to exploit the enormous and increasing quantities of biological and health data. Students, undertaking a Masters or PhD in Bioinformatics, are educated through a series of team-taught graduate courses that include ethics training¿an area that is currently topical in health research. The instructors also use progressive teaching approaches, such as problem-based learning. The innovative research rotation portion of the training program engages students in multiple research areas and different methodologies, which adds important skills for resolving major health issues and scientific challenges. Students rotate to academic laboratories and translational research groups at hospitals and industry both in Canada and abroad. By expanding the scope of a student¿s research interactions, each is better equipped with team-based research skills, which are an increasingly valuable asset in solving critical health care issues. A renewed training program will continue to provide excellence in bioinformatics training through innovation and integration of ethics, and will further expand its strong team-based and translational research skills¿all of which set it apart from other bioinformatics programs.

Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHMA; BIOCHEMISTRY; BIOINFORMATICS; BIOPHARMACEUTICAL; CHEMICAL; CHEMICAL BIOLOGY; CHEMISTRY; CYSTIC FIBROSIS; GENETICS; INFECTIOUS DISEASES; PHARMACOLOGY; STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Chemical Biology is a new research field that seeks to identify and to exploit novel small molecules as tools to determine precisely the ways in which specific biochemical and genetic processes contribute to the normal, and in some cases the pathological, behavior of cells and organs in humans and other organisms. We propose to develop our existing program in Chemical Biology to offer trainees not only rigorous training in the discipline of chemical biology itself, but also a meaningful exposure to the challenges and potential of translating basic research findings into clinically useful diagnostic, preventative and  therapeutic approaches to two major types of human disease: respiratory disease, focusing on asthma and cystic fibrosis, and infectious diseases. Graduates of our training program will be equipped not only with outstanding training in the methods and strategies of chemical biology, but also with a heightened awareness of the nature of translational research and of the opportunities (and needs) for them to contribute their skills in this vital research area.
