TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en immunotoxicologie de l'environnement
Keywords-MotsClés: Pollution and protection of the environment, Other research on the environment
Abstract-Résumé: À sa mise en place, la CRCIE visait à : 1) déterminer les relations de cause-effet entre lexposition aux mélanges de contaminants et les effets immunotoxiques, 2) comprendre les mécanismes cellulaires et moléculaires 3) documenter la plus haute sensibilité aux toxiques de certaines périodes critiques du développement. Ces objectifs ont été poursuivis avec succès et en plus des retombées classiques telles lavancement des connaissances (publications, communications, etc.), la formation de personnel hautement qualifié, la CRCIE a aussi servie de moteur principal à des efforts de structuration de la recherche en santé environnementale sur les plans national et international.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Endothelial cell signaling and angiogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Endothelial cells line all of our arteries and veins. This makes them well-positioned strategically to control both blood pressure and the formation of new blood vessels, named angiogenesis. The growth, survival and differentiation of endothelial cells are regulated by specific growth factors, which work through detailed intracellular mechanisms that contribute to the regulation of angiogenesis. Our overall objective is to understand the molecular events that control endothelial cell growth, migration and survival to better understand how to modulate new vessel formation. The modulation of angiogenesis is attractive as a therapeutic target in anti-tumor therapy in hopes of destroying the tumor blood vessels and ultimately starving the tumor or in ischemic cardiovascular diseases to promote new vessel formation in areas deprived of oxygen.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Signal Transduction and Molecular Pharmacology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) constitute the largest family of proteins involved in cell signaling, with > 800 members involved in a wide variety of physiological processes. They represent pharmacological targets for the development of new drugs with potential applications in all clinical fields. However, only a small fraction of their therapeutic potential has been exploited. Drugs have been developed for less than 10% of GPCR and our incomplete understanding of their mechanisms of action limits the development of innovative therapeutic agents. This Chair aims at unravelling the molecular mechanisms of GPCR function with the intention to accelerate drug discovery.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Imaging Physics
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Imaging of the spinal cord with MRI is the only direct way to see the effects of injury or disease, or even to study how the spinal cord works in healthy people.  This research will result in advanced MRI methods for imaging the structure and function of the spinal cord in healthy people or in patients, and will be linked with existing methods to show the brain as well.   For the first time we will be able to study function, or assess injury, in connected systems across the brain, brainstem and spinal cord, in people who can report their sensations.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Membrane Protein Structure and Function
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Many membrane proteins are involved in disease-related states. Approximately 60% of commercially available drugs are targeted towards membrane proteins. Advancements toward understanding the role of these membrane proteins in disease is limited by the difficulty in obtaining structural information on this class of proteins. The focus of my work is the structural study of three membrane proteins involved in diseases including blindness, diabetes, neurodegeneration, and childhood respiratory illnesses. By uncovering the structural features of these proteins, we hope to identify the mechanisms by which they carry out their functions and their role in these disease states.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Patient Safety and Quality Improvement
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: Numerous studies document that medical care often causes harm and that major gaps exist between routine practice and the care expected on the basis of the best available scientific evidence. The Chair in Patient Safety and Quality Improvement will aim to improvw the safety and quality of medical care, so that Canadians can derive maximal benefit from their healthcare system. The Chairs research will improve existing methods for identifying medical injuries, investigate the relatively unstudied field of diagnostic errors, synthesize evidence supporting patient safety and quality improvement interventions, and identify optimal implementation strategies for these often complex interventions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de Recherche du Canada en Neurobiologie Respiratoire
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Le développement des circuits nerveux régissant la commande respiratoire est sensible à lenvironnement. Nos recherches chaire ont démontré que chez le rat, l'exposition à un stress néonatal perturbe le développement neurologique et prédispose l'adulte à des désordres respiratoires tels que l'apnée du sommeil. Un aspect important de cette découverte est que ces effets sont observés chez les rats mâles seulement. Puisque la prévalence de plusieurs troubles respiratoires est plus élevée chez les hommes que chez les femmes, nos travaux viseront à mieux comprendre les mécanismes neurobiologiques expliquant 1) les effets du stress sur l'activité respiratoire, ainsi que 2) le dimorphisme sexuel des conséquences de ce stress.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Health Knowledge Transfer and Uptake
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Clinical research continually leads to new discoveries that can improve health but too often they are poorly implemented in clinical practice with the result that benefits to the health care industry and the health of citizens are delayed or unrealized. Many factors influence uptake of research discoveries into clinical practice. As Canada Research Chair in Health Knowledge Transfer and Uptake, Dr. Jeremy Grimshaw studies factors that influence health care professionals and looks for ways to help them use health knowledge more effectively. Dr. Grimshaw has established himself as an international leader in this field known as implementation research.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Health Equity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: I have developed a unique research program focused on applying evidence-based methods and perspectives of clinical epidemiology to the field of Health Equity.  National and international policymakers have emphasised the pressing need to base health policies and decisions on the best available evidence, and for researchers to work to strengthen the public health evidence base. This proposed programme of work directly meets these needs; without methods to extrapolate existing evidence and set priorities for new evidence, we run the risk of denying efficacious treatment to those who might benefit the most, thus perpetuating global health inequities.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in eHealth Innovation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social change, social processes and social conflicts
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Jadad will study innovative ways to improve health and wellness for all, through the use of information and communication technologies. Using the solid foundation of the Centre for Global eHealth Innovation, he will lead the creation of new services that meet the needs of a rapidly ageing population living with complex chronic diseases. He will also explore how social networking tools level the playing field for other disadvantaged groups in society, including youth and immigrants, and foster collaborative networks of innovators willing to cross geographic, institutional, disciplinary, and multicultural boundaries to accelerate the transformation of the health system, worldwide.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Genetics and Angiogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: My lab seeks to understand the molecular pathways involved in angiogenesis, the process of blood vessel development. Our studies are of fundamental importance given that the regulation of angiogenesis is a major clinical target for the treatment and control of diseases such as cancer, diabetes and stroke. Moreover, angiogenesis is fascinating in its own right, providing an excellent system to study how different cell types migrate, interact and signal to each other. We focus our research on understanding how reciprocal signalling between endothelial cells and neighbouring cell populations generates vascular pattern and stabilizes nascent vessels during embryonic development. We use a genetic approach to identify critical molecules and pathways for these processes. With this approach we have made great strides towards identifying new pathways as key regulators of vascular development, including the plexin-semaphorin, betaPix and sonic hedgehog pathways.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Imaging Science
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The goal of this program is to develop, enhance and better understand new technologies to improve our ability to detect vascular diseases, including stroke and atherosclerosis. This research program is based upon anatomical and functional imaging. Over the next five years, the CRC will extend these efforts so that the program increasingly focuses on cellular function using novel molecular imaging modalities in three target areas: stroke, vascular occlusion by arterial plaques and venous thromboses and dementias caused by vascular lesions in the brain. Imaging molecules represents an innovative approach to detecting, studying and managing vascular disease and stroke in a non-invasive manner, and will facilitate the investigation of the molecular determinants of disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Medicine and Transgenic Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Health
Abstract-Résumé: A diverse interdisciplinary research program was established, combining development of transgenic animals with the application of advanced phenotyping technologies (e.g., microcomputed tomography, metabolomics, bioluminescence) to the study of gene mutations and disease processes at the whole animal level. The research themes have included analyses into the DNA regions controlling gene expression, discovery of a gene that regulates the size of the skeleton, novel ways to interfere with breast cancer metastasis to bone, discovery that the prion protein can alter immune responses, and development of novel mouse cancer models to identify genes and environmental factors that either prevent or promote cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Integrative Vascular Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in Canada and is a major contributor to reduced quality of life and health care expenditure. Hypertension is a major contributing factor causing blood vessel dysfunction and cardiovascular disease. The proposed Canada Research Chair program will discover how novel, specific cellular and molecular defects determine poor arterial function in hypertension. Identification of the molecular basis for exercise and dietary antioxidant influences on blood vessel function will provide transformational, ground-breaking information that is expected to result in identification of unique therapeutic targets to help prevent, treat, and reduced the burden of cardiovascular disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in the Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Disorders
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: This Chair in the genetics of neuropsychiatric disorders contributes to the international investigation of the genetic underpinning of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, with the ultimate goal of developing efficient diagnostic means, novel individual treatments in order to finally impact the quality of life of these patients who make up 3% of the Canadian population and whose treatments cost 13% of the Canadian health budget. The unique DNA bank gathered so far and the follow-up of the affected families will permit to uncover early roots of the diseases and to characterize the shared and specific genetic mechanism of the two disorders.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Behavioural Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The research has focused on two major two themes which involve assessment of the role of the inflammatory immune system: 1. in the degeneration of neurons that occurs in Parkinsons disease (PD), and 2. the development of depressive-like neurochemical and behavioural changes. Dr. Hayley has explored how environmental toxins (e.g. pesticides) promote brain inflammation, causing damage to dopamine neurons (those lost in PD). The research has also indicated that messengers of the immune system (cytokines) cause neurotransmitter changes and symptoms of depression. These findings should have important implications for the development of novel treatments, as well as informing environmental health policies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Parasitology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Led by Dr. Kain, this unique translational research program assembles a team of multi-institutional, trans-disciplinary Canadian and international investigators with complementary expertise in the fields of infectious diseases, genetics, immunology, molecular biology, and biochemistry.  It focuses on: (i) elucidating the molecular basis for adverse outcomes in life-threatening infectious diseases and translating this knowledge into novel therapeutic interventions; and (ii) the discovery of innovative diagnostics, host biomarkers, and molecular surveillance strategies aimed at improving the diagnosis and management of emerging infectious disease threats, especially those associated with global travel, migration, and blood safety.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Structural Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Proteins are essential parts of organisms that participate in all cellular processes. Dr. Pai uses biochemical and structural methods to determine their three-dimensional structures to better understand their functions. He combines this with an unusually broad palette of techniques, ranging from chemistry to molecular biology and laser physics. His work addresses the molecular evolution of enzyme specificity and antibody maturation, the transport of ions across cell membranes and the use of antibodies in trapping folding intermediates and in the design of new vaccines. The research also addresses immune responses to viral infections, cardiovascular and heart disease and aging, and targets prion diseases like BSE. The laboratory also participates in technologically advanced experiments to observe chemical reactions as they progress in protein crystals.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular & Cellular Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Gene regulation is fundamental to cellular differentiation in mammalian development and cellular homeostasis. Studies in other laboratories have shown that the failure to properly activate or silence genes contributes to numerous human diseases, including cancer. Regulation of gene activity is being studied extensively at the level of DNA:protein interactions, which includes how regulatory molecules interact with a genes promoter, and how changes in chromatin structure through epigenetic marks on both histones and DNA contribute to the expression or silencing of specific genetic loci. Building on his earlier work applying imaging methods to address regulation at these levels, Dr. Bazett-Jones's current effort is to address how compartmentalisation of function within the cell nucleus also contributes to gene regulation. Although sub-nuclear organisation is much less studied, his hypothesis is that it is equally important as a regulatory mechanism.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in PET Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Positron emission tomography (PET) provides images of the entire human brain at all depths, offering many different measures of brain function. This project will significantly advance the raw data processing methodology for a newly installed high resolution PET scanner, thus enhancing the scanners utility for researchers studying brain function and disease. Recent developments indicate that the computationally intensive image reconstruction methods used on the acquired PET data have a very significant impact on PETs image quality, so this project will advance the reconstruction, modelling and analysis of PET data, to deliver enhanced functional information for use by clinical researchers.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Research Chair in Genetic Epidemiology of Complex Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Asthma is a chronic disease of the lungs and airways and affects as many as 300 million people in the world, and the rates of asthma are increasing worldwide as communities adopt western lifestyles and become urbanized.  Asthma can be diagnosed at any point in a persons life, during childhood, puberty, pregnancy, or even late adulthood.  This proposal will focus on the genetic and environmental determinants of asthma in early life, and the contributions that gender, genetics and environment make in the development of asthma.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Pain and Child Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic pain is a serious health problem that affects as many as 20% of children and is associated with significant disability and frequent use of health care services. The proposed research program will investigate the role of developmental, psychological, and social factors involved in pediatric pain. The research will advance the current biopsychosocial understanding of pediatric pain and provide the basis for new management approaches for children in pain. Effective assessment and management of pediatric pain are critical in preventing the development of pain and disability in children and reducing unnecessary burden on the health care system.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Clinical Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Pharmaceutical products, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Since chronic neurological diseases exert an immense social and economic impact on Canadian society, there is a crucial need for effective new drugs to treat devastating disorders such as Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy.  Although there are drugs currently available for these disorders, these conventional agents provide only symptomatic improvement and are not truly "curative".  Dr. Weaver is using state of the art computer design techniques to design and develop new drugs for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy.  These new drugs are designed to be truly curative disease-altering agents that will halt the progression of these devastating diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chair in Chemical Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Manufacturing and processing techniques
Abstract-Résumé: Carbohydrates play key roles in biological systems in mediating the interactions between cells and their environment.  My research has centred on understanding and exploiting the enzymes that attach these sugars to the cell surfaces, as well as those that remove them in order to both engineer them to make different sugars as well as to design molecules that control their activities  Using high-throughput approaches we shall evolve the activities of these enzymes to make the products we want. We shall also develop methods for specifically detecting these enzymes within highly complex mixtures.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Physiology of visual perception
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: How does brain activity underlie our conscious experiences?  Although neuroscience has made great strides in explaining how information is represented in brain areas such asthe visual cortex, little is known how this neuronal activity is used by the rest ofthe brain to generate representations of the world around us.  My research applieselectrophysiological, behavioral and computational approaches to reveal how neuronalactivity in visual cortex is linked to perceptions and behavior. Our results will helpus understand the rules neurons use to encode information, which is critical forunderstanding how the brain underlies our mental life and the basis of diseases thataffect mental health.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neurocognition of Language
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Education, training, recurrent education and retraining
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Steinhauers multidisciplinary research programs use cutting-edge electrophysiological and imaging techniques to uncover how the human brain learns and processes language in real-time. Studies comparing brain activation of early and late language learners at various stages of proficiency will reveal how the brain adjusts its processing mechanisms depending on age, practice and training environment. Another program investigates the brain systems underlying speech and music processing in musicians, non-musicians, and patients with focal brain lesions. One long-term goal of Dr. Steinhauers research is to develop realistic models of language cognition that are relevant not only to linguists and neuroscientists, but also to teachers, stakeholders in educational policy, and clinicians dealing with language disorders.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Oncology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Although breast cancer is one of the leading killers of Canadian women, the molecular basis for the events involved in breast cancer initiation and progression remain poorly understood. To address this important problem, we will employ state of the art transgenic mouse models and conditional knock-out models to assess the relative contribution of particular signaling molecules to each stage of breast cancer progression.  Given the prevalence of breast cancer in human populations, our research program will provide important insight into molecular basis of these poorly understood human diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cell Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Over the past decades, thousands of cellular components and corresponding molecular interactions have been identified.  We need now to integrate this hugely complex information.  Our laboratory addresses this complexity at two levels: 1) We study the nature and regulation of large complexes where the activity of many proteins must be coordinated to transmit signals from the cell surface to the nucleus.  2) Cell behavior has mostly been studied in culture cells.  We have now developed methods to study cell migration within whole tissues.  Using this approach, we investigate the fundamental question of how tissues form during embryonic development.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Anesthesia: From Molecular Mechanisms to Patient Safety
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: General anesthesia is one of the greatest medical discoveries, but we do not yet understand how anesthetics alter brain function. Our goal is to determine how anesthetics disrupt memory and cause amnesia. Some patients who seem to be unconscious experience insufficient amnesia and may recall traumatic surgical events. Others suffer from persistent memory impairment for weeks after anesthesia. We discovered that anesthetics enhance inhibitory signals in a structure that is critically involved in memory. We will determine how such inhibitory signals modify memory and develop a mouse model for memory impairment after anesthesia, so that new treatments can be developed.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuropsychiatry
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Patients with schizophrenia and depression suffer from emotional abnormalities that are associated with changes in a particular brain region, the prefrontal cortex. How prefrontal cortical abnormalities are modulated by different metabolites like glutamate/glutamine and GABA remains unclear.  By combining different functional imaging techniques (fMRI, Magnetoresonancespectroscopy/MRS) in a novel way, the goal is to investigate the relationship between prefrontal neural activity and its glutamate- and gaba-ergic modulation by drugs like ketamine and lorazepam in depressive and schizophrenic patients. This will allow the direct link of emotional symptoms and metabolic prefrontal modulation which may foster the development of symptom-oriented treatment strategies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Genome Bioinformatics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Software development
Abstract-Résumé: The human genome project has accelerated the discovery of mutations that cause human diseases. Many mutations do not alter protein sequences, but instead modulate gene regulation. Chromosomal rearrangements that alter gene copy number or disrupt genes affect gene expression or structure. Effective and accurate approaches are needed to determine chromosomal genotypes and interpret the significance of genetic variants that cause diseases. The applicant has pioneered methods to understand sequence variation and methods to produce DNA probes for precise diagnosis of chromosome abnormalities. These will be used to predict and determine clinical impacts of mutations in the genome and transcriptome.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Global Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The aim of this research programme is to improve the lives of those infected and affected by HIV/AIDS and inform policy at an international level to continue scale-up of antiretroviral treatment.   My academic objective is to inform the development of HIV/AIDS treatment and prevention to populations that have historically been under-serviced. My overall goal is to assess the effectiveness of increased antiretroviral treatment as a strategy of reducing patient infectiousness and thus potentially preventing new infections. To do so, I intend to examine two initiatives for which I have led research and informed policy : (1) assess whether rapid scale-up of treatment reduces population incidence of new sexual HIV infections through reduced referent partner HIV-1 RNA, and; (2) the success of treatment options for populations residing in resource-poor settings where there may be an under-service of laboratory abilities and health care staff. My research will initially focus on the Northeastern Ugandan context through a large scale-up of services to internally displaced persons (IDPs).

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Gastrointestinal Cell Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Colon cancer is the third most common cancer in Canada. How dietary calcium supplementation works to reduce colon cancer and diminish recurrence of adenoma is uncertain.  Our research is focused on how stimulating the intestinal extracellular calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR) triggers the production of molecules which inhibit the signaling of genes which cause colon cancer.  In the normal intestine, when calcium triggers production of these molecules, not only does the gut become healthier, but recovery from damage is accelerated.  Our work provides a molecular understanding of calciums chemoprevention and suggests new drug targets to reduce adenoma and repair the intestine.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cardiovascular Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: The focus of Dr. Heximer's  work is to characterize the integration of heart and blood vessel function during normal blood pressure regulation. Specifically, Dr. Heximer studies the molecular pathways used by vascular and heart cells to interpret physiologic signals initiating from the central nervous system and kidneys. In hypertensive patients  it is known that signaling through many of these same pathways is augmented. Accordingly, Dr. Heximer will investigate the molecular mechanisms by which these communication pathways are attenuated to inform novel strategies to prevent and control of hypertension at the level of the affected tissues.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cancer Care Evaluation
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The goal of Dr. Groomes research is to improve cancer outcomes through the study of the cancer care delivered to whole populations of cancer patients. She describes how treatment practice varies geographically and whether those variations are associated with differences in cancer cure rates. She seeks to understand why some patients are diagnosed later than others with a view to identifying ways that early diagnoses can be more common. She investigates the quality of cancer care delivery by looking in detail at treatment delivery. Her research program focuses on the head and neck cancers and prostate cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Imaging Modalities to Assist with Guiding Therapy and the Evaluation of Patients with Heart Failure (IMAGE-HF)
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; CARDIAC IMAGING; CLINICAL EVALUATION; HEART FAILURE; IMAGE TECHNOLOGY STANDARDIZATION; IMAGING BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Medical imaging is one of the fastest growing sectors in health care. Marked increases in utilization underscore the need to ensure imaging technology is developed and used effectively. However, evaluation of the clinical and economic impact lags behind the pace of the technology development. Heart failure represents the final common pathway for most forms of heart disease. Despite advances in therapy, morbidity and mortality for heart failure remain high. There is a need to identify imaging approaches that have a positive impact on therapy decisions, patient outcomes and costs. As well as a need for standard methods to evaluate new and emerging techniques to better test their potential in a clinical management setting. OBJECTIVES 1) determine the impact of current and emerging imaging strategies on relevant clinical outcomes and decision making in patients with heart failure; 2) establish standard quality assurance (QA) measures and central databases in order to achieve reliable outcome driven research; 3) apply this as a platform for evaluation of new and emerging imaging techniques in heart failure. The primary recruitment goal will be 2522 patients presenting with symptoms of heart failure. IMAGE-HF applies a novel approach with direct integration into clinical practice, enabling evaluation of strategies and knowledge translation into practice, policy and identification of key targets for future randomized clinical trials. The IMAGE-HF QA program will yield reliable data in a ground breaking new approach to standardization. The scope of the projects in this proposal is beyond the capability of any individual centre. The IMAGE-HF team will build capacity and conceptual bridges through interaction of investigators, trainees and staff via the collaborative projects, the QA process and knowledge translation initiatives. The IMAGE-HF project will yield data that can ultimately be directed towards improved patient care, management and outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR Team in Thoracic Imaging Network of Canada
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY; COPD; CORONARY VASCULAR DISEASE; EMPHYSEMA; IMAGE ANALYSIS; MRI
Abstract-Résumé: Smoking related lung disease is a serious medical condition in Canada.  While lung cancer related to tobacco smoking is still the leading cause of cancer death in Canadians, the greatest source of death and disability stems from heart disease and complications of the lung condition known as COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease).  COPD is the only major illness for which the mortality rate is increasing worldwide.  Over one million Canadians have COPD and every year 60,000 are hospitalized for major lung or heart problems and 10,000 die from their disease. To put this in context, lung and heart side-effects to COPD are the single greatest source of patient admissions from emergency departments in the province of British Columbia.  While there have been dramatic advances in the diagnosis, monitoring and treatment of heart disease there is a lack of new tools for the early diagnosis and treatment of COPD.  Our collective vision is to develop and implement imaging strategies that will accelerate the understanding and treatment of lung and heart disease caused by smoking and to provide better methods to test new treatments. We will realize this vision through a research program that combines established and cutting edge imaging tools.  While many of these imaging tools are well established in Canadian medical institutions standard imaging applications that help understand smoking related diseases are not well used.  Finally, some of the approaches we will develop and implement are still in the development phase but hold great potential for the future.  Our team consists of basic research scientists (providing discoveries), clinician-scientists (providing the framework of translation), epidemiologists and outcome scientists (providing observations about the burden & progression of disease), who will work together to stimulate new opportunities for advances in basic and clinical investigations.

ResearchClassEN: STROKE, HEART FAILURE; MULTIPLE DISEASE RELEVANCE
ClasseRechercheFR: APOPLEXIE, INSUFFISANCE CARDIAQUE; RECHERCHES SE RAPPORTANT A PLUSIEURS MALADIES
TitreApplicationTitle: CIHR/HSFC Team in Synchrotron Medical Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: HARD X-RAY; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; METAL METABOLISM; STEM  CELL THERAPY; STROKE; SYNCHROTRON IMAGING
Abstract-Résumé: The CIHR Team in Synchrotron Medical Imaging will build on existing strengths in biomedical imaging at the Canadian Light Source (Saskatoon, Canada). The team links world-class experts in synchrotron imaging and magnetic resonance imaging to stroke researchers and clinicians. These researchers will work together to develop new ways to visualize and treat brain injury from stroke.  Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability for Canadians. Brain injury from a stroke can take several days to months to develop. Currently, there are no therapeutic approaches that address this treatment window. In addition, there are several other types of insults (cardiac arrest, hypoxia, and trauma) that result in similar brain injury cascades. Developing a comprehensive understanding of the damage that occurs post-injury will provide an opportunity to assess the impact of treatments that arrest and reverse brain damage.   The CIHR Team in Synchrotron Medical Imaging will: - Apply advanced imaging techniques to develop an understanding of how different therapies, including stem cell treatments, can be applied or improved; - Use new technology to visualize brain damage as it happens; - Assess imaging techniques that use endogenous biomarkers to map brain damage, building the basis for non-invasive clinical applications; - Compare new technologies for non-invasive pre-stroke preventative screening; - Evaluate the effect of neuroprotective treatments in animal models; and  - Work towards the development of next generation computed tomography technology.

TitreApplicationTitle: A portable wireless near infrared spectroscopy system combined with electroencephalography for bedside monitoring of stroke and cardiac patients.
Keywords-MotsClés: ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHY; EPILEPSY; INTRAOPERATIVE CARDIAC MONITORING; NEAR INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY; REHABILITATION; STROKE
Abstract-Résumé: Stroke and epilepsy are the two most common neurological problems. Because it is so prevalent, stroke is identified as the most common cause of epilepsy in adult and infant population and the second most common cause of dementia in adults. For these neurological conditions, neuroimaging continues to be a mainstay of diagnosis, management, and investigation. Near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), a novel technique, which can non-invasively monitor the rapid changes of regional cerebral volume and tissue oxygenation (as seen during stroke or seizures), may be of great value in the understanding, evaluation and treatment of these conditions. Preliminary studies using relatively short NIRS recordings and a limited number of optodes have shown their clinical potential in distinct situations. Long-term NIRS monitoring however remains difficult with existing commercial devices being too bulky and/or too heavy for long-term measurements in epilepsy, stroke or intensive care units. Over the last few years, we have established a multidisciplinary collaborative task force to evaluate, design and build dual imaging NIRS-videoEEG system for real-time monitoring. Building on work already started, we propose in this research program to implement an ultra-lightweight ultra low-power wireless combined multichannel NIRS-videoEEG intended for long-term monitoring applications. Once the system completed, prototypes will be prepared and validation exploiting its capacity will be performed. Of particular interest in clinical testing, four projects are proposed for bedside long-term monitoring of both NIRS and EEG: 1) monitoring in a stroke unit; 2) monitoring of aphasic patients in a rehabilitation unit; 3) monitoring during cardiac intraoperative procedures; and 4) monitoring in at risk infants. International collaborations are undertaken to facilitate both the system implementation and its clinical evaluation.

ProgramNameEN: Michael Smith New Investigator Award - Schizophrenia
NomDuProgrammeFR: Bourse nouveau chercheur Michael Smith - schizophrenie
TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of oligodendrocyte abnormalities in schizophrenia
Keywords-MotsClés: IMMUNOCYTOCHEMISTRY; MYELIN; NMR; OLIGODENDROCYTE; POST-MORTEM; SCHIZOPHRENIA
Abstract-Résumé: Recent evidence suggests that the symptoms of schizophrenia may arise from dysfunction of the nerve fibres that connect different brain regions together. However, exactly how this might occur at the microscopic level is not clear. Oligodendrocytes are brain cells that produce a fatty insulating substance called myelin, which surrounds nerve fibres and speeds up the transmission of nerve impulses between brain regions. We suggest that the number of oligodendrocytes is lower in individuals with schizophrenia then in healthy people. We believe that this may result from genetic or environmental events that take place during brain development. Having fewer oligodendrocytes would lead to lower levels of myelin surrounding nerve fibres and accordingly faulty transmission of nerve impulses between brain regions. In this study we intend to use post-mortem samples to compare the number of oligodendrocyte cells in the brains of individuals with schizophrenia against that in healthy subjects. We will also measure levels of proteins and fats found in myelin to test if less myelin is present in individuals with schizophrenia. We will then compare the levels of N-acetylaspartate, a molecule that is an indicator of how well axons are working, between the two groups. Finally, we plan to test if antipsychotic drugs are causing changes in the schizophrenia samples by giving these drugs to rats. Identifying abnormalities in nerve fibre connections could offer clues as to the causes of schizophrenia and may provide us with targets for new drugs.

NomDuComitéFR: Subvention de fonctionnement : Histoire de la médecine
TitreApplicationTitle: Généalogie des maladies nerveuses et dépressives au Québec, 1860-1920: entre pratiques médicales et profanes
Keywords-MotsClés: 1860-1920; DEPRESSION; HISTOIRE; MEDECINE; NEURASTHENIE ET TROUBLES SERVEUX; PSYCHIATRIE; THERAPEUTIQUE
Abstract-Résumé: La depression apparait de plus en plus, chez les experts, les medias et le public, comme une maladie qu¿on peut  controler ou guerir grace a un traitement pharmacotherapeutique approprie. Toutefois, au-dela d¿un certain optimiste therapeutique, la forte augmentation de sa prevalence et l¿incapacite rattachee a cette maladie generent, depuis quelques annees, des discours epidemiologiques assez alarmistes. Or la tendance a s¿inquieter de la prevalence grandissante des troubles «nerveux» au sein de la population ne date pas d¿hier. Deja la fin du 19e siecle, la prevalence de la neurasthenie, de «la prostration nerveuse» et autres maladies nerveuses etait vue comme ayant atteint des sommets jusque la inegales en Amerique du Nord et en Europe. Ce projet a pour objectif de cerner l¿histoire des «nervosites d¿adaptation», «problemes de nerfs», neurasthenie et petites nevroses au tournant du 19-20 siecle au Quebec, de maniere a faire une genealogie de la depression telle qu¿on la connait a l¿heure actuelle. Bien que l¿histoire de la psychiatrie dans le monde occidental ait donne lieu a des ouvrages magistraux, notamment depuis les annees 1970, c¿est essentiellement sous l¿angle de l¿institutionnalisation de ce champ et de cette profession que la question des «nerfs» a ete traitee. Quant a l¿hysterie, la melancolie et la neurasthenie, elles ont inspire de nombreuses analyses litteraires des representations de la maladie. Toutefois, entre une histoire intellectuelle des idees medicales et scientifiques de la maladie mentale et une histoire culturelle des representations de celle-ci a travers les romans d¿epoque, peu de place a veritablement ete consacree aux pratiques concretes de gestion therapeutique de ces problemes si prevalents en medecine au tournant du siecle. En empruntant une demarche historique d¿analyse des journaux medicaux et de la presse populaire au Quebec entre 1860 et 1920, cette recherche contribuera a combler cette lacune.

DomainesScientifiquesFR: DIMENSIONS SOCIALES ET CULTURELLES DE LA SANTÉ
ResearchClassEN: SOCIETAL & CULTURAL DIMENSIONS OF HEALTH; HEALTH CARE DELIVERY
ClasseRechercheFR: DIMENSIONS SOCIALES ET CULTURELLES DE LA SANTÉ; DISTRIBUTION DES SOINS DE LA SANTE
TitreApplicationTitle: Interpreting Remote Medicine and Health Care in Pre-Confederation Newfoundland as "Ecosystem"
Keywords-MotsClés: CONTENT ANALYSIS; GROUNDED THEORY; HEALTH CARE DELIVERY; HOSPITALS HISTORY; PUBLIC HEALTH; REMOTE MEDICINE
Abstract-Résumé: This research examines the history of remote medicine in Newfoundland and Labrador (NL).  By understanding areas of NL as regions, our study holds promise for work on other jurisdictions, for health researchers and historians alike are increasingly calling for study of health care delivery in the North and other rural regions globally.  Issues in Canada today foucs on scope of practice-primary care (nurse practitioners; physician assistants; midwives; and supply of providers), access to care and to diagnostic technology-and on public vs private funding.  All have earlier counterparts in NL, where studies have portrayed health care and its delivery in the pre-confederation era as inadequate to non-existent compared with that after NL joined Canada in 1949.  We propose not only to examine these claims for validity but more importantly, to postulate an alternative concept that a relatively effective"ecosystem"of health care existed, suitable to the place and its population in the 1930s and 1940s.  As historians, we will primarily analyze documents in hospitals and archives to understand the nature of health care before modernizaion -with clear implications for condisering what is enduring and what may have been lost in the process.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Alan Edwards - Canada Research Chair in Pain Control
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Neuropathic pain syndromes occur when nerves are damaged by trauma, toxins, and other insults.  This kind of pain is especially difficult to treat because it responds poorly or not at all to traditional analgesic drugs like aspirin and morphine.  Professor Bennett's research program is focused on the neuropathic pain conditions caused by chemotherapeutic drugs that are used to combat cancer and a post-traumatic condition known as Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type-I (formerly Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy, RSD).  Working with animal models of these two conditions, he has made new discoveries about the causes of the pain and about several new drugs that may be able to treat and prevent the pain.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Genetic Diversity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: A diverse antibody repertoire is crucial to neutralize the many different antigens to which a vertebrate is exposed during its lifetime. This diversity is achieved by genetic alterations of the immunoglobulin genes in B cells. The mechanisms behind diversification depend on the coordinated action of several enzymes which paradoxically include some that would normally avoid those alterations. We investigate how these enzymes are regulated and coordinated to potentiate antibody diversification by avoiding mutation repair. Understanding these mechanisms can provide insight into the molecular causes of human immunodeficiencies and B-cell lymphomas that are caused by the abnormal functioning of these processes.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Drug Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Pharmaceutical products, Health
Abstract-Résumé: After cancer patients undergo chemotherapy or when individuals suffer a stroke or a heart attack, their heart muscle or brain tissue undergoes oxygen free radical damage as a result of iron being released from the tissues. Chelation, or binding, of this iron in the tissues by small molecule iron chelating drugs has the potential to prevent this irreversible free radical tissue damage. Dr. Hasinoffs research program aims to synthesize new drugs for use in the prevention of oxygen free radical tissue damage, thus, improving the quality of life when these medical conditions occur.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Immune Regulation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Over 30 percent of  Canadians are affected by asthma, hayfever or food allergies, one of the highest incidences in the world. These are the most common human immune diseases. CRC Chairholder Kent HayGlass is a leading researcher in the field of immune regulation who has made important discoveries regarding the biological roles of cytokines and chemokines. Understanding differential production of these immunological hormones that control development, activation and inhibition of immunity, will explain why immune activation in some people promotes protective immunity and clinical unresponsiveness to allergens while in others it leads to maladaptive immune regulation and a spectrum of allergic diseases.

Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Assisted reproductive technologies have been successful in the treatment of some forms of human infertility; however, a significant fraction of couples fail to successfully conceive. Many of these failures are due to delayed or abnormal embryo development. Dr. Jurisicova will investigate  three candidate maternal lethal effect genes which have been linked to human infertility. She will identify sequence mutations that may be associated with developmental defects observed in the embryos of patients with repeated IVF failure. Furthermore, she will investigate the biological role of these genes in animal models, which could be used to devise clinically useful rescue approaches.

Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: An iterative technology assessment framework describes this translational, multidisciplinary research in musculoskeletal health through a series of related projects:  systematic review of existing evidence, decision analytic modelling using value of information analysis techniques to quantify uncertainty and identify gaps in knowledge, pragmatic clinical trials to fill knowledge gaps and generate new primary evidence, and updating prior knowledge.   This research is at the forefront of current trends towards data requirements on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of health interventions in routine practice settings.  The results will inform evidence-based policy decisions about optimal treatment and translate into evidence-based practice to improve quality and efficiency of bone and joint care of Canadians.

Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Dr David Thomas is the recipient of the Tier I Canada Research Chair in Molecular Genetics.His group does research on a class of degenerative disease termed "protein trafficking diseases" of which cystic fibrosis is an example. In these diseases mutant but otherwise functional proteins are localized incorrectly in the cell. His research is on the mechanisms that result in this mislocalization of mutant proteins and in the development of therapies to correct them.

Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The focus of this CRC is thrombosis (blood clotting). Heart attacks and strokes are the number one cause of death and disability in Canada.  Most heart attacks and strokes are triggered by blood clots that form on top of ruptured atherosclerotic plaques in heart or brain arteries and block blood flow.  Thrombosis at these sites reflects perturbation of the balance between clot formation and clot breakdown.  The overall goal of this CRC is to understand the complex genetic and biochemical events that trigger thrombosis and to use this information to develop new strategies for disease prevention and to identify novel targets for drug intervention.

Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Agriculture
Abstract-Résumé: The Canada Research Chair in Infectious Bacterial Diseases will support research to further understand  the complex interactions that occur between bacterial pathogens and their hosts during the disease process, with particular emphasis on diseases caused by bacterial pathogens of importance to both human and animal health. Research will focus on identification and characterisation of bacterial as well as host genes that are expressed during infection in different animal or cell culture models.Research will combine the use of RNA capture methods, analysis of gene transcription in vivo,  molecular genetics, microbiology, and immunology.This research may identify new bacterial targets or host defences mechanisms and lead to the development of vaccines or novel therapies to prevent and control infectious diseases caused by bacterial pathogens.

Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The transfer of signals within cells is essential for their ability to grow, to carry out specific functions or to survive. The underlying mechanisms have been surprisingly well conserved among multicellular organisms and thus their study is greatly facilitated by using less complex models such as Drosophila fruit flies. This research program seeks to use Drosophila to characterize novel proteins involved in signal transfer mechanisms closely linked to cancer. Moreover, it proposes to exploit flies to study leukemia-causing oncogenes. This innovative proposal will likely identify novel anti-cancer targets or lead the way to unexplored avenues in our quest against cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Terry Fox Foundation Strategic Health Research Training Program in Cancer Research at CIHR
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATION SKILLS; PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING; PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT; TRANSDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer research trainees currently have excellent training in their specific research area.  The Cancer Research Training Program (CRTP) complements this traditional training by (1) exposing trainees and their colleagues to a broad spectrum of cancer issues and research challenges, transdisciplinary perspectives, and professinal skills (2) providing real-world experiences for trainees to develop their professional skills and practice overcoming cancer research challenges in transcisciplnary teams, and (3) connecting trainees with a network of cancer researchers and cancer care professionals.  The program recruits and funds outstanding trainees (postdoctoral fellows, graduate, medical and other health professional students) undertaking cancer research.  The learning sessions are attended by many 'external participants' who benefit from CRTP while diversifying the perspectives in discussions.  CRTP has become extremely valuable in Nova Scotia.  In the next phase, CRTP will develop the infrastructure to extend its benefits to, and gain the expertise from, all four Atlantic Provinces.  Furthermore, CRTP will implement several new and innovative training strategies that promote learning and practical experience in important professional and team skills such as grant-writing and working with industry.  Consequently, trainees throughout Atlantic Canada will be better prepared to apply their research in the 'bigger picture', work together with other cancer researchers, health professionals, industry, and policy makers, and have maximum impact on cancer care across Canada.

Abstract-Résumé: Excellence in Radiation Research for the 21st Century (EIRR21) training program will continue to train the next generation of leaders in trans-disciplinary radiation research, for the benefit of Canadian cancer patients.  Radiation is a highly effective targeted treatment, utilized for half of all cancer patients, yet there remains opportunities to further increase cure, and reduce toxicity.  To achieve this objective, we need future leaders in radiation research who will easily traverse the many disciplines of science, ranging from basic molecular biology of DNA damage and repair, in vitro and in vivo cancer biology, imaging science, clinical physics, translational research using human bio-specimens, bio-informatic analyses and modeling of genomic and proteomic data, radiation clinical trials, and health outcome research.  This is the focus of the EIRR21 training program.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Terry Fox Foundation Strategic Health Research Training Program in Molecular Pathology of Cancer at CIHR
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICIAN-SCIENTISTS; MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY; ONCOLOGY; PATHOLOGY; TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: Recent advances in our knowledge of the basic mechanisms of cellular function at the molecular level have revolutionized our diagnosis and treatment of human disease, especially in the area of cancer.  Future treatment of cancer will increasingly depend on knowing the specific molecular changes that occur in an individual's cancer tissue, since therapeutic agents will increasingly be targeted to these changes. Pathologists, who are medical doctors with special expertise in laboratory medicine will play critical roles in effecting this transition into the era of molecular medicine.  This requires significant changes in our current teaching practices in this discipline and requires increasing exposure of trainees to molecular pathology.  However, there is presently an acute shortage of clinical pathologists with molecular biology expertise throughout Canada and North America.  This training program is aimed at producing 20-30 such individuals during the next six years with the intention that they form the core of the next generation leaders in pathology, to re-invigorate this medical specialty back to its traditional role as a leader in medical research and innovation.

Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CANCER CONTROL; DRUG DEVELOPMENT FELLOWSHIPS; GRADUATE STUDENTS; POST DOCTORAL FELLOWS; POST MD-FELLOWS; TRAINING PROGRAM; TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer-related deaths in North America now exceed those from coronary heart disease and stroke. Thus, there is increasing public pressure to accelerate the application of advances made in the understanding of the basic science of cancer to disease prevention, diagnosis and therapy.  This transition requires teams of collaborative researchers with a broad understanding of the field of cancer control who can comprehend, and effectively address, the molecular, clinical, social, and economic implications of the disease.  The Queen's University Transdisciplinary Training Program in Cancer Research is a successful program providing future investigators with state-of-the-art knowledge in diverse fields and a broad understanding of the cancer problem.  The Program provides a unique opportunity for established researchers in diverse disciplines to cooperate in the training of future leaders in Canadian cancer research. The Program is designed to provide high school, undergraduate, and graduate students,  Post-PhD and Post-MD fellows with an appreciation of the breadth of cancer research and improve their ability to collaborate effectively with experts in other disciplines.  Our renewal builds on our existing successful program in order to expand its reach.   Our ultimate goal is to translate the advances made in research into clinical applications and health care policies that reduce the societal burden of cancer.  Key to our Program's success has been its ability to attract trainees at all stages of their research career and offer them stage appropriate courses and research opportunities to expand their understanding of a multidisciplinary approach to research on cancer control.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health care utilization by centenarians in Ontario: The impact of formal and informal care on advanced aging, health, and well-being
Keywords-MotsClés: CENTENARIAN; FUNCTIONAL ABILITY; HEALTH STATUS; INFORMAL CAREGIVING; RESIDENT ASSESSMENT INSTRUMENT - HOME CARE (RAI-HC); THE RESIDENT ASSESSMENT INSTRUMENT 2.0 (RAI 2.0)
Abstract-Résumé: The growing population of centenarians represent a heterogeneous cohort that is understudied in Canadian literature.  The proposed PhD research and thesis will investigate health care system utilization of centenarians living Ontario.  Under the direct supervision of Dr. John Hirdes, Provincial level data from the Resident Assessment Instrument 2.0 (RAI 2.0) used in Ontario Complex Continuing Care Hospitals and data from the Resident Assessment Instrument - Home Care (RAI-HC) used in Ontario Community Care Access Centers will be assessed.  Data related to care service utilization, indicators of physical and mental health, as well as, levels of quality of life will be analyzed.   Conclusions of this study will assist in effective funding allocation through increased understanding of how centenarians access and use the health care system.  Recommendations will be made to ensure health care services will be effectively targeted to meet the needs of the oldest old and help to empower them.  The care provided by informal caregivers reduces the demands on the health care system and can prevent or delay institutionalization or the need for more formal paid caregiving services.  In my previous research caregivers of centenarians tended to be older and in poorer health.  By building upon previous findings and investigating the determinants of centenarian caregiver health status, health care providers and policymakers will better understand how they affect institutionalization of care recipients.  With increased knowledge in this area, it may be possible to decrease the levels of caregiver burden and depression, as well as increase quality of life.  In turn, if resources are properly directed to meet the actual needs of burdened caregivers, institutionalization can be delayed or avoided completely, and the burdens of the aging society on the health care system may be partially alleviated.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude de la connectivité inter-hémisphérique dans l'autisme par le paradigme de Poffenberger.
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTISME; COGNITION; CONNECTIVITE INTER-HEMISPHERIQUE; CORPS CALLEUX; DTI; IRMF; POFFENBERGER
Abstract-Résumé: Ce projet vise a etudier les connections entre les deux hemispheres du cerveau des personnes autistes. On sait que le corps calleux, qui est une structure composee de fibres de matiere blanche qui assurent la communication entre l'hemisphere gauche et droit du cerveau, serait reduit chez les autistes. Toutefois, on ignore si cela a un effet sur la fonction de ces fibres ou sur des aspects comportementaux. Des reductions microstructurales observees au niveau du corps calleux pourraient avoir un effet sur la vitesse de transfert de l'information entre les hemispheres. Le but de ce projet est de mesurer directement le temps de transfert de l'information par le corps calleux chez des autistes et des non-autistes a l'aide de la tache visuo-motrice de Poffenberger pour voir s'il differe entre les deux groupes. On verifiera ensuite si cette mesure comportementale est correlee aux proprietes microstructurales du corps calleux mesurees sur des donnees d'imagerie cerebrale (l'imagerie du tenseur de diffusion, ou DTI) acquises pour chaque participant. Une deuxieme etape de ce projet sera de faire passer la tache de Poffenberger aux memes participants mais en imagerie par resonnance magnetique fonctionnelle (IRMf) afin d'identifier si la localisation et l'intensite des activations cerebrales associees a cette tache sont les memes pour les autistes et pour les controles et donc de savoir quel est l'effet fonctionnel des differences anatomiques dans le corps calleux et si elles necessitent une certaine reorganisation cerebrale. Les resultats obtenus permettront de mieux definir les modeles de connectivite cerebrales dans l'autisme. Une meilleure description des differences neuro-anatomique pourra eventuellement servir comme marqueur diagnostique. De plus, si le transfert entre les deux hemispheres du cerveau est plus lent chez les autistes, cela pourra contribuer a expliquer les ralentissements moteurs particuliers a l'autisme.

TitreApplicationTitle: Psychosocial predictors of acute rejection in adult transplant recipients
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC STRESS; COPING; HEALTH PSYCHOLOGY; IMMUNOLOGY; PSYCHOBIOLOGY; TRANSPLANT
Abstract-Résumé: Kidney transplant is the only successful treatment for patients with kidney failure, with a high patient survival rate and slightly lower transplanted organ survival rate. Across Canada, 2963 people were on the waitlist for a kidney transplant in December 2007. Kidney donation is becoming an increasingly scarce resource, and patients may wait years for a donor. This is due in part to the increasing number of re-transplants - more and more people are requiring a second, third or even fourth kidney transplant. After a kidney transplant, the patient's immune system recognizes the new kidney as foreign, and tries to reject it. To prevent this from happening, patients take medication for the rest of their lives, but this is not always entirely effective. The patient's body can still try many times to reject the new kidney and over time, there might be permanent damage to the transplanted kidney, and the patient might need a new transplant. It's not always clear why organs are rejected, and it could be that psychological factors such as anxiety and depression play a role.  At the moment, there is very little research which studies the effects of a patient's psychological functioning on the likelihood of the transplanted kidney being rejected. It could be that episodes of rejection are influenced by a patient's psychological functioning before or after surgery. If we can identify psychological factors contributing to re-transplant, interventions can be designed to try and prevent organ rejection. The goal of this research is to study the relationship between psychological variables and rejection for kidney transplant recipients. Psychological variables of interest are perceived stress, anxiety, depression, social support, and coping. This unique study will determine the impact of various psychological factors on kidney graft rejection via biological pathways, and is therefore a valuable first step in identifying relevant psychological variables for intervention.

TitreApplicationTitle: Prediction Rule to Identify Patients with Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Responding to Exercises
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENT IDIOPATHIC SCOLIOSIS; BACK PAIN; CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT; PHYSICAL EXERCISE; PHYSICAL THERAPY; PREDICTION RULE; QUALITY OF LIFE; REHABILITATION; SPINAL DEFORMITY; THREE-DIMENSIONAL TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Introduction Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a 3D deformity of the spine. It affects 2-3% of the population, usually females. AIS often results in pain, loss of function, external deformity, and poor self-image. Exercise studies have shown positive effects on these symptoms. However, evidence is inconsistent due to variation in the type of exercises prescribed, the training of therapists, the compliance from patients, and research design. The Schroth technique is a 3D sensorimotor exercise program consisting of correction of the scoliotic posture and breathing pattern. Exercise therapy may not have as negative an impact on self-esteem as more invasive interventions and may be more positively viewed by peer groups. Patients with AIS form a heterogeneous group with some patients possibly more likely than others to benefit from exercises. The objective of this study is to guide treatment prescription for patients with AIS by determining clinical predictors of positive response to exercises. Methods Females (aged 13-18) with AIS (n=100) showing spinal curves between 10° and 50° will be recruited. Treatment consists of a 3 month exercise protocol based on the Schroth technique.  Patients will undergo standardized baseline and discharge exams, measuring self-image, function, and pain domains with the SRS-22 questionnaire.  Secondary outcomes will be measured including spinal curvature, postural measures, Global Rating of Change (GRC), pain, and muscle endurance. Potential predictors of success will be collected at baseline.  Subjects will be categorized as successful or not based on GRC ratings. Predictors of success will be identified first, and then the best combination of variables will be selected to enter into the prediction rule. Relevance A prediction rule will help prescribe exercise therapy only to patients likely to benefit and avoid requiring teenagers unlikely to respond to commit to an intensive exercise program.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the role of the medico-scientific community in translational biomedical research
Keywords-MotsClés: BOUNDARY ORGANISATIONS; COLLABORATIONS; COMMERCIALISATION; ELSI/GE3LS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MEDICO-SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY; RESEARCH NETWORK; SCIENCE AND INNOVATION POLICY
Abstract-Résumé: Regenerative medicine (RM) is an interdisciplinary field of research and clinical application which focuses on the repair, replacement or regeneration of cells, tissues or organs. For my PhD thesis I will analyse how scientific discovery in RM translates into new medical treatments and therapies and how scientific and medical knowledge interact during this translational process. I will conduct a series of case studies of regenerative medicine laboratories involved in translational biomedical research to better understand the relationships and processes. RM research appears to draw heavily on both scientific and clinical knowledge, making it an ideal field to analyse interactions between these two knowledge types. These case studies will detail the incentives and support, as well as the impediments, experienced by scientists and clinicians in translating research to medicine.  I posit that differences exist between clinicians and scientists in value systems and organisational and reward structures and that these differences often impede the translation of biomedical knowledge from research to application. My project will explore whether these impediments exist and develop a series of practices and policies to decrease obstacles and facilitate the translation of biomedical research to medicine. This has significant implications for Canada's health delivery system. Part of the CIHR mandate is to translate new knowledge into improved health for Canadians. If barriers exist in this translation process, ideas for potentially life saving novel treatments may not be getting from the bench to the bedside. My project aims to increase the efficiency of the process through which new scientific ideas become medical therapies to help treat Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude de cohorte prospective sur les déterminants biologiques et psychosociaux des problèmes de comportement chez l'enfant inuit d'âge scolaire.
Keywords-MotsClés: DETRESSE PSYCHOLOGIQUE; DEVELOPPEMENT; ENFANCE; INUIT; SANTE MENTALE; SANTE PUBLIQUE; TROUBLES DE COMPORTEMENT; TERATOGENES; VIOLENCE CONJUGALE; EPIDEMIOLOGIE
Abstract-Résumé: Les objectifs de cette recherche sont de documenter la prevalence des problemes de comportement (PC) chez les enfants inuits du Nunavik ages de 10 ans. Elle vise a etudier la contribution des determinants biologiques prenataux et psychosociaux postnataux dans l'etiologie de ces troubles, ainsi que les differences entre les genres. Les PC comprennent des problemes tels l'agressivite ou la depression. Ils touchent de 2 a 16% des enfants. Des teratogenes relies aux habitudes de vie de la mere (e.g. alcoolisme) et l'exposition prenatale aux contaminants environnementaux sont associes a des perturbations comportementales. Des associations entre les PC et des caracteristiques de l'environnement psychosocial de l'enfant (e.g. statut socio-economique) ont egalement ete observees. Chez les Inuits, plus du tiers des references faites aux Directions de protection de la jeunesse concernent les jeunes ayant un PC serieux. Cette population presente egalement plusieurs facteurs de risque psychosociaux comme la pauvrete et la violence familiale. Le projet propose s'integre dans une etude de cohorte prospective ayant cours au Nunavik. 300 meres inuits et leur enfant age de 10 ans participent a cette etude. La presence de PC est mesuree a 10 ans par cinq evaluateurs independants qui un instrument valide utilise pour evaluer la presence des symptomes de PC. L'exposition aux contaminants environnementaux est mesuree dans le sang du cordon ombilical et a 10 ans dans le sang de l'enfant. La consommation de tabac, d'alcool et de drogue durant la grossesse est documentee soit dans l'entrevue prenatale de la mere ou retrospectivement. Les determinants psychosociaux sont mesures via l'entrevue maternelle perinatale et a 10 ans et se regroupent en trois categories : socio-demographiques, conflits parentaux et detresse psychologique maternelle. Une meilleure connaissance des PC chez les Inuits pourrait permettre la mise en place de programmes d'intervention ou de prevention.

Keywords-MotsClés: BARRIERS TO HEALTH CARE ACCESS; HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY; HIV/AIDS; HIV/AIDS AND GENDER; HIV/AIDS IN ENDEMIC COUNTRIES; HIV/AIDS IN VULNERABLE POPULATIONS; PEDIATRIC TESTING & TREATMENT- HIV/AIDS; SOCIOCULTURAL ASPECTS OF HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: In Uganda, Antiretroviral therapy (ART), in particular Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy (HAART) programs for HIV positive adults aged 15 or older, have been increasingly successful over the past number of years, with current treatment coverage rates of approximately 56% (AVERT, 2009). However, Ugandan children infected with HIV/AIDS have a treatment coverage rate that is very low in comparison. In Uganda, of the over 100,000 children living with HIV/AIDS, 50,000 of whom meet the requirements for needing HAART treatment, only about 24% or 12,000 receive it, despite the availability of international donor financing for children's HAART programming (Kaiser Network, 2008). This project will examine why this occurs and what the barriers are to HIV testing and providing HAART treatment to children in Kabarole district, Uganda.
