TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the cytoplasmic roles of hnRNP A1
Keywords-MotsClés: CDNA MICROARRAY; HNRNP A1; IRES; POLYSOME PROFILE; RNA-BINDING PROTEIN; TRANSLATION INITIATION
Abstract-Résumé: Genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein, and this information flow is regulated at several points. How the information encoded by RNA is regulated depends on proteins that bind to the RNA, which affect how the RNA is used to make new proteins. Importantly, the flow of information from RNA to protein is changed in diseases such as cancer due to changes in the activities of RNA-binding proteins. One such RNA-binding protein is the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A1 (hnRNP A1), which has a well-characterized role in regulating how newly-made RNA is processed into mature RNA capable of making new proteins. The regulation of RNA maturation by hnRNP A1 occurs in the nucleus of the cell; however, hnRNP A1 also plays important roles outside of the nucleus in the cytoplasm, where it regulates how long a RNA exists (RNA stability) and how RNA is used by the machinery that makes new proteins (RNA translation). Little is known about how hnRNP A1 performs its cytoplasmic activities, and therefore we do not know what may happen to change hnRNP A1 cytoplasmic activity in cancer cells. Furthermore, we do not know which RNAs are affected by deregulated hnRNP A1 activity in cancer cells. I propose to investigate how hnRNP A1 affects RNAs in the cytoplasm through the identification and characterization of the protein partners that bind to hnRNP A1 to regulate its activity. I will also identify and characterize the RNAs that are dependent on hnRNP A1 for their translation into protein to gain a better understanding of the cellular activities that are affected by cytoplasmic hnRNP A1. These studies will help us understand how RNA is made into protein, which will provide insight into what goes wrong in cancer cells. Moreover, by identifying the RNAs that are affected by hnRNP A1 cytoplasmic activities we will also understand more about the cellular functions that are changed in cancer cells.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mapping the Pax-5 cancerous interactome in breast cancer cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; CANCER BIOLOGY; GENE EXPRESSION AND REGULATION; GENE INACTIVATION TECHNOLGIES; INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING; ONCOGENES
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer is the most common female malignancy worldwide. In Canada, 1 in 8 women are predisposed to develop breast cancer where 33% of these women will succumb to their disease. Thus, the identification of genes involved in the development of cancer (oncogenesis) is essential for a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer origins and to identify new targets for the establishment of new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. As a result, our research group has turned its attention to cellular elements that have the ability to transform a healthy cell into its cancerous counterpart (called oncogenes). One of these factors, Pax-5, normally regulates pivotal biological processes in cells such as cellular growth, cell differentiation and cell death events. However, an aberrant expression of this pivotal factor results in the development of a cancerous state.  Past studies have shown irrefutable evidence linking the abnormal expression of Pax-5 gene products with the development, maintenance and progression of various cancer types. We and others have recently discovered the foreign presence of Pax-5 gene products in breast tumours which appears to be completely absent in healthy mammary tissues.  Also, our research demonstrates that an uncontrolled level of Pax-5 in breast tissue elicits breast cancer development and increased malignancy. Despite these interesting results, the role of Pax-5 in breast cancer at the molecular level still remains unknown.  We believe that Pax-5 gene products and their downstream co-acting elements and cell activation cascades are primary cancer causing agents responsible for breast cancer development.  The studies proposed herein will bring a better understanding of the mechanisms of the Pax-5 oncogene in breast tumour formation and may lead to a major improvement in the diagnosis and treatment options for breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Sex Differences in Adverse Drug Reactions in patients with Atrial Fibrillation
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVERSE DRUG REACTIONS; ATRIAL FIBRILLATION; SEX DIFFERENCES
Abstract-Résumé: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia requiring medical care, with tremendous disease burden given its influence on quality of life, morbidity, and mortality. The treatment of AF requires multiple drugs use and some of these agents have serious adverse effects in the long term. It has been previously suggested that female sex is a risk factor for the development of these adverse drug reactions; however to date, the incidence of these events in women compare to these in men in the setting of AF is unknown. Thus, our main objective is to determine whether differential beneficial or adverse effects exist with drug therapy between men and women with AF.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the mechanism(s) controlling mouse retinal progenitor cell competence
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL REPLACEMENT THERAPY; MACULAR DEGENERATION; NEURODEGENERATION; REGENERATION; RETINA; RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA; STEM CELLS; VISION
Abstract-Résumé: In increasingly aging population, degenerative diseases of the retina are becoming more and more frequent. Retinitis Pigmentosa affects roughly 12 000 Canadians, and Macular Degeneration already afflicts approximately one million. When these diseases strike, they lead to a permanent loss of neuronal cells in the retina, which is the structure that receives and transforms light into neural transmissions. These neurons could theoretically be replaced by stem cells, either by transplanting them into the eye, or by harnessing the stem cells that are present within the human retina. Previous experiments have shown that both approaches can generate new retinal neurons in principle; however these processes are currently too inefficient to be used therapeutically. To enhance the ability of neural stem cells to repair retinal damage, we need to increase our understanding of the biology that governs the ability of these cells to generate retinal neurons. To do this, I intend to study the gene Ikaros, a gene that has been previously shown to control the capability (competence) of retinal stem cells to generate all of the different types of retinal neurons. How the Ikaros gene does this is completely unknown. Therefore, I will perform experiments to determine how Ikaros functions. I will use the developmental formation of the retina as an experimental system, since this is the context in which Ikaros functions in nature. I anticipate that the information provided by these studies will have direct implications for harnessing neural stem cells to repair neurodegenerative disorders of the retina.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving End-of-Life Care in First Nations Communities: Generating a Theory of Change to Guide Program and Policy Development
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL PEOPLES' HEALTH; COMMUNITY BASED RESEARCH; CULTURALLY COMPETENT CARE; PALLIATIVE CARE; PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH; QUALITATIVE METHODS
Abstract-Résumé: The number of Aboriginal Canadians facing end of life is increasing each year due to the growing number of Aboriginal seniors and the high burden of chronic and terminal disease amongst this population. About one third of Aboriginal Canadians live in rural or remote First Nations communities. Residents of these communities face many barriers to accessing health services, including palliative care. In addition, existing services are often not culturally appropriate. Addressing this unmet need for accessible, culturally appropriate palliative care services for Aboriginal people in First Nations communities is a growing social obligation and an emerging Canadian policy priority.  The overall goal of this intervention research is to improve end-of -life care in four First Nations communities through developing palliative care programs and creating a culturally appropriate theory of change to guide palliative care program and policy development nationally. The proposed research adopts community capacity development as its theoretical perspective and a participatory action research approach (PAR). There are four First Nations communities as partners and study sites: Naotkamegwanning First Nation, Fort William First Nation, Six Nations of the Grand River Territory and Peguis First Nation.   The knowledge created by this research will include a tool kit of interventions for implementing palliative care in First Nations communities and a culturally appropriate theory of change to guide program and policy development nationally. Such theories of change are currently lacking, limiting the ability to evaluate the processes and outcomes of capacity development and create health services and policies consistent with a capacity development approach.

TitreApplicationTitle: A Poverty Reduction Approach to Improving the Health and Well- being of First Nation Communities
Keywords-MotsClés: FIRST NATION POVERTY AND HEALTH; HEALTH AND WELL-BEING OF FIRST NATION COMMUNITIES; INTERVENTION RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: Current news reports about the vulnerability of First Nation  communities to the H1N1 virus provide a stark and tragic  reminder of the relationship between poverty and ill health.   In this project, we propose to intervene with 5 volunteer  First Nation communities from different parts of Canada (urban,  rural, north, etc.). The intervention includes establishing an  Advisory Committee drawing on academic expertise, the  experience of First Nations in the region who have had success  with economic development and poverty reduction, and  government personnel.   The committee would undertake an initial study of  needs/barriers/strengths/opportunities facing the community.  This information would contribute to the development of a  strategic plan for poverty reduction and economic development.  Committee members would also contribute their expertise and  resources to working with the community in the implementation  of the strategic plan.  Ongoing research would monitor the interaction of  social/health/political factors as impediments to, or facilitators  of, the reduction of poverty and the achievement of sustainable  economic development. The outcomes of the intervention would  also be measured, both in the selected communities and in a  selection of those not subject to the intervention.  The proposal is being submitted by a research team of  Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal scholars with expertise in the  determinants of health, population health, gender and health,  development and labour economics, business, native studies  and the sociology of development. Most are members of the  Make Poverty History Expert Advisory Committee for the  Assembly of First Nations, which joins the group as the principal  community-based partner in the intervention research project.

TitreApplicationTitle: The WNT signalling pathway and its involvement in follicular and oocyte competence
Keywords-MotsClés: DEVELOPMENT; FOLLICLE; GENE KNOCK-OUT; IN VIVO; INFERTILITY; WESTERN; WNT SIGNALING
Abstract-Résumé: Previous research in the Kidder lab has shown that CX43-based gap junctional communication among granulosa cells is required for those cells to respond optimally to the oocyte-derived paracrine factor, GDF9 and that the canonical WNT signaling pathway is active in granulosa cells and, at least in vitro, controls their proliferation through regulation of beta-catenin, adherens junction formation, and CX43 expression.  I plan to extend this research with the aim of elucidating the role of WNT signaling in promoting the development of competent oocytes in vivo.  Specifically, I will test the hypothesis that WNT2, by promoting granulosa cell proliferation and gap junctional communication within the developing follicle, is a critical factor in ensuring oocyte quality. In order to test this hypothesis the effect that the loss of WNT2 signaling in granulose cells has on oocyte developmental competence will be tested.  Also,the relationship between WNT signaling and oocyte quality in human assisted reproduction will be studied.  If it can be established that WNT signaling is a determinant of oocyte quality in assisted conception, potential new avenues of oocyte/embryo selection or oocyte quality enhancement will have been identified.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of the dynamin I - endophilin interaction in clathrin mediated endocytosis.
Keywords-MotsClés: DYNAMIN I; ENDOCYTOSIS; ENDOPHILIN; KNOCK-OUT MICE; SPLICE VARIANTS; SYNAPTIC VESICLES
Abstract-Résumé: Communication between neurons is mediated by the release of synaptic vesicles (SVs) containing neurotransmitter from the presynaptic nerve terminal. Two methods of SV endocytosis - clathrin mediated endocytosis (CME) and activity dependent bulk endocytosis (ADBE) are required to prevent synaptic fatigue at different levels of activity. However, the mechanisms regulating the switch between CME and ADBE are unknown. Recent studies suggest that dynaminI (dynI), a large GTPase enzyme, is a key component of this switch. Two isoforms of dynI known as dynIxa and dynIxb, with a long and short C-terminal tail respectively, are expressed in neurons. Differences in the tail sequences suggest they play a role in specifying the recruitment of distinct binding partners. In particular, dynIxa has an additional binding site for the SVE protein endophilin. Here we will test the hypothesis that the interaction between dyn1xa and endophilin is required for CME rather than ADBE. We will express mutants of dynIxa in cerebellar granule cells from wild-type or dynI knock-out mice and determine their effect on CME. Using fluorescent styryl dyes for live cell imaging, or horseradish peroxidase for electron microscopy we will monitor uptake and distinguish between CME and ADBE. We will also develop peptide mimetics to block binding between dynIxa and endophilin to determine if the interaction is specifically required for CME. By characterizing the unique role of a dynI splice variant in SVE we will advance our understanding of the regulation of synaptic transmission. This knowledge can subsequently be applied to the treatment of diseases such as Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Arf, Stem Cell Function, and Aging
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; NEUROGENESIS; REGENERATIVE MEDICINE; STEM CELLS; TUMOR SUPPRESSORS
Abstract-Résumé: In the central nervous system, stem cells reside in the brain and produce new brain cells throughout life. The production of new brain cells is thought to regulate specific types of learning and memory as well as the response to anti-depressants. During aging, stem cell function and the production of new brain cells are altered. Cognitivie functions, including learning and memory capacity, also decline with age, and the incidence of depression increases. These observations raise the possibility that changes in stem cell regulation during aging contribute to certain types of age-related cognitive and mood disorders. p19Arf is a protein that protects us from cancer by blocking the inappropriate growth of cells. Cancer cells, including those within brain tumors, frequently mutate this gene to enable their increased proliferation. We have discovered that p19Arf expression increases with age within stem cells in the brain, raising the possibility that this increase might prevent cancer, but cause some of the changes in stem cell function that are observed during aging. The aim of this proposal is to examine the role of Arf in regulating stem cell function and the production of new brain cells, and to determine whether it contributes to changes in stem cell function during aging. These findings may reveal the mechanisms that change stem cell function during aging, as well as insights that could lead to new therapeutic strategies to improve cognitive function, promote tissue regeneration, and eradicate cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of mutations in microRNA biogenesis genes in cancer development.
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL CYCLE ANALYSIS; CHEMOSENSITIVITY; DNA DAMAGE RESPONSE; DNA REPAIR; GENOME INSTABILITY; IMMUNOFLUORESCENT STAINING; MICRORNA; NUCLEAR REPAIR FOCI; RADIOSENSITIVITY; WESTERN BLOT
Abstract-Résumé: Resistance to DNA damaging agents used in chemotherapy and radiotherapy is a major problem in cancer treatment. Mammalian cells have developed an elaborate DNA damage response (DDR) system and DNA repair machinery, which play a critical role in development of resistance to DNA damaging agents in cancer cells. Key components of DDR, such as H2AX, 53BP1, BRCA1 and FANCD2, accumulate, form DNA damage-induced nuclear foci, and regulate repair at sites of DNA damage. Formation of these nuclear foci is therefore a good marker of DDR pathway integrity. Precise regulation of DDR pathways is crucial for cell survival and its abrogation often results in genetic instability. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short, non-coding RNA molecules that negatively regulate gene expression. Some miRNAs function as oncogenes or tumor suppressors. However, the role of miRNAs in DDR is largely unknown. By screening a human miRNA mimics library I have identified 8, 10, 20 and 15 miRNA mimics that decrease nuclear foci formation of H2AX, 53BP1, BRCA1 and FANCD2, respectively. Based on this preliminary study, I hypothesize that DDR and DNA repair pathways are regulated by miRNAs. To test it, I will first validate these miRNAs individually in response to various DNA damaging agents in multiple cancer and normal cell lines. I will also demonstrate how these validated miRNAs modulate DNA repair by identifying their direct targets. I will then examine the biological significance of validated miRNAs in DNA repair assays and DNA damage sensitivity assays, and determine whether miRNA-mediated inactivation of DNA repair pathways is functionally relevant in cancer. This study will identify miRNAs that regulate DDR and DNA repair pathways and provide new insights into the regulation of DDR and DNA repair. Understanding of these regulations will further clarify the pathogenesis of cancer and the mechanism of resistance to DNA damaging agents and may eventually lead to new approaches for defeating cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Predicting the impact and cost-effectiveness of technical and non-technical approaches to TB control in low and middle income countries
Keywords-MotsClés: COST EFFECTIVENESS ANALYSIS; EPIDEMIOLOGY; HEALTH POLICY; INFECTIOUS DISEASE DYNAMICS; POPULATION HEALTH; SIMULATION MODELING; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; TUBERCULOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Background: Globally, tuberculosis (TB) remains a major source of illness and mortality. Cases have increased in recent decades.  The reasons for the increase are complex, however often overlooked socially based factors such as smoking and alcohol consumption have played a role. The implementation of interventions designed to address these determinants could be a cost effective approach to TB control and may have a greater impact than the technical approaches currently advocated by the World Health Organization.     Objective: To predict, in 3 low and middle income countries, the epidemiologic impact and cost effectiveness of a technical approach to TB control (using improved diagnostic tests for earlier diagnosis of active TB disease) versus a non-technical population level intervention designed to reduce tobacco use and alcohol consumption. Outcomes estimated include: TB infections, cases and deaths under each strategy as well as cost per death averted and per QALY gained.  Methods:  Dynamic computer simulation models (Susceptible- Latent-Infectious-Recovered models) will be used to predict the behavior of the TB epidemic with each intervention.  India, Russia and Zambia will be modeled as they represent a range of alcohol and smoking use, as well as HIV and TB epidemiology. HIV and drug resistance will be incorporated into models.  Pathogenetic parameters, as well as estimates of the impact of risk factors and interventions, will be obtained from literature reviews, publicly available databases and expert panels. Extensive sensitivity analyses will be conducted.  Implications: New approaches to TB control are desperately needed.  This study should generate new information regarding the epidemiologic impact of undiagnosed cases and the potential merits of non-technical preventative approaches, focusing on social determinants, for disease control.  Policy makers rely on such information to make informed decisions and improve the health of the populations.

TitreApplicationTitle: Caring for a Child with Cancer: Understanding Single Parent Families' Experiences
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CAREGIVERS; GROUNDED THEORY; QUALITATIVE; SINGLE PARENTS; WOMEN
Abstract-Résumé: Single parents represented 16 percent of all census families in 2006 in Canada, higher than any other recorded census figure in the last 75 years. Brown et al in a recent review called single parents of children with chronic disease an "understudied phenomenon". Studying the experiences of single parent families is important because the recent trend towards early discharge and care in the home has shifted the burden of care to parents who are increasingly involved in providing care for their children. For parents of children with cancer, it is unknown how the intensive and prolonged treatment for childhood cancer, which can result in increased burden on the primary caregiver and the family unit, impacts on the lives of single parent families. This study will use a qualitative design, with constructivist grounded theory as the guiding theoretical orientation. Interviews will be conducted with approximately 30 single parents of children with cancer. The specific aims are as follows: (1) to elucidate and to understand how single parents of children with cancer describe their experiences of caregiving;(2) to explore any special problems or challenges that single parents experience due to issues associated with being a single parents; (3) to explore single parents' descriptions of the care received from healthcare professionals looking after their child and the extent to which it is perceived by parents as being family-centered; and (4) to compare the caregiving experience of single mothers with that of single fathers. The interviews will provide extensive accounts of personal experience from participants. Coding will involve line-by-line, focused and theoretical coding. Theoretical sampling will be used to check and refine the emerging conceptual categories until data saturation is reached. Understanding the caregiving experience of single parent families will help us to determine whether and in what areas this subgroup of parents requires additional supports.

TitreApplicationTitle: Modulation de l'activité neuronale de l'habénula latéral par la prokineticine 2 et son implication dans la dépression.
Keywords-MotsClés: DOPAMINE; DEPRESSION; INJECTION STEREOTACTIQUE AU CERVEAU; LATERAL HABENULA (LHB); MALADIE DE L'HUMEUR; MODELES ANIMAUX DE DEPRESSION; PROKINETICIN RECEPTOR 2 (PKR2); VECTEUR VIRAL; VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA (VTA); ELECTROPHYSIOLOGIE
Abstract-Résumé: La depression est la maladie psychiatrique la plus repandue et est l'une des dix causes les plus importantes de morbidite et de mortalite a travers le monde. Les mecanismes neuronaux impliques dans la depression ne sont toujours pas tres bien caracterises et peu d'approches pharmacologiques sont disponibles afin de traiter la depression. Une region du cerveau, l'habenula laterale (LHb), recoit une attention particuliere presentement pour son implication potentielle dans la depression. Des etudes recentes chez le singe suggerent que la LHb serait le centre de 'desappointement' central du cerveau et lorsque active, par omission de recompense ou administration d'une punition, inhibe le 'ventral tegmental area' (VTA). Le VTA est implique dans les mecanismes de reponse et de memorisation associes aux recompenses principalement par la production et la secretion de dopamine. Chez des gens depressifs et des modeles animaux de depression, la LHb est hyperactive. Il est donc propose que l'activation aberrante de la LHb contribue au developpement de la depression par inhibition du VTA. Nous avons identifie un recepteur, PKR2, exprime presque exclusivement dans la LHb au niveau du cerveau. De facon interessante, une etude recente a montre que l'injection au cerveau de PK2, l'hormone activant PKR2, induit les symptomes de la depression chez la souris. Notre hypothese principale est donc que l'activation du PKR2 augmente l'activite des neurones de la LHb inactivant le VTA et participe au developpement de la depression. La recherche proposee vise a decortiquer, par des etudes au niveau de la cellule et du comportement chez le rat, comment l'activation/inhibition de PKR2 au niveau de la LHb peut mener au developpement de la depression. Notre approche cellulaire et comportementale de l'action de PKR2 sur les neurones de la LHb pourra potentiellement mettre en lumiere une nouvelle cible therapeutique afin d'ameliorer la condition des gens souffrant de depression.

TitreApplicationTitle: Analysis of genomic diversity and dynamics in breast and ovarian cancers
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CELLULAR DIFFERENTIATION; COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY; DATA VISUALIZATION; EPIGENETICS; GENETICS; GENOMICS; NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING; SMALL MOLECULES; STEM CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: The billions of cells in your body generally all share the same DNA sequence, and yet they display a vast array of morphologies and functions. Understanding how the same genetic material is interpreted in diverse cell types remains a challenge in modern biology. Diverse processes in a cell drive these heritable changes that do not involve alternations to the genome sequence (epigenetic modifications). There is significant therapeutic potential in improving our understanding of this epigenetic code and in discovering pharmaceuticals capable of altering a cell's epigenetic state. Promising applications include disrupting abnormal cell divisions in cancer or promoting self-renewal in stem cells for clinical use in regenerative medicine.  This proposal focuses on the genome-wide characterization of epigenetic changes in stem cells. Stem cells offer a powerful model of the earliest cell commitments to either self-renewal, producing identical daughter cells, or to differentiation into specialized cell types. I will use next-generation sequencing technologies to examine histone modifications, DNA methylation and gene expression patterns in normal stem cells before and after differentiation. In addition, I plan to profile the epigenetic modifications in chemically induced stem cells to compare the patterns to those of normal self-renewing cells. My research will tackle the challenges of computationally distilling biologically meaningful patterns and displaying them in intuitive interfaces that serve to accelerate the transition from raw data to discovery within the health sciences. Using these datasets and the tools I develop, I plan to address questions relating to whether a characteristic epigenetic pattern exists for self-renewing cells. Such an approach will be valuable in evaluating the extent to which chemically induced cells have been reprogrammed and are appropriate for therapeutic use.

TitreApplicationTitle: Studies on Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C in a Unique Mouse Model for Viral Hepatitis
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIVIRAL THERAPY; CHIMERIC MOUSE MODEL; HEPATITIS B VIRUS; HEPATITIS C VIRUS; INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE
Abstract-Résumé: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) are the primary causes of chronic viral hepatitis that can lead to end-stage liver disease (cirrhosis) or hepatocellular carcinoma.  There is an estimated 400 million chronic carriers of HBV and 170 to 200 million chronic carriers of HCV.  Research on these viruses has been limited by the lack of adequate cell culture systems on animal models.  We have recently developed an immune-compromised transgenic mouse (SCID/beige Alb-uPA) that can accept human hepatocytes transplanted via intrasplenic injection.  These mice develop chimeric human/mouse livers and are proving very valuable for the study of the innate immune responses, the responses to biological and small molecule antiviral agents, and to study the host and viral genetics contributing to chronic viral infection as opposed to an acute infection that resolves quickly.  While we initially thought this model was excellent for studying viral infection and replication, recent studies have shown the model can be expanded to study virally-induced oxidative stress and apoptosis and has provided key insights into the underlying pathogenesis of viral-induced fibrosis - a precursor to the development of cirrhosis.  The proposal outlined in this study examines several genes that are involved in "putting the brakes" on the innate immune response to HCV infection.  We will use the mouse model to examine the effect of inhibiting these "braking proteins" and essentially taking the "brakes" off the innate immune response may permit a stronger response to clear HCV infection.

TitreApplicationTitle: Homeostasis in autonomic functions: seeking  therapeutic targets in diseases of aging
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR AND AUTONOMIC FUNCTIONS; CELLULAR ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; NEURAL REGULATORY MECHANISMS; NEUROPEPTIDES; NEUROPHARMACOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: A significant area of the brain is involved in the moment-to-moment control of vital physiological functions, many of which fluctuate over the day-night period, and are beyond our conscious experience. Examples include arterial blood pressure, blood glucose, energy-related and stress-related hormones circulating in the blood. The brain's "silent" monitoring systems also attempts to introduce automatic corrective measures whenever a situation arises that may be detrimental to health and well being. Stress (psychological or physical)& aging can introduce disturbances that affect physiological functions and their daily rhythms, contributing to, and possibly causing hypertension, obesity, disorders in sleep-wake cycles, psychiatric and cognitive disturbances (e.g. alzheimer's and parkinson's disease, schizophrenia). We use rodent models in efforts to identify the cell and molecular mechanisms in the central nervous system that normally control these vital functions, in particular blood pressure / heart rate, fluid balance, hormone secretions, wakefulness, motivation and reward. Our reasoning is that this information is essential to understanding what, where and how certain disease conditions may arise, and give clues as to how to correct the abnormality in humans. Our research is focused in two areas. One examines the control mechanisms used by brain cells in the spinal cord to sustain normal levels of activity in the sympathetic nerves that regulate cardiovascular and adrenal functions. It has been shown that excess activity at this level is common in hypertension and obesity, and that measures to reduce this activity may be have a therapeutic value. A second project evaluates the activity of cells in brain areas called the hypothalamus and thalamus, where cells appear to participate in regulating motivation and mood, and control rhythms in physiological functions. This project is particularly suited to characterize the actions of drugs that may improve mental health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Drug Use and Drug Treatment Careers: Advancing Longitudinal Drug Abuse Research
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOSTATISTICS; ECONOMIC EVALUATION; EPIDEMIOLOGY; INJECTION DRUG USE; METHAMPHETAMINE ABUSE; PROGRAMME EVALUATION; PUBLIC HEALTH; SUBSTANCE ABUSE TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: The study of drug use and drug treatment careers aims to identify and understand key factors influencing the development of, and transitions in, the course of drug dependence and its treatment over an individual's lifetime. An understanding of how individuals progress through drug use and drug treatment over time is required for effective, targeted treatment.  The proposed research will draw upon Health administrative data on drug treatment utilization from British Columbia, Canada and California, USA as well as long-term follow up studies of drug users to uncover patterns of treatment and use as they unfold over a drug users' lifetime.  Illicit drug use is predictive of elevated risks of infectious disease transmission and mortality, while prolonged drug treatment decreases these risks and improves health and social outcomes. A deeper understanding of the patterns of drug use, treatment and associated health resource utilization will enhance our ability to plan and develop patient-centered treatment for the highest-risk illicit drug users. Comparisons between British Columbia and California drug treatment provision will further develop the case for policies that increase access to effective drug treatment internationally.

TitreApplicationTitle: A comprehensive approach to understanding Ras-stimulated macropinocytosis.
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL BIOLOGY; CELL GROWTH; CELL PROLIFERATION; CELL SIGNALLING; DRUG DELIVERY; ENDOCYTOSIS; GENE SILENCING; GENETIC SCREENING; MEMBRANE TRAFFICKING; RNAI
Abstract-Résumé: My research project is focused on studying a process known as macropinocytosis.  Macropinocytosis is the mechanism whereby cells internalize fluid from their environment.  This process is critical in the detection of foreign substances by immune cells, is exploited by deadly pathogens such as Salmonella and Legionella, and is stimulated in mutated cancer cells.  Very little is known about how macropinocytosis is controlled and what genes are involved.  To fully understand macropinocytosis and its effects on human health and disease, we are using the wealth of knowledge provided by the human genome project to determine which genes control macropinocytosis.  Our studies will use human cells that contain an oncogene that stimulates macropinocytosis.  With the help of sophisticated robotics and advanced microscopic techniques, we will test over 20,000 human genes for their effects on macropinocytosis.  This approach will allow us to determine which human genes control fluid uptake.  As an extension to our analysis, we are also studying how nutrients affect macropinocytosis.  We have determined that concentrations of glutamine, the most abundant amino acid, affect macropinocytosis.  This suggests that macropinocytosis may be linked to metabolism. This research is important to human health and disease in many ways.  First, knowing which genes function in macropinocytosis could lead to novel drug targets and therapeutics for cancer and infections.  Second, a wide range of bioactive molecules such as cell penetrating peptides, DNA for gene therapy and nanoparticles use macropinocytosis to enter cells.  Therefore, understanding how macropinocytosis works could lead to more efficient drug delivery in the treatments of many diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Factors guiding dopamine receptor expression in MSN neurons: implications for schizophrenia.
Keywords-MotsClés: CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; DOPAMINE RECEPTOR COLOCALIZATION; DOPAMINE RECEPTORS; GENE EXPRESSION; NEURODEVELOPMENT; QUANTITATIVE REAL TIME PCR; SCHIZOPHRENIA; STRIATUM; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS; TRANSFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Neurons that respond to the neurotransmitter dopamine play a key role in neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders. These include schizophrenia, movement disorders, Parkinson's disease, as well as addiction. These neurons are the target of all antipsychotic drugs used to treat these diseases. Abnormal maturation or functioning of these neurons is thought to be the main cause of the above disorders. Yet, nothing is known about the factors that determine the maturation of these neurons. This creates a void in our knowledge, which needs to be addressed. We have identified a list of candidate factors, which are likely to guide the maturation and function of these neurons. By following their appearance at different points of brain maturation, we will identify which of these factors play a key role in this process and how they may function abnormally in disease. We hope to use this knowledge to identify new, more direct, treatments for these diseases. Using different techniques aimed at returning the function of these factors to normal, we may be able to develop treatment for at-risk individuals and perhaps even prevent the onset of the disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Impact de la relation d'attachement sur la fonction cardiovasculaire des enfants présentant un retard de croissance intra-utérin.
Keywords-MotsClés: ATTACHEMENT; DEVELOPPEMENT; ENFANTS; FONCTION CARDIOVASCULAIRE; FREQUENCE CARDIAQUE; PRESSION ARTERIELLE; RETARD DE CROISSANCE INTRA-UTERIN
Abstract-Résumé: Les enfants qui naissent avec un retard de croissance intra-uterin sont plus a risque de developper des problemes de sante physiques et psychologiques. Cependant, des etudes effectuees chez les rats  montrent que les rats qui recoivent de meilleurs soins par leur mere produisent moins d'hormones de stress, ce qui a un effet protecteur contre certaines maladies. Il semble donc que la qualite de la relation entre la mere et son enfant peut renverser les facteurs de risques associes aux problemes de developpement du foetus. La recherche proposee comparera le fonctionnement cardiovasculaire des enfants avec un retard de croissance intra-uterin et celui des enfants dont le poids a la naissance etait dans la normale. Puis, les resultats seront evalues en considerant egalement le type d'attachement de l'enfant a sa mere, pour verifier si le sentiment de securite de l'enfant envers sa mere peut avoir un effet protecteur. Les enfants participant a l'etude ont ete suivis depuis la naissance et ont ete evalues a differents moments de leur developpement. On a notamment evalue leur type d'attachement alors qu'ils avaient 18 et 36 mois. Ils seront maintenant revus a l'age de 7 ans ou leur frequence cardiaque et leur pression arterielle seront enregistrees durant 24 heures, afin d'evaluer leur fonction cardiovasculaire durant le jour et durant leur sommeil. Cette etude permettra de savoir si les enfants avec un retard de croissance intra-uterin ont une fonction cardiaque alteree et si le fait d'avoir un attachement secure avec la mere peut avoir un effet protecteur sur cette meme fonction. Les resultats de ce projet de recherche permettront de developper des programmes d'intervention cibles et precoces chez les enfants a risque de developper des problemes d'attachement et des maladies cardiovasculaires.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification and characterization of molecular targets for novel small molecule inhibitors of lung adenocarcinoma
Keywords-MotsClés: AFFINITY CHROMATOGRAPHY; BIOCHEMISTRY; CELL BIOLOGY; DRUG DEVELOPMENT; LUNG CANCER; ONCOGENES; QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS; SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITOR; TARGET IDENTIFICATION; TUMOR BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is a devastating disease suffering from the lack of effective chemotherapeutic strategies.  Recently, our laboratory has screened a panel of 189,290 diverse chemical compounds in search of new agents to treat lung tumours.  This analysis revealed four drug candidates that were able to inhibit the growth of lung cancer cells without toxicity to healthy, normal lung cells.  However, the processes by which the compounds carry out their effects remain unknown.  The focus of this proposal is to identify the specific gene products targeted by these compounds in order to understand their mechanisms of action.  First, I outline a novel strategy for the robust and accurate identification of drug targets which uses the compounds as "baits" to "fish" out binding proteins from cancer cells.  Second, by programming cancer cells sensitive to the drugs to overproduce the identified targets, I aim to rescue these cells from the inhibitory effects, confirming the role of the proteins in mediating drug response.  Third, by analyzing changes in the levels of other genes in response to drug treatment, I will be able to further characterize the cellular pathways in which the drug targets are involved and clarify their potential role in lung tumour development.  Lastly, I will look for mutations in the targets, as well as other genes, in an attempt to uncover the features that make tumours vulnerable to drug treatment.  Together, this work will lead to a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the properties of these novel anti-lung cancer compounds.  Not only will this be essential in order to further develop these drugs for clinical use, it will ultimately lead to the discovery of other process that lung cancer cells remain dependant on for sustained growth that may be further exploited for therapeutic means.

TitreApplicationTitle: Functional CD8+ and FoxP3+ tumor infiltrating T-cells in ovarian cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER IMMUNOLOGY; MOUSE MODELS OF CANCER; OVARIAN CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Rationale: Although ovarian cancer is highly responsive using current treatment with surgery and chemotherapy, a high proportion of these women will have their cancer return. There are multiple factors that can be used to predict if this. Intriguingly, this includes the presence of tumor-reactive T-cells. In fact, two specific types of T-cells seem to account for this effect, CD8+ T cells and regulatory T cells (cells that attenuate the immune response). While early studies reported that FoxP3+ T cells (a transcription factor associated with regulatory T cells) attenuate the tumor-reactive CD8+ T cells, more recent studies in ovarian cancer show the opposite. This may be due to an alternate type of FoxP3+ T cell that acts to stimulate an immune response.  Scientific Question (hypothesis): We hypothesize that FoxP3+ cells are acting to stimulate the CD8+ cells in ovarian cancer and provide a stronger anti-tumor response.  Scientific Plan (Aims): Viable cells from 30 cases of ovarian cancer have been collected that include CD8+ cases with (n=15) and without (n=15) FoxP3+ T cells. To compare CD8+ and FoxP3+ T cell function in these two groups, we will measure cell surface markers and expressed molecules by flow cytometry. In addition, we will test these results in a mouse model that mimics human ovarian cancer by depleting or enriching FoxP3+ T cells.  Relevance: By determining which cell types and functions promote a favourable outcome in ovarian cancer we can tip the balance toward a more robust and effective immune response in ovarian cancer patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Re-admission and Mortality in children under 5 years of age following hospitalization for sepsis in Uganda: A prospective cohort study
Keywords-MotsClés: COHORT STUDY; EPIDEMIOLOGY; INTERNATIONAL HEALTH; PEDIATRICS; POPULATION HEALTH; SEPSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Worldwide, more than 10 million children die annually before their fifth birthday.  Most of these deaths occur in resource poor countries and are preventable. The Millennium Development Goals (MDG), signed by all countries, including Canada, commit to reducing child mortality in the under five age-group by two thirds before the year 2015.   Most child deaths in the under-five age group are due to complications related to sepsis, a syndrome arising from severe infections. Previously published literature has shown that among children admitted to the hospital with sepsis, more children die within the two month period following discharge than during hospitalization. While extensive literature exists regarding hospital-based interventions to reduce child mortality due to sepsis, no studies have been conducted to investigate predictors of death in the critical two month period following discharge.  Research into the clinical, laboratory and demographic predictors of hospital re-admission and death following discharge is essential before further interventions can be implemented to reduce disease burden. Our research aims to identify a cohort of children under age five hospitalized for sepsis at the Mbarara University Hospital (Uganda) and to follow them for a period of three months following discharge. Through this research we hope to determine the predictors of readmission and death following hospital discharge. This will serve as a fundamental foundation for future research aimed at the development of outpatient interventions to reduce death due to sepsis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigation into the cause of Myoclonus Dystonia
Keywords-MotsClés: EPSILON SARCOGLYCAN; HUMAN GENETICS; MASS SPECTROMETRY; MOVEMENT DISORDER; MYOCLONUS DYSTONIA; NEURONAL CELLS; SARCOGLYCAN COMPLEX; TANDEM AFFINITY PURIFICATION
Abstract-Résumé: Myoclonus dystonia (MD) is a neurological disorder characterized by rapid muscle contractions (myoclonus) and sustained twisting movements resulting in abnormal postures (dystonia). Symptoms begin in the 1st or 2nd decades of life and are associated with subtle psychiatric symptoms (obsessive-compulsive disorder). MD can range from mild to severe, even in the same family. Most patients have a drastic reduction of myoclonus in response to alcohol ingestion, however, as the alcohol level in their system lowers, their symptoms become worse than before. This temporary and severe rebound affect makes alcoholism a significant problem. Forty percent of MD patients have mutations in the gene e-sarcoglycan (SGCE), which is a member of the sarcoglycan (SG) family. To date, 6 sarcoglycan genes (a,b, e,g,d,and z) have been identified. Mutations in a, b, g and d sarcoglycan are responsible for recessive (both parents must be carriers) limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The sarcoglycans are members of the dystrophin-dystroglycan complex (DGC) in muscle. Mutations in other members of the complex are also responsible for other forms of muscular dystrophies. Interestingly, SGCE is expressed in more tissues than the other family members. Its expression within the brain explains how a mutation in the gene encoding SGCE causes the movement disorder, MD. To date, evidence of its role or interacting partners within the brain are unknown. The aim of my project is to identify the components of the SGCE complex in the brain using a method called, Tandem affinity purification-mass spectrometry. My goal is to identify the SG-complex in the brain including new members not seen in the complex found in muscle. By determining the proteins which interact with SGCE we will determine the reason mutations in this gene cause MD. Furthermore, the interacting proteins will be candidates for other similar movement disorders, just as the binding partners in muscle cause other forms of muscular dystrophy

TitreApplicationTitle: Determinants of Quality of Life in Children with Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC ILLNESS; MIXED METHODOLOGY; ONCOLOGY; PEDIATRICS; QUALITY OF LIFE; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: There is growing interest in assessing quality of life (QOL) in children with cancer, especially now that most children survive their disease.  While validated measures have been used extensively to describe QOL, what is lacking is the availability of a theoretical model that describes factors and processes associated with QOL and that can be used to guide future research.  This study addresses this important gap in research and represents the first step in an innovative program of research that will help to better understand what factors can explain variability in QOL for children with cancer. A systematic review will be conducted of the scientific literature to identify all studies that measured QOL in children with cancer using validated pediatric generic or disease-specific QOL questionnaires.  The primary aim of the review is to extract information about factors related to QOL, including treatment variables, child characteristics, family variables and community factors; each forming part of the broader context within which the children live and which may influence their QOL. These findings will be used to develop a conceptual model of determinants of QOL and the model will be applied in a large-scale multi-center study of children with cancer and childhood cancer survivors. Understanding variables that can explain the different patterns of QOL, how these relate to important child, disease, family and community variables, and how these change over time, is a necessary first step towards designing interventions to improve the QOL of this vulnerable population. Assessment of child health-related QOL has typically relied on parents' proxy reports, but many questionnaires can also be completed by children themselves. There are, however, many questions remaining about parent-child agreement. A secondary aim of the review is to extract information about parent-child agreement about the child's QOL and to identify variables that may impact on parent-child agreement.

TitreApplicationTitle: Optimizing Audit and Feedback for Chronic Disease in Primary Care: A Mixed Methods Approach
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL; FAMILY MEDICINE; GUIDELINE DISSEMINATION; IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MIXED METHODOLOGY; PRIMARY CARE; QUALITY IMPROVEMENT; QUALITY INDICATORS
Abstract-Résumé: There remains a large gap between ideal and actual care provided to patients with chronic diseases. Performance feedback reports describing the percentage of patients receiving evidence-based treatments and up-to-date investigations are often used when trying to influence the way that care is delivered by clinicians. Despite the prominence of this quality improvement tool, the best way to design and deliver feedback reports to family physicians so that they will lead to improved quality of care for patients with chronic disease is uncertain. At this point, the important question to ask is not whether feedback reports can help improve quality, but how to optimize feedback interventions to accomplish that goal.   This research proposal aims to determine how feedback reports can be best used to improve quality of care provided by family physicians to patients with chronic diseases. Building on evidence from psychology, education, and industrial behaviour, a worksheet will be developed to encourage recipients to set goals and develop action plans in response to the feedback reports. Half of the family physician participants will be randomly selected to receive this worksheet while the other half will not. In the months following distribution of the feedback, a purposively sampled group of participants will be interviewed to determine how the feedback design may be improved and explore barriers and facilitators to acceptance and utilization of the performance feedback for quality improvement. After six months, the groups will be compared to test the hypothesis that when they develop goals and action plans in response to feedback reports, clinicians' performance will improve.   We believe that this project will lead to improved quality of care for the 50,000+ patients in the participating physicians' practices, but also that the lessons learned will be broadly applicable to quality improvement projects for chronic disease management in primary care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Economic Evaluation of Strategies to Prevent and Treat Chemotherapy-Induced Neutropenia in Lymphoma Patients
Keywords-MotsClés: DECISION ANALYSIS; HEALTH POLICY; LYMPHOMA; OUTCOMES RESEARCH; PHARMACOECONOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: Febrile neutropenia (FN), defined as a low count of neutrophils which are white blood cells involved in helping the immune system fight infection in combination with fever, is a common, potentially life-threatening complication of chemotherapy in lymphoma patients, and often requires hospitalization. The Canadian Institute for Health Information reports that hematologic malignancies, such as lymphoma, were one of the fifteen most expensive medical conditions in Canada in 2005 with respect to acute, inpatient medical costs; a large part of these costs were attributable to complications including neutropenia. Information on how patients prefer to be treated for FN and economic evaluations of interventions used to prevent FN will help to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of Canadian healthcare system.  My research focuses on two areas related to the delivery of health services to lymphoma patients who are at risk of developing FN or who develop this condition: 1) examining factors that influence patient preferences for treatment of FN in hospital or at home as well as how FN affect patients' quality of life; and 2) conducting cost-effectiveness evaluations of filgrastim and pegfilgrastim, medications used to prevent FN.  Lymphoma patients suffering from FN will be asked to complete questionnaires on their quality of life and on how different factors, (e.g., out-of-pocket expenses) would affect whether they choose to be treated at home.  A decision model, combing information on costs, patient preferences and clinical effectiveness will be used to estimate the cost-effectiveness of the two strategies available to prevent FN. I expect the results of this study will be highly relevant to healthcare decision makers as they can be used to formulate policy on improving the delivery of high quality, cost-effective care to lymphoma patients with FN.

TitreApplicationTitle: Statistical model to characterize genome-wide DNA methylation patterns from multigenerational families
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING-RELATED DISEASES; BAYESIAN ANALYSIS; BIOSTATISTICS; CAMOS COHORT; COMMON DISEASES; GENETIC DETERMINANTS; GENOMICS; OSTEOPOROSIS; STATISTICAL-GENETICS; VITAMIN D
Abstract-Résumé: Canadians are at high risk of Vitamin D deficiency. Low levels of vitamin D have been associated with many chronic aging-related diseases, such as cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis among others. Several studies have shown that there is a strong genetic component influencing vitamin D levels. Despite this strong influence of genetic factors, the genetic determinants of vitamin D are mainly unknown.   Using data from the Canadian Multicentre Osteoporosis Study (CaMos) cohort, we intend to identify the genetic and environmental determinants of vitamin D levels in the Canadian general population.  Based on physiologic parameters, we will define healthy vitamin D levels, and identify subgroups of the population who should receive higher doses of vitamin D based upon high risk genetic and environment profiles. At present, there is no consensus on optimal levels of vitamin D and prevalence of this hypovitaminosis.  The CaMos cohort is uniquely positioned to address these research questions. 9423 patients have been followed for over 10 years for osteoporosis-related outcomes. Supplemental calcium and vitamin D intake, medication use, anthromorphic measures as well as several hundred other behaviours and environmental determinants have been systematically accrued from administered questionnaires which will facilitate the study of environmental determinants of vitamin D levels. Blood samples are available for DNA genotyping for over 3000 subjects.  This study should have an important positive impact on public health of Canadians as vitamin D is associated with multiple chronic diseases and the identification of these determinants could consequently identify groups of individuals to be targeted for vitamin D administration. Therefore, this work may have a large impact on several chronic aging-related diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Loneliness and social engagement among older adults: Examining the importance for health and for the development of age-friendly communities.
Keywords-MotsClés: AGE-FRIENDLY COMMUNITIES; HEALTH CARE SERVICE UTILIZATION; HEALTHY AGING; LONELINESS; SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: A lot of research suggests that our social relationships are important to our health. In fact, in one provocative study, the authors concluded that being lonely or dissatisfied with relationships is as strong a risk factor to our health as smoking (House et al., 1988). The present study is about further examining this connection between our social relationships and health. This project is also about exploring ways that communities can help older adults be socially engaged. The first research question is: given evidence that loneliness and lack of social participation is detrimental to health, does this also translate into greater health service use? This question is important, especially given the associated costs of health care, and will be addressed by examining information gathered from older adults and health care records. Results of this study may have important implications for health care professionals providing rehabilitation services and programming for older adults.   One way to address the social participation and loneliness of older adults is to create supportive, inclusive, or age-friendly environments. Therefore, the second research question is: what are communities in Manitoba doing to address the social engagement of their older community members? This question follows from a study conducted as part of the larger Manitoba Age-Friendly Communities Initiative which asked municipality representatives about the age-friendliness of their community (e.g., housing, social programs). A good proportion answered that they have programs for socially isolated adults and the present study will gather additional information on how these programs function. This information could be used to help other communities address the social engagement of older adults, make communities more age-friendly, and, ultimately, improve the health and well-being of older adults in our community.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mécanismes moléculaires impliqués dans l'arrêt de cycle cellulaire en G2 induit par la protéine accessoire Vpr du VIH-1.
Keywords-MotsClés: ARRET DU CYCLE CELLULAIRE EN G2; E3 UBIQUITINE LIGASE; INTERACTION VPR/PROTEINES CELLULAIRES; PROTEINES ACCESSOIRES; PURIFICATION D'AFFINITE EN TANDEM; SUBSTRAT; VIH
Abstract-Résumé: L'infection par le virus de l'immunodeficience humaine de type 1 (VIH-1) provoque la mort des lymphocytes T CD4+ et conduit au syndrome de l'immunodeficience acquise (SIDA). Plus de 33 millions de personnes dans le monde sont seropositives, et le VIH provoque la mort de plus de 2 millions de personnes par an dans le monde. Au cours des dernieres annees, de nombreuses etudes ont montre l'importance des proteines dites accessoires (Vpr, Vpu, Vif et Nef) dans la replication du VIH-1 in vivo et la manipulation des processus cellulaires fondamentaux de l'hote. Vpr est donc actuellement le sujet de recherches actives afin de mieux comprendre son role dans l'infection et la pathogenese du VIH-1. Des partenaires cellulaires de Vpr ont ete decrits et ces interactions sont principalement a deux activites biologiques : Vpr aide a la replication du virus dans les macrophages primaires, et Vpr induit un arret du cycle cellulaire, facilitant la transcription et la replication virale. Le but de ce projet de recherche est de definir les interactions de Vpr avec ses partenaires cellulaires et afin de comprendre les mecanismes moleculaires qui menent a ses activites biologiques.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of translation initiation factors eIF4,PABP, 4E-BPs and the miRNA pathway in regulating translation and stability of HIV-1 mRNAs
Keywords-MotsClés: HIV; IN VIVO EXPRESSION OF REPORTER GENES; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PROTEIN KINASES; RACK1; RETROVIRUSES; RIBOSOMAL E-SITE; RIBOSOMAL FRAMESHIFT; SIRNA-MEDIATED KNOCK-DOWN; TRANSLATIONAL CONTROL
Abstract-Résumé: Viruses are molecular complexes consisting of a nucleic acid of only one type (DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein coat. Viruses exist in two forms: resting extracellular form (virion) and actively reproducing (replicating) intracellular form. When virus penetrates into the host cell and thus represents the actively replicating form, it needs to produce new copies of its components: nucleic acid and proteins. Proteins are produced inside the host cell by special machinery - the ribosome, which uses the RNA molecule as a template. Production of proteins from a RNA template decodes ("translates") the RNA code into protein. The RNA of Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) also depends on the ribosome to produce all the proteins essential for the viral life cycle. Particular to HIV is that it requires an unusual step during RNA translation into proteins by the ribosome, called the programmed frameshift, for the production of all of its proteins. Some cellular proteins can modulate synthesis of viral proteins by the ribosome. Our research project aims at studying one of such proteins called RACK1. We will study how RACK1 interacts with the ribosome to modulate synthesis of HIV proteins, and the programmed frameshift, and its quantitative effect on the production of new HIV particles.  Having established the role of RACK1 in synthesis of HIV proteins and in production of new HIV particles, we will be able to designate ways to develop drugs that will block the stimulatory effect of RACK1 on synthesis of viral proteins and, hence, will block HIV replication. Thus, our project will open new avenues for innovative antiretroviral therapy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Innovation for HIV/AIDS care:  Exploring the application of the Chronic Care Model
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC CARE MODEL; CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT; HIV/AIDS; PRIMARY CARE
Abstract-Résumé: The Chronic Care Model (CCM), which aims to improve the quality of care at the community, health care organization, practice and patient levels, is increasingly being applied in the management of chronic diseases. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is the causative agent of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).  Thanks to dramatic improvements in managing this infection, we can now view HIV/AIDS as a chronic condition affecting approximately 58,000 Canadians. Despite the CCM's popularity, there is limited research specifically examining how this model is applicable to patients living with HIV/AIDS as a chronic condition.   The proposed research will consist of 3 inter-related projects that explore the extent to which the CCM, or its elements, are being applied to HIV/AIDS care nationally and internationally.  First, we will review published literature for studies describing any aspect of the CCM in relation to the care of people living with HIV/AIDS.  Second, an environmental scan of existing specialized HIV treatment centers in Canadian urban centers will be performed to determine the extent to which these centers integrate elements of the CCM to the care of people living with HIV/AIDS. Finally, a survey of 200 randomly selected Ontario-based primary care physicians will be assessed to understand a) the extent of HIV/AIDS care they provide, b) their willingness to assume an increased role in HIV/AIDS care, c) their information and support needs to acquire competence in this regard, and d) their attitudes and receptivity to the application of the CCM in HIV/AIDS care.  The information gained from this study will serve to inform new, coordinated primary care approaches to improving HIV/AIDS care in Canada. Furthermore, the results from this project may provide a foundation of knowledge for future research, such as the subsequent implementation and evaluation of HIV/AIDS care models in primary care settings.

TitreApplicationTitle: The linkage between natural killer (NK) cell anti-viral functional potential and KIR/HLA genotypes
Keywords-MotsClés: DENDRITIC CELLS; HIV/AIDS; HLA; INHIBITION OF VIRAL REPLICATION; INNATE IMMUNITY; KIR; NK CELL FUNCTION; NK CELL PHENOTYPE; NK CELLS; PROTECTION FROM INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Natural killer (NK) cells are a key player in innate immunity. There is evidence they play a role in host defenses to viruses such as HIV. NK cells have surface receptors called KIR that recognize HIV infected cells through binding some cell surface molecules on infected cells. These molecules, called HLA, are present on the surface of most cells in the body, including those that HIV targets in an infected person. NK cells can control infection by killing the HIV-infected cells and inhibiting HIV replication when the number of HLA molecules that KIR receptors recognize is downregulated by HIV in infected cells. The KIR receptors and HLA molecules have many variants that differ from one person to another and influence the functions of NK cells when they meet a target cell infected with HIV. There are KIR/HLA variants that are seen more frequently in people who remain uninfected despite exposure to HIV (exposed uninfected or EU subjects) than in HIV susceptible individuals. I hypothesize that the mechanism underlying why cetain KIR/HLA variants are associated with protection from infection is that NK cells from people expressing protective KIR/HLA variants are more readily activated to kill cells infected with HIV or prevent HIV from replicating and spreading. In this project I will study the anti-viral functions of NK cells from both individuals carrying certain KIR/HLA combinations associated with protection from HIV infection and individuals not carrying these combinations. This project will contribute to understanding the mechanism of protection from HIV infection in EUs and may provide clues on how to prepare HIV vaccines to reduce the risk of HIV infection.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular pathogenesis of BRCA1-associated and triple-negative breast cancer: mechanism of tissue specificity and identification and characterization of cooperating tumorigenic pathways.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS OF CANCER; BRCA1 ASSOCIATED CANCER; CANCER; MEDICAL ONCOLOGY; ONCOGENES AND TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENES; RNAI
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer affects almost 23 000 Canadian women each year, and remains a major cause of death. Five percent all breast cancers, and 80% of inherited cases, are caused by mutations in the BRCA1 gene. Women who carry these mutations are also at high risk for the development of ovarian cancer, but not tumors at other sites. The reasons why individuals with these mutations develop cancers in these specific organs may be related to estrogen activity, but the mechanism of this process is not clear.  Furthermore, abnormalities in BRCA1 function are found in a significant proportion of non-inherited breast cancers. They are especially common in a subset of tumors that do not respond to currently available targeted therapies (hormone therapies like tamoxifen, and treatments directed against HER2/neu, an abnormal tumor cell protein ie. Herceptin). The goals of this project are therefore to: (1) elucidate the molecular factors that contribute to the predisposition to breast and ovarian cancers in women who carry BRCA1 gene mutations; and (2) identify other molecular abnormalities that could be targeted for the treatment and/or prevention of these tumors.   My research will use an animal model of BRCA1-associated breast cancer to explore these questions, and incorporate RNA interference (RNAi), a powerful new tool in molecular biology, to identify candidates for further characterization, validation, and study in patient samples. Collaboration with our clinical and drug development programs will enable us to use this model to explore new leads for future drug development in this population. This bench-to-bedside approach may result in effective new treatments for these difficult-to-treat cancers, potentially leading to improved survival or cure for women with this disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Novel Determinants of Change in Health Related Quality of Life Among Vulnerable Seniors
Keywords-MotsClés: COST; ECONOMICS; FALLS; HEALTH RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE; HEALTH RESOURCE UTILIZATION; PATIENT REPORTED OUTCOME MEASURES; QUALITY ADJUSTED LIFE YEAR
Abstract-Résumé: A relatively recent but significant shift in health research gives credence to outcomes as reported by patients themselves. The BMJ reported the need to complement 'clinical outcomes' with patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) to overcome the case characterized by the cliche that "the operation was a great success, but the patient died." PROMs are assessments of health related quality of life (HRQoL) that may be used to assess medical interventions. The EuroQol-5D (EQ-5D), a generic, widely-used PROM, produces a single summary score based on patients' responses to a question in each of 5 domains -- mobility, usual activities, self care, pain and anxiety/ depression. The EQ-5D's summary score allows comparison of HRQoL across different clinical populations. Despite the increasing appreciation of PROMs in health research, this methodological advance has yet to impact the study of seniors' falls and fall-related injuries. Falls are the 5th greatest cause of death in the US and in Canada, with the direct cost exceeding $1 billion (CAN) annually. My own research puts the global burden of falls at > $23 billion annually. Two CIHR Institutes (Aging, IMHA) include fall prevention within their key research mandates. I propose to use PROMS to examine the association between HRQoL determined from a 12 month period and the clinical characteristics in senior fallers aged 70 years and older. Furthermore, I will assess whether HRQoL at baseline predicts health resource utilisation (HRU) over a 12-month followup period. My study is highly relevant given the magnitude of the burden of falls and the scarcity of PROMs research in this field in Canada. The EQ-5D and falls-related HRU data will enable me to determine which of the comprehensive baseline measures used at the Falls Clinic explain variation in HRQoL and HRU. As such, it will provide important data for policy makers allocating resources for falls prevention.

TitreApplicationTitle: The molecular mechanisms of microgliosis in GM2 ganglioside lysosomal storage diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL BEHAVIOUR; FLOW CYTOMETRY; GM2 GANGLIOSIDOSIS; HEXOSAMINIDASE B; INFLAMMATION; LYSOSOMAL STORAGE DISEASE; MICROGLIA; NEURODEGENERATION; PURINERGIC RECEPTORS; QRT-PCR
Abstract-Résumé: Lysosomal storage diseases cause progressive neurodegeneration and are characterized by an inherited genetic error in the breakdown and recycling of carbohydrate-linked lipids, which presents most prominently in cells of the central nervous system. Buildup of these substances in neurons leads to neuron dysfunction and death, as well as the over-activation of cells that act as the garbage collectors of the CNS known as microglia. Substances leaking from dying neurons interact with receptors on microglia to provide homing and 'eat me' signals that direct microglia to areas of damaged neurons. Unfortunately, the positive clearing activities of microglia are also associated with exacerbation of neuron cell death.  This research focuses on the role of the microglia in the perpetuation of  neuron death in lysosomal storage disease and how certain receptors on the cell surface of microglia participate in this process. We plan to knock out a receptor that is normally upregulated on activated microglia and determine how this affects the clinical progression of a mouse model of Sandhoff disease. This receptor could be a potential pharmaceutical target to inhibit the development of disease, and thus have an important impact on individuals living with lysosomal storage disease.

Keywords-MotsClés: ASSISTED; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CLINICAL RESEARCH; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; INFERTILITY; PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION; REPRODUCTIVE TECHNIQUES; RISK FACTORS; STROKE; THROMBOEMBOLIC DISEASE; WOMEN'S HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Infertility, which affects 1 in 6 couples, is defined as failure to become pregnant after intercourse for one year. The diagnosis can include enormous medical, emotional and financial consequences. In the last 30 years fertility treatments, such as artificial insemination and in-vitro fertilization, have helped millions of women become pregnant.  These treatments are popular, but can be complicated, and focus attention on achieving pregnancy rather than the long-term effect on general health. Decision making, to an extreme degree, is driven by the hope of a successful pregnancy.  We wonder whether the hormones used in fertility treatments might lead to serious heart and lung disease later in life. There are many reasons to consider this a possible risk. Studies have shown an association between long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and; a) certain causes of infertility; b) estrogen supplements in women of all ages; c) pregnancy complications such as gestational hypertension or diabetes; and d) direct circulation damage from hormone exposure. The potential risk is also relevant given societal changes that translate to more people delaying a family until an older age, when they have a higher likelihood of infertility or heart disease.  Regardless of eventual success, fertility specialists rarely follow their patients into older age to monitor for unforeseen side effects. In addition, cardiologists who care for older women may neglect to take an obstetrical history. For example, the onset of a heart attack in middle-age usually prompts a search for immediate triggers and rarely a search for remote exposures.  A better understanding of the long-term risks would help inform women's decision making in the use of reproductive assistance and inform care in women who have used fertility therapy.  The goal of this study is to assess if women who had pregnancies associated with reproductive assistance are at higher risk of premature cardiovascular and lung disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterizing emergence from general anesthesia through human intracranial neurophysiology.
Keywords-MotsClés: AROUSAL; CLINICAL MONITORING; CONSCIOUSNESS; EEG; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; EMERGENCE; GENERAL ANESTHESIA; HUMAN SUBJECTS; INTRACRANIAL RECORDINGS; NEUROSCIENCE
Abstract-Résumé: General anesthesia is widely used across Canada, but its effects are poorly understood, and it carries a significant risk of serious side effects, including cognitive impairment, delirium, and morbidity. My project will characterize the effects of anesthesia on the human brain, with the goal of developing better patient monitoring. We have a rare opportunity to record electrical signals from within the brain of human patients, and this data will be examined in relation to behavioural measures in order to provide a link between neural signals and level of consciousness. This research will result in better patient care, as it will enable anesthesiologists to better assess the physiological and mental states of the patient undergoing surgery, and adjust dosage so as to minimize side effects accordingly.

Abstract-Résumé: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) accounts for 50% or more of all trauma deaths, and an estimated 2% of the population live with lifelong disabilities resulting from TBI.  There appears to be a direct link between TBI and violence, which itself is a major issue for Canadians.  The goal of the research team is to undertake a coordinated and comprehensive program of research based on the hypothesis that vulnerable populations carry the mutual burden of violence and brain injury for which there are shared, modifiable risk factors. The team will initiate research in five areas:identifying and characterizing high risk populations vulnerable to violence and TBI; studying the relationship between alcohol, cannabis, violence and TBI; examining TBI and violence in the homeless; examining TBI in sport; and examining cultural factors that propagate the problem.  As well, the research team will undertake program and product evaluations and undertake knowledge translation activities designed to transform information into action.

TitreApplicationTitle: Trauma System Development in Canada:  Overcoming the challenges of geography through an evaluation of structure and process.
Keywords-MotsClés: GIS - GEOSPATIAL INFORMATION SYSTEM; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; IMPLEMENTATION BARRIERS; PRELIMINARY CARE; RURAL HEALTH; TRAUMA SYSTEMS
Abstract-Résumé: Severely injured patients have a lower mortality risk if cared for in a trauma centre. Thus survival is dependent on an integrated regional system of care to assure these patients are identified, supported and rapidly transported to a trauma centre. Trauma centres are only located in urban regions, limiting prompt access to the 20% of Canadians living in rural areas. Due to the distribution of trauma patients and centres, 50% of patients receive preliminary care at non-designated centres before transfer to a trauma centre. As trauma system configuration and preliminary care might have significant impact on assuring the "right patient gets to the right place at the right time," we propose the following overarching objectives:  I. To assess the relationship between trauma system structure and process II. To optimize the preliminary care of the patient with major injury  The findings will influence changes in policy & practice to improve access and quality of trauma care.

Abstract-Résumé: The primary goal of this team grant is to create a novel program  of collaborative research between universities, government  agencies, and end users, for the development of innovative  technologies to prevent hip fractures and other fall-related  injuries in older adults. Our efforts involve an integrated set of  research and demonstration projects in long-term care (LTC)  living facilities. Collectively, these projects address two  fundamental barriers to the prevention of fall-related injuries in  older adults: (1) the need to develop technologies (such as  wearable sensors and video-based networks) for reliably  detecting falls, and providing objective, real-time data on the  cause and circumstances of these events; and (2) the need to  develop, implement, and evaluate improved technologies (such  as compliant flooring and active wearable hip protectors) for  reducing the risk for injury in the event of a fall. Our specific  objectives are: (1) To utilize networks of video cameras  to record the cause and characteristics of real-life falls; (2) To  develop wearable fall recorders to accurately detect and log the  onset of a fall, and provide high-resolution data on body  segment movements during the initiation, descent, and impact  stages of falls; (3) To obtain new knowledge on the relative  importance of established and novel risk factors for falls in the  LTC environment; (4) To test the effect of force-attenuating  compliant flooring on mobility, falls, and fall-related injuries in  high-risk environments; and (5) To develop and evaluate ¿smart¿  next-generation wearable hip protectors, which incorporate (a)  integrated sensors to monitor user adherence and proper  positioning in wearing the device, and (b) active, inflatable  elements for improved force attenuation to protect against  fracture.
