TitreApplicationTitle: The Structure and Function of Smurf Ubiquitin Ligases
Keywords-MotsClés: BMP; CELL SIGNALLING; MORPHOGENESIS; PLANAR CELL POLARITY; SMURFS; UBIQUITIN LIGASES; WNT
Abstract-Résumé: To make the body plan and organs of all animals, specialized proteins are used to pass signals between the cells and thereby control cell behaviour. These signalling proteins employ complex communication networks that can become garbled in complex diseases such as cancer.  To control the wiring of these networks enzymes termed ubiquitin ligases can act to remove specific nodes of the communication net, thus regulating information flow.  In the previous term of this grant we showed that two closely related ubiquitin ligases, Smurf1 and Smurf2, play key roles in regulating cell behaviour.  We also began to dissect at the atomic level how these enzymes work to get rid of specific nodes in communication networks. The current grant builds on this groundwork and is focussed on further defining how Smurfs control the wiring of communication networks in the cell to regulate complex cell behaviours and at understanding how these Smurf enzymes remove nodes.

ClasseRechercheFR: THERAPIE DU CANCER EN GENERAL; RECHERCHES MULTIDISCIPLINAIRES
TitreApplicationTitle: Chemical Biology of Amanitin-Induced Transcriptional Inhibiton
Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSIS; CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; CHEMICAL BIOLOGY; TRANSCRIPTION
Abstract-Résumé: Most chemotherapeutics act by associating with DNA which is being copied into messenger RNA by the cellular machinery - a process known as transcription.  RNA polymerase is a multi-component protein machine that is physically bound to (touching) the DNA and catalyzes transcription.  When chemotherapeutics like cis-platin, chlorambucil, and mitomycin bind to DNA, they not only damage the DNA but stall RNA polymerase on the DNA and prevent it from moving along the DNA, thus inhibiting transcription.  Other cellular proteins sense that RNA polymerase is stalled and degrade it to remove it from the DNA in order to repair the damaged DNA.  When there is too much damage to the DNA, cells undergo programmed cell death (called apoptosis), a desired effect of the chemotherapy.  Therefore understanding how RNA polymerase stalls and is degraded will provide essential knowledge for understanding how chemotherapies cause cell death.  Amanitin, a toxin that is found in mushrooms, is a specific RNA polymerase inhibitor that causes it to stall, be degraded, and ultimately kills cells. Our publications uniquely qualify us to prepare synthetic amanitins to probe RNA polymerase inhibition, degradation, and cell death.  This understanding, along with our synthetic know-how, enables us to investigate amanitin as a targeted therapeutic.   Targeted therapies, which link toxins to anticancer agents like antibodies (e.g. mylotarg), and bioreductive drugs (e.g. mitomycins) are now used in patient management.  Although many drugs are being targeted to cancer, amanitin has not been investigated in this manner.  Here, we propose a unique approach that combines both bioreduction and targeting to investigate the possibility of using amanitin to kill cancer cells.  This proposal therefore will use amanitin to explore both fundamental aspects of cell death as well as investigate its potential for use in anticancer therapeutic development.

TitreApplicationTitle: Global approaches to unravel PP2A function
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL GROWTH AND PROLIFERATION; CEREBRAL CAVERNOUS MALFORMATIONS; MASS SPECTROMETRY; PHOSPHORYLATION; PROTEIN SERINE/THREONINE PHOSPHATASES; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; QUANTITATIVE PROTEOMICS; TARGET OF RAPAMYCIN
Abstract-Résumé: We aim to better understand the function of an enzyme called PP2A.  PP2A is a tumor suppressor, and is also implicated in Alzheimer disease. PP2A relays information from the outside to the inside of cells by removing phosphate groups on other proteins.  Because of this activity, it is called a phosphatase. Phosphatases such as PP2A oppose the action of another enzyme family called kinases.  Deregulation of the phosphatase versus kinase balance is detrimental to the cells and often leads to cancer and other diseases.  We aim to identify the protein targets for PP2A as a first step to understanding its physiological role. We have already identified many proteins that can associate with PP2A by using mass spectrometry, a technique that measures with great precision the patterns that can uniquely identify a protein, in a manner similar to how fingerprints can uniquely identify an individual.    One group of proteins binding to PP2A is associated to a disease called cerebral cavernous malformations, which is linked to an array of problems, including headaches, seizures, dizziness and strokes. Our central hypothesis is that PP2A may remove phosphate groups on some of the proteins implicated in the disease, and that this phosphate removal changes the activity of the proteins.    We will continue our analysis regarding the biological functions of PP2A, and in particular, we will determine whether the proteins that we have identified as associating with PP2A are directly targeted by the activity of the enzyme.  We will also investigate further the role of PP2A on key processes involved implicated in cerebral cavernous malformations.  This study may lead to better therapeutic avenues for patients afflicted with this disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Long QT Syndrome in Northern British Columbia:Understanding the impact
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; COHORT STUDY; COMMUNITY BASED RESEARCH; COPY NUMBER VARIANT ANALYSIS; LINKAGE ANALYSIS; LONG QT SYNDROME
Abstract-Résumé: Long QT Syndrome (LQTS) is a hereditary conduction defect of the heart named for the region of the ECG noted to be prolonged in those affected, predisposing to an irregular heart rhythm which may lead to cardiac arrest and sudden death. Although usually rare the Gitxsan of Northern British Columbia, have a disproportionately high rate of this condition. Events can be avoided with medical management, appropriate health care and in particular, an avoidance of triggers such as a large number of medications which alter the QT interval increasing the risk. The genetics of the condition is complicated in that at least 12 known genes are responsible. As we embarked on our baseline study we had identified the novel mutation causing LQTS in the potassium channel gene, KCNQ1 and subsequently confirmed the pathogenesis. As a result of a community based research initiative, more than 40 community members have been identified with the mutation and another 240 community members have volunteered to participate in the research.  The current study will focus on understanding the clinical impact of the condition by following our cohort for another 5 years for cardiac events, hearing loss and even diabetes which can result from mutations in this gene. We will explore the low rate of compliance of medical treatment (beta blockers), the low rate of participation of men in testing and the effect of having the condition during child birth and surgery. Furthermore, this study will build on our first study during which culturally integrated model of genetic counseling was developed.  The current study will utilize that information to develop a community screening program for those who have not already had the opportunity to participate.

TitreApplicationTitle: Delineation of Hic1 function in skeletogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: ARTHRITIS; BONE FORMATION; BONE MORPHOGENESIS; CARTILAGE FORMATION; CONGENITAL MALFORMATIONS; OSTEOPOROSIS; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; SKELETAL DEVELOPMENT; SKELETAL DISEASE; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Vitamin-A and its metabolites, the retinoids, play important roles in the development and maintenance of the skeleton.  Excess intake of retinoids (typically through vitamin supplements) has been associated with congenital defects of the skeleton and more recently it has been linked to osteoporosis and an increased incidence in bone fracture.  In some studies, vitamin A intake just above the recommended daily allowance (RDA) was associated with increased fracture risk and multiple groups have advocated that the RDA for vitamin A needs to be reevaluated and possibly reduced.  Derivatives of retinoids have also long been used to treat various skin aliments and long-term increased intake has consistently been associated with decreased bone mass and aberrant bone formation at sites of tendon-bone attachment.      The retinoids function through the retinoic acid receptors (RARs), to regulate the expression of genes.  In a series of studies we have shown that the RA pathway regulates the formation of bone and cartilage.  However, the mechanisms through which this pathway influences these cellular programs is unclear.  More recently, we have discovered several genes that the retinoids regulate and herein we will focus on one particular RAR target gene named Hypermethylated in cancer 1 or Hic1.  This gene was originally identified because it is silenced in a variety of tumors in humans.  We have recently generated a mouse in which this gene can be removed in various tissues, and removal of this gene in the developing limb or skull leads to various skeletal defects. This proposal aims to define the function of Hic1 in the formation and maintenance of a functional skeleton.  Information from this research will provide greater insight into these processes and the identification of potentially useful clinical targets for the treatment of diseases such as arthritis and osteoporosis, and strategies to promote skeletal repair following injury.

TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation of protein trafficking by epithelial polarity proteins
Keywords-MotsClés: APKC; CDC42; CRUMBS; ENDOCYTOSIS; EPITHELIAL POLARITY; NEUROECTODERM; PAR COMPLEX; RECYCLING; RETROMER
Abstract-Résumé: Epithelial cells are a fundamental building block of the human body and form a major component of most organs. Epithelial cells align like cobblestones to form sheets. These epithelial sheets can be shaped into a multitude of different forms during development that cover our body (the skin) or compose many organs such as the lungs, liver, pancreas, gut, blood vessels and many others. The significance of epithelial tissues to give the human and animal body its structure and to determine the physiology of many organs is reflected in the many diseases that are caused by defects in epithelial cells including approximately 80% of all human cancers. The ability of epithelial cells to form sheets is at the heart of the ability of epithelia to fulfill their divers functions. This ability of epithelial cells depends on the asymmetric structural organization of each individual cells that is referred to as apical basal polarity. Thus, each cobblestone has a front and a back end, and all front and back ends need to be aligned to form a functioning epithelial sheet. Our laboratory has investigated the genetic and molecular mechanisms that allow epithelial cells to build their apical basal polarity for over 20 years. We and many colleagues in this field have made great progress in understanding how this polarity comes about. However, many gaps in our understanding of this fundamental aspect of all animal life remain. We have recently made an exciting discovery that links two of the cellular machineries that are at the core of epithelial polarity. This applications request funding to fully explore this link, which will deepen our understanding of epithelial polarity, and therefore will enhance our ability to identify biomakers or therapeutic targets for diseases that are caused by defects in epithelial cell architecture.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular dynamics at the postsynaptic density
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL CULTURE; CELLULAR MODELS OF LEARNING AND MEMORY; GABA RECEPTOR; GLUTAMATE RECEPTOR; NEUROBIOLOGY; POSTSYNAPTIC DENSITY DYNAMICS; SUBCELLULAR TRAFFICKING
Abstract-Résumé: Learning and memory occur by changes in strengths of connections in the brain, in part by changes in the local density of neurotransmitter receptors at the postsynaptic density. We are studying two major types of neurotransmitter receptors, excitatory NMDA and inhibitory GABA receptors. Excitatory receptors increase firing rates to the next nerve cell in a circuit, whereas inhibitory receptors reduce firing rates. A balance must be maintained for brain health. Over-activation of NMDA receptors contributes to damage during stroke, and impairment of GABA receptor transmission to epilepsy. Our goal is to understand how the local density and function of these neurotransmitter receptors is determined. For example, how do individual receptor subunits and scaffolding proteins contribute to receptor trafficking? How does activity modulate this process? These studies may aid in the development of better treatments for stroke and epilepsy. Given the central role of the NMDA receptor in learning and memory, we also hope that this research will lead to the design of molecular and pharmacological therapies for improvement of learning, to maintain cognitive function in neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Charecterization of "memory" NK cells induced by viral pathogens
Keywords-MotsClés: GENETICS; HOST:PATHOGEN INTERACTION; INTRACELLULAR BACTERIA; SUSCEPTIBILITY TO INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: More than a century after Pasteur put forth his microbial theory of disease and decades after the advent of antibiotics,infectious disease remains the second leading cause of death worldwide. Furthermore, susceptibility to infectious agents varies widely among individuals, which can impact therapy and public health management. Disease severity is largely dependent on genetic variation in the host but also influenced by genetic variation in the pathogen. This project aims to identify common variants in the human population that confer susceptibility to the intracellular pathogen, Francisella, the highly infective, causative agent of tularemia. As a potential bio-warfare agent, Francisella represents a unique threat to public health and safety; it also serves as an excellent model to study the pathogenesis of intracellular bacteria. We will use a high throughput screen to assess various cellular phenotypes, including invasion, replication and cell death in cell lines derived from >500 individuals of diverse ethnic backgrounds. With this method, we can examine the association between natural polymorphisms and variation in response to infection without the confounding effects of exposure level, pathogen strain or treatment availability. The identified variant alleles will be characterized at the cellular level, through various RNA interference and over-expression approaches, to probe the mechanistic basis of how host genetic variation influences susceptibility to Francisella. A greater understanding of the cellular host response to infection, with particular emphasis on components of innate immunity and inflammation, will begin to elucidate the host genetic contribution to microbial disease. In addition, examining the natural occurring genetic variants will provide some insight into natural selection by infectious pathogens throughout human evolution and the potential negative impact of such "infection protective" alleles on inflammatory diseases or autoimmunity.

TitreApplicationTitle: Le champ francophone de la désinstitutionalisation en santé mentale : enjeux sociohistoriques, normes et pratiques, 1920-1980
Keywords-MotsClés: CANADIENS-FRANCAIS; DESINSTITUTIONNALISATION; HISTOIRE DE LA SANTE; NORMES MEDICALES ET PARAMEDICALES; RELATIONS PATIENT-SOIGNANT; SANTE MENTALE; SERVICES COMMUNAUTAIRES; SOCIOLOGIE DE LA SANTE; SOINS PSYCHIATRIQUES; STIGMATISATION
Abstract-Résumé: Cette recherche d'histoire et de sociologie de la sante s'interesse a la periode 1920-1980. Les institutions psychiatriques du Quebec, d'Ottawa et du Nouveau-Brunswick seront au cur de notre enquete, afin de decouvrir le contexte canadien-francais entourant la transition interinstitutionnelle des patients psychiatriques vivant en institution asilaire et diriges vers des pavillons satellites au sein de leur communaute. Notre equipe reunit des chercheurs des disciplines de la criminologie, de l'histoire, de la sociologie, du travail social et des sciences infirmieres. L'expertise de chacun - sur les politiques d'hygiene mentale, la deviance, le controle social, les medicaments psychotropes, la sante mentale, les soins infirmiers et la marginalisation des malades mentaux - favorisent une demarche methodologique multidisciplinaire permettant de mettre au jour un patrimoine materiel et immateriel en matiere de sante mentale present au Canada.  Nous voulons explorer les relations avec la parentele, les politiques publiques en sante mentale, le developpement des therapies, les reactions sociales, le cadre systemique qui est mis en place au cours du 20e siecle dans les provinces du Quebec, de l'Ontario et du Nouveau-Brunswick. A l'heure ou on remet en question les ressources communautaires dans le but de transferer les malades mentaux dans des logements dits supervises, notre etude fournira une meilleure lecture des tenants et des aboutissants d'une premiere vague de desinstitutionnalisation qui a marque les annees soixante et soixante-dix. Elle produira egalement une analyse critique de cette periode de transition en matiere de sante mentale, evaluera les consequences des transferts sur la vie des patients sortis des asiles ainsi que le role des intervenants ayant la tache de les accompagner et, finalement, soulevera des pistes d'intervention quant aux nouveaux enjeux sociaux concernant la prise en charge des malades mentaux.

TitreApplicationTitle: Function and regulation of Numb alternative splicing in cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: ALTERNATIVE SPLICING; CELL BIOLOGY; NOTCH PATHWAY; NUMB; RECEPTOR TRAFFICKING; SIGNALING PATHWAYS; TUMOR SUPRESSOR
Abstract-Résumé: In a normal cell, growth and proliferation is regulated by signals that come from the surrounding tissue and neighbouring cells. Signals from outside are interpreted by protein receptors that span the limiting membrane of the cell (half inside and half outside). A signal received outside is transmitted inside by the receptor which then passes the signal on to molecules in the cell that control cell behavior. Once a receptor molecule is activated it is quickly pulled inside the cell where it is destroyed and the signal is stopped. This is process called receptor down regulation. In some cancers, this control mechanism is lost, and the receptor stays at the surface of the cell, and continues to send signals. As a result the cell divides, or migrates and invades surrounding issue inappropriately. The focus of this proposal is a molecule called Numb, that controls the down regulation of receptors. There is evidence from our lab and others that the Numb protein is lost or that altered forms of the protein are present in human breast, lung and brain tumors. We hypothesize that these changes in the Numb molecule disrupts the normal down regulation of receptors and contributes to tumor formation. In this proposal we will use biochemical and cell biological studies to: 1. Investigate what causes the altered forms of Numb observed in cancer cells. 2. To determine how changes in normal Numb activity affects the growth of human tumor cells. This information will help us to evaluate whether changes in the Numb molecule is a useful way to identify tumors that have a failure of receptor down regulation. This could lead to the development of new cancer drugs that specifically target cell receptors in an effort to shut them off. In addition, it will also give us specific information on how Numb becomes altered in human cancer, and whether restoration of normal Numb activity is useful and potentially achievable therapeutic goal.

OrgNm: Ottawa Hospital Research Institute/Institut de recherche de l'Hôpital d'Ottawa
TitreApplicationTitle: Weaning and Variability Evaluation (WAVE)- a multicenter evaluation of altered heart rate and respiratory rate variability to predict extubation failure
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPLEX SYSTEMS SCIENCE; CRITICAL CARE MEDICINE; FAILED EXTUBATION; VARIABILITY ANALYSIS; WEANING
Abstract-Résumé: Knowing when to liberate patients from mechanical ventilation (i.e. removal of breathing or endotracheal tube or extubation) is critically important, as both prolonged ventilation and failed extubation are both associated with harm and risk of death. Our objective is to improve the safety of extubation by harnessing hidden information contained in the patterns of variation of heart and respiratory rate measured over intervals-in-time. Currently, to assess a patient's ability to be extubated, a spontaneous breathing trial (SBT) is routinely performed, where the level of ventilator support is reduced, and their response is observed in order to help predict if they will tolerate extubation (i.e. complete removal of ventilator support). Given that health is associated with a high degree of variation of physiologic parameters (e.g. heart and respiratory rate), and illness & stress are associated with a loss of variability, we aim to uncover the loss of variation as a measure of stress during SBT's. We hypothesize that maintaining stable heart rate and respiratory rate variability (HRV and RRV) throughout the SBT will predict subsequent successful extubation, and conversely, a reduction in either HRV or RRV manifest during a SBT predicts extubation failure. A pilot study has demonstrated feasibility, and compelling preliminary results. A website, centralized data storage and analysis, and a trans-disciplinary team of scientists are in place to definitively test this novel technology. Determination of when to extubate critically ill patients remains a high-stakes clinical challenge; and improved prediction of extubation failure has potential to save lives and reduce costs in critically ill patients.

NomDuComitéFR: Investigation clinique - B : Arthrite, os, peau et cartilage
TitreApplicationTitle: The anti-inflammatory activities of prostaglandin E2 and cyclic AMP-elevating agents in human neutrophils: Delineation of molecular pathways.
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASES; INFECTION; INFLAMMATION; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; RESOLUTION OF INFLAMMATION; SIGNALING PATHWAYS
Abstract-Résumé: Preventing tissue damage in arthritis: Validation of a new approach.   For the 4 million canadians suffering from arthritis, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are their most prescribed class of medication. These compounds block swelling and pain, in part through inhibition of an enzyme termed cyclooxygenase, responsible for the generation of prostaglandins. On the other hand, the use of NSAIDs is associated with severe side effects ranging from gastric ulcers to kidney malfunctions, and to death in extreme cases. Moreover, NSAIDs do not slow down progression of chronic inflammatory diseases as they do not stop the cells responsible for bone and cartilage destruction.   Recent in vitro observations have justified a strong interest for the development of cAMP elevating agents as anti-inflammatory drugs. Indeed, cAMP appears to be a strong anti-inflammatory signal in leukocytes, cells which are held responsible for tissue degradation in arthritis. We plan to test this approach in vivo with a selection of compounds known to increase intracellular cAMP levels, such as prostaglandin E2, in experimental models of arthritis and of inflammation. Results of this project may immediately find clinical potential as a treatment for slowing down disease progression.

TitreApplicationTitle: Glucocorticoid receptor and RORalpha in cartilage development and osteoarthritis
Keywords-MotsClés: CARTILAGE; GLUCOCORTICOID RECEPTOR; KNOCKOUT MICE; OSTEOARTHRITIS; RORALPHA; SKELETAL DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Growth and maturation of cartilage cells (chondrocytes) is strictly regulated to allow for normal development of the skeleton. Perturbation of these processes - for example, through gene mutations or adverse effects of drugs - usually leads to skeletal deformities and dwarfism. Moreover, altered maturation of chondrocytes has been linked to the process of osteoarthritis, a common and painful disease characterized by the loss of cartilage in our joints with enormous impact on both individual quality of life and our health care system. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms controlling both normal chondrocyte behavior and changed behavior during disease progression are not completely understood. Our preliminary results suggest important roles of two genes, named glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and RORalpha, in cartilage development. We will now study the roles of these genes in detail. We will first use genetic tools to specifically inactivate the two gene (individually and in combination) in cartilage of mice and examine the effects of these manipulations on skeletal growth and development. We will then induce osteoarthritis in these genetically manipulated mice using surgical techniques established in our laboratory. We will examine whether loss of GR, RORalpha or both protects from osteoarthritis or worsens disease progression. Parallel studies will be performed using samples of normal and osteoarthritic human cartilage obtained from surgeries. Finally, we will use cellular and biochemical techniques to determine the molecular mechanisms through which these two genes exert their effects in chondrocytes. Together these studies will yield insights into the processes that control skeletal physiology and disease progression and will contribute to new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches for management of osteoarthritis and other skeletal diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Structural determinants for the activation of the chemokine receptor CXCR4
Keywords-MotsClés: CXCL12; CXCR4; METHIONINE PROXIMITY ASSAY; PEPTIDE SYNTHESIS; PHOTOAFFINITY LABELLING; SDF1; SITE-DIRECTED MUTAGENESIS
Abstract-Résumé: Understanding the molecular machinery of the HIV co-receptor CXCR4 is essential for the successful development of improved HIV drugs with less side effects and resistance development.  CXCR4 is not only a target of HIV infection but is also essential for the correct development of the foetus and control of the immune system, therefore drugs are to be developed that do not interfere with the normal functions.  The present project is aimed towards this goal by elucidating the molecular machinery of the system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Neonatal oxygen exposure leads to premature aging of the vascular system and the kidneys: role in adult hypertension
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMMING; HYPERTENSION; OXIDATIVE STRESS; OXYGEN
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of mortality and morbidity in North America. Incidence of risk factors such as hypertension and renal disease increase steadily with advancing age. In fact, aging is now regarded as an independent risk factor for the development of cardiovascular diseases. Vascular aging is characterized by increased vascular stiffness and oxidative stress. Individuals born with growth restriction or prematurely are at increased risk of hypertension when reaching adulthood; the mechanisms underlying the long term cardiovascular consequences of early life are not completely understood but indicate a critical role for perinatal oxidative stress. This is further supported by recent data from our laboratory showing elevated blood pressure, vascular oxidative stress and enhanced vascular stiffness in adult rats exposed to high oxygen concentration in the newborn period. We therefore speculate that altered perinatal conditions, more specifically hyperoxic stress, leads to accelerated aging of the cardiovascular and the renal systems resulting in prematurely elevated blood pressure. To verify this hypothesis, we plan to study the impact of neonatal hyperoxic stress on indices of aging, both at the organ structural and functional level and at the cellular level. We will translate our experimental findings to the clinic and examine adults born prematurely for enhanced vascular stiffness and markers of aging in circulating cells from the blood. The proposed research should shed light on the mechanisms underlying major health issues: the impact of oxygen-related damage in prematurity to cardiovascular risks in adulthood and the overall concept of developmental programming of hypertension.

OrgNm: Research Institute of the McGill University Health Centre/Institut de recherche du Centre universitaire de santé McGill
TitreApplicationTitle: Th17/IL-17 specific mechanisms regulating inflammation and remodeling in allergic airways disease
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; ASTHMA; CELL CULTURE; CYOKINES; IMMUNOLOGY; RETROVIRAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence, morbidity and mortality of asthma have increased dramatically despite improved understanding of the disease. One important recent finding is that the newly identified inflammatory cells, so-called Th17 cells, may contribute to pathogenesis in asthma. Th17 cells produce large amounts of the inflammatory mediator, interleukin-17 (IL-17), which regulates recruitment of other cells to sites of inflammation. Data from human asthmatics suggest that Th17 cells and their protein products may play a particularly important role in more severe, steroid-resistant forms of asthma. However, the mechanisms by which these cells contribute to airway dysfunction are not understood. One of our main goals with this project is to take advantage of rodent models to better understand how Th17 cells and their cytokine product, IL-17, contribute to allergic airways disease. We will exploit models we have developed in which we can control the timing of delivery to the airways of well-defined populations of asthma-inducing inflammatory cells. We will either remove IL-17 or, using unique methodologies developed in my laboratory, overproduce IL-17 in the airways of animals with experimentally induced allergic airways disease. With these techniques, we will define the contribution of Th17 cells and IL-17 to the functional and structural changes in allergic airways, in both acute and chronic asthma models. We will also assess how Th17 cells and IL-17 affect the response to steroid treatment. Finally, we have developed a new system to investigate how IL-17 interacts with another important mediator of allergic airways disease, IL-13. Using these novel methodologies, we are uniquely placed to better understand how Th17 cells and IL-17 regulate allergic airways disease.

ClasseRechercheFR: MALADIES INFECTIEUSES ET PARASITAIRES; MALADIES A VIRUS
TitreApplicationTitle: Immune regulatory role of host lipid mediators in pulmonary influenza infection
Keywords-MotsClés: ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY; ANIMAL MODEL; INFLUENZA; INNATE IMMUNITY; LIPID MEDIATORS; PULMONARY INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Influenza virus remains a persistent threat to humans causing 3-5 million cases of severe illness and around 500,000 deaths during a non-pandemic year. However, during pandemic influenza virus- associated mortality is drastically increased. For instance, the 1918 "Spanish" influenza pandemic killed 40 million people in just one year, the single greatest loss of human life in history. Intriguingly, most influenza-related mortality results from the host immune response rather than influenza virus itself. This highlights the importance of immune regulation in determining who is protected from the consequences of influenza infection. We have recently demonstrated that lipids produced by the host play a critical regulatory role in pulmonary tuberculosis infection. In the present proposal, we aim to investigate the immune-regulatory mechanism of host lipid mediators during pulmonary influenza infection. Considering the availability of pharmacologic interventions to manipulate levels of these lipids, our findings can translate directly into clinical interventions to selectively modulate pro-inflammatory cascade and its associated pathology. This may potentially be important during the influenza outbreak as an adjunct to anti-viral therapy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Combination pharmacotherapy for the management of pain in fibromyalgia
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTICONVULSANT; ANTIDEPRESSANT; CLINICAL TRIAL; COMBINATION PHARMACOTHERAPY; FIBROMYALGIA; PAIN
Abstract-Résumé: Pain is a major public health problem affecting one-third of the population and costing $165 billion/year in North America alone. Individual pain-relievers provide incomplete relief and can often produce troubling side effects. It has been suggested that combining different kinds of pain-relievers may improve effectiveness and reduce side effects. Some drug combinations have been proven better than each of their components alone. However, this theory has been tested for very few specific drug combinations. Studies show that, on their own, the antidepressant drug, duloxetine, and the antiseizure drug, pregabalin, partially relieve pain due to fibromyalgia. The main objective of this grant proposal is to determine whether using a combination of these two drugs relieves pain more effectively and/or causes less side effects than when using either drug alone. This objective will be met by conducting a clinical trial in patients with pain due to fibromyalgia. The research plan involves a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized crossover trial which compares chronic oral administration of a duloxetine/pregabalin combination to each drug alone in patients with fibromyalgia. During each of these treatment periods, drug dosage will be gradually increased to the highest possible dose, yet a dose which produces only minimal side effects. We expect to determine whether this combination is more beneficial than either drug alone. Future research using these methods will allow for the testing of other analgesic combinations for pain management.

TitreApplicationTitle: Stromal-epithelial interactions in the regulation of mammary gland development and in breast cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; DEVELOPMENT; MAMMARY GLAND; TRANSGENIC MICE; WNT-SIGNALLING
Abstract-Résumé: Our lab is concerned with the mechanisms that are used by mammals to control the development of the mammary gland (mice) or the breast (humans).  We are interested in these processes in embryonic animals, where mammary gland development begins, as well as in postnatal animals.  In particular, our studies examine a group of protein molecules, called the Wnts. These proteins are important in directing how the three-dimensional structure of many tissues and organs are organized and formed. This same group of molecules, when expressed incorrectly, can cause cancer in many tissues, including the breast.  We will, therefore, perform experiments in order to understand how this group of protein molecules direct the development of breast tissue as well as to learn how, when expressed incorrectly or due to mutations, they lead to malignant transformation and cancer in breast tissue.

NomDuComitéFR: Aspects biologiques et cliniques du vieillissement
TitreApplicationTitle: Characterizing the role of the endosomal/ lysosomal system in Alzheimer's Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE; CELL BIOLOGY; CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; ENDOCYTOSIS; FLUORESCENT PROTEIN TAGS; FREE FLOW ELECTROPHORESIS; TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION MICROSCOPY
Abstract-Résumé: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is the most common degenerative disease of the brain in adults.  Currently there are more than 500,000 Canadians with Alzheimer's disease, and this number is going to grow to rise to over 1 million within the next 20-30 years.  Most researchers believe that Alzheimer's disease is caused by a buildup in the brain of a toxic protein called beta-amyloid.  Beta-amyloid is produce by cutting up a large protein called the Amyloid Precursor Protein (APP).  This is done by 2 enzymes referred to as the beta-secretase (or BACE) and the gamma-secretase.  Although this field has been extensively studied, there is currently no agreement on where  beta-amyloid is produced.  We have found that APP and the gamma-secretase enzyme are present in a compartment in the cell called a lysosome, and we believe this may be an important site for making beta-amyloid.  Recently, we have discovered 3 completely new ways for APP to move inside a cell both to and from the lysosome. These include moving directly from the cell surface to the lysosome, from the Golgi to the lysosome, and from the lysosome back to the cell surface.  We have cloned APP and attached to it antibody binding sites and a fluorescent protein tag that allow us to directly see this protein moving in live cells under the microscope.  We will use Laser Scanning Confocal Microscopy and Total Internal Fluorescence Microscopy to study where APP moves inside the cell, where APP interacts with the gamma-secretase, and where beta amyloid is produced and secreted. We will compare this with APP mutants that cause early onset Alzheimer's disease. We will also investigate where in the cell APP interacts with the gamma secretase enzyme to produce beta-amyloid.    This work will help us understand the normal biology of APP and beta amyloid production, which we hope will allow us to design better treatments for Alzheimer's disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification of autosomal recessive mutations associated with developmental abnormalities through next-generation resequencing
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; DEVELOPMENTAL GENETICS; GENETICS OF BIRTH DEFECTS; GENOMICS; NEXT-GENERATION SEQUENCING; WHOLE GENOME EXOME CAPTURE
Abstract-Résumé: Mental retardation (MR) (or intellectual disability) is the most frequent severe handicap of childhood, affecting 1-3% of the population. With its high burden for families, its high cost for society, and the lack of an etiological diagnosis in more than half of patients, MR remains one of the most important unsolved problems in medicine. Several observations indicate that genetic factors play an important role in the development of these disorders. We propose to validate new approaches that allow the study of thousands of genes at once for the exploration of the genetic causes of MR. We will focus our attention on 18 families with at least 2 sibs with MR. Working with such families increases the likelihood of identifying genetic changes. We will try to identify the genetic changes that cause MR in these families by dissecting the sequence of virtually all genes of the affected individuals. Understanding the genetic basis of MR is an important step toward improving diagnostic accuracy and implementing novel preventive strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Hemi-Arthroplasty of the Elbow: The Effect of Implant Surface Design and Materials on Joint Kinematics and Contact Mechanics
Keywords-MotsClés: ARTHRITIS; BIOMECHANICS; ELBOW; FRACTURES; IMPLANTS
Abstract-Résumé: Replacement of the diseased human joint with artificial implants is a routine procedure in orthopaedic surgery.  At the elbow, complete implant systems (i.e. generally consisting of metal on plastic articulations that replace both sides of the joint) have been developed, typically for the management of arthritis. Replacement of one side of the articulation or hemi-arthroplasty is advantageous as less bone is violated. Hence, the surgery is less complicated and therefore less invasive and potentially safer. However, wear of the native joint cartilage on the un-replaced joint surface may lead to failure of the partial joint replacement. The overall goal of this application is to investigate these implant systems for the elbow with special interest in determining the influence of surface shape and materials on joint function and the potential for cartilage wear.  We will employ our well established laboratory-based experimental testing protocols to optimise these implants prior to employing them in patients. We hypothesize that (1) an optimal combination of shape and materials can be designed for these implants that restore function of the elbow to that of the normal state; (2) implant surface shape and positioning influence the potential for cartilage wear due to abnormal and increased joint contact forces: an optimal tolerance zone can be defined to minimize cartilage stresses. This research will lead to less bulky, minimally invasive implants, permitting the preservation of more bone than is currently achieved, and ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes.  In addition, the new knowledge acquired on the interaction between the synthetic implant surfaces and cartilage will have widespread implications for all joint replacements.

TitreApplicationTitle: Tissue engineering- and femtosecond laser assisted corneal endothelial transplantation
Keywords-MotsClés: CORNEAL ENDOTHELIAL DECOMPENSATION; CORNEAL GRAFT REJECTION - CORNEAL GRAFT FAILURE; CORNEAL TRANSPLANTATION - AGING; DEEP LAMELLAR ENDOTHELIAL KERATOPLASTY; FEMTOSECOND LASER; TISSUE ENGINEERING - CORNEAL ENDOTHELIAL CELL CULTURE
Abstract-Résumé: The cornea is the transparent protective layer in front of the colored (blue, brown, etc.) iris. When the internal part of the cornea (called the corneal endothelium) is diseased or damaged (for instance due to a cataract surgery complication), a severe and painful blindness results. The only treatment is corneal transplantation: 41.5% of the 57,736 corneal transplantations performed each year in Canada and the US are aimed at the replacement of the corneal endothelium.  Our goal is to improve significantly the outcome of corneal transplantation for endothelial diseases. Thanks to tissue-engineering technological advances, a highly functional corneal transplant will be reconstructed from the patient's own natural cells, thus eliminating the risk for rejection (rejection can occur when the transplant comes from another human being). Tissue-engineering will allow to significantly decrease the waiting times for corneal transplantation. The transplant will also be cut and shaped using a femtosecond laser prior to its insertion in the patient's eye, allowing for additional improvement in the quality of the vision after transplantation.

ResearchClassEN: LIPOPROTEINS, LIPID TRANSPORT; METABOLISM AND NUTRITION
ClasseRechercheFR: LIPOPROTEINES, TRANSPORT LIPIDIQUE; METABOLISME ET NUTRITION
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular characterization of esterase Es-x
Keywords-MotsClés: ATHEROSCLEROSIS; GENETIC ENGINEERING; LIPOLYSIS; NAFLD; TYPE 2 DIABETES; VLDL SECRETION
Abstract-Résumé: Triacylglycerol (TG, generally referred to as fat) is the most concentrated form of energy storage available for mammals. Excessive fat storage is manifested as obesity, which is a major health problem in Canada. Increased fat storage also augments secretion of lipoproteins carrying bad cholesterol (LDL-cholesterol) into blood stream. High fat levels thus contribute to development of atherosclerosis and heart disease and stroke. Therefore, there is substantial pharmacological interest in enzymes that control TG metabolism in tissues. We have characterized a protein, named Es-x, that plays a role in the intracellular fat metabolism. Our objective is to introduce more of this protein into the liver in animal models and study the effect of this protein on lipid metabolism (fat metabolism in particular). We also plan to investigate lipid metabolism in an animal model in which the protein has been genetically deleted. The research proposed in this application will yield better understanding of how fat metabolism is regulated. The proposed research could become important in designing new therapeutic approaches for decreasing fat synthesis and/or secretion.

TitreApplicationTitle: Magnetic Resonance PARACEST Imaging of In-vivo Protease Activity
Keywords-MotsClés: ALZHEIMER DISEASE; CHEMICAL EXCHANGE; CONTRAST AGENTS; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; PARACEST; PROTEASE
Abstract-Résumé: The impending threat of Alzheimer disease looms large as the health care system struggles to cope with increased demands from an aging population.  Alzheimer disease is the most common neurodegenerative disease in adults.  It currently afflicts about 500,000 Canadians and represents a tremendous burden on our society.  If no treatments are developed it will affect 1 million Canadians within the next 25 years.  Conquering this disease requires immediate investment in both therapeutic strategies and methods for early detection.  Using magnetic resonance imaging, we can create pictures of the human body that show Alzheimer disease progression.  However, very early detection will require the use of compounds that identify the earliest sub-cellular changes.  Recently a new method to generate contrast in MR images was discovered.  The method involves the injection of a compound that can be targeted to proteins in the body.  The physical mechanism that produces contrast using these new compounds is different than the mechanism that produces contrast for compounds already used for clinical MR imaging.  Although the new compounds are promising, there are also challenges related to detection sensitivity in tissue.  However, we have recently discovered a new formulation of these compounds that may result in much greater detection sensitivity in tissue.  Therefore, the purpose of this work is to develop these new compounds in combination with a novel MR imaging method that will allow detection of a specific protein that is found in high concentrations in subjects with Alzheimer disease.  These studies will be completed in a preclinical model of Alzheimer disease using a very high magnetic field imaging system.  Such compounds may provide a means for the early detection of Alzheimer disease by targeting the earliest cellular changes.

OrgNm: Centre hospitalier de l'Université de Montréal (CHUM)
TitreApplicationTitle: Testing the effects of radiofrequency ablation following endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms: An alternative method to decrease recurrences?
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGRAPHY; ANIMAL MODELS; BRAIN ANEURYSM; ENDOTHELIAL DENUDATION; ENDOVASCULAR TREATMENT; RADIOFREQUENCY ABLATION
Abstract-Résumé: A cerebral aneurysm is an abnormal bulge or "ballooning" of the wall of an artery of the brain. An estimated 600000 Canadians have a cerebral aneurysm. About 3000 will suffer rupture from their aneurysm per year, with potentially catastrophic outcome. Most people (2/3) will die or suffer permanent disabilities; 50% of survivors will experience considerable neuropsychological dysfunction. Endovascular embolization is a minimally invasive procedure used to treat aneurysms. This involves making a small hole in a groin artery and driving a small tube up to the brain aneurysm under X-Ray guidance. Through the tube, small platinum coils or stents (metallic mesh tubes) are deposited in or near the aneurysm to cause the aneurysm to clot off. Although well-tolerated by patients, the biggest problem is that the aneurysm are not always completely healed, with as high as 20-40% recurrence rate. Even though nearly 15 years have elapsed since the initial clinical trial that led to approval of the platinum coil for treatment of brain aneurysms, important shortcomings remain that have negative impact on patient care. Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) is a widely used medical procedure that generates heat at the end of a probe. The heat generated induces endothelial injury. Mechanisms of recurrences are still poorly understood, but we have shown that they relate to inhibition of endothelial invasion of the blood clot that forms in the aneurysm after coil occlusion. We believe that RFA could be used to promote complete healing. RFA can be performed under image guidance, and could likely be readily combined with ET of aneurysms to improve results. In recent pilot experiments, we have found that aneurysms heal better when ET is combined with RFA. However, we need to examine and understand the basic underlying changes occurring in the blood vessels as a result of using RFA before we can translate it to the treatment of aneurysms.

TitreApplicationTitle: Genetics and genomics of the antimycobacterial activity of vitamin D.
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CHIP-SEQ; CYP24 INHIBITORS; GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING; INNATE IMMUNITY; MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS; TARGET VALIDATION; VITAMIN D
Abstract-Résumé: Tuberculosis (TB) has been resurgent, with approx. 9 million cases and 1.7 million deaths in 2004, and represents the leading cause of death from a curable disease. M. tuberculosis has evolved to replicate within macrophages - the cells designed to kill it. Macrophages are sites of vitamin D action, and there is broad evidence that vitamin D modulates macrophage responses to TB. Vitamin D was discovered as the curative agent of nutritional rickets, which arises from insufficient uptake of dietary calcium. Work in the 1820's showed that cod liver oil or sunbathing cured rickets. Indeed, vitamin D can be produced by moderate exposure of skin to solar ultraviolet B radiation. Notably, cod liver oil was used to treat TB in 1849, and Niels Finsen won the 1903 Nobel Prize for showing that UVB could be used to treat cutaneous TB. As a result of sun avoidance and inadequate dietary intake, vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency is widespread, and elevated levels of TB, particularly in vulnerable immigrant populations, have long been associated with vitamin D deficiency.  Vitamin D is converted to 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, the active form. 1,25D binds to the nuclear vitamin D receptor (VDR), which functions as a ligand-stimulated regulator of gene transcription. Altering the transcription of specific genes ultimately leads to changes in protein content and function of cells. Our previous genomics work led to the discovery that 1,25D directly stimulates antimicrobial innate immunity through its effects on specific gene transcription. We hypothesize that 1,25D acts to stimulate innate immune responses to TB and regulates pathways leading to infected cell death. Our preliminary data for this application suggest that 1,25D acts to create a more hostile environment within both infected cells and adjacent tissue. The application is composed of 4 aims designed to extend this data to understand the genomic and molecular events that underlie the antibacterial activity of vitamin D.

CommitteeNameEN: Behavioural Sciences - A: Neurobiological Basis of Behavioural Processes
NomDuComitéFR: Sciences du comportement - A: Fondements neurobiologiques des processus comportementaux
TitreApplicationTitle: Stress and Obesity: the Ghrelin connection
Keywords-MotsClés: GHRELIN; GHRELIN RECEPTORS; HYPOTHALAMUS; OBESITY; SOCIAL STRESS; VENTRAL TEGMENTUM
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity is related to a variety of pathologic conditions that include cancer, heart disease, diabetes, and renal insufficiency, all of which can lead to an early death and poor quality of life. In Canada, the rate of obesity and the health and economic issues associated with this condition have reached alarming levels. While it is clear that there are genetic factors that are closely associated with obesity, environmental factors also to the behavioral and physiological responses that lead to body weight alterations and ultimately to obesity and metabolic syndrome. Stress, for example has been associated with a number of metabolic changes that ultimately can lead to obesity, insulin resistance, and cardiovascular disease. Of interest to my lab is the fact that the hormone ghrelin is released following stress. Ghrelin, a stomach derived hormone, is commonly associated with the stimulation of appetite and food intake (particularly the intake of high calorie foods), as well as with the accumulation of body fat. Because ghrelin is released following exposure to stressors, it is possible that the pathologic alterations in body weight and metabolism that are seen following stress are mediated in part by ghrelin. This proposal seeks to provide evidence that this is the case. In addition we intend to determine if ghrelin targets the brain directly mediate these effects. The results from the proposed studies will lead to a better understanding of the hormonal mechanisms by which stress responses alter behavioral and metabolic processes, and possibly produce new avenues for the treatment and prevention of metabolic disorders.

DomainesScientifiquesFR: NUTRITION; EFFETS ENVIRONNEMENTAUX SUR LA SANTÉ
TitreApplicationTitle: Effects of prenatal folate exposure on DNA methylation in the newborn infants
Keywords-MotsClés: DNA METHYLATION; EPIGENETICS; FETAL HEALTH; FOLATE/FOLIC ACID; GENE-NUTRIENT INTERACTIONS; MATERNAL NUTRITION; VITAMINS
Abstract-Résumé: Folate, a B vitamin, play an important role in human health and disease. Folate and its synthetic form, folic acid, have generally been regarded as safe and purely beneficial.  In Canada, an overwhelming body of evidence for a protective effect of maternal folic acid supplementation on neural tube defects led to mandatory folic acid supplementation in 1998.  Also, up to 40% of the Canadian population are taking folic acid supplementation for several possible but as yet unproven health benefits. As a result, intake and blood measurements of folate and folic acid in Canada have dramatically increased over the past decade. Furthermore, it is recommended that all women planning a pregnancy or capable of becoming pregnant take folic acid supplementation before and during pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects. These facts suggest that intrauterine exposure of the developing fetus to folate has significantly increased in Canada. Recently, an emerging body of evidence has warned of potential harmful effects of high levels of folate and folic acid and has suggested that folic acid supplementation may promote, rather than prevent, the development of certain chronic diseases. Folate plays an important role in DNA methylation, an important molecular process that affects expression, structure and function of critical genes that play a mechanistic role in the development of chronic diseases including cancer.  DNA methylation undergoes extensive programming during embryogenesis and hence, the embryonic stage is highly susceptible to changes in the intrauterine environment. Animal studies from our and other laboratories have indeed demonstrated that maternal folic acid supplementation can influence DNA methylation in the offspring and modify their susceptibility to certain diseases in adulthood.  We propose a clinical study to determine the effect of maternal intake and blood measurements of folate and folic acid on DNA methylation of the newborn babies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Differential role of myogenic regulatory factors in establishing muscle-specific gene expression
Keywords-MotsClés: COACTIVATORS; GENE EXPRESSION; IN VITRO TRANSCRIPTION; MUSCLE DIFFERENTIATION; PROTEOMICS; TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR
Abstract-Résumé: Myogenin is a regulator of gene expression that is critically required for muscle formation. However, the mechanism by which this important protein mediates its role in muscle development is not well established. Using technologies that allow us to determine the other cellular proteins that specifically associate with myogenin, our work will determine how this critical factor decides which genes to turn on in muscle cells. The knowledge gained from these studies of myogenin function will facilitate the development of novel therapies to treat muscular dystrophy.

ClasseRechercheFR: MALADIES A VIRUS; SUBSTANCES CANCERIGENES (ET ENVIRONNEMENTALES)
TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation of viral gene expression
Keywords-MotsClés: FLUORESCENT RECOVERY AFTER PHOTOBLEACHING (FRAP); HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS; INNATE INTRACELLULAR ANTIVIRAL DEFENSES; REGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSION; VIRAL DISEASE; VIRAL REGULATORY PROTEINS
Abstract-Résumé: We are interested in studying how viruses replicate and produce disease. A critical stage in viral replication is the activation of expression of viral proteins in infected cells. Surprisingly, the regulation of gene expression of human herpes virus (HSV) types 1 and 2 is not yet well understood. We have recently made two discoveries that strongly suggest a major mechanism for the activation of expression of most HSV genes. We propose now to continue our studies, to fully decipher the regulation of HSV gene expression and consequently of HSV replication. HSV are most prevalent human viruses that produce cold sores and genital infections but also major diseases such as encephalitis, stromal keratitis and disseminated neonatal infections. HSV-2 is also a critical risk factor in the transmission of HIV. Moreover, HSV-based vectors are currently being analyzed for their potential in gene therapy and as oncolytic agents. Expression of genes from the HSV genome is required for both applications. Our studies therefore not only directly address an important human pathogen but have also direct implications on the potential uses of HSV vectors in molecular medicine.

TitreApplicationTitle: How Suggestibility May Influence Placebo Response: Insights From a Novel Experimental Design
Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHMA; ATTENTION; COGNITION; EXPECTATION; PLACEBO; SUGGESTION
Abstract-Résumé: While placebos are known to exert powerful therapeutic effects on some patients, we still have a poor understanding of the mechanisms which underlie them, as well as the characteristics of placebo responders. A leading explanation for placebo effects emphasizes the role played by patients' expectations. While we know that expectations can be produced or changed more easily in people who are susceptible to suggestion, the role of suggestibility in placebo response is not understood. Employing the pharmacological treatment of asthma as a model, the present study uses a novel experimental approach to examine whether highly suggestible individuals exhibit a stronger placebo effect than less-suggestible persons. On two separate occasions, each research subject will receive a pharmacological treatment for asthma under two conditions: once while the treatment is administered openly, and once while the subject is unaware that the administration is taking place. If there is a difference in the treatment's effects under these two conditions -- a placebo effect -- we can attribute it to the patient's knowledge that therapy is occurring. In other words, this experimental design will allow us to measure the degree to which individual research subjects are responsive to placebo. This approach will permit us to answer important question -- for example, should certain individuals be more amenable to psychological intervention than others? -- and allow us to characterize parameters contributing to good placebo response, and will likely pave the road to a greater understanding of placebo phenomena.

TitreApplicationTitle: Electrical and Second Messenger Communication in Resistance Arteries
Keywords-MotsClés: GAP JUNCTIONS; ION CHANNELS; SMOOTH MUSCLE PHYSIOLOGY; VASCULAR COMMUNICATION
Abstract-Résumé: Tissue and organ blood flow is controlled by a network of blood vessels found throughout the body, including in the heart and the brain.  To make sure that blood vessels work in a joint fashion, single cells within the vessel wall must share information with one another.  This sharing of information between cells is aided by proteins called gap junctions.  These gap junctions are small pores which act like gates that permit ions and other small molecular to move back and forth between cells.  The overall goal of my research program is to develop an understanding of cell to cell communication and how this process shapes the ability of an artery to dilate and constrict.  We employ a wide range of techniques that include: 1) functional and structural measurements on intact arteries; 2) biochemistry; and 3) computer based modeling.  At a basic level, this work will increase our knowledge of how a complex network of arteries accurately controls tissue blood flow and organ function.  From the applied point of view, it will help create an understanding of harmful disorders such as endothelial cell dysfunction, arterial vasospasm and cardiac syndrome X.  This research project will help us understand how disease states like hypertension and diabetes change vessel size.

NomDuComitéFR: Sciences du comportement - B: Études cliniques du comportement
TitreApplicationTitle: Anatomical, functional connectivity and gray matter development as risk factors for bipolar disorders - longitudinal MRI study in offspring of bipolar parents
Keywords-MotsClés: BIPOLAR DISORDERS; ENDOPHENOTYPES; FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY; NEUROIMAGING; TRACTOGRAPHY
Abstract-Résumé: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a severe mental illness affecting tens of thousands of Canadians. It ranks as the 6th most important cause of disability according to the World Health Organization. BD imposes a high burden to patients, their families and society. While the cause of BD is not yet known, the role of genetic factors has clearly been established. Relatives of bipolar patients inherit subtle changes in the structure of the brain, which increase their vulnerability for BD (biological risk factors). Some of the neuroimaging findings in bipolar patients represent biological risk factors whereas others are secondary to progression/burden of the illness. The best way to identify the biological risk factors is to study affected and unaffected offspring of bipolar parents. Any changes found in both the affected and unaffected offspring of bipolar parents, relative to healthy controls without family history of BD likely represent inherited biological risk factors. The best way to directly study the effects of BD on brain structure, is to follow subjects with BD over time. We propose to undertake a study of offspring of bipolar parents between 15 and 30 years of age, to identify biological risk factors for BD. We will carry out brain imaging, in order to identify subtle differences in brain structure and function between offspring of bipolar parents and controls. We will also compare our findings with results of our initial study done 4 years ago in order to find whether there are differences in brain development between controls and offspring of bipolar patients (effects of illness burden). This study will provide greater understanding of biology and development of BD. Identification of biological risk factors might aid in early diagnosis and intervention thus markedly decreasing the economic and human burden of the illness, which would be of paramount importance not only to patients and their families, but also to general public.

TitreApplicationTitle: Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully: An RCT of an Individual Psychotherapy for the Treatment of Depression in Patients with Metastatic Cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVANCED CANCER; DEPRESSION; PSYCHOLOGICAL GROWTH; PSYCHOTHERAPY; QUALITY OF LIFE; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: Depression is a common expression of emotional distress in patients with advanced cancer, but is often undetected and untreated by medical caregivers.  We have shown that it arises in response to multiple factors related to the disease, the individual, and the social context.  Based on this research we have designed a psychological treatment to address the issues that contribute to depression in advanced cancer patients.  This individual psychotherapy, called Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully (CALM), has been tailored for patients with advanced disease.  It consists of three to six individual sessions delivered over three months by specially trained social workers, with two booster sessions offered in the subsequent three months.  CALM addresses issues related to: 1) symptom management and communication with health care providers; 2) changes in self and relations with close others; 3) spiritual well-being, or maintaining a sense of meaning and purpose; and 4) preparing for the future, sustaining hope and facing mortality.  We will test the effectiveness of this intervention to relieve depression and promote psychological well-being in advanced cancer patients by comparing its effects to those achieved with group therapy and with usual care.  If shown to be effective, CALM can be recommended for the treatment of depression in patients with advanced disease and shared with other centers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of eIF4E in stress granules formation and the associated resistance to chemotherapy
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTI-CANCER PROTEASOME INHIBITORS; APOPTOSIS; CHEMORESISTANCE; EIF4E; IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE; MRNA EXPRESSION; RNA FISH; RNA INTERFERENCE; STRESS GRANULES; XENOGRAFT
Abstract-Résumé: In response to environmental stresses such as exposure to toxic components, to radiation, and to low oxygen conditions, the cell uses a defense mechanism to fight the stress and survive. Stress can also be produced during anti-cancer treatment. Exposure to patients to prolonged chemical or radiation treatment can induce stress conditions to which cancer cell will respond by mobilizing a defense mechanism. This will allow cancer cells to resist to treatment and grow. This resistance is one of the major obstacles in treating patients suffering from cancer. Our objective is to understand how cancer cells managed to resist anti-cancer treatment We have been investigating the role of a novel cellular bodies recently identified as important players in mediating the resistance of cancer cells to stress. These cellular bodies form within the cell only under stress conditions promoting cell survival. I believe that these cellular bodies are sites where specific gene products that are essential for cell survival are protected. My research focuses on defining the molecular mechanisms by which these cellular bodies mediate cancer cell resistance to therapy. To achieve our goal, my team is using cancer cells as a model. We will investigate strategies to prevent the formation of the cellular bodies and the associated cell resistance to chemotherapy. The major issue in cancer therapy is to develop strategies that prevent cancer cell resistance and recurrence upon treatment. Our study is important to understand how cancer cell resist treatment which will allow us to better design new treatments using conventional anti-cancer drugs together with drugs that prevent the formation of these cellular bodies.

TitreApplicationTitle: A comparative study of pathways to first episode care for psychosis in three ethnic groups in Ontario
Keywords-MotsClés: ETHNO-RACIAL GROUPS; MENTAL HEALTH; PATHWAYS TO CARE; PSYCHOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: The sooner an individual gets treatment for psychotic illnesses such as schizophrenia, the better the outcome. In an effort to assist this goal, early intervention services have been set up across Ontario. However, studies of these services suggest that there is a greater delay between developing symptoms of psychosis and getting treatment in people of African and Caribbean origin than European Canadians. These delays may lead to more severe illness with worse prognosis and more involvement of emergency services and the prison and justice systems.  The reason for the differences between groups is not clear. It could be that  people of African and Caribbean origins are less likely to know how to get help from first episode services, or that they are less likely to attend their general practitioner and be referred to services, or the fact that some in these groups may prefer to use complementary therapies before trying first episode services. In order to promote early treatment and better outcome, a clear understanding is needed of the different routes people take to getting care and why they take a particular route. For instance if there is significant delay in treatment because of the use of complementary treatment, health planners may want to work with complementary therapists in areas where people of African and Caribbean origin live in order to develop better pathways to first episode care.  This study will document and compare the pathways taken to first episode psychosis services for African, Caribbean and European origin Canadians living in Toronto. Pathways to care will be assessed using a methodology designed by the World Health Organization. Where differences in pathways are identified, the study will use focus groups involving clients, their families, carers and community members to help researchers further understand the reasons why these occur. This information could form the basis of targeted interventions to increase health equity in Ontario.

TitreApplicationTitle: Towards the correction of Rett-like behaviour in MeCP2-deficient mice
Keywords-MotsClés: EPIGENETICS; EPILEPSY; MOUSE BEHAVIOUR; MUTANT MICE; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; RETT SYNDROME
Abstract-Résumé: Rett syndrome is one of the most common genetic forms of developmental delay affecting girls.  We know the gene responsible for the condition, and there are mice that develop a Rett-like condition.  Even though we have known the gene responsible for Rett syndrome for over 10 years, we still do not which types of cells in the brain play a key role in causing Rett syndrome, nor do we really know if the condition can be corrected.  Our previous work suggests that correcting Rett syndrome is possible, as we showed that if one fixes the mutated gene in the brain of affected mice, some behavioural improvements are seen.  But our rescue was incomplete - and we do not know why.  Perhaps we targeted the wrong types of cells, or not enough cells in the brain to fix the condition, or perhaps not all of the problems with Rett syndrome can be fixed.  Our current project will determine how well some of the most problematic symptoms of Rett syndrome can be corrected, and test which types of cells in the brain must be considered for the best treatment strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms of macrophage priming for LPS signaling by oxidative stress
Keywords-MotsClés: BACTERIAL LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE; ISCHEMIA/REPERFUSION; PHOSPHATIDYL-INOSITOL 3-KINASE (P13K); THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TO TRAUMA PATIENTS; TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4(TLR4)
Abstract-Résumé: Civilian trauma is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Canada and globally.  One of the primary sources of morbidity is the development of organ dysfunction in trauma victims who survive the initial hours following injury.  Patients who sustain hemorrhagic shock are at particularly high risk for the development of organ dysfunction, due to the ability of shock/resuscitation to prime immune cells for increased responsiveness to subsequent inflammatory stimuli such as gram negative bacterial lipopolysaccharide, a phenomenon called the 'two-hit hypothesis'.The knowledge generated from this study will provide novel insights into the strategies for prevention and treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: "Source" Country Perspectives on the Migration of Highly Trained Health Personnel: Causes, Consequences and Responses
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS; CONSEQUENCES; HEALTH HUMAN RESOURCES; MIGRATION POLICY; POLICY RESPONSES; SOURCE COUNTRIES
Abstract-Résumé: This research will address some of the causes, consequences and responses of source countries to the migration of their highly trained health personnel. This will include a focus on doctors, nurses and health care managers and educators. The countries that we are going to examine specifically include the Philippines, India, South Africa, and the Caribbean region. We will be gathering details about who is migrating, how they are migrating and to where. We will then look at what some of the consequences have been of the migration of highly trained health personnel from these countries using a variety of indicators considered important by those actually within the countries being studied. Finally, we will examine what have been some of the responses to minimize the negative consequences highlighting some useful examples that could be implemented across these and other countries experiencing similar problems. This topic should be of interest to those in Canada because it is one of the countries that these personnel are migrating to and we should understand the consequences this has for countries of origin. Further, this information will help to ensure that Canada meets its international obligations to improve situations in countries from which it benefits from highly skilled migration.

ClasseRechercheFR: RECHERCHES SE RAPPORTANT A PLUSIEURS MALADIES; RECHERCHES MULTIDISCIPLINAIRES
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural and Functional Characterization of Spliceosome Assembly and Activation
Keywords-MotsClés: CHEMICAL BIOLOGY; GENE EXPRESSION; MULTIPLE DISEASE RELEVANCE; NUCLEIC ACID BIOCHEMISTRY; RNA PROCESSING; SPLICING
Abstract-Résumé: Protein-coding messenger RNA (mRNA) in humans is synthesized as a precursor molecule (pre-mRNA) containing both coding (exon) and non-coding (intron) sequences.  Intron sequences are removed from the pre-mRNA in a process, referred to as splicing, which is catalyzed by a large RNA/protein machine:  the spliceosome.  Proper expression of the genetic material depends on precise splicing and alternative splicing events are critical in development and tissue differentiation.  Over 95% of human pre-mRNAs are spliced and ~2/3 of human genetic diseases are due to splicing errors.  Our understanding of the mechanisms by which pre-mRNAs are recognized and then processed by the spliceosome is incomplete.  This proposal describes a series of experiments to investigate the assembly, activation, and transitions that occur within the fully assembled spliceosome.  They are focused on two proteins, SF3b14 and PRP8, both of which have been shown to form part of the core of the splicing machinery.  Our recent determination, using X-ray crystallography, of the structures of human SF3b14 and Domain IV of PRP8 provides the basis for a set of experiments to investigate further the function of these molecules.  Using a combination of biophysical, biochemical, and cell biological methods we propose to study the role of these proteins in the spliceosome.  The experiments outlined here will provide important insights into the mechanisms of a fundamental mode of gene regulation in humans.

ClasseRechercheFR: RECHERCHES SE RAPPORTANT A PLUSIEURS MALADIES; THERAPIE DU CANCER EN GENERAL
TitreApplicationTitle: Investigations of the drug and organic anion transporter ABCC4
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER CHEMOTHERAPY; DRUG AND ORGANIC ANION TRANSPORT; DRUG DISPOSITION; GENE REGULATION; MEMBRANE PROTEIN TRAFFICKING; MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE PROTEIN
Abstract-Résumé: There are many factors that determine both the effectiveness and toxicity (adverse side effects) of drugs. In the case of an anticancer drug, this is largely determined by how much of the drug is able to reach the tumour (desired target) versus how much drug is taken up by normal cells (side effect). The ABC efflux pumps are one class of proteins that control the amount of drug that accumulates in cells; these pumps can also influence how efficiently drugs penetrate tissues such as the brain or are eliminated from the body through urine and feces.  Some ABC proteins have a second function which is to export naturally occurring molecules that regulate diverse functions in both normal and malignant cells. The intent of this research is to study the ABC efflux pump known as ABCC4. ABCC4 is involved in the effectiveness (and toxicity) of an important group of drugs that are used to treat many diseases including certain cancers (eg prostate) and HIV infections. ABCC4 also plays a unique role in determining the amounts of several 'signaling' molecules (eg prostaglandins and cyclic AMP) that transmit information from one cell to another.  This type of cell-to-cell communication is critical for a wide variety of physiological processes including those controlling cell growth and the perception of pain. This project seeks to understand (i) how ABCC4 can pump so many different drugs and signaling molecules out of cells by determining how mutations introduced into ABCC4 affect its transport activity and specificity; and (ii) how the amount of ABCC4 present at the surface of the cell is regulated by investigating how ABCC4 interacts with other proteins in the cell, and by exploring how the activity of the gene that encodes ABCC4 is controlled. Knowledge of these properties of ABCC4 is essential if we are to fully understand the role(s) of this ABC efflux pump in normal and malignant cell growth as well as its role in determining drug safety and efficacy.

CommitteeNameEN: Clinical Investigation - C: Digestive, Endocrine and Excretory Systems
NomDuComitéFR: Investigation clinique - C : Systèmes digestif, endocrinien et excrétoire
TitreApplicationTitle: Congenital nephron deficit and essential hypertension.
Keywords-MotsClés: GENETICS; HYPERTENSION; MOUSE MODELS; NEONATES
Abstract-Résumé: Among normal people, the number of functional nephrons varies widely from individual to individual (between 0.3 and 1.3 million nephrons per kidney). While this was once dismissed as a benign reflection of human diversity, recent evidence suggests that babies born with small kidneys may be at high risk for hypertension later in life. In preliminary studies, we found that babies born in India have smaller kidneys than babies in Montreal and hypothesize that this is due to a combination of inadequate vitamin A during pregnancy and inheritance of genes that influence the efficiency with which the fetus metabolizes vitamin A. In this project, we will first study a cohort of 300 newborns from Bangalore, India, to determine whether small kidney size is associated with maternal vitamin A deficiency plus an unfavorable combination of vitamin A pathway genes. We will then show that dysfunction of these specific genes lead to hypertension in mice. Finally we will test for an association between these genes and hypertension in a large cohort of adults from India and nearby regions. These studies should ascertain whether there is a link between vitamin A pathway genes and hypertension; if so, our studies will also provide a rationale for trials of vitamin A supplementation during pregnancy in the developing world.
