Abstract-Résumé: The hippocampus is a brain structure involved in memory. We aim to understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying synaptic organization of various cell types (principal cells, interneurons and glial cells) that compose hippocampal networks; the mechanisms of long-term synaptic plasticity in these networks that contribute to memory formation; and how mutations in genes coding for proteins involved in synaptic plasticity cause genetic human brain diseases such as mental retardation. This will advance knowledge about synaptic networks at multiple levels: from the molecular biology of cells, their role in learning and memory, and their dysfunction in genetic brain diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Smooth Muscle Pathophysiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The coordinated regulation of smooth muscle contraction is a key property of theintestine, which when functioning normally contributes to general health and wellness, but when dysfunctional is associated with morbidity and mortality. This proposal will examine the signaling pathways that operate to regulate intestinal smooth muscle contractility under normal physiological conditions.  A key unanswered question that will be addressed is how different regulatory networks contribute to vascular and intestinal smooth muscle contraction. Moreover, with intestinal inflammation, it is thought that smooth muscle cells undergo a change whereby normal rhythmic contractions are supplanted by sustained contractions that persist long after the inflammatory injury has subsided. Thus, the study of underlyingmechanisms for the regulation of intestinal contractility will be important for the understanding of the basis for loss of functional intestinal efficiency that char-acterizes the inflammatory bowel diseases and other intestinal dysmotility disorders.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Child Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Many children and youth suffer from mental health disorders or chronic disease.  Medical treatments may relieve the symptoms, but psychosocial interventions can improve quality of life, disease management and reduce health system access. Most children and families are denied access to these interventions because of a shortage of specialized health professionals, a lack of policy support and high incidental costs (e.g. transportation, time from work). The Chairs work will further his contributions in this area by advancing understanding of the psychosocial scaffolding required to support sick children and their families, through development of patient-centred accessible treatments using innovative technology.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Innate Immunity, Inflammation and Kidney Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Kidney disease is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in the population. Currently the management of most kidney diseases are supportive, conservative and/or empiric. New areas of research are required to develop specific and effective therapies for patients with kidney disease. The  main focus of this research chair will be to establish a critical mass of basic science researchers focused on identifying the role of inflammation in many acute and chronic kidney diseases. In addition, a program in molecular epidemiology will be created that will form a seamless transition between science and clinical medicine and outcomes. This initiative will be essential to quickly usher in new discoveries to clinical medicine that will ultimately have a positive impact on patient care.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Biomolecular Nanoprobes
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Exploration and exploitation of space
Abstract-Résumé: The purpose of my research is to design nanomaterials that push the boundaries of biological sensing. By creating probes that are brighter, longer-lasting, smaller and more sensitive, we will be able to address critical questions such as how networks of cells communicate, how bacterial communities form, and what signals cause cell death. We will also be able to explore remote and harsh environments, such as the Polar regions and the surface of Mars. This work will also provide insight into the potential health hazards of nanotechnology and lead to guidelines for safe use and disposal of these increasingly common materials.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Proteomics and Systems Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: As we overfeed, we store more and more energy as fat. At some point, we develop diabetes-2 and other illnesses. The research of the applicant is geared towards understanding how lipid droplets which are the main fat deposits, form with the help of small transport vesicles termed COPI in the biosynthetic pathway and how formed droplets communicate with mitochondria which in brown fat, convert stored energy into heat. The goal is to enhance energy to heat conversion and to identify genetic and environmental markers to diagnose and prevent obesity-related diseases. The latter will be part of a systems medicine approach.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The brain is mostly a self-organized system which generates and modulates neural circuits through synapses according to neuronal activity. The goal of this research is to elucidate the molecular mechanisms controlling synapse structural plasticity that underlie the activity-dependent, self-organization of neural circuits- brain rewiring. By developing novel molecular genetic engineering and optical methods to create light-inducible molecular switches and fast live cell imaging in the brain tissue, Dr. Okamoto intends to understand how neural circuits assemble in an activity-dependent manner to facilitate various higher order brain functions such as learning and memory. He will also utilize this novel molecular switch technology to study the repair and regeneration of various neurological disabilities.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Health, Ecosystems & Society
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research on the environment, Other research relating to social structures and relationships
Abstract-Résumé: Health in rural, remote and Indigenous communities is especially sensitive to ecosystem degradation that disrupts social determinants of health and creates environmental hazards. The research will examine the relationship between ecosystem change and the determinants of health, focusing on water resource management as a strategy to promote health and wellbeing through ecosystem sustainability and social equity. Working with communities, organizations and researchers involved in governance of the upper Fraser River basin, we will identify practical innovations to advance collective action for health and sustainability, increase the profile of Indigenous knowledge and improve the application of environment and health impact assessment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in the Regulatory Lymphocytes of the Immune System
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Autoimmune diseases like type 1 diabetes (T1D) result from a breakdown in immunological self-tolerance. Non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice spontaneously develop T1D, a T cell-mediated autoimmune disorder resulting from a defective regulatory mechanism and leading to the destruction of insulin-producing beta islet cells in the pancreas. My laboratory specializes in the role of CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T (Treg) cells in the pathogenesis of T1D. As CD4+Foxp3+ Treg suppress T1D development in NOD mice, we focus on their mechanism of action in the induction of antigen-specific T cell tolerance and control of autoimmunity. These studies may lead to novel approaches to prevent T1D in humans.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Protéomique ciblée
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: La chaire de recherche du Canada en protéomique permettra de poursuivre nos études sur la poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation dont nous prévoyons cartographier les sites sur les poly(ADP-ribose) polymérases (PARP) par spectrométrie de masse. De plus, les interacteurs de PARP et poly(ADP-ribose) seront analysés par imagerie en temps réel.  Les interacteurs seront étudiés sous forme intacte et fractionnée ; les protéines intactes seront étudiées par résonance magnétique nucléaire couplée à la spectrométrie de masse ; les protéines fragmentées à la trypsine seront analysées en utilisant deux modes dionisation complémentaires.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Tier 1 Chair in Inflammatory Airway Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Human rhinovirus infections are a major cause of acute attacks of asthma and COPD. Such attacks are a serious health care problem. This unique research program seeks better therapeutic approaches to treat viral exacerbations of these diseases using two complementary approaches.  First, by identifying specific pathways the virus uses to cause airway swelling and structural changes we hope to be able to block these pathways and reduce attacks.  Second, we are identifying the key pathways the body uses to fight rhinovirus infections with the idea that enhancing or supplementing these natural defences would be an ideal treatment approach.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Mechanisms of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal adult-onset neurodegenerative disease that afflicts 1:50,000 Canadians annually. The disease destroys motor neurons of the brain and spinal cord, causing a mild muscle weakness progressing to paralysis and eventual death, usually within 2-3 years from diagnosis. My research is focused on understanding the mechanisms that cause motor neurons to degenerate using a unique multidisciplinary approach ranging from laboratory-based experimentation through to translational approaches in the clinic.  My aim is to make a major impact on providing an earlier diagnosis of ALS via identification of biomarkers, through to developing effective therapeutics and ultimate cure.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Human Ecology and Public Nutrition
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Nutrition and food hygiene
Abstract-Résumé: Dr Sellen's objectives are to expand and strengthen a new Program for the Study of Constraints on Child Care and Nutrition. The applicant's cross-disciplinary team will design and conduct problem based, anthropological, basic science and applied community based action research to address the mismatch that exists in many industrialized and developing communities between actual caregiver practice and current global recommendations for care and nutrition of children between birth andfive years of age. This will enhance Canada's expertise in and contribution to four United Nations priority areas: food and nutrition capacity development, breastfeeding and complementary feeding, food security, and nutrition of school-age children.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Transcriptional Regulatory Networks
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Metabolic diseases originate from genetic and environmental factors that affect complex cellular pathways. To understand these diseases we study relevant genes/pathways.  However, we often cannot do this in mammals, especially with large-scale genetic approaches. Because the worm Caenorhabditis elegans and mammals employ similar genes/pathways, we use these worms to study genes affecting fat storage/ handling and responses to nutrient contamination. When we identify interesting genes, we study them in human cells. We aim to find new information about how genes respond to the environment and how this causes disease. We hope this strategy will help developing new medical treatments.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Pediatric Gastroenterology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Food-borne bacteria such as Listeria, Salmonella and E. coli pose major health threats in Canada. Through the support of my Canada Research Chair, I have established a unique research program that explores how our immune systems recognize these and other bacteria that are found within our intestines. So far, I have demonstrated that immune recognition of intestinal bacteria not only causes inflammation that kills these bacteria, but it also promotes tissue repair, as a way to limit intestinal damage. While these findings identify a novel form of host defense against intestinal microbes, in some cases the resulting repair processes can progress out of control, causing intestinal fibrosis, a condition affecting many of the 200,000 Canadians with Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Oral Motor Function Across the Lifespan
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Speaking is an extremely complex behaviour, because there are many factors that determine whether speakers are successful in doing it properly.  The current project provides a systematic investigation into how lower order motor and higher order cognitive linguistic and emotional factors may impact on the stability of control processes in the speech motor system.  Understanding these mechanisms is an important prerequisite for developing new or better interventions to handle motor instabilities in patients with speech disorders. The studies will be informed by a novel theoretical framework with a unique take on how speech articulators are controlled by the brain.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Signaling in the Immune System
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: André Veillette is interested in elucidating the molecular mechanisms that control the functions of immune cells, in particular immune cells known as "T cells" and "natural killer cells". He is using a combination of biochemical approaches and genetic studies in the mouse to understand how immune cells control health and diseases such as diabetes, lupus, immunodeficiencies and cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Diabetes
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity and type 2 diabetes are characterized by high levels of sugar and fat in the blood, which is associated with a decrease in pancreatic beta-cells. These cells produce and secrete insulin, a key protein that helps to control blood sugar levels. It is thought that prolonged exposure to high levels of sugar and fat may induce stress upon beta-cells that results in reduced responsiveness to sugar levels, decreased insulin secretion and increased susceptibility to cell death. The proposed research aims to uncover the mechanism by which stress induces these changes with the aim of restoring normal function in beta-cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Zoonotic diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Emerging and existing zoonotic diseases (diseases that are transmitted from animals to humans) have significant effects on human and animal health, as well as social and economic impacts.  They frequently involve complex pathways from animal to human hosts, and require broad-based research spanning from basic bench-top to applied field investigations and collaboration of medical, veterinary and public health researchers. This research program will investigate aspects of epidemiology, pathogenesis, prevention and control, with a focus on emerging concerns. Its focus on both food-producing animals and companion animals such as household pets will be unique as companion animals have traditionally been overlooked.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Chaperones
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: A fundamental biological process is the conversion of genetic information into functional proteins which are folded and arranged into sophisticated three-dimensional structures. A special class of proteins termed Molecular Chaperones are essential for the folding of other proteins, and defend against the formation of misfolded protein aggregates which underlie neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinsons and Alzheimers diseases. My research program investigates the complex chaperone system and how it is regulated by various cofactors whose activities are still poorly understood. My work addresses the biochemical mechanisms of chaperone activity and the consequences of chaperone function, or dysfunction, at a cellular level.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Inflammation and Immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: White blood cells are a critical component of the immune system which works to detect and eliminate damaged cells and invading pathogens from the body. Different populations of white blood cells have different functions in protecting the body. Therefore, the localization and activation of  different types of white blood cells must be carefully orchestrated in order to ensure that the right kind of response is generated. This is critical for the recognition and elimination of cancer cells, bacteria, and viruses. However, there are times when excessive or inappropriate signals lead to the improper activation of white blood cells which than contributes to inflammatory disease and tissue injury (eg. arthritis, asthma, and transplant rejection). Understanding the mechanisms that mediate localization and activation of different white blood cell populations is important as this information could be used to manipulate the immune system to enhance cancer responses or reduce the injury in inflammatory diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en métabolisme cellulaire des lipides
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: This research program investigates how polyunsaturated fatty acids are regulated in cells. These fatty acids which are of dietary origin can be converted to molecules involved in cell communication and signalling processes that are important for normal immunity. However, they are also involved in the progression of inflammatory diseases like asthma and atherosclerosis. A better understanding of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of these molecules can allow for the development of pharmaceutical or dietary strategies to treat or prevent associated diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Oncology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer kills thousands of women in Canada and worldwide. The research program is directed to finding the genetic causes of the most aggressive forms of breast cancer and in defining the molecular fingerprints of breast cancers. This work will establish new targets for drug therapy, define the number of different types of breast cancer and provide insight into the earliest events in cancer that may allow screening to target high risk groups. This work is only possible because of the unique linkages between patient tumours and the outcomes (behaviour) of those tumours over many years that are monitored by the BC Cancer Agency tumour banks and breast tumour outcomes units.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Schizophrenia Genetics and Genomic Disorders
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The research program for the Canada Research Chair in Schizophrenia Genetics and Genomic Disorders will forge new paths of discovery in finding the causes for schizophrenia. It will also develop better understanding of newly identified conditions called genomic disorders.  These involve changes in the structure of the human genome that cause changes in development and later in life, including heart defects, learning difficulties and neuropsychiatric illness. Using the latest genetic techniques and assessments, this research will lead to more specific diagnosis and delineation of disease pathways. This will help develop new management strategies to improve these complex lifelong conditions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Physiopathologie intestinale
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Le programme de recherche proposé dans le cadre de cette chaire vise à élucider les mécanismes responsables de l'expression des gènes dans l'épithélium intestinal humain normal et pathologique. Dans un contexte intégré de la régulation de l'expression des gènes, notre stratégie vise tout d'abord à comprendre les mécanismes tissulaires, cellulaires et moléculaires impliqués dans le renouvellement normal de l'épithélium intestinal puis à identifier les mécanismes en cause dans le développement des principales pathologies intestinales soit les cancers colorectal, les maladies inflammatoires chroniques de l'intestin et l'entérocolite nécrosante.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neuroendocrinology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: My laboratory is studying the biology of gonadotropin-releasing hormone(GnRH)-secreting neurons located in a specific region of the brain, the hypothalamus. GnRH is the primary regulator of reproduction, and is controlled by estrogen. Knowledge of the signals involved in the control of GnRH synthesis is important for our comprehension of reproductive function and failure. Our research will provide insights into the control of GnRH and other neuroendocrine genes by estrogen. Further, unravelling the complexities involved in the control of GnRH neuronal activity by specific hormones, at the molecular level, will contribute critical knowledge for applications with both physiological and therapeutical relevance.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Musculoskeletal Trauma and Surgical Outcomes
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Bhandari's proposed Canada Research Chair in Musculoskeletal Trauma will set new benchmarks in trauma research both nationally and internationally. In his world-recognized musculoskeletal trauma research unit, he will resolve the optimal approach to repairing fractures of the hip, determine whether ultrasonic waves can make fractures heal faster, explore the utility of soap to clean complex fractures with open wounds, and better understand the role of the orthopaedic surgeon in the care of abused women with musculoskeletal injuries. His research will be accomplished by large, multi-national, randomized trials with collaborating surgeons and researchers across the world.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Epidemiology and Global Public Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program is designed to apply epidemiologic principles and research to further develop the scientific basis for developing public health policy and delivering public health programs. There are two main components to the research program. The first focuses on the factors that drive epidemics of sexually transmitted infections and HIV, with a series of research activities in diverse locations of India. The second component focuses on research into the distribution and health outcomes of diabetes and inflammatory bowel disease in Canada. This research programis expected to gain new insights into why some communities are less healthy than others.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation of Gene Expression
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Beta-thalassemia and sickle-cell anemia are widespread blood diseases caused by mutations in the gene coding for ß-globin, a component of hemoglobin. People born with this disease cannot make normal hemoglobin, which is needed to produce healthy red blood cells. Blood cancers, also known as leukemia, are more complex diseases, but they also originate from defective genes, which trigger uncontrolled growth and malignant transformation of blood cells.The Brand laboratory is using advanced genomics and proteomics technologies to identify the proteins and genes that are at the origin of these diseases and to understand how they deregulate blood cells. These studies will identify new therapeutic targets for an improved treatment of blood diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Physical Activity and Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The research program has two major aims: a) to understand the physiological and psychological factors that contribute to balance deficits associated with advanced aging, and neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease and spinal cord injury, and b) to examine the efficacy of physical activity and other interventions for improving balance performance in those with balance problems. The results of the research program will provide unique insights into the underlying causes of falls, help to develop new ways to predict those at greatest risk of falling and devise the most effective treatment strategies to reduce the prevalence and impact of falls.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Health Law and Policy
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Emerging technologies, such as those resulting from stem cell, neuroscience and genomic research, remain central to science policy agendas throughout the world.  There is great hope that these areas of research will lead to health benefits, commercializable therapeutics and vast increases in our basic understanding of human biology and the disease process.  However, these technologies (and associated research techniques) continue to generate profound ethical, legal and social challenges. The overarching objective of Caulfields work is to provide evidence, thoughtful analysis and the opportunity for interdisciplinary dialogue that will facilitate informed policy making and the ethical implementation of emerging technologies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Retinal and Early Eye Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Understanding the molecular mechanisms that underlie heritable vision defects is critical for the development of therapies and cures for these defects. The primary tissue affected in a vast number of heritable vision defects is the retina, which is the light-sensing and processing center of the eye. Using sophisticated genetic approaches, my laboratory will use the mouse as a model system to identify the key regulatory pathways and genes essential for the formation and function of the retina. This research will contribute to our broad understanding of retinal biology and will provide insight into the molecular pathology of inherited retinal defects.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Developmental Neurobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: The formation of accurate circuitry during development of the nervous system is critical for our ability to process information from the environment through our sensory systems. The elaboration of precise connections, or synapses, between nerve cells relies on the ability of these cells to detect molecules that direct the growth of their axons to their appropriate synaptic partner. Understanding how these molecules regulate the formation of synapses during development is critical and will allow us to apply the knowledge acquired to the development of regenerative therapies following injuries to the nervous system or neurodegenerative diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: We have made major advances in three fields of Neuroscience.  1. The mechanism of myelin formation, 2. Central nervous system synapse formation, and 3. By studying a protein we found at the synapse, we have discovered a mechanism of cell migration that is used by cancer cells to spread from the primary point of tumour origin.  The major contribution of the CRC Tier One Chair has been to allow each of these studies to develop to full potential through the leveraging of new funds for these studies from other sources.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Infectious Diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Parasitic pathogens employ enzymes, termed proteases, to invade and feed on their host's tissues, and to suppress their immune responses. Because proteases play such a pivotal role in the survival of parasites they are ideal targets at which we can develop new treatments to stop them in their tracks. Thus, we will study proteases of the malaria parasite, which kills over 2 million people per year, and of major worm pathogens that infect >600 million people worldwide. By elucidating the structure and function of the parasite proteases we will provide the necessary information required for the design and development of a new drugs against these major pathogens.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Protein Engineering
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Peter Davies's laboratory is researching the fundamental question of how a proteins structure enables it to carry out its function. Dr. Davies's research group is focusing on two examples: antifreeze proteins and calpain. Antifreeze proteins have many different structures but share the remarkable ability to bind irreversibly to ice to stop its growth. Knowing how they work will allow protein engineering to make improvements like increasing their activity. Calpains are enzymes that remodel protein networks in the cell in response to calcium ion signals. One of the main goals of this research group is to design inhibitors of calpain to prevent over-activation in various diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Microbiologie cellulaire
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Macrophages plays key roles in our ability to fight infections.  These immune cells are able to "eat" microbes at sites of infection in order to kill and digest them.  Although this process called phagocytosis is in principle sufficient to clear infection, macrophages will also present microbial peptides at their surface in order to stimulate the contribution of T lymphcytes and build a sustained immune response.  We will study two distinct pathways of macrophages important for the immune response: phagocytosis and autophagy.  Autophagy is a process that allows macrophages to help present viral antigens at their cell surface, also to stimulate T lymphocytes.  We will use a variety of methods to study these processes in macrophages including cell biology and proteomics approaches.  Our research program will allow us to learn new aspects of the immune response in macrophages and how to improve the response to infection.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Stem Cell Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Blood cells are created in a highly organized process that is dependent on hematopoietic stem cells (HSC). HSCs are at the beginning of a long line of cell divisions that create lineages of cells. These cell lineages continue to divide and eventually mature into blood cells, such as red and white blood cells. There is evidence that leukemia cells are organized in a similar way, with leukemic stem cells (LSC) at the top of this lineage system. Dr. Dick's lab uses animal model systems and genetic techniques to identify and understand the differences between normal HSCs and LSCs. This will provide the basis for therapeutic advances in leukemia and other blood-related diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cardiovascular Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Aspirin and other 'blood-thinning' drugs are among the most widely used treatments worldwide but can cause bleeding we still do not know the correct dose to achieve the best outcomes for patients. My studies are evaluating blood, urine and genetic tests to determine the best dose of aspirin that maximizes effectiveness and minimizes bleeding for different individuals and in those undergoing surgery. I will also investigate how we might reduce the risk of bleeding caused by aspirin and other blood thinning drugs and prevent serious complications that can occur as a result of bleeding. This is an understudied and growing problem as an increasing number of persons in our aging population receive blood-thinning drugs to prevent heart attack and stroke.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Drug abuse and addiction, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: We will focus on the novel G protein coupled receptor complexes we discovered in brain that mediate dopamine and opioid signaling. The major goals are to understand how these complexes generate novel signals different from those generated by the component receptors and the functions associated with selectively activating them. Targeting these complexes for drug discovery is a goal, as they have implications for neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia, depression, drug addiction and for narcotic dependence and pain mechanisms. We will use the novel technology we devised that screens for compounds targeting these receptors that can provide leads for drug design.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Drosophila Neurobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: Neuronal connections, known as synapses, are the site of neurotransmitter release in the nervous system. Once formed, synapses undergo continuous change and modification in their structural and functional properties, what is thought to be a fundamental process during learning and memory formation. My research combines the powerful genetic and molecular tools in fruit flies with electrophysiology and imaging, to identify and characterize genes and mechanisms that govern synaptic plasticity.  We also target fly counterparts of human genes involved in brain diseases to unravel their function at the molecular level. Our findings will pave the way for the development of novel therapeutic approaches to tackle brain diseases in humans.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Stress-related Disorders in Women
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The program of research focuses on increasing understanding about how the contexts of women's lives affect their biological systems and thus impact physical and mental health.  A particular focus is on biological stress systems and behavioral stress responses in populations of women who have experienced trauma during pregnancy, intimate partner violence, postpartum depression or childhood adversity. Dr Hegadoren works within several transdisciplinary research teams, using various research methods to explore how psychosocial and biological factors interact to affect health outcomes.  The overall aim of her work is to develop and test interventions and service delivery models that can more fully meet the health care needs of women.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Behavioural Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The increasing prevalence of psychiatric disorders such as anxiety and depression has placed an enormous social and economic burden on society. Many current drug therapies for these disorders provide no relief. At present, our understanding of the biological causes of these problematic disorders is limited and this is a major obstacle impeding the development of more efficacious pharmacological treatments. This research program will use animal models of human psychiatric disorders in which both behavioral symptoms and underlying neurobiological mechanisms can be studied in the same animal. This powerful approach will identify the biological cause of specific symptoms, which will lead to the development of new drugs that target specific aspects of the disease in specific populations of patients.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Cancer and Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: My research program focuses on determining how cells in the nervous system develop, survive insults, regenerate following injury and neurodegenerative disease, and occasionally form tumors in children. Our objective is to identify proteins within nervous system cells that control these processes, and determine their mechanism of action. Using this information, we discovered novel drugs that have been administered to children with fatal nervous system cancer. The understanding of how such proteins act in the nervous system will provide us with important clues about how to treat neurodegenerative diseases and cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Health Psychology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Pain is the silent epidemic of our times. It presents a challenge to the health care system and is estimated to account for $200 US billion annually in direct and indirect health care costs. The cost of pain in terms of human suffering also is enormous. Dr. Katz has proposed a four-pronged approach to the problem of pain, including studies (1) in preventive analgesia designed to improve management of acute postoperative pain and prevent the transition to chronicity; (2) aimed at identifying psychosocial factors that predict the transition of acute, time limited pain to chronic pathological pain; (3) designed to better understand and manage pain in hospitalized infants; and (4) focused on advancing knowledge about placebo analgesia and the placebo response.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Health Disparities
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Health disparities are a crucial concern for any society that aspires to a social contract based on principles of equality and justice.  There is nothing more precious to guarantee the citizens of a democratic nation than a fair opportunity to enjoy long life and good  health.  Although we can define health disparities across a number of possible characteristics, the disparities that constitute the greatest moral affront and the greatest challenge to our core notions of equal citizenship are those defined along the axes of our identities: race/ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, nativity and language.  As a social epidemiologist, I study the etiology of these kinds of disparities in social structure, public policy and the provision of medical care, and I consider components of these disparities across a range of disciplines, from population genetics to ethics, from statistical methods in medical research to the history of colonization and industrialization.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Obesity
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity and related metabolic disorders are growing at epidemic proportions around the world.  Increased food intake and liver glucose production contribute to the disruption of energy and blood sugar equilibrium levels, respectively, which are found in obese and diabetic individuals.  The objective of my proposal is to unveil biochemical, molecular and physiological nutrient-sensing mechanisms in the central nervous system (CNS) which will further our knowledge about their relationships to energy and blood sugar equilibrium levels.  Using this novel approach to understanding metabolic disorders, we will also test whether the associated CNS mechanisms are impaired in high fat diet-induced obesity.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur l'étude des déterminants génétiques de l'asthme
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Des millions de Canadiens sont atteints dasthme et la prévalence est en augmentation faisant de cette affection lun des plus importants problèmes de santé pour la société. Lasthme est déterminé par des facteurs génétiques et environnementaux. Ce programme de recherche bénéficie dune biobanque dasthme et sassocie à dautres cohortes dans le contexte de collaborations nationale et internationale pour définir la composante génétique de lasthme. Il vise également à définir le rôle de certains gènes impliqués dans lasthme et lutilisation des résultats pour le développement de modèles prédictifs et doutils de transfert des connaissances. Les résultats permettront de mieux comprendre la biologie de lasthme pour ultimement améliorer sa prévention et son traitement.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Glaucoma Genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Glaucoma is a very common disease that affects the optic nerve - the part of the eye that carries the images we see to the brain. Dr. Lehmann's laboratory is investigating glaucoma's substantial inherited component, looking at the ways mutations (DNA sequence changes) affect optic nerve development. Concentrating on early-onset (pediatric) phenotypes will reveal mechanisms by which developmental anomalies cause glaucoma and clarify these pathways role in commoner adult-onset disease. By improving our understanding of the role played by these mutations in glaucoma, we will be better placed to detect and treat the disease before appreciable vision has been lost.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Magnetic Resonance Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program of the Canada Research Chair in Magnetic Resonance Imaging is focused on molecular imaging and quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).  First, improvements to novel MRI contrast agents are aimed at quantifying the activity of matrix metalloproteinases, which are important biomarkers of tumor aggressiveness.  Second, the pharmacokinetic modeling of dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI will be validated and tested in phantoms and in animals. Dynamic positron emission tomography modeling will be incorporated into MRI modeling to improve the quantitation of both techniques.  Finally, MRI will be applied to research in neuro-oncology, in neuropediatry and in pharmacology.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Innate Pathogen Resistance
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: New viral epidemics are a constant threat to human health. However, we have naturally occuring cell types within our bodies that can be manipulated to provide instant protection from virus infection. These include innate killer cell types called natural killer cells that have the ability to quickly kill infected cells to limit viral spreading in the body. My research focuses on the cell surface receptors used by this type of innate cell to recognize viral infection. My research has shown that by modulating the level of these receptors on innate cells, the subsequent immune response to viral infection is likewise altered. This research potentially paves the way to producing artificial compounds that can bind to these receptors, and activate the innate immune system and thus avert a potentially harmful infection.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Early Psychosis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: This CRC will involve following studies in early psychosis: early case detection to reduce delay in treatment; mechanisms underlying differences in outcome at socio-culturally different centres in Chennai, India and Montreal; role of brain structure and function in short and long term outcome; conduct a first ever controlled study comparing outcome using the early intervention model in comparison to regular care over the first 5 years; and study what increases risk or protects individuals who are at risk for developing psychosis. These studies will improve our understanding of long term outcome in psychotic disorders and how to improve such outcome.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Antibody Diversification
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Antibodies are essential for the development of protective immunity against pathogens.To efficiently clear these intruders from the circulation, B-cells must produceantibodies that bind very tightly to these pathogens. This phenomenon is achieved bythe poorly understood somatic hypermutation process. Although somatic hypermutation isachieved by the mutation of antibody genes, some oncogenes are also mutated. Ourresearch program will be directed at uncovering the mechanistic details of somatichypermutation, and the role of this process in the development of lymphomas. In turn,this knowledge will be used to develop novel technologies for antibody-basedtherapeutics against pathogens and toxins.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Visual Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: How the brain implements cognition from the activity of neurons and how is this process disrupted during mental disease is poorly understood. To target these issues, I have built a research laboratory that allows measuring and manipulating signals from individual neurons in the living brain. Over the last years, our work has revealed how attention modulates sensory information processing in the brain, and how is this process controlled by the frontal lobe. We are currently investigating how is attention affected during mental disease. Our work will advance our understanding of the neural basis of cognition during health and mental disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Breast Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The objective of this research program is to develop a strategy for prevention and management of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer.  We will follow 5000 healthy women with a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation and identify hormonal factors which modify the risk of cancer. These studies will provide avenues for intervention in women with mutations in susceptibility genes. We will also develop a cohort of non-carrier women at  high risk and identify genetic, pathologic and serologic risk factors for breast cancer.  We will follow 400 women with breast cancer and a BRCA1 mutation and try to identify optimal  treatments.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Gap Junctions in Health and Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Communication between cells is essential for all life processes. This is particularly evident for cells constituting the various tissues and organs in the body, to integrate and coordinate proper function.  Channels or pores with the membranes of cells are an important mechanism for communication.  Gap junctions are a unique type of channel interconnecting cells in all tissues in the body. Their importance has become evident with regard to diseases such as stroke and cancer. These diseases are reproduced in genetically altered mice lacking these specific channels, providing both understanding into these diseases, and tools for discovery of new therapeutic approaches.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: éducation à la santé
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: La Chaire de recherche du Canada en éducation à la santé vise lamélioration de létat de santé des populations vulnérables par la revalorisation de léducation à la santé comme stratégie centrale en matière de promotion de la santé. Léducation à la santé peut contribuer à la mise en place de politiques publiques favorables à la santé par la mobilisation des communautés et le renforcement de leurs capacités. Le programme de recherche aidera à mieux comprendre comment, par la recherche participative et la mobilisation des connaissances, léducation à la santé peut contribuer à améliorer le contrôle des communautés sur leur santé.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Genetic and Molecular Epidemiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program will enhance our collective understanding of the etiology of stroke by identifying and validating novel genetic and molecular markers to assist in the development of effective prevention strategies.  Prevention holds the greatest promise of reducing the burden of stroke since even the most promising acute therapies have limited ability to alter the outcome of a stroke. Integrating genetic, gene expression and protein data,  Dr. Pare's proposed research will provide an innovative approach expected to lead to the development of novel risk prediction algorithms.  This builds on his unique expertise in cardiovascular genetics, biomarkers and bioinformatics.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neonatal Respiratory Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The Canada Research Chair in Neonatal Respiratory Physiology will aim at increasing general knowledge on respiratory control in the neonatal period, using unique ovine models. The research program includes studies on the interrelationships between respiratory control and control of cardiac activity. Simultaneous development of clinical research on the pathologies of cardiorespiratory control in the neonatal period will accelerate transfer of new knowledge to practitioners involved in the daily care of newborns and infants. Ultimately, results of the research will benefit frequent and/or dramatic problems in newborns, such as apneas of prematurity, apparent life threatening events and sudden infant death syndrome.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Leukocyte Migration in Inflammation and Injury
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: The bodys response to injury is to lure white blood cells from the bloodstream to the affected site. Once there, white cells stick to blood vessels overlying the inflamed tissue. When activated by the right signals, white cells migrate through the vessel into the injured organ, poised to combat the invader. Sometimes the system goes awry, causing excessive influx and activation of white cells. The resulting inflammation characterizes many diseases, including atherosclerosis. The proposed studies will investigate signals that master-regulate white cell trafficking and explore novel strategies to interrupt white cell influx into specifically targeted organs.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Learning and Memory
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Several genes (Ncs1, DISC1, PDE4B, GSK3, Srr, DAO, ATP1a3, Vgcnl1) regulate cognition and when dysregulated cause schizophrenia, depression, and epilepsy. We will carry out forward and reverse genetic screens for mutations in the mouse.  In mice, we propose to modify gene expression using molecular tools, pharmacology, short peptides. We will record effects on behaviour, morphology, biochemistry, calcium imaging, electrophysiology (synaptic response, plasticity).  Parallel work in a simple worm system will allow precise activation of single neurons by a new photoactivation technique we developed.  These studies will allow us to decipher how these genes control various cognitive functions and provide a basis for our studies to design and test peptides and drugs to interfere with and restore molecular and cognitive function.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chemical Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program advances and applies powerful new methods in protein analysis to research questions in cancer biology and infectious disease management.  Currently, there are limitations in how we study the structure and dynamics of protein systems, limitations which present significant barriers in the development of next-generation therapeutics.  The research program is designed to advance new concepts in Structural Mass Spectrometry specifically to promote in-depth characterization of protein systems that function at critical phases of disease progression.  Outcomes of our research, performed within a collaborative translational environment, will include new experimental treatments for cancer and childhood infections.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: The Proprotein Convertases and their Relationship to Health and Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Thanks to the Canada Chair we remained at the forefront of international research in the field of Proprotein Convertases and their implication in health and disease. Since 2003, my major accomplishment has been the discovery of PCSK9, a protease genetically implicated in the regulation of circulating LDL-cholesterol and in the development of familial hypercholesterolemia. The definition of its mechanism of function and the generation of mouse models and human studies resulted in a deeper understanding of its physiological functions and the consequences of its silencing. This led to the first clinical trials set to start in 2009 at the IRCM.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural Neurobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Research conducted by Dr. Shaw will examine the three-dimensional structures and mechanisms of proteins involved in neurodegenerative Parkinson's and Alzheimer's diseases. The proteins include S100B and S100A10 that control movement of dopamine and serotonin receptors to the cell membrane and parkin, a protein involved in the removal of unwanted cellular proteins. Our goal is to identify the structural details and determinants of protein-protein interactions responsible for these functions. The S100 protein results will be useful for drug therapy to control depression. In the protein parkin single amino acid mutations can cause Autosomal Recessive Parkinson's disease. Our goal is to identify how these mutations modify the structure and function of parkin and its interaction with substrates. These results will help build a foundation establishing the cause for the disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Structural Principles of Signal Transduction
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Protein kinases are regulated by diverse mechanisms and the break down of these mechanisms gives rise to many human diseases including cancer. The primary research focus of this proposal is to uncover how the DNA damage checkpoint kinase Rad53/Chk2 is regulated. This protein kinase plays an important role in allowing cells to repair DNA damage and hence minimize the accumulation of cancer causing mutations. I will aim to uncover how regions flanking the kinase domain of Rad53/Chk2 repress kinase activity and how specific events turn the kinase on. My lab will use X-ray crystallography to visualize Rad53/Chk2 at an atomic level.  This work will be complemented by functional experiments to test ideas generated by our structure analyses.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Pathology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program is directed at studying the specific role of the X chromosome in cancer progression and at creating a Molecular Pathology research facility that will be used to identify new X chromosome-related targets for cancer therapy, and to validate them in a large cohort of tumour samples. This will be developed primarily in a variant of breast cancers that is refractory to current therapies and in cutaneous melanomas. The results will be tested in other forms of cancers, especially in prostate and colon cancers. It is expected that the establishment of this infrastructure will lead to new treatments of cancer and faster processes for biomarkers validation.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Primary Health Care Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Stewart proposes a two-pronged program of research in the field of Primary Health Care whose overarching purpose is to improve the care delivered by Primary Health Care providers such as family physicians, nurses, social workers, psychologists, dieticians and pharmacists.  The first program is to create an evidence-base on multiple concurrent chronic conditions, for the first time in Canada, using a unique researchable database.  The second program is the next step in Dr. Stewart's world-class research on patient-centred care, and will reveal patients' perceived roles for themselves and providers in the new context of interdisciplinary care.  Results will be used to evolve new interventions to improve care.  Multiple channels of knowledge translation will assist in the goal of putting the research results to use thereby improving PHC and ultimately the health and well-being of Canadians.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Craniofacial Stem Cells and Tissue Engineering
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Two groups of Canadians have to live with permanently dry mouths: about 160,000 whohave Sjogrens syndrome, and patients with head and neck cancer (about 4,000 new casesannually). Such patients experience great discomfort, pain, tooth decay, andoropharyngeal infections. At present there is no adequate treatment for irreversiblesalivary gland damage and these patients have to constantly sip water to reduce theirdiscomfort a little. The aim of this research program is to offer to these patientseffective treatment through the regeneration or repair of their salivary glands using stem cells that are drawn from their own tissues.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Telomere Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: During its transition from a normal to a cancerous cell, virtually all types of human cells pass through phases of increased genome instability. The resulting gross chromosomal aberrations can be the reason for newly acquired mutations and changes in gene expression, all features required for malignant cellular transformation. The research described for this chair will investigate the reasons for genomic instability due to a malfunction of the protection mechanisms in place at all chromosomal ends, the telomeres. Furthermore, we aim to know more about the regulation affecting an enzyme that is crucial for telomere function, namely telomerase. This research therefore has the potential to shed light on basic and ubiquitous mechanisms of very early events in carcinogenesis.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Health Populomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: My program of research will develop and apply computer microsimulation methods that integrate statistical evidence on the determinants and dynamics of individuals health within their population contexts.  The objectives are first to deepen understanding of population health by taking explicit account of the complex network of causal factors involved, and second to apply this integrated evidence to bear on important issues in health policy and health care.  Such a broader and more integrative approach will yield challenging results, not least in coherently spanning topics where analyses to date are generally disjoint.  A key objective is to inform health policy in directions that will be more cost-effective, and ultimately improve population health.

OrgNm: Direct payment to individual outside Canada/Versement direct à un invididu à l'extérieur du Canada
ProgramNameEN: Fellowship - Priority Announcement - Longitudinal Study on Aging
NomDuProgrammeFR: Bourse de recherche - Annonce de priorités : étude longitudinale sur le Vieillissement
NomDuComitéFR: Bourses de recherche destinées aux Professionnels Paramédicaux
TitreApplicationTitle: Anomalies cérébrales associées à l'anxiété chez les personnes âgées:  liens avec le fonctionnement cognitif et la santé cardiovasculaire
Keywords-MotsClés: DECLIN COGNITIF; DEPRESSION; SANTE MENTALE; TROUBLES ANXIEUX; TROUBLES COGNITIFS; VIEILLISSEMENT; EPIDEMIOLOGIE PSYCHIATRIQUE
Abstract-Résumé: Au cours du vieillissement, certaines personnes verront leur fonctionnement cognitif decliner de facon anormale alors que d'autres maintiendront un fonctionnement cognitif normal. Un des enjeux actuels de la recherche est de determiner les facteurs qui distinguent ces deux groupes de personnes agees pour identifier celles qui sont le plus a risque de declin cognitif. Ce projet s'insere dans cette problematique et a comme objectif d'identifier les facteurs qui predisent l'apparition d'un trouble cognitif chez des personnes agees ayant un fonctionnement cognitif normal. Il existe des facteurs connus associes au declin cognitif : des facteurs biologiques tels que des anomalies dans les taux d'hormones liees au stress et la presence de certains genes, et des facteurs sociodemographiques comme un age avance et une faible scolarite. La depression, l'anxiete et les troubles du sommeil pourraient aussi etre des facteurs lies au declin cognitif, mais ces variables n'ont pas encore ete suffisamment etudiees et leurs relations avec les autres facteurs sont peu connues. Le but du projet est d'etudier l'impact de facteurs sociodemographiques, biologiques et psychologiques sur l'evolution du fonctionnement cognitif des aines sur une periode d'un an. L'objectif #1 est de determiner si la depression, l'anxiete et les troubles du sommeil predisent un declin cognitif. L'objectif #2 est d'identifier le groupe de facteurs qui predit le mieux l'apparition d'un trouble cognitif chez les aines. Les resultats serviront a mieux cibler les aines a risque de declin cognitif afin de les identifier precocement. Le depistage precoce des aines qui developperont des troubles cognitifs permettra d'envisager l'implantation hative de mesures preventives ou therapeutiques susceptibles d'empecher ou de ralentir un eventuel declin.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Rare Genetic Variants in Common Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY; HUMAN GENETICS; OSTEOPOROSIS; OSTEOPOROTIC FRACTURE; STATISTICAL GENETICS
Abstract-Résumé: Common, chronic, aging-related diseases, such as osteoporosis inflict a growing burden on our health care system, due to our aging population. Most common diseases are influenced by both genetic and environmental factors; with genetic factors influencing approximately 40-60% of the risk of common diseases. While much study has led to the identification of some of the environmental determinants of common diseases, the genetic determinants have remained elusive until recently. New technologies have identified common genetic variants which influence common diseases in the past 2 years. Despite this success, these "common" genetic variants seem to only account for a small fraction of the genetic risk of disease. Thus, while we have discovered the tip of the iceberg, we plan to identify the rare genetic variants which influence risk of disease. This study will enable us to better understand the cause of common diseases, such as osteoporosis and provide new drug targets. Importantly, since we expect these "rare" genetic factors to impart a high risk of disease, their identification, years before the onset of the disease, may allow clinicians to intervene with preventive therapies.

Abstract-Résumé: Les Hommes ayant des relations sexuelles avec des hommes (HRH) constituent une des populations masculines les plus touchees par l'infection au VIH en Afrique sub-saharienne. Peu d'etudes se sont cependant penchees sur ce phenomene jusqu'a recemment bien que les HRH soient une population vulnerable a cause des normes sociales defavorables a leur endroit.  Le but de cette etude sera de mesurer la proportion de personnes infectees par le VIH dans cette population a Abidjan, capitale de la Cote-d'Ivoire qui est le pays le plus touche par l'epidemie en Afrique de l'Ouest. La nature prospective de l'etude permettra egalement de mesurer le taux de nouvelles infections dans cette population. Les facteurs individuels, inter-individuels et sociostructurels associes aux nouvelles et anciennes infections seront etudies. L'etude visera egalement a caracteriser les types de virus VIH presents chez les HRH qui auront ete depistes seropositifs afin de comparer ces types a ceux presents dans la population generale et ainsi, de mieux de comprendre la dynamique de transmission du virus. Enfin, les virus presents chez les personnes seropositives seront egalement analyses pour connaitre leur potentiel de resistance aux molecules therapeutiques contre le VIH appellees antiretroviraux qui sont offerts en Cote-d'Ivoire.  Cette etude permettra de fournir des donnees importantes pour l'elaboration et la conduite d'interventions de prevention et de traitement chez les HRH. Elle permettra egalement un renforcement des capacites locales en matiere de depistage de la resistance du virus aux molecules therapeutiques.

TitreApplicationTitle: Building a sociomedical framework for coordinated HIV-tuberculosis care
Keywords-MotsClés: COINFECTION; GLOBAL HEALTH; HEALTHCARE DELIVERY; HEALTHCARE INTEGRATION; HIV/AIDS; MDR-TB; QUALITATIVE METHODS; SOCIOBEHAVIOURAL RESEARCH; TUBERCULOSIS; XDR-TB
Abstract-Résumé: The combination of HIV and tuberculosis (TB) has resulted in greater illness and death compared to that caused by either infection alone. The effect is greater still in the case of drug-resistant TB, including multi and extensively drug-resistant TB (M/XDR-TB). The impact of dual infection is most severe in South Africa where about 75% of patients with TB, and over 90% with M/XDR-TB, are also infected with HIV. Coinfection gives rise to numerous clinical complications related to diagnosis and treatment. Based on the candidate's PhD research, it is also laden with social complications affecting the delivery and usage of related healthcare. These social issues are exacerbated in the case of M/XDR-TB, which requires 2-3 years of complicated treatment, long-term hospitalization and separation from families, increases providers' burden of work, and is associated with higher rates of treatment discontinuation and death. In the proposed research, qualitative methods will be used to build a framework for the delivery of coordinated HIV/TB healthcare, drawing on lessons learned from the candidate's PhD research, and further examination of patient- and provider-related challenges with dual healthcare for HIV and drug-resistant TB. Research will be set at a specialist TB hospital in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. An in-depth analysis of interviews conducted with 12 men and women coinfected with HIV and M/XDR-TB will be collectively used to initiate interactive discussions with practicing healthcare workers. Four focus groups of 5-8 persons each will be held with doctors, nurses, allied health professionals including pharmacists, dietitians, social workers and counsellors, to examine their encounters with patients, and to engage their responses with issues arising from patient interviews. The proposed research will promote context-sensitive health practice and policy development in South Africa, and globally, where TB is a burgeoning public health threat in the context of HIV/AID

TitreApplicationTitle: An examination of HIV in the context of disability and rehabilitation in pediatric populations in sub-Saharan Africa and Canada
Keywords-MotsClés: CANADA; DISABILITY; HIV/AIDS; PEDIATRIC; QUALITATIVE; REHABILITATION; RESOURCE-POOR; SUB-SAHARAN AFRICA
Abstract-Résumé: Despite significant efforts aimed at combating HIV and AIDS, a large number of individuals are infected with this disease worldwide, with many new cases reported each year.  Of those individuals that are HIV-positive, children account for a high percentage of existing cases, with most of these children living in resource-poor countries.  To date, there has been little to no research focused on disability and rehabilitation in this vulnerable population in any region of the world.  Thus, this research is novel, and proposes to exam the experiences of children who are living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa and Canada, to ascertain their experiences, functional, and participatory limitations from a disability and rehabilitation point of view.  Various research methods will be employed to answer the research questions, and may include review of the existing literature, interviews with children and their families, focus groups and participant observation.  The resulting data will be analyzed using a critical approach, and the results will be shared with the research participants and their families.  In addition, the results will be presented at various international health and disability conferences, and will be submitted to peer-reviewed journals for publication.  By gaining a better understanding of the issues related to disability and rehabilitation in children living with HIV, both in Canada and sub-Saharan Africa, this research serves to provide new information to further advance the global efforts to combat HIV.
