TitreApplicationTitle: Out of Sight Out of Mind: Do Electrophysiological Markers Elicited by Nicotine Related Visual Cues Predict Relapse in a Sample of Adult Smokers? A Longitudinal Study
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTIONS; EEG; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; ERPS; FRONTAL LOBE DYSFUNCTION; HUMAN NEUROPSYCHOLOGY; NICOTINE DEPENDENCE; ORBITOFRONTAL CORTEX; RELAPSE BEHAVIOUR; VISUAL CUEING
Abstract-Résumé: A great deal of research has been put forward to understand the factors involved in nicotine dependence, yet there is a lack of research that employs modern neuroimaging techniques with humans to identify possible neurobiological markers of vulnerability to relapse. Recurrence rates in smokers that try to quit is very high (40-50% at 3 months).  Importantly, in addiction research, sensitivity to drug-related stimuli is viewed as an important factor in predicting whether users in abstinence programs will resume drug use or will keep drug-free.  In the current project, event-related brain electrical activity will be measured in tobacco smokers while they view smoking cues just before quitting the habit.  Abstinence success or failure will be assessed with monthly interviews up to 3 months, and at the end of this period, smokers will be classified into a relapse group or an abstinence group.  Thirty cigarette smokers and 15 healthy controls will participate in this study.  All participants will view smoking related, as well as emotional and neutral stimuli.  We hypothesize that the relapse group will report increased craving sensations and greater activity in target emotional regions within the brain compared to the abstinence group.  Because scalp-recorded electrical activity is considerably less costly than other neuroimaging techniques, the results of the present project can add a sensitive and feasible measure to facilitate prevention and early intervention strategies, ultimately yielding financial and health benefits for Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: The impact of the implementation of the Canadian Paediatric Society's guidelines on the detection, management and prevention of hyperbilirubinemia: a population health perspective.
Keywords-MotsClés: ADMINISTRATIVE DATABASES; GUIDELINE IMPLEMENTATION; HEALTH DISPARITIES; HEALTH SERVICE UTILIZATION; HOSPITAL READMISSION; NEONATAL HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA; POPULATION BASED STUDY; QUESTIONNAIRE; SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS; UNIVERSAL SCREENING
Abstract-Résumé: Newborn jaundice is a common condition that is usually benign and resolves without treatment.  Unfortunately, in rare cases severe jaundice can cause permanent brain damage.  When jaundice is severe enough to require treatment, timely initiation of therapy can prevent long term consequences.  Concern that babies with jaundice requiring treatment were not being identified in a timely manner led the Canadian Paediatric Society (CPS) to release guidelines in 2007 that recommend screening every newborn for jaundice before discharge from hospital.  There is debate in the research literature about whether this is the best approach for preventing the serious but uncommon harm that can be caused by severe jaundice.  My research will examine the impact that the guidelines have had within the province of Ontario.  I will investigate how the CPS guidelines have been implemented in Ontario hospitals and the impact that this has had on the treatments and services received by newborns.  I will also examine the whether the guidelines have reduced socio-economic disparities in newborn readmission for jaundice.  My research will provide evidence that will help us to quantify the balance of benefits and costs and harms of universal screening for jaundice within a Canadian context.  My findings also will be useful in identifying potential strategies to improve efforts to prevent the adverse consequences of severe jaundice and to reduce health disparity, and will inform policy development regarding the delivery of health services to newborns.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of the evolutionarily conserved KEOPS complex in transfer RNA function
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER BIOLOGY; KEOPS; PROTEOMICS; STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY; TRNA M1A58 METHYLTRANSFERASE; TRNA POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL MODIFICATIONS
Abstract-Résumé: KEOPS is an evolutionary conserved protein complex consisting of the proteins: Kae1, Bud32, Cgi121 and Pcc1. In fungal species, the complex has a fifth subunit Gon7, whose identity in other domains of life is unknown. Mutations in the KEOPS complex results in extremely slow vegetative growth and shortened telomeres via an unknown mechanism. My recent work has led to the discovery that KEOPS associates with multiple aminoacyl tRNA synthetases and the tRNA m1A58 methyltransferase complex, an enzyme responsible for the methylation of a specific adenosine on most transfer RNAs (tRNAs). Furthermore, analysis of tRNA isolated from a bud32 deletion yeast strain shows a substantial change in nucleoside composition compared to wild-type cells, hinting that KEOPS may be a general regulator of tRNA post-transcriptional modification. The stability and activity of tRNA is controlled by numerous modification events and they are critical in maintaining normal cellular growth. In the absence of proper tRNA maintenance, excessive tRNA function can lead to the onset of cancer formation. I now aim to identify the post-transcriptional modifications KEOPS influences in human cells. In addition, I will investigate the mechanism underlying the ability of KEOPS to modulate tRNA modification. In doing so, I will demonstrate whether KEOPS interacts directly with the tRNA m1A58 methyltransferase complex, tRNA, or both molecules in a higher order complex. Using X-ray crystallography, I can determine the atomic structure of the KEOPS bound complexes, allowing us to discern the mechanism KEOPS employs to control tRNA modifications. My studies will advance our limited knowledge in the molecular function of KEOPS and can aid in the discovery of novel therapeutic targets for cancers where pathogenesis is dependent on dysregulation of tRNA activity.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification and characterization of quiescent brain tumor stem cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN TUMOR; CANCER; CANCER HETEROGENEITY; CANCER STEM CELLS; CELL CYCLE; QUIESCENCE
Abstract-Résumé: In Canada, brain tumors are the most common cause of childhood cancer death and remain a significant cause of adult mortality. Disease recurrence after surgery and chemotherapy in patients with malignant brain tumors glioblastoma and medulloblastoma proves that conventional therapies miss critical targets necessary for complete cures. The discovery that only a fraction of cancer cells, called cancer stem cells, can divide to reform a tumor, suggests that these are the targets that must be eliminated. However, it is not known if a subpopulation of cells within the cancer stem cell pool withdraw from the cell cycle, making them resistant to standard chemotherapy and radiation. Such silent, or quiescent, cells exist in chronic myelogenous leukemia, but have not been identified in solid tumors like those of the brain. My research will use cell culture, transgenic mouse models, and primary human brain tumor samples to identify, purify, and characterize quiescent brain tumor cancer stem cells. Studying their properties will reveal whether, paradoxically, cells that rarely divide support tumor growth and are the essential therapeutic targets. Molecular and genetic analyses of quiescent cancer stem cells will provide insight into mechanisms of tumor dormancy and resistance to therapy. By understanding the pathways that govern the quiescent state, it will be possible to develop new therapies and treatment strategies that eradicate these essential targets. This study will serve as a model for the characterization and treatment of quiescent cancer stem cells in solid tumors. Its results will have the potential to reduce future brain tumor mortality rates in Canadian children and adults by providing novel approaches for the creation of durable cancer cures.

TitreApplicationTitle: Marginalized and muted: Experiences of social inclusion and exclusion from dis/abled children who communicate differently
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDREN AND YOUTH; COMMUNICATION DISORDERS; DISABILITY; PAEDIATRIC REHABILITATION; PARTICIPATION; QUALITATIVE METHODS; SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Children and youth with complex communication needs, i.e. with little or no speech, are vulnerable to social exclusion and marginalization with subsequent negative impacts on their physical and mental health. Little is known about non-speaking disabled children's perspectives, in part, because researchers lack appropriate methodologies to elicit these children's perspectives. This study aims to use innovative, primarily qualitative methods to elicit the 'voices' of non-speaking children to understand and describe their experiences and responses regarding social inclusion and exclusion. A series of three qualitative in-depth interviews each will be conducted with 15 to 20 non-speaking children and youth between the ages of 10 and 16. Participants will contribute additional data about daily social activities, personal geographies and social networks; generated using global positioning software, a social networks mapping tool and photographs/video taken by the participant. The data will be analyzed using a flexible coding system consistent with the research questions and theoretical underpinnings. The findings will impact understandings of social inclusion and exclusion and will inform clinical practice as well as health, education and social policy with a view to increasing participation and maximizing the health and well-being of children with complex communication needs. Strategies for sharing the study results will include formats that are engaging and accessible for children and youth.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the mechanism of the interaction of flaxseed and flaxseed oil with trastuzumab in the treatment of HER2-overexpressing breast tumours
Keywords-MotsClés: ATHYMIC MOUSE; BREAST CANCER; DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS; DRUG-DIET INTERACTION; FLAXSEED; FLAXSEED OIL; HER2; NUTRITION; TRASTUZUMAB; XENOGRAFT
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer in Canadian women and in about 25% of cases a protein called HER2 is present at abnormally high levels. This cancer type is aggressive and very difficult to treat. Currently these patients are treated with a drug called Herceptin but it only works in about one quarter of patients and when it does this only lasts for one year. Flaxseed and its oil have been shown to help reduce breast tumour growth and flaxseed oil has been shown to improve the effect of Herceptin in reducing tumour growth. The goal of this research is to understand, at the molecular level, how flaxseed oil improves the effect of Herceptin and also to determine whether flaxseed is as effective as flaxseed oil. Mice with tumours similar to those of HER2 positive patients will be given Herceptin treatment alone or while fed diets rich in flaxseed or flaxseed oil. The tumour growth and the levels of important cancer protein and gene markers and other changes at the molecular level will be measured in the tumours to understand how the growth is being affected. This research is important because most breast cancer patients change their diets to include dietary supplements, including flaxseed and flaxseed oil, therefore it should be studied whether these food components affect, beneficially or adversely, Herceptin`s action.  If these dietary compounds can in fact improve the drug`s action it could lead to a simple, inexpensive, complementary treatment that may help to ultimately save lives.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Targeting of Aurora Kinases in Glioblastoma Multiforme
Keywords-MotsClés: AURORA KINASES; BRAIN TUMORS; CELL CYCLE CONTROL; CHEMOTHERAPEUTICS; NANOTECHNOLOGY; TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: There is no cure for brain cancer at the present time and our best therapies only prolong survival by a few months. The current treatment of brain cancer involves surgical removal of the tumor, chemotherapy, and radiation. We know that despite complete or almost complete tumor removal and subsequent standard chemotherapy and radiation, cancer cells continue to divide and invade producing new tumors at the surgical site or at other sites in the brain.  Our study will shed light on the process that allows brain cancer cells to divide and grow. We are in the process of developing smart drugs that will hone in to brain cancer cells, blocking their growth and inducing cells to self-destruct. These novel therapies will be specific and overcome challenges of entry into the brain substance which limit current treatment. As such they will provide new options for the treatment of brain cancer patients. The ability to stop cancer cells from growing and to induce their self-destruction is expected to improve the quality of life and survival of patients with brain cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Determining the Immunogenicity of Decellularized Tracheal Allografts
Keywords-MotsClés: AIRWAY TRANSPLANTATION; COMPOSITE TISSUE ALLOTRANSPLANTATION; DECELLULARIZATION; HEAD AND NECK SURGERY; REGENERATIVE MEDICINE; THORACIC SURGERY; TISSUE ENGINEERING; TRACHEAL ALLOGRAFTS
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer, trauma and narrowing following surgical resection of the airway is a major problem in head and neck and thoracic surgery. These patients often require permanent artificial airways to be able to breathe and speak. Recently, the concept of transplanting an airway from a donor has been proposed as a potential solution for this problem. The cells from the donor airway are removed in order to avoid giving the recipient medication to reduce their immune system and then repopulated with the recipient's own bone marrow cells. Our study focuses on determining if these structures are safe for transplantation. This significantly advances the current area of research as it will allow for transplantation of organs without the need for the highly toxic immunosuppressive medication and will allow the use of organs which have been previously deemed unsuitable for transplantation. This represents a potential solution for the shortage in organs available for transplantation.

TitreApplicationTitle: Emotion Regulation in Adolescence and the Development of Depression and Anxiety
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENCE; ANXIETY; DEPRESSION; DEVELOPMENTAL; EMOTION REGULATION; LONGITUDINAL; PREVENTION; SCHOOL-BASED INTERVENTIONS
Abstract-Résumé: Adolescence is a period of significant physical, cognitive and social changes. While some individuals navigate through adolescence without great difficulty, some find this period to be particularly stressful and emotional (Arnett, 1999). Some studies estimate that 15 to 25 percent of young people have mental health problems (Waddell & Sheppard, 2002; Asarnow et al., 2005). Early life is critical in the development of mental health disorders, as 75 percent of mental disorders emerge before the age of 24 (Kessler, Berglund, Demler, Jin & Walters, 2005) and these disorders often persist throughout adulthood (Fichter et al., 2009). Waiting to treat depression and anxiety in adulthood prolongs suffering and is costly to the health care, employment, justice sectors, and society at large (Santor, Short & Ferguson, 2009). My overarching goal is to improve health and reduce the burden of chronic mental illness. I will do this by researching the causes and developmental course of emotional mechanisms thought to contribute to depression and anxiety. I plan to collect a rich longitudinal data set on emotion management and related factors as children age and pass through puberty. Ultimately, I intend to use this research to inform targeted prevention programs to implement during critical periods of development. The school-based invention program will consist of interactive activities that teach age appropriate emotion management and social skills. Pre and post intervention scores for mental health symptoms and emotion management strategies will be compared to scores at a control school (without intervention). If the program is successful, I will make it available online so that it can be accessed by parents, educators, and researchers across the country.

TitreApplicationTitle: Angiopoietin-1 mimetics: new therapeutic agents for cancer treatment.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGENESIS; ANGIOPOIETIN LIGANDS; ANTI-METASTATIC AGENTS; ANTI-TUMOR AGENTS; ENDOTHELIUM-TARGETED CANCER TREATMENT; MOUSE MODELS; TIE RECEPTORS; VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Traditional chemotherapy targets cancer cells.  A newer class of cancer treatment called anti-angiogenic cancer therapy seeks to restrict the development of a solid tumour's blood supply, effectively inhibiting a tumour's growth by suffocating it.  Most anti-angiogenic agents that have received FDA approval for cancer treatment in the past decade have a mechanism of action that inhibits the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) pathway.  Other than VEGF, another protein family that regulates blood vessel growth is the angiopoietin family, which includes Ang1 (a 'blood vessel stabilizer' that reduces vessel leakiness and keep vessels quiescent) and Ang2 (a 'blood vessel destabilizer' that renders vessels leaky and initiates new capillary growth).  In recent years, preclinical and early clinical studies have started investigating the use of Ang2 inhibitors (anti-Ang2 agents) as anti-angiogenic cancer therapeutic agents.  While inhibitors of the VEGF and Ang2 pathways are designed to limit the growth of tumours once tumour cells have seeded into body organs, another potential anti-cancer strategy is to target the metastatic process - by preventing circulating tumour cells from escaping blood vessels and seeding into body tissues in the first place.  Here we hypothesize that Ang1 mimetics (pro-Ang1 agents) - engineered peptides that recapitulate endogenous Ang1's ability to activate its endothelial receptor, Tie2, thereby inducing Ang1 effects - may serve as a new class of vascular-targeting cancer therapeutics with anti-metastatic capacity through their ability to stabilize host microvascular beds.  Hence we propose to investigate the potential anti-tumour and anti-metastatic efficacy of Ang1 mimetics, using mouse models of cancer, when administered as single agents and in combination with traditional chemotherapy or VEGF/Ang2 pathway-targeted agents.

TitreApplicationTitle: Social learning in action: a motor control approach to observational learning
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTION UNDERSTANDING; EYE MOVEMENTS; MIRROR NEURON SYSTEM; MOTOR CONTROL; MOTOR LEARNING; SOCIAL LEARNING
Abstract-Résumé: Social learning by observation is a topic that really needs no introduction, as we are all constantly engaged in it. The basic skill of learning from looking at each other's actions is widely held as being central to human culture and therefore our minds. It is a key focus of many different disciplines (developmental and social psychology, animal cognition, ...) and even sciences (natural and social sciences, education, arts, ...).  I believe the neurosciences will continue to make major contributions to unraveling how social learning from observation actually works at a micro-level. Previous research has focused on the role of action simulation - the mirror neuron system - in understanding the goals and actions of other persons. Having established the importance of our own action plans in action observation, we can use the tools of computational motor control to extend the study of social learning.  We will create an innovative setup and run a series of experiments to find out in more detail how we look at the actions of another person. The setup will enable us to control the skill level of the actor and the physical properties of the objects being acted on. We will be able to find out under what conditions people choose to learn primarily about an object (physical learning) or primarily about the actor (social learning in the motor domain). We can do so by measuring their eye movements and reconstruct and analyze their learning strategies and goals from their gaze behavior.  We hope this research will ultimately further our understanding of autistic persons. Autism spectrum disorder is characterized by an imbalance of interest in learning about objects rather than people: autistic children may persistently handle a simple object for hours and remain totally oblivious to the emotional state of their caregivers. We would like to contribute to understanding what they learn and why they do not immerse themselves in the social world.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessing the value of genetic counselling and translation of emerging genetic discoveries for schizophrenia
Keywords-MotsClés: 22Q11.2 DELETION SYNDROME; CLINICAL GENETICS; COMPLEX DISEASE; COPY NUMBER VARIATION; DIGEORGE SYNDROME; EMERGING GENOMIC DISORDERS; GENETIC COUNSELLING; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; SCHIZOPHRENIA; SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS
Abstract-Résumé: Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness that affects about 1 in 100 Canadians in their lifetime. The disease is often called "youth's greatest disabler." The illness has a significant burden on those afflicted, their families, and society in general. Schizophrenia is a disorder with a large genetic component that is yet to be completely understood. Genetic counselling is a communication process that deals with the concerns associated with the occurrence, or risk of occurrence, of a genetic disorder in a family. Increasing public awareness of genetic risk for disease and the advent of personalized medicine makes it likely that those with a family history of schizophrenia will more often desire genetic counselling in the future. The purpose of this study is to assess for the first time the value of genetic counselling for schizophrenia. Results of this novel study will help us understand how people make sense of their own risk for developing schizophrenia. We will discover how genetic counselling may be helpful in addressing concerns and misconceptions about the illness and how it may or may not run in families. In addition, the results promise to provide much needed strategies to improve the procedure, availability, and uptake of genetic counselling in mental healthcare. Through the pioneering study of 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome and other emerging genomic disorders, we will examine the importance of having a specific, identifiable genetic cause for schizophrenia. Our goal is to actively translate genetic discoveries into valuable services for Canadians with serious mental illness and their families.

TitreApplicationTitle: Adherence to guidelines on the clinical management of dystocia in British Columbia.
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL PRACTICE; GENDER AND HEALTH; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH; PERINATAL EPIDEMIOLOGY; POPULATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: While most women have normally progressing labours during childbirth, up to 37% of women experience a prolonged or slow progression that requires medical intervention (Kjargaard et al., 2009). Clinical practice guidelines have been put forth by the Society of Obstetricians and Gynecologists of Canada (SOGC) and the Ottawa Hospital on the management of slowly progressing labours, in order to improve outcomes for both women and their unborn children (Society of Obstetricians and Gynecologists of Canada, 1995; Sprague et al., 2006).  These guidelines could potentially lower the use of certain medical interventions, such as cesarean deliveries.  However, it is uncertain if they are currently being followed in clinical settings in British Columbia.  This study proposes to investigate if these guidelines are being followed in British Columbia and to determine the risk factors that are associated with slowly progressing labour during childbirth.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms of human islet amyloid polypeptide-induced pancreatic islet inflammation
Keywords-MotsClés: BETA CELL; CYTOKINES; DIABETES; INFLAMMATION; ISLET AMYLOID; ISLET TRANSPLANTATION; MACROPHAGE; PEPTIDE AGGREGATION; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease that affects over 280 million people worldwide. At least two million Canadians currently live with the condition, a figure expected to double in the next ten years. Long-term complications include heart disease, stroke, kidney failure, and blindness. Type 2 diabetes accounts for at least 90% of cases and is currently treated with medications that have limited efficacy and significant side effects.  Insulin is a hormone that lowers blood glucose levels and is released by beta cells in the pancreatic Islets of Langerhans. Patients with type 2 diabetes are unable to produce sufficient insulin to meet their peripheral demand. The majority of islets from type 2 diabetic patients contain amyloid deposits formed by aggregation of a small protein, islet amyloid polypeptide (IAPP). IAPP aggregates are toxic to beta cells and can impair insulin secretion. Type 2 diabetic islets also release increased levels of inflammatory proteins that recruit immune cells and directly inhibit beta cell function. Because potent pro-inflammatory effects have been attributed to protein aggregates found in other diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, we hypothesize that IAPP aggregation contributes to beta cell dysfunction by activating a local immune response.  This project will determine the mechanisms of immune cell activation by IAPP and assess the effects of IAPP-induced inflammation on pancreatic islet function. We will evaluate potential therapeutic strategies for blocking IAPP-induced inflammation using mouse models of type 2 diabetes and islet transplantation, a potential curative therapy for type 1 diabetes that is also associated with amyloid formation. This work will contribute to our understanding of how protein aggregates interact with the immune system in multiple disease states. Furthermore, it may aid in the development of strategies to preserve beta cell function in both type 2 diabetic patients and islet transplant recipients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular mechanisms driving the development and phenotypes of non-small cell lung cancer subtypes
Keywords-MotsClés: DNA ALTERATIONS; DNA METHYLATION; GENE EXPRESSION; GENOMICS; INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS; LUNG CANCER; SUBTYPE SPECIFICITY
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is the number one cause of cancer death worldwide. High mortality rates are attributed to poor therapeutic strategies and a lack of screening for early detection. Two subtypes of lung cancer, adenocarcinoma (AC) and squamous cell carcinoma (SqCC) account for more than 70% of all lung cancer cases. These subtypes differ in their location within the lung, cell type composing the tumor and importantly, in their response to therapies, suggesting they may develop from distinct molecular alterations. However, subtype specific aberrations and the biological pathways they deregulate remain largely unknown. As such, AC and SqCC tumours are treated primarily as a single disease, likely contributing to the poor prognosis and therapeutic responses typically observed in lung cancer. The goal of my research is to address the hypothesis that lung AC and SqCC develop through distinct genetic alterations, and that these differences contribute to subtype specific development.  My aim is to identify causal subtype specific alterations and distinguish the molecular pathways they regulate. To accomplish this, I will use an integrative approach to assess multiple levels of DNA and gene expression disruption in a panel of lung cancer specimens. Only DNA alterations causing gene expression changes will be further examined as these are most likely to promote lung cancer development by disrupting cell signaling pathways. Comparison of alterations identified in AC and SqCC via this approach, will likely reveal causal subtype specific alterations as well as shared and uniquely altered pathways. If my hypothesis is correct, my findings could identify diagnostic markers for early detection, and new subtype specific therapeutic targets. This work will directly improve the health of Canadians by providing evidence to change the way lung cancer patients are classified and treated, which will improve the poor prognosis and survival associated with lung cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Functional and Molecular Characterization of Human Breast Cancer Stem Cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; STEM CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: Human breast cancers represent very complex populations of malignant cells and, by the time the disease has begun to spread, this results in very poor outcomes to available treatments. It is thus important to understand the cellular composition of breast tumors, and how this differs from normal breast tissue, so that new therapies to target and abolish the cancer more effectively can be developed. Recent research in our lab has identified a rare subset of "stem" cells in normal human breast tissue. These cells appear able to regenerate a complete normal mammary gland structure when they are placed in a gel that is then transplanted under the kidney capsule in mice that lack an immune system. Interestingly, it appears that human breast cancers are also mixed populations of cells of which only a few can actually propagate the tumour further. If this idea proves to be generally correct, it will be critical to understand what the features of these breast cancer "stem" cells are so they can be effectively killed to prevent any regrowth of the tumour at a later time. The goal of my project is to apply a new method for tracking the growth potential of many single human malignant breast cells transplanted together into mice to test the idea that those able to grow are as rare as believed. This method will also help to establish whether a single breast cancer stem cell has the ability to regenerate a palpable tumor, how to isolate it separate from tumour cells that lack this activity and then analyze the unique molecular features of these malignant breast stem cells. The results will provide understanding of the basic biological properties of human breast cancer stem cells and provide new insights about their abnormal behavior that may lead to the design of new therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: The embodiment of inequity: The impact of social suffering on the sexual health of marginalized youth - vulnerability, resiliency and healing strategies of youth-headed households in Rwanda.
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH INEQUITIES; HIV/AIDS; PARTICIPATORY COMMUNITY-BASED APPROACHES; POST-GENOCIDE; RWANDA; SEXUAL HEALTH; SOCIAL AND CULTURAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; SOCIAL SUFFERING; VULNERABILITY AND RESILIENCY; YOUTH-HEADED HOUSEHOLDS
Abstract-Résumé: As a result of the 1994 genocide and a wave of deaths from the HIV virus in the past decade, many households in Rwanda are now led by youth. Facing extreme poverty and a lack of protection, these households are sexually vulnerable, and therefore at risk of HIV infection. And yet, youth demonstrate resiliency, as they care for siblings and as solve their daily challenges.   A social suffering approach argues that it is often the poor and weak members of a society that suffer physically from social injustices. In this view, the vulnerability of youth-headed households to HIV is strongly linked to social inequalities. This study takes a qualitative, participatory, community-based approach to examine the sexual health of youth. The daily experiences of youth in the face of sexual vulnerability will be explored as well as the social factors that influence their ability to be resilient. Finally, youth's healing strategies and their access to health and social services will be examined. A total of 70 male and female youth-heads of household aged 15-24 years from one urban and one rural area in Rwanda will participate. Methods include observation, in-depth interviews and participatory group activities with youth. Focus group discussions with community members and health and social service providers will also be done. This is an Interdisciplinary Studies Doctoral project and it will be carried out between 2011 and 2013.  The data generated from this study will be communicated to health and social policy-makers in Canada and Rwanda, as it will inform decision making on programs designed to decrease HIV infection rates and improve the sexual health of youth. This study will also generate new approaches that can be used in Canada and internationally to work with young people to develop better links between health and social policy as a means to alleviate both individual and societal suffering and to reduce resultant sexual health inequities experienced by marginalized youth

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Task Importance in the Positive Illusory Bias in Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
Keywords-MotsClés: ADHD; ATTENTION-DEFICIT/HYPERACTIVITY DISORDER; CHILDREN WITH ADHD; PIB; POSITIVE ILLUSORY BIAS
Abstract-Résumé: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood psychological condition involving inattentiveness and/or hyperactivity or impulsivity. Children with ADHD have a Positive Illusory Bias (PIB) where they overestimate their abilities. This bias is different from the normal optimism of typically-developing children because it is more extreme, counterintuitive, and maladaptive. Most research suggests that the PIB exists to protect the child's self-esteem. Indeed, receiving positive feedback lowers the PIB in children with ADHD, presumably because this feedback decreases their need to protect themselves. No studies examine whether the importance of a task affects the presence of the PIB. The proposed study tests the association between task importance and the PIB, and also examines whether the effect of positive feedback in reducing the PIB is stronger when the task is of higher importance to the child. Children with ADHD will rate the relative importance of their functioning in social and academic tasks, and predict how well they will perform on these tasks. They will receive positive or neutral feedback after they complete the tasks, and then rate their performance again. I argue that children with ADHD will show little or no PIB in areas unimportant to them and their estimates in these areas will not be affected by feedback, because their self-esteem is not dependent on their functioning in these non-important areas. Specifically, children are predicted to have a higher PIB before performing a task if it is more personally important to them, and a greater decline in their PIB for a specific task after receiving positive feedback for a task that is more important to them. Those receiving neutral feedback should have no changes in their PIB, irrespective of task importance. Given that the PIB has been shown to be a barrier to treatment success, better understanding what contributes to this bias can enhance treatment outcomes for children with ADHD.

TitreApplicationTitle: Teaching empowerment: Grass-roots educators' strategies to address gender equity in the context of the HIV epidemic in South Africa
Keywords-MotsClés: CURRICULUM; EDUCATION; ETHNOGRAPHY; GENDER EQUITY; HEALTH PROMOTION; SOUTH AFRICA; YOUTH
Abstract-Résumé: A key issue in HIV prevention education is addressing the unequal gender power relations (relations between men and women within a particular society) that make many young women more vulnerable to HIV infection. For example, it can be difficult for young women to negotiate condom use with their partner.  The importance of teaching gender equity is particularly evident in South Africa, where the HIV prevalence in young women aged 20 to 29 is double that of young men in the same age group.  There is however a significant gap in our understanding of how HIV prevention curricula are taught, and how messages related to gender equity are communicated and understood in the everyday context of people's lives.  My research, which builds on my professional experience working in South Africa, aims to deepen our understanding of how gender equity is taught, understood and taken-up at a community level.  I will conduct a year-long ethnographic study with a South African non-profit organization that develops youth peer education training curricula.  The program provides a unique opportunity to explore how adult educators interpret and implement messages as they train peer educators (youth ages 14 to 16 who engage in educational activities with their peers in secondary school settings), as well as how peer educators take-up these messages as they engage with their peers. This research will contribute to our understanding of how we can bring together local and global leadership to promote more equitable gender relations through health education, in this instance to empower young women and young men to protect themselves from a life threatening disease. Furthermore, the research aims to be more broadly applicable to the field of sex education, and will offer Canadian educators a unique opportunity to learn from strategies that promote gender equity and apply these strategies to their own work with Canadian youth.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterizing the role of high-mobility group A2 (Hmga2) expression in regulating the heightened regenerative properties of fetal/neonatal hematopoietic stem cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BONE MARROW TRANSPLANT; DEVELOPMENT; FETAL LIVER; HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: Blood stem cells are a rare group of cells that are responsible for maintaining life long blood cell production.  They are also the cells that must be present in a transplant to recover blood formation in patient's with innate deficiencies in blood formation or whose cancers can only be cured by an otherwise lethal dose of chemotherapy.  Blood stem cells can also initiate leukemia if they acquire certain genetic changes, therefore a further understanding of what controls the normal and abnormal expansion of blood stem cells underpins progress in many areas of medicine.  Previous research has established that blood stem cells from fetal compared to adult mice have a number of distinct properties including a higher expansion potential, higher turnover rate and different response to immune-mediating cytokines; however, the mechanistic basis of this difference remains a mystery.  A greater understanding of developmental processes governing blood stem cell properties would have valuable clinical applications including the possibility of learning how to make stem cell transplants more effective and enabling the wider use of umbilical cord blood collections for use in adult patients where they are currently inadequate due to small stem cell numbers.  Our lab has shown that many of the fetal properties of blood stem cells change abruptly and in unison soon after birth and behave as if these co-ordinated changes are governed by a common mechanism.  The goal of my research is therefore to test this hypothesis that there is a developmental mechanism that coordinates the simultaneous change in many key biological properties of blood stem cells.  To achieve this goal I will search for some of its critical molecular features and then test their role in this process.  If successful, this could provide a new approach to increase the effectiveness of adult blood stem cell transplants and possibly reveal new targets for the treatment of some leukemias.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development and Evaluation of a Self-management Intervention for Older Wheelchair Users: A Mixed-method Approach to Inform Best Practices.
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; SELF-MANAGEMENT; WHEELCHAIR USE
Abstract-Résumé: Background and Rationale: The population of older adults is growing exponentially and a parallel increase in wheelchair use is suspected. Although wheelchairs can augment mobility, wheelchair use is associated with reduced numerous health risks. A proactive approach to improving health outcomes for this population may result from self-management interventions that focus on improving health behaviours. Such interventions have been successful in improving the health of older adults with various chronic diseases and other health conditions.  Purpose: To develop and evaluate a self-management program for older wheelchair users. Objectives: Evaluate the effectiveness of a self-management intervention on improving: 1. self-efficacy; 2. Health status and health behaviours.   Hypotheses: Self-management programs for older adult wheelchair users will lead to improvements in: 1. self-confidence; 2. health status and health behaviours. Methods: Mixed-methods  Phase 1- QL: Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with community-dwelling wheelchair users who are 60 years of age and older to explore their perceptions and experiences of self-efficacy and healthy behaviours. These findings will inform the development of the intervention.  Phase 2- QN: A parallel group, randomized controlled trial will be used. Fifty community-dwelling wheelchair users who are 60 years of age and older will complete outcome measures for self-efficacy, health status and health behaviours at baseline, post-intervention and follow-up. The intervention will consist of 6 weekly, 2.5-hour sessions, which will be facilitated by a pair of trained peer-leaders. Participants in the control group will receive no intervention. Data will be analyzed using a generalized linear mixed model analyses.  Significance: Self-management interventions may lead to improved self-efficacy, health status and health behaviours in older adult wheelchair users, which may lead to improvements in overall well-being.

TitreApplicationTitle: Implementing aerobic exercise regimens to reduce PTSD symptom severity
Keywords-MotsClés: AEROBIC EXERCISE; MENTAL HEALTH; PHYSICAL HEALTH; POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER; TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) exerts tremendous amounts of unnecessary economic strain and obstruction on the Canadian healthcare system every year, in part due to increased healthcare utilization and high comorbidity with medical disorders experienced by individuals with PTSD. To address the unproductive utilization of healthcare resources it is important to explore new treatment methods aimed at ameliorating the mental and physical well-being of individuals affected by PTSD.  Contemporary research suggests much potential for implementing aerobic exercise to reduce PTSD severity. Aerobic exercise has been shown to reduce depressive symptoms and fear of arousal - a significant contributor to PTSD severity. Further, aerobic exercise provides incidental benefits (e.g., improved physical health leading to decreased instances of medical health disorders) not directly accessible through current evidence-based treatments. To date, the potential effects of aerobic exercise to reduce PTSD symptoms, and the working mechanisms responsible for the mental health benefits of aerobic exercise remain unexplored. The proposed research will assess the utility of implementing an aerobic exercise regimen to reduce PTSD symptoms as well as investigate potential psychological and physiological mechanisms which may explain the benefits exerted by aerobic exercise on mental health and well-being. If validated, aerobic exercise will compliment current evidence-based treatments for PTSD, ultimately leading to improved physical and mental health of the thousands affected by PTSD and lessening the economic and obstructive burden on the Canadian healthcare system. Expectations, implications, and directions for future research will be discussed.

TitreApplicationTitle: Information for youth perinatal health: Experiences of pregnant youth and their health care providers
Keywords-MotsClés: EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; HEALTH BEHAVIOUR; HEALTH INFORMATION; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PERINATAL HEALTH; PREGNANCY AND CHILDBIRTH; PUBLIC HEALTH PROMOTION; YOUTH SEXUAL HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: What information matters when pregnant youth and their health care providers are making health-related decisions?   Canada dedicates substantial resources to information campaigns for pregnant women and health care providers (HCPs), with the aim of improving the health of pregnant women and newborns. Despite our investment in these "knowledge translation" campaigns, we know little about the role of such information in informing health decisions related to pregnancy and childbirth. Teenage pregnancy and childbearing is associated with a higher risk of many health problems to mother and baby, yet we know even less about the information behaviour of pregnant youth than we do about mothers in general.   The perinatal period (that encompassing pregnancy and a short time after birth) is a time of much health decision-making. Many perinatal health questions, such as whether to prescribe or consume a given medication, require careful weighing of risks and benefits. By exploring the information experiences of young (13-19 years) pregnant women in BC and their perinatal HCPs, this project aims to describe what information they think about, seek, access, value and use in making health decisions.  Data collected via focus groups and individual interviews with pregnant youth and perinatal HCPs in British Columbia will be qualitatively analyzed in order to improve our understanding of how these individuals and populations interact with health information. The goal of this project is to generate usable theory that can be applied to improve the way we communicate health information to young pregnant women and their HCPs, in order to improve the health of teenage mothers and their babies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Bioinformatic methods for investigating the prevalence of cancer-specific alternative splicing and expression using large cohorts of cancer samples.
Keywords-MotsClés: ALLELIC EXPRESSION; ALTERNATIVE SPLICING AND EXPRESSION; CANCER EVOLUTION; CANCER GENOTYPING; CANCER TREATMENT; GENE PREDICTION; HIDDEN MARKOV MODELS; HIGH THROUGHPUT SEQUENCING; MRNA SEQUENCING; MUTATION DISCOVERY
Abstract-Résumé: Alternative splicing (AS) plays a major role in amplifying the complexity encoded by the genome by producing proteins with distinct structures and functions from the same gene locus. In this project we aim to study the scope of AS in cancer and associate alterations to disease phenotypes. By regulating the inclusion of coding sequences in a context specific manner, different proteins can be produced for each type of tissue at specific developmental stages. The splicing machinery is complex, composed of DNA sequence signals and many proteins that coordinate in the regulation of alternative expression. Cancers are known for their genomic instability which can greatly affect this machinery. Mutations which alter splicing signals or related factors may have an effect on alternative splicing, some changes may be damaging the cell and others could be beneficial for a tumor. Although specific patterns of AS have been detected for some cancers, the extent to which this is central to the disease is not fully known. In the past few years, technological advances have allowed us to obtain a sample representation of the transcriptome, the set of expressed genes in their active configuration. RNA-Seq is the application of next-generation sequencing to the analysis of transcriptomes. By taking advantage of large cohorts of cancer samples for which we already have RNA-Seq data, we can conduct large-scale analysis to find patterns specific to cancer. Novel bioinformatic methods will need to be developed when existing ones do not provide us with enough information. We will then use this data to analyze AS patterns on 50 breast cancer samples, and use genomic DNA data to try to determine the genomic causes for thiese changes. This project has the potential of discovering markers for cancer detection and treatment response prediction. Information generated by our project will also help subsequent studies with data analysis by eliminating artifacts and highlighting significant results.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding Long-Term Mechanical Ventilation in Canada: A Programmatic Approach
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC RESPIRATORY FAILURE; CRITICAL CARE; LONG TERM MECHANICAL VENTILATION; MECHANICAL VENTILATION
Abstract-Résumé: The number of individuals that require prolonged and long term mechanical ventilation (PMV/LTMV) (breathing support) as a result of acute illness or progression of chronic disease continues to rise. Currently in the Canadian health care system there is insufficient capacity to deliver care to ventilator-assisted individuals in both the acute and chronic care sectors. As well, significant barriers exist to the negotiation of transition point in the health care system e.g., transitioning from acute to chronic care needs. This results in suboptimal care, decreased quality of life for individuals and their families, and inappropriate use of expensive and limited acute care resources. This project, developed through consultation with multi-professional experts in mechanical ventilation, will enable and inform seamless integrated care, development of clinical best practices, identification of health information needs of patients and families and description of health care use and costs. We propose to explore these issues for individuals (a) at-risk for LTMV in the community, (b) requiring LTMV in the community, (c) requiring PMV/LTMV in an institution; and (d) transitioning from paediatric to adult care requirements. We will conduct our project in four stages. We will meet our study objectives through the conduct of expert surveys to define key transition points, the development of a national inventory of providers of services to individuals at risk, or requiring PMV/LTMV, national surveys, and interviews of patients and families. Through the conduct of this project we will establish a national network focused on improving care delivery for our target population thus promoting collaboration and partnerships across health sectors, professions, and jurisdictions, as well as sharing of best practices to improve health outcomes, patient safety, and quality of life for our target population across the continuum of care.

Abstract-Résumé: Le gouvernement du Quebec vient d'annoncer le deploiement de 500 infirmieres praticiennes specialisees de premiere ligne au cours des prochaines annees. Il s'agit d'une annonce importante sur le plan des ressources investies (117 millions de dollars) et sur le plan des benefices pour l'amelioration de l'accessibilite et de la qualite des soins de premiere ligne.  Le projet vise a soutenir efficacement le deploiement des infirmieres praticiennes specialisees de premiere ligne au Quebec en developpant a court terme des connaissances robustes, contextualisees et utilisables  sur des processus d'implantation efficaces et des modeles performants de pratique infirmiere avancee de premiere ligne. Pour ce faire, le projet va s'appuyer a la fois sur la litterature scientifique disponible et sur six etudes de cas dans quatre regions au Quebec.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mise en oeuvre d'un réseau intégré de prévention et de gestion du risque cardiométabolique en 1re ligne à Montréal
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC CARE MODEL; COLLABORATION INTERORGANISATIONNELLE; DIABETE; HYPERTENSION ARTERIELLE; INTERDISCIPLINARITE; MALADIES CARDIOMETABOLIQUES; MALADIES CHRONIQUES; RESEAU INTEGRE DE SERVICES; SERVICES DE PREMIERE LIGNE; SERVICES DE SANTE
Abstract-Résumé: Au Canada, la gestion des maladies chroniques est au coeur de plusieurs transformations visant a ameliorer la performance du systeme de sante. Parmi les solutions proposees, on retrouve lapplication de modeles inspires pour la plupart du «Chronic Care Model» (CCM). Cette solution merite d'etre evaluee, afin d'apprecier dans quelle mesure les effets qui en resultent sont durables, tant au niveau des patients que des pratiques professionnelles. De plus, est-ce que l'application du CCM et la creation des reseaux integres de services pour les maladies chroniques favorisent une plus grande integration systemique? C'est a ces questions que veut repondre notre recherche, qui porte sur l'implantation du CCM dans six territoires de CSSS a Montreal. Les objectifs sont: 1- d'evaluer les effets du programme sur les patients inscrits et sur la pratique des medecins participants; 2- d'apprecier le degre de mise en oeuvre du PRC dans chacun des territoires de CSSS participants et d'identifier les facteurs contextuels pouvant l'expliquer; 3- d'etablir la relation entre les effets observes, le degre de mise en oeuvre du PRC et les facteurs contextuels; 4- d'apprecier l'impact de la mise en oeuvre du PRC sur la consolidation des reseaux locaux. Pour realiser ces objectifs, nous aurons recours a une strategie mixte, faisant appel a des methodes quantitatives et qualitatives et a des instruments de mesure que nous avons developpes dans nos recherches anterieures. Le projet sera mene en partenariat etroit avec l'Agence regionale de Montreal et les six CSSS participants. L'evaluation d'une strategie de developpement de reseaux integres pour la gestion des maladies chroniques, favorisant le developpement de reseaux locaux de services centres sur la premiere ligne, fournira des solutions fondees sur l'evidence pour le developpement de la premiere ligne et pour l'integration des services au Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Developing a Patient and Family-Centred Approach for Measuring the Quality of Trauma Care
Keywords-MotsClés: CONSENSUS METHODS; FOCUS GROUPS; INJURY; PATIENT-CENTRED CARE; QUALITY INDICATORS; SURVEY; TRAUMA
Abstract-Résumé: Each year, injuries affect 700 million people worldwide including 2 million Canadians. In Canada, injuries are the leading cause of death among those under the age of 45 years and account for more premature deaths than heart disease, lung disease or HIV infection. The human and societal burden is even greater with many survivors being permanently impaired and never returning to school, work or their "regular" lives.  Any Canadian can suffer an injury on any given day. Yet medical errors and substandard care threaten patient care. The quality of trauma care is a major public health concern and urgent action is needed to ensure quality and patient safety. Every injured Canadian should receive access to high-quality trauma care. Quality should not be determined by who we are, where we live or where we receive care. However, at present it is not possible to tell what the quality of trauma care is in Canada because it is not routinely measured or reported. But, efforts to improve care risk being ineffective unless they reflect what patients need and want. Patients and families want be involved in developing health care measures so that efforts to improve quality reflect what patients want.    We plan to begin a major work to measure and improve the quality of trauma care delivered in Canada. We propose to do this by developing the first set of patient and family-centred measures of trauma care. First, we will run focus groups to learn from patients and families what aspects of trauma care are most important to them and what they consider to be "high quality trauma care." Second, we will present the lessons learned from our focus groups to a panel of trauma care experts to develop a quality measurement tool. Finally, we will pilot test our tool and use it to map the quality of trauma care across Canada to identify opportunities to improve the way trauma services are delivered to ensure that all injured Canadians receive high quality patient and family-centred care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Why are so many patients dissatisfied with knee replacement surgery? Exploring variations of the patient experience.
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL OUTCOMES; KNEE REPLACEMENT SURGERY; ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY; PATIENT EXPERIENCE; PATIENT OUTCOMES; PATIENT SATISFACTION
Abstract-Résumé: Knee replacement surgery is the most requested joint replacement surgery in Canada.  Knee replacements in Canada among those aged 55 to 64 tripled for men, and more than tripled for women, between 1995 and 2005, and will continue to increase in response to the needs of an aging population.   As knee replacement surgery is a costly and high-demand procedure, decision makers are faced with the difficult challenge of how to provide high quality patient care that is equitable, efficient, cost-effective, and provided on a timely basis.  To date, research and policy making have focused on satisfactory outcomes and satisfied patients - the approximate 80 percent who experience significant improvement in knee joint pain reduction and increased mobility following knee replacement surgery.  Until very recently, less attention had been given to patients who are dissatisfied with their outcomes, even though they comprise about 20 percent of knee replacement patients. Recent research has identified several causes of poor outcomes and patient dissatisfaction, but we don't conclusively know why patients are dissatisfied with their outcomes, how these factors combine, or how they contribute to the patient experience.   We therefore propose to study the factors that lead to variation in the patient experience with knee replacement surgery, by interviewing patients and having them complete questionnaires on their knee replacement experiences.  The question of variation is important for different audiences: 1) patients, who want to be able to carry out normal, everyday activities 2) physicians, who want their patients to recover fully 3) health care administrators, who need to apply scarce health care dollars where they will yield the greatest benefit and 4) policy makers, who are accountable to the population.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evidence, values and priority setting methods in cancer control
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CANCER CONTROL RESEARCH; EVIDENCE-INFORMED DECISION MAKING; HEALTH ECONOMICS; INTEGRATED KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT; PUBLIC VALUES; RESOURCE ALLOCATION
Abstract-Résumé: The overarching aim of this study is to examine how we can combine evidence and public values to set priorities for cancer control programs (including prevention, screening, treatment and palliative/supportive care). Its objectives are to: (a) develop better methods for identifying, interpreting and applying evidence in different cancer control decision-making contexts; and (b) better understand if, when, and how public engagement and public values should play a part in priority setting processes for cancer control.  The study will consist of five phases:   1. Refining an existing model for evidence-based decision making to focus on cancer control, and to explicitly incorporate public values.  2.Conducting a national survey of cancer control decision-makers, focusing on how evidence and public values are used in priority setting. 3.Conducting in-depth case studies of current cancer control priority setting processes in two Canadian provinces, to explore how evidence and public values should be combined when setting priorities for cancer control. 4.Conducting pilot public engagement exercises in two Canadian provinces. 5.Developing a decision-support tool for priority setting processes in cancer control.  This study will result in guidance for decision makers on how to integrate evidence and public values in their own priority setting and resource allocation processes. By bringing together key cancer control researchers, decision-makers and members of the public, the work will seek to inform resource allocation across cancer prevention, screening, treatment and palliative care programs. The study will be based at the Canadian Centre for Applied Research in Cancer Control (ARCC), and carried out by a highly experience team of researchers and decision-makers from British Columbia and Ontario.

TitreApplicationTitle: An Interprofessional Approach to Improving the Health of Obese Adults in New Brunswick.
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE; EXERCISE; INTERVENTION STUDY; OBESITY
Abstract-Résumé: This intervention study is a joint venture between a provincial health authority, university researchers and community groups in New Brunswick aimed at creating a physician referral destination program for obese patients seeking to improve their health through behavioural change, nutritional education and physical activity. The proposed intervention utilizes an interdisciplinary team of family physicians, registered dietitians (RD), certified exercise physiologist (CEP) and psychologists to deliver a community-based lifestyle modification program that is reliant on minimal infrastructure.   A novel aspect of this work is our examination of community size and its impact on the process, viability and efficacy of an adult obesity intervention.  New Brunswick, like many regions of the world, has few large urban areas and many small rural communities. Some successful obesity intervention programs have been developed in large urban centres but these programs rely on resources, facilities and infrastructure that is unavailable in small rural communities.  The minimalist program we developed can be administered in any community with access to a community centre or gymnasium and thus has the potential to have a large impact on the management of this disease. This research team will examine the process, viability and efficacy of the proposed adult obesity intervention.  The research team and principle decision maker have collaborated previously to pilot the intervention program for overweight adults.  They will continue to work together to create a program research centre at the University of New Brunswick and to create a business plan for establishing the program in provincial communities should it prove feasible.  The work is important for all provincial and national health care bodies to consider when developing economically viable strategies to address rising obesity rate and its complications in their populace.

Un projet de recherche-action participative, formative et évaluative au sein du Réseau Planetree Québec
Keywords-MotsClés: ENVRIONNEMENTS DE TRAVAIL SAINS; FORMATIVE ET EVALUATIVE; HUMANISANT; IMPACTS-EVALUATION GLOBALE ET INTEGREE DES SYSTEMES DE SANTE; METHODE "PARCOURS COLLECTIF D'APPRENTISSAGE ORGANISATIONNEL"; PERFORMANTS; PHILOSOPHIE ET PRATIQUES PLANETREE; RECHERCHE ACTION PARTICIPATIVE; STRATEGIES D'ACCELERATION DE CHANGEMENTS DURABLES; TRANSFERT DE CONNAISSANCES; ETUDE MULTI-CAS INTERSITES (5 SITES); EVALUATION DU PROGRAMME DE SOUTIEN DU RESEAU PLANETREE
Abstract-Résumé: Comment accelerer le transfert des modeles integres de gestion d'etablissements centres sur la creation d'environnements de travail sains et performants et sur l'humanisation des soins tout en s'assurant de la perennite des changements vises et de l'atteinte des enjeux « qualite-performance » ? L'objectif central de ce projet consiste a mettre au point et rendre accessible aux utilisateurs de connaissances une methodologie de transfert de connaissances en lien avec le modele Planetree qui accelere et perennise le changement tout en permettant de mieux composer avec les enjeux qualite-performance. Cette methodologie est appelee « parcours collectif d'apprentissage organisationnel » (PCAO). Le cadre conceptuel utilise pour repondre a notre question est constitue de trois champs disciplinaires : le modele sur la dynamique de transfert de connaissances fonde sur les capacites de Parent, Roy et St-Jacques, les theories liees a l'introduction d'innovation et a l'etude du changement dans les organisations. Selon le modele utilise, l'organisation doit posseder ou acquerir quatre capacites pour assurer le succes du transfert de connaissances, soient les capacites de generation, de dissemination, d'absorption et d'adaptation et de remise en question. Au plan methodologique, il s'agit d'une recherche-action participative, formative et evaluative qui se realisera dans cinq etablissements membres du reseau Planetree. Pour repondre a la premiere partie de la question de recherche (accelerateurs de changement durable), le PCAO sera utilise a deux reprises pendant le projet. Pour la seconde partie de la question, nous utiliserons le modele d'evaluation globale et integree de la performance des systemes de sante (EGIPSS). L'un des produits exportable du projet prendra la forme d'un guide de pratique qui presentera les meilleures pratiques de transfert du modele Planetree, une revue de la litterature utilisee pour le projet, un modele integrateur et une marche a suivre par etapes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Advance Care Planning Evaluation in Hospitalized Elderly Patients: A multicenter, prospective study. The ACCEPT Study
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVANCE CARE PLANNING; AUDIT AND FEEDBACK; END OF LIFE CARE; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PROCESS IMPROVEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Our health care system is under siege- an aging population, patients living longer with chronic illness, and an increasing demand for services at end of life contribute to escalating costs. In a recent national survey, more than 80% of Canadians were concerned the quality of health care in Canada will decline as a result of increased strain on the health care system as our population gets older. Advance Care Planning (ACP) may offer some assistance with reducing health care costs for older Canadians and yet, at the same time, improving quality of care. ACP is the process by which a person considers options about future health care decisions and identifies their wishes. An advance care plan is a verbal or written instruction describing what kind of care an individual would want (or not want) if they are no longer able to speak for themselves. ACP has been shown to increase the quality of life of dying patients, improve the experience of family members, and decrease health care costs. To date, there has been no evaluation of the effectiveness of ACP from the perspective of patients and families. We need this information to guide successful implementation of ACP in our society at large and in hospitals specifically.  In 10 hospital sites in BC and Alberta , we propose to conduct a prospective audit of current practice related to ACP in elderly patients at high-risk for dying and their families. The insights we gain from evaluating ACP can be used to improve the quality and quantity of ACP in Canada and thus, we have the potential to improve end of life care and reduce health care costs.

TitreApplicationTitle: Managing the Social Environment: What Matters for First Line Managers

Abstract-Résumé: The broad span of control of first line hospital managers translates into influence. Their direct reports look to them for direction. They also look to their supervisors to explain their complex work environment. Maintaining a strong level of collegiality is a foundation for managers' influence. The purpose of this research project is to develop and assess methods for helping first line managers fulfill their role in managing the social environments of their work groups. Through interviews, focus groups, surveys and a two phase intervention program, we will develop and assess methods for helping first line managers fulfill their role in inspiring teamwork and addressing difficult interpersonal situations. The research initiative will provide a deeper understanding of the role of first line managers and their impact on employee engagement and productivity, which in turn, directly affects patient care. The project targets improving care delivery through an examination of health human resource issues. The impact of this research initiative will provide the impetus for policy change within administrative and organizational sectors of health care institutions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Care and Construction: Assessing Differences in Nursing Home Models of Care on Resident Quality of Life
Keywords-MotsClés: CONTINUING CARE POLICY; CULTURE CHANGE; FAMILY INVOLVEMENT; INTEGRATED TRANSLATION; LONG TERM CARE; MIXED METHODS; MODELS OF CARE; RESIDENT CENTERED CARE; RESIDENT QUALITY OF LIFE; SATISFACTION; STAFF EXPERIENCE
Abstract-Résumé: A team of researchers and nursing home representatives are working  together to learn about the differences that different physical designs and staffing approaches in nursing homes may have on their resident quality of life.  Across Canada, long term care providers, funded both publicly and privately, are struggling to meet the care needs of an aging population while operating with aging buildings and staffing challenges. At the same time, many are working to transform their environments, practices and policies to focus on the resident. Nova Scotia is implementing a 10-year continuing care strategy that includes increasing bed capacity, building new facilities that feature a series of small, home like neighborhoods, and adopting changes in approach to staffing. These changes have implications not only for the resident, but also for their family and the staff. How will changes in approach to care and nursing home design impact residents and their quality of life? This three-year project will use multiple research methods to address this question, for the first time, from three important perspectives - the resident, the family, and the staff - as all three are important to understanding and advancing resident-centered care in nursing homes. Key to the success of the project is the opportunity afforded to participants and knowledge users to provide input and/or validation of research results.  The knowledge generated by the project will guide seniors, families, and service providers, in Nova Scotia and beyond, who strive to improve our capacity to provide high quality long term care.

TitreApplicationTitle: The First National Retinopathy of Prematurity Survey: Formulating Evidence-Based Screening Recommendations
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH POLICY; NATIONALLY BASED; NEONATES; PROSPECTIVE DATA COLLECTION; RETINOPATHY OF PREMATURITY; SCREENING GUIDELINES; THRESHOLD DISEASE
Abstract-Résumé: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is a leading cause of preventable blindness and visual impairment in the developed world.  It involves the formation of blood vessels in the retina of very premature newborns, leading to bleeding, detachment of the retina and potentially blindness if not treated. Currently in Canada, over four thousand newborns are screened for ROP each year, yet there is no nationally accepted standard as to which children should be included in the screening program or how often they should be screened. The current published Canadian recommendation is to screen all infants under 1501g at birth and/or whose gestation period prior to birth was less than 30 weeks. However, a survey of 16 centres across Canada revealed that at least six different screening protocols are currently being used. Since ROP has severe consequences, it is very important to focus on screening to catch the newborns at risk of blindness before they develop the disease. However, it is not desirable to screen every baby, since there are several drawbacks to ROP screening. ROP screening is expensive to the health care system, painful for the child, stressful for the parents, and time consuming for the examining doctors and nurses. The goal of our study is to formulate and implement the first ever scientifically backed guidelines for ROP screening in Canada. Our recommendations aim to enroll the least number of children into the ROP screening program and minimise the number of examinations for those enrolled, whilst still capturing all those who develop severe disease that will need treatment. This will save the health care system money that can be used for other programs, avoid unnecessary pain and anxiety to newborns and their families, and allow doctors and nurses to make better use of their time.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Network for Observational Drug Effect Studies (CNODES)
Keywords-MotsClés: DATABASES; DRUG EFFECTIVENESS; DRUG SAFETY; OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES; PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Despite extensive pre-approval studies of safety and effectiveness of prescription drugs, it has been estimated that up to 10,000 Canadians die yearly and 150,000 are hospitalized from adverse drug reactions.  The need for post-approval studies of drug safety and effectiveness is well recognized.  New challenges challenges require large and quickly accessible databases for the study of rare and serious adverse events, of drugs used for infrequent diseases, and to study medications early after they enter the Canadian market. A grant of 17.5 million dollars has just been awarded by CIHR's DSEN initiative to the Canadian Network for Observational Drug Effect Studies (CNODES), headed by Dr Samy Suissa of the Jewish General Hospital's Lady Davis Institute and McGill University in Montreal, to address these challenges over the next five years.  This network assembles the top pharmacoepidemiologists in the country, using a pan-Canadian collaborative approach.  CNODES will use existing healthcare databases on over 27 million people and sophisticated, cutting edge and powerful analytical methods, to rapidly evaluate the risks and benefits of medications on the health of Canadians. The creation of the Canada-wide CNODES will thus provide a powerful tool to rapidly evaluate the risks and benefits of medications used by Canadians, and disseminate this information widely to all stakeholders, including clinicians, patients and decision makers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Impacts of Policy and Quality Improvement on the Determinants of Quality in Ontario Long-Term Care
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; LONG-TERM CARE; QUALITY IMPROVEMENT; REGULATION; RESIDENT OUTCOMES
Abstract-Résumé: Residents in Long Term Care have considerable difficulties in caring for themselves, suffer the impact of multiple medical conditions, and are often cognitively impaired. While staff in Long Term Care Homes do their best to care for these complex residents, Homes must manage demands of resident and families as well as provincial legislation and regulations with limited financial resources. Gaps in quality have been identified as a concern in LTC homes by researchers, policy makers and in media stories.  In Ontario, the Ministry of Health and Long Term Care introduced a new LTC Homes Act and regulations on July 1, 2010. At the same time, the Health Quality Council is actively trying to help LTC Homes improve quality of care by engaging with homes in a province-wide Quality Improvement program called Residents First. The Quality Council is also publicly reporting measures of the quality of care in LTC Homes. Our research study will examine what effects these different approaches to quality assurance and improvement are having on resident outcomes. We will also study how LTC Homes respond to these programs and observe changes in staff outcomes. Our research will describe the effects in Ontario and offer lessons to other provinces and jurisdictions regarding the effects of regulation and quality improvement programs on LTC residents, staff and homes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Soutenir l'amélioration de la qualité des soins de première ligne pour les troubles anxieux et dépressifs: Cible Qualité II
Keywords-MotsClés: APPLICATION DES CONNAISSANCES; DEPRESSION MAJEURE; INDICATEURS DE QUALITE; MODELE DE SOINS CHRONIQUES; PREMIERE LIGNE; QUALITE DES SOINS; RECHERCHE PARTICIPATIVE; SYSTEMES D'INFORMATION CLINQIUE; TROUBLES ANXIEUX; ETUDE DE CAS MULTIPLE
Abstract-Résumé: Une personne sur cinq souffre d'anxiete ou de depression au cours d'une annee. Alors qu'il existe des psychotherapies et medications efficaces, moins de la moitie des personnes qui en souffrent obtiennent un traitement qui correspond aux meilleures pratiques. Au Quebec, les services de sante mentale sont offerts principalement par les medecins generalistes et les autres intervenants de premiere ligne. Dans le but de soutenir la premiere ligne dans les soins a offrir a cette population, nous avons developpe et evalue le programme Cible Qualite. Ce programme rassemble six strategies qui ont fait leurs preuves pour ameliorer le systeme de sante, tels que le travail en collaboration et l'utilisation de la recherche dans la prise de decision clinique. Suite a cette premiere experience appreciee par les milieux de pratique, nous proposons maintenant un programme Cible Qualite II qui permettra d'aller plus loin au niveau de l'evaluation de la qualite des soins et de la collaboration entre les professionnels. Nous proposons d'implanter et d'evaluer Cible Qualite II aupres de six cliniques de sante mentale de Centres de sante et de services sociaux, et six cliniques medicales partenaires, dans differents regions du Quebec. Les milieux sont maitres d'oeuvre et peuvent choisir les elements du programme qui repondent le mieux a leurs besoins. Du point de vue de la recherche, nous souhaitons etudier le choix des strategies, examiner les facteurs qui influencent le changement et explorer l'impact du programme pour les patients. Renforcer la premiere ligne en sante mentale contribue a une meilleure efficacite du systeme de sante, a de meilleurs services de sante mentale, a un meilleur etat de sante de la population quebecoise, et a une meilleure qualite de vie des personnes atteintes et de leurs proches.

TitreApplicationTitle: Ethics and values in health policy:  improving care transitions for Ontario patients across the continuum of care
Keywords-MotsClés: CONTINUITY OF CARE; ETHICAL ANALYSIS; HEALTH POLICY; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PATIENT CARE TRANSITIONS; POLICY ANALYSIS; QUALITATIVE METHODS; SYSTEM COORDINATION; VALUES IN DECISION-MAKING
Abstract-Résumé: Patient care transitions are emerging as a priority policy issue in health systems across Canada. In recent years, there have been considerable efforts to improve patient flow to address increased demands on emergency departments and hospitals. However, concerns have been raised about the impact of these initiatives on the quality of institutional care and patient outcomes following discharge. Health policymakers are increasingly acknowleding the need to address values-based considerations more explicitly and systematically in their policymaking process. This has taken on a new urgency as governments endeavour to refocus the health system on improving quality and the patient experience, particularly related to patient care transitions. In this study, we explore the role and influence of values and other contextual factors on health policy related to patient care transitions across the continuum of care in Ontario.
