TitreApplicationTitle: Neuro-biomechanical factors in the design of transfemoral knee prostheses
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMECHANICS; KNEE JOINT MOTION; MOBILITY; NEURO-CONTROL OF MOVEMENT; TRANSFEMORAL KNEE PROSTHESIS
Abstract-Résumé: Although the ability to walk safely and efficiently is greatly reduced for a lower-extremity amputee, powered (micro-controlled) knee prostheses are now commercially available and have shown dramatic improvements in walking ability of amputees who use them. However, while technically advanced, these devices cannot predict a user's intent when performing daily activities around the home, workplace or community. For safe and efficient locomotion a powered knee prosthesis must be able to determine intent during movements and be able to respond appropriately when intent changes. This problem has been addressed quite well in the upper-extremity prosthesis field. By using muscle electrical signals in the amputee's residual limb, a micro-controlled arm prosthesis can be trained to respond very accurately to a user's intent.  However, when walking and performing physical activities the legs are acted upon by forces from the environment . These forces cause muscles to respond, "contaminating" the EMG signal and making it very difficult to predict the user's intent. However, the mechanics of a knee prosthesis follows the same rules of physics that the intact knee does, regardless of intent. When two bones (or prosthetic components) are joined together with a muscle (or motor) between them, the pattern of energy flow through the joint at any particular time will dictate what the future energy patterns can be. This could allow a prosthesis to be "thinking ahead" whilst the user is going about their business. Furthermore, the knee energy patterns are quite distinct for different activities and thus may also be used to help the prosthesis recognize specific activities, and learn new activities as they occur. Of great value is that the method can easily be implemented in current prosthesis designs. This project will develop and test this approach to determining user intent for improving the performance of micro-controlled prostheses for use during everyday human activities.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Pacemaker Channel Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Since coming to UBC in 2005 as a Canada Research Tier II Chair, Dr Eric Accili research program has made great strides and become an international leader in pacemaker channel structure and function. Pacemaker channels are proteins found in the primary pacemaker and conducting regions of the heart as well as in a variety of nerves in the brain. Using sophisticated approaches, he has developed an integrated research program that addresses broad and important issues regarding the function of pacemaker channels and their dysfunction in pathologies of the heart and nervous system. Dr Accili has had an outstanding first 4 years as a Tier 2.  He has made key and well-cited contributions to pacemaker channel research, presented his research at high-profile international meetings and developed a robust training program. His research program fits with the UBC Strategic Research Plan; it has helped to create a strong cluster of researchers and encourages trainees to undertake cutting edge research in ion channels.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: human retrovirology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Human HIV-1 and HTLV-1 retroviruses as well as Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs) are agents, which are associated with various forms of human diseases.  In this research program, the objective is to characterize new viral genes important for HIV-1 and HTLV-1 and study their potential impact in infected cells.  Furthermore we will focus our attention on the role of HERV genes in the function of the placenta.  Results from these studies will  provide important knowledge on these viruses and might contribute in the elaboration of new treatment of HIV-1 and HTLV-1-associated diseases as well as placenta-related disorders such as pre-eclampsia.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Musculoskeletal Rehabilitation
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The overarching aim of the research program is to compare the effectiveness of different rehabilitative and surgical interventions for musculoskeletal conditions, a leading cause of pain, physical disability and healthcare use internationally.  The major focus will be on interventions intended to halt or slow the progression of knee osteoarthritis by altering the joints local biomechanical environment. This aim requires a transdisciplinary approach that uses rigorous clinical research designs and incorporates the best available technologies to measure function at the joint- and patient-levels. The majority of research takes place in the Fowler Kennedy Sport Medicine Clinic and Wolf Orthopaedic Biomechanics Laboratory.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Public Health Informatics
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Health
Abstract-Résumé: My research will develop and evaluate innovative computational methods for detecting and responding to disease epidemics. These methods will be able to scan large health databases and allow public health personnel to detect disease epidemics rapidly and to initiate effective epidemic control strategies promptly with the goal of reducing illness and death. I will work to implement these methods in public health settings, and apply them to the surveillance and control of disease such as gastroenteritis, tuberculosis, anthrax, and influenza. I will disseminate findings from this research broadly to influence surveillance by public health agencies and other stakeholders within Canada and Internationally.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Synchrotron Bone Imaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic skeletal diseases, such as osteoporosis, are taking an increasing toll on Canadians and costing our Health Care system billions each year. The objective of this Canada Research Chair will be to explore innovative, powerful new methods of three-dimensional bone micro-imaging, made possible by the Canadian Light Source synchrotron.  This will provide greater insight into the processes of bone adaptation, aging and disease beyond that possible with traditional imaging technologies. The related discoveries and novel techniques generated will be translated so as to expedite further research and ultimately improve the health of Canadians.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: RNA Metabolism in Health and Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The unexpectedly small number of genes identified in the human genome underscored theimportance of post-transcriptional mechanisms in the generation of the enormous protein diversity found in human cells.  My laboratory will be investigating the physiological role of arginine methylation, a post-translational modification often harbored by RNA binding proteins, which are major players in these processes.  The functional consequences of this modification remain unclear in most cases, as do the mechanisms involved in its regulation.  I will address fundamental questions, such as how arginine methylation is modulated during cellular differentiation, but also investigate the implication of arginine methylation in various diseases, including Spinal Muscular Atrophy and cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cell Cycle Regulation and Genomic Integrity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Most advanced cancers in humans are characterized by an abnormal number of chromosomes. Our main objective is to understand how chromosomes are separated when a mother cell divides into two daughter cells. Obtaining this knowledge is a key step to allow us to understand cancer development in humans. In our previously work, we have identified a new way cells use to efficiently separate chromosomes when they divide. Our current studies show that a key cancer-associated family of proteins is involved in the new chromosome separation mechanism we have identified. We now aim at understanding how this cancer-associated protein and others regulate chromosome structure within cells. These studies will shed new light on the way that chromosome are compacted and then separated during cell division. Furthermore, this research will likely provide crucial insights into the specific causes of cancer, how we can detect them better and, finally, how we can treat them more efficiently.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chair in Epigenetic Regulation of Transcription
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The development of effective stem cell therapies for neuromuscular disease requires optimization of the survival and functional activity of transplanted cells. An understanding of the genetic program which directs the growth and development of muscle is crucial to achieving this goal.  The Canada Research Chair in Epigenetic Regulation of Transcription is dedicated to elucidating this genetic program by which mature muscle is developed from stem cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Human Cognition, Decision-Making, and Brain Plasticity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: We are continuously faced with decisions in daily life: Which breakfast cereal? Which shoes? Which school? Which job? Should I exercise? Yes but which exercise? Decision-making also affects business development and even public policy decisions. The high relevance of the proposed program has a broad implication and the objective of this research is to understand and promote healthy choices in decision-making behaviors. The uniqueness of this program lies in the integrated approach of several methods and disciplines based on sound theoretical principles from neuroscience, medicine, psychology and psychiatry. The importance stems from the potential to alleviate increasing costs to our Health System by developing strategies for improvement in behaviors related to addiction, obesity, social choice and rehabilitation following damage to brain areas and neuropsychiatric disorders related to decision-making.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Innate Immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The innate immune response is a potent first line of defense against bacterial and viral invaders that counters the proliferation of pathogens and activates far-reaching secondary defenses. With support provided by the CRC program, I established a laboratory to probe the entire genome of the humble fruitfly for critical regulators of the innate immune response. Fruitflies are ideal tools for such studies, as they are readily amenable to complex genetic manipulations and reproduce central aspects of human innate immunity. Thus, insights into fly immunity may illuminate core elements of human immunity and identify novel targets for therapeutic or pharmacological manipulation.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Bacterial Pathogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Enterohemorrhagic E. coli (EHEC) and related bacteria cause diarrheal outbreaks withpotentially fatal complications. EHEC poses a significant health threat in Canada, asillustrated by the Walkerton, Ontario outbreak. My research aims to understand the interactions between these microbes and the hosts they infect. Our bodies utilize a wide range of mechanisms to counteract bacterial infections. However, microbes such as EHEC have developed ways of overcoming resistance mechanisms in order to cause disease. My research examines this interaction from both angles, investigating the mechanisms employed by bacteria to cause disease, and the mechanisms employed by the host to resist infection.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Viral Immunity & Pathogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Infections with naturally occurring or emerging viruses represent one of the gravest threats to mankind. To date, the most effective ways to combat viral infections rely on the ability of immune mechanisms, including those orchestrated and executed by T-cells. Although viral proteins harbor thousands of peptides that can be theoretically recognized and targeted by T-cells, viral infections induce T-cell responses of varying magnitude against few peptides only. The objectives of the proposed research are to explore the reason(s) for this limitation and to invent novel immune-based strategies to induce T-cell responses of sufficient magnitude and breadth against disease-causing viruses.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Neurobiology of Synaptic Plasticity
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Nerve cells communicate at synaptic contact sites through release and detection of neurotransmitters. Synapses undergo constant changes in their ability to relay information between cells. These alterations are thought to subserve the experience-dependent adaptation of the nervous system. Our research focuses on the molecular and cellular mechanisms in presynaptic nerve cells that elicit the reorganization of neuronal connections during development and sustained alterations in neurotrans-mitter release in the mature nervous system. We will contribute to a comprehensive understanding of the cellular processes underlying learning and memory and may help to identify mechanistic determinants of neurodevelopmental disorders such as Autism.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Human Nutrition and Vitamin Metabolism
Keywords-MotsClés: Nutrition and food hygiene, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Moderate vitamin B-12 deficiency states and high intake of folic acid, the synthetic form of the vitamin folate, have been associated with increased risk of chronic diseases. This is of great public health concern because marginal vitamin B-12 deficiency is very common in the Canadian population and folic acid intake has increased since food fortification started in 1998. Dr Lamers aims to uncover the metabolic consequences of suboptimal vitamin B-12 and high folic acid intake in humans using stable isotope tracer protocols. This unique research methodology will help determine underlying mechanisms between nutrition and disease and review current public health policies related to nutrient intake recommendations.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural Biology of RNA
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: RNA is a master regulator of gene expression, and disruption of RNA-dependent events can lead to devastating human diseases, such as viral infections and cancer. The main goal of the Canada Research Chair in Structural Biology of RNA is to better understand the role of RNA in the regulation of gene expression and help the development of RNA-based tools for biochemical and therapeutic applications. The Chair will investigate fundamental aspects of RNA structure, function and engineering using a unique and innovative approach that combines biochemical and biophysical methods, NMR spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography and bioinformatics.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CANADA RESEARCH CHAIR ON INNOVATION IN HEALTH: THE IMPACT OF DESIGN STRATEGIES ON THE DISSEMINATION AND UTILIZATION OF HEALTH TECHNOLOGY
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research on industrial production and technology, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: Although health system users and planners welcome the benefits that innovative health technologies can bring, they are also wary of the risks and high costs they generate. Yet the upstream processes that influence the design of innovations and their characteristics (e.g., safety, technical features, ease of use, etc.) remain largely opaque, especially from a health care perspective. The goal of this five year CRC research program is to develop and share knowledge on the way designers and stakeholders such as R&D funders, users, regulators and media interact and shape the design of new health technologies. The CRC program will examine more especially how norms, knowledge and judgments orient strategic decisions about technological change in health care.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Genetics of Obesity
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity is dramatically increasing worldwide, and is associated with a decrease in life expectancy. Genetic factors strongly influence obesity risk, and genetic dissection of the disease is an important step towards better prevention and care. My objectives are to estimate the ethnic-specific contribution of known monogenic genes tin overall obesity, to identify the main factors delaying or worsening the monogenic obesity phenotype during the life course, to estimate the relevance of early genetic screening for personalized medicine in monogenic patients, and to identify novel genes contributing to mendelian forms of obesity by innovative approaches.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Health, ethics and diversity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: Accessibility is a fundamental value of the Canadian healthcare system. Accessibility is influenced by Canadas vast rural geography and diverse socio-demographic profile. These realities pose important ethical questions about providing good care to individuals across the spectrum of diversity in the face of limited resources.  The goal of this Canada Research Chair in Health, Ethics and Diversity is to improve care for individuals at end-of-life who are at risk for health disparities because of geographic, cultural or social differences. The unique focus on the important and intersecting influences of rurality and diversity will generate important knowledge for high quality care.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Genetics and Genomic Medicine of Inflammation
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The Canada Research Chair in Genetics and Genomic Medicine has the mission to (1) identify genetic risk factors for rare and common diseases of importance to Canadians, (2) determine the biological mechanisms by which these genetic variants can impact (positively or negatively) on an individual's risk to develop disease, and (3) translate these genetic discoveries into improved tools for the diagnosis and treatment of patients.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in postnatal neurogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: In the past decades it has become clear that new neurons can be generated throughout life in certain areas of the adult brain. This indicates that the brain may have a capacity for healing itself and offers new potentials for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases and brain trauma. The research program undertaken under this Chair is aimed at investigating the mechanisms orchestrating different steps of adult neurogenesis and to use this knowledge to improve cell recruitment in the diseased/damaged brain areas. The long-term goal of this research is to identify new strategies for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases and brain trauma.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur les réseaux de signalisation intracellulaires et la réponse inflammatoire
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer are the leading cause of death in Canada and in Western society. When death is not the end point, they jeopardized the quality of life. CVD and cancer are also the leading cause of hospital admissions and despite progress in their prevention, detection, and treatment, which exact an enormous toll in Canada (billions of dollar each year); it will still kill thousand of Canadian this year. The important role of chronic inflammatory reaction in the development of atherosclerosis, cancer and other chronic diaseses like scleroderma makes inflammation an attractive target for the future treatment of these diseases. Since several proinflammatory cytokines are responsible for the onset and progression of these diseases, the proposed research program and infrastructure aim at understanding and demonstrating the role of two family of protein kinases involved in the production of many proinflammatory cytokines associated with cancer, atherosclerosis and autoimmune diseases development.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Optimal care of people with chronic kidney disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: Despite the huge sums allocated to healthcare, there is little direct engagement between researchers and decision-makers. Thus, new programs may be implemented without incorporating best available evidence, and marginally effective programs may continue for years without an evaluation of their impact on health outcomes or costs. The ultimate objective of my research program is to improve the health of people with or at risk for chronic kidney disease. I will do this by assessing the impact of current health programs that serve this population; partnering with decision-makers to identify key areas where improvement is needed; then developing and evaluating novel interventions aimed at closing existing care gaps.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Lipids, Metabolism and Human Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Adipose tissue, i.e. fat, secretes a wide variety of substances that regulate whole body glucose and fat metabolism. Accumulating evidence suggests that impairments in adipose tissue function and metabolism are involved in the development of type 2 diabetes. While anti-diabetic medications are effective in improving adipose tissue function they are associated with a host of undesirable side effects and as such alternative approaches are needed to treat this disease. In this context, the purpose of the Tier 2 CRC in Lipids, Metabolism and Human Health is to determine the mechanisms by which insulin resistance leads to alteration in adipose tissue function, how exercise can prevent and/or reverse these changes and to determine the consequences of altered adipose tissue function on whole body metabolism.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Biostatistics and Epidemiologic Methods
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Medical and public health studies must generate accurate and reliable data that formthe basis for effective disease prevention, treatment, and health policy/promotion.Biostatistics and epidemiology are disciplines that ensure methodological rigor inthese studies by promoting scientifically-sound and resource-efficient study design,conduct, and analysis. The proposed research will tackle methodological problems inmedical and public health research through developing and applying novelbiostatistical/epidemiologic methods with a unique focus on two emerging importantareas: (1) discovery of signature patterns of genetic and gene/protein expression markers that are associated with disease risk, detection, and differences in treatment effects/toxicities; and (2) large population-based investigations on health and environment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Rural and Northern Children's Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Rural and northern children face unique health challenges, have compromised access to healthcare, and are often excluded from research, because they are geographically distant from major health services/research centres and are culturally and linguistically distinct. Thus, there is a dearth of evidence to guide health policy and practice for rural and northern children.CRC funding will support an innovative research program that will include: (i) general child health projects; (ii) special rural and northern childrens health projects; and (iii) methodological foundational projects. This program will ensure the voices and issues of rural and northern children are included in research, and build capacity in the north.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Community Child Health Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Early experiences during infancy are unequivocally important in allowing infants to achieve a "good start" in life. This research program focuses on caregiver-infant interactions in the first weeks of life to (1) determine if a community educational prevention program (the Period of PURPLE Crying) can significantly reduce the number of cases of shaken baby syndrome and infant abuse; (2) determine the importance of feeding as an enhancer of infant memory for spoken words; and (3) determine if early caregiver-infant contact is a determinant of later markers of genetic expression during the toddler years.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: The Social Determinants of Child Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social structures and relationships
Abstract-Résumé: The primary objectives of this research program are: to quantify the adverse effects of socioeconomic status on the health of our children, and to identify the characteristics of families, communities and nations which mute these effects. As a Canada Research Chair in the Social Determinants of Child Health, I will achieve these objectives through the secondary analysis of large-scale general population studies of child health and a proposed national study of child and adolescent mental disorder in Canada. This research will improve the life quality of children by identifying ways to combat the impact of socioeconomic disadvantage experienced in childhood.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: The Molecular Biology of Lyme Borreliosis
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Lyme borreliosis is an emerging disease transmitted by a bite from an infected tick. It is a problem world-wide and in Canada. Our research focuses on understanding the causative agent, which has several unique features: segmentation of its genetic material, much of which has an unusual DNA structure; the ability to continually disguise itself to avoid the host immune system through a process involving gene rearrangements; and promotion of generalized disease by entering and exiting the bloodstream to spread throughout the body. We have recently reported important findings on these subjects and will continue our investigations, which may provide information to help combat the disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Developmental Neuropathology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Del Bigio is one of the few neuropathologists in the world who can excel at both clinical and experimental neuropathology. He has described in detail the brain abnormalities associated with several diseases, in particular those of children (including complications of premature birth, hydrocephalus, cerebral palsy, and brain injury). He has developed animal models to explore novel methods for treatment of those diseases. The opportunities afforded by the Chair expand the horizons of neuropathology by intense integration with advanced imaging and engineering methods.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur la gouvernance et la transformation des organisations et systèmes de santé
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Management of businesses and institutions
Abstract-Résumé: Les systèmes de santé à travers le monde cherchent des voies pour améliorer leur fonctionnement et sadapter aux besoins de la population.  La Chaire sur la Gouvernance et la transformation des organisations et systèmes de santé vise à mieux comprendre les conditions qui permettent aux systèmes de santé dopérer des transformations importantes et daccroître leur performance.  Les travaux de la Chaire portent principalement sur limplantation des réseaux afin de mieux coordonner les soins et services et sur le rôle des connaissances scientifiques pour appuyer les efforts de transformation des décideurs politiques, gestionnaires et professionnels de la santé.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Virology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most people worldwide and persists for the life of the host.  During persistent infection, cells are induced to proliferate and can develop into malignant tumours under some circumstances. The EBNA1 protein of EBV is responsible for replicating and maintaining the viral genomes in cells and also contributes to cell proliferation and tumourigenesis.  We are studying how EBNA1 contributes to these processes and the cellular proteins involved.  Our research is unique in our application of proteomics approaches to answer these questions and has led to previously unknown connections between EBNA1 and cancer. Our research will help to elucidate how EBV genomes are maintained in proliferating cells and will identify potential drug targets to prevent or treat EBV-associated cancers. In addition our viral studies have shown how some cellular proteins normally regulate cell proliferation and survival, information that will shed light on the development of cancer in general and on potential treatments for a variety of cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada en épidémiologie périnatale
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: As the CRC in Perinatal Epidemiology at lUniversité de Montréal, my primary focus has been the evaluation of strategies to prevent maternal and perinatal mortality and morbidity through research designs including clinical trials, birth cohort studies as well as molecular epidemiology. The CRC is a lever to develop an interdisciplinary group that is emerging as a world leader in perinatal clinical research.  For example, we are conducting the first Canadian National Birth Cohort study (Maternal Infant Research in Environmental Chemicals -MIREC) to assess the maternal and perinatal burden and effects of environmental chemicals.  We are evaluating, in the context of cluster randomized trials, strategies to reduce maternal mortality and caesarean through evidence based approaches.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Chair in Diabetes Complications
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The epidemic of diabetes brings with it the enormous burden of its associated complications such that diabetes now accounts for ~1/3 of heart failure hospitalisations and almost 50% of kidney failure cases in Canada.  Despite the enormity of these problems, there has been a dearth of therapeutic advances in their treatment over the past 20 years.  Building on a background of moving laboratory research into the clinical arena, the proposed CRC in diabetes complications will focus on therapeutic discovery, examining the potential of new small molecules, biological and cell-based treatments to prevent, arrest and even reverse cardio-renal disease in diabetes.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Neurodegeneration
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: This Chair uses powerful technologies of molecular genetics, transgenic mouse models and induced pluripotent stem cells to make important contributions to our understanding of pathogenic pathways associated with neurodegenerative disorders, especially amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and to develop new experimental therapeutics. For instance, we study the mechanisms by which protein misfolding and specific genetic variations act as risk factors for sporadic ALS. We also generate cell-based systems to study the causes of ALS. The findings are translated into development of diagnostic assays and immunotherapy for ALS.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Law and Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The research programme of the Centre of Genomics and Policy (CGP) at McGill University covers five emerging areas of scientific endeavour:  reprogenetics, paediatrics, population biobanks, privacy issues and personalized medicine.  The policy challenges posed by these areas require a multidisciplinary approach.  Policy development cannot be accomplished in a vacuum.  As science becomes increasingly international, analysis of the positions of other countries, non-governmental organizations and interested stakeholders is essential.  This comparative methodology makes knowledge transfer possible and useful in the global community. The CGP will undertake such research in the hope of providing both the tools (infrastructure) and prospective analysis leading to policy guidance.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Cystic Fibrosis and Microbial Glycobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Joseph Lam is a world-class expert in Glycobiology and bacterial cell surfaces.  He chaired two FASEB Conferences on Microbial Polysaccharides and a Symposium on Biofilms and Bacterial Cell Surfaces. He has published 119 papers and 4 US patents. He has made seminal contributions toward the understanding of biosynthesis of lipopolysaccharide, and the significance of glycoconjugates on biofilm structures, motility, and adhesion of bacteria. Some protein targets from his work have been exploited for antimicrobial development. Dr. Lam has received numerous distinctions including the Roche Diagnostic/CSM Award, Fellowship of the American Academy of Microbiology, and Distinguished Professorial Teaching Award.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Genome Science
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Genes are instructions contained within the chemical DNA.  Cells obey the instructions to perform the work that the body needs them to do.  When the genes contain errors (mutations), the cells can be mistakenly instructed to behave in ways that are inconsistent with their normal functions, and cancer can result.  My team uses powerful new instruments that, for the first time, allow researchers to find all of the instructions and the mutations in the genes.  With this information, new, more effective treatment strategies can be designed to treat and cure cancers based on the specific mistakes within the cancer cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Neurogenetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: First, we wish to determine, in inherited diseases called retinal degenerations, why the mutant retina cells suddenly die, after functioning well for decades.  We predict that by dampening two hyperactive signaling pathways, we can prolong the life of the mutant photoreceptors, preserving vision.  Second, we predict that two brain proteins (Neto1, Neto2) we discovered are critical to the formation of brain synapses, signaling through synapses, and regulating the neuronal excitability that allows the brain to respond to the environment.  Elucidation of the role of the Netos in these critical processes will provide important insights into how our brains function.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Comparative Genomics and Evolutionary Bioinformatics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research, Protection of species and habitats
Abstract-Résumé: One hundred and fifty years after the publication of Darwins Origin of Species we are finally able to reconstruct the earliest phases of evolution of Life on Earth by characterizing and comparing the genome sequences of diverse unicellular organisms. In this research program we will use high-throughput DNA sequencing and bioinformatics methods to investigate two important evolutionary transitions: (i) the origins of the multicellular kingdoms of animals and fungi, and (ii) the ability of some unicellular nucleus-containing organisms to thrive in the absence of oxygen and cause disease. From these investigations, we will gain an enhanced understanding of the mechanisms by which the major kingdoms of life first evolved, as well as the major forces driving the diversification of microbes that impact on human health and our environment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Integrative Physiology of Exercise and Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The benefits of physical exercise affect the health and function of many body systems including blood vessels, the brain, and peripheral nerves. Dr. Shoemakers research is unique in that it emphasizes cellular and whole-body processes linking the brain, peripheral nerves and blood vessels, as well as how these systems are related to disease and lifestyle.  His research includes three major objectives that will establish greater information on neural discharge patterns and neurovascular interactions, determine cortical regions involved in monitoring and affecting sympathetic nervous system function, and quantify the role of exercise in neuroprotection through improved vascular supply of brain and nerves.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Knowledge Translation and Quality of Care
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Hospital structure and organization of medical care
Abstract-Résumé: The public will only benefit from research if research findings are appropriately translated into policy and practice. Evidence shows that health systems fail to optimally translate evidence which impacts quality of care. Knowledge translation (the implementation of knowledge) has emerged as a potential solution.  This program will support the growth of a transdisciplinary research team focused on advancing the science and practice of knowledge translation. It will place Canada in a position of leadership by providing a unique model for research to improve the health of Canadians through the nurturing of collaborations amongst researchers and trainees from various fields.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Genomics Applied to Nutrition and Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Nutrition and food hygiene
Abstract-Résumé: Several diseases such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes and obesity have both genetic/epigenetic and environmental causes. Dietary modification is considered as the cornerstone of primary prevention for such diseases. This is the central argument to adopt population-based nutritional guidelines. However, a large inter-individual variability in the response to dietary interventions exists. This variability is determined by genetic/epigenetic factors. The objective of the proposed research program is to understand how genetic/epigenetic factors and environment act together to cause chronic diseases, and how the environment (e.g., diet) in a given genetic background might be manipulated to prevent or delay the onset of disease.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Imaging for Cardiovascular Therapeutics
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: With recent advances, cardiovascular disease is being transformed from a sudden killer into a chronic treatment challenge. Emerging therapies can improve blood supply and reduce heart tissue damage which causes arrhythmias and heart failure. Realizing this potential requires better treatment planning, intervention guidance, and outcomes monitoring through advances in cardiovascular imaging. Specifically, the proposed research program will transform cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging into quantitative volumetric mapping of pathophysiology for more accurate disease characterization. Furthermore, more effective therapeutic targeting is facilitated by unique strategies combining these maps with real-time imaging and with localized physiological measurements from new catheter-based sensors during interventions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Neuroimmunovirology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Viruses may be involved in neurological diseases of unknown etiology such as multiple sclerosis (MS). Coronaviruses are respiratory viruses that cause such disease in genetically susceptible rodents. We showed they can infect cells of the human nervous system, persist in human brains, and produce potentially harmful white blood cells in MS patients. This research program will  characterize the potentially neuropathologic interaction of coronaviruses with the nervous and immune systems, both in human cells and in an animal model. Understanding mechanisms and consequences of such interactions will be essential to the design of diagnostic and intervention strategies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Voltage- and ligand-gated calcium channels are important players in the regulation of calcium entry into neurons under both physiological and pathophysiological conditions.  Our laboratory uses a combination of state of the art experimental approaches to examine how these calcium channels are regulated, and how they contribute to disease. Our work on voltage gated calcium channels revolves around their roles in pain and in seizure disorders, and how they are modulated by cellular signaling pathways.  Our role on NMDA receptors is concerned with their regulation by cellular prion protein, and how this regulation protects from neuronal cell death.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Pain and Cognition
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Psychiatric and neurological illnesses are among the most common and serious health problems worldwide, and their prevention and treatment are dependent on advances in neuroscience.  We hypothesize that mechanisms for chronic pain may share some common signalling pathways and neuronal networks with mental diseases. Therefore we propose to study long-term plastic changes in higher cortical regions after nerve injury or inflammation.  Complementary approaches will be used to explore important signalling pathways related to sensory synaptic transmission, regulation and plasticity.  Findings from these studies will lay the groundwork for treatment of patients with neurological illnesses, including chronic pain, anxiety and depression.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Translational Psychiatric Genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: As a society, we have great interest in how genetics influences health and illness. Among individuals with mental illnesses and their families, there is great interest in how genetics might influence these conditions. Progress in psychiatric genetics is being made, and we need to translate this complex information into benefit for individuals who have mental illnesses and their families. The aim of this program of research is to use knowledge from psychiatric genetics to develop new talk-based and biological treatments to improve outcomes for individuals with mental illnesses and their families.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chemical and Functional Genomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Renewable energy sources
Abstract-Résumé: Yeast are an excellent model for human cells because their basic cellular functions are nearly identical to that of humans.  Dr. Baetz is integrating innovative high-throughput yeast chemical and functional genomics techniques with traditional biochemistry and molecular biology to identify proteins and signaling molecules that contribute to Cancer and Alzheimers disease progression. Dr. Baetzs genomic studies will significantly advance our understanding of these disease and help in the development of effective new therapeutics. Dr. Baetz is using genomics to improve the efficiency of industrial yeast used for cellulosic fermentation, potentially improving the economic feasibility of cellulosic biofuel industry in Canada.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cardiovascular Disease and Physical Activity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The purpose of my research is to (1) identify key correlates of physical activity using a social ecological model and (2) utilize this information to develop effective multi-level physical activity interventions in patients living with heart disease.  The end goal is to figure out how to deliver cardiac care services in a cost-effective way that will increase the patients physical activity levels to help prevent recurrence and mortality, the development of comorbidities, and improve their quality of life.  This is the only research of its kind to utilize a multi-level approach in the cardiac population.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neural Information Coding
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: We rely on our senses constantly in everyday life. While most of us take this for granted, this does not apply for over 3,600,000 Canadians suffering from impaired sensory function (e.g. deafness). My research program aims to uncover the algorithms used by the brain to accurately represent our environment using a strongly interdisciplinary approach combining both experimental and theoretical approaches. Developing quantitative methodologies in order to assess brain function will lead to novel tools for diagnosis and treatment of these sensory deficiencies; in part by developing improved neural prosthetics that will alleviate the symptoms of these people.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Research Chair Molecular Neurobiology of Brain Repair
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Fawcett's research program focuses on characterizing intracellular signaling pathways that regulate actin dynamics to control neuronal development. His laboratory utilizes molecular and genetic approaches in his studies. He has characterized a novel role for the SH3/SH2 family of adaptor proteins in mammalian locomotion. Further, he has made significant progress in identifying a novel intracellular signaling pathway that controls synapse development. Interestingly, this pathway has been implicated in neurological diseases such as schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. His laboratory is currently funded through operating grants from CIHR, NSERC, and a Research Scholar award from the EJLB Foundation.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cell signaling, virus infection and cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Our research focuses on the understanding the cellular signaling mechanisms that control the expression of genes involved in the first line of immune response against Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection and in the uncontrolled proliferation of breast cancer cells. An original aspect of our research is to characterize the role of oxygen derivatives in the modulation of these mechanisms. Our research has wide therapeutic implications, as many validated target molecules of drug research are signaling related molecules. We anticipate that our research will provide a previously uncovered panel of potential molecular targets to control specific outcomes for antiviral or anticancer therapies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Airway Cell and Molecular Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: In the past two decades asthma rates in Canadian children (>10%) and adults (>5%) are climbing despite greater use of asthma medications. Though symptoms are controlled in most patients with inhaled steroids that limit lung inflammation, a hallmark feature of asthma, about 15% of asthmatics are steroid insensitive and exhibit severe, life threatening disease. They account for >50% of asthma costs, so new effective therapies are needed. Lung inflammation in severe asthma is unique because it features cells called neutrophils that are resistant to steroids and release damaging proteins. This project examines one such protein, called S100A8/A9, and to identify targets for new drugs we aim to understand how it generates responses in lung cells that result in severe asthma. Our project also assesses compounds based on drugs (called statins) that lower serum cholesterol, that may reveal a new class of therapy for inflammation in asthma, bronchitis, emphysema and influenza virus infection.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neonatal Health and Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Infants born prematurely are cared for in neonatal intensive care nurseries where they undergo repeated diagnostic and therapeutic procedures that are needed to save their lives, but that can be painful and stressful.  For these infants, early exposure to pain and stress can cause injury to their  brains and are linked to developmental abnormalities seen later in childhood.  Dr. Holsti works with parents, nursery staff and other researchers to find new ways to assess and treat the pain and stress associated with neonatal intensive care, research that is aimed directly at improving the developmental outcomes of these vulnerable infants.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Physical Activity and Obesity
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The research program is focused on two health determinants, obesity and physical inactivity.  Population-based approaches that rely on thousands of participants will be used.  The research program will address three theme areas.  The first theme will develop evidence that will be used to improve physical activity guidelines.  The second theme will determine what features of the built environment (e.g., street networks, playgrounds, local food retailers) influence dietary patterns, physical activity, and obesity in youth.  The third theme area will address how emerging changes in dietary and physical activity patterns impact obesity in developing countries such as Mexico and Kenya.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: CRC Tier 2 in Neurological Health Services and Population Health Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Despite the significant impact of neurological conditions on patients and society, our knowledge of their frequency, their co-existing conditions and their health services utilization patterns remains limited. Such knowledge is critical in planning for the health care needs of Canadians with brain and spine conditions.  Apart from stroke, surveillance of neurological diseases is rudimentary in Canada. The work proposed here will enhance capacity for national neurological disease surveillance and improve quality and access to neurological care across a spectrum of conditions such as Alzheimers disease, Parkinsons disease, epilepsy and multiple sclerosis to name a few.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Global Perspectives on HIV and Sexual and Reproductive Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Health
Abstract-Résumé: In many regions of the world, HIV incidence is increasing most dramatically among young women aged 18-30 years - women in their peak reproductive years. While evidence indicates that HIV positive women continue to desire children, become pregnant and give birth after contracting HIV, little research has been done to examine the sexual and reproductive health concerns of people living with HIV in low resource settings     Advances in HIV treatment (i.e., highly active anti-retroviral therapies) have made it possible for people living with HIV to live long and productive lives and more evidence is needed to inform the development of appropriate and responsive health services for HIV positive women globally that addresses both HIV prevention and their fertility goals.  Dr. Kaida's research program will investigate trends and predictors of sexual and reproductive behaviours and outcomes in two HIV endemic countries: Uganda and South Africa. Her vision is to lead a Centre for Global Health Research on HIV and Seuxal and Reproductive Health in sub Saharan Africa.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Electrophysiology and Adult Congenital Heart Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease is the most common type of birth defect.  Most infants now born with moderate or severe heart disease survive to adulthood.  Abnormal heart rhythms are the leading cause of death and impaired quality in adults with congenital heart disease.  The proposed comprehensive multifaceted research program strives to better understand population trends related to arrhythmias and overall survival incongenital heart disease, characterize the different forms of arrhythmias, better identify patients at risk of dying from arrhythmias, and improve directed therapies in the hopes of ameliorating quality of life and prolonging survival in this rapidly expanding population of patients.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Pharmaceutical Sciences
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Reactive oxygen species are ubiquitous reactive molecules formed in the body. Their generation can be enhanced by various chemicals or by environmental stimuli. These species have numerous adverse, and some beneficial effects on cells. The proposed research program will investigate the mechanisms by which reactive oxygen species are generated and how and to what end they disrupt or stimulate cellular and intercellular communication pathways. Signaling cascades identified as being affected by reactive oxygen species will be investigated further in order to identify novel targets and develop strategies to modulate stress-induced signaling to either diminish toxic or augment desired effects.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Osteoclast biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: The destruction of bone is characteristic of several classes of musculoskeletal disorders, including osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis and cancer metastases to bone. My research program is aimed at understanding how the cells responsible for bone destruction, osteoclasts, are controlled by different cells, molecules and mechanical forces present in bone and bone marrow, using innovative technologies, such as high-speed imaging of live cells and atomic force microscopy, as well as mathematical modeling. These studies will improve our understanding of physiological and pathological bone turnover, and may lead to the development of new types of therapy for inflammatory, metabolic and metastatic bone diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Physical Activity Promotion for People with Mobility Impairment
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Health
Abstract-Résumé: A mobility impairment is any condition that affects a person's ability to move.  Nearly 1,580,000 Canadians between 25 to 64 years of age have a mobility impairment. These people often experience poor health. Participation in physical activity can reduce some of burden associated with mobility impairment. Yet, there have been no systematic efforts to increase physical activity in this population. To address this gap, the proposed research aims to 1) develop guidelines recommending the amount and type of physical activity for adults with mobility impairment to gain health benefits and 2) evaluate messages and communication strategies that optimize adherence to the guidelines.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de Recherche du Canada en Génétique des Maladies Cardiovasculaires et Hématologiques / Canada Research Chair in Cardiovascular and Hematological Diseases Genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: My research program tackles the genetic roots of some of the main debilitating human diseases worldwide: cardiovascular and hematological diseases. Recent progress has been made in the identification of DNA polymorphisms that predispose to, or protect from, common complex human diseases. Because these initial findings only explain a small proportion of an individuals genetic risk to develop a disease, we will continue our search for genetic risk factors using large and unique genome-wide association study datasets. We will also use emerging technologies  in particular next-generation DNA re-sequencing  to characterize all genetic variation in genes associated with cardiovascular and hematological diseases, and to identify rare mutations that cause or modify disease severity.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Functional Genomics and Cellular Proteomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: A major challenge of the post-genome era is to understand how dynamic protein-protein interactions regulate normal cell physiology and how aberrant interactions result in diseases such as cancer. The goal of this CRC is to identify, systematically, protein-protein interactions and the resultant signaling networks mediated by phosphorylation, a prevalent post-translational modification occurring on numerous regulatory proteins. We will uncover, using proteomic approaches such as peptide and protein microarrays and mass spectrometry, how changes in protein tyrosine phosphorylation and the accompanying changes in the underlying phosphorylation signaling network affect cellular state and leads to cellular transformation and metastasis of cancer.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Spatial Genome Organization
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Much like the proper arrangement of furniture items within a room ensures its proper function; we have recently discovered that the organization of DNA inside a structure called the nucleus protects our DNA.  Interestingly, we discovered that proteins present in both yeast and human cells play a key role in spatial DNA organization.  Moreover, mutations in the human forms of these proteins lead to premature aging and several muscle diseases.  Using both yeast and human cells, we study how these proteins protect DNA and sustain health.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural Biology of Signal Transduction
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: My research focuses on understanding the regulation of eukaryotic proteins in 3 important biological areas: 1) signal transduction, 2) protein translation and 3) RNA silencing. We use a variety of biophysical approaches to tackle these systems including techniques that provide 3D structural information like X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance and small-angle Xray scattering, and techniques to analyze function such as enzymology and mutagenesis. By deducing the mechanisms that regulate proteins at the molecular level, we can devise drugs to modulate their function in diseased states such as cancer and autoimmune disorders.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Airway Inflammometry
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The primary objective of the Airway Inflammometry progam is to develop and evaluate new methods to non-invasively assess airway inflammation in patients with severe asthma and COPD in the hope that this will lead to better management of these conditions and to the development of new therapies. The focus of research for the next five years is to identify mechanisms of severe asthma in non-allergic patients and in patients with chronic rhinosinusitis, automate the methods that we have developed to assess inflammation in order to make them available widely globally, develop new and more precise methods to non-invasively assess airway inflammation particularly eosinophilic inflammation and apply these methods to develop new and more effective therapies that are immediately available to treat patients with severe asthma.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Proteomics and Molecular Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: How a cell senses its environment, then relays this information to the internal cellular machinery, is a critical research area.  In response to these intracellular signals, a cell may grow, stop growing, or even commit suicide.  Many diseases (e.g., cancer or Alzheimer's disease) are a result of cells losing their ability to interpret or control these signals.  One important way that cells regulate their internal machinery is via the addition or removal of chemical modifications on proteins.  To understand how these modifications regulate protein function, my laboratory uses mass spectrometry to identify and characterize them in normal and abnormal cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Injury Prevention and Mobility Biomechanics
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: As a Tier II Canada Research Chair in Injury Prevention and Mobility Biomechanics at Simon Fraser University, my research focuses on preventing hip fractures and other fall-related injuries in older adults. The proposed research program involves capturing real-life measures (through video and wearable sensors) of fall mechanisms and mobility patterns, and examining how these associate with physical and cognitive function. It also involves the development and evaluation of compliant flooring for high risk environments, and next-generation wearable protective gear, for preventing fall-related injuries. This work is recognized internationally for addressing important, yet underexplored topics in bone health and mobility.

TitreApplicationTitle: Chair in Ischemic Proliferative Retinopathies
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: In its various manifestations, pathological retinal blood vessel growth is the leading cause of blindness worldwide. Examples include diabetic retinopathy (DR) and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) (the main causes of blindness in pediatric and working age individuals) and age related macular degeneration (AMD) (the prominent blinding disease in the mature (>65 yrs) population). The proposed research program presents two distinct research projects that set out to decipher the cellular mechanisms governing these diseases with the ultimate translational goal of devising novel therapeutic strategies. The first investigates the role of molecules classically reported to be involved in neuronal development (Semaphorins) as mediators of pathological vessel growth in DR and ROP. The second explores the molecular mechanisms by which ù-3 lipids and their derivatives participate in preventing AMD progression.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Apoptotic Signaling
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Signaling proteins called kinases make excellent drug targets. In the first term of the Chair, we have developed a novel screening tool to rapidly identify candidate kinases that modulate the biological activity of proteins that control critical cell functions, such as cell growth  and cell death. This information will permit the rapid identification of potential targets for therapeutic interventions in numerous human disease settings. In addition, the Chair has developed a multi-million dollar cell-based screening facility for disease gene identification in the post-genomic era. This facility is one of two in Canada, and represents a key institutional resource for future recruitment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Although most cells in our bodies are exposed to biomechanical forces, little is known about how these forces regulate cell function to cause growth and disease. The proposed research program uniquely integrates engineering and new technologies with advanced cell and molecular biology to dissect the mechanisms by which mechanical cues regulate cell function. This research will help identify factors that cause heart valves to calcify and skeletal tissues to regenerate, ultimately leading to novel therapies. Trainees from this program will be equipped with the interdisciplinary tools required to turn ideas into innovations that will solve Canada's most important health challenges.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neuroepidemiology and multiple sclerosis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a degenerative disease of the brain and spinal cord.  Every day, 3 more Canadians are diagnosed with this progressive disorder with no cure.  My research goals are to investigate possible underlying factors driving disease progression  from genes to the environment. Whether current MS drugs have any long-term beneficial or even harmful effects will also be examined. A core component of this program will focus on bringing together, for the first time, multiple large health databases created for over two decades by physicians and pharmacists. Ultimately, we aim to improve the health, treatment options and outcome for people with MS.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Primary Care Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: In the next five years, the Canada Research Chair in Primary Care Research will focus on two broad objectives that affect the health of all Canadians. The research will focus on chronic diseases in primary care, specifically understanding the complexities of living with and caring for individuals with multiple chronic diseases, particularly among seniors. The research program will also address ethical issues related to pandemic influenza response, such as allocating scarce resources, communicating risk and building public trust, and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations, particularly in light of the recent H1N1 pandemic influenza.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Nutrition, Development and Aging
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: My research aims to improve bone health by studying key nutrients such as vitamin D and omega fats at all ages.  Many studies are conducted in newborn infants and young children who are followed for long-term outcomes.  Some studies focus on aging and nutritional needs to stay healthy while others focus on ethnic groups at risk for not getting enough vitamin D and omega fats such as First Nations and Inuit people.  The impact on the health of Canadians is building healthy bones to last a lifetime and by providing new information to guide food fortification and public health policy.

ClasseRechercheFR: TRAUMATISME,REGENERATION; AFFECTIONS DE LA MOELLE EPINIERE
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular pathways regulating long-term maintenance of adult stem cells
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL BIOLOGY; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; NEUROBIOLOGY; NEURONAL APOPTOSIS; NEURONAL DEVELOPMENT; NEURONAL INJURY; NEURONAL REGENERATION; NEUROTROPHINS; STEM CELLS; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Increasing evidence indicates that tissue repair and regeneration are mediated, at least in part, by adult stem cells, and that the negative effects of aging are due to reduced function of these stem cell populations.  However, the molecular factors that promote maintenance and longevity of adult stem cells and, thus, the longevity of tissues are largely unknown. In this regard, the Miller laboratory previously identified and characterized an adult stem cell from the skin that they called SKPs for Skin-derived Precursors, which had striking similarities to stem cells identified in a particular region of the brain.  Importantly, the Miller lab recently demonstrated that SKPs derive from a sox2-positive endogenous dermal stem cell, the first such to be identified, that apparently serves to maintain and repair the dermis layer of the skin. The Miller lab also recently started to identify particular molecular pathways that are responsible for maintenance of endogenous SKPs; in particular, two proteins of interest were identified, called TAp63 and sox2.  Specifically, mice lacking TAp63 displayed aberrant wound-healing and premature skin aging, coincident with enhanced SKPs senescence, and, in initial studies sox2+/- mice displayed decreased hair follicle morphogenesis and aberrant wound-healing.  In other words, the TAp63 and sox2 are proteins that help to maintain the SKP cell population as aging progresses.  I have therefore hypothesized that TAp63 and sox2 function to maintain dermal stem cells for the lifetime of the animal, and to thereby promote tissue repair and prevent tissue aging.  I will test this hypothesis using mice with genetic alterations to specific groups of skin cells to identify the exact role of the proteins TAp63 and sox2 in those cell types.  The findings of this proposed research will improve our understanding of stem cells and how they can be effectively used in regenerative medicine and may lead to improved health of Canadians.
