TitreApplicationTitle: Multi-modality imaging assessment of metabolic and vascular effects of radiation and chemotherapy in malignant glioma
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGENESIS; DYNAMIC CONTRAST-ENHANCED COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (DCE-CT); FUNCTIONAL IMAGING; HELICAL TOMOTHERAPY; MALIGNANT GLIOMA; POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY (PET); RADIOTHERAPY; STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY; TRACER KINETIC ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: With an average life expectancy of 14 months, malignant glioma is the most common and deadly brain cancer. More intensive radiation and novel chemotherapeutic agents that target tumour vasculature are finding their ways into clinics. Large-scale evaluations of these new treatments require a non-invasive and quantitative biomarker to assess treatment response. Tumour hypoxia (reduced oxygen level) leads to resistance to cancer therapies. Under hypoxic conditions (e.g. low blood flow), tumour cells can upregulate anaerobic glucose metabolism and stimulate the growth of new blood vessels (angiogenesis). Thus, hypoxia, metabolism, and angiogenesis are targets for cancer treatments and biomarkers of treatment response. We are testing a new imaging combination to assess treatment response based on tumour hypoxia, metabolism, and angiogenesis. Dynamic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (DCE-CT) can be used to assess angiogenesis by mapping out tumour blood flow, volume, and vascular permeability. Dynamic positron emission tomography (PET) can be used to map out the rate of glucose metabolism. The ratio between blood flow and metabolic rate is our surrogate of hypoxia. We are currently using DCE-CT to monitor treatment response of this cancer to radiation in an animal model. We are also developing an automated method for measure blood glucose concentration to circumvent the difficulties of manual blood sampling in dynamic PET imaging. Thirdly, DCE-CT coupled with PET will be used to assess the vascular and metabolic effects of radiation and a novel agent that targets tumour blood vessels (Bevacizumab). Using a hybrid PET/CT scanner, an ongoing clinical study will correlate hypoxic tumour regions with the site of tumour recurrence. The outcomes of this research offers the promise of an early biomarker to measure treatment response even before tumour shrinkage, which will help physicians tailor treatments to individual patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health and housing: Determinants of food security among social housing residents in B.C.
Keywords-MotsClés: DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; FOOD SECURITY; HEALTH EQUITY; HOUSING
Abstract-Résumé: Food insecurity occurs when people or families lack affordable, accessible, and nutritious food.  This may occur for many reasons, including lack of money to purchase quality food, and adverse physical or mental health problems which prevent access to food.  People who live in social housing often experience food insecurity, even though there are some food security programs in place to prevent this.  Food insecurity can have serious health consequences: it has been linked to diabetes and obesity, and it can worsen other physical and mental health issues.  However, food insecurity can also be caused by health problems.  This research project investigates how the health problems of social housing residents affect their ability to access nutritious food, and whether their neighbourhood and housing situation affects this relationship.  For example, the availability of a community kitchen and storage facilities, or the proximity of a good grocery store or food bank might affect whether people are able to eat well, especially if they are already ill and having trouble accessing food.  This study will identify what neighbourhood and housing environments contribute to the reduction of  food insecurity, and how food and housing programs can further support people living in social housing to eat healthily.

TitreApplicationTitle: First Nations perspectives on strengths and needs in western mental health service provision
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL; COUNSELLING; FIRST NATIONS; MENTAL HEALTH; PSYCHOLOGY; PSYCHOTHERAPY; THEMATIC ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Aboriginal peoples in Canada experience a range of psychological issues at higher rates than the general population, including depression, anxiety, suicide, substance abuse and domestic violence. Despite these mental health concerns, First Nations peoples underutilize mental health services, such as psychotherapy. The majority of First Nations report a preference for traditional healing methods or an Aboriginal therapist; however, there are few Aboriginal psychologists in Canada and some First Nations peoples prefer not to seek traditional resources. Thus, the primary alternative is to obtain services through non-Aboriginal psychologists. Unfortunately, these experiences may be unhelpful due to practitioners' lack of knowledge about working with Indigenous clients. This study will explore First Nations' experiences in seeking western mental health services, reasons they may seek or avoid seeking western services, and themes associated with positive or unhelpful experiences with non-Aboriginal therapists. Themes will be used to improve mental health service provision and therapeutic training that reflect the needs and desires of the First Nations community. Themes associated with First Nations help seeking and avoiding behaviours can inform successful promotion of mental health services among this population. In addition, themes perceived to contribute to positive and negative therapeutic experiences can be integrated into educating psychological professionals in how to work effectively with these clients. Overall, this research will build on the lack of available literature regarding counselling Aboriginals, and will ultimately contribute to more effective psychological practice to empower and heal this oppressed and devalued population.

TitreApplicationTitle: Enhancing Trust and Communication in North-South Research Collaborations: A commons theoretical framework to equitable use and management of databases and biorepositories to support translational biomedical research
Keywords-MotsClés: BIORESOURCES; COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH; COMPARATIVE CASE STUDY; DATABASES; HEALTH ETHICS; LAW AND POLICY; NORTH-SOUTH RESEARCH PARTNERSHIPS; QUALITATIVE ANALYSIS; RESEARCH COMMONS; RISK COMMUNICATION; TRUST
Abstract-Résumé: Canadian biomedical researchers participate in significant international collaborations, increasingly with research partners in low- or middle-income countries.  These research partnerships produce data, materials and/or products at faster rates than ever before.  How these research outputs are managed and who has access to use them is becoming a research problem on its own.    Countries like Canada have enough money and expertise to use research outputs easily, while developing countries often do not have the necessary resources or capacity to use the research outputs that they have helped generate.  This can lead to issues of global impact in resource sharing and collaborations, as richer countries receive more of the benefits from the research.    This study will focus on: 1) identifying proven ways to promote communication and trust between Canada and partners in low-and middle-income countries, and 2) how to manage the sharing and use of research outputs in a fair and equitable manner.  Specific cases of biomedical research collaborations that include Canada and low-or middle-income countries and the generation of data and materials will be examined.  I will collect information from researchers, funders, policy makers, non-governmental organizations, industry and representatives from patient and community groups.  By analyzing sharing policies and collaborations from a variety of viewpoints, Canadian and international researchers will be provided with guidance on what conditions will likely lead to improved research relationships.  The overall aim of this project is to a create systems for sharing research outputs that ensure fair access, and increase the potential of biomedical research to impact the lives of Canadians and others globally.

TitreApplicationTitle: Ethnicity as a determinant of sentinel health outcomes among young Canadians
Keywords-MotsClés: CLUSTER ANALYSIS; ETHNICITY; INJURY; MULTILEVEL MODELLING; NEIGHBOURHOODS; OBESITY; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY; SOCIOCULTURAL; VIOLENCE; YOUTH
Abstract-Résumé: Canada's immigration policy is built on principles of multiculturalism and diversity. However, this diversity may also mean that Canadians will have different health risks and health problems. Even though new immigrants may define themselves as "Canadian," their home environment may result in different health risks for them compared to other new immigrants, or even those who have grown up in Canada. This may be magnified among youth, who rely heavily on their parents for guidance and support.  This study of Canadian young people will investigate differences between ethnicities for 1) physical activity and obesity, and 2) violence and intentional injury. We will also explore the effect of the ethnic composition of communities on youth. To conduct this study, we will use the Health Behaviours in School-Aged Children survey, which is a national survey of 25,000 children in 500 schools in all provinces and territories in Canada. This study will be the main focus of my Ph.D.  The results from my Ph.D. can be used by policymakers to improve programs aimed at new immigrants to Canada. For example, if we saw that certain ethnic groups had higher injury rates, we could investigate why and prevent this from happening. The outcomes I am interested in (physical activity, obesity, violence and injury) are important to investigate as they can have serious long-term consequences for our youth.

TitreApplicationTitle: A knowledge translation study to identify the best practices for disseminating parent education about drowning prevention in children
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILD SAFETY; CHILD-INJURY PREVENTION; DISSEMINATION; DROWNING PREVENTION; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PARENT SUPERVISION
Abstract-Résumé: In Canada, as in many nations, drowning is a leading cause of death and disability for children. Worldwide, drowning has resulted in a higher rate of mortality than any other cause of injury in children under the age of 15, with the highest drowning mortality rates being in children under the age of five. In Canada, drowning is a threat to children both inside and outside the home.   While teaching children how to swim is one approach to drowning prevention, research has consistently supported the protective function of close parent supervision as well. However, a false sense of security can occur among parents as their children accumulate swim lessons (i.e., parents believe that their child needs less direct supervision around water when they spend more time in lessons).  Therefore, finding the most effective ways to reach parents to educate them about young children's drowning risk and the need for close supervision is very important.  The proposed research project will identify the best strategies for delivering parent education information about drowning and supervision in cost-effective ways. Online education tools and an educational video for parents to watch at the same time that their child is in swim lessons may be effective strategies. Extensive discussion and consultation will be done with parents as well as swim lesson organizations to identify specific strategies to test and how best to implement these. Excellent relationships have already been established with the swim organizations and we are presently in collaboration with them on another research project. Community-based testing of the strategies that are identified will take place in the swim organizations, and results will then be used to direct planning about how to make information available to parents. Results of this research will help to reduce the burden of drowning risk among young Canadian children.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of time perspective in understanding and predicting smoking behaviour: Findings from the International Tobacco Control (ITC) Surveys
Keywords-MotsClés: CESSATION; CULTURE; HEALTH BEHAVIOUR; PERSONALITY; POLICY IMPACT; PSYCHOSOCIAL MODERATORS; SURVEY ANALYSIS; TOBACCO
Abstract-Résumé: Smoking remains the leading preventable cause of mortality in the world today, thus more research is needed to understand why people engage in behaviours such as smoking that are so harmful to their health. This is one of the goals of the International Tobacco Control (ITC) Project, the first major study to evaluate the impact of tobacco control policies worldwide by conducting parallel prospective surveys in 20 countries. In my doctoral research, I am using ITC data to investigate the role of psychological factors in explaining how and why a given policy may lead to changes in smoking behaviour. Specifically, one factor that I have examined as an important predictor of smoking-related behaviour is time perspective - the extent to which individuals think their current actions have future consequences. In an analysis of ITC data from five countries where both smokers and non-smokers were surveyed, I found that smokers were significantly less likely to hold a future time perspective than non-smokers. In a follow-up study, I found that stronger future time perspective among the smokers in this sample was positively associated with having a stronger orientation towards quitting. In future analyses, the longitudinal nature of the ITC surveys will enable further investigation into the predictive ability of this trait on actual quitting behaviour. I am also examining the influence of time perspective as a moderator of policy interventions designed to reduce tobacco use, such as the enhancement of warning labels on cigarette packages. Overall, the proposed research will provide insight into how tobacco control policies influence behaviour by improving our understanding of the role of personality constructs in explaining smoking uptake and cessation. This knowledge will be valuable to both researchers and policymakers in the field of tobacco control in their ongoing efforts to reduce the toll of tobacco use in Canada and across the world.

Abstract-Résumé: Head and neck surgery presents complex 3D anatomy in close proximity to critical structures (e.g., nerves, arteries, eyes), which can potentially limit surgical performance, even for the experienced surgeon. Recent advances have produced intraoperative 3D imaging systems that can provide anatomical information during surgery (e.g., surgeons can see if a tumour has been fully resected). This research will extend these systems further by overlaying optical information about the disease site (e.g., the colour and texture of a lesion) with the anatomical information (e.g., location of bones and soft-tissue in the body) to provide a more complete picture from which surgeons can evaluate the efficacy of the surgical intervention.  The aim of this research is to enable safer and more complete tumour resections in order to improve health outcomes for cancer patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of the cytosolic prion protein in the regulation of Bax ubiquitination and its impact on cell survival.
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; APOPTOSIS; ER STRESS; PRION PROTEIN; UBIQUITINATION
Abstract-Résumé: A defect in the prion protein is generally known to cause Creutzfeldt-Jacob disease in human and Mad Cow disease in bovine, two devastating diseases causing the destruction of the brain. However, little is known about the role of the normal version of the prion protein in the physiology of the cell. The prion is usually anchored to the exterior of the membrane of cells but can also exist as a free-floating protein inside of the cell. Recently, research has shown that the intra-cellular version of this protein can protect against cell death by a mechanism still under investigation. Our study should lead to a better understanding of this mechanism, by focusing on two prion-interacting proteins. This research will deepen our knowledge about the regulation of cell death, a crucial field of study in the fight against cancer, since cancerous cells generally escape cell death, as well as in neurodegenerative diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Chemical-chemical combinations: as tools to elucidate mechanism of action and as routes to drug discovery.
Keywords-MotsClés: BACTERIAL MICROBIOLOGY; CHECKERBOARD ANALYSIS; CHEMICAL COMBINATIONS; ENZYMATIC ASSAYS; HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING; MINIMUM INHIBITORY CONCENTRATIONS; PROTEIN PURIFICATION; SYNERGISTIC INTERACTIONS; SYNTHETIC SMALL MOLECULE LIBRARIES; TARGET IDENTIFICATION
Abstract-Résumé: The new field of systems biology is shedding light on the nature of cellular organization in microbes. New information suggests that cellular components exhibit network-like behaviour that is buffered by plasticity and redundancy. This reality exposes flaws in the conventional one-drug-one-target route in drug discovery and in probe development, predicting that drug combinations should have considerable advantages over one-drug approaches. In the proposed work, we will exploit this capacity with studies involving chemical combinations for a task as critical as characterizing modes of action for uncharted compounds and gaining insights into the complex biological network. We have previously shown the utility of a novel high-throughput methodology for target identification; the ability to gauge information about the pathway a compound of interest is involved in based solely on phenotypic responses to combinatory studies provides a simple and useful method for screening novel chemical matter. Full characterization of the mode of action of new bioactive molecules will add to our growing repertoire of bacterial growth inhibitory molecules. Additionally, from a drug discovery perspective, our new understanding of cell complexity strongly suggests that combinations of small molecules will have greater benefits in achieving maximum therapeutic effects. Thus, we propose to strategically survey the full combination matrix of 2,000 existing drugs through pooled screening for new synergistic combinations with therapeutic potential. Further, a screen for combinations of molecules that affect the different components of bacterial proton motive force will yield novel effective synergistic interactions. Overall, where traditional drug discovery approaches have largely overlooked systematic searches for chemical combinations, new information strongly suggests that combinations of small molecules will have a unique and powerful capacity as probes and as antimicrobial agents.

TitreApplicationTitle: Multimodal Imaging of Structure and Function Changes Associated with Leukoaraiosis
Keywords-MotsClés: ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE; BIOPHYSICAL MODELLING; HIGH FREQUENCY ULTRASOUND; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; TWO-PHOTON FLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY; WHITE MATTER
Abstract-Résumé: Brain lesions in the tissue responsible for transmitting brain signals that appear bright on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images are referred to as white matter hyper-intensities (WMH).  They are found in 25% of healthy individuals over the age of 65 and have been linked to dementia. In the healthy population the number of WMH has little impact on a person's cognitive abilities, however if a patient has Alzheimer's Disease (AD) WMH appear to be very detrimental. We aim to investigate the differences in the structure and function of WMH, and to apply this knowledge to develop an MRI method that will be able to distinguish benign WMH from those that cause damage and a loss of cognitive function. To characterize the WMH we will study an animal model of AD in which we will induce brain lesions. The natural progression of the WMH will be studied using MRI, high frequency ultrasound imaging, coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy, and histology.  Using these techniques we will look at the structure and damage of the white matter, it's physiological state, and the blood vessels supplying it. The changes in the WMH will be compared to the recovery of the animals cognitive function. By identifying which changes in the structure of the WMH are related to behavioral recovery in animals, we hope to develop an MRI method to identify those WMH that cause cognitive impairment.  This novel MRI protocol will be tested on 20 subject at various points of AD progression, namely healthy, mild cognitive impairment, early AD, and AD.

TitreApplicationTitle: The impact of tobacco smoke on immune activation during the progression of pulmonary mycobacterial disease.
Keywords-MotsClés: IMPACT OF SMOKING ON BACTERIAL IMMUNITY; LUNG DISEASE; TUBERCULOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Despite vaccination and antibiotic treatment, pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the top three infectious disease killers worldwide, responsible for 2 million deaths and 8 million new cases annually. Currently, it is estimated that one third of the world's population is latently infected with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), the causative bacteria of tuberculosis. Following primary infection, greater than 90% of infected individuals enter into an asymptomatic latency period, providing bacterial control, but never clearance. Endemic to the developing world, many TB-infected individuals do not have access to treatment, escalating the significance of TB in these vulnerable regions. Furthermore, it has been identified that tobacco smoke enhances an individual's risk for tuberculosis disease reactivation, resulting in a failure to control bacterial replication and if un-treated death. An estimated 85% of all cigarettes are consumed in the developing world. In countries such as China, it is estimated that greater than 60% of males smoke tobacco products regularly. China leads the world in cigarettes consumed daily and the number of new cases of TB detected annually. In Canada, the incidence of TB is highest in Native reserves, prisons and the homeless population. The increased incidence of TB in these populations is largely due to their close quarter living conditions. Moreover, these populations have a higher than average percentage of habitual smokers, making the impact of tobacco smoke on tuberculosis a particular concern. Despite a strong epidemiological relationship, little is known about how tobacco smoke influences the immune response of TB infected individuals, limiting their ability to control bacterial replication and prevent disease progression. Our studies will aid in the understanding of both, how tobacco smoke impacts the immune system of the lung, and the impact tobacco smoke has on TB disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effect of sepsis on the viability and function of osmosensory neurons
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL DEATH; DEAFNESS; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; FLUORESCENCE MICROSCOPY; HAIR CELLS; IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS); TRPM2; VESTIBULAR DISORDERS
Abstract-Résumé: Hair cells are the sensory cells located in the inner ear that are responsible for hearing and balance. The loss of these highly specialized cells results in deafness and balance problems, and affects people of all ages. Hair cells are unusually susceptible not only to the effects of aging and noise, but also to a number of chemotherapeutic drugs and antibiotics. Therefore, a major opportunity in the prevention of hair cell death is to understand the underlying mechanisms of death. This thesis aims to investigate the role of a specific ion channel, called TRPM2, in hair cell death. Research has shown that aging, noise, and some chemotherapeutics and antibiotics produce destructive chemical agents in hair cells as by-products of cellular stress, resulting in hair cell mortality. Based on research in other cell types, it is known that those same destructive chemical agents are able to activate TRPM2, inducing cell death. Our preliminary data show that TRPM2 is strongly expressed in hair cells. In addition, we have a unique tool for probing the function of this channel, a mouse model that lacks TRPM2 only in hair cells. The proposed research will first characterize the channel properties of TRPM2 in hair cells and then investigate its role in hair cell death. The goal is to identify drugs that will effectively block TRPM2 thereby preventing hair cell loss. TRPM2 is a relatively new player in molecular biology research, and most of what is known about it comes from cells that have been induced to artificially express it. No study has investigated its function in hair cells, and despite being implicated in numerous diseases (e.g. diabetes, stroke) very few studies have looked at how TRPM2 behaves in the cells that naturally exhibit this ion channel. Therefore, this research has the potential to give new insights into TRPM2's role in cell death and to identify therapeutic approaches for the prevention and treatment of many ailments.

Keywords-MotsClés: CELL-FREE SYSTEMS; DEADENYLATION; DEVELOPMENT; FLUORESCENT IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION; GENE REGULATION; MICRORNA-MEDIATED SILENCING; MICRORNAS; POLY(A) TAIL; PROCESSING BODIES; TRANSLATION
Abstract-Résumé: Nucleic acids are large molecules that carry the genetic information universal to all living organisms. DNA and RNA are the two most common nucleic acids. Whereas DNA is used mainly to store information, the role of RNA includes carrying the amino acid sequence that encodes for proteins and assisting in transcribing information from genes to proteins. In the last two decades, several new classes of RNAs emerged. These novel RNA molecules are small in size and can shut down protein synthesis, or in other words, silence gene expression. This phenomenon, termed RNA interference (RNAi) is evolutionarily conserved. One specific class of small RNAs, known as microRNAs (miRNAs), participates in diverse biological pathways which includes metabolism, cell death, cell fate, and development. In addition, they are also implicated in cancer and diseases. One application of RNAi is in drug therapy, in which small RNA mimics can be used and administered in patients to inhibit the expression of threatening genes, as in the case of antiviral therapy, or to knockdown specific genes that are over-expressed, as in many cancer cases. Although our knowledge of small RNAs in gene regulation has greatly advanced since their discovery, their mechanism of action and interactions with other biological processes remains unclear. The proposed research project will focus on studying the mechanism by which miRNAs regulate gene expression. We will also investigate the proteins and factors that are implicated in this phenomenon, using various molecular and biochemical approaches, and C. elegans, a powerful model organism where miRNAs were first discovered and characterized. Our studies will provide a better understanding of the biological function and the mechanism of action of miRNAs, and advance our knowledge of their regulation on gene expression in physiology and disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Comparison of flexor and extensor motoneurons to serotonin application and channel and receptor distributions in activity dependent states
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTIVITY; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; EXCITABILITY; INACTIVITY; LASER CAPTURE; LOCOMOTION; MONOSYNAPTIC REFLEX; MOTONEURON; PCR; SEROTONIN
Abstract-Résumé: Following a spinal cord transection, it has been shown in cat and rat the application of the neuromodulator serotonin (5-HT) can restore locomotor-like behaviour.  This locomotor-like behaviour is characterized by the alternating muscle activity between the flexor muscles and extensor muscles.  The restoration in locomotor-like behaviour occurs at least in part by 5-HT activating channels in the spinal network that increases the excitation of spinal motoneurons, ultimately causing muscle to contract.  Evidence has suggested that a potential difference in extensor motoneurons (neurons that cause extensor muscles to contract) and flexor motoneurons (neurons that cause flexor muscles to contract) to activate these channels exist  - favoring the extensor motoneurons.  Furthermore, after a spinal cord injury, spasticity is generally seen in extensor muscles but not flexor muscles and spasticity is thought to occur by an increase in sensitivity to 5-HT.  Combined, this suggests that differences exist in sensitivity to 5-HT between extensor and flexor motoneurons.  The purpose of my PhD will be to examine which motoneurons properties 5-HT alters in a normal state and a period of inactivity.  As well to examine if there are differences in how 5-HT modulates extensor and flexor motoneuron properties and to compare the potential differences in the number of channels and receptors on the motoneurons that 5-HT is known to activate.  This research is significant because it will provide insight into how motoneurons are modulated by 5-HT in different activity levels.  As well, it will provide important information about differences in extensor and flexor motoneurons for the purpose of therapeutic and pharmacological interventions aimed at restoring walking after a spinal cord injury.

TitreApplicationTitle: Refining Imaginal Exposure Procedures for Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY DISORDERS; COGNITION; COGNITIVE BEHAVIOURAL THERAPY; COGNITIVE PROCESSES; GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER; IMAGINAL EXPOSURE; MENTAL IMAGERY; MODERATORS; WORRY; WRITTEN DISCLOSURE
Abstract-Résumé: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is a chronic condition marked by excessive worry. GAD is common and is associated with many other illnesses. Relative to people without an anxiety disorder, people with GAD have higher rates of unemployment, and overutilize the Canadian healthcare system. Given this, it is concerning that the current psychological treatments for GAD are failing to reduce symptoms for up to 40% of treatment completers. This can be addressed by examining ways to improve the effectiveness of GAD treatment.  People with GAD worry about catastrophic scenarios, and thus, avoid imagining such scenarios clearly. Avoidance maintains all forms of anxiety, including GAD. Confronting the object or situation that is being avoided is an effective way to reduce anxiety. In GAD, the object or situation being avoided is mental images of feared scenarios that have not yet occurred, so these mental images must be confronted in the imagination (called imaginal exposure [IE]). IE is currently used to treat GAD, and studies show that it reduces worry. For my Master's research I compared the impact of imagining the same worrisome scenario during IE to imagining several different scenarios. Confronting the same scenario reduced GAD symptoms over time, while confronting different ones did not. To further test factors that may improve IE, I have proposed two studies. Study 1 is based on the finding that people with GAD have great difficulty tolerating uncertainty. This study will test the effectiveness of asking people with GAD to imagine scenarios that are purposely uncertain. Study 2 is based on research that suggests that talking aloud may evoke more emotion than writing. This study will examine whether making an audio-recording of a feared scenario and repeatedly listening to it is more effective than repeatedly writing about it. The findings of the proposed research will be used to refine how IE is conducted in practice and may improve the success rate of GAD treatme

Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER ET MALADIES CARDIOVASCULAIRES; CELLULE; ESSAI D'ACTIVITE LUCIFERASE; HYPOXIA-INDUCIBLE FACTORS; HYPOXIE; MUTAGENESE; PCR EN TEMPS REEL; PROTEIN ARGININE METHYLTRANSFERASES; SIGNALISATION; SYSTEME CRE/LOX
Abstract-Résumé: L'oxygene est une molecule essentielle a une multitude de processus biologiques necessaires a la vie. Une carence en oxygene (hypoxie) est une situation pouvant avoir lieu de facon generalisee ou regionale dans l'organisme lors d'un desequilibre entre l'approvisionnement et la demande en oxygene. Par exemple, de l'activite physique ardue, de l'altitude ou une mauvaise circulation sanguine peuvent entrainer un etat physiologique hypoxique. La reponse cellulaire a une carence en oxygene est mediee principalement par la proteine HIF-1. Cette proteine est generalement absente dans des conditions normales d'oxygene mais elle est stabilisee lorsque la concentration en oxygene diminue. HIF-1 permet a la cellule et a l'organisme de s'adapter, a court ou long terme, a un manque d'oxygene. Ceci est possible grace a son role dans l'activation de nombreux genes specifiques. D'un point de vue pathologique, les tumeurs sont des environnements souvent hypoxiques ou la proteine HIF-1 est activee. Dans plusieurs cas, la presence de HIF-1 a l'interieur de tumeurs semblerait correler avec un mauvais pronostique. HIF-1 est implique dans la survie des cellules cancereuses, dans la progression tumorale et dans le developpement de metastases. Le cancer touche environ une personne sur trois, faisant de cette maladie une preoccupation essentielle. De meme, HIF-1 semblerait contribuer au developpement de plusieurs maladies cardiovasculaires, qui sont responsables du deces de plus de Canadiens que toute autre maladie. Ce projet vise a etudier les mecanismes d'activation et de regulation de la proteine HIF-1. La comprehension des mecanismes d'action de HIF-1 dans le contexte de ces maladies est importante pour l'acquisition de connaissances essentielles au developpement de therapie efficaces.

TitreApplicationTitle: Positional cloning of the Char10 malaria susceptibility locus
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOCHEMISTRY; EXPRESSION ANALYSIS (MICRO-ARRAY; FACS; GENETICS; MALARIA; MOUSE MODEL; PLASMODIUM CHABAUDI; POSITIONAL CLONING; QTL ANALYSIS; RT-PCR...); SEQUENCING
Abstract-Résumé: Malaria, caused by Plasmodium parasites, is the world's most important parasitic disease. Over 250 million clinical cases occur annually, with 1 million associated deaths mostly affecting children under five years of age. The majority of these cases take place in sub-Saharan Africa. However, malaria is present in over 100 countries. In these areas, the problem has been exacerbated by the emergence of widespread resistance to antimalarial drugs and by the absence of an efficacious vaccine; hence the important need for developing new therapeutic strategies. Several major gene effects have been characterized and are known to modulate susceptibility to malaria in humans. Our lab uses a mouse model of infection with P. chabaudi to mimic the blood stage of the disease, which is associated with clinical symptoms such as fever and anemia. Common inbred strains of mice show a marked inter-strain difference in susceptibility to P. chabaudi, which has formed the basis of several genetic studies to identify chromosomal regions controlling host-response. The aim of my project is to identify new genetic factors controlling susceptibility to malaria in mice. A cross between a susceptible and a resistant strain was generated in order to perform genetic mapping. Linkage analysis revealed the presence of a major region on central chromosome 9 that we designated Char10 and that is likely to be responsible for resistance to malaria. In order to reduce the size of the Char10 interval, congenic lines carrying smaller portions of the Char10 segment were created. Phenotyping of these lines demonstrated that the Char10 effect is likely found between 50-60Mb. Future experiments will allow us to further narrow the interval and ultimately find the causative gene. This genetic analysis will allow us to find new proteins and pathways responsible for the susceptibility to malaria infection and may therefore help us improve current antimalarial therapies by discovering new drug targets.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mast cells facilitate cardiac wound healing after a myocardial infarction (MI) by induction of epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) and proliferation of epicardial derived cells (EPDCs) and resident fibroblasts.
Keywords-MotsClés: INFLAMMATION; MAST CELLS; MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION; MYOFIBROBLASTS; PROLIFERATION
Abstract-Résumé: Following a heart attack (a myocardial infarction, MI), heart cells die and trigger a cascade of events that results in scar formation and  ultimately a dilated, dysfunctional heart. Many cells repair the heart including mast cells and fibroblasts. Mast cells reside in the heart and accumulate in the heart after injury. Fibroblasts are the predominant cellular contributors of fibrous skeleton of the heart. This skeleton prevents ventricular dilation and subsequent progressive heart failure. Maintaining the skeleton structure of the heart is essential to prevent heart failure and preserve the ability of patients to function normally. After an MI both mast cells and fibroblasts accumulate in the damaged heart. Mast cells release various mediators which facilitate tissue repair. Fibroblasts express contractile protein and exert tensile forces on the surrounding tissue to prevent scar expansion, heart dilation and heart failure.   The origins of fibroblasts in myocardial repair have not been fully investigated. These cells may arise from reproduction of cells resident in the heart or from the alteration of stem cells in the heart. However, the proposal we will test is that these cells may be derived from the outer covering of heart, or epicardium. Previous studies showed that a large number of mast cells present in the heart are localized at the epicardium. Also the accumulation of mast cells in the heart after an MI coincides with increase in the number of contracting fibroblasts.  My recent studies indicated that bone marrow derived mast cells improved the reproduction of cardiac fibroblasts as well as bone marrow stem cells. Based on these facts, we hypothesise that the release of proteins from the cardiac mast cell triggers the transformation of fibroblasts from the epicardium which then enhance cardiac repair. If these studies confirm our theory, then we may be able to develop a new therapy to prevent heart failure in patients who have suffered an extensive MI.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of integrin-linked kinase in TGFbeta-induced dermal wound repair
Keywords-MotsClés: DERMIS; FIBROBLASTS; INTEGRIN-LINKED KINASE; MYOFIBROBLAST DIFFERENTIATION; REGENERATIVE MEDICINE; TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR RECEPTOR; TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR-BETA; WOUND HEALING
Abstract-Résumé: Abnormal wound healing is a significant health care problem that can lead to disability and reduced quality of life, thereby, increasing the financial burden on our health care system. In the normal healing process, cells within the wound area called fibroblasts become activated by factors released during injury to develop into myofibroblasts, specialized cells that function to contract and close the wound. However, in some situations, the healing process is disrupted by excessive or insufficient release of factors, such as Transforming Growth Factor(TGF)-beta, leading to chronic wounds or fibrosis. A protein called integrin-linked kinase (ILK) has been shown to affect different aspects of wound healing depending on where it is found in the skin. This proposal will determine the role of ILK in the process of TGFbeta-induced myofibroblast development and wound contraction. The elucidation of the mechanism of ILK function in fibroblasts of the skin is a crticial step in understanding the process of wound closure and tissue regeneration after injury. Ultimately, this work will provide valuable insight for the development of better therapeutic interventions for wound repair.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effets des contraintes psychosociales au travail et des responsabilités familiales sur la tension artérielle (TA) ambulatoire et la santé mentale (SM) des femmes : une étude prospective de 5 ans menée auprès de cols blancs de la région de Québec.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYSES PAR MODELES D'EQUATIONS GENERALISES; CONTRAINTES PSYCHOSOCIALES AU TRAVAIL; DEVIS PROSPECTIF DE 5 ANS; MODELE DEMANDE-LATITUDE (KARASEK); MODELE DESEQUILIBRE EFFORTS-RECONNAISSANCE (SIEGRIST); QUESTIONNAIRE AUTO-ADMINISTRE; RESPONSABILITES FAMILIALES; SANTE DES FEMMES; SANTE MENTALE; TENSION ARTERIELLE AMBULATOIRE
Abstract-Résumé: A l'echelle mondiale, les maladies cardiovasculaires (MCV), souvent considerees comme un probleme "masculin", constituent la principale cause de deces chez les femmes. Pres d'une Canadienne sur cinq a une tension arterielle (TA) elevee; l'un des principaux facteurs de risque de MCV. Les problemes de sante mentale (SM) constituent un second enjeu populationel important en figurant parmi les principales causes d'absences pour maladie certifiee dans plusieurs pays industrialises. Ces absences sont plus longues et deux fois plus frequentes chez les femmes. De plus, au Canada, 28 pourcents des femmes qui occupent un emploi presentent des symptomes de detresse psychologique elevee (un indicateur de la SM) par rapport a 22,4 pourcents des hommes. Des evidences demontrent que certains stresseurs de l'environnement de travail peuvent contribuer a l'elevation de la TA ainsi qu'au developpement des problemes de SM. En plus d'avoir davantage tendance a etre exposees a ces stresseurs que les hommes, les femmes consacrent deux heures de plus par jour aux responsabilites familiales. La double exposition a ces stresseurs et a des responsabilites familiales elevees peut entrainer une surcharge et, consequemment, divers effets indesirables sur la sante. Les etudes anterieures portant sur les effets de cette double exposition sur la TA sont peu nombreuses et souffrent d'importantes limites methodologiques. Aucune etude anterieure n'a evalue les effets de cette double exposition sur la SM. Cette etude propose de determiner, sur une periode de 5 ans, les effets de la double exposition a des stresseurs de l'environnement de travail et a des responsabilites familiales elevees sur la TA et la SM des femmes. Les resultats de cette etude contribueront a la prevention primaire des MCV et des problemes de SM en accentuant l'importance de reduire les stresseurs de l'environnement de travail et de concilier le travail et les responsabilites familiales.

TitreApplicationTitle: Skin Self Examinations: The roles of coping and distress in reducing melanoma related mortality
Keywords-MotsClés: COPING; DISTRESS; HEALTH PSYCHOLOGY; MELANOMA; PREVENTION; PSYCHOSOCIAL ONCOLOGY; SKIN SELF EXAMINATION
Abstract-Résumé: Cutaneous melanoma (CM) is the fastest growing skin tumor and accounts for 90% of deaths caused by skin cancer. It is the second most common type of cancer in persons aged 15-29 and its incidence doubles every 10 years. While it is visible, recognizable and highly curable in early stages, CM becomes increasingly therapy-resistant and lethal in later stages. Survival mainly depends on the depth and spread of the melanoma. The majority of CMs are detected by patients themselves, and their close ones. Research thus far has shown that those who perform skin self examinations (SSE) present for treatment at an earlier disease phase, have 50% less advanced CM and a significantly lower CM related mortality. Despite the fact that CM is visible on the skin surface, systematic and regular SSE are performed by a minority of melanoma survivors; only 13%. These observations have prompted research efforts to determine what factors may affect SSE in order to develop a more effective preventive melanoma education program. Studies have shown that medical, demographic and psychosocial variables are associated with the performance of SSE. However, existing literature fails to examine key psychological variables such as distress and coping in relation to SSE. Since the predictors of SSE need to be identified and understood in order to design effective patient education programs, my research project will examine the link between distress and coping styles on SSE acquisition. Two-hundred melanoma patients from 2 McGill-affiliated hospitals will participate in this quantitative study. Augmenting our understanding of the psychosocial variables involved in adhering to SSE, will allow us to define key factors that facilitate compliance to general medical advice.  Ultimately, the development of preventative services that promote early detection of cancer through non-invasive, cost-effective methods will reduce melanoma-related mortality and further improve the health care system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude des mécanismes responsables des effets de la diète méditerranéenne, avec et sans perte de poids, chez des hommes souffrant du syndrome métabolique
Keywords-MotsClés: APOLIPOPROTEINES; DIETE MEDITERRANEENNE; HOMEOSTASIE DU CHOLESTEROL; MALADIES CARDIOVASCULAIRES; MARQUEURS INFLAMMATOIRES; METABOLISME DES LIPOPROTEINES; NUTRITION; OBESITE; PERTE DE POIDS; SYNDROME METABOLIQUE
Abstract-Résumé: Les maladies du cur sont une des premieres causes de deces au Canada. Plusieurs facteurs augmentent le risque de faire un infarctus, dont l'obesite. La perte de poids est donc l'intervention a privilegier chez les gens avec surpoids et a risque d'avoir une maladie du cur. Plusieurs travaux ont demontre l'efficacite de la diete mediterraneenne (DietMed) a reduire les risques de maladies du cur en facilitant la perte de poids, mais aussi en ameliorant la sante du cur par une baisse du taux de cholesterol sanguin (mauvais cholesterol) et de la tension arterielle. La DietMed est riche en produits cerealiers a grains entiers, fruits, legumes, legumineuses, noix et graines, poisson et huile d'olive; elle est donc consideree comme une diete tres sante. Toutefois, bien que la DietMed soit reconnue comme benefique pour la sante du cur, tres peu d'informations sont disponibles sur les mecanismes responsables de ces effets, particulierement en absence de perte de poids. Le projet de recherche propose vise donc a comprendre comment la DietMed agit dans l'organisme afin d'etre en mesure de fournir des recommandations nutritionnelles aux patients a risque de maladies du cur. En effet, l'amelioration des methodes de prevention et de traitement des maladies du cur repose principalement sur la comprehension des changements dans l'organisme qui surviennent suivant ces traitements (ex : DietMed). Les retombees de ce projet pour la sante des populations sont donc tres importantes, car elles fourniront aux professionnels de la sante des arguments plus convaincants pour aider leurs patients a risque de maladies du cur a adherer aux principes de la DietMed, et ce, sans avoir a mettre l'emphase uniquement sur la perte de poids. Cette approche alternative representerait alors un objectif plus facile a atteindre par les patients que la perte de poids.

TitreApplicationTitle: Fecal transplantation for the treatment of recurrent Clostridium difficile infection: a randomized controlled trial
Keywords-MotsClés: 16S RRNA SEQUENCING; CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE INFECTION; FECAL TRANSPLANTATION; INTESTINAL MICROBIOTA; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: Clostridium difficile infection (CDI) is the most important cause of hospital-acquired diarrhea. In the majority of patients, CDI resolves after initial antimicrobial treatment. However, recurrent CDI can occur in as many as 35 percent of these patients. Recurrences are associated with the persistence of a compromised intestinal flora. Fecal transplantation, which consists of infusing feces from a healthy donor into a patient's gastrointestinal tract, has recently been described as an effective alternative for the treatment of recurrent CDI. The procedure is thought to restore a normal, functional intestinal flora. However, it has not been widely implemented. We propose to conduct a randomized controlled trial (RCT) of fecal transplantation in patients with relapsing CDI. The objectives of this study are to (i) test the effectiveness of fecal transplantation in relapsing CDI patients, and (ii) describe changes in the composition of the intestinal flora following transplantation. The effectiveness of fecal transplantation (n=55 patients) will be compared to the standard antimicrobial therapy for recurrent CDI (n=55 patients). Stool specimens will be collected from each patient at multiple time-points before and after transplantation. These specimens will be subjected to 16S ribosomal RNA-based sequencing in order to examine the composition of the patients' intestinal flora. This RCT will rigorously test, for the first time, the effectiveness and safety of a defined fecal transplantation procedure for the treatment of recurrent CDI. The implementation of a proven protocol will dramatically improve the quality of life of the patients and will result in significant medical cost savings. The study will also provide important new insight into the mechanism of normal intestinal flora restoration and CDI resolution. Although speculative, diseases such as irritable bowel syndrome and obesity may be amenable to similar therapeutic approaches.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigating Mechanisms of Change in Motivational Interviewing: Reducing Resistance and Improving Treatment Outcomes in Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY DISORDERS; COGNITIVE BEHAVIOURAL THERAPY; MECHANISMS OF CHANGE IN TREATMENT; MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING; PSYCHOTHERAPY; RESISTANCE TO CHANGE
Abstract-Résumé: Although empirical investigations strongly support the use of Motivational Interviewing (MI) as a prelude to further treatment, the underlying mechanisms of MI that lead to change remain to be clarified. In a recent randomized controlled trial, Westra et al. (2009) demonstrated that adding MI pretreatment to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), compared to CBT without a pretreatment, was substantially and specifically helpful in reducing worry for patients with high symptom severity. Patient resistance to treatment was found to directly mediate the relationship between getting MI pretreatment or not and outcome. The findings suggest that patient resistance can be used as an outcome measure for the efficacy of MI, opening up new possibilities to examine MI mechanisms. Although studies have demonstrated that patient resistance is a critical predictor of treatment outcome, this central component of MI is currently understudied. The present study addresses this important gap by empirically investigating mechanisms through which MI leads to reduced resistance and better outcomes. The Motivational Interviewing Skill Code (Miller et al., 2003) will be used to code videotaped sessions of MI for patients who received MI prior to CBT in the Westra et al. trial. Therapists will be rated on dimensions of MI-consistent techniques and interpersonal skill, and patient responses will be rated for talk for or against change, to examine the extent to which hypothesized mechanisms of change in MI are predictive of patient resistance in subsequent therapy. The present study has very important implications for understanding specific mechanisms of change in MI, which can explain how the addition of MI to CBT might be effective in enhancing patient response to subsequent treatment. Such knowledge can enhance clinical care by suggesting methods for managing resistance and improving treatment outcomes for patients with high symptom severity GAD.

TitreApplicationTitle: Intégration des mesures intermédiaires de survie dans les évaluations économiques en cancer du sein métastatique
Keywords-MotsClés: ADHESION AUX MEDICAMENTS; ANALYSE DE BANQUES DE DONNEES ADMINISTRATIVES; ANALYSE DE SURVIE; CANCER DU SEIN; MODELISATION; PHARMACOECONOMIE; PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGIE; TESTS PHARAMCOGENOMIQUES; TRAITEMENTS ANTICANCEREUX
Abstract-Résumé: Compte tenu du lourd fardeau economique et clinique du cancer au Canada, les instances gouvernementales responsables du remboursement des medicaments doivent se doter de meilleurs outils d'aide a la decision afin de faciliter l'evaluation de la valeur therapeutique des nouveaux agents anticancereux. De nos jours, il est de plus en plus courant de recourir a des mesures intermediaires d'efficacite au lieu d'une mesure finale afin d'estimer l'efficacite d'un nouvel agent anticancereux. Ainsi, les evaluations economiques de ces traitements reposent souvent sur le rapport entre le cout et une mesure intermediaire d'efficacite telle que la survie sans progression. Par contre, l'absence de resultats cliniques finaux comme la survie globale complexifie la prise de decision, puisque d'un point de vue cout efficacite, il peut etre difficile d'etablir la valeur d'une annee de vie sans progression. A cet effet, l'objectif principal de ce projet de recherche consiste a etablir une relation entre la survie sans progression et la survie globale chez les femmes atteintes d'un cancer du sein metastatique, ce qui permettra de predire la survie globale resultant d'une estimation de survie sans progression. Plus specifiquement, les objectifs de ce projet sont, d'une part, d'etablir une relation entre la survie globale et la survie sans progression et d'identifier les facteurs determinants d'une relation significative et, d'autre part, de developper un modele fournissant une estimation de la survie globale plus pres de la realite en tenant compte, entre autres, de l'observance aux traitements. Bref, ce projet permettra d'introduire les donnees de survie sans progression dans les evaluations economiques en oncologie et de realiser des evaluations economiques plus facilement interpretables. Ce projet contribuera donc concretement a la prise de decision et aura un impact significatif sur l'acces aux nouveaux traitements anticancereux pour les Canadiens.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health Literacy and Women's Understanding of Breast Cancer Representations in Canadian and U.S. Media
Keywords-MotsClés: AESTHETICS AND WELL-BEING; BREAST CANCER; HEALTH COMMUNICATION; HEALTH LITERACY; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MEDIA ANALYSIS AND IMPACT; MIXED-METHODS; PSYCHOSOCIAL ONCOLOGY; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; WOMEN'S HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer among Canadian women: one in nine will develop breast cancer in their lifetime and two-thirds will survive. The popular media, especially magazines, are an important source of information for women about risks and treatments related to breast cancer, and media reports are often accompanied by visual images. When linked with text, visual images can affect attention, recall, and understanding of health information. Media images impact women's attitudes, beliefs, and behaviours. Health literacy is the ability to find, process, understand, and act on health information. Images may have an especially important role for women with low health literacy. Accordingly, the nature of breast cancer information and images in the media, how these images affect women's expectations, understanding, and health choices related to the disease, and how health literacy shapes this understanding, is planned as a two part doctoral research study. Part One will involve a rigorous content analysis of breast cancer coverage in the ten highest circulation French- and English Canadian women's and fashion magazines, and five similar US magazines (with the largest Canadian readership), over the most recent 10 year period. Part two will consist of interviews and focus groups to learn how such images affect women -- with different levels of health literacy -- about their understandings, expectations, and experience of the disease, and its impact on many important aspects of their lives. Findings will be submitted to journals and conferences and distributed to the media, magazine editors, and breast cancer organizations. This research will inform women's health by focusing on how best to use mass media to help women become more knowledgeable in their decision-making about breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigating Stress and Coping Mechanisms in a Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) population recruited from a longitudinal Epidemiological Catchment Area study
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL RESEARCH; EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CATCHMENT AREA; EPIDEMIOLOGY; MENTAL HEALTH; POSTTRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER (PTSD); STRESS AND COPING; TRAUMA
Abstract-Résumé: PTSD is a chronic condition that has become a global health concern. Though it affects about 9.2% of Canadians, there is very little current Canadian data on PTSD. PTSD is notoriously difficult to treat and its persistence has been related in part to poor coping strategies.There is virtually no literature looking at the daily stressors and coping strategies used by PTSD patients who fail to remit compared to those who remit.  This is a longitudinal study to investigate the nature of daily stressors and coping mechanisms in a random sample of 2,433 of individuals taken from a large Epidemiological Catchment Area (ECA) study. Additionally, the candidate will use her previous training in qualitative research to further explore daily stress and coping methods from the subjective perspective of individuals with current or past PTSD. We hypothesize that at wave 2, wave 1 participants with PTSD who use less avoidant emotional coping strategies will improve more (ie. have less PTSD symptoms) than those who are more prone to avoidant emotional coping. Additionally, qualitative content analysis from in-depth interviews will provide a clearer descriptive summary of the latent content of participants' views surrounding coping strategies.   Trauma exposure, and PTSD diagnosis will be assessed with use the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS 1.2): Military Supplemen7. The CCHS 1.2: Stress and Coping Section will evaluate sources and frequency of stress, along with stress management abilities. Qualitative data will be collected using semi-structured interviews examining experiences related to stress and coping from the perspectives of the individuals.   Successful completion of the proposed research will provide much needed Canadian based psychiatric epidemiological data. It also has the potential to suggest innovative and feasible strategies to improve current methods of PTSD treatment avenues thus leading to improved quality of life for those burdened by PTSD.

TitreApplicationTitle: Choice or circumstance? An exploration of breastfeeding practice among obese, low income, food insecure Nova Scotian mothers
Keywords-MotsClés: BREASTFEEDING; EXPLORATORY; FOOD INSECURITY; HEALTH SERVICE DELIVERY; INFANTS; OBESITY; POPULATION HEALTH; QUALITATIVE; SOCIOECONOMIC; WOMEN
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity is a major public health concern and improving breastfeeding behaviour is a recommended strategy to support obesity prevention in the population. Low breastfeeding rates are of concern in Nova Scotia, particularly among mothers from nutritionally vulnerable (food insecure) households. High poverty may partially account for Nova Scotia's low breastfeeding rates but maternal obesity (a possible issue among food insecure mothers) is on the rise in Nova Scotia and being obese can also affect one's ability to successfully breastfeed. We know little about the experience of breastfeeding from the perspectives of obese women and more specifically, obese women who are also low income and food insecure. By exploring breastfeeding practice among women sharing these multiple realities, this research will fill a critical void in our understanding of how we might improve breastfeeding in this demographic. This research aligns with both national and regional research priorities on obesity and the social determinants of health, as well as supporting Canada's recent reaffirmation of improving maternal and child health across the globe - of which improving (exclusive) breastfeeding behaviour among all mothers is a priority.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Relation of Childhood Maltreatment to Stress Sensitization in First Onset and Recurrent Major Depression: An Examination of Depression History, Age, and Maltreatment Characteristics
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENT AND ADULT DEPRESSION; CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT; CONTEXTUAL INTERVIEWS; DEPRESSION ETIOLOGY; GOLD-STANDARD; RISK FACTORS; STRESS PROCESSES; STRESSFUL LIFE EVENTS; VULNERABILITIES
Abstract-Résumé: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a recurrent and impairing condition that affects approximately 1.25 million Canadians each year. Because of this, research aimed at understanding factors that cause and maintain depression is extremely important. Stress is a potent risk factor that has been implicated in the onset of MDD. Further, the role stress plays in triggering depression changes over the course of the disorder. The stress sensitization hypothesis suggests that severe stressors (e.g., spouse dies from cancer) are important for triggering the first episode; however, as the disorder progresses, minor stressors (e.g., argument with a friend) become more capable of eliciting a recurrence. Additionally, it has been demonstrated that a history of childhood maltreatment increases vulnerability to stress even prior to the very first depressive episode.  The proposed study will examine the relation of maltreatment to stress sensitization in a way that will potentially impact the ability to recognize individuals vulnerable to stress and depression, and inform prevention, early intervention, and treatment planning. Specifically, this study will investigate whether the role of maltreatment in stress sensitization is dependent on several factors. These factors include depression history (first onset vs. recurrent), age (adolescence vs. adulthood), and specific characteristics of maltreatment including the type (physical vs. sexual vs. emotional abuse) and timing (maltreatment perpetrated in childhood vs. adolescence). Results from these objectives will help clarify the role of maltreatment in the initial etiology and ongoing pathology of depression across different developmental periods. This knowledge will help inform more effective treatments that target distal and proximal risk factors most strongly implicated in MDD. Further, it will help guide clinicians in allocating treatment resources to those most vulnerable to depression in the face of stress.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving Outcomes in First Episode Psychosis: the Role of Genetic Variation of NPAS3
Keywords-MotsClés: ASSESSMENT OF TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR FUNCTION; CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT; MOLECULAR ANALYSIS OF GENE REGULATION; MRI ANALYSIS; NEURODEVELOPMENT; PSYCHIATRIC GENETICS
Abstract-Résumé: Schizophrenia (SZ) is a complex psychiatric disorder with an incidence of 1% worldwide. SZ has a strong genetic component. Symptoms of SZ include hallucinations, delusions, impaired emotional processing and disorganization of thought and speech. To date no single "SZ gene" has been identified; rather, multiple genes have been implicated in SZ, but not all of these genes are altered in all SZ patients. It is important to identify the specific effects of each candidate gene in the pathology of the overall disease. NPAS3 was identified as a SZ candidate gene in a family where a chromosomal rearrangement lead to a break in the NPAS3 gene only found in individuals with SZ. NPAS3 variants have also been identified in multiple association studies of SZ. NPAS3 encodes a transcription factor expressed in the developing mouse central nervous system and neuronal stem cells of the hippocampus of adult mouse brains. These cells are important in social learning and memory, both found to be deficient in SZ patients. Our team is working with a normal population of high school students to determine the effects of known SZ-associated variants of NPAS3 which, when independent of other SZ variants in other genes, don't cause disease (known as an endophenotype). Recruited students undergo genetic analysis, tests of cognition and MRI analysis of brain structure. We will also undertake molecular analysis of NPAS3 to determine its molecular functions. We will determine its localization in the cell, its stability, and the genes regulated by NPAS3. Variant forms of NPAS3 will be analyzed to determine how their function varies compared with normal NPAS3 to possibly explain the cognitive and structural endophenotypes observed in the normal high school student population. Through our studies we will identify the specific role that variant NPAS3 plays in development and onset of SZ. This will allow streamlining of therapies allowing more targeted therapy for individuals who carry NPAS3 variants.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigation of the Salmonella enterica SsrA sensor kinase activation mechanism and stimulus identity.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTI-VIRULENCE; BIOINFORMATICS; GENETICS; HOST-PATHOGEN; PROTEIN CHARACTERIZATION; SALMONELLA; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Salmonella enterica is a major cause of food borne gastroenteritis in Canada and abroad leading to significant health care costs and patient morbidity.  Abroad, host adapted serovars of S. enterica cause millions of cases of the systemic illnesses, typhoid and paratyphoid fever, each year.  While largely eradicated in Canada due to water sanitation programs, serious cases are identified and treated in Canada due to international travel each year.  Due to the rise of antimicrobial resistant strains of S. enterica, at home and abroad, typhoidal strains may re-emerge in North America.  Recent work has focused on understanding the mechanisms of bacterial virulence in order to develop anti-virulence drugs as an alternative to antimicrobial treatment.  This research proposes to identify and understand the signal detected within host cells by S. enterica which allows it to proliferate leading to an often fatal systemic infection.  Application of this project's findings may lead to the development of anti-virulence drugs for the treatment of typhoid and paratyphoid fever as well as a more general understanding of the signal encountered during infection by S. enterica and other bacteria that possess a similar detection system used during infection of humans and animals.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude du rôle pharmacologique et toxicologique des nouvelles formes d'épissage de la voie du métabolisme des médicaments UGT1A
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CULTURE CELLULAIRE; ENZYMES MEMBRANAIRES; ENZYMES UDP-GLUCURONOSYLTRANSERASES; INTERACTIONS PROTEINES-PROTEINES; METABOLISME DES MEDICAMENTS; REGULATION DOMINANT-NEGATIF; EPISSAGE ALTERNATIF
Abstract-Résumé: Le metabolisme des medicaments ainsi que l'elimination de composes nefastes pour le corps est pris en charge par plusieurs voies dont celle de la glucuronidation qui elimine ces composes. Cette voie est mediee par une famille de proteines nommees UDP-glucuronosyltransferases (UGT) qui sont egalement impliquees dans l'inactivation de molecules endogenes, telles que les hormones. Mon projet de doctorat porte sur l'etude d'un nouveau mecanisme de regulation de cette voie metabolique faisant intervenir des evenements d'epissage alternatif. Les produits de l'epissage alternatif permettent d'augmenter la diversite des proteines et contribueraient possiblement a la variabilite du metabolisme entre les individus. Ce dernier phenomene est important puisqu'il peut entrainer une reponse variable aux medicaments en termes d'efficacite et d'effets indesirables. Dans le cas des UGT, nos observations suggerent que les formes d'epissage modulent de facon negative l'activite et le metabolisme cellulaire. Ainsi, en utilisant divers modeles de cellules humaines, je tenterai de determiner si ce processus influence la reponse aux medicaments et aux effets de carcinogenes auxquels nous sommes exposes.

Abstract-Résumé: Computers, mobile phones and recently smartphones (e.g., Blackberry, iPhone) have become mainstream in our daily lives. Smartphones, with multiple capabilities including the ability to run applications, or apps, have become especially popular. The popularity and full-day access of smartphones and their apps offers an exciting opportunity to develop and test state-of-the-art approaches to track dietary intake and support positive dietary change. This is especially needed at a time when poor nutrition (e.g., excess caloric intakes leading to obesity) is responsible for a high incidence of preventable chronic diseases (e.g., heart disease and diabetes) in Canadians. Research in this area is novel, timely and crucial for the public, dietitians, government, and industry as it is important to ensure that nutrition apps are safe (as no regulations currently exist), understandable and effective.  This study will examine the readability, reliability, and currency of newly available smartphone nutrition apps from app stores aimed at the general public. Following this, consumer research will be conducted to better understand user experiences with current nutrition apps. This will be investigated through interviews with individuals who have used newly available nutrition apps, and designing and implementing a survey for current users of a national web based food and exercise tracking system. These results will be used to design a nutrition app for consumers followed by pre-testing and pilot testing. This new app will then be implemented amongst a large group of current smartphone users to test behavior change. Feedback on application usability and satisfaction will be obtained using surveys and interviews. This research will help to ensure better quality assurance of nutritional apps, will inform dietitians of new treatment options to use in their practice and will provide Canadians with an easy to use and accessible tool to help them make better nutrition choices.

TitreApplicationTitle: "Placing" HIV Risk and Prevention among Men in Nova Scotia: An Intersectional Determinants of Health Approach
Keywords-MotsClés: ETHNOGRAPHY; GENDER; HIV/AIDS RISK AND PREVENTION; NOVA SCOTIA; PLACE; POPULATION HEALTH; QUALITATIVE METHODOLOGIES; REGIONAL HIV/AIDS STRATEGIES; SEXUALITY; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: This project integrates health geography and health promotion approaches to examine the ways in which local context in Nova Scotia informs the ways in which men (including men who have sex with men) encounter HIV risk and respond to prevention strategies. The study hypothesizes that place-mediated determinants of health such as social support networks, social environments, gender, and sexuality influence: (1) constructions of maleness and masculinity, (2) related risk factors for HIV, (3) non-normative health-seeking behaviors such as HIV counseling and testing and (4) the effectiveness of HIV prevention strategies traditionally geared toward men in metropolitan areas. Nova Scotia, with a varied social and political landscape that differs from more commonly studied provinces, is an ideal location to explore how place factors (e.g., urban/rural cultural differences and access issues, variations in support for non-mainstream sexualities and uptake of health services) influence HIV risk and prevention among men. This project employs an exploratory, qualitative methodology consisting of in-depth interviews with individual men (HIV-positive and -negative) and sexual health/mental health workers in the nine Nova Scotia district health authorities tasked with meeting the complex sexual, mental, and physical health needs of the diverse populations of men across the province. This study will also examine how the ways in which gender is constructed across places and sexual contexts (e.g., having unprotected sex or opting out of testing as "masculine" behaviors) contribute to HIV risk and, conversely, inform the uptake of prevention messaging. This research will provide a more sophisticated understanding of how key determinants of health, including place, gender, and sexuality, shape HIV risk. It will also inform recommendations for how to integrate these factors into the provincial HIV strategy, resulting in a more nuanced approach to HIV prevention among men in Nova Scotia.

TitreApplicationTitle: An examination of the social and structural production of violence and HIV risk among youth and women who use illicit drugs in two Vancouver drug scenes.
Keywords-MotsClés: DRUG USE; ETHNOGRAPHY; GENDER; HIV; POPULATION HEALTH; VIOLENCE; WOMEN; YOUTH
Abstract-Résumé: People who inject drugs continue to experience some of the highest rates of violence and among the worst health outcomes in Canada and internationally. Research has demonstrated that women and young people experience violence and engage in HIV risk behaviours in unique ways. Therefore it is important to examine how social and structural factors affect youth and women who use illicit drugs to better inform the development of tailored interventions addressing violence and HIV infection.   The objective of my proposal is to inform policy and programming to improve the health of drug users in Canada, particularly women and youth. I will examine structural features of health programmes and services for youth, including age limits on HIV prevention supplies and abstinence-based policies in health and housing services, and how these features affect exposure to violence and associated HIV risk. Second, I will examine the role of social networks and supports including friends, partners and family on the production of violence and HIV-related risks. I will conduct a nine-month critical ethnography and conduct in-depth interviews with street youth and adults who inject drugs and local service providers. The findings will contribute to developing knowledge and strategies to reduce the violence and harms young people and women who use drugs face.

TitreApplicationTitle: Access, acceptance and adherence to drug therapy: Modeling complex dynamic systems for Aboriginal persons living with HIV/AIDS
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; BEHAVIOURAL SCIENCE; COMPLEX SOCIAL SYSTEMS; DRUG THERAPY; HIV/AIDS; MIXED METHODS (QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE); PARTICIPATORY ACTION RESEARCH; PUBLIC HEALTH; SYSTEM DYNAMICS MODEL; SYSTEMS SCIENCE
Abstract-Résumé: A disproportionate number of Aboriginal persons in Canada are infected with HIV. Aboriginal persons living with HIV/AIDS (APLWHA) are less likely than non-APLWHA to access and adhere to HIV drug therapy. However, the evidence to date has aimed for generalization and not focused enough on contextual factors. Furthermore, research on HIV drug therapy remains largely siloed in its approach to generating knowledge, not fully taking advantage of interdisciplinary understanding despite the fact that HIV drug treatment access, acceptance and adherence occurs within a context beyond the disease itself and involves structural (e.g., social, cultural), behavioural as well as biomedical (e.g., drug effectiveness, drug side-effects) issues that intersect, creating a complex environment. Moreover, no studies have been conducted examining the combined effect of these factors on HIV drug therapy specific to APLWHA. The objective of my research is to explore and explain factors affecting HIV drug therapy among APLWHA by modeling this complex system. My research question is: What is the relationship between personal, interpersonal, and structural factors and APLWHA health outcomes? I will use a systems science framework incorporating a participatory action research design. My study population will include APLWHA, service providers, and other key informants in one Canadian province. I will collect data using interviews and surveys to create a model, analyze that data using thematic analysis and statistics, and then interpret the study results. The aim of my study is to create new knowledge that can be applied by interested parties to develop effective health systems, services and policies to support APLWHA within the context of HIV drug therapy. Finally, my proposed research has implications for fostering multi-stakeholder engagement and collaboration to ensure a comprehensive approach to addressing HIV drug therapy access, acceptance and adherence among APLWHA.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dissemination of clinical practice guidelines to patients: a mixed method approach to explore barriers, facilitators and strategies
Keywords-MotsClés: BARRIERS; CLINICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES; DISSEMINATION; FACILITATORS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PATIENTS
Abstract-Résumé: Clinical practice guidelines are being produced to help guide health care providers to provide the appropriate care for their patients. These guidelines could also provide important information to patients who make their own decisions about their health.  Many guideline organisations are starting to provide this information to patients but there is little research about how to do this.  For example, we do not know what patients think about guidelines, such as their attitudes and beliefs; how patients would perceive the guidelines; or whether patient groups or other organisations could improve how the information is distributed.   This research will explore these issues by reviewing the current research, and by interviewing and surveying patients, patient groups and guideline developers.  The results of this research will help inform strategies to distribute guidelines to patients to help patients make informed decisions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Hormonal and Mechanistic Evaluation of Increasing risk of diabetes and Cardiovascular Disease in India: from Bench to Bedside.
Keywords-MotsClés: ADIPOKINES; ADIPOSE TISSUE; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; INSULIN RESISTANCE; SUBCUTANEOUS; VISCERAL
Abstract-Résumé: Non-infectious diseases such as diabetes and cardiovascular disorders are increasing in incidence in lower and middle income countries such as India. It has also been observed that Asians have higher risk for the development of these diseases as compared to other population groups and the risk is observed to be even higher in immigrants to countries such as Canada. This has been attributed to a number of factors such as changes in diet/lifestyle, genetic factors etc. Although a number of factors are under scrutiny, no reliable associations have been found as yet. Some of the suggested criteria for risk evaluation have been the measurement of body surface area, waist-to-hip ratio, levels of cholesterol in the blood and the distribution of body fat, etc. Along with these, some hormones produced by fat tissue, such as; leptin, adiponectin and ASP, which influence fat metabolism, are also under investigation. The proposed study has been designed so that different attributes, which may be responsible for the above mentioned phenomena, may be studied in both the immigrant (to Canada) and native (to India) populations and compared with the native population (of Canada). It will evaluate a panel of markers which will give us a better insight into cause and effect relationships, assist in identifying better predictive factors as well as targets for intervention.
