ClasseRechercheFR: METABOLISME ET NUTRITION; MALADIES DU FOIE
TitreApplicationTitle: Transcriptional Regulation of the Metabolic Syndrome
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMARKER; FATTY LIVER DISEASE; INFLAMMATION; INSULIN RESISTANCE; METABOLISM; MITOCHONDRIA; OBESITY; PGC-1ALPHA; REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES; TRANSCRIPTION
Abstract-Résumé: Fatty liver disease affects one third of the population of North America.  The disease has few symptoms, but over time leads to irreversible damage to the liver.  Having a fatty liver not only increases your chance of liver failure, but also of developing other disease such as diabetes and heart problems.  The cause of the disease is unknown, but being overweight dramatically increases the likelihood of being afflicted.  Diets high in fat and sugar and low physical activity both contribute to the rising number of cases, particularly in children. Patients with fatty liver disease will likely face significant health problems in the future if not treated early on.  There is no cure for the disease and diagnosis is difficult, mainly because we do not understand what triggers it.  We have shown that low levels of a protein called PGC-1alpha in the liver may cause or worsen fatty liver disease and our new studies will help to understand how this happens. Identifying the cause of fatty liver disease will help to discover ways to diagnosis patients early and to design more effective treatments.

ClasseRechercheFR: TROUBLES DE SOMMEIL; MALADIE DE PARKINSON
TitreApplicationTitle: Diagnostic, pathophysiologie et traitement du trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal
Keywords-MotsClés: EEG QUANTIFIEE; IMAGERIE PAR RESONANCE MAGNETIQUE; MALADIES NEURODEGENERATIVES; NEUROPSYCHOLOGIE; POLYSOMNOGRAPHIE; SPECT; TROUBLES COGNITIFS; TROUBLES DU SOMMEIL
Abstract-Résumé: Le trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal est une maladie qui se manifeste par des comportements indesirables souvent violents au cours du sommeil. Ces episodes sont etroitement associes aux periodes de reve, ils perturbent le sommeil et peuvent entrainer des blessures graves au sujet ou a son partenaire de lit. Le trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal touche 1% de la population generale et apparait generalement chez l'homme apres l'age de 50 ans. Nous avons observe qu'un grand nombre de patients atteints d'un trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal developpaient apres quelques annees une maladie degenerative comme la maladie de Parkinson. On a de plus observe chez la moitie de ces sujets la presence de marqueurs precoces de la maladie de Parkinson. Le but du present programme de recherche est d'entreprendre le suivi de ces patients pendant 5 ans afin de definir le profil evolutif de la maladie et d'identifier les sujets a risque de developper une maladie de Parkinson. Un deuxieme objectif est d'identifier les regions du cerveau impliquees dans la maladie. Cette recherche ouvrira la porte a de nouvelles approches therapeutiques dans le but non seulement de diminuer les comportements anormaux au cours du sommeil mais surtout de prevenir ou de retarder l'apparition de maladies neurologiques plus graves comme la maladie de Parkinson.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Genetics of the DNA damage response
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The genetic blueprint of every cell is contained in nuclear DNA. This blueprint is constantly read to ensure the functioning of the cell and of organs. It is therefore understandable that cells protect its DNA at all costs. A failure to repair damage in DNA leads to cell death or pathologies such as cancer. The overarching goal of this research proposal is to elucidate the responses to DNA damage. In particular, we propose to decipher how cells communicate the presence of DNA lesions. This process is also a paradigm to understand how cells communicate in general.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Protein (de)phosphorylation, the addition/removal of a phosphate group by kinases/phosphatases is fundamental in controlling cellular functions:  a switch to turn on/off a proteins activity. Recently, protein phosphorylation was discovered to exist in bacteria.  We determined the first structure of a bacterial tyrosine kinase, Etk, which is involved in cell surface protection.  We also solved the structure of AceK, a unique bacterial enzyme containing both kinase and phosphatase activities, which enables growth in nutrient-deficient environments. We aim to gain insights into bacterial phosphorylation which may provide novel strategies for antibiotic development, preventing water- and food-borne bacterial contamination, and eco-friendly industrial applications.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Integrative Cancer Informatics
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Igor Jurisica is a world-leading expert in informatics and cancer.  This program will create tools and resources for systematically discovering clinically-relevant biomarkers of cancer. Prognostic, predictive and early disease detection biomarkers will be identified and characterized for lung, ovarian, pancreatic, head & neck, prostate, breast and kidney cancer and for melanoma and leukemia. These cancers represent a particularly grave health threat, and, through Dr. Jurisica's innovative drive, extensive network of collaborations and industry connections, represent high potential for effective follow-though and translation to improve patient care.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Molecular Cardiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: After birth cardiac cells lose their ability to actively divide. Death of cardiac cells through apoptotic or necrotic processes following heart-attack has been postulated to be an underlying cause of ventricular remodelling and heart failure. Heart failure represents a major financial and socio-economic burden to Canada, since patients diagnosed with this form of heart disease require costly medical treatments and long-term care. This research will uniquely identify the cellular pathways and signaling molecules involved in the cell death processes with the longterm objective of discovering new innovative strategies to suppress cell death and improve the lives of patients with heart failure.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Evidence Based Emergency Medicine and Health Outcomes
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The majority of Canadians seek care in a hospital emergency department (ED) at some point in their lives; it is the primary portal of entry into the health care system for many people. This is especially the case for certain chronic respiratory (e.g., asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), cardiac (e.g., heart failure, atrial fibrillation), and neurological (e.g., migraine headaches) health conditions where exacerbations often result in ED presentations. There has been limited attention paid to the epidemiology, practice variation, evidence-based care, and health outcomes for patients with acute presentations. Since ED management decisions have a profound impact on patients return to health and future relapses, patient-oriented research in this setting is urgently needed.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Breast Cancer Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: The key objectives of the proposed research program are: (1) to conduct clinical trials to determine the optimal approach to radiation therapy for women with breast cancer; (2) to conduct translational research to help individualize treatment for women with breast cancer; and (3) to evaluate new technologies in radiation therapy. The new knowledge gained from this research will benefit patients, clinicians, and the cancer care system.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Before undertaking massive randomized trials of interventions for prevention of Alzheimers disease (AD) dementia, we need preliminary data to improve the probability that these costly and lengthy trials will succeed.  Because AD brain degeneration begins decades before symptoms appear, we will investigate the evolution of pre-symptomatic AD using several biochemical and neuroimaging markers of the disease process.  Applying these techniques in a new volunteer cohort, we will 1) quantitate the evolution of pre-symptomatic AD, and 2) conduct brief pilot trials to discover which regimens may halt its progression, while 3) investigating in the laboratory how and why they do this.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Toxicology and Environmental Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pollution and protection of the environment
Abstract-Résumé: The main theme of my research program is to study the toxicology of chemical contaminants found in the various ecosystems in Canada, particularly the Arctic. We will develop innovative approaches to improve the preventative, diagnostic, and prognostic aspects of ecosystem management, and to contribute to the understanding of relationships between ecosystem health and human health. Our research will help to develop a framework for assessing the potential health risks for wildlife species and the peoples in the Arctic and other Aboriginal communities and to improve the environmental health of Canadians everywhere.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Cardiovascular Clinical Trials
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Over 50,000 Canadians die suddenly each year, mostly from rapid heart rhythms. Heart attack survivors are at particular risk. An implantable defibrillator (modified pacemaker) effectively treats sudden death, but is expensive and cannot be practically applied to all of those at risk. In the REFINE study we found that a simple, practical combination of tests readily identify heart attack survivors at risk for sudden death. This is a major step forward, but solid proof is required before recommending the routine use of this expensive technology in this group of patients. The REFINE ICD trial will definitively determine if implantable defibrillator therapy will prevent death after a heart attack. This International clinical trial will alter how these patients are treated and has the potential to save thousands of lives each year. Other goals of this project are to further improve our understanding of the mechanisms of sudden death, to enhance collaborations with other researchers and to train students and highly qualified personnel in clinical trial research methods.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Myelin Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex disease for which the cause is unknown. In MS, the myelin sheath, which insulates nerve fibers, is actively degraded because the body's immune system attacks it and prevents its repair. An essential structural component of myelin, called myelin basic protein, may be the key to understanding the molecular events of MS. As the brain develops, this protein undergoes numerous modifications that affect how myelin is structured. During MS, the protein changes in other ways that cause myelin to degenerate. Toxic amino acid homologues found in low amounts in the Western diet can cause myelin to become unstable and thus vulnerable to other triggers, potentially enabling MS to arise. Our research studies the intricacies of MBP within the central nervous system, to understand how it works and how neurodegenerative diseases progress.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: RNA viruses and host interactions
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: RNA viruses cause the vast majority of viral diseases in humans. For instance, more people died as a result of the 1918 influenza pandemic than in World War 1. While vaccines have reduced the impact of pathogens such as influenza virus, many important viruses such as dengue, hepatitis c virus and related viruses have left billions of people at risk due to lack of vaccines/therapeutic treatments. Our research is focused upon understanding how RNA viruses interact with human cells. In doing so, we hope to understand the nature of viral diseases as well as identify new targets for anti-viral therapy.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Medical Genomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: This research proposal has the objective of creating a new research programme that will use the most recent advances in DNA sequencing, bioinformatics and other techniques to understand the genetic causes of human diseases such as cancer, asthma and heart disease. This understanding will be used to formulate new approaches to diagnose and treat disease. The proposed programme is unique in its scope in Canada.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Applied Molecular and Mitochondrial Medicine
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: This program will study how metabolism and mitochondria (the organells within the cells that produce energy) are involved in the cause of cancer and pulmonary hypertension (high blood pressure in the blood vessels of the lung).  These two diseases share common features since the cells in the wall of the lung blood vessels in pulmonary hypertension, grow like cancer cells until they occlude the lumen of the vessels.  In addition to work in animals this program will also perform studies to test these experimental therapies on human beings, for the first time.  In addition to potential new treatments for these devastating diseases, this work will support a training program to teach scientists and doctors how to study the mitochondria and also how to move their findings from the laboratory to the clinic.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Child & Youth Injury Prevention
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: In Canada unintentional injuries are the leading cause of death for children. The proposed research will increase knowledge for understanding and preventing injuries in preschool children (< 6 years), school-age children (7-12 years) and adolescents (13-17 years). Utilizing innovative methods the research reflects an explanation-oriented approach and examines interactions between risk factors. The focus is on psychological factors that impact risk, with the long-term goal being the identification of best practices for preventing common types of injuries within each age range. Cutting across all projects is an emphasis on promoting methodological advancements, promoting end-user involvement particularly in Knowledge Translation activities, and training/capacity building. The research will yield both practical and theoretical advancements in the field.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Integrative Stem Cell Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Despite the vast potential of stem cells to transform medical care, considerable challenges remain before this potential can be realized. The Chair in Integrative Stem Cell Biology will address these challenges through a research program focused on understanding the biology of stem cells, developing strategies to manipulate their behaviour and the establishment of models of human diseases. Utilizing a spectrum of stem cell types including the new highly promising human iPS cells, the research program will lead to new pathophysiologic insight and therapeutic approaches for chronic and degenerative diseases, as well as enhanced knowledge of the molecular mechanisms controlling stem cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Communication in the nervous system is mediated by chemical, electrical and ephaptic transmission. Electrical and ephaptic communication through gap junctions or gap junction hemichannels is far less understood than chemical transmission, but accruing evidence suggests a significant contribution in health and disease conditions like epilepsy, ischemia or cancer. In my research, I address the functional role of electrical and ephaptic communication in the vertebrate visual system starting from characterization of genes encoding gap junction type proteins in vitro to the development of animal models for functional analysis in vivo. The ultimate goal of my research is to answer the question of how these communication pathways contribute and interact to form a functional nervous system.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Ethnic Diversity and Cardiovascular Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity, diabetes, heart disease and stroke  collectively account for over half of the world-wide  burden of  chronic diseases.  The Canada Research Chair in Ethnic Diversity and Cardiovascular Disease research program aims  to identify  the major environmental  (i.e. diet  and physical activity)  and genetic causes of   obesity,  diabetes,  other heart disease risk factors including abnormal cholesterol and high blood pressure. This research will focus upon high risk ethnic communities  including  South Asians, Aboriginal peoples, and other non-white ethnic groups.  Novel discoveries made in these high risk populations will enable us  to develop new approaches to  prevention of obesity, diabetes and heart attacks in the future.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Signalling Networks in Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: The activity of a cell and how it responds to its environment is governed by signaltransduction pathways and it is the disruption of such pathways that underliesvirtually every human disease. My research is focused on two signalling pathways thatregulate many processes and when altered can contribute to human diseases, includingcancer. For this, we are investigating the molecular mechanisms that govern thesesignalling pathways through a variety of innovative biochemical and cell biologicalapproaches. In addition, we are utilizing the latest high-throughput, robotics-basedtechnologies to translating our molecular discoveries into the development of usefultherapeutics.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Psychopharmacology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: This tier I Canada Research Chair (CRC) in Psychopharmacology is dedicated to better understanding the neurochemical processes contributing to major depressive disorder (MDD) and to improving its treatment. Through the identification of the brain circuits involved in the effects of antidepressants, we have charted out new ways of augmenting their relatively poor clinical outcomes; we have found that the simultaneous use of  a combination of specifically targeted medications markedly improves clinical outcomes.  Indeed, we have published the results several controlled clinical studies using this approach showing a doubling of the usual remission rates of MDD within six weeks.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Biology of the Cell Nucleus
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: My laboratory studies a cancer-causing gene called the eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF4E. eIF4E is elevated in about 30% of cancers where it is associated with poor outcomes. My laboratory studies the biochemical functions of eIF4E in the cell, in order to understand how its dysregulation leads to cancer. We identified a drug to target eIF4E activity, ribavirin. We led clinical studies in poor prognosis leukemia patients and showed that ribavirin targeted eIF4E activity and led to transient clinical benefit in many patients. Studies continue to better elucidate these eIF4E related processes and to improve clinical outcomes in these patients.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Physical Activity and Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer is one of the most distressing diseases of our time. Over 170,000 Canadians are diagnosed with cancer each year and over 75,000 die from the disease. Over 1 million Canadians live with the effects of cancer and its treatments. The goal of my research program is to study the role of physical activity in the fight against cancer. More specifically, we are trying to find out if physical activity can help prevent some cancers, improve the quality of life of persons being treated for cancer, and even reduce the risk of recurrence and early death in cancer survivors.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Preventive medicine, Social medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Executive functions (EFs: selective attention, self-control, working memory, mental flexibility) are impaired in many mental health disorders. Well test interventions to reduce the incidence and/or severity of EF disorders and to enhance EF development. Weve shown that the Tools of the Mind curriculum improves EFs in at-risk children short-term.  We will address the next important questions:  Are these benefits lasting?  Do more-advantaged children also benefit? For the first time this will be studied in Canada. Well also investigate whether storytelling or dance enhance EF development. There's already evidence that aerobic exercise improves EFs. Might dance show even greater benefits?

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Cell Biology of Insulin Action
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity leads to insulin resistance of the muscle and inflammation, which predispose to type 2-diabetes. Exercise overcomes insulin resistance, but how this happens remains elusive. During tenure of this CRC Dr. Klip has created cellular systems of insulin resistance in a dish, exercise in a dish, and a unique transgenic mouse model to track the movement of glucose carriers in muscle tissue. She proposes a comprehensive plan to map in detail the insulin-sent signals inside muscle cells that direct small vesicles containing glucose carriers to the muscle surface, and how this process is subverted by saturated fats and inflammatory compounds.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Neuroscience
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: In several neurological disorders, small numbers of brain cells behave in an erratic manner and transmit this abnormal activity throughout the brain to cause major problems. Such disturbances are involved in Parkinsons disease and depression, and possibly in Alzheimers disease. Dr. Lozanos research focuses on identifying the brain cells that are malfunctioning in these disorders and finding ways to correct their activity.  The goal of this research is to develop new neurosurgical treatments, such as deep brain stimulation, to restore normal brain function in patients who continue to suffer from these disorders in spite of currently available therapies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Troubles du sommeil / Sleep Disorders
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Sleep disturbance is an important public health problem affecting more than 10% of the population. Chronic insomnia is the most prevalent of all sleep disorders, yet there is a significant gap in our understanding and treatment of this condition. The objectives of this research program are to document the prevalence, risk factors, and consequences of insomnia, and develop effective therapies. A unique feature will be its focus on psychological and behavioural therapies for a condition traditionally treated with medication. This research will improve the recognition and treatment of insomnia and reduce the individual and societal costs associated with this public health problem.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Biochemistry and Signal Transduction
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Regulation of proteins that reside at the surface of cells (plasma membrane) is critical for normal cellular and body functions, and when disrupted causes human diseases such as hypertension, cystic fibrosis, colitis and cancer. Dr. Rotins work has focused on the regulation of these membrane proteins by the ubiquitin system and by kinase and phosphatase enzymes in cells. Her planned work will elucidate how ubiquitination and phosphorylation of these membrane proteins are regulated and how they become mis-regulated in disease. Moreover, she plans to identify drugs and treatments that can correct this mis-regulation, to provide new treatments for these diseases.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 1
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 1
TitreApplicationTitle: Host Response to Virus Infection
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: We propose a novel approach towards the understanding of susceptibility and resistance to infections with clinically-important respiratory viruses modeling in mice severe influenza pneumonia, SARS and smallpox. Research progress of our group and others clearly indicated that host genes play an essential role in the onset, progression and ultimate outcome of infection with many pathogens. These genetic factors are often impossible to find in patients and infected populations, without the prior knowledge of their existence, location, and function, which can only be discovered in experimental animals, primarily the mouse. Our findings will provide invaluable information as to the genes, and mechanisms regulated by these genes, in our search for new anti-viral drugs and vaccines in humans.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Optogenetic probing of sleep-wake circuits of the brain
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: While the functions of sleep are still a matter of debate and may include memory consolidation, brain plasticity and energy conservation, the neural substrates of sleep and wakefulness are the subject of intense study. Dr. Adamantidiss objectives aim at investigating the functional properties (connectivity, firing dynamics and plasticity) of the neural circuits from the hypothalamus that controls sleep and wake states in normal and pathological conditions using optogenetics, including the Melanin-Concentrating Hormone (MCH)-expressing neurons and the Hypocretins/Orexins (Hcrt/Ox). Long-term perspectives will investigate how these hypothalamic circuits integrates environmental cues (i.e., circadian, arousal, metabolic, motivational) into appropriate goal-oriented behaviors.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cerebrovascular Function in Health and Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: The brain is absolutely dependent on adequate blood flow to function normally.  When brain blood flow drops below a critical level, within one-minute brain cells begin to die (called an ischemic stroke) which leads to a loss of mental abilities (termed dementia); these changes unfortunately occur during normal aging, and in diseases such as obesity and diabetes. Using state of the art brain imaging techniques, my research program explores ways to maintain brain blood flow in disease, and throughout aging. Our clinical ability to manage cerebral diseases will acutely improve by understanding mechanisms that regulate blood flow in the brain.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Synaptic physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: Many thousands of Canadians and more than 1.5 million people worldwide suffer from varying degrees of irreversible vision loss associated with neurodegenerative disorders of the retina.  However, currently there are no known ways to halt neurodegeneration.  New and innovative approaches are required to address this issue. Using an inter-disciplinary approach, Dr. Awatramani combines state-of-the-art two-photon laser scanning microscopy, electrophysiological and molecular biological techniques to understand how visual information is processed by neural circuits in the healthy retina. This information is then used to devise strategies to restore retinal function during neurodegenerative diseases that are known to lead to irreversible blindness.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Quality Control of Gene Expression
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: RNA is the functional entity expressed from the genome of all human cells. Accordingly, specific RNA molecules such as messenger RNAs (mRNA) are responsible for protein synthesis, whereas different types of noncoding (nc) RNAs are known to associate with proteins to form ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes. It is now clear that errors during the synthesis and processing of RNA, as well as during RNP assembly do occur in cells, but are largely prevented by poorly characterized quality control mechanisms. The proposed research program will make use of two innovative and complementary experimental systems to characterize important RNA quality control pathways. The proposed research is of significance, as errors during RNA synthesis and RNP assembly could result in mutant and possibly deleterious proteins and RNPs, which are known to contribute to cancer biology.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Critical Care Nephrology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: In sick patients requiring support in an intensive care unit, the development of acute injury of the kidneys is common. A significant proportion of these patients need to have acute dialysis started. The start of dialysis in these patients is not only associated with a high risk for death and long-term need for dialysis, but also greatly increases the complexity and cost of their care. Unfortunately, we still do not know the optimal time to start dialysis for these patients. Currently, there is no general consensus on this issue and practice patterns across the country are very variable. We believe this is a critical gap in knowledge. Accordingly, this proposal is for a program of investigation to better understand and improve the delivery of acute dialysis to these sick patients.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Chaire de recherche du Canada sur le vieillissement et la prévention du déclin cognitif
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Le vieillissement normal saccompagne souvent dun déclin cognitif qui peut nuireà la qualité de vie. Ce programme de recherche tentera de mieux comprendrecomment on peut modérer et prévenir le déclin cognitif associé au vieillissementnormal en étudiant limpact de la stimulation cognitive et de lentraînementphysique sur les performances cognitives des personnes âgées. Ces recherchesnous permettront de mieux comprendre comment on peut favoriser la santé cognitive des aînés et prévenir le déclin des fonctions cérébralesau cours du vieillissement normal.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Rehabilitation Engineering Design
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Canadian seniors and people with disabilities are growing relative to other populations.  This major demographic shift will impact all aspects of individual and community life, especially around health care use and social services.  The goal of the Canada Research Chair in "Accessible Technology for Mobility and Community Participation" is to develop novel solutions that improve and expand activities of daily living and community participation for people with disabilities, making a positive impact to their health and quality of life.  Research will be conducted into home access innovations, mobility solutions that support independent access to more environments, and other assistive technologies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cellular Science and Human Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heritable, psychiatric disease that affects 190,000 Canadians and the number of cases is increasing worldwide. Despite an obvious need, treatments for many disabilities associated with ASD do not exist. To design new therapies, scientists must first understand the cause of the disorder. This has proven difficult but recently genetic mutations linked to ASD have been discovered. My research aims to understand how some mutations disrupt brain cell function by targeting a fundamental cellular process called endocytosis. This laboratory will be one of few in the world using basic medical sciences to study ASD.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Viral Pathogenesis and Immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Despite 30 years of clinical, social, and biomedical research, HIV/AIDS remains a global health pandemic.  Over 33 million individuals worldwide are currently living with HIV, including approximately 65,000 Canadians.  The need for a safe and effective vaccine is clearly great, but biological correlates of protection are unknown.  Significant challenges in vaccine discovery, development and delivery also remain.  The proposed research program will examine the human immune response to HIV in rare individuals who spontaneously control infection.  The results of these studies are expected to improve our understanding of natural immunity to HIV and to identify new targets for vaccine and therapeutic intervention.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Évaluation et amélioration du système de santé
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: Transformer lorganisation des services de santé pour mieux répondre aux besoins de la population est un défi, compte tenu de lévolution technologique, démographique et des ressources financières limitées. L'évaluation est un champ de connaissances théoriques et méthodologiques qui permet de fournir les informations nécessaires pour porter un jugement éclairé sur l'organisation du système de santé, tout en appuyant les organisations dans limplantation des interventions. L'objectif de ce programme est d'utiliser l'évaluation comme un levier pour l'amélioration du système de santé. Il s'appuie sur une démarche imbriquée de recherche sur l'analyse du système de santé et sur les approches évaluatives.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cerebrovascular Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: Stroke is the leading cause of disability and second most common cause of death among adults in the world. There are very few treatments for stroke. Stroke occurs when a blood vessel in the brain is either blocked (ischemic stroke) or ruptures (cerebral hemorrhage). In both types blood flowing to the brain is affected. Until recently, doctors have had no way of seeing how much and where blood flow is reduced. Dr. Butcher uses new imaging technology to generate a picture of brain blood flow, which can be used to guide important treatment decisions. These include which patients should be given clot busting drugs and the best time to lower blood pressure after stroke. This research will lead to an increase in the number of patients with stroke who receive early treatment.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Mental Health Epidemiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Depression is the leading cause of disability in the world and is linked with many poor health outcomes including suicidal behaviour. Despite much research linking individual risk factors to depression, including many early in life, causes of depression are not well understood. Similarly, long-term outcomes of depression are not well defined. My research uses population-based surveys to better understand causes and outcomes of depression and other common mental disorders from a long-term perspective, and in particular uses progressive statistical techniques to disentangle the complex relationships between various factors that influence the development or course of these illnesses.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Infectious Disease Pathogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The major enteric pathogens affecting Canadians are transmitted through water and by domesticated food animals. My research investigates how these pathogens infect humans and how human and environmental activities influence the evolution of these infectious diseases. The major impact of my work has been in the life sciences, but has also influenced innovation in agriculture and animal health by uncovering important molecular details of bacterial evolution and pathogenesis in hosts. We are now at the stage where our command of the mechanisms can be leveraged into new diagnostic and potentially restorative strategies to improve food and water safety.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Environment, Culture and Values
Keywords-MotsClés: Other research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: As CRC in Environment, Culture and Values in Laurentian Universitys Department of Philosophy, I will explore novel solutions to conceptual problems regarding environments and cultures. Project A  in the philosophy of science  will explore how to identify relationships between cultures and environmental habitats that have recently been emphasized in the literature on cultural evolution. Project B  in bioethics  will focus on the ethical challenges raised by the migrations of people in order to provide or receive health care services, and how these inter-cultural phenomena can be encouraged or constrained in order to promote the outcomes that are most valued.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: socio-microbiologie / sociomicrobiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Protection of species and habitats
Abstract-Résumé: Despite medical advances in fighting various pathogens, infections remain the most important cause of mortality worldwide and the third leading cause of mortality in developed countries such as Canada. Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a prevalent pathogen responsible for many hospital-acquired infections. The genus Burkholderia comprises many species that inhabit remarkably diverse ecological niches. A number of Burkholderia are increasingly prevalent human pathogens. «Quorum sensing» (QS) is an intercellular communication system used by many bacteria, including P. aeruginosa and Burkholderia, to control their virulence factors. Because of their adaptability, persistence and multi-resistance to antibiotics, P. aeruginosa and Burkholderia are virtually impossible to eradicate. It is therefore imperative to search for new therapeutic approaches. We have found a remarkable QS mechanism required for the full virulence of P. aeruginosa. We have identified a similar system in Burkholderia. We believe QS represents a target for new anti-infection therapeutic strategies.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Food Marketing, Policy and Children's Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed Chair will focus on the socio-cultural aspects contributing to childrens health, and their impact on dietary habits and nutrition. In particular, the research program will: (1) assess food marketing and its implications for childrens diet and health; (2) probe the reception of food, media and nutrition messages by children; and (3) investigate Canadas regulatory environment with respect to food, food policy and food labeling. Overall, my program of research seeks to document and interrogate the complex and expansive nature of childrens food marketing, and to connect the issue of food communication to childrens health and regulation/policy.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Technologies and Practices in Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The Chair proposes an integrated research program aiming at optimizing implementation of innovative technologies in health care practices. To be successful, implementation must be driven by the knowledge translation process which transposes the best available scientific evidence, patients preferences, and clinicians experience into applicable action. A unique feature of our program is its multidimensional approach for studying individual, organizational and contextual factors influencing the integration of innovative health care technologies into practices. The proposed projects will help identifying strategies based on the best scientific evidence in order to reduce integration challenges of these technologies, thus increasing chances of success.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cell adhesion and proliferation
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, NA
Abstract-Résumé: In cancerous cells, normal controls regulating cell division are lost. Genes such as tumour suppressors encode do not divide signals. When these are inhibited, excess cell divisions produces a tumour. Equally important are signals that tell cells to stick together. These two signals must be balanced. Cancer proceeds when the signals for cells stick together and cells do not divide are mis-regulated.  How these processes are regulated is thus an important question. Our laboratory focuses on the tumour suppressor Merlin. Loss of Merlin activity leads to Neurofibromatosis Type 2 (NF2) which causes tumours in the brain and spinal cord.  How Merlin tells the cell do not divide is not understood. We are using genetic analysis in fruit flies  to identify proteins that interact with Merlin to help it carry out its functions. We propose that large complex of proteins, work together with Merlin to control cell proliferation and adhesion. Our ultimate goal to aid in diagnosis and therapy of NF2 tumours is to understand how Merlin acts as a tumour suppressor.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Viral Infection and Immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: Natural killer cells (NK cells) are a type of lymphocyte (white blood cell) and a component of our innate immune system.  Immune responses during virus infection are critical for combating infection but often cause collateral damage to the host when not appropriately controlled.  In addition to their anti-microbial role against virus infections, NK cells regulate immune response by releasing anti-inflammatory molecules.  This research is focused on mechanistically characterizing novel NK cell regulatory functions specific to sustained viral infections.  NK cells are at the forefront of immunology, thus results will provide new insights for therapeutic intervention during chronic infections.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Oral microbial genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Microbiologists have traditionally focused on free-swimming bacteria growing in laboratory cultures; yet they have recently come to realize that in the natural world more than 99% of all bacteria live in biofilm communities. Of importance with respect to medicine, biofilms are more tolerant to antibiotics. As a result, pathogens can persist several months (sometimes years) and give rise to recurrent infections exceedingly difficult to eradicate. Identification of the signalling mechanisms that regulate cell growth arrest has relevance to a number of important aspects of bacteria, including antibiotic tolerance, maintenance of pathogen reservoirs, and chronic biofilm infections.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Political Economy of Global Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Preventive medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Mental health disorders are predicted to account for a growing proportion of the global burden of disease, particularly in lower-income nations. Evidence from high-income countries suggests economic factors ranging from job-loss to recessions, as well as the policies that influence them, drives risk for mental health disorders. However, evidence is limited from low-and-middle income countries, where clinical interventions for improving mental health are impractical and population-level interventions may be more efficient. My objective is to estimate the multilevel effects of economic and social policies and economic characteristics on global mental health, with the motivation of informing interventions for improving health.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Structural Biology of Macromolecular Machines
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPS) are huge macromolecular machines that produce a vast variety of small molecules with important and diverse biological activity, including anti-virals, immunosuppressants and antibiotics, such as penicillin and cyclosporin. There is great potential to engineer NRPS for production of novel therapeutics and chemicals.This research uses structural and biochemical techniques to expand our understanding of mechanisms that NRPS employ to synthesize bio-active molecules. Topics addressed range from precise analysis of the chemical reaction NRPS uses to link together building blocks, to the large movements required by NRPS to processively synthesize their important products.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Movement Disorders and Neuroimaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Parkinsons disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder. Current therapies for PD focus mainly on relieving motor deficits but do not effectively manage the non-motor symptoms, which also have a significant impact on quality of life of these patients. The recent advances in functional neuroimaging provide unparalleled approaches for studying brain dysfunction and non-motor symptoms in PD. Using positron emission tomography (PET) imaging, this research program will investigate in-vivo the relationship between cognitive and behavioral complications and dopaminergic receptor abnormalities in the striatum and prefrontal cortex in patients with PD.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Aboriginal and Womens Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Social structures and relationships
Abstract-Résumé: The main objective of my research is to explore the implications of chronic illness and disability for marginalized populations. Given the prevalence of chronic illnesses, such as cancer, there is an increasing demand to understand the care needs of vulnerable populations from multiple perspectives. My program of research focuses on the social impact of chronic illness and disability on Aboriginal peoples and womens health, using innovative research methods, such as photography and drama. Two other key areas involve rehabilitation and knowledge translation, both of which emerge from the needs of research participants and health care professionals, as they articulate them.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neurovascular Coupling
Keywords-MotsClés: Biomedical engineering and medicines, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Normal brain function requires an ever-changing supply of blood in order to deliver oxygen and glucose to neural tissue in a timely and localized fashion.  This is triggered by the neural activity which is produced via the communication of neurons in the brain.  The delicate balance by which changes in neuronal activity regulate local cerebral blood perfusion is referred to as neurovascular coupling (NVC).  Currently, it is unknown whether NVC in the brain varies from region to region, or how it is affected by disease.  The Canada Research Chair in NVC will use safe, non-invasive tools to image both the neural and vascular components of human brain function.  State of the art analysis techniques will pinpoint variations in NVC from healthy individuals, which will then be compared to that obtained in patients with brain tumours.  These NVC studies are expected to result in new, non-invasive methods for improving the diagnosis and treatment of tumours.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Epigenetics, Reproduction and Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The use of assisted reproductive techniques for infertile couples is increasing. Will the use of sperm and oocytes (gametes) from infertile parents increase birth defects and alter offspring health?  Infertility has been associated to changes in the epigenetic program of sperm. Epigenetics is used to describe heritable information that is associated with the DNA and serves as a map to guide embryo development.  This research program investigates how epigenetic information on gamete DNA contributes to embryo health.  The information from this program will delineate how parents can cause disease in their offspring through heritable information outside of the DNA.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Membrane Proteins
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Biomedical engineering and medicines
Abstract-Résumé: I have developed a research program that occupies two interfaces:  between the physical and life sciences; and between basic academic research and commercial drug development.  These synergies have allowed me, and the research team I have assembled, to make a number of research discoveries centered around membrane protein structure, and begin to translate some of the discoveries towards clinical use.  For example, we have partnered with a local biotech company to develop improved treatments for psoriasis.  We have made several basic research discoveries that support the development of treatments for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS), a common and frequently fatal condition, as well as the development of peptide-based antimicrobial therapeutics, which are badly needed to combat the increasingly urgent problem of microbial resistance to conventional drugs.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Pathogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: This proposal elucidates the mechanisms of pathogenesis for two medically relevant spirochetes, Treponema pallidum and Leptospira, causative agents of syphilis and leptospirosis, respectively.  The first objective will be to gain an understanding of the capacity of Treponema pallidum to disseminate throughout the host and establish chronic infection, with the goal of identifying targets for inhibiting dissemination.  The second objective will be to determine the protein methylation status of outer membrane proteins within Leptospira, with the goal of gaining insight into Leptospira pathogenesis and identifying vaccine candidates.  These investigations represent unique research directions not being performed elsewhere in the world.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neural Circuit Development
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: GABAergic neurons powerfully control the function of cortical circuitry, and their dysfunction has been implicated in the pathogenesis of epilepsy, autism, schizophrenia and other brain diseases. The goal of the proposed research project is to identify the molecular pathways underlying the formation of specific subsets of GABAergic synapses (junctions that permit a neuron to communicate with another cell), by combining high-resolution imaging with single-cell gene manipulation of candidate genes. These findings will shed light both on the mechanisms underling the development GABAergic synapses and on the pathologic process leading to their disturbances and may aid in designing targeted treatment strategy.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Functional Proteomics
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The Canada Research Chair in Functional Proteomics will enable Dr. Gingras to continue the development of cutting-edge experimental and computational approaches which will be used to provide a better understanding of protein machineries inside each human cell.  By sharing her tools with Canadian colleagues, the position of Canada in the field of proteomics will be strenghtened.  Dr. Gingras will also study how cellular communication is altered in disease, with a special emphasis on a protein complex implicated in vascular diseases, and on another complex which is linked to resistance to anticancer drugs.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Innate Immunity and Microbial Pathogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: The host is in constant contact with microbes at the level of its mucosal surfaces. The innate immune system relies on microbial sensors that help avoiding invasion of deeper tissues. Our research program aims at understanding how pathogens can overcome these defense mechanisms. Specifically, we study the contribution of a new family of intracellular sensors, the Nod-like receptors. These investigations impact on our understanding of the patho-physiology of some important food-borne human diseases (Listeriosis, Shigellosis, Salmonellosis). Our research program will help unraveling the mechanisms that lead to inflammatory disorders at mucosal surfaces, such as Crohns disease and asthma.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: The Epidemiology of Type 2 Diabetes
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Nutrition and food hygiene
Abstract-Résumé: There is currently a global epidemic of adult-onset diabetes. Although fewpopulations have been spared increases in diabetes rates, several groups carry adisproportionate burden, including Aboriginal Canadians and people of Hispanic andAfrican origin. In addition, disorders including the Metabolic Syndrome andinsulin resistance indicate high risk for diabetes and thus provide a window tostudy early stages in the natural history of the disease. The goals of my researchare to identify factors related to the onset of diabetes in high risk populations, andto understand the progression of metabolic disorders that represent early stages indiabetes development

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Research Chair in Molecular Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Transporters are membrane proteins that allow the rapid passage of small molecules into or out of cells. In doing so, they regulate the concentration of these molecules in the cytoplasm and cell function secondarily. The applicant will determine how certain of these systems (some of which he uncovered himself) operate in general and by which mechanisms they regulate cell contractility and proliferation in blood vessels. The studies proposed should lead to the identification of therapeutic targets to decrease abnormal cell contractility/proliferation (as seen in high blood pressure and atherosclerosis) and open up many areas of investigations in cardiovascular research.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Neuroimaging
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: This innovative research program will continue to address one of the major health concerns in Canada with the use of advanced MRI techniques to study acute and chronic strokes in adult and pediatric patients. Our two key goals are to apply cutting edge imaging technology to extend the treatment window for acute ischaemic stroke patients and to assess blood flow abnormalities and related stroke risk in children with sickle cell disease. This research program aims to advance stroke treatment, improve the quality of life of people who suffered a stroke and reduce the economic burden on the Canadian health care system.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Health Services Research
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other research
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program has two overarching themes. Theme 1 seeks to understand how lifestyle factors (diet and physical activity) influence health status and the use of health services, while theme 2 seeks to apply this understanding. Using a social-ecological approach, which takes into account the interaction between an individual and their environment, and building on findings from my current research program, the proposed research will involve the implementation and evaluation of interventions to support healthy active lifestyles, across a number of settings where people live, learn or play, to address the complex problem of excessive weight gain (obesity).

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular embryology and genetics
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: Numerous human congenital malformations, including severely disabling and lethal malformations are associated to impaired function of genes from the Hox family. It is therefore essential to understand how these genes function and how their activity is controlled to improve prognosis and help developing appropriate therapies.The aim of this research program is to uncover mechanisms by which the activity of Hox genes is controlled during the development of the embryo and improve our understanding of the molecular mechanisms mediating Hox genes function.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Cell Division and Differentiation
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Stem cells are a population of cells that allow the regeneration of tissues in humansand other multicellular organisms. It is important to understand how stem cellsfunction because problems in their division can lead to the occurrence of cancer. The Canada Research Chair in Cell Division and Differentiation capitalizes on using a simple organism (a nematode earthworm called Caenorhabditis elegans) to understand how stem cells normally divide. Several genes that control cell division have been identified, and deciphering the function of these genes in the nematode worm will lead to better understanding their function in dividing human stem cells.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Implementation of Shared Decision Making in Primary Care
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Other medical research
Abstract-Résumé: The Chairs main goal is to give health professionals and their patients the skills they need to promote shared decision-making throughout the healthcare continuum. Shared decision-making is a process by which patients and their health professional share decisions. It ensure that both evidence and patients preferences are taken into account in the decision making process. Our findings will provide new knowledge on how health care professionals can be trained in order to provide better decision support to patients. In turn, this will help patients make more informed value-based decisions.

ProgramNameEN: Canada Research Chairs - CIHR Funded - Tier 2
NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Islet Biology
Keywords-MotsClés: Other medical research, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Diabetes affects more than 2.8 million Canadians and costs the healthcare system more than $15 billion per year. Diabetes results from loss or dysfunction of the insulin secreting pancreatic islets of Langerhans. Despite the prevalence of diabetes, islet function in health and disease is not fully understood. My work focuses on insulin secretion, particularly the molecular and electrical events that control insulin secretion when blood glucose is increased. This work will shed new light on pancreatic islet function and regulation of insulin secretion, contributing to the identification of islet defects in diabetes and targets for the pharmacological treatment of this disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Social and Environmental Aspects of Nutrition
Keywords-MotsClés: Nutrition and food hygiene, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Marquis' research program focuses on improving the dietary intakes and nutritional status of infants and young children living in poverty.  The research activities span from studies that examine the biological effect of a pregnancy-lactation overlap on birth outcomes and early infant health to community-based trials that test multi-sector interventions to improve child feeding.  The range of research activities are needed to develop infant and young child feeding policy recommendations, Optimal nutrition in early life is a key factor for physical and cognitive development. These early benefits are carried into adulthood and help communities achieve their full potential.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Pharmaceutical Outcomes
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: Canadians are taking more medications than ever before. With new medication use, serious side-effects can occur. Still, some medications are underused, resulting in poorer health and greater healthcare costs. A system is needed to monitor medications and ensure patients receive proper care.Dr. Carlo Marra has a strategy: pharmacists can monitor and improve medication use.  People see pharmacists more frequently than doctors, and studies show that involving pharmacists can significantly improve patient care. Dr. Marra's research uses powerful databases and a network of pharmacists to collect data, now showing real-world medication safety and effectiveness- and pharmacists role in improving health.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Immunology
Keywords-MotsClés: Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery, Pharmaceutical products
Abstract-Résumé: The immune system is critical to human health. The protective functions of immune cells are activated by cell surface receptors that deliver signals to the interior of the cell through the molecular process of signal transduction. Dysfunction of immune cells can result in chronic debilitating diseases such as immunodeficiency, autoimmunity, allergy and asthma. This research program will define the roles of specific signal transduction components that regulate activities of immune cells. The molecular definition of immune cell signaling will provide new concepts and molecular targets upon which to base rational therapies for diseases where these regulatory networks have gone awry.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires de recherche du Canada - financées par les IRSC - Niveau 2
TitreApplicationTitle: Systems of Trauma Care
Keywords-MotsClés: Hospital structure and organization of medical care, Health
Abstract-Résumé: Each year approximately 15,000 Canadians die from injuries and over 225,000 are hospitalized. If an injured patient is treated at a designated trauma centre, their chance of surviving is much greater.  By virtue of geography and population distribution, there are significantchallenges in accessing trauma centres, with approximately 40% of severely injured patients never receiving such care.  It might take as long as 6 hours to receive definitive care in some areas. This research program identifies the gaps in access to definitive trauma care and seeks to identify modifiable factors that lead to improvements in accessing trauma care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mental Health and Addiction
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Drug abuse and addiction
Abstract-Résumé: Dysfunction of the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is thought to be an important factor in a number of psychiatric diseases, such as schizophrenia, ADHD and addiction. The role of the PFC is especially important for the cognitive aspects of the disorders.The main goal of my research program is to understand how various aspects of higher-order cognition are represented by networks of PFC neurons. This involves recording from large groups of PFC cells as rats perform tasks similar to those affected in patients with schizophrenia. Understanding cognition at this cellular level is a fundamental step towards developing  appropriate therapeutic strategies

TitreApplicationTitle: Lung Development, Injury and Repair
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, Medical research, hospital treatment, surgery
Abstract-Résumé: Dr. Thébaud is a pediatrician-researcher whose primary research focus is to understand how the normal lung forms, what happens when the lung is injured and from this knowledge design new treatments for patients with lung diseases. This is important because chronic lung diseases will be the third leading cause of death by 2030. Dr. Thébauds research is discovering how stem cells heal injured lungs in the laboratory, how this can be used in the clinic to cure or improve life-quality of patients with life-threatening lung diseases, and how babies with severe lung injury do as they grow up.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Research Chair in Population Health
Keywords-MotsClés: Health, NA
Abstract-Résumé: The proposed research program investigates the impacts of program and policies related to school-based promotion of healthy eating and active living. This includes the evaluation of the effectiveness in terms of improvements in healthy eating, active living and prevention of overweight among students. It also includes cost-effectiveness whereby we balance program costs against cost savings resulting from prevented chronic diseases. It further includes benefits of health promotion to learning and self-esteem.  The research program is essential to public health decision makers to weigh investments in school-based health promotion against benefits in terms of disease prevention, avoided health care costs, and better education.

TitreApplicationTitle: Optimizing evidence synthesis for informed decision-making
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILD HEALTH; EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS; EVIDENCE-BASED MEDICINE; GRADING EVIDENCE; INDIRECT COMPARISONS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MIXED TREATMENT COMPARISONS; NETWORK ANALYSIS; OVERVIEWS OF REVIEWS; SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS
Abstract-Résumé: Patients, healthcare providers, and policy-makers rely on high quality evidence to make important decisions about medical treatments. Overviews of reviews are a new method of bringing together high quality health evidence about the effectiveness and safety of different treatments for a health condition or illness. Overviews offer one-stop shopping or a "friendly front-end" for decision-making by bringing together evidence from different, often complex, sources into a single product. Overviews are relatively new in the medical literature, therefore the methods for their production are not consistent. Research is needed to refine how they are done to make sure that they include all relevant information and present accurate information about whether or not treatments are safe and effective. Overviews of reviews have the potential to become an important tool for patients, healthcare providers, and policy-makers when making treatment decisions. This research will refine the methods for producing and reporting overviews of reviews to ensure that they provide the highest quality evidence for informed decision-making.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Cardiovascular Safety of Varenicline: A Population-Based Cohort Study
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; DATABASES; DRUG SAFETY; MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION; PHARMACOEPIDEMIOLOGY; SIDE EFFECTS; SMOKING CESSATION; STROKE; VARENICLINE
Abstract-Résumé: Varenicline is a pill that is used to help people quit smoking.  It is sold under the trade name Champix.  Previous studies have shown that it is the most effective pill used to help people stop smoking.  However, there is now some evidence that varenicline may have harmful effects on people's hearts and that it might increase the chances of having a heart attack.  Government agencies like Health Canada and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration are currently studying the safety of varenicline.  Unfortunately, available information about its safety is limited.  For this reason, more studies are needed to determine if varenicline causes heart problems in people who are trying to stop smoking.  The proposed study will examine the safety of varenicline using information from the General Practice Research Database, or GPRD.  The GPRD is a database that contains the medical records for more than 11 million people in the United Kingdom.  We will use the GPRD to identify two groups of patients: those who took varenicline and those who took bupropion.  We will then compare the number of people in each group that had a heart attack in the 3 months after they started taking the pill.  We will also check if varenicline increases the chances of dying or being hospitalized for a stroke, heart failure, or heart operations.  To perform these comparisons, we will use a new type of statistical analysis called high-dimensional propensity scores.  This study will take 2 years to complete.  If varenicline increases the chances of having heart problems, patients and doctors need to know about these potential side effects.  On the other hand, if varenicline is safe, they need to know so that it can be prescribed to help people stop smoking.  Either way, this study will have important clinical and public health implications.
