TitreApplicationTitle: Injecting Evidence into Health Policy Coverage: Working with the Media
Keywords-MotsClés: COMMUNICATING EVIDENCE THROUGH THE MEDIA; EVIDENCE BASED DECISION-MAKING; EVIDENCE ON CONTROVERSIAL POLICY ISSUES; HEALTH POLICY; KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION
Abstract-Résumé: Academics research important policy issues and the media communicate with the public about these issues. Often there is little overlap between what researchers say is the evidence and what the media report. This project attempts to change this.      EvidenceNetwork.ca seeks to improve the use of research evidence by the media in their coverage of key health policy issues. We have built a website which profiles evidence on controversial health policy topics, and helps journalists access 40+ highly qualified non-partisan Experts to discuss these topics. We have established links to media across the country and our Experts have already published more than 90 OpEds in Canadian newspapers.        We collaborate with Canadian Health Services Research Foundation, the Health Council of Canada, Canadian Institute of Health Information and Canadian Institutes of Health Research on this project and we are building ties with the Science Media Centre of Canada and the Atkinson Charitable Foundation.       In the next three years we will meet with editorial boards across the country, develop an internship program and a teaching module for journalists, double the number of experts and OpEds, evaluate what works and what doesn't and integrate EvidenceNetwork.ca into the operations of one of our partners.      Why focus on evidence?  Because the public debate around health policy is important to Canadians. The Canadian Health Accord is scheduled for renegotiation in 2014. The country will have to make decisions about many complex issues, including health care spending, user fees, the role of the private sector and the sustainability of Medicare. These are issues which directly affect Canadians, and about which they seek evidence from unbiased reliable sources.      With staffing cutbacks at many media outlets, the time is right for providing Canadians with an accessible, credible, non-partisan health policy news resource. That is what EvidenceNetwork.ca is all about.

TitreApplicationTitle: Partnership for applied research in fracture prevention programs for the elderly
Keywords-MotsClés: FALL ACCIDENT; FALL PREVENTION; FRAGILITY BONE FRACTURE; HEALTH SERVICES; INTERPROFESSIONAL COLLABORATION; KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER; NON-INFERIORITY TRIAL; OSTEOPOROSIS; POST-FRACTURE SCREENING; PRAGMATIC TRIAL
Abstract-Résumé: During their lifetime, approximately 50% of Canadian women and 30% of Canadian men will experience at least one fracture due to bone fragility (FF). Evidence is growing regarding prevention programs' effectiveness to prevent falls, but prevention of fractures through fall prevention programs has enjoyed limited success. Falls prevention programs and post-fracture screening programs leading to pharmacological treatment are very different strategies, with a shared ultimate goal. Coordination between those who repair fractures and those who manage the patient to prevent the next fracture is critical.  The overarching aim of this proposal is to generate evidence-based knowledge about the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of an integrated FF prevention program, as well as a portrait of the barriers and facilitating factors for such programs. More specifically, the objectives are: 1) to combine existing fall prevention and post-fracture management programs in the province of Quebec into integrated FF prevention programs; 2) to compare the performance of these integrated programs to control sites, using a pragmatic study design; 3) to identify barriers as well as factors that improve effectiveness across different implementation milieu; and 4) to develop and engage in active knowledge transfer activities in Quebec regions where integrated FF prevention programs are neither adequately nor successfully implemented. The proposed team is poised to develop new interdisciplinary collaborations among healthcare practitioners and decision makers involved in the prevention of FFs. The program is built upon existing healthcare and structures and programs and in turn, will truly measure the effectiveness of an integrated FF prevention program. The results will ultimately lead to improvements in the existing knowledge base, address policy-relevant and health systems problems, and assist in the design and implementation of FFs prevention programs.

TitreApplicationTitle: Five views on a journey: Developing a systems model of treatment and care for mental health, substance use and violence problems
Keywords-MotsClés: ADDICTION; HEALTH SYSTEM; MENTAL HEALTH; VIOLENCE
Abstract-Résumé: A team of researchers and knowledge users is interested in developing strategies for improving the system of services for persons experiencing challenges or problems related to mental health, substance use/addiction and/or violence (MSV). The research has three main objectives: (I) to collect data on services for MSV problems in four diverse sites (i.e., Welland and Port Colborne, Windsor, Kettle Point and Aamjiwnaang First Nations, Sudbury); (II) to develop a model for each community showing how people with MSV problems use services and to identify and address major problems in system functioning in these communities; and (III) to develop an overarching model of how the service system operates for people with MSV problems and identify ways this system can be improved to provide optimal and cost-effective care. The project will be conducted in three phases. In Phase I, data will be collected about services for MSV problems in each community from five perspectives: (a) persons who have MSV problems; (b) family members of persons who have MSV problems; (c) a general population community sample; (d) two databases of use of health and addictions treatment services; and (e) formal and informal service providers. In Phase II, findings from Phase I will be used by knowledge users and researchers to develop a comprehensive model of service use by persons with MSV and to develop a plan for addressing major problems within each community. In the third and final phase, a workshop will be held with local, regional and provincial knowledge users and researchers to identify various strengths and weaknesses of each local system and develop a preliminary general model of service use by persons who have MSV problems. Researchers will work closely with community partners to define research questions, interpret findings and apply knowledge. This research will be used to develop cost-effective approaches that optimize care for people with MSV problems.

TitreApplicationTitle: Vers l'amélioration des services et des soins palliatifs de fin de vie : Adapter et implanter des programmes de soutien en milieu de travail et évaluer leur effet sur la SATisfaction, le sens au travail et le bien-être des INfirmières -SATIN II
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPETENCE EN SOINS PALLIATIFS; COMPETENCE ETHIQUE; DETRESSE; FACTEURS DE RISQUE PSYCHOSOCIAUX; INFIRMIERES; ORGANISATION APPRENANTE; PROGRAMME DE SOUTIEN; SATISFACTION AU TRAVAIL; SENS AU TRAVAIL; SOINS PALLIATIFS
Abstract-Résumé: Avec le vieillissement de la population,  les Canadiens reclament un meilleur acces a des soins palliatifs (SP) de qualite et les services dans ce secteur de soins demeurent a organiser. L'organisation de tels services necessite la formation et le soutien aux soignants.  Les soins de fin de vie sans soutien peuvent contribuer a l'intensification du travail aupres d'une population de travailleurs deja a bout de souffle. L'intensification du travail et le stress sont associes a la detresse, l'insatisfaction au travail et l'epuisement professionnel. Chez les infirmieres, ces facteurs de risque psychosociaux sont particulierement susceptibles d'engendrer des problemes de retention, de roulement et d'absenteisme au travail. Les resultats du projet SATIN I en cours (5 etudes transversales terminees - projet IRSC-PASS en partenariat avec le MSSS et l'IRSST) demontrent que le travail en SP se traduit par une souffrance ethique. De plus, notre modele de stress permet d'expliquer pres de 40% de la detresse et plus de 80% de la satisfaction au travail et ce, par des facteurs psychosociaux occupationnels, tels le manque de reconnaissance, la perte de sens au travail et le manque de ressources. Malgre le fait que plusieurs etablissements de sante sont a implanter des services de SP, les besoins de soutien organisationnel des infirmieres pour ameliorer le contexte dans lequel elles les prodiguent sont criants. S'appuyant sur le concept de l'organisation apprenante, 4 etudes sont proposees avec le projet SATIN II. Le but est la selection, l'adaptation, l'implantation et l'evaluation de 4 programmes de soutien dans 4 milieux de soins de Quebec et Montreal selon une approche participative. Chaque programme vise d'abord le soutien de l'infirmiere et de l'equipe de soins par l'integration d'une approche palliative dans des secteurs cibles.

TitreApplicationTitle: New Graduate Nurse Retention: A National Study of Factors Influencing New Graduate Nurses' Job and Career Transition in the First Two Years of Practice
Keywords-MotsClés: CAREER SATISFACTION; CAREER TRANSITION; JOB SATISFACTION; NEW GRADUATE NURSES; NURSING WORK ENVIRONMENT; NURSING WORKFORCE; RETENTION
Abstract-Résumé: New graduate nurses are a precious resource in today's nursing workforce shortage. To promote retention, every effort must be made to ensure that new graduates work in supportive environments that encourage their professional growth, career satisfaction, and personal wellbeing. Heavy workloads and stressful work environments complicate the transition from student nurse to professional, contributing to increased burnout and turnover rates as high as 57% within the first two years of practice (1). The purpose of this study is to describe new graduate nurses' worklife experiences in Canadian health care settings in the first two years and to examine predictors of job and career satisfaction and turnover intentions across time. A longitudinal survey design will be used to examine the factors that influence new graduate nurse transition at two points in time (1-year apart).  A sample of new graduate nurses working in each province across Canada will be obtained from the respective provincial regulatory body (estimated N=3300).  Focus groups of new graduate nurses from four regions across Canada (West, Quebec, Ontario, and Atlantic) will be conducted (3 groups per region) following the survey to obtain more in depth information about factors that facilitated or impeded their transition over the first two years.  Themes emerging from these focus groups will be compared to the survey findings and used to enrich the interpretation of the quantitative data. We will also conduct focus groups with nurses in unit level leadership roles (1 per region) to obtain their perspectives on what is important for optimizing new graduate transition to practice in their organizations and to obtain their interpretation of how the results may inform new graduate retention strategies. This approach should provide a national database identifying new graduate nurses' experiences of transitioning to the graduate role and factors that influence their transition.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude Québécoise d'Intervention pour les Parents d'Enfants d'âge préscolaire avec des problèmes de comportements (ÉQUIPE)
Keywords-MotsClés: INTERVENTIONS PARENTALES; PROBLEMES DE COMPORTEMENT CHEZ LES JEUNES ENFANTS; PREVENTION; SANTE MENTALE DES ENFANTS
Abstract-Résumé: Les problemes de comportements (ex: agressivite, hyperactivite) chez les jeunes enfants, sont le principal motif de consultation en sante mentale. Ces problemes sont frequents  et perturbent le developpement de l'enfant et sa famille. Sans traitement, les problemes persistent a l'adolescence et s'aggravent avec le decrochage scolaire. Chez l'adulte, s'y ajoutent les depressions, l'abus d'alcool et de drogues et le chomage, d'ou leur cout economique tres eleve. S'ils sont traites efficacement, et surtout precocement ces enfants peuvent se developper normalement. Malheureusement, au Canada, les longues listes d'attente rendent difficile l'intervention precoce, et les traitements utilises ne sont pas toujours bases sur des preuves scientifiques. Devant l'urgence pour ces enfants d'avoir une reponse a leurs besoins, les services de sante doivent mettre en place des traitements de groupes, de courte duree et scientifiquement efficaces. Le programme COPE (developpe en Ontario) repond a tous ces criteres. COPE qui permet aux groupes de parents, accompagnes de professionnels, de trouver leurs solutions face aux problemes de comportements de leurs enfants, existe en anglais, en espagnol et suedois, mais pas en francais. L'Etude quebecoise de l'intervention parentale chez les enfants avec problemes de comportements (EQUIPE) qui reunit des chercheurs et des decideurs des programmes de soins, vise a developper la version francophone de COPE et a etudier son impact sur les problemes de comportements et les listes d'attentes dans une population francophone, dans le cadre du systeme de soins quebecois. Cette etude permettra de voir les difficultes et les facilites pour l'utilisation future de ce programme dans d'autres milieux francophones canadiens et internationaux (Belgique, France et Tunisie). EQUIPE permettra aux milliers d'enfants francophones du Canada et dans le monde qui souffrent de problemes de comportement d'avoir acces rapidement aux meilleurs traitements disponibles

TitreApplicationTitle: Reducing inequities in access to and use of prenatal care in the Winnipeg Health Region through health system improvement
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESS TO CARE; INEQUITIES IN HEALTH CARE; INTEGRATION OF HEALTH SERVICES; MIDWIFERY CARE; PRENATAL CARE; SOCIAL MARKETING
Abstract-Résumé: Prenatal care has the potential to improve the health of pregnant women and reduce the incidence of poor infant outcomes, and is more likely to be effective if women begin receiving care in the first trimester of pregnancy and continue to receive care throughout pregnancy.  Despite the emphasis placed on the value of prenatal care, some pregnant women continue to receive inadequate prenatal care.  Previous research has shown wide regional variations in use of prenatal care in Manitoba, with a geographic concentration of high rates of inadequate prenatal in northern areas of the province and in the inner-city areas of Winnipeg.  These inequities in use of prenatal care emphasize the need for effective targeted services and programs. The purpose of this study is to assess the effectiveness of three "health system improvement" initiatives aimed at improving access to and use of prenatal care by inner-city women, including: (1) incorporating midwifery care at existing Healthy Baby community support groups; (2) expanding existing mobile van services to offer prenatal care and link women to the appropriate health care providers; and (3) implementing a social marketing campaign (e.g., brochures, posters, Facebook/Twitter, text messaging) to promote the importance of prenatal care and provide information on where women can receive prenatal care. This study will evaluate the rates of inadequate prenatal care before and after the initiatives are implemented, as well as women's and health care providers' experiences with receiving and providing prenatal care within these initiatives.

TitreApplicationTitle: Working with Parents to Prevent Childhood Obesity: A Primary Care-based Study
Keywords-MotsClés: FAMILY; INTERVENTION; OBESITY; PEDIATRICS; PRIMARY CARE
Abstract-Résumé: Childhood obesity is an urgent public health issue. Roughly one-quarter of Canadian children are overweight, putting them at risk for chronic diseases. Because most families access health services in primary care, it is an ideal venue for obesity prevention. Specifically, programs in primary care can prevent unhealthy weight gain in healthy weight children (primary prevention) AND reduce unhealthy weight gain in children who are already overweight (secondary prevention). Parents play a key role in children's health, so it is vital to include parents in strategies to prevent childhood obesity.  Our team will work with the Edmonton Oliver Primary Care Network (EOPCN) to prevent childhood obesity through the following objectives:   1.Develop a web-based, brief (20-30 minutes long) program for parents as an educational tool to (i) motivate parents to support healthy lifestyles in children, and (ii) access community resources and health services that can prevent childhood obesity; 2.Assess the acceptability of the program using focus group interviews with parents (n=15) and health professionals (n=12); 3.Determine family recruitment (n=140) and retention rates at baseline, 1-, and 6-months follow-up; 4.With the same sample (n=140), collect preliminary data at baseline, 1-, and 6-months follow-up to explore if the program led to changes in (i) parents' motivation to support their children's lifestyle habits, and (ii) families' use of resources and health services to prevent childhood obesity.  Findings from this developmental study will inform a future clinical trial to test intervention efficacy. The collaborations we will develop between our researchers, decision-makers, and the EOPCN are very important. These partnerships will help us to develop a novel program for parents as well as share our results with professionals and families dedicated to preventing childhood obesity in Alberta and across Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving Functional Capacity and Reducing Falls among Frail Older Adults: Delivery of Exercise Intervention Through Home Care Network
Keywords-MotsClés: EXERCISE PROGRAM; FALLS PREVENTION; FRAIL ELDERLY; FUNCTIONAL CAPACITY; HOME CARE NETWORK
Abstract-Résumé: Unintentional falls are one of the leading causes of mortality and morbidity among frail older adults. The consequences of falls  include considerable physical, psychological, and economic costs. While a majority of the community-based falls prevention programs have been shown to reduce falls and falls-related injuries, there is a need for exploring this issue among frail, largely home-bound older adults. The higher incidence of falls coupled with a higher number of individuals at risk for poor physical function among this group make it critical to explore this issue within the proposed context. Thus, the purpose of the study will be to examine the impact of a home-based exercise program on functional capacity, falls, and fall-related injuries among seniors living in rural and urban areas using a factorial design. For the purpose of the present study, 164 individuals over 65 years of age will be receiving home care will be recruited through the Health Region. Specifically, comparisons across the four study groups -- exercise rural, exercise urban, comparison rural, comparison urban - will be made. The  participants in the exercise group will perform the Home Support Exercise Program developed by the Canadian Center for Activity and Aging. The participants background information, status on health, function, nutrition, and falls will be assessed and compared at baseline, at 6-months and again at 12 months. A 12-month time frame is proposed to use fall rates and functional capacity as study outcomes. The management structure will consist of a Falls Prevention Advisory Group, which will be composed of representatives from community partners (e.g., Safe Saskatchewan, Regina Health Region, and Saskatchewan Ministry of Health) and the research team.

TitreApplicationTitle: A Family Integrated Care Model for the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
Keywords-MotsClés: FAMILY INTEGRATED CARE; NEONATAL INTENSIVE CARE; PRETERM INFANTS
Abstract-Résumé: In the modern neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) the infant is separated from its parents, which damages parent/infant interaction and is harmful to the infant. In response to this, programs such as family centered care, kangaroo care and skin to skin care have been developed. However, they are based on the idea that only health care professionals with special skills can care for the infant. Parents play a mainly supportive role, and still feel anxious and unprepared to care for their infants when they leave the unit. We have developed a new model in which parents provide all except the most advanced medical care for infants instead of nurses, while nurses became teachers for parents. Results and feedback from an initial study of this Family Integrated Care (FIC) model show that it is both workable and safe. We now propose to take this model to 16 centres across Canada, for a complete evaluation. We will assess weight gain, breastfeeding, clinical outcomes, safety, satisfaction, stress and anxiety of the parents, and resource use. Parents will learn to provide care for infants with nursing supervision in the areas of feeding, bathing, dressing, holding skin to skin, supported by volunteer parent buddies and special education sessions. This trial has the potential to dramatically change the way care is delivered in NICUs, and outcomes data will be collected and compared with hospitals that are not participating, and additional data regarding parental anxiety and satisfaction, and nurses satisfaction will be collected to determine its impact.

TitreApplicationTitle: The effect that inactivation of the RNA interference machinery has on endogenous levels of microRNAs and their gene targets
Keywords-MotsClés: ADENO ASSOCIATED VIRUS; ALLELE SPECIFIC EXPRESSION; ARGONAUTES; EMBRYO DEVELOPMENT; GENE THERAPY; HIGH THROUGHPUT SEQUENCING; LIVER TOXICITY; MICRORNAS; NON-CODING RNAS; RNA INTERFERENCE
Abstract-Résumé: The discovery of RNA interference has revolutionized the potential for gene therapy and personalized medicine.  In this process a small portion of virtually any gene (a small RNA) in the human genome can use the body's own natural mechanism for eliminating that very same gene from being expressed and functionally active.  Since any gene can be targeted, a tailored approach can be used to eliminate any gene that is mutated and responsible for a particular disease that an individual may have.   The greatest challenge at present is effective delivery of this small RNA.  While this barrier is being overcome, we are focused on another critical area:  the safety of delivering this therapeutic.  We know that by adding too much of these small RNAs, the natural use of the RNA interference system can be overwhelmed in the body leading to unintended and drastic consequences.  We have addressed this by cataloging all of the small RNAs and target RNAs that are affected when one of the key genes in this pathway, argonaute-2, is eliminated in the mouse.  These mice have severe defects in embryo growth.  We have been able to characterize which small RNAs are required for this portion of embryo development and shown that they require argonaute-2 for identifying and removing their target genes.  Our next goal is to characterize the small RNAs in adult mice with a given gene therapy target.  We believe that the same small RNAs in our preliminary studies with argonaute-2 will be impaired when many non-specific small RNAs are delivered.  With this information, we will be able to devise mechanisms to ensure that these small RNAs are monitored and acted upon to prevent adverse events in response to this form of gene therapy.  The exciting potential of this gene therapy mechanism can then be realized and be applicable as a therapeutic to cure a broad range of genetic diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'implantation d'une clinique de suivis intégrés de maladies chroniques en misant sur la deuxieme ligne de soins
Keywords-MotsClés: DIABETE; IMPLANTATION D'UN SUIVI; MALADIES INFLAMMATOIRES; PRATIQUES DE GESTION; PRATIQUES PROFESSIONNELLES; SUIVI DES MALADIES CHRONIQUES
Abstract-Résumé: Au Canada, l'organisation des soins est reactive en visant le soulagement des symptomes et le traitement des episodes aigus, rendant les trajectoires de soins deficientes et les acces aux services difficiles. Afin de corriger la situation, plusieurs modeles d'organisation du suivi des maladies chroniques sont mis de l'avant mais c'est le Chronic Care Model qui semble le plus complet et le plus utilise. Cependant, des obstacles lies aux pratiques existantes et aux modes de gestion semblent empecher d'ancrer l'approche voulue. Il apparait qu'il faille chercher a mettre en evidence la complementarite et le caractere unique des apports des acteurs impliques. Pour cette raison, le projet d'implantation d'une  clinique de maladies chroniques mene par le Centre hospitalier affilie universitaire de Quebec (CHA) sera etudie afin de : 1) decrire et analyser les modes actuels de pratiques et les arrangements aptes a etre pris par chacun des groupes d'acteurs impliques dans les activites sous-jacentes du CCM pour les maladies etudiees; 2) comprendre les pratiques organisationnelles et cliniques qui en resultent en cours d'implantation pour les maladies etudiees ; 3) evaluer les resultats patients pour chacune des maladies etudiees ; 4) comparer et contraster les pratiques organisationnelles et cliniques de chacune des maladies etudiees pour en degager ce qui en resulte ; 5) elaborer un modele de reorganisation de l'offre de services aux personnes atteintes de maladies chroniques. Cette etude mise sur une strategie mixte de recherche faisant appel a des methodes qualitatives et quantitatives. Elle permettra le developpement de projets novateurs d'utilisation de la 2eme ligne de soins pour l'amelioration du suivi des maladies chroniques en adoptant une approche realiste qui consiste a adapter un modele d'organisation (le CCM) aux pratiques au lieu de chercher a adapter des pratiques aux modeles issus de la litterature et a des imperatifs de changement non encore realises.

TitreApplicationTitle: Impact de la détermination de la structure et de l'interaction membranaire de la rétinol déshydrogénase 8 pour les maladies de la rétine
Keywords-MotsClés: ACYLATION DE PROTEINES; BIOLOGIE STRUCTURALE; BIOPHYSIQUE; LIAISON MEMBRANAIRE; RETINOL DESHYDROGENASE; VISION
Abstract-Résumé: La malvoyance et la cecite ont un impact social et financier tres important et affectent les gens qu'ils soient vieillissants ou pendant leur meilleure periode de production economique. L'oeil est l'organe ou on retrouve le plus grand nombre de maladies hereditaires car elles ne causent pas le deces des gens affectes. De plus, le glaucome et les degenerescences et dystrophies retiniennes comptent pour plus de 80% des cas de cecite au Canada. L'objectif majeur de ce travail est de determiner la structure d'une enzyme pour expliquer le role des mutations de ces proteines dans les degenerescences et dystrophies retiniennes. Le pigment visuel des photorecepteurs est responsable de l'absorption de la lumiere au niveau de la retine de l'oeil. La retinol deshydrogenase 8 (RDH8) est une enzyme impliquee dans le cycle visuel des retinoides qui est le processus cyclique permettant de regenerer ce pigment visuel. La RDH8 est localisee dans les segments externes des photorecepteurs et serait responsable de la premiere modification chimique de ce retinoide suite a l'absorption de la lumiere. La resolution de la structure tertiaire de la RDH8 representerait une decouverte importante car cela permettrait d'expliquer comment des mutations de la RDH5 et la RDH12 sont responsables de maladies de l'oeil. En effet, une mutation anti-sens dans le gene codant pour la RDH5 est associee a une maladie autosomique recessive rare appelee «fundus albipunctatus». De plus, une dysfonction de la RDH5 entraine une cecite nocturne, une accumulation de points blancs a la retine ainsi qu'une dystrophie des cones chez les personnes agees. Une mutation dans le gene codant pour la RDH12 est associee a l'amaurose congenitale de Leber qui est une maladie qui entrainera la cecite en quelques decennies seulement. Il parait donc essentiel de determiner la structure de la RDH8 afin d'expliquer le role des mutations de ces proteines dans les degenerescences et dystrophies retiniennes pour mieux les traiter.

Abstract-Résumé: Street-involved or homeless youth are subject to dramatic health inequities; specifically they are at increased risk for suicide attempts, substance abuse, injection drug use, survival sex, as well as a wide range of health concerns compared to housed youth of a similar age. Despite this dramatic level of healthcare need, these vulnerable youth are far less likely to seek healthcare and/or social services for a variety of complex reasons including: stigma; discrimination; and barriers to access. By far the largest barrier to improving the circumstances of street-involved youth is the profound difficulty of engaging these youth in helping relationships and services. It is readily acknowledged that significant numbers of youth do not successfully participate in available services and programs that would support positive adaptation and re-integration. Furthermore, our decision making partners indicate that overwhelming mental health issues, such as those identified above, frequently preclude youth from fully engaging in a range of healthcare services (including mental health services), as well as educational or employment programmes, that could ultimately lead to independent and healthy lives. TitreApplicationTitle: Les laboratoires de promotion de la santé comme outil de développement professionnel et organisationnel en santé publique : étude de cas
Keywords-MotsClés: APPRENTISSAGE ORGANISATIONNEL; COMMUNAUTES DE PRATIQUE; DEVELOPPEMENT PROFESSIONNEL; ORGANISATIONS DE SANTE PUBLIQUE; PROMOTION DE LA SANTE; SANTE PUBLIQUE; ETUDE DE CAS
Abstract-Résumé: De nouveaux modes d'organisation des services de sante et les developpements contemporains en terme de concepts et methodes en sante publique amenent le besoin de renouveler les pratiques des professionnels evoluant dans ce secteur.  De nombreux efforts sont en cours afin d'ajuster l'offre de formation et ainsi habiliter la main-d'uvre a confronter plus efficacement ces nouveaux defis.  Dans cet esprit, ce projet vise a evaluer une intervention novatrice de developpement professionnel en promotion de la sante developpee par la Direction de la sante publique de Montreal et offerte a des equipes de professionnels d'organisations locales de sante publique que sont les Centres de la sante et des services sociaux.  L'intervention implique la participation a des laboratoires de promotion de la sante, une formule s'apparentant a une communaute de pratique, et visant le developpement professionnel et organisationnel au regard des pratiques actuelles en promotion de la sante.  S'appuyant sur un cadre conceptuel inspire des theories de performance des equipes de travail et de creation de connaissances organisationnelles, la methodologie d'evaluation implique un devis d'etude de cas et des strategies de collecte de donnees incluant le questionnaire, l'analyse documentaire, l'entrevue individuelle et de groupe avec des participants des organisations concernees (DSP et CSSS) evoluant au sein des laboratoires et a l'exterieur de ceux-ci. Parmi les retombees de ce projet, figure une avancee des connaissances sur les effets des communautes de pratique dans un contexte d'organisation locale de sante publique et ce, tant au plan des professionnels que des organisations impliques. De tels resultats sont importants en ce qu'ils permettront d'alimenter la prise de decision eu egard a l'intervention de developpement professionnel en sante publique de sorte a assurer une main d'oeuvre mieux preparee a repondre aux defis contemporains dans ce secteur.

TitreApplicationTitle: Vers un continuum de services pour l'AVC, Evaluation des structures, processus et indicateurs de rendement des services de réadaptation
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESSIBILITE; ACCIDENT VASCULAIRE CEREBRAL; AUDIT DE QUALITE; CONTINUUM DE SOINS; MEILLEURES PRATIQUES; ORGANISATION DES SERVICES; READAPTATION
Abstract-Résumé: L'accident vasculaire cerebral (AVC) cause des incapacites dans differents domaines d'activites et souvent une diminution de la qualite de vie. Au Quebec, plus de 12,000 personnes subissent un AVC chaque annee. Ce nombre s'eleve a 50,000 individus au Canada ce qui entraine d'importants couts de systeme. En raison du vieillissement accelere de la population, le nombre d'AVC risquera d'augmenter au cours des annees a venir. La readaptation est un moyen efficace pour reduire les incapacites des personnes avec un AVC. Toutefois, les services de readaptation ont des lacunes au niveau de l'acces aux services et de l'identification des besoins au moment opportun. Afin d'eliminer ces lacunes, le Ministere de la Sante et des Services sociaux (MSSS) veut mettre en place un continuum de services pour cette clientele et encourager l'application des meilleures pratiques. Les objectifs de cette etude sont donc de : a) decrire les services de readaptation; notamment les services de readaptation precoce, les services specialises de readaptation b) decrire la trajectoire actuelle des services selon le niveau de severite de l'AVC, c) mesurer les ecarts entre les services actuels et les pratiques optimales recommandees sur le plan national et d) definir les indicateurs qui serviront a surveiller l'offre et la continuite des services de readaptation. Nous proposons de mener un sondage dans plus de 75 etablissements de sante du Quebec offrant des services de readaptation et de recueillir des donnees cliniques et administratives dans pres de 5000 dossiers patients. Ce projet fournira au MSSS, un ensemble d'informations pertinentes a la mise en place du continuum de services pour l'AVC. Il favorisera un partenariat dynamique entre decideurs, professionnels et chercheurs. Finalement, le projet mettra en lumiere des informations pour le futur systeme d'information clinique et identifiera des bases pour l'amelioration continue des services.

TitreApplicationTitle: Elucidating the Role of Skeletal Muscle SIRT1/PGC-1a Metabolic Axis in Modulating Angiogenesis: Can Vascular Aging be Reversed?
Keywords-MotsClés: ADENOVIRAL TRANSFECTION/CELL CULTURE; AGING; ANGIOGENESIS; ELISA; ISCHEMIA DISEASE; PGC-1A/SIRT1 METABOLISM; QUANTITATIVE REAL-TIME RT-PCR; SKELETAL MUSCLE - HIND LIMB ISCHEMIA MODEL; TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODELS; WESTERN BLOT
Abstract-Résumé: Over the last 50 years, the proportion of the Canadian population over 65 y has nearly tripled, with a concomitant rise in the incidence of aging-associated ischemic diseases that continuously threatens to overwhelm our healthcare system. Investigating mechanisms that may prevent and reverse ischemic diseases to enhance the quality of life and reduce mortality in our elderly population has become a public health priority. Ischemic tissues can create new blood vessels (angiogenesis), in an attempt to recruit more oxygen and nutrients. That response, however, declines profoundly with age resulting in functional impairment, disability, and even amputation in the elderly. What instigates the ischemic disease process remains unclear. We have recently identified, in skeletal muscle, a new genetic program for making new blood vessels that is driven by a protein: PGC-1alpha. PGC-1alpha is a powerful physiological regulator of metabolism uniquely poised as a potential target for aging-associated diseases. The SIRT1 lifespan regulator positively modulates PGC-1alpha, and treatment with naturally occurring SIRT1-activating compounds leads to PGC-1alpha activation in skeletal muscle. Hence, PGC-1alpha provides a novel and powerful link between metabolism, vascular function, and pathways known to be critical in the aging process. Together, the data support the hypothesis that declines in the activity of the SIRT1/PGC-1alpha pathway underlie the profound age-associated loss of angiogenic capacity in skeletal muscle, and that reversal of this process will improve the tolerance to ischemia in the elderly. We aim to critically test this hypothesis using both cell culture systems and genetically modified mouse models. The proposed studies will provide new insight into vascular balance in the elderly, and identify novel therapeutic targets for ischemic diseases of all guises.

TitreApplicationTitle: Country foods and cardiovascular health in Nunavik, northern Quebec:  studying the complex balance between nutrients and environmental contaminants
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES RISK FACTORS; COUNTRY FOODS; ECOSYSTEM APPROACHES TO HEALTH; MARINE MAMMAL CONSUMPTION; MERCURY; NUTRIENT-CONTAMINANT EARLY INTERACTIONS; PARTICIPATORY APPROACHES; SELENIUM; SELENOPROTEINS
Abstract-Résumé: Food insecurity is frequent in Nunavik and the promotion of country foods can improve food quantity and quality in the villages. The Inuit diet is rich in selenium (Se), omega-3 fatty acids (n-3) and other nutrients, but can accumulate environmental contaminants such as mercury (Hg) and other persistent organic pollutants (POPs). Se is an antioxidant involved in several body functions through selenoprotein expression. High dietary Se intake may offsets Hg-toxic effects on health. Recently, high Se has been related to insulin resistance and other cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) risk factors in Europe and the US. To date, diabetes prevalence is low among Inuit and they present an excellent lipids profile. No association between blood Se and diabetes is observed, but recent results show significant associations between blood Se and arthrogenic lipids in young adults. Hg and POPs are risk factor for CVDs, while n-3 is a preventive factor. Several new Se biomarkers (eg. selenoproteins) may help to better characterise Se interactions with contaminants and CVDs and the chemical forms of Se in foods may influence selenoprotein synthesis. A detailed profile of nutrients and contaminants in Nunavik country foods is also lacking. Using data from the Inuit in Transition Study and samples of country foods, the objectives of this study are to (i): measure new Se biomarkers in archived blood samples and examine their interactions with contaminants and CVD risk factors in adults; (ii) measure nutriments, contaminants and Se chemical forms in country foods. Data will be analysed by a combination of advanced laboratory procedures and statistical modelling. This project will improve the understanding of the role of Se interaction with contaminants and CVDs, and help to maximize benefits and minimize risks from country foods in Nunavik. This research is a collaboration between local stakeholders, community members and scientists; results will be returned and discussed with communities.

TitreApplicationTitle: Plasticity and Sensitivity of Renal Cell Carcinoma Cancer Stem Cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BASIC BIOLOGY OF KIDNEY CANCER INITIATION AND PROGRESSION; CANCER STEM CELLS IN KIDNEY CANCER; DEVELOPMENT OF BIOMARKERS FOR PROGNOSIS IN KIDNEY CANCER; DISCOVERY OF RESISTANCE PATTERNS TO VEGFR-TKI; IMPROVING RESPONSE TO TARGETED THERAPY IN KIDNEY CANCER; INDIVIDUALIZING PATIENT THERAPY IN KIDNEY CANCER; TUMOUR HETEROGENEITY IN KIDNEY CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Most patients diagnosed with advanced kidney cancer (renal cell carcinoma; RCC) will die of their cancer. Therapies targeting tumour blood vessels can improve survival, but are toxic and fail patients as the cancer becomes resistant. We now know that not every cancer cell is the same; cancers may be like beehives, with "queen-bee" and worker cancer cells. These queen-bee cancer cells, or "cancer stem cells" (CSCs) may be the cells that spread and resist treatment. CSCs are rare in some cancers, but common in others like melanoma. No-one has properly studied if there are CSCs in RCC. We have grown RCC in mice and in the lab from kidney cancers donated by patients undergoing surgery. We have found that CSCs in RCC are rare, but with two important caveats. First, we have found that RCC from patients are highly dependent on human cell support in the lab. We are testing this in tumours in mice; if true, it implies that the microenvironment around RCC cells could be targeted to stop RCC growth, it establishes a new model to test therapies against RCC and more radically it may challenge the CSC idea itself. Secondly, to count how many cancer cells are needed to form a tumour, we must identify and separate normal cells, like blood vessel cells. We've found that some blood vessel cells in RCC behave like cancer cells in the lab. We are testing to see if the mutations for each patient's cancer are present in their cancer's blood vessel cells. Cancer cells turning into blood vessels would be a revolutionary explanation for the failure of targeted therapies in RCC patients, and has recently been discovered in brain cancer. These ideas have massive impacts for the understanding and treatment of RCC. Our work may lead to treatments blocking signals outside of RCC cells, combining drugs with blood vessel targeted treatments and better selecting treatments for individual patients will improve the lives of people with RCC.

TitreApplicationTitle: Lifetime effects of weight and weight related health conditions on healthy aging and maintenance of autonomy
Keywords-MotsClés: EFFECTS OF OBESITY; FUNCTION AND AUTONOMY; GERIATRIC EPIDEMIOLOGY; HEALTHY AGING
Abstract-Résumé: Currently 4.8 million Canadians are over 65 years of age and by 2026, more than one out of every five Canadians will be over 65.  This represents a major shift in demographics and emphasizes the importance of understanding factors that influence healthy aging and maintenance of independence.  Already more than 2.5 million Canadians over 65 report having more than one chronic health condition.  Of this 2.5 million, half report moderate to severe disability.  The trend towards increasingly heavy body weights in Canada may also impact disability and intensify the problem.  However, studies on the relationship between weight, body composition (amount of muscle and adipose) and disability have largely been confined to one time point and limited measures of function.  As a result, many questions remain about critical periods during lifetime for risk associated with obesity, chronic disease, and the subsequent impact on healthy aging.  Using comprehensive lifetime data on weight, body composition and function from several major population studies comprising over 12,000 older men and women, we propose to determine the impact of health conditions and a lifetime of obesity on function and health outcomes in old age.  Potential novel associations between function, inflammatory markers, genetic markers and telomere length will also be investigated.  It is hypothesized that maintenance of non-obese body weight over the lifetime will be most closely associated with healthy aging (fewer health conditions, lower levels of inflammation, greater function and quality of life).  Although life expectancy in Canada has increased, this has not been equaled by an increase in disability-free life expectancy.  This research will contribute to our understanding of factors which impact upon function and health outcomes in old age and may lead to new approaches to make these later years as healthy and productive as possible.

TitreApplicationTitle: Deciphering the function of Type VI secretion systems in an emerging human pathogen Photorhabdus asymbiotica
Keywords-MotsClés: CHIP-SEQ; PATHOGENESIS; PHOTORHABDUS; REGULATION; RNA-SEQ; SECRETION; T6SS; VIRULENCE
Abstract-Résumé: Bacterial secretion systems play an important role in pathogenesis. The newly identified type VI secretion system (T6SS) has been found in many important human pathogens. Many pathogens possess multiple copies of T6SS clusters. The functions of these T6SS remain largely unknown. Photorhabdus asymbiotica (PA) is an emerging human pathogen that causes infection to soft tissues and bacteremia. The genome of PA contains multiple T6SS clusters. PA is symbiotic in nematodes but pathogenic in insects and humans. This complex interaction of PA with hosts provides an ideal model to study the relative function of multiple T6SS clusters.   This proposed study will generate valuable insight to increase our understanding of this important secretion system.  Given the fact that T6SS has antimicrobial activities and Photorhabdus is pathogenic to insects, this research may lead to development of new treatment strategies, antimicrobial production and insect control to improve public health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Structural and mechanistic characterization of sensor-transducer membrane proteins BlaR1 and MecR1 in environmental sensing and antibiotic resistance in MRSA using cell-free protein expression.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE; BLAR1; CELL-FREE PROTEIN EXPRESSION; ENVIRONMENTAL SENSING; MECR1; METHICILLIN RESTISTANT STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS; NMR SPECTROSCOPY; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; TRANSMEMBRANE PROTEINS; X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY
Abstract-Résumé: Beta-lactam antibiotics are invaluable in the battle against pathogenic bacterial infection. This powerful group of antibiotics acts to destroy the integrity of bacterial cell-walls, leaving bacteria highly vulnerable to cell lysis and death. Certain bacteria nevertheless have developed resistance mechanisms that block beta-lactam action, rendering them useless. A notable example is the "superbug" Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus (MRSA) which is resistant to all classes of beta-lactam antibiotics, including the commonly prescribed penicillins and cephalosporins. Of particular concern is the rapid emergence of "community-acquired" MRSA affecting previously healthy individuals outside the healthcare setting, presenting an urgent world-wide health threat.  The environmental sensing of beta-lactams is key to the antibiotic resistance mechanism of MRSA and is mediated by sensor-transducer proteins BlaR1 and MecR1. Upon detection of beta-lactams in the milieu, these proteins trigger a signaling pathway resulting in the production of enzymes that allow bacteria to both destroy and ignore the antibiotic and avert cell-death. Understanding the structure and function of these beta-lactam sensing proteins would greatly benefit drug design efforts aimed at bacterial re-sensitization to present antibiotics as well as novel antibiotic development. Structural investigation of BlaR1/MecR1 which demands large amounts of protein has been notoriously challenging using conventional cell-based expression. Alternately, here we employ a customized "cell-free" protein synthesis system to allow overexpression of BlaR1/MecR1 for structural studies.  In partnership with the Centre for Drug Research and Discovery at UBC, the acquired structural and mechanistic data will be used to screen and optimize novel lead inhibitors against BlaR1/MecR1 induced antibiotic resistance in the MRSA "superbug".

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of Polycomb-RNA interactions in stem cell pluripotency
Keywords-MotsClés: CHROMATIN; EMBRYONIC STEM CELLS; EPIGENETICS; GENE REGULATION; GENOMICS; HIGH THROUGHPUT SEQUENCING; NON-CODING RNA; PLURIPOTENCY; RNA-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS
Abstract-Résumé: The majority of the cells in the human body share the same DNA sequence, or genome, yet they are able to carry out many distinct functions. This ability of cells to become specialized for particular roles relies on differences in how each cell interprets its genome, including switching certain genes on or off as well as changing the physical packaging of DNA. The factors that control these differences in genome interpretation play important roles in cell growth, cell death and cell fate decisions. This proposal will investigate how such factors work. In particular, I will focus on a class of genome products which, unlike traditional genes, do not result in the production of proteins and are therefore known as 'non-coding' elements. The functions of these non-coding genome products are largely unknown, but they are emerging as key players in disease processes such as tumor growth. This research will provide a better understanding of how cells acquire different fates during normal development and how this process is deregulated in disease. The work will also provide insight into how stem cells are able to develop into different cell types, thus facilitating the development of effective stem cell-based therapies. In addition, by understanding how non-coding genome products are deregulated in human cancers, this work will provide a basis for the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: The thrombin-complement connection:  Gaining new insights into their cooperation in promoting inflammation and thrombosis
Keywords-MotsClés: ARTHRITIS; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; COAGULATION; COMPLEMENT; ENZYMOLOGY; INFLAMMATION; STROKE; THROMBOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: By the year 2050, over 15% of the world's population will be older than 65. The leading cause of illness and death for these individuals will be blood clots (thrombosis).  In fact by that time, over 1 million people in North America annually will suffer from life-threatening thrombosis in their veins.  In addition, many more will have heart attacks and strokes that are due to excess blood clotting in the arteries (atherothrombosis).  There is thus an urgent need to develop new strategies to prevent and/or treat these thrombotic diseases.  In spite of advances in our understanding of why blood clots form, there is still much to learn. Recently, work from Dr. Conway's lab revealed that the blood clotting system interacts very closely with another system in the blood, called the complement system. Together, these two systems appear to amplify each other, possibly increasing the risk of blood clots. If we understand how these systems interact, new treatments or preventative strategies might be developed for diseases associated with excess blood clots.  The goal of this proposal is to increase our understanding of how the complement and coagulation systems interact.  This will be accomplished by using components (proteins) of one system to see how they affect the function of the other system. Using modern biochemical approaches, we will also be able to create sensitive ways of measuring the changes in the activity of each system under different conditions. By these techniques, we expect to find new pathways and new proteins that control complement and coagulation. This information will be valuable in developing new tests to predict the risk of thrombosis and new drugs to prevent or treat thrombosis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Direct conversion of human skin fibroblasts to the lymphoid lineages
Keywords-MotsClés: B CELLS; DIRECT CONVERSION; FIBROBLASTS; LYMPHOPOIESIS; T CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: T and B cells are major constituents of white blood cells and play a key role in fighting infections. However in diseases such as HIV and leukemia, there is a lack of functional T and B cells and these diseases lack robust treatments and require constant monitoring. Current treatments for leukemia involve bone marrow transplant, but the sources of patient-matched bone marrow sources are very limited and usually patients end up requiring multiple bone marrow transplants along with intense chemotherapy. Intense chemotherapy further destroys T and B cells and renders the patient more susceptible to opportunistic infections. Therefore, there is a need to develop novel sources for reconstitution of healthy T and B cells. In this proposal, I aim to develop a novel approach whereby cells from human skin can be induced to directly undergo conversion into T and B lineages. This will offer a method for generating patient specific T and B cells, which are not available from other sources.

TitreApplicationTitle: Salmonella Pathogenesis: Characterization of Bacterial-Mediated Inhibition of Host Trafficking
Keywords-MotsClés: BACTERIAL PATHOGENICITY; BIOCHEMISTRY; CELL IMMUNOLOGY; CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; ENZYMOLOGY; INFECTIOUS DISEASES; MOLECULAR MICROBIOLOGY; PHAGOCYTOSIS; SALMONELLA; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Salmonella is one of the leading causes of food poisoning, responsible for more food-related deaths in Canada than any other bacteria. Found in a wide range of food sources from meat to dairy products to vegetables, it can cause diarrhea, fever, vomiting and abdominal cramping in patients of all ages, although children, the elderly and those with impaired immune systems are particularly susceptible. In recent decades, effective treatment by the healthcare community has been hampered by increases in drug-resistant Salmonella infections and decreases in new antibiotic therapies.  Disease-causing bacteria have evolved unique and diverse strategies to evade the human immune system in order to cause infection. Upon infection, one of the most immediate and aggressive immune responses is to engulf or eat the invading bacteria, trapping them in specialized compartments to be targeted for death. Salmonella is able to evade the human immune system by taking control of these specialized compartments and reproducing within them, although this process is not well understood. This research proposes to study how Salmonella takes control of this process inside our cells. We have recently identified a bacterial factor (toxin) that plays an important role in this process. We plan to study how it interacts with human cells by examining bacteria-human cell interactions microscopically. By watching how this toxin interacts with human cells, we can elucidate its role in the infection process and design more effective ways to stop it from exerting its harmful effects. We will also utilize biochemical and genetic techniques to study these interactions in depth and identify its mechanism of action. Collectively, this work will provide new insights into how Salmonella causes infections, and new methods for developing therapeutic strategies aimed at targeting the infection process. Thus, understanding the infection process is one way that we can ultimately fight infectious diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2): a mechanistic investigation of its role in normal and leukemia stem cells.
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CHROMATIN; HEMATOPOIESIS
Abstract-Résumé: The polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) consists of a number of proteins that together regulate the activity of adult stem cells in our body. In the blood system, their tightly regulated activity is important to ensure the life-long production of blood cells. At the same time, it has become evident that in many blood cancers, the PRC2 genes are frequently mutated, suggesting that defective PRC2 activity can be fundamental in the etiology of hematological malignancies. In this project, I am proposing research to study the role and molecular regulation of key components of the PRC2 complex. My research will expand our understanding on the basic mechanisms involved in PRC2 activity hoping that we can one day use this knowledge to cure, or even prevent, blood disease which are still refractory to currently available therapy.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of the epithelial cell receptor nectin 4 in measles virus pathogenesis and oncolytic therapy
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; CANCER THERAPIES; CELLULAR IMAGING; CELLULAR RECEPTORS; EPITHELIAL CELLS; MEASLES VIRUS; MEMBRANE FUSION; ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES; VIRUS ENTRY; VIRUS-HOST INTERACTIONS
Abstract-Résumé: In unvaccinated individuals measles virus causes an acute respiratory disease that can lead to immune suppression resulting in secondary infections by bacteria or parasites.  Measles viruses used in vaccines are weakened/attenuated by growth in non-human cells.  These weakened strains of measles virus also possess cancer-killing properties and can be used to destroy certain tumours.  This makes measles virus an attractive tool to fight cancer.  We recently showed that that a protein found on the surface of certain human cancer cells of breast, lung, and colon, makes them prone to measles virus attack.  This tumour marker protein is known as poliovirus receptor related protein (PVRL)/Nectin 4.  The localization of PVRL4 in primary differentiated normal human bronchial epithelial cultures and human trachea explants will be characterized to determine whether measles virus can use this receptor to exit the host via the airway.  The molecular mechanism of how measles virus attaches to PVRL4 will also be investigated.  Regions within PVRL4 will be changed to identify potential measles virus binding sites to increase the killing efficiency of measles virus to PVRL4 positive tumours.  Animal models containing PVRL4 positive breast, colon, and lung tumours will be infected with measles virus to determine whether measles virus can replicate in these cancers, while avoiding normal cells, as normal cells typically do not contain PVRL4 on their cell surface.  Collectively, this work will provide new insights into the molecular mechanisms of how measles viruses infect certain tumour cells, and will open the doors for the development of therapeutic interventions aimed at targeting PVRL4 positive tumours.  Thus, understanding the infection process is one way that we can utilize measles virus to fight cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Wnt Pathway as a Modulator of Tolerogenic APCs in MS
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIGEN PRESENTATION; DENDRITIC CELLS; EAE; LYMPHOCYTES; MONOCYTES/MACROPHAGES; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; TOLERANCE; WNT PATHWAY
Abstract-Résumé: Antigen-presenting cells (APCs) account for a significant proportion of the cells found within lesions of multiple sclerosis (MS) and its animal model, experimental allergic encephalomyelitis (EAE). These APCs have the ability to capture myelin debris and to promote either an inflammatory response or either a tolerogenic response from the effector lymphocytes. I intend to understand the molecular mechanisms which govern the switch between these two opposite type of immune responses. This project will focus on the Wnt signalling pathway since previous studies have shown that an activation of this pathway on APCs could lead to a reduced inflammation in the gut. I will first demonstrate that during the remission phase of the disease, APCs of the brain express higher levels of Wnt receptors. Secondly, I will demonstrate that activation of this pathway on APCs leads to an anti-inflammatory profile from the APCs, which induce a tolerogenic response from effector lymphocytes. Finally, I will demonstrate that abrogation of the Wnt pathway on APCs leads to a worst EAE disease. This study aims to demonstrate that manipulation of the Wnt pathway on APCs favors the induction of an anti-inflammatory response, and will help in the development of strategies to design new therapies in the treatment of autoimmune diseases, such as MS.

TitreApplicationTitle: Functional Assessment with Computed Tomographic Coronary Angiography: Comparison with Rubidium-82 Positron Emission Tomography
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY; CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE; CORONARY FLOW RESERVE; MYOCARDIAL PERFUSION IMAGING; POSITRON EMISSION TOMOGRAPHY
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease is the leading cause of illness and death in Canada. Arteries which supply blood to the heart muscle get blocked and clogged leading to heart attack. It is thus essential to have a comprehensive test which maps out the entire blood supply of the heart. We therefore aim to develop and validate a new non-invasive technique that can provide information about the blood supply of the heart muscle. In our project, by using specially designed protocols and software modifications, we will manipulate existing special X-ray technique (computed tomography (CT)  scan) to get this information. The information thus obtained will be validated against another well established technique called positron emission tomography (PET). At present, by using CT scan, we can only evaluate blood supply in larger arteries of the heart. If successful, our technique will be of immense clinical use in patients of heart attack (scheduled for operation) or patients likely to suffer heart attack in future and may also reduce dependence on other techniques which are logistically more challenging.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development and characterization of new antivirals against ebolavirus
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIVIRALS; CLICK CHEMISTRY; EBOLA VIRUS; HEMORRHAGIC FEVER VIRUSES; MASS SPECTROMETRY; SMALL MOLECULE INHIBITORS; VIRAL ENTRY
Abstract-Résumé: Ebolavirus is an enveloped RNA virus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with a lethality rate that can reach up to 90%. The increasing number of ebolavirus outbreaks in endemic regions of Africa and its potential use as a biological warfare agent are alarming. Importantly, there is no available vaccine or effective therapy against this virus, and this is partly due to the poor understanding of the underlying mechanisms of Ebola entry into host cells. We propose to investigate Ebola entry using state-of-the-art technology to screen for cellular factors that play critical roles during infection. The discovery of cellular proteins involved in Ebola entry will help to better understand how the virus initiates infection. Our study will ultimately lead to the development of new antiviral drugs that can help in blocking viral entry and spread, which can have a great impact in the fight against this deadly virus.

TitreApplicationTitle: A systems-level study of the mechanisms leading to RAF dimerization and activation
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOLUMINESCENCE; CANCER THERAPIES; CELLULAR BIOLOGY; FLUORESCENCE; HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PHARMACOLOGY; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS
Abstract-Résumé: Hyperactivation of RAS/ERK signaling is among the key events leading to tumor initiation and progression. Signaling within this pathway requires the proper assembly of three core kinases (RAF, MEK and ERK) that convey incoming signals by the means of a phosphorylation cascade. Of all kinases, RAF (particularly BRAF) is the most frequently mutated in various types of human cancers. Recent work has shown that RAF activation requires the essential homo or heterodimerization of its kinase domain with other RAF paralogs (ARAF, BRAF or CRAF) or with KSR family members (KSR1 or KSR2). The RAF kinase domain dimerization surface was mapped at IRIC by Dr. Marc Therrien and has recently been implicated in adverse and paradoxical effects of RAF inhibitors used in clinical studies. These findings make RAF dimerization a logical target for identification and development of new cancer therapies. We have recently developed a bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (BRET) assay to study RAF family members interactions. We want to use this assay to define the spectrum of RAF/RAF interactions in live human cells in a normal or drug-induced context. We will also determine the impact of upstream (RAS) and downstream (MEK) pathway components as well as ATP-competitive drugs on the formation of RAF dimers. Finally, we will use a highly innovative technology based on single molecule pull-down to determine the stoichiometry and higher-order structure of the RAS/RAF/MEK signaling complexes. We expect that this research program will allow determining what configurations of the RAF/RAF dimer are important for normal and drug-induced cancer signaling. This research program will lead to a better understanding of the mechanism of RAF activation and this will eventually translate into better anti-cancer therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Advancing Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte Therapy for Ovarian Cancer to the Clinic
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CELL-CELL INTERACTIONS; CELLULAR IMMUNOLOGY; IMMUNE REGULATION; IMMUNE SURVEILANCE; IMMUNE THERAPY; IMMUNOLOGICAL TOLERANCE; IMMUNOPATHOLOGY; LYMPHOCTYE BIOLOGY; TUMOUR MICROENVIRONMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Recent advances in our understanding of how the immune system can be manipulated to target cancer cells has opened the door to new therapeutic approaches. There is growing interest in harnessing T cells, a population of white blood cells trained to attack harmful pathogens that also have to capacity to protect our bodies against tumour cell growth, as a cell-based therapy for cancer. This approach involves the isolation of tumour-targeting T cells from a patient followed by subsequent expansion and re-infusion of large numbers of these cells back into the same patients to complement their primary therapeutic regiment. This approach has shown some of the highest clinical response rates for metastatic melanoma, and as such there is intense interest in applying it to other types of cancer. Ovarian cancer is a prime candidate, due to the late stage of diagnosis, high relapse rate, limited therapeutic options and no significant change in the number of cancer-related deaths. However, every cancer is unique in terms of types of immune cells that are present, and the kinds of molecules expressed by these cells. To allow us to predict how best to use this therapy for ovarian cancer patients, I am performing a detailed investigation of ovarian tumours looking closely at immune cells present within the tumour and whether they express molecules that promote or inhibit T cell function. This will allow us to predict which patients would benefit from infusion of tumour-specific T cells or if combination therapies would be required to promote effective T cell-mediated killing of cancer cells. Moreover, I am developing new methods to improve how we expand these tumour-targeting T cells, to generate the most potent anti-tumour response possible. Collectively, these studies will provide necessary information to design a thoughtful clinical trial for the treatment of ovarian cancer and will have applications for a broad range of other cancers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Balance between life and death: the crucial role of caspase regulation during apoptosis and cell differentiation
Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSIS; CANCER; CASPASES; CELL DIFFERENTIATION; CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC; DEGRADOMICS; HUMAN CELL LINES; PROTEIN ENGINEERING; PROTEOLYSIS; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: The ~600 proteases encoded in the human genome are involved in a diverse number of biological processes. Some function as non-specific degradative enzymes associated with protein catabolism, while others function as selective post-translational modifiers, cleaving only a few protein substrates. Apoptosis is an important example of a biological process that is regulated by limited and specific intracellular proteolysis, predominantly carried out by the caspase family of proteases. This genetically programmed and non-inflammatory form of cell death is a central component of homeostasis and tissue turnover. Since chemotherapeutics typically kill cells by induction of apoptosis, this process is also highly relevant from a therapeutic standpoint. Beyond working toward a detailed molecular understanding of the apoptotic process, the broad goals of this work include phenotyping of chemotherapeutics and cancer cell types by the observed patterns of intracellular proteolysis, discovery of caspase substrates that i) may serve as novel targets for chemotherapeutic intervention and ii) that are essential for cell differentiation.

Abstract-Résumé: Fabry disease is an inherited disorder due to a deficiency of an enzyme that breaks down fats in the body. It is a rare disorder - with just over 300 patients identified so far in Canada - that affects many organ systems and results in a reduced life expectancy. As the disease progresses, patients develop heart problems, kidney problems, and strokes in mid-life. Treatment for Fabry disease is mostly directed at lessening symptoms - although enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) has now been developed. Unfortunately, ERT only really shows a benefit in slowing progression of the disease and does not treat the core genetic defect itself. It is also very costly, dependent on availability, and often requires patients to travel biweekly to drug infusion sites. Patients also have to receive this therapy for the rest of their lives with many developing immune reactions against the drug itself.    For many years we have been working to develop gene therapy for Fabry disease. Gene therapy seeks to supplement expression of absent or defective genes with the actual corrective factor. We use viruses to transfer the correct DNA sequence into cells, which then generates the corrective factor in the host. We have tested this therapeutic strategy in a number of pre-clinical models including a new strain of Fabry mice that we generated that can harbor human hematopoietic (blood) cells. TitreApplicationTitle: Chronic childhood vasculitis: Characterizing the individual rare diseases to improve patient outcomes
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMARKERS; DISEASE CLASSIFICATION; GENOMICS; INTEGRATED KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; OUTCOMES; PEDIATRICS; PHARMACOGENOMICS; REGISTRY; SYSTEMS BIOLOGY; VASCULITIS
Abstract-Résumé: Childhood chronic vasculitis describes a group of rare life-threatening diseases that have in common inflammation of blood vessels in vital organs such as kidneys, lungs and brain. Most knowledge about them comes from adult patients. Severe disease requires aggressive life-saving treatments with steroids and some cancer drugs which can themselves cause damage, and increase risks of cancer and bad infections. Thus milder disease needs less toxic drugs. Different classifications and "scoring tools" are used to define the types and severity of vasculitis and to measure damage caused by disease or drugs. These in turn help direct how aggressively to treat a patient and to measure outcome. None of these tools have been assessed in children and the best balance of disease and treatment risks against outcome for children is not known. Although causes of these diseases in children and adults are probably the same, the effects of the disease and the responses (good and bad) to drugs will differ in growing children. Because specialists may see only one new child with any vasculitis each year, obtaining enough information to learn about childhood vasculitis will require massive cooperation. We will use an international web-based registry to which doctors from 50 or more centers can contribute patient data. We will determine the features which help better classify and diagnose children compared to adults. Through the web we will share with contributors, collective information on patients similarly classified and "scored" so that most successful treatments can be identified. Children with vasculitis are less likely to have diseases associated with aging, alcohol and smoking etc., and therefore may be a better group in whom to study the underlying biology of vasculitis. We will use this opportunity and collect spit, blood and tissue from registry patients for laboratory study with an aim to find tests to better classify, define and direct optimal treatment and outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: New emerging team on Autosomal Recessive Spastic Ataxia of Charlevoix-Saguenay (ARSACS): from models to treatment strategies
Keywords-MotsClés: ATAXIA; AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE SPATIQUE ATAXIA OF CHERLEVOIX-SAGUENAY; CHAPERONE; DRUG SCREENING; FRENCH-CANADIAN POPULATION; MITOCHONDRIA; ORPHAN DISEASE; STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY; TRANSGENIC KNOCKOUT MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Autosomal recessive spastic ataxia of Charlevoix-Saguenay (ARSACS) is a progressive neurological disease in which certain types of neurons die and patients thus have problems with balance and coordination. It was originally identified in the Charlevoix and Saguenay regions of Quebec and remains more common in French-Canadians, but is in fact found worldwide. Although in 2000 a Quebec research team identified the gene that is altered in ARSACS, there had been little progress in understanding what actually goes wrong in neurons from patients. The proposed New Emerging Team builds on a four-year collaboration that has demonstrated that the protein made by the ARSACS gene, called sacsin localizes to mitochondria in normal cells. Mitochondria are an important type of organelle found in neurons and in fact all cells, and when the function of sacsin is lost in experimental systems, as occurs in the patients, mitochondrial fail to function properly. This disrupt the development of neurons and they eventually die. We thus hypothesize that as for other major neurodegenerative diseases including Parkinson's and Alzheimer's, ARSACS results from a deficit in mitochondrial function. We will test this hypothesis in a way that ensures that improved knowledge of the biological basis of ARSACS allows us to screen for drugs that reverse the cellular problems seen in the disease. To allow the rapid launch of clinical trials of these drugs, we will develop a Canadian patient registry and validate a scale to measure the severity of the disease. Together the objectives of this New Emerging Team is to shape an integrated research program to uncover treatments for an orphan disease that shares features with both rare and more common neurodegenerative disorders.

Abstract-Résumé: Psychosocial and rehabilitation interventions play an important role in limiting disability and improving health-related quality of life (HRQL) for people with chronic diseases. Such interventions, however, are typically not available for people with rare diseases, largely due to the difficulty in conducting clinical trials with enough participants to confidently draw conclusions in a rare disease context. Scleroderma, or systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare chronic autoimmune connective tissue disease, which manifests itself in the formation of excess connective tissue and thickening of the skin and key internal organs. People with SSc experience significant disability from limitations in physical mobility and hand function, pain, fatigue, depressive symptoms, and body image distress from disfiguring appearance changes. The objectives of the Scleroderma Patient-centered Intervention Network (SPIN), a collaboration of patient organizations, clinicians, and researchers from Canada, the US and Europe are (1) to develop an infrastructure that can be used on an ongoing basis to test accessible, low-cost interventions to reduce disability and improve HRQL; and (2) to work with partner patient organizations to make these interventions available to persons with SSc across Canada. SPIN will use innovative methods to conduct large clinical trials, including the creation of a large, multinational, ongoing cohort of patients who will participate in one or more trials over a number of years. In addition, SPIN will leverage technology (e.g., internet, videos) to deliver interventions, in partnership with Canadian patient organizations. In addition to establishing the SPIN Cohort, SPIN will develop and pilot test 4 psychosocial or rehabilitation interventions that have been prioritized by SPIN investigators and patient partners. SPIN's work will provide a model for developing and testing these kinds of interventions in other rare diseases.

Keywords-MotsClés: BIOETHICS; BLINDNESS; CLINICAL TRIAL; GENE THERAPY; HEALTH POLICY; IMAGING; PRENYLATION; RETINA; RIAK DETERMINATION; TRAFFICKING
Abstract-Résumé: We propose a collaborative, multidisciplinary approach to further our understanding of choroideremia (CHM), a rare eye disorder, and develop a gene therapy protocol for its treatment. CHM is a sex-linked progressive retinal disorder that results in legal blindness in the third decade of life and may result in complete blindness later in life, depriving affected individuals of livelihood and diminishing their quality of life. Currently there is no treatment for this disorder. Gene therapy, shown to be effective in Leber congenital amaurosis, another heritable retinal disease, offers the best opportunity to prevent vision loss in CHM patients. This proposal fits the criteria for an Emerging Team Grant for Rare Diseases, combining both basic and clinical research.  Our University of Alberta team will combine clinical and basic research with experts in human genetics, ophthalmology, clinical trials (MacDonald, Tennant), health policy (Bubela), as well as basic scientists with expertise in cell biology, visual neuroscience and pharmacology (Posse de Chaves and Sauve). Their expertise will assist in the development of health policy in gene therapy and in the exploration of ethical, legal and societal issues that arise from gene therapy initiatives. By providing this research opportunity, a CIHR Emerging Team grant will enable the development of research expertise in ocular gene therapy in Canada, foster the development of a clinical trial targeting a rare genetic disease and encourage synergies of research direction. By undertaking an ocular gene therapy experiment for CHM, our team will help pave the way for others in Canada to consider potential treatments based on gene therapy in the eye.  In a collaborative framework, we plan to work with patients, patient organizations, clinicians and researchers to develop ethical practices and risk communication strategies to ensure the responsible translation of gene therapy for this human eye disorder.
