TitreApplicationTitle: Palliative care on the heart failure care team: mapping patient and provider experiences and expectations
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPLEXITY THEORY; GENRE THEORY; HEALTHCARE TEAM; HEART FAILURE; INTERPROFESSIONAL COLLABORATION; MEDICAL COMMUNICATION; PALLIATIVE CARE; PATIENT-CENTRED; QUALITATIVE METHODS
Abstract-Résumé: Palliative care addresses the physical, emotional and spiritual needs of patients and their families in situations where an advanced disease is going to end a patient's life. In Canada, heart disease is one of the leading causes of death. Although quality palliative care is a right of all Canadians, very few patients with advanced heart failure receive such care. To address this situation, national heart failure care guidelines now recommend that palliative care be provided alongside other medical care for patients with advanced heart failure. However, before such recommendations can become reality, we need to better understand the complex heart failure care team in which they would take place. This team includes patients, family caregivers, specialist doctors, family doctors, nurses, social workers, homecare workers, and others, many spread over different institutions with different roles, resources and routines. Our research asks: In particular patient situations, what expectations and experiences do these team members have of palliative care for advanced heart failure? What factors currently shape their interactions to provide palliative care? We will explore these questions through a qualitative study set in three Canadian centers. We will conduct interviews with patients and members of their care team. We will also collect and analyse documents that guide care activities, including policy documents and local practice documents used in clinics. Our results will add necessary team-centred insights to the recent literature, which focuses on individual knowledge and needs but does not explore how these play out in the complex system of the HF care team. Our results will inform the next phase of our research program: the development, implementation and assessment of a palliative care integration initiative that is responsive and resilient to the team conditions in which HF care is negotiated.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Differential Functions of DGAT Enzymes on Lipid Droplets and in the ER
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL IMAGING; DGAT ENZYMES; ER STRESS; LIPID DROPLET; LIPID METABOLISM; MASS SPECTROMETRY; TG SYNTHESIS
Abstract-Résumé: Many common diseases such as heart disease, obesity and diabetes, are related to the over storage of fat. However, fat is not necessarily bad under normal conditions. On the contrary, it serves as important energy source for our body. Normally fat is stored at a special location in the cell, called lipid droplets, similar to a bag of fat. Fat stored in lipid droplets is considered biologically inert and does not interfere with normal cell functions. However, the building blocks of fat, known as fatty acids, are toxic to cells and needs to be converted to fat and stored in lipid droplets to keep cells from harmful effects. When the mechanism controlling the conversion from fatty acids to fat is overwhelmed, fatty acids will spillover which causes cell damage. As the activity for such a conversion takes place in more than one location in the cell, including lipid droplets and elsewhere, an unanswered question in the fielded is which of the localizations is important for protecting cells from the toxic effects of fatty acids. We hypothesize that lipid droplets play an important role by converting fatty acids to fat locally on lipids droplets and by separating the conversion burden from other important cell functions, thus efficiently prevent fatty acids from spillover. We will test this hypothesis and determine the mechanism by which this separation is achieved. Our work will enhance our understanding to the cause of common diseases at cellular level and help to develop therapeutic approaches to prevent toxic consequences of fat accumulation during disease development.

TitreApplicationTitle: A population-based outcome and economic evaluation of interventions for gastric cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: COST COMPARISON ANALYSIS; ECONOMIC ANALYSIS; OUTCOMES; STOMACH CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Stomach cancer is the second leading cause of death from cancer worldwide. In Canada, there were 7 new patients/100,000 people in 2011. The 5-year survival is only 24%, making stomach cancer a leading cause of cancer-related death. Doctors caring for patients with stomach cancer make many treatment decisions, such as what chemotherapy (cancer fighting drugs) should be used, the best surgical approach (open or laparoscopic "key-hole" surgery), and if radiation might help. Although doctors make these recommendations based on the best evidence available, this evidence is incomplete since competing alternatives have not been directly compared to each other. Treatment costs and the quality of life for patients on these treatments also have not been studied. We will study 1300 patients in Ontario who received different treatments for stomach cancer to determine the results of these treatments (whether a patient's life was prolonged), treatment costs, and quality of life of the treated patients. Details about each patient and their cancer will have been gathered during a primary chart review, and will be linked to physician and hospital billing data. Treatment costs will be determined by interviews, review of published studies, and Ontario physician billing schedules. To get an idea of quality of life and out-of pocket costs, 140 patients will be given questionnaires. Cost, quality of life, and survival time will be combined to show the cost per life year gained by a treatment. The results of this study will help doctors decide which treatments achieve the best results. If two treatments have similar results, doctors could use the less expensive treatment. Doctors will also be interviewed to help determine what will help increase adoption of our recommendations.  Our findings will be presented at international forums and will be published in a medical journal. We will also work with Cancer Care Ontario, to make sure doctors treating cancer patients have this information.

TitreApplicationTitle: Oxidative damage and compromised neuronal integrity in bipolar disorder
Keywords-MotsClés: BIPOLAR DISORDER; MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION; OXIDATIVE STRESS; POSTMORTEM BRAIN STUDIES
Abstract-Résumé: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a major public health problem associated with significant functional impairment for many patients. The complete pathophysiology of this disorder remains under investigation, limiting the progress in the development of novel therapeutic strategies. There are, however, robust data supporting the increased activity of the dopaminergic system during mania, which is one of the key features of BD. In fact, antipsychotics have long been shown to exert their effects through the blockage of dopaminergic signalling, which has an important behavioral role in decreasing manic symptoms patients with BD. More recently, another interesting molecular pathway that has been consistently reported in BD is decreased mitochondrial function and increased oxidative stress, which can impair cell function. Interestingly, dopamine, its metabolites, and the proteins involved in the regulation of synaptic dopamine levels have been shown to be greatly vulnerable to oxidative stress. Although the relation between dopamine and oxidative stress has been shown to be critical in a number of neurological diseases, it has yet to be carefully examined in BD. Therefore, this proposal we will further investigate mitochondrial function and oxidative damage in brain tissue from patients with BD, focusing on the intracellular targets of oxidative stress at a subcellular level i.e. mitochondria, synapses, and study their relation to the dopaminergic system. We are particularly interested in how these changes can compromise neuronal function and thus be relevant to the manifestations of BD. Ultimately this project will allow us to identify potential biomarkers for BD and to elucidate more fully pathophysiological mechanisms that could lead to the development of novel therapeutic interventions for BD and consequently better patient care and outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Treatment with Ginseng as an Effective Cardiac Antihypertrophic and Antiremodelling Strategy
Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSIS; CARDIAC HYPERTROPHY; GINSENG; HEART FAILURE; MITOCHONDRIA
Abstract-Résumé: Although used in Asian societies for thousands of years, the use of ginseng as an herbal medication for a variety of disorders has increased tremendously worldwide in recent years. Although many beneficial cardiovascular effects have been attributed to ginseng there are very few if any detailed in-depth studies aimed at determining how ginseng works.  We have shown that ginseng can effectively reduce the severity of heart failure and, remarkably, can reverse heart failure after it has already been established.  Here, we propose to carry out detailed studies to determine how ginseng works and whether it can interact favourably with established heart failure medication.  This will be done using multifaceted experimental approaches encompassing both in vitro and in vivo models of heart failure and excessive cardiac growth,  termed hypertrophy.  It is hoped that these studies will reveal beneficial effects of this traditional medication for the treatment of heart failure, especially in combination with existing therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Signaling Events Regulating Local Neuronal Degeneration Events
Keywords-MotsClés: CASPASE; CHEMOTHERAPY; DEGENERATION; HTRA2; IKK EPSILON; INHIBITORS OF APOPTOSIS; NEURON; NEUROPATHY; SMAC; TRANSGENIC
Abstract-Résumé: Neurons have complex architectures that change with time. Most neurons initially produce extensive and elaborate processes that are subsequently pruned so that only those that are used to mediate neuron-neuron communication, and thus form part of a neuronal network, are retained. After injury, damaged neuronal processes can be removed, through activation of these same pruning mechanisms.   My lab studies the intracellular cascades that regulate cellular life and death decisions. Our cells have the capacity to activate an intrinsic suicide program and this plays a crucial role in sculpting tissues during development and in maintaining homeostasis in the adult. This suicide program can have dire consequences if it is not tightly controlled and therefore cells use a variety of overlapping mechanisms to regulate this process.   Recent findings have shown that the core cellular machinery that drives cell suicide is also used to selectively prune processes in the nervous system. Thus, the same pathways that drive cellular lethality can be used to regulate sub-lethal events in the nervous system. The goal of this proposal is to understand precisely how this program is controlled  - we want to understand how the neuron activates the program that drives neuronal pruning and, at the same time, restrains it so it sculpts the neuron but does not kill it.   This research program will identify fundamental conserved mechanisms that allow neurons to remove some of their processes while retaining others, while keeping the neuron itself alive. This work may have translational implications since emerging evidence indicates that inappropriate re-activation of the sculpting program is an early pathogenic event in neurodegenerative disease. Gaining new insights into the fundamental signaling and regulatory mechanisms that regulate neurite destruction may reveal therapeutic opportunities to slow neurodegenerative disorders.

Keywords-MotsClés: BDNF; DOPAMINE; MATERNAL BEHAVIOUR; MOTIVATION; OXYTOCIN
Abstract-Résumé: Health is defined by the ability to both sustain emotional well-being and meet the metabolic and psychological demands of life. The gap in our knowledge is that of understanding the neural systems that operate to sustain positive affect in the face of challenge.  We propose a novel approach to the study of neurobiological systems associated with affective disorders.  We focus on brain systems that mediate positive emotional states over the course of pregnancy and lactation in female rats.  Such events are indeed challenging, metabolically as well as psychological, as evidenced by the high rate of clinical depression that accompanies pregnancy and childbirth.  Of course the same events can also lead to very positive emotional states.  Indeed, reproduction in human females associates with profound changes in affective states, with astounding individual differences. We suggest that an understanding of the mechanisms that mediate such variation in affective states over the course of reproductive life provides a naturalistic model for the studies of the neurobiology of emotional health, and one with direct consequences for human emotional well-being.

Abstract-Résumé: Ionizing radiation (IR) is used extensively in the treatment of many forms of cancer. It acts by inducing lethal DNA damage, in particular a form called a DNA double strand break or DSB. The major pathway for the repair of IR-induced DSBs in human cells is called non-homologous end-joining  or NHEJ. We have identified IR-induced modifications of two of the key proteins in NHEJ: XRCC4 and PNKP. This grant explains how we will characterize these modifications to understand how they regulate how cells repair IR-induced DSBs. This work will help us to understand the basic processes by which cells detect and repair IR-induced DNA damage and could lead to better treatments for cancer patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Visceral fat and hypertension: towards sex-specific lipidomic biomarkers
Keywords-MotsClés: LIPIDOMICS; OBESITY-INDUCED HYPERTENSION; SEX DIFFERENCES; SYMPATHETIC VASOMOTOR TONE; VISCERAL FAT
Abstract-Résumé: Having too much body fat increases the risk of developing high blood pressure (hypertension). In Canada, the number of patients with hypertension has increased dramatically in recent years (by 60% between 1995 and 2005). This trend has been attributed to growing rates of obesity. But the relationship between obesity and hypertension is not absolute: (1) only 1 in 2 obese individuals develops hypertension, and (2) some individuals who have an excessive amount of intra-abdominal (visceral) fat but are not "classically obese" (have normal body weight and waist size) do develop the disease. Adipose tissue releases molecules, such as lipids, that can increase blood pressure by acting on the nervous system. Some types of fat, such as visceral fat, may release more of such molecules and, therefore, may increase blood pressure much more. Thus, individuals who accumulate fat viscerally are at higher risk of hypertension. Currently, we are unable to identify (with a simple test) viscerally obese individuals who are at the highest risk of developing the disease so that they can be offered timely interventions and secondary preventions. Our main aim is to identify circulating lipids as novel biomarkers of the risk for developing hypertension due to visceral obesity. We propose to conduct a comprehensive assessment of circulating lipids with a state-of-the-art lipidomics approach (examining over 700 circulating lipid species) in 1020 adolescents and 900 adults. We will relate these lipidomic profiles to the measurements of visceral fat obtained with body scans and to blood pressure recorded continuously with a special device during an hour-long cardiovascular protocol. The adolescents and adults will be studied in a family-based manner. The use of this transgenerational (adolescent-parent) approach will help us identify mechanistic pathways enhancing or diminishing disease trajectories that emerge in adolescence and become established in adulthood.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dynamic interactions of the type IV secretion system assembly factor VirB8
Keywords-MotsClés: BACTERIAL VIRULENCE; BIOCHEMISTRY; MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY; MOLECULAR DOCKING; NOVEL ALTERNATIVE TO ANTIBIOTICS; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; SECRETION SYSTEMS; SMALL-MOLECULE INHIBITORS; STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY; STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP PROGRAM
Abstract-Résumé: All pathogenic bacteria need weapons to defend themselves against the immune system in order to thrive in the human body. Among those weapons the secretion systems are especially important since they transfer toxins and other virulence factors into human cells. We study a special secretion system from pathogenic bacteria, the type IV secretion system, which erects structures on the surface of bacteria that engage in toxin transfer into the host. In the absence of the secretion system, the bacteria do not cause disease, because they can not defend themselves against the immune system. The aim of this project is to analyze and understand the molecular details of the interactions of the type IV secretion system component VirB8, which is an Achilles heel of the secretion system. Once we understand these interactions we will be able to block the function of VirB8 and thereby block the secretion system and bacterial pathogenicity. This approach could lead to the development of novel anti-microbial drugs against bacterial pathogens and in our preliminary work we have already identified interesting candidate molecules.

TitreApplicationTitle: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Live Attenuated Vaccine versus Trivalent Inactivated Vaccine in Hutterite Children
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL TRIAL; INFLUENZA; RESPIRATORY ILLNESS; VACCINE
Abstract-Résumé: Influenza epidemics continue to pose an important threat to the health of persons over the age of 65 years, as well as to persons with cardiopulmonary and other high risk conditions. Healthy children are felt to be an important source for community transmission of influenza. Immunizing school-aged children has been proposed as one strategy to protect high risk individuals; by immunizing children spread of influenza is prevented and persons at high risk for complications are protected. There is uncertainty however about whether a live attenuated vaccine (LAIV) offers additional benefit over inactivated trivalent influenza vaccine (TIV) in providing indirect benefit to those who are unvaccinated through herd immunity. The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to determine whether immunizing children in Hutterite colonies with LAIV can provide increased community-wide protection over TIV.

Keywords-MotsClés: ETHNICITY; HEALTH DISPARITIES; HEALTH SERVICES; IMMIGRATION; INFANT MORTALITY; MATERNAL MORTALITY; SERIOUS NEONATAL MORBIDITY; SEVERE MATERNAL MORBIDITY; VULNERABLE POPULATIONS
Abstract-Résumé: Immigrants are an important part of the fabric of Canada. More than half of the 225,000 newcomers to Canada each year choose Ontario as their destination. Immigrant women comprise 25% of the approximately 380,000 live births in Canada each year; in Ontario, they represent 37% of all births. Canada increasingly receives immigrants from world regions (e.g., India, Sub-Saharan Africa) where maternal illness and mortality may be up to 100 times higher than that in Canada. However, little is known about how serious illnesses in the perinatal period affect immigrant mothers to Canada and their offspring. We will study 1.35 million deliveries in Ontario in the past decade to identify those immigrant groups at highest risk of severe maternal and newborn baby illness and mortality. The approximately 400,000 immigrants that we will study will be differentiated from Canadian-born women, and further compared on indicators of their immigration status (i.e., country of origin, time since immigration and refugee status). We have the research capacity and partnerships to help Canadian healthcare providers and policy makers optimally identify those immigrant mothers (and their infants) who can benefit from focused, and, perhaps, language-specific and culturally attuned care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Usefulness of Computed Tomography and Cardiac Biomarkers in Risk Stratification of Aortic Stenosis
Keywords-MotsClés: AORTIC STENOSIS; CARDIAC BIOMARKERS; COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY; DIAGNOSIS; DOPPLER-ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY; MULTIMODALITY IMAGING; PROGNOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of death in Canadian population. Aortic Stenosis is the third common cardiovascular disease after coronary artery disease and hypertension, making it the most frequent valvular disease in North America. Aortic Stenosis occurs when the heart's aortic valve narrows. This narrowing prevents the valve from opening fully, which obstructs blood flow from the heart into the aorta and onward to the rest of the body. When the aortic valve is obstructed, the heart needs to work harder to pump blood to the body. Eventually, this extra work limits the amount of blood it can pump and may weaken the heart muscle. If Aortic Stenosis is severe, the patient will usually need surgery to replace the valve. Left untreated, Aortic Stenosis can lead to serious heart problems and death. Doppler-echocardiography is the method of choice to assess the severity of valvular obstruction and the cardiac function in patients with Aortic Stenosis and decide when surgery is needed. But about 30% of the patients can't be well evaluated by Doppler-echocardiography and may be misdiagnosed and thus do not receive the appropriate therapies which would result in a poor outcome. The first objective of this prospective multicenter study is to develop and validate new indices to improve diagnostic and decision making in patients with Aortic Stenosis. We believe that other diagnosis exams, as computed tomography and analysis of cardiac hormone, may contribute to assess Aortic Stenosis severity and myocardial impairment and thus improve the risk stratification and outcome in Aortic Stenosis patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: A randomized controlled trial of an online support group for sexual distress due to gynecologic cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: BODY IMAGE; DEPRESSION; GYNECOLOGIC CANCER; ONLINE SUPPORT GROUP; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; RELATIONSHIP SATISFACTION; SEXUAL DISTRESS; SEXUAL FUNCTION
Abstract-Résumé: When a woman has been diagnosed and treated for gynecologic cancer, she may feel distressed about her body and about herself as a sexual being. Because sexuality is such a personal and sensitive issue, she may feel uncomfortable talking to her doctor, her partner, or others in her life about it. Dr. Classen and her colleagues have developed an online support group that is run by professionals and is designed to give women useful information as well as a place where they can talk openly about their concerns. This web-based support group, "GyneGals," uses a bulletin board format, which means that women can go onto the website at any time of the day or night to participate. The program is 12 weeks long and each week the moderator introduces a new topic for discussion and provides a link to information on that topic. The preliminary research on GyneGals suggests that women are interested and willing to participate in such a group. In this next phase of research the aim is to demonstrate that this online support group is effective in reducing sexual distress. The research team plans to recruit 480 women over four years from Ontario, British Columbia, Alberta and the state of New York. Women must be disease free for at least three months and no longer than five years from the date of diagnoses. Participants will either receive the online intervention or online educational materials. There will be up to 20 women in each group. Dr. Classen and her team hope to show that giving gynecologic cancer patients the opportunity to talk about these sensitive and highly personal topics in an online group that is secure, private and safe, will lead to less distress and greater satisfaction. This group might be especially beneficial for women who desire anonymity or who do not have easy access to support.

Abstract-Résumé: Pathways controlling POMC cell function and transcription  La glande hypophysaire est le chef d'orchestre du systeme endocrinien et l'une de ses fonctions importantes consiste a diriger la reponse systemique au stress. Ce relais est assure par l'action neuroendocrine de l'hormone hypothalamique CRH qui integre les influx nerveux alors que les cytokines du type IL6 assurent le lien avec l'etat du systeme immunitaire. Dans l'hypophyse, ces signaux sont integres au niveau de la transcription du gene de la proopiomelanocortine (POMC) et nous etudions les mecanismes moleculaires de cette integration, ainsi que la retroaction negative exercee par les glucocorticoides surrenaliens dont la synthese depend de l'hormone ACTH produite a partir de la POMC.  Etant donne le role des hormones qui derivent de la POMC dans la reponse au stress, l'activite metabolique, l'activite du systeme immunitaire et le comportement, il n'est pas surprenant que ce systeme soit perturbe dans des situations de stress chroniques ou meme lors de la depression chez l'homme. Des lors, il est essentiel de comprendre comment s'exerce le controle de la POMC pour mieux traiter les consequences pathologiques reliees au stress ou a la depression.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mitochondria as Mediators of Metabolic and Neuro-Endocrine Stresses on the Epigenome
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; APOPTOSIS; BIOENERGETICS; METABOLIC HEALTH; METABOLIC STRESS; MITOCHONDRIA; MTDNA; NEUROHORMONAL STRESS; PHYSIOLOGY; REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES
Abstract-Résumé: Mitochondria are the parts of the cell that transform the nutrients that we ingest into cellular energy. Because of their central role in cell life, mitochondria are sensitive to both metabolic and neuro-hormonal stressors, and produce important signals for the cell to adapt to changing environmental conditions. A major process by which cells adapt to environmental condition is through the epigenome, which consist in modifications of the DNA that determine weather certain genes can be expressed or not. This is important because alterations of the epigenome have recently been linked to aging and implicated in the etiology metabolic diseases. However, we do know what mechanisms control epigenetic marks in human cells. This prevents us from designing effective strategies that could help maintain a healthy epigenome and thus keep organs healthy through aging. The goal of this research proposal is therefore to determine whether mitochondria mediate the deleterious effects of metabolic and neuro-endocrine stresses on the epigenome. This will be achieved using state of the art technologies and integrative research strategies to explore this questions at multiple levels of analysis, from the molecular to the physiological level. This new knowledge will help us to determine if mitochondria are a potential therapeutic target for which specific interventions could be designed to extend healthy lifespan and prevent the occurrence of age-related metabolic diseases in Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Prenatal and early postnatal environmental effects on the development of DNA methylation: A monozygotic twin study
Keywords-MotsClés: ENVIRONMENT; EPIGENETICS; HEALTH; INFANCY; PARENTS; PREGNANCY
Abstract-Résumé: The aim of this research is to study prenatal and early postnatal environmental effects on gene expression while controlling for genetic inheritance. We have two central hypotheses. First, the early human environment leaves its mark on gene programming, thus changing the program of expression of genes critical for health development through altering the way genes are marked by a chemical coating of DNA termed DNA methylation. Second, responses to early life environment are system wide adaptations that can be observed in the brain as is expected, but also in peripheral tissues such as cells found in saliva. In order to test these hypotheses it is critical to distinguish between differences in DNA methylation driven by inherited genetic variance and those that are consequences of the environment. To achieve this aim we will study twins that inherit the same genes (monozygotic), but often have different prenatal environments, as evidenced by differences in birth weight shown to predict health differences later in life. Cotton swabs will be used to collect buccal epithelial cells from the children at 1 and 12 months after birth for comprehensive DNA methylation mapping. The changes in DNA methylation will be associated with discordance in birth weight and environmental characteristics assessed between 1 and 12 months after birth. Results from this study will provide crucial data on the early gene-environment interactions which may be associated with long term health development. Moreover, DNA methylation profiles from buccal epithelial cells during infancy may serve as non invasive diagnostic biomarkers for identifying children at risk of health problems.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of Core Competences for Advanced Surgical Practice: Understanding Surgical Judgment and Decision Making during Challenging Surgical Situations
Keywords-MotsClés: DECISION MAKING; JUDGMENT; QUALITATIVE RESEARCH; SURGERY; TRAINING
Abstract-Résumé: The concept of "expert judgement" is highly valued and highly influential in medical education. However, in reality the concept of expert judgement is poorly operationalized, especially once we get beyond the domain of routine and technical skills. We have little systematic evidence about what expert judgement looks like in non-routine situations in medicine, even though this is what is expected to be evaluated during high stakes assessments. Oral examinations are used to assess candidates' clinical judgement; but we need to recognize that an oral examination is a tool with limitations. For example, it is extremely difficult to evaluate intraoperative judgement and decision making in a purely verbal encounter. Our research will operationalize the features of expert decision making in the specific context of experts facing difficult or challenging situations.  We will start exploring this phenomenon in surgery with future work to elaborate a model of expert decision-making in nonroutine situations that is transferrable across clinical situations. This research will produce a model of the features of expert judgement and decision-making that can inform the design of curricula to train these skills and assessment tools to track their development.

TitreApplicationTitle: The molecular basis of cardiac muscle development
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIAC MUSCLE MATURATION; CARDIOMYOGENESIS; GENE EXPRESSION; SIGNALING PATHWAYS; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease and dysfunction can lead to the death of heart muscle cells, termed cardiomyocytes, resulting in the loss of cardiac muscle function.  A method to replace damaged muscle cells using cell therapy would be greatly beneficial for the restoration of heart muscle function.  Human embryonic stem (ES) cells have shown some promise as a source of cardiomyocytes for cell therapy.  One drawback of ES cell work is that these cells can form any cell type in the body.  Thus directing the differentiation into one cell type has been a challenge.  While protocols have been developed to induce ES cell differentiation into cultures containing 40-80% cardiomyocytes, the procedure is variable and the cardiomyocytes are a mixture of working myocardium (from the atrial or ventricles) and pacemaker cells (from the conduction system that generate the heart beat).  To increase our ability of using ES cells for cell therapy, a detailed understanding is required of the molecular pathways that drive an embryonic stem cell to differentiate and mature into cardiac muscle.   The overall goal of this grant is to enhance our understanding of the molecular events that regulate cardiomyogenesis with an ultimate goal of using this knowledge to develop cell therapy methods to repair damaged heart muscle.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the mechanisms of lung cancer development in never smokers
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL MODELS; DNA METHYLATION; GENE EXPRESSION; GENES; GENOME PROFILE; LUNG CANCER; MOUSE MODELS; MUTATIONS; NEVER SMOKERS; PATHWAYS
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is a common cause of cancer  deaths in non-smoking individuals worldwide. However, since lung cancer is primarily viewed as a smoker¹s disease, the risk of non-smokers developing lung cancer is often overlooked, leading to delays in diagnosis and treatment. We propose that lung cancer in non-smokers develops through mechanisms different from those induced by tobacco carcinogens. The goal of our study is to determine the mutations and genes involved in the development of lung cancer specifically in non-smokers, in order to identify genes and pathways that are specifically disrupted in non-smoker tumours. By discovering causal events and key functions disrupted during cancer development in non-smokers, we will identify targets for developing diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for lung cancer in non-smokers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms of limb specification
Keywords-MotsClés: HOMEOBOX GENES; KNOCKOUT MICE; LIMB DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Nous acceptons d'emblee que les jambes et les bras soient differents. Mais pourquoi le sont-ils ?  Au meme titre, nous reconnaissons des similarites de structures au niveau de ces membres: deja Darwin reconnaissait cette similitude en comparant les membres de differentes especes.  Ce projet de recherche porte sur le mecanisme moleculaire qui dicte la difference entre les jambes et les bras. En effet, notre groupe a clone il y a une dizaine d'annees le gene Pitx1 qui est le determinant principal du programme genetique des membres posterieurs. D'autres ont identifie le gene Tbx4 pour son implication dans le meme processus et l'expression de Tbx4 est sous controle de Pitx1. Les deux genes contribuent a l'identite des structures (os et muscle) ainsi qu'au controle de la croissance des bourgeons qui prefigurent les membres.  Par des manipulations genetiques chez la souris, nous avons demontre au cours de la derniere periode de financement, que la plupart des caracteristiques des membres posterieurs sont directement controles par Tbx4 et une activite repressive qui est unique a Tbx4; nous avons aussi identifie un domaine activateur partage par Tbx4 et son homologue des membres anterieurs, Tbx5, qui contribue au controle de la croissance dans les deux membres. Le present projet investiguera les mecanismes moleculaires responsables de ces activites divergentes et identifiera par des methodes genomiques developpementales appliquees a l'ensemble du genome les reseaux de regulation genetique qui expliquent la difference entre bras et jambes. Des mutations du gene Tbx4 ont ete associees a des malformations du genou et du pied mais nous connaissons tres peu les mecanismes/genes qui constituent le programme genetique de l'identite des membres. Les travaux proposes identifieront des genes responsables de malformations congenitales des membres : cela permettra de mieux comprendre les origines de ces malformations et d'en faire un diagnostic et une prevention moleculaires.

TitreApplicationTitle: Integration of human herpesvirus type 6 into chromosomes: Mechanisms and consequences.
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD; CHROMOSOME INTEGRATION; CORD BLOOD BANK; HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL; HERPESVIRUS 6; INFECTION; TELOMERES; TRANSPLANTATION; VIRUS
Abstract-Résumé: Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) is avery common pathogen that infects children.  However, this virus is unique among herpesviruses by its ability to insert is genetic material into human chromosomes. Epidemiological studies indicate 1% of of the world population (approximately 70 million individuals) carry a copy of integrated HHV-6 in every cell of their body.  The virus does not insert itself at random. It selects the ends of chromosomes, a region we call telomeres. Telomeres play an important role on the long-term renewal capacity of cells, i.e. their ability to divide. Defects in telomeres are linked to many different diseases, ranging form heart disease to cancer. Although the study of HHV-6 integration is still in its infancy, studies show that the risk factor for disease is 2.3x greater if you have integrated HHV-6.   The biggest handicap we face in our quest for understanding the biology of integrated HHV-6 is the lack of usable biological material and the low number of cases studied so far.   Consequently, our first objective if to generate a repository of biological specimens from individuals with integrated HHV-6.  To do this, we will screen blood donors in collaboration with the help of Hema-Quebec. Once we have those specimens we will study the effect of integration of cells.  We will also look at the mechanisms by which this virus integrates the chromosome.  Lastly, we will try to identify diseases that are linked with viral integration.  To do this, we will use an existing CARTaGENE bio bank, that contains contains in-depth information on over 20 000 individuals, including sociodemographic, life-style and health data and familial history of disease, 190 physiological parameters, biochemical analyses and haematological analyses.We anticipate finding ~200 individuals with integrated virus whose medical records will be compared to control subjects.

TitreApplicationTitle: Pilot KT intervention to address gender differences in access to post arrest care
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOPULMONARY RESUSCITATION; GENDER; HEART ARREST; KT INTERVENTION; OUT-OF-HOSPITAL CARDIAC ARREST; POST ARREST CARE; SURVIVAL TO HOSPITAL DISCHARGE; WOMEN
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease is the most common cause of death in Canada. Forty thousand Canadians experience cardiac arrest each year. Thirty-three per cent of these are women. Women have a greater chance of surviving cardiac arrest long enough to reach the hospital. However, they have less chance than men do of surviving the event. Research suggests that a reason for this may be that women receive different treatment for cardiac arrest in the hospital. Gender may often influence the way people are cared for after a cardiac arrest. This may contribute to unfavourable outcomes in women and affect how guidelines are applied, gaps in knowledge, and the attitudes and behaviours of caregivers. This study will identify potential barriers to post arrest care that patients experience. We will also develop a pilot knowledge translation (KT) intervention to address these. The objective of the KT intervention is to help doctors and nurses to provide best medical care to patients suffering cardiac arrest, especially women. The KT intervention will be take place in six hospitals. Three hospitals are connected to universities and have specialized heart centres. The other three are community hospitals with no specialized heart centres. The KT intervention will use knowledge sharing activities and techniques, such as research networks, social networking tools and other communication and education activities. We will evaluate the KT tools that we use in the project. We will also develop a KT strategy that fits with our network of experts and local champions. This will help us to improve the tools and also improve access to care for Canadian women who suffer cardiac arrests.We believe that our qualitative study will make clearer why gender bias is a problem in knowledge transfer in post arrest care. The pilot KT intervention will help us address this inequality. It will generate new, gender sensitive knowledge, improve knowledge in post arrest care and the care of all cardiac arrest patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Function of Neurogenesis During Stroke Recovery
Keywords-MotsClés: ADULT NEUROGENESIS; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; HIPPOCAMPUS; MCAO; PHOTOTHOMBOSIS; RODENT BEHAVIOR; SENSORIMOTOR CORTEX; STROKE; SUBVENTRICULAR ZONE; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: For nearly 300,000 Canadians who currently are living with the after effects of stroke, there are no treatments that can reverse the massive and progressive loss of cells called neurons in the brain that cause severe motor and cognitive deficits.  Historically, scientists believed that the adult human brain could not make new neurons suggesting that if we wanted to make new neurons we would have to transplant them into the brain. But within the last 10 years there has been new hope for future treatments that will replace the lost neurons with new cells that are developed within the adult brain.  This hope arose since scientists discovered that the adult brain makes new neurons through the process of neurogenesis in many species, including humans.  Remarkably, following a stroke new dividing cells in the brain go to the site of the injury produced by the stroke, suggesting that the brain might be trying to repair itself.  This suggests that enhancing neurogenesis could aid in recovery.  However, it is still unknown what role the dividing cells and new neurons have during stroke recovery.  The objective of this work is to determine the function of the new cells in the adult brain and determine if they enhance recovery.  By using a variety of mouse models we have created, we can specifically remove the new cells, or alternatively, increase the number of new cells in the adult brain, and determine how this affects mouse behavior after a stroke.  We will also determine if the new neurons that develop at the site of injury after stroke can generate electrical signals with the surrounding resident cells, and thus determine whether these new neurons are functioning correctly.   The results from these experiments will provide us with important insights into the role of the new neurons in the adult brain during stroke recovery, a finding which will be essential for harnessing the potential of these new neurons in treatments designed to aid in stroke recovery.

TitreApplicationTitle: Enhancing Participation In the Community by improving Wheelchair Skills (EPIC WheelS): A Feasibility Study
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; HOME INTERVENTION; MANUAL WHEELCHAIR; REHABILITATION; TABLET
Abstract-Résumé: For Canadians over the age of 65, difficulty walking is the most common barrier to independent living. Restricted mobility can lead to loss of social connections, isolation, and reduced quality of life. For over 80,000 elderly Canadian, a wheelchair offers the potential for continued participation in important activities at home and in the community. Unfortunately, most older adults receive little, if any, training in how to use their wheelchair effectively. Many stop participating in activities because the demands of dealing with carpet, ramps, curbs, sidewalks and longer distances is too much for them or their caregiver. This is a costly problem, both socially and financially. Specific wheelchair training programs have proven to be effective but, until now, rely on numerous 1:1 appointments with a skilled clinician, which is expensive and inconvenient. Enhancing Participation In the Community by improving Wheelchair Skills (EPIC WheelS) is a training program specifically designed for older adults. An expert trainer conducts 2 training sessions and individualizes and monitors a home program. A portable computer tablet provides instruction, demonstrations, interactive training activities, and on-line communication with the trainer. Participants can learn and practice at their own pace at home or in community venues. This study investigates the potential for using EPIC WheelS with older adults in Vancouver and Winnipeg, shortly after they first obtain a wheelchair. Once we confirm EPIC WheelS can be delivered effectively and improves older adults' wheelchair mobility skills, broader studies can be conducted including a national clinical trial with older adults and distance-training programs for people living in rural and remote communities. EPIC WheelS offers promise for improving participation and quality of life for older adults, reducing caregiver burden, and providing much needed rehabilitation services without undue cost or burden on the health care system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular mechanisms regulating the myotubularin-related 2 lipid phosphatase mutated in the neuromuscular disorder Charcot-Marie Tooth disease
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOLOGICAL MASS SPECTROMETRY; CHARCOT-MARIE TOOTH DISEASE; MYOTUBULARIN-RELATED PHOSPHATASES; PHOSPHOINOSITOL PROTEOMICS; REGULATION OF MTMS BY PHOSPHORYLATION; REGULATORY KINASES
Abstract-Résumé: The myotubularin (MTM) enzymes are conserved from yeast to humans. Three MTM genes have been found mutated in the often fatal and debilitating neuromuscular diseases myotubular myopathy (MTM1) and Charcot-Marie tooth disease (MTMR2 and MTMR13). Furthermore, it is likely that mutations in related MTM family member genes will be identified in other neuromuscular disorders in the future. Interestingly, the different diseases associated with specific MTMs indicates family members perform different functions in the cell even though the genes are similar, and the enzymes transform the same types of molecules.      Our recent studies have shown that chemical tags added to MTM gene products can control their physiological abilities like molecular light switches. Therefore, a major focus of the proposed research is to fully understand the forces that control when these enzymes are on and off. Also, we have identified novel targets for MTMR2 and propose to test if these targets could contribute to the neuromuscular disease when the MTMR2 gene is inactivated.      Although the exact cellular function of MTMR2 is unclear, the pathologies associated with this gene highlights its importance in fundamental biological processes. The first step necessary to develop treatments is to acquire a more detailed understanding of how MTMR2 functions in normal cells, in addition to finding the target proteins that are affected by the enzymatic activity of MTMR2. This information can then be used as a platform for developing inhibitor strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Influence of motor behaviour on sensory feedback to primary motor cortex
Keywords-MotsClés: NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; PRIMARY MOTOR CORTEX; STRETCH REFLEXES; UPPER LIMB; VOLUNTARY MOTOR CONTROL
Abstract-Résumé: Humans are able to perform a broad range of motor skills, from the rapid spinning of an elite diver to the precise staccato of a violinist. Recent theories suggest that sensory feedback from the limb (and vision) are essential for performing these voluntary motor skills. In particular, the theory suggests feedback is always present and that the properties of the arm and the movement goal influence the use of this feedback for controlling the limb. Our recent studies on humans show how feedback from the limb is used to modify and correct perturbations (unexpected bumps applied to the limb) during reaching or other motor tasks. The timing of these corrections suggest that they are generated from signals transmitted down to the spinal cord from primary motor cortex. Primary motor cortex is known to be important for voluntary control, but its use of feedback for control is not well recognized nor understood. The present proposal will highlight how feedback to this brain region scales with perturbation magnitude, interacts with spinal activity and importantly is modified based on the behavioural goal. This research will change our view on how primary motor cortex controls movement by emphasizing the importance of sensory feedback. This knowledge provides a foundation for understanding how various neurological disorders such as stroke impact brain function and motor performance. The behavioural tasks used in this proposal will also be used in parallel studies to quantify motor deficits in various patient groups.

TitreApplicationTitle: Ventilator-induced diaphragmatic dysfunction.
Keywords-MotsClés: DIAPHRAGM; MECHANICAL VENTILATION; MITOCHONDRIA; MUSCLE CONTRACTILITY; MUSCLE WEAKNESS AND WASTING
Abstract-Résumé: Patients with respiratory failure from different causes often require temporary respiratory support by a breathing machine (ventilator), a treatment known as mechanical ventilation. Unfortunately, mechanical ventilation itself has many side effects, and this includes the development of respiratory muscle (especially diaphragm) weakness. Once the diaphragm is weak, it becomes very difficult to remove patients from the ventilator.  This proposal will investigate the role of abnormal mitochondrial function in causing this problem. Mitochondria are the major energy generators within the cell, and can also be the source of harmful substances such as damaging free radicals. We will study diaphragm samples obtained from genetically altered and drug-treated mice, as well as humans who received mechanical ventilation prior to death. These studies will provide new information about the cellular mechanisms linking mitochondrial dysfunction to diaphragmatic weakness in mechanically ventilated patients, which is a very commonly encountered clinical problem.

TitreApplicationTitle: Optimization of the antidepressant action of ketamine in treatment-resistant depression and investigations on it's mechanism of action
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIDEPRESSANT; CLINICAL TRIALS; DEPRESSION; GLUTAMATE; GLUTAMATERGIC SYSTEM; KETAMINE; MAJOR DEPRESSION; MOOD DISORDERS; NMDA ANTAGONIST; TREATMENT RESISTANT
Abstract-Résumé: Depression carries the largest burden of all medical disorders in middle to high income countries, as determined by the World Health Organization. Despite many antidepressant strategies, only a third of patients get well after their first treatment and a third remain ill after several treatments. Moreover, antidepressant treatments all have a delayed action ranging up to several weeks. Ketamine (KET) has been used for decades as a sedative and anesthetic. In treatment-resistant depressed patients(TRD), an intravenous dose much lower than necessary for anesthesia may produce a robust antidepressant effect and may even abolish suicidal thoughts within hours, peaking within 24 hours. But, its antidepressant effect generally lasts only days.Previous studies examining KET in TRD have been critiqued for lack of an effective placebo measure due to brief perceptual experiences associated with KET. Thus, the current study compares KET against a short-acting sedative. The second phase of this study compares the response to a single KET injection to 6 injections over 2 weeks. Next, KET responders are given 1 injection a week for 4 weeks of KET to assess duration of its benefits after repeated administration. The genetic profile of patients for a substance promoting contacts between brain cells will be determined to investigate if response to KET could be predicted with that blood test. This substance, as well as several chemicals that produce inflammation, will also be measured in the blood to investigate their role in the effect of KET. Patients will receive, in total, no more than the equivalent of three anesthetic doses of KET over about 8 weeks. Results from this study will help establish the beneficial effects of a single KET injection as a rapid intervention for major depression, and to investigate the possibility of obtaining a prolonged antidepressant effect with repeated injections.

TitreApplicationTitle: Defective prostaglandin biosynthesis pathways and abnormal crosstalk at the endometrial/peritoneal interface: role in the pathophysiology of endometriosis.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGENOSIS; CELL CULTURE; CHIP; CYTOKINES; ELISA; ENDOMETRIAL CELLS; ENDOMETRIOSIS; ENDOMETRIOTIC CELLS; ENDOMETRIUM; IL-1; IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE; IN VIVO MODEL; INFLAMMATION; MICROARRAY; PROLIFERATION; PROMOTER; REAL TIME-PCR; RECEPTORS; SIGNALISATION; SIRNA; TRANSFECTION; WESTERN BLOT
Abstract-Résumé: Endometriosis is a major cause of pelvic pain, menstrual disorders and infertility in women. The disease is mainly diagnosed in the peritoneal cavity (abdomen) by the presence of     lesions (tumors), which are thought to originate from the endometrium (the inner membrane of the uterus). Endometrial tissue may reach the abdomen during menstruation by circulating in the opposite way, but it is not clear why it implants and grows only in some women. Little is known about the causes of endometriosis and no targeted treatment is available. Our studies were the first to show functional defects in the endometrium, i.e. before this tissue migrates and grows into abnormal locations. Our current main hypothesis is that endometriosis development requires a combination of dysfunctional endometrium and a receptive host tissue. This is supported by our preliminary data showing that in women with endometriosis, the peritoneal host tissue is more responsive to endometrial signals. In fact, we first found high levels of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF), a major growth and inflammatory factor, in the endometrium and initial endometriotic lesions of patients. We then found that MIF stimulates peritoneal cells to release powerful mediator of angiogenesis (development of new blood vessels), inflammation and pain, including prostaglandins (PF; hormones kown to induce labor, pain...), but has much less effect in healthy women. This may facilitate abnormal endometrial tissue growth and contribute to the disease clinical symptoms. Using endometrial, endometriotic and peritoneal tissues, we will first identify what is wrong in PG biosynthesis and use cell culture and co-culture models to investigate how such an abnormal interaction at the endometrial/peritoneal interface plays a role in the development of endometriosis. We will then study the potential benefit of using specific inhibitors of MIF and PG activation pathways to develop specific and more efficient treatment strategies

TitreApplicationTitle: A gender and dyadic based analysis of chronic genital pain in men and women
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME; GENITAL PAIN; PROVOKED VESTIBULODYNIA; SEXUAL PAIN
Abstract-Résumé: Men and women both experience chronic genital pain, which negatively impacts their daily lives. It also affects their relationships, and sex lives. We already know that men and women experience pain differently, and that how a significant other reacts to our pain can have an impact on how well we cope. The present study will examine the differences in men and women with genital pain, and how it influences their health, relationships, and sex lives. In addition, we will examine whether male and female partners of genital pain patients react differently to their partner's pain. Understanding this will allow treatments to be tailored more specifically to patients based on their gender. It will also allow the development of couple based treatments to improve the lives of men and women with genital pain.

TitreApplicationTitle: Probing for sphingosine-1-phosphate signalling in asthma
Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHMA; CHEMICAL PROBES; EPITHELIAL CELLS; HUMAN; IMMUNOPATHOLOGY; INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS; LYMPHOCTYES; MICE; SPHINGOSINE-1-PHOSPHATE; SPHINGOSINE-1-PHOSTHATE RECEPTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Asthma affects up to three hundred thousand Canadians. In spite of significant advances in the field of symptom management, a proportion of asthmatics are refractory to current interventions and no cure is available for this lifelong disease. A class of molecules (sphingolipids) have recently emerged as important modulators of immunity, with therapeutic potential demonstrated in clinical trials for immune-related diseases like multiple sclerosis. Recently, synthetic analogs of these molecules were shown to prevent the development of experimental asthma. This new class of drugs affects the function of many actors involved in asthma pathogenesis. As a consequence, we currently ignore exactly how these new modulators act to alleviate experimental asthma. This research program is dedicated to further define the beneficial effects and mechanisms of action of these analogs and of their targets. To do so, we will combine the use new pharmacological agents, asthmatic human cell cultures as well as murine models of asthma, and genetically-modified mice. Classical and cutting edge analytical methods of immunology, molecular biology, biochemistry and physiology will be employed to integrate how this new class of molecules modulates sub-cellular, cellular, tissular and functional characteristics of the disease. The results of this program will improve our knowledge of novel modulators of asthma and ameliorate our general comprehension of the disease with possibility of rapid application for treatment since sphingosine analogs are currently approved for human use.

TitreApplicationTitle: Discovering genetic pathways to schizophrenia
Keywords-MotsClés: SCHIZOPHRENIA GENETICS
Abstract-Résumé: Schizophrenia is a serious and costly illness that affects many families in Canada and elsewhere. Genetic factors have shown the strongest evidence for increasing risk for schizophrenia. However, as for other common illnesses like diabetes or breast cancer, the genetics of schizophrenia are complex. We have been studying schizophrenia in Canadian families for many years. We have found some genetic changes that are associated with schizophrenia but do not always cause this serious disease.  In this study we will use the most advanced methods possible to investigate genetic changes in Canadian patients with schizophrenia and their close relatives. We will study new and inherited changes in genes that may play a role in increasing risk for schizophrenia. Identifying genetic changes that belong to specific brain pathways associated with schizophrenia will help us reach a new understanding of the brain mechanisms that lead to the illness, an important step towards being able to develop better treatments. As has been the case for other illnesses, we also look forward to these discoveries helping to decrease the stigma that is attached to this serious illness.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification and regulation of methylation marks in prostate carcinoma
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; DIAGNOSTIC MARKERS; KIDNEY CANCER; MASS SPECTROMETRY; PATHWAYS ANALYSIS; PERSONALIZED MEDICINE; PROGNOSTIC MARKERS; PROTEOMICS; RENAL CELL CARCINOMA; TUMOR MARKERS
Abstract-Résumé: Kidney cancer is one of the most common cancers and its incidence has been steadily increasing. Unfortunately, because the kidney is a hidden organ, it does not present itself, and kidney cancer is often detected when the tumor has already spread all over the body and the hope for a cure is minimal. There is currently no blood test for the early detection of kidney cancer. With the use of tumor biomarkers (substances that increase or decrease expression in cancer patients relative to healthy individuals), we will be able to detect kidney cancer early. In addition, after patients are treated, some kidney cancers will spread to other parts of the body (aggressive), while other tumors do not behave in this manner. It is important to be able to predict the aggressiveness of the tumor as this will help determine the patient treatment plan. Our research is focused on identifying tumor biomarkers using a new, sensitive technique, called mass spectrometry, that is being successfully used in other cancers for comparing proteins of normal and cancer patients to identify tumor biomarkers. Preliminary experiments showed that this technique can identify biomarkers for kidney cancer. We will first analyze the proteins produced by cancer and compare them to the normal kidney to identify markers that will aid in the early detection of kidney cancer. This will be followed by advanced computer (bioinformatics) and experimental analyses to investigate the role of these biomarkers in cancer. We will also compare proteins of patients who have advanced kidney cancer and compare them to patients who have early and less aggressive kidney cancer. These markers will help to decide the best treatment option for each patient and will have a great impact by avoiding unnecessary costs and unwanted side-effects resulting from treatments that are no benefit to a certain patient. A better understanding of kidney cancer will lead to improved detection and ultimately better health care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of a Transgenic Mouse Model and Testing Platform of Multiple Myeloma Bone Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: BISPHOSPHONATES; BONE DISEASE; MULTIPLE MYELOMA; NOVEL THERAPIES; OSTEOBLASTS; OSTEOCLASTS
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple Myeloma is a cancer of bone marrow cells that, despite recent advances in its treatments, remains incurable and deadly.  The majority of patients with this disease develop bone disease characterized by lytic (holes) lesions in their bones, osteoporosis (weakened bones), fractures and pain.  The current strategies for treating this complication are inadequate and merely reduce the rate of complications, they do not eliminate them.  Key to the understanding of myeloma bone disease and to the promotion of new and effective treatment strategies is the development of a good animal model that faithfully recapitulates all aspects of human myeloma. Current models are all deficient in one crucial aspect or another.  In this proposal we have preliminary evidence that a genetically manipulated mouse can reproducibly develop all facets of human multiple myeloma, including key aspects of its associated bone disease. We aim to further study this model in order to better understand the key events and processes that lead to bone lesions.  We will also endeavour to try various strategies, based on our initial studies, to halt or even reverse myeloma bone disease.  It is our hope that these studies and this model lead to new ways to study and treat myeloma bone disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Comparative Genomics and Environmental Diversity of Intracellular Parasites
Keywords-MotsClés: APICOMPLEXA; ENVIRONMENTAL; FUNGI; GENOMICS; INTRACELLULAR PARASITE; MICROSPORIDIA; POPULATION; PROTOZOA
Abstract-Résumé: Microsporidia and Apicomplexa are obligate intracellular parasites that include numerous medical and commercially important pathogens. Both lineages also have surprising evolutionary origins that have forced us to re-interpret basic characteristics such as genomes, metabolism, and infection apparatus. Microsporidia were formerly considered to be primitive, but we now know they are in fact closely related to fungi and that their simplicity is the really  result of severe reduction. In the case of apicomplexans, despite being intracellular parasites they were found to contain a plastid, the organelle responsible for photosynthesis in plants and algae. we have learned a great deal about these parasites from comparative genomics, but population- and environmental-genomic data remains limited for both groups, restricting our fundamental knowledge in several ways. Here, we propose to fill these gaps, and address specific key questions. For microsporidia, we will focus on population genomics and potential environmental reservoirs of the human parasite Encephalitozoon, which includes species with the most reduced nuclear genomes known. Sequencing whole genomes from genetically distinct strains will reveal how their extremely reduced genomes change over time, and whether cultivation affects model strains at the genomic level, while environmental surveys will reveal whether parasites can jump between vertebrate and invertebrate hosts. For apicomplexans, we will test the hypothesis that they emerged through a symbiotic interaction with animals based on photosynthesis by genome -wide characterization of several newly-discovered free-living and photosynthetic relatives, to determine what roles the loss of photosynthesis and the infection apparatus played in their adaptation to parasitism. Overall, this work will use high-throughput genomic methods to address fundamental questions about two important groups of parasites at levels previously restricted by the absence of data.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of Magnetic Seizure Therapy in Treatment Resistant Depression
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN STIMULATION; ELECTROCONVULSIVE THERAPY; MAGNETIC SEIZURE THERAPY; MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; TREATMENT RESISTANT DEPRESSION
Abstract-Résumé: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) has unparalleled efficacy in treating severe depression that is resistant to common modalities of treatment, such as antidepressant medication.  Although treatment with ECT has benefited many individuals with treatment resistant depression (rates as high as 50-75%), its more widespread use is hindered by the social stigma associated with the treatment, as well as by its significant cognitive side effects.  Moreover, ECT cannot be precisely targeted, since it produces a widespread activation of the brain surface, in turn, affecting many different functional areas.    Magnetic seizure therapy (MST) is currently being investigated as an alternative to ECT, as it is more focused to one area of the brain.  Rather than applying electrical stimuli to induce a seizure, as is done in ECT, MST uses repetitive magnetic stimulation to produce the seizure. Preliminary research suggests that MST can result in therapeutic effects comparable to those produced by ECT, but without the negative side effects on cognition.  The proposed study is a randomized, controlled trial, in which the efficacy and side effect profile of MST will be compared to those of ECT. If successful, the results of this study may lead to increased treatment availability and accessibility, as well as lessen the substantial health care costs associated with treatment resistant depression.

TitreApplicationTitle: Intestinal colonization and virulence mechanisms of Campylobacter jejuni
Keywords-MotsClés: CAMPYLOBACTER JEJUNI; COLONIZATION; FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC; GUT MICROBIOTA; IRON; METABOLISM; PROTEIN STRUCTURE; REGULATORY NETWORK; STRESS RESPONSES; TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATOR
Abstract-Résumé: Campylobacter jejuni is a food and water-borne pathogen. It is the major cause of diarrhea with up to 1.8 billion illnesses and 3 million deaths each year worldwide. Our understanding of how C. jejuni causes disease is extremely limited. There is currently no vaccine against C. jejuni and our current antibiotic treatments are threatened by the emergence of antibiotic resistance. The main objective of our research proposal is to understand how Campylobacter jejuni colonizes the host's intestine, a prerequisite to disease development. In a healthy individual, the intestine is colonized by trillions of microbes which constitute the "normal" microbiota. In order to be a successful pathogen and cause diarrhea, C. jejuni must either compete or cooperate with the host's microbiota for nutrients. We propose here to characterize the interactions between C. jejuni and the host's microbiota. We will study how C. jejuni acquires essential nutrients and how it adapts to the harsh conditions of the intestine. This work will generate a better understanding of C. jejuni metabolism and how it survives in the host. This information will provide targets and facilitate the design of novel strategies for preventing or treating Campylobacter infections.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the pathophysiology of Rasmussen's encephalitis
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTO-IMMUNE EPILEPSY; CYTOKINES; EPILEPSIA PARTIALIS CONTINUA; T-LYMPHOCYTES
Abstract-Résumé: Rasmussen's encephalitis (RE) is a rare but severe epileptic disorder. RE typically affects children and begins with seizures that are refractory to conventional seizure medications. The seizure disorder progresses over time culminating in continuous seizures and a progressive neurological deficit characterized by paralysis of one side of the body and atrophy of the opposite half of the brain. A number of clinical and laboratory reports suggest that RE is a disorder of the immune system.  Our group has developed an animal model of epilepsy that appears to be specific for RE. Indeed, by injecting blood taken from patients with active RE we are able to reproduce in mice the clinical and pathological findings of RE. When injected with blood from patients with other epileptic syndromes or other auto-immune diseases, animals do not develop seizures or brain inflammation. We now propose to use this model to understand the immune mechanisms that lead to RE. To do so, we have established a collaboration with the RE Children's project which will provide us with access to blood from patients with a new diagnosis of RE worldwide. We will induce the disease using our mice model and study the role of circulating factors and immune cells that modulate the activity of these cells in the induction and progression of the disease. We will also use this model to develop new therapies for this severe epilepsy. We believe that our innovative approach will help us better understand a disease with a poor prognosis, but more importantly improve the outcome of patients who up to now require to control their seizures a surgical procedure that leaves them with a permanent neurological deficit, the hemispherotomy. We then hope to bring these new treatments to clinical trials.

TitreApplicationTitle: Integrated proteomics and genomics approach to characterize a risk locus for type 2 diabetes
Keywords-MotsClés: BETA CELL PHYSIOLOGY; COMMON GENETIC VARIANTS; DIABETES GENETICS; DIABETES PATHOGENESIS; FUNCTIONAL GENOMICS; GENE EXPRESSION; PROTEIN NETWORKS; PROTEOMICS; RARE GENETIC VARIANTS; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Adult-onset diabetes frequently occurs in family members as a result of inherited changes in the sequence of their genes. We have discovered a number of changes in DNA can make people more prone to developing diabetes. None of these genetic changes are sufficient to cause diabetes by themselves; rather, they work together to impair specific functions of cells in the body that leads to disease. In the current project, we will use state-of-the-art technologies to study a large number of proteins that are affected by a genetic risk locus on chromosome 6 to determine how it affects the pancreas's ability to make adequate amounts of insulin.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effets du counseling basé sur l'entretien motivationnel dans le contexte de l'offre de dépistage rapide du VIH aux HRSH montréalais (projet SPOT) sur l'occurrence des relations anales à risque et sur ses déterminants.
Keywords-MotsClés: COMMUNAUTAIRE; COUNSELING; ENTRETIEN MOTIVATIONNEL; ESSAI CONTROLE RANDOMNISE (ECR); FACTEURS PSYCHOCOMPORTEMENTAUX; HRSH; PREVENTION; SIDA; TEST DE DEPISTAGE RAPIDE DU VIH
Abstract-Résumé: En 2009, une equipe de chercheurs montrealais a mis en oeuvre SPOT, une intervention visant a limiter la transmission du VIH chez les hommes ayant des relations sexuelles avec des hommes (HRSH)  par l'offre de test de depistage rapide en milieu communautaire. Au cours de la premiere phase, un counseling base sur les lignes directrices quebecoises sur le depistage rapide du VIH etait offert (CS) et en seconde phase, un counseling base sur l'entretien motivationnel (CEM) a ete developpe et valide. La presente proposition a pour but de renforcer les travaux entrepris pendant ces premieres phases. Son objectif est d'evaluer les effets a court et moyen termes du CEM sur l'occurrence de relations anales a risque et sur ses determinants.  Pour se faire, les futurs participants seront alloues de facon aleatoire soit au CS, soit au CEM et ils repondront a un questionnaire documentant leurs comportements sexuels et leur profil psychosexuel avant l'intervention (T0), immediatement apres (T1), 3 mois (T 2) et 6 mois plus tard (T3).  L'originalite de notre proposition repose sur l'integration d'un counseling base sur l'EM a un contexte de depistage rapide du VIH offert dans un local communautaire par des equipes composees d'intervenants communautaires et de personnel infirmier. SPOT offre l'opportunite d'etudier ces pratiques qui ne sont pas offertes ailleurs au Canada et qui n'ont pas ete evaluees dans des contextes similaires ailleurs dans le monde.

TitreApplicationTitle: Long-term remodeling of the auditory thalamocortical system:  Studies in frequency-specificity, intracortical contributions and cholinergic modulation
Keywords-MotsClés: AUDITORY CORTEX; AUDITORY PLASTICITY; CHOLINERGIC; INTRACORTICAL; LONG-TERM POTENTIATION AND DEPRESSION; THALAMOCORTICAL
Abstract-Résumé: The brain acquires information from the external world, processes it and then induces the appropriate response.  This is an automatic learning process based on neural re-wiring within specific neural circuits, and is an everyday occurrence.  Sound remodels the brain in this manner.  Abnormalities in the processing of sound may result in brain dysfunction and strongly impact the quality of life such as the cognitive deficits seen in Rett syndrome, Down syndrome, autism and Alzheimer disease.  This study intends to add to our knowledge of the neural mechanisms involved in sound and how it is processed by the brain.  Specifically, this involves examining a fundamental neural circuit in the auditory thalamocortical system that is responsible for learning-induced changes (plasticity) in the brain.  Our work may contribute to new clinical measures for the treatment of hearing and/or mental disorders including tinnitus, auditory hallucinations and autism.

TitreApplicationTitle: Croiser les savoirs pour changer les pratiques: une recherche participative pour améliorer l'interaction entre les personnes en situation de pauvreté et les professionnels dentaires
Keywords-MotsClés: APPLICATION DES CONNAISSANCES INTEGREE; ENTREVUES DE GROUPES; HUGIENISTES DENTAIRES); METHODES QUALITATIVES; PERSONNES EN SITUATION DE PAUVRETE (AIDE SOCIALE); PROFESSIONNELS DENTAIRES (DENTISTES; RECHERCHE PARTICIPATIVE
Abstract-Résumé: Les etudes que nous avons conduites au Quebec montrent que les personnes prestataires de l'aide sociale vivent des experiences negatives dans les cliniques dentaires et, souvent, se sentent rejetees. Parallelement, nos recherches revelent aussi que les dentistes comprennent tres mal les personnes en situation de pauvrete. Aussi sont-ils souvent frustres par leurs comportements et meme reticents a les recevoir dans leur clinique dentaire. Ces incomprehensions mutuelles sont inacceptables: elles creent des barrieres presque insurmontables dans l'acces aux soins dentaires et nuisent a la sante des personnes prestataires de l'aide sociale.   Notre objectif est donc de developper des approches favorisant l'interaction positive entre personnes prestataires de l'aide sociale et professionnels dentaires. Plus precisement, nous tenterons de repondre aux questions suivantes: 1) Quelles sont les situations que les personnes PAS et les professionnels de la sante dentaire jugent "difficiles", frustrantes, ou conflictuelles dans leurs interactions? 2) Quels facteurs favorisent ou, au contraire, previennent ces situations difficiles?  3) Quelles solutions concretes permettraient d'eviter ou de resoudre ces situations difficiles?  Pour repondre a ces questions, nous conduirons une recherche-action dans laquelle des personnes en situation de pauvrete et des professionnels seront reunis dans des entrevues de groupes. C'est dans ce cadre qu'ils confronteront leurs perspectives et, ensemble, degageront des solutions concretes. Precisons que cette etude est le fruit d'un partenariat avec des organismes qui representent plusieurs secteurs de la societe: les personnes en situation de pauvrete, les professionnels dentaires, et les educateurs des ecoles professionnelles dentaires. Ces partenaires s'engageront ensemble pour mettre en pratique les solutions que nous aurons trouvees.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of biomarkers in relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma.
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMARKERS; CANCER; GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING; HODGKIN LYMPHOMA; TISSUE MICROARRAYS; TREAT OUTCOMES
Abstract-Résumé: Hodgkin lymphoma is the most common form of malignant lymphoma affecting young people in the Western World. Despite advances in treatment over the last half century, 25% of patients will relapse after initial treatment. Most of these people are then treated with high intensity chemotherapy and bone marrow transplant with 50% subsequently being cured. Currently, we lack reliable tools to predict which patients will be cured by this second line treatment and in whom the disease will progress or relapse. In this proposal we plan to develop tools to predict outcome of second line treatment by examining the lymph node biopsies of patients taken at the time that the lymphoma returns. In Hodgkin lymphoma, the cancer cells make up only ~1% of the cells present in these biopsies, with the remainder being normal cells attracted by the cancer cells - the so-called "tumor microenvironment". We have recently shown that the cells present in this microenvironment are important predictors of response to the initial treatment. We will determine whether the mix of cells in the relapse biopsies predict outcome of the second treatment. We will also use recently described special techniques to measure the expression of genes in the relapse biopsies. A predictor will then be produced using information about how the patients responded to the second line treatment. This tool will ultimately inform patients and doctors about the likely outcome of the high intensity chemotherapy and bone marrow transplant and will allow us to identify people who may be better served by new treatment options.
