TitreApplicationTitle: Effects of sleep deprivation with low blood alcohol levels on executive functions in young drivers.
Keywords-MotsClés: DECISION MAKING; DRINK DRIVING; DRIVING SIMULATION; EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS; HAZARD PERCEPTION; NEURODEVELOPMENT; PREFRONTAL CORTEX; ROAD TRAFFIC CRASHES; SLEEPINESS; YOUNG DRIVERS
Abstract-Résumé: According to the World Health Organization, road traffic crashes are the leading cause of mortality in young adults (< 25 yrs.). Driving while impaired by alcohol and sleep deprivation are two frequently observed crash causes in young drivers. About one-third of the young Canadian drivers who died in traffic crashes involving alcohol had legal blood alcohol concentration (i.e. BAC < 0.08%). The sleep deprivation in young adults is common, and is expected to intensify their crash vulnerability even at legal low BAC. In particular, both sleep and alcohol may diminish underlying cognitive capabilities critical for safe driving, namely decision-making and hazard perception, but their combined effect on these systems in young drivers is unknown. As these cognitive capacities undergo significant development in young people under 25, with their rate and nature of development differing between males and females, both age and gender may be additional vulnerability factors. This study aims to clarify to how and to what degree sleep deprivation combined with low, legal levels of alcohol consumption influences driving in young drivers than either of these conditions alone or when rested and sober. Young male and female drivers aged 18-34 years will be subjected to either of 4 conditions: 1) rested and sober, 2) sleep deprivation, 3) low BAC (0.03%), 4) combined sleep deprivation and low BAC. The impact of these 4 conditions will be assessed on safe driving capacities using driving simulation, and on hazard perception and decision-making using neuropsychological testing. Age and gender effects will be explored in relation with maturation of neurocognitive functioning. The results will inform policy-making (e.g. extension of zero tolerance, graduated licensing with night-time restriction) and public health interventions (e.g. targeted awareness). This would contribute to the reduction in the catastrophic impact of traffic crashes on the health of young Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Mechanisms of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) due to Mutations in Cellular Junctions Proteins
Keywords-MotsClés: ARRHYTHMIAS; ARRHYTHMOGENIC RIGHT VENTRICULAR CARDIOMYOPATHY; CELLULAR JUNCTION PROTEINS; DISEASE MECHANISMS; GENETIC SUSCEPTIBILITY; MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS; MOUSE MODELS; PHENOTYPIC VARIABILITY; TRANSLATIONAL MEDICINE
Abstract-Résumé: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) is an inherited cardiac condition characterized by life threatening heart rhythm disturbances, cardiac arrest or sudden death in young people. The disease affects mainly the right heart and is diagnosed with a wide range of tests that focus on the function and electrical signals of the right ventricle. Genetic testing has identified mutations in at least five different genes, responsible for maintaining cell-cell contacts, causing ARVC in about 50% of patients. The main objective of the proposal is to understand how mutations in those genes lead to the disease. Based on our previous observations in mouse models lacking components of those cellular junctions we propose that alterations in the cell-cell contacts impair mechanical transduction leading to damage of the cell membrane. Thus, membrane repair mechanisms will be activated, but their exhaustion causes at the end heart failure due to fibrosis and necrosis and arrhythmias due to changes in calcium homeostasis. The research program will discover the specific molecular, cellular and genetic mechanisms of a novel mutation (p.Q554X) in a gene called desmocollin-2 which we identified in the Alberta Hutterite population. This mutation appeared to be very common (1/10) and is causing early-onset arrhythmic signs in people who carry two mutant copies of the gene. Besides the mechanistic approach we also aim to characterize clinical features in gene carriers which will help us to identify genetic and environmental factors influencing variability between family members. The new insights gained from this proposed study provides an enormous future perspective for predicting, understanding and may be treating arrhythmias in ARVC and in many other, more common cardiac diseases which frequently recapitulate defects of single gene disorders.

TitreApplicationTitle: Lifestyle Activity and the Promotion of Emotional Well-Being, Biological Functioning, and Physical Health Among Breast Cancer Survivors Over Time
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOLOGICAL FUNCTIONING; BREAST CANCER; LONGITUDINAL DESIGN; MENTAL HEALTH & WELLBEING; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY; PHYSICAL HEALTH; SEDENTARY BEHAVIOUR; STRESS AND ADAPTATION; SURVIVORSHIP
Abstract-Résumé: Women never really "get over" their experience of breast cancer. Survivors are faced with persistent and pervasive health challenges that increase the risk for other chronic diseases. It is a priority to identify factors that can mitigate the adverse physical and psychological health problems for breast cancer survivors that often leave them physically, emotionally, and functionally impaired. We propose that lifestyle activity - a combination of being physically active and limiting sedentary time - can help improve the long-term health and quality of life of women surviving breast cancer.  Our existing longitudinal study examines the natural changes in lifestyle activity, psychological and physical health, and related underlying biological functioning during the first 1.5 years after treatment for breast cancer. Increases in physical activity after treatment are linked to improved emotional well-being, decreased inflammation, lower levels of biological stress, and better physical health, all of which may relate to improved overall health over time. We now propose to collect data from these women to see if the protective effects of lifestyle activity are maintained as women move further away from treatment and enter longer-term survivorship phases. This current proposal extends our study to: (i) examine links between physical activity and sedentary behaviour and long-term patterns of key indicators of psychological and physical health; and (ii) identify factors that predict engagement in lifestyle activity over time. These objectives will be met by collecting a mix of data at 3 times in the next 4.5 years - allowing us to examine short and long-term survivorship phases. The findings will help inform intervention strategies, guide theoretical tenets, and identify key lifestyle activity strategies for improving health and well-being during survivorship among the 450 Canadian women diagnosed with breast cancer each week.

TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation and Function of Soluble IL-7 Receptor Alpha (CD127) in HIV Infection
Keywords-MotsClés: CD8+ T-CELLS; FLOW CYTOMETRY; GAMMA CHAIN CYTOKINES; HIV IMMUNOPATHOGENESIS; IL-7 RECEPTOR; LUMINEX; SIV INFECTION; THYMOCYTES; WESTERN BLOT
Abstract-Résumé: Impaired cytotoxic T-cell (CTL) activity and altered thymic function likely contribute to progression of HIV disease but the reasons for this remain to be established. Interleukin (IL)-7 signaling is essential for both CTL and thymic function and recent findings in our laboratory implicate a role for the regulation of the IL-7 receptor alpha (CD127) in the immunopathogenesis of HIV infection. We have shown that a soluble form of CD127 (sCD127) is released by CD8+ T-cells and demonstrated that sCD127 can inhibit IL-7 activity in vitro. In addition, we have detected sCD127 in human plasma and found that it is increased in HIV infection. The proposed work will investigate the mechanism(s) by which sCD127 is released by CD8+ T-cells and thymocytes and its role in HIV infection in vitro. Lastly, we will examine the effects of IL-7 therapy on the expression of sCD127 in SIV infection of rhesus macaques (an established model of HIV infection) as well as in effectively-treated HIV+ adults. Regulation and/or function of sCD127 may be important in explaining HIV-associated immune dysfunction and may lead to the development of novel immune-based therapies. Soluble CD127 has the potential to be clinically useful, both as an indicator of disease activity but, more importantly, as an immunotherapeutic agent.

TitreApplicationTitle: Validation of non-invasive rapid eye movements measurement as screening tool for mild traumatic brain injury
Keywords-MotsClés: INJURY CONTROL; INJURY PREVENTION; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING AND SPECTROSCOPY; MILD TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY; NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TESTING; NEUROSURGERY; OPHTHALMOLOGY; POST-CONCUSSION SYNDROME; QUALITY OF LIFE; SACCADOMETRY
Abstract-Résumé: Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI; including concussion) is a common problem. Properly identifying mTBI is important in order to prevent premature return to activities and to start timely and appropriate treatments.  Presently there are no validated, portable tools available to objectively identify such injuries and to measure the progress of recovery from injury.  Rapid eye movements, otherwise known as saccades, are natural movements of our eyes which allow us to perform activities such as reading, walking, and driving. Specific areas in the brain control these movements. An injury to any of these areas will change the normal patterns of these saccades. Thus, measuring saccades could provide an objective, non-invasive measure of brain injury.  The purpose of this study is to see whether changes in measures of rapid eye movements can predict structural and functional changes in the brains of patients following mTBI. In addition to having implications for a whole field of new mTBI research, the results from this study may also have significant implications for the accurate diagnosis and timely treatment of mTBI.   Specifically, measuring saccades will help doctors determine when their patients can return to regular daily activities and sporting activities.

Abstract-Résumé: One last morsel of food remains on your dinner plate. You hesitate but in spite of feeling full you manage to manage to eat the last bite. Your plate is clean and your hunger satisfied. Without a conscious thought of eating anything more your eyes glance over the dessert menu. The anticipation of the novel sensory experience presented by these tasty desserts makes you perk-up and before you know it you are devouring another mouthful. The rewarding effects of palatable foods can drive us to eat even when we are feeling full. Which mechanisms in the brain are responsible for motivating us to consume foods rich in fat and sugar? Our work explores the neural pathways that underlie motivation for food and other behaviors linked to energy balance. We and others have demonstrated how hormonal signals like leptin can act in the midbrain to influence food intake and the mesolimbic dopamine system, a pathway well implicated in the rewarding effects of drugs of abuse and natural stimuli. Our goal is to identify the mechanisms by which hormonal and nutrient signals influence dopamine circuitry and motivated behavior. As we are confronted with the health, social and economic consequences of obesity and obesity-related illnesses, elucidating the mechanisms that regulate motivation for food remains an important goal.

TitreApplicationTitle: Sex differences in risk for chemically induced liver cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER RISK; CHEMICAL CARCINOGENESIS; HORMONAL INFLUENCES; MOUSE MODELS; SEX DIFFERENCES
Abstract-Résumé: Aside from obvious differences between women and men in the occurrence of cancers in organs such as the ovary and breast in women and the prostate and testis in men, there are also sex differences in the risk for cancers that occur in some other organs such as the liver.  Men have more than 3 times higher risk for liver cancer than women, even after accounting for male-female differences in exposure to cancer-producing chemicals or viruses.  The reasons for these differences are not known.  Some strains of mice can mimic the sex differences in liver cancer risk seen in humans, and may therefore provide a way to investigate the reasons for these differences.  We have seen a much higher amount of liver tumor growth in male mice than in female mice after they were exposed early in life to one type of cancer-causing chemicals called the 'aromatic amines', which are found in some factory settings, in cigarette smoke and in some hair dyes.  Our goal is to better understand the reasons for these sex differences in risk for liver cancer growth in mice.  By doing so, we hope to better identify different risk factors in men and women for human cancers of the liver and other organs.  With this understanding, we hope that our studies will eventually lead to the discovery and use of novel medical treatments or lifestyle changes that could reduce the risk for cancers of the liver and possibly other tissues in both men and women.

TitreApplicationTitle: The McGill Immersive Wheelchair (miWe) Simulator for the clinical assessment and at-home training of powered wheelchair driving skills
Keywords-MotsClés: ASSESSMENT; AT-HOME PROGRAM; COMPLEX TASKS; COMPUTER SIMULATION; CONFIDENCE; DRIVING; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; POWERED WHEELCHAIR; SAFETY; TRAINING
Abstract-Résumé: Mobility impairment is a major form of disability affecting Canadians of all ages, and many require a powered wheelchair. However, due to their size and speed, powered wheelchairs have an inherent risk of causing injury to the driver or to bystanders. That is why training is so important. However, both clinicians and users of powered wheelchairs think that the amount of training currently being given is insufficient. To provide additional training, we have designed a powered wheelchair driving simulator. This simulator runs on a computer and can be used at home. In this project, we plan first to test the simulator as a tool to evaluate powered wheelchair driving skills in new users. We will also run focus groups, including rehabilitation professionals and experienced powered wheelchair users, to determine a list of driving tasks that are especially challenging and cannot be easily practiced at the clinic or rehab center. Such tasks could include driving the wheelchair in the adapted transport vehicle, or navigating in a crowded corridor. These tasks will then be added to the simulator. People who need a powered wheelchair often need to wait 6-8 weeks for its delivery. During that time, they will be given the simulator, so that they can train at home. We will then evaluate their powered wheelchair driving skills, to measure the effectiveness of the simulator. Finally, a website will be created to distribute the simulator software and information about its use and effectiveness. This project will be conducted by a team of occupational therapists, engineers and other rehabilitation specialists. It is hoped that training in the simulator will improve powered wheelchair driving skills. This project will likely reduce the number of harmful accidents, increase mobility and quality of life in people who greatly need it.

TitreApplicationTitle: Neuroprotection and immunomodulation in the enteric nervous system for the treatment of  Parkinson's disease
Keywords-MotsClés: DOPAMINERGIC NEURON; ESTROGEN; GASTROINTESTINAL DISEASE; GENDER AND HEALTH; IMMUNOMODULATION; MACROPHAGE; NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER; NEUROPROTECTION; PARKINSON'S DISEASE; THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Most patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experience autonomic dysfunctions involving the gastrointestinal system, which complicates the clinical management of the disease and lowers the quality of life. Interestingly, these gastrointestinal dysfunctions often precedes motor dysfunctions and are associated with the degeneration of the myenteric nervous system. The presence of Lewy bodies (LB) has been described in the whole myenteric and submucosal plexi in PD patients, supporting the hypothesis that PD could start in the gut and subsequently spread out to the brainstem. Therefore, considering the potential role of environmental toxins capable of inducing the degeneration of dopamine (DA) neurons such as pathogens, and taking into account the high exposure of myenteric DA neurons to these pathogens, it is crucial to gather more data about this peripheral degeneration, which might be the missing key to understand both the etiology and progression of PD. In this research project, we will study the contribution of the immune response in the degeneration of the enteric nervous system. Moreover, we will also test new immunomodulating approaches involving estrogens to promote the neuroprotection of enteric neurons and we will validate these new molecular targets in colonic biopsies from PD patients. We anticipate that this research project will generate critical data on the role of inflammation in periphery in PD and will lead to the discovery of crucially needed biomarkers at early stages of the disease. Moreover, we expect to validate new therapeutic targets that could help limit the progression of the disease before the apparition of motor dysfunctions in patients, i.e. long before the degeneration of DA neurons in the brain.

TitreApplicationTitle: Children's Psychological and Behavioral Responses  Following Pediatric Intensive Care Unit Hospitalization
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDHOOD MEDICAL TRAUMATIC STRESS; LONGITUDINAL; MIXED METHODS; PEDIATRIC CRITICAL CARE; PEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE UNIT; PROSPECTIVE COHORT; PSYCHOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL RESPONSES
Abstract-Résumé: Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) hospitalization places children at increased risk of persistent psychological and behavioral difficulties following discharge. More than 210,000 children are admitted to PICUs in North America every year, and despite tremendous advances in sophisticated medical technology and treatment regimes approximately 25% will demonstrate negative psychological and behavioral responses within the first year post-discharge. Little is known about children's responses beyond one year post-discharge, or about the risk and protective factors that may impact them. Enhancing our understanding of the impact of PICU hospitalization on children's psychological well-being will allow us to identify areas for health care promotion and intervention. This study aims to: (1) examine psychological and behavioral responses in children over 3 years following PICU hospitalization, and compare their responses with those of a comparison group of children who underwent day surgery; (2) determine whether previous hospital experiences, characteristics of the PICU admission (e.g., the number of invasive procedures the child is exposed to during treatment), and child and parent post-discharge factors (e.g., anxiety and stress) predict children's psychological and behavioral responses during the 3-year follow-up period; (3) explore a subgroup of these parents' perceptions of the impact of hospitalization on their children. We will enroll 220 children aged 3 to 12 years into the study: 110 in the PICU study group, and 110 in the day surgery group. Data will be collected at 6 weeks and at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months post-discharge. Children will be recruited from 4 Canadian pediatric hospitals located in Montreal, Toronto, Ottawa, and Halifax. We will collect study data using well-established questionnaires, and interview a subset of 40 parents to explore their perceptions of how hospitalization impacted their children to enhance our understanding of the questionnaire data.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'insertion professionnelle du personnel infirmier: Liens entre environnement de travail, motivation et engagement
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYSES PAR EQUATIONS STRUCTURELLES; ENGAGEMENT PROFESSIONNEL ET ORGANISATIONNEL; ENVIRONNEMENT PSYCHOSOCIAL; GESTION - COMPORTEMENT ORGANISATIONNEL; INSERTION PROFESSIONNELLE; MOTIVATION AU TRAVAIL; PERSONNEL INFIRMIER; SANTE PSYCHOLOGIQUE; SCIENCES INFIRMIERES; TRAJECTOIRES DEVELOPMENTALES
Abstract-Résumé: En debut de carriere, le personnel infirmier est rapidement confronte a des difficultes d'adaptation au travail. En effet, au Quebec, on estime que 21% du nouveau personnel infirmier quitte le reseau public au cours de leurs cinq premieres annees de travail (OIIQ, 2010). Ces donnees sont particulierement alarmantes dans un contexte de penurie de personnel - penurie qui devrait quintupler d'ici les 15 prochaines annees (AIIC, 2009). Si plusieurs facteurs de l'environnement de travail ont ete associes a la problematique de retention/desertion, la motivation au travail, c'est-a-dire les raisons qui poussent le personnel infirmier a s'engager dans leur travail, tarde a etre davantage etudiee. De surcroit, peu d'etudes ont tente d'evalue comment les facteurs de l'environnement de travail et les facteurs motivationnels du personnel infirmier interagissent et affectent leur engagement professionnel et organisationnel, ainsi que leur retention/desertion. Notre projet veut eclairer precisement ces questions: a) quel profil motivationnel presente le personnel infirmier en debut de carriere? b) comment les facteurs de leur environnement de travail (climat et organisation du travail) peuvent-ils influencer leur motivation et donc, favoriser leur retention dans la profession et leur fidelisation a l'egard de l'employeur? c) quels facteurs de l'environnement de travail sont le plus susceptibles d'agir sur la motivation, ainsi que sur leur engagement professionnel et organisationnel? En plus d'identifier des facteurs explicatifs de la retention et de l'engagement du personnel infirmier, les resultats ouvriront sur des pistes d'harmonisation entre les imperatifs des etablissements de soins de sante et les besoins du personnel infirmier.

TitreApplicationTitle: The impact of hearing impairment on mobility in older adults: Moving from lab to life
Keywords-MotsClés: 3D MOTION ANALYSIS; BALANCE; COGNITIVE-MOTOR DUAL-TASK PERFORMANCE; DUAL-TASK TRAINING; DYNAMIC POSTUROGRAPHY; GAIT; HEALTHY AGING; PRESBYCUSIS; SPEECH PROCESSING; VIRTUAL REALITY SIMULATION
Abstract-Résumé: The maintenance of balance and walking is critical social participation, and to the safety and independence of Canadian seniors. Emerging research shows that these motor skills are increasingly reliant on cognitive processes with old age. For example, walking stability can be compromised when simultaneously performing an absorbing mental task such as carrying on a conversation. Similarly, recent research shows that central cognitive resources are used by older adults to compensate for hearing impairment when listening to sentences. Consequently, listening becomes more effortful and demands more cognitive resources. Combining these two independent areas of research, a strong implication is that older adults with hearing impairment may be particularly vulnerable to imbalance and falls. To date, this hypothesis has not been systematically examined. The proposed project is designed to address this gap in the aging literature. We will compare healthy young (aged 18-35), older (aged 60-85) and older hearing impaired (aged 60-85) adults in a series of experiments involving listening comprehension and simultaneous motor tasks (walking, balancing). These studies will range from controlled laboratory-based assessments of mobility and listening to a simulated everyday situation: street crossing while listening to directions. These experiments will then form the basis for an intervention component, in which older adults with and without hearing impairment undergo cognitive and physical training to improve mobility. Together, the planned work will advance existing knowledge about the interacting effects of age-related losses in hearing and mobility. This evidence in turn will inform training intervention programs and contribute to improved mobility, and in turn, social participation, in our rapidly aging population.

TitreApplicationTitle: Les services de santé mentale en milieu carcéral fédéral
Keywords-MotsClés: IMPULSIVITE; PERSONNALITE; PRISON; SANTE MENTALE; SERVICES
Abstract-Résumé: Les detenus atteints de troubles mentaux ne recevraient pas les services de sante mentale auxquels ils ont droit. Les objectifs du projet sont d'etablir le taux de detection, et la justesse de la detection,  des besoins en sante mentale par le Service correctionnel du Canada, d' identifier les detenus pour lesquels un trouble mental serait apparu en cours de detention, d' identifier les facteurs associes aux difficultes  d'adaptation au milieu carceral des personnes atteintes de troubles mentaux ou de deficience intellectuelle, de decrire la nature des services de sante mentale recus, d'identifier les facteurs associes aux requetes presentees par les detenus pour recevoir des services de sante mentale, d'etablir les taux de revocation et de recidive, et leurs facteurs associes pour ceux qui auront ete liberes sous conditions.  Le projet s'inscrit dans la poursuite d'une etude deja subventionnee par les IRSC portant sur l'epidemiologie des troubles mentaux, des troubles de la personnalite et de la deficience intellectuelle en milieu carceral federal. L'etude devrait influencer l'organisation des services de sante mentale, notamment en permettant de justifier l'importance de bien identifier les besoins des l'entree au penitencier, en mettant en lumiere les difficultes possibles de coordination des programmes, en demontrant possiblement la tendance a augmenter le niveau de securite rattache a l'etablissement lorsque les detenus sont perturbes mentalement et perturbants. Elle permettra de verifier la qualite du processus et des expertises des intervenants cliniques dans le champ de l'identificateur des troubles mentaux et du risque suicidaire.

TitreApplicationTitle: Elucidating the mechanism of human skin fibroblast conversion to blood
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL FATE CONVERSION; HEMATOPOIESIS; OCT-4; PLATELETS; RED BLOOD CELLS; REPROGRAMMING; TRANSFUSION
Abstract-Résumé: Our laboratory at McMaster's Stem Cell and Cancer Research Institute (SCC-RI) was recently able to convert small amounts of skin samples to red blood cells that transport oxygen, and to platelet-producing cells that prevent bleeding and assist in wound-healing. This process is faster than using embryonic or pluripotent stem cells, and allows the patient's own cells to be transplanted back in so no rejection will occur - thereby providing a superior approach to others reported/published to date. The ability to generate these critical cells from human skin has the potential to provide a completely new and alternative source for blood transfusions, and also provides a new method to correct genetic diseases of the blood system such as anemias and thalassemia. Since publishing our work in Nature, this finding has changed the field and our current proposal aims to move this initial discovery to clinical reality. In order to do this, we must better understand the exact process and mechanism by which skin cells become blood. This information is essential to increase the efficiency and ability to increase the numbers of these cells to levels and dosages that can be used for a full-grown adult. We have made considerable headway to understand this process and by using our preliminary data we hope to obtain funds from CIHR to continue this work that we believe will be critical to improved health care and applications for those in desperate need of novel sources of blood product.

TitreApplicationTitle: Enhancing the wisdom of young people with migraine to promote self-care:  An iPhone and web-based application
Keywords-MotsClés: EFFECTIVENESS; ELECTRONIC DIARY; FEASIBILITY; HEADACHES; PERSONALIZED HEALTH CARE; PROBLEM SOLVING; SELF-MANAGEMENT; TECHNOLGY; USABILITY; YOUNG PEOPLE
Abstract-Résumé: Migraine is a common problem among young people and is ranked within the 20 most common reasons for disability in the world. The vast majority of young people with migraine deal with their condition alone, without consulting with their doctors. However, their actions to cope with their migraines do not often have positive effects. The reasons for this lack of results may be due to the fact that migraineurs may not really understand the cause of their headache episodes. Some sufferers may come to erroneously believe that a determinate coping strategy (e.g., sleep) works because of their past experience, when in fact it does not. They trust their biased past memories, and often do not know what else to do besides taking medication and sleeping.  The goal of this program of research is to empower adolescents and young adults with migraines to improve self-management of their migraines by developing an iPhone and web-based application. This application will allow migraineurs to track their headache episodes and learn personalized strategies for managing their migraines. For this study we will use an application that includes a headache diary developed and initially tested through the course of a previous CIHR operating grant. We will extend the functions of this application by adding features of personalized guidance and feedback to make it easier for migraineurs to deal with their headaches. This extended application will be developed and evaluated using a sequential phased approach: (1) creation of the full iPhone and web based application, (2) a pilot study with young migraine sufferers to evaluate its usability and feasibility, and (3) a controlled study to preliminary test its effectiveness. This application can help bring personalized care to the young migraineurs and  help improve their headaches.

TitreApplicationTitle: Optimization of stair design to reduce falls
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESSIBILITY; AGING; BIOMECHANICS; FALLS PREVENTION; MOBILITY; MOTION ANALYSIS; STAIR AMBULATION; UNIVERSAL DESIGN
Abstract-Résumé: One of the most prevalent yet preventable forms of risk to health across the lifespan is falling. Research consistently identifies stairs, particularly those found in homes, as the most common location of falls and falls on stairs are rapidly increasing for individuals of all ages. However, for older adults and those at-risk, the consequences can be significant, disabling and fatal. To address this problem, prevention is of key importance. It has been estimated that a significant portion of falls on stairs each year are due to stair geometry inconsistencies. However, there is little quantitative evidence regarding safe stair design and the role of step geometry inconsistency on user behaviour, such as the biomechanical markers of falls risk. This results in difficulty guiding safe stair design, improving stairway usability, and minimizing the risk of falls on stairs. The proposed research will be the first to explore stair ambulation across age and disability to understand the relationship between risk of falls, balance control, stepping behaviour and modifications in step geometry. Importantly, the results of this research will be used to provide evidence-based guidelines for safe stair design and guide the development of new approaches to rehabilitation treatment to improve mobility and usability of stairs. Ultimately, the findings from this work will foster a greater understanding of the challenge of stair ambulation and prevent falls on stairs. With the knowledge gained, we aim to minimize the risk of falls, enhance community ambulation, and improve health related quality of life in people across the lifespan.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of cholesterol in the modulation of ER stress and diabetogenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: DIABETES MELLITUS; FATTY ACIDS METABOLISM; GENE KNOCKOUT MICE; HIGH DENSITY LIPOPROTEINS; OBESITY; REGULATION OF GENE EXPRESSIONS
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence of obesity and diabetes have reached epidemic proportions globally and is expected to continue to increase. Although environment factors have been implicated to play key roles in the development of both conditions, a better understanding of the underlying physiological changes in response to such environmental stress is required to design and develop novel therapeutic strategies. Recent studies in my laboratory revealed a novel pathway by which diabetes development may be slowed or halted. We discovered that, through studying a mouse model of specific genetic disorder in humans, the cholesterol content of a particular cell compartment called endoplasmic reticulum is of critical importance in promoting diabetes. Here we will use combined animal models and biochemical approaches to further elucidate these pathways with the hope that we can better pharmacological strategies to combat the diabetes epidemic.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of placental adaptations to stress during pregnancy in the mouse
Keywords-MotsClés: ADAPTATION; MOUSE; PLACENTA; PREGNANCY; STEM CELL; TROPHOBLAST
Abstract-Résumé: The primary role of the placenta is to promote exchange of nutrients and gasses between the mother and the developing baby and it is absolutely essential for a successful pregnancy. Abnormalities in the structure of the placenta are associated with complications during pregnancy that can include miscarriage, intrauterine growth restriction and preeclampsia. Evidence in humans as well as in animal models suggests that babies born from these pregnancies are at an increased risk of hypertension, cardiovascular diseases and diabetes later in life. To date, research has focused on understanding how the changes in placental development can result in these complications. However abnormal placental structure may also result from injury or environmental challenges later in gestation, for example by changes in blood flow (hypoxia).  Many studies have characterized adaptive responses in placental physiology, including changes in nutrient transport, in response to these types of challenges. Other studies have characterized changes in placental architecture as adaptive responses. Interestingly, the cell biology and/or molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations have been largely uncharacterized. Therefore, the overall objective of this proposal is to define the ability of the placenta to adapt to stress during pregnancy as well as to characterize the mechanism(s) by which this occurs.  Building on my previous studies investigating the role of trophoblast stem cells in support of mouse placental development, I will address the following hypothesis: The placenta can adapt to challenges during pregnancy through the recruitment and differentiation of trophoblast progenitor cells. The results of these studies will provide novel and important insight into how the placenta maintains its function during pregnancy in order to support the growing fetus.  In addition, I expect that they will also lead to a better understanding of the development of complications of pregnancy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Coordination of Spindle Assembly and Function by the g-Tubulin Complex
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTOMATED TRACKING AND FEATURE FINDING; CELL BIOLOGY AND MOLECULAR GENETICS; CELL DIVISON; COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY; CYTOSKELETON; EXPERIMENTAL BIOPHYSICS; GENOMICS; INTRACELLULAR SIGNALING; MICROSCOPY AND IMAGE ANALYSIS; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: In order to divide, cells must coordinate the completion of DNA replication with growth and assembly of the mitotic spindle,which will segregate the chromosomes into daughter cells. The research program will investigate how cells use a biochemical version of a traffic "hub" to process information that must be transferred from one location in the cell to another in order to achieve this coordination. These control principles ensure proper "decision-making" during the assembly of the mitotic spindle, an essential part of the biological machinery that ensures daughter cells receive a complete set of chromosomes at the end of each cell division.

TitreApplicationTitle: Catecholamines as primary mediators of post-burn hypermetabolism:  A clinical prospective trial.
Keywords-MotsClés: BETA BLOCKER; BURN; CATECHOLAMINES; ER STRESS RESPONSE; INFLAMMATION; INSULIN RESISTANCE; STRESS; SURVIVAL
Abstract-Résumé: Morbidity and mortality of severely burned patients still remain unacceptably high. Recent evidence indicates that hypermetabolism, a hallmark of severely burned patients, is a major contributor to these detrimental outcomes. The upstream mediators inducing these changes were long thought to be cortisol, catecholamines, and glucagon. However, neither blockade of cortisol nor attenuation of glucagon alleviated post-burn hypermetabolic inflammatory responses. Also, several unexpected cellular processes have come into the spotlight in the glucose and lipid metabolism research recently as potential mediators of metabolic dysfunction in various settings, namely: endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. We therefore hypothesize that catecholamines, which are 10-40 fold increased post-burn, are the central mediators inducing post-burn hypermetabolism, associated with cellular stress responses of ER stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and activation of the inflammasome, resulting in poor clinical outcomes. To test this hypothesis, we suggest blocking catecholamine effects by administration of a non-selective beta 1/2-receptor antagonist, Propranolol. We chose Propranolol, not only because of its long-demonstrated clinical efficacy and safety, but also as it has been shown to affect post-burn lipolysis. We expect that catecholamine blockade via Propranolol will attenuate the intracellular stress signaling cascades of ER stress and inflammasome activation, normalizing burn-induced alterations in glucose and lipid metabolism, leading to decreased hypermetabolic responses, which will improve post-burn morbidity and mortality. The relevance of this project is that we will not only determine fundamental mechanisms leading to hypermetabolism in severely burned patients but that we will use a clinically effective perturbation that is readily available and safe in burn patients with the hope of improving their outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Generation of effective carbohydrate-based inhibitors of a glycosidase implicated in Alzheimer disease and their molecular mechanism of action.
Keywords-MotsClés: CHEMICAL SYNTHESIS; ENZYME INHIBITOR; INHIBITOR DESIGN; NEURODEGENERATION; PHARMACOKINETICS; PROTEIN GLYCOSYLATION; TAU
Abstract-Résumé: Alzheimer disease (AD) manifests both by the development of extracellular amyloid deposits (plaques) and intracellular aggregates known as neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs). The plaques result from accumulation of an insoluble peptide known as amyloid beta (Abeta). The NFTs arise from a form of the protein tau that assembles into aggregates. A feature of AD is that patients show impaired brain glucose metabolism and this correlates with conversion of patients from mild cognitive impairment to AD. Recently, a sugar modification of proteins has been implicated in AD. It is believed that because this sugar modification is derived from glucose its levels decrease as glucose impairment occurs in early stage AD. Data suggests that increasing levels of this sugar modification could be beneficial to slow the progression of AD. We aim to generate useful inhibitors that can efficiently increase levels of this sugar modification and to determine how this sugar modification acts to prevent the tau-driven death of neurons.

TitreApplicationTitle: Causes and consequences of co-occurring gambling involvement and substance use during adolescence: A process-oriented genetically-informed study
Keywords-MotsClés: GAMBLING; LONGITUDINAL STUDY; QUANTITATIVE GENETICS; SUBSTANCE USE; YOUTH
Abstract-Résumé: Gambling involvement and use of substances such as alcohol or cannabis are highly prevalent during adolescence. They also often co-occur within the same individuals. It is unclear, however, whether these two problem behaviours also have similar causes and whether they develop in a similar manner from early to late adolescence. Hence, the first goal of this research is to examine the overlap in the development of gambling behaviour and substance use throughout adolescence in a sample of 525 twin pairs who are followed longitudinally from early to late adolescence. The second goal is to determine the extent to which common underlying genetic and-or environmental influences account for the overlap in the development of gambling behaviour and substance use from early to late adolescence. The third goal will be to examine the role of specific environmental factors, notably those related to the family or to the peer group, in explaining the overlap between gambling and substance use. Finally, the fourth goal will be to determine the possible protective role of social norms and school-based prevention programs for adolescents who are at risk for gambling problems or substance abuse. The results of this research will help identify risk and protective factors that are common or specific to the two types of addictive behaviours. These common, or specific, factors should be the main targets of preventive interventions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of the Role of Inpp4 in Bone Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: BONE HOMEOSTASIS; BONE MINERAL DENSITY; INOSITOL PHOSPHATASE; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; OSTEOCLAST DIFFERENTIATION AND ACTIVATION; OSTEOPETROSIS; OSTEOPOROSIS
Abstract-Résumé: The overall objective of our laboratory is to understand the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate bone homeostasis. Bone homeostasis requires equilibrium between bone formation by the osteoblast and bone resorption by the osteoclast. To gain insights into these complex mechanisms, we are studying the role of novel genes in osteoclast and osteoblast differentiation and activation. We have recently isolated the murine inositol phosphatase gene Inpp4b, which represents a novel negative regulator of osteoclast differentiation. Importantly, we showed that the human INPP4B is associated with bone mineral density and this gene can become a novel susceptibility factor for osteoporosis in the general healthy population. Because we found that Inpp4b is also expressed in osteoblast, Inpp4b role in osteoblast lineage will be investigated. Characterization of the cellular and molecular functions of Inpp4 will provide critical information on key steps of the intracellular signaling mechanisms in bone cells. These studies may lead to the discovery of novel prognostic risk factor and novel target genes translatable into design of therapeutic approaches for treatment of patients suffering from bone defects.

TitreApplicationTitle: Gender Identity Disorder in Children: A Prospective Study of Its Relation to Separation Anxiety, Internalizing Behaviour Problems, and Parental Factors
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILD PSYCHIATRY; CHILD PSYCHOLOGY; FAMILY ENVIRONMENT; GENDER IDENTITY DISORDER; MENTAL HEALTH; MOOD DISORDERS; PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; SEPARATION ANXIETY; SEX DIFFERENCES
Abstract-Résumé: There are a number of children who experience confusion about their gender identity, wishing or believing they were of the opposite sex. These children often experience a number of other mental health issues as well. These mental health issues include high levels of anxiety and mood disorders, such as depression. It is not clear, however, which mental health issues most often accompany gender identity confusion in children. Similarly, it is not clear what impact the family environment might have on the mental health of these children. To fill these gaps, my research will utilize 600 case files on children who were confused about their gender identity. These case files belong to the Gender Identity Service at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health and contain extensive information gathered during clinical assessments. This information includes details about the mental health issues experienced by gender-confused children as well as various aspects of their parents, including their mental health status, substance use history, relationship quality, and parenting style. By compiling the information in these files, I will be able to identify those mental health issues that accompany gender identity confusion in children as well as the family environments that are related to these issues. Importantly, this information will be useful for informing mental health issues in gender minority groups and contribute toward a more equitable and inclusive Canadian health system.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Gender in Emotion Focused Therapy for Depression
Keywords-MotsClés: AFFECT CODE; EMOTION-FOCUSED-THERAPY; GENDER; PSYCHOTHERAPY PROCESS RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: This study will look at how an individual's self-identified gender affects the outcome of Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT) for depression. EFT aims to help clients become aware of and work through their emotions. Several studies have demonstrated that gender may contribute to the outcome of psychotherapy since one's expression of emotion is often relative to one's self-identified gender. Therefore, it is particularly relevant to consider the effects of gender on the outcome of EFT since the emphasis of this treatment is on emotion. To conduct this study, I plan to measure the affect of several EFT sessions, where half the therapist and client dyads are gender matched and the other half are not. Understanding how the expression of emotion interacts with gender to predict success of therapy could be extremely useful when preparing a client's treatment plan. Specifically, results could suggest how EFT could be modified to best suit a client's self-identified gender, or, if gender matching of client and therapist appear to affect therapy outcome, this should also be considered. The relevancy of this study is therefore to not only gain a better understanding of how affect is expressed in EFT, but also, to help maximize the effectiveness of EFT.

TitreApplicationTitle: Topical Granzyme B Inhibitor Research and Development
Keywords-MotsClés: EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX; GRANZYME; PROTEASE; SKIN ULCERS; SMALL MOLECULE DEVELOPMENT; WOUND HEALING
Abstract-Résumé: Granzyme B (GzmB) is an enzyme that has been found to accumulate in tissues and bodily in conditions associated with aging and inflammation and contributes to tissue deterioration and loss of function. GzmB is elevated in a number of skin disorders involving increased age and/or unresolved inflammation. Our data suggests that GzmB accumulation in the skin can not only cause further injury and inflammation, but can also impair the repair of damaged skin. It is estimated that up to 20-26% of patients in long-term care facilities suffer from chronic inflammation and impaired wound healing. Further, when wounds do actually heal in the elderly, the skin never regains its original strength and is therefore much more prone to further injury and skin tearing. Our evidence in several models suggests that inhibition of GzmB not only prevents tissue injury, but has the potential to prevent future re-injury as its inhibition in models of aging and impaired healing is associated with increased skin thickness and strength. The present grant seeks to capitalize on these discoveries to develop a topical treatment that will be tested in models of impaired wound healing and skin inflammation.

TitreApplicationTitle: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center, proof of concept study to evaluate the effect of sildenafil citrate (Revatio) 20 mg TID on hemodynamics in patients with Portal- Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PPAH) Short title: Revatio Portal Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension  Trial (RePo1 trial)
Keywords-MotsClés: PORTAL HYPERTENSION; PULMONARY HYPERTENSION; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; SILDENAFIL
Abstract-Résumé: Patients with liver disease can develop a condition known as pulmonary hypertension. In pulmonary hypertension there is a progressive narrowing of the small blood vessels as they travel through the lung. This narrowing puts stress on the right side of the heart as it tries to keep blood flowing through the lungs. Over time these patients develop right heart failure and may die from this condition. At present there is no approved treatments for this condition. Furthermore these patients are not able to have liver transplants because it will put a stress on their heart. Therefore they may also die from their liver disease. We want to see if we can improve the blood flow in the lungs using a drug called Revatio (sildenafil) to an extent that would allow them to live longer and potentially have a liver transplant.

TitreApplicationTitle: Social, behavioral and transmission properties associated with diversity in HIV epidemics among people who inject drugs and other key populations
Keywords-MotsClés: EPIDEMIOLOGY; HIV; INJECTING DRUG USERS; PAKISTAN; TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS
Abstract-Résumé: Persons who inject drugs are at much greater risk of acquiring HIV than the general population. HIV prevalence has reached 50% among persons who inject drugs. In many countries, HIV epidemics in these populations spill over into other groups at higher risk such as sex workers, thereby greatly increasing the overall burden of HIV. Little is understood about why HIV epidemics in these populations at high risk are so diverse, with some expanding rapidly and others staying at a low level. This project will investigate reasons for this observed heterogeneity of HIV prevalence in six different cities in Pakistan, using studies of injecting behaviours and laboratory studies to see how how the HIV virus is spreading in networks of persons injecting drugs, and from those networks to sex worker populations. The study will also use mathematical models to simulate epidemics using the behavioural and molecular data to study why some epidemics expand faster than others. The study will also assess how important injecting drugs are in the overall spread of HIV in different cities, in comparison to spread through sexual routes. This project will provide a uniquely comprehensive understanding of the HIV epidemics in Pakistan, helping public health program planners to design effective HIV prevention programs for key populations in Pakistan. This information will also be valuable to understand Canada's HIV epidemic, which is also largely concentrated in key populations at greater risk for HIV, including persons who inject drugs and sex workers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of an innovative brain-penetrating technology to improve pain management
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN PENETRATION; G PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTORS; NEUROPEPTIDE; PAIN
Abstract-Résumé: The tridecapeptide neurotensin (NT), inducing antinociception in the brain through interaction with two identified receptors subtypes, NTS1 and NTS2, presents great potential for the development of a new class of analgesics. However, because NT penetrates only poorly through the blood-brain barrier (BBB), its potential as a therapeutic agent is limited to spinal injections, thus with weak clinical outcomes. Angiochem is a pharmaceutical group focused on technologies to improve the BBB penetration of centrally active compounds. Our goal is to initiate collaboration with Angiochem to investigate the brain uptake and analgesic effects of a new chemical entity formed by the conjugation of NT to Angiopep-2, a 19-amino-acid peptide that crosses the BBB. Preliminary results of in-situ brain perfusions in mice demonstrated that the Angiopep-2-NT conjugate, ANG2002, efficiently penetrated the blood-brain barrier with a transport rate 10-fold higher than that of unconjugated NT. Through our collaboration, we intend to determine, by in vivo studies, if the systemically administered ANG2002 induces antinociceptive effects consistent with those of centrally administered NT in a variety of acute, inflammatory, and neuropathic pain models. Our expertise in pain neurophysiology will allow determining the potential of Angiochem's NT derivatives to address the reality of intractable chronic pain.

TitreApplicationTitle: Heparin AnticoaguLation to improve Outcomes in septic shock:  The HALO pilot
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTICOAGULATION; CLINICAL TRIAL; CRITICAL CARE; INFECTION; PILOT STUDY; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; SEPSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Life-threatening infections account for 10% of all intensive care unit admissions and constitute the second more frequent cause of death in the ICU after heart diseases. The most common cause of death in patients admitted with life-threatening infections is multi-organ failure that is mediated by severe inflammation. Given the relationship between inflammation and blood clotting, blood-thinners (also called anticoagulants) have been used to decrease inflammation and the formation of small clots. Several lines of evidence suggest that heparin, a proven and inexpensive blood-thinner, may reduce improve survival in patients diagnosed with life-threatening infection. The primary objective of this study is to demonstrate the feasibility of enrolling patients in a large randomized controlled trial investigating heparin in patients with severe infections. In this study, 70 patients with life-threatening infections will have an equal chance of receiving an intravenous infusion of heparin at 18 units/kg, or a low dose of a similar drug to prevent of blood clots while patients are immobile. The primary purpose of the study is to demonstrate that an average of 2 patients per site, per month, can be enrolled. Other measures of feasibility include the consent rate, the number of protocol violations that occur during the trial, and the number of dose reductions needed due to excessive anticoagulation. To study the biologic effects of heparin in patients with severe infection, specific laboratory markers will be measured and analyzed. If the feasibility of the trial is confirmed, a large randomized trial designed to tell if heparin can safely improve survival will be conducted. Given its low cost and availability, if heparin is shown to improve survival in patients with severe infection, adoption of this therapy on a global scale is anticipated.

TitreApplicationTitle: Early Determination of long-term Prognosis in critically ill patients with Severe Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI-Prognosis multicenter prospective study)
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL DECISION RULE; CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS; END-OF-LIFE; INJURY; OUTCOME RESEARCH; PROGNOSTIC TOOL; TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY
Abstract-Résumé: Traumatic brain injury is the leading cause of death and severe disabilities among adults under 45 years of age. Most deaths following severe traumatic brain injury are related with the decision made by families and medical teams to withdraw life-sustaining therapies. Because severe traumatic brain injury occurs mainly in a young healthy population, this decision is likely to be based on the perception of an unfavorable long-term outcome. However, recent practice guidelines and current knowledge showed that our capacity to accurately predict outcome in this population is limited. Our prior work showed a significant variation in the frequency of life-sustaining therapy withdrawals across Canadian trauma centers. More importantly, a significant proportion of deaths occurred in the first 3 days, a time-period considered by several experts as being relatively premature to accurately predict the patient outcome. The purpose of the TBI-Prognosis study is to develop a prognostic model and clinical prediction rule by using a multimodal approach of different prognostic indicators and their evolution over time in the acute phase of care. This study, taking place in 15 Canadian trauma centers, will improve our ability to prognosticate and identify patients who will benefit from aggressive care in the acute phase, and help preventing erroneous evaluation of prognosis that could have profound consequences when used to decide to pursue or to withdraw life-sustaining therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Discovery & Development of Novel Small Molecule Inhibitors of Viroporin Proteins for the Treatment of Acute & Chronic Viral Infections.
Keywords-MotsClés: DENGUE FEVER; HEPATITIS C; INFLUENZA M2; ION CHANNELS; VIROPORINS
Abstract-Résumé: The public enjoys protection from viral infectious diseases through the use of modern day vaccines. However, when vaccines are not possible, medications are available to reduce the effects of certain viruses such as herpes simplex, influenza, shingles, cytomegalovirus, and even HIV-1, the cause of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS). Notably, very new medications for hepatitis C (HCV), for which there is no vaccine, show particular promise by targeting key steps in the HCV life cycle. However, the need for newer, more effective antiviral medications remains a priority as new viruses invade naive populations and conditions in developing countries continue to allow for the propagation of neglected viral diseases. For example, Dengue, Chikungunya, West Nile, new strains of HCV, and pandemic influenza variants are emerging threats.  Many of these emerging viruses have also been resistant to vaccine development, further underscoring the need to develop new medications.  This proposal is designed to exploit new antiviral targets called viroporins, which appear to be involved in virus life cycles. Initially studied for influenza, the viroporins have now been characterized in many viruses, and recent data suggest that viroporins may be a viable therapeutic intervention for many viral infectious diseases. In this proposal, we will 1) Develop the means to identify molecules that can inhibit the viroporins of several problem viruses; 2) Determine the effectiveness of identified molecules to block the life cycles of HCV, Dengue, and Influenza viruses.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigating Maladaptive O-glycosylation Signaling in Aortic Aneurysm
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYTICAL CHEMISTRY; AORTIC ANEURYSM; CARDIOVASCULAR; GENETICS; PHARMACOLOGY; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: Inappropriate alterations in localized portions of the aorta produce a weakened and structurally altered vessel wall. This remodeling, referred to as aortic aneurysm, can produce a tear or rupture of the aortic wall and can thus ultimately prove fatal. Prevention of untimely death from ruptured aneurysm depends on early detection by routine imaging and preventative surgical repair. Unfortunately, this disease does not progress uniformly for all patients making clinical outcomes unpredictable, surgical repair carries with it a high risk of morbidity and mortality, and therapeutic options for patients with aortic aneurysm are lacking. The development of new therapies is predicated on a deeper appreciation of the different cellular processes that contribute to the alteration of the aortic architecture. My research will focus on defining the interplay between specific types of sugar- and phosphate-based modifications on signaling proteins that are similarly altered in two different models of aneurysm formation. In this way my contribution will clarify the fundamental upstream process in maladaptive cell function and tissue morphology within the context of aortic aneurysm.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'effet de la voie Wnt7a sur la régulation de la myogenèse
Keywords-MotsClés: ATROPHIE; CACHEXIE; EMSA SUPERSHIFT; INFLAMMATION; MUSCLE-SQUELETTIQUE; NF-KB; PROPRIETES CONTRACTILES; REGENERATION; SARCOPENIE; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Chez l'humain, les muscles squelettiques perdent environ 30% de leur masse entre l'age de 20 et 80 ans, provoquant une diminution de la force et une augmentation de la fatigabilite. Ce phenomene appele sarcopenie est associe a une augmentation du risque de chute, a une perte des capacites fonctionnelles et a une augmentation de la morbidite et de la mortalite. Considerant le vieillissement rapide de la population au Canada (et ailleurs dans le monde) et les couts sociaux et economiques induits par la sarcopenie, il est evident qu'une meilleure comprehension de la maladie et des traitements plus efficaces sont necessaires. Des etudes anterieures dans notre laboratoire ont demontre qu'une voie signaletique nommee NF-kB est chroniquement surexprimee dans plusieurs maladies musculaires comme la cachexie liee au cancer et les dystrophies musculaires. De plus, l'inhibition de la voie NF-kB dans ces maladies protege contre l'atrophie musculaire et promeut la regeneration musculaire. Nous emettons l'hypothese que la voie NF-kB est egalement chroniquement surexprimee dans les muscles ages sarcopeniques et que l'inhibition de cette voie protegera contre la sarcopenie. Pour ce faire, nous determinerons l'expression et l'activite de cette voie chez les souris jeunes Vs agees. Ensuite, nous utiliserons des souris modifiees genetiquement ou des inhibiteurs pharmacologiques de NF-kB pour evaluer le potentiel therapeutique de l'inhibition de NF-kB. La fonction musculaire, la masse musculaire, la composition musculaire (fibrose, calcification, tissu adipeux, type de fibre), la capacite regenerative des cellules satellites et la reaction inflammatoire seront mesurees pour determiner la qualite des muscles. Le role central de la voie NF-kB dans la degradation proteique et dans l'inflammation font des inhibiteurs de NF-kB une nouvelle avenue prometteuse pour le traitement de la sarcopenie associee au vieillissement qui n'a pour l'instant aucun traitement efficace.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the impact and cost-effectiveness of alternative Tuberculosis screening strategies of health care workers (HCWs)
Keywords-MotsClés: COST-EFFECTIVENESS; EPIDEMIOLOGICAL IMPACT; HEALTH CARE WORKERS; HEALTH ECONOMICS; LATENT TB INFECTION (LTBI); MODELLING; OCCUPATIONAL SCREENING; TB DIAGNOSTICS; TRANSLATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading cause of infectious mortality, with an estimated 1.7 million TB deaths worldwide in 2009.  Health care workers serve on the front lines of the battles against TB, and as such are at even higher risk for exposure to this deadly disease.  Most developed countries such as Canada reccommend annual screening for TB to identify new cases of infection that can be treated to avoid disease.  The aim of this proposal is to: 1) Estimate the long term heath impact (identifying cases and preventing transmission) of screening for TB using different testing strategies, 2)identify and assess different costs associated with alternative testing strategies, and finally 3) to develop models that can be used by decision-makers worldwide to translate information specific to their pouplation into decisions about what testing strategies would work best in their environment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanistic Studies of Notch-Ligand Interactions
Keywords-MotsClés: CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; ENDOCYTOSIS; LEUKEMIA; NOTCH RECEPTOR; PROTEIN PURIFICATION; X-RAY CRYSTALLOGRAPHY
Abstract-Résumé: A major focus of current cancer research is to identify signals responsible for selectively stimulating the growth of different cancer cell types, with the goal of subsequently developing targeted therapies directed at blocking these growth-promoting pathways. This research is focused on acquiring a thorough understanding of the Notch signalling pathway, a central biological process that controls key steps in development by allowing adjacent cells to communicate with each other, but is frequently dysregulated in cancer. Whereas Notch signals are normally conveyed in response to stimulatory proteins called ligands on adjacent cells, this process becomes abnormal in several different types of cancer as a result of mutations, increases, or even decreases in the level of activating signals. In certain leukemias, for example, there are mutations that freeze the Notch receptor in the active state, resulting in a growth-stimulatory signal that is independent of ligand stimulation and not properly controlled in the cancer cells. In the studies pursued here, we intend to address several gaps in current understanding of how Notch receptors interact with their partner ligands. First, we will evaluate the strength of the receptor-ligand partnerships and learn whether certain pairings of the four Notch receptors and their five ligands are preferred. Then, we will investigate how many receptor and ligand molecules must come together to yield a productive signal, and finally, we will seek to learn how the specific shapes of the Notch receptors and their ligands complement each other to form productive partnerships. These studies will be performed using state of the art approaches, including X-ray crystallography and fluorescent imaging.  The results of our studies should give detailed mechanistic insights that will facilitate the therapeutic modulation of Notch signalling in cancer and other diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of O-GlcNAc glycosylation in protein stability
Keywords-MotsClés: CHEMICAL BIOLOGY; DEGENERATIVE DISEASE; GLYCOBIOLOGY; O-GLCNAC; PROTEIN AGGREGATION
Abstract-Résumé: Keeping proteins stable and functional is a crucial aspect of the cell health especially when cells are placed under certain forms of stress. Several mechanisms have been identified within cells that act to verify that proteins are properly assembled, appropriately stable, and are shuttled through cells to their correct cellular locations. Among these mechanisms, the modification of proteins inside and at the surface of cells with specific carbohydrates has been found to play a crucial role in numerous biological processes. Failure to properly modify and process proteins with these sugars leads to troubles such as proteins that do not adopt their proper conformation and therefore that are unable to perform their appropriate functions. The critical importance of protein stability in cellular health is highlighted by the observation that protein aggregation could lead to pathological plaques and tangles in Alzheimer disease. Research in the area is therefore a topic of considerable current interest.   I aim to study the role of one less explored, but essential sugar modification in cells. Based on recent studies, I propose that defects in this modification could contribute to the loss of protein stability and the occurrence of age-related pathologies in human. Therefore, I propose to use new chemical biology methods to identify subsets of proteins that are modified with this specific sugar in order to study how the sugar modification influences the stability of relevant proteins. Proteins that show decreased stability due to a loss of sugar modification will be studied in cells to evaluate their ability to function properly when cells encounter various forms of stress. Identification of the proteins that are stabilized by this sugar modification and, how stabilization occurs will enable a better understanding of its biological role as well as potentially lead to therapeutic approaches to treating associated diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Super-Resolution Imaging of Receptor Dynamics and Structure: Self-Association of CEACAM and Its Implications for Cancer,Infection, and Inflammation
Keywords-MotsClés: FLUORESCENCE; MEMBRANE PROTEINS; MICROSCOPY; MOLECULAR DYNAMICS; OPTICAL IMAGING; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; SCANNING PROBE MICROSCOPY; SINGLE MOLECULE IMAGING; SUPER-RESOLUTION MICROSCOPY
Abstract-Résumé: How cells behave and interact is largely determined by interactions between molecules, known as receptors, located on their surface. These interactions are controlled by signals within the cell, through other molecules, and interactions with neighbouring cells. In this project, we are examining the CEACAM family of receptor molecules that have been linked to numerous forms of cancer. These same molecules have also been hijacked by opportunistic bacteria responsible for diseases such as meningitis, gonorrhea, and pneumonia. It is believed that errant signalling of CEACAM is in part responsible for the onset and progression of these diseases. The aim of this project is to develop and apply new ways of directly observing CEACAM molecules in live cells. These new imaging platforms will provide us with the unique opportunity of seeing how CEACAM molecules interact with each other, either on the same cell or between cells.  These platforms will allows us to track how these interactions lead to the activation of certain signaling pathways in the cells, and ultimately, will provide us with strategies for repairing or even manipulating these pathways therapeutically.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterizing the Potential Transplant Tourist in Canada: A Survey on Transplant Tourism among Canadians with Kidney Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESS TO TRANSPLANTATION; CANADA; ETHNIC MINORITIES; ORGAN TRAFFICKING; PURSUIT OF LIVING DONOR KIDNEY TRANSPLANTATION; TRANSPLANT TOURISM
Abstract-Résumé: "Transplant Tourism" is the practice of traveling to another country to illegally purchase an organ for transplantation. Despite the fact that transplant tourism is illegal and has been widely denounced by the World Health Organization, increasing numbers of Canadians who need a kidney transplant have opted for transplant tourism in recent years.  Multiple reports have described the exploitation of the poor and the serious medical risks that are associated with transplant tourism, including a higher risk of serious infections among patients that come back after buying a kidney abroad, highlighting that this is a dangerous practice for everyone involved.  Currently, there is little known about who is likely to consider transplant tourism and what factors drive this practice.  This study aims to better understand what factors will identify Canadians at risk for considering transplant tourism, what their understanding is regarding the risks and benefits of this practice, and what barriers they perceive to limit them from pursuing living donor transplantation locally.  We plan to survey British Columbians with kidney failure about their level of interest in transplant tourism, their level of interest in purusing a living donor transplant locally, their understanding of the pros and cons of transplant tourism and their perceived barriers to pursuing transplantation locally.   Specifically we hope to understand what types of patients are more likely to consider transplant tourism, whether these patients understand the potential risks associated with this practice, whether they understand the options for transplantation locally and what has prevented them from pursuing these options locally.  Also, we will understand what types of strategies may be helpful in increasing the ability of patients to get transplanted locally and to deter them from opting for transplant tourism.
