TitreApplicationTitle: Dynapénie et capacités fonctionnelles chez des personnes âgées: Impact de l'activité physique
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTIVITE PHYSIQUE; AUTONOMIE; CAPACITE FONCTIONELLE; DYNAPENIE; EPIDEMIOLOGIE; METABOLISME; PREVENTION; SARCOPENIE; SEXE; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Le vieillissement est accompagne d'une diminution progressive de la capacite fonctionnelle (capacite a effectuer les activites de la vie quotidienne). Des etudes recentes ont montre que la perte de force musculaire serait le premier facteur de cette diminution de la capacite fonctionnelle. De plus, les effets de l'obesite seraient cumulatifs a ceux de la perte de force musculaire. L'activite physique, lorsqu'elle est adaptee aux particularites du sujet age, permet de prevenir la diminution de la capacite fonctionnelle. Les recommandations en termes d'activite physique chez la personne agee demeurent non consensuelles et non specifiques aux pathologies. Nous ignorons aussi comment evolue la composition corporelle et les capacite fonctionnelles des personnes agees actives. L'objet de cette etude est donc, dans un premier temps, de comparer la prevalence des personnes ayant une faible force musculaire en fonction du type d'activite pratique, puis de caracteriser la composition corporelle et les capacites fonctionnelles des personnes agees actives ayant une faible force musculaire, et de comparer ces caracteristiques en fonction de leur type de pratique. Cette etude impliquera 1000 personnes actives (hommes et femmes) agees de 50 ans et plus, membres des YMCA. Leur composition corporelle, leur force musculaire, leur capacite fonctionnelle et habitudes passees et actuelles en terme d'activite physique, ainsi que leur fonction cardio-respiratoire seront mesurees. L'etendue des activites pratiquees par les participants nous permettra de determiner les activites les plus adaptees a la prevention des incapacites fonctionnelles chez les personnes agees de 50 ans et plus. Nous pourrons affiner ces recommandations en fonction du sexe, de l'age et des pathologies et clarifier le discours de prevention presente aux personnes agees, ainsi qu'aux jeunes adultes afin de reduire l'occurrence des incapacites fonctionnelles et des couts qui leurs sont associes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Innovations in Knowledge Translation: Addressing Inequities in Mental Health
Keywords-MotsClés: GENDER; INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY; INTERSECTIONALITY; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MENTAL HEALTH; QUALITATIVE METHODS; SOCIAL INEQUITIES
Abstract-Résumé: A challenging dilemma faced by most health researchers is how to undertake appropriate, effective, and meaningful knowledge translation (KT). While various models of KT have been proposed (e.g. Jacobson, Butterill, & Goering, 2003; Kitson et al., 2008), CIHR has adopted the comprehensive knowledge-to-action (KTA) model developed by Graham and colleagues (see Straus, Tetroe, & Graham, 2009).  Models of KT are useful for organizing and planning research projects but actual effective mechanisms for KT are also needed. This is particularly true for qualitative research on mental health and social inequities because KT development in this area is still in its nascent stages. Thus, the goal of my PhD work is to explore the effectiveness of two mechanisms for the translation and exchange of mental health knowledge that is qualitative in nature.  Specifically I have three objectives: 1. Conduct an environmental scan of existing KT models and recommended KT strategies within health sciences; 2. Evaluate the current use and impact of two communication strategies (targeted online publication and World Cafes) for the translation of knowledge at two mental health research centres housed at Simon Fraser University; 3. Provide recommendations for effective KT strategies that best meets the needs of stakeholder groups (i.e., mental health researchers, decision makers, service providers, service users, etc.) and are sensitive to the human and social context of knowledge implementation.  Effective KT of mental health and social inequities research could facilitate the utilization of this knowledge in policy and practice, thus reducing inequities and improving mental health care in Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular mechanisms underlying the ability of an anti-aging compound to extend longevity by altering mitochondrial composition, structure and function
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL BIOLOGY; CELLULAR AGING; CHEMICAL BIOLOGY; LIPIDOMICS; MECHANISMS OF AGING; MITOCHONDRIA; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PROTEOMICS; SUBCELLULAR FRACTIONATION; SYSTEMS BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Aging of humans is due to a lifelong build-up of unrepaired damage to cellular macromolecules and organelles. Progressive accumulation of such damage impairs normal functioning of the entire organism, thereby increasing a risk of disease and death. Therefore, the pace of aging depends on the rates and spatiotemporal organization of cellular processes producing the damage and repairing it. We use the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae for defining the mechanisms of aging, which in this unicellular organism is mechanistically similar to cellular aging in multicellular organisms. We elucidate how various interventions alter the rates of numerous cellular processes and their organization in space and time and how such alterations affect longevity. Recent work from our laboratory has shown that a number of cellular processes, which we call modules, are integrated into a longevity network. Our findings imply that, by setting up (in a diet- and genotype-dependent fashion) the rates of the processes taking place within each of the network's modules during early adulthood, yeast establish a particular configuration of the network that specifies the pace of their aging during late adulthood. Our study suggests a concept of the longevity control system governing progression through a series of checkpoints that occur at various stages of life. We have recently revealed several small molecules that significantly delay aging of yeast. The experiments that are now proposed are aimed at elucidating the molecular mechanisms regulating longevity. I will examine how a novel anti-aging molecule that we discovered increases life span by modulating longevity- and disease-related processes in cellular organelles called mitochondria. This knowledge is fundamental to understand the molecular defects underlying numerous disorders of aging, including neurodegenerative diseases caused by mitochondrial dysfunction, and lays the foundation for future therapeutic approaches to their treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Rôle de la Stearoyl-CoA Désaturase1 (SCD1) dans le cancer du sein.
Keywords-MotsClés: ACIDES GRAS MONOINSATURES; METABOLISME D'ACIDS GRAS; ONCOLOGIE; QPCR; SCD1; SYNTHESE DE NOVO DES ACIDES GRAS; WESTERN BLOT
Abstract-Résumé: En 2011, selon la societe canadienne du cancer, en moyenne chaque jour, 64 canadiennes recevront un diagnostic de cancer du sein et 14 canadiennes meurent des suites de cette maladie tous les jours. Le cancer du sein reste l'un des cancers le plus rependu chez les femmes, mais heureusement grace au depistage precoce et l'amelioration du traitement le taux de survie a atteint 88% entre 2004 et 2006.  Selon des etudes menees ulterieurement, l'echec du traitement et la recurrence de cette maladie sont dus a un developpement d'une certaine resistance aux medicaments utilises. Il est donc imperatif de trouver de nouvelles cibles therapeutiques autres que celles vises par les traitements actuels. Notre etude vise une enzyme responsable de la production des acides gras monoinsatures, la SCD1, qui se trouve particulierement augmente lors de l'apparition de certains cancers notamment le cancer du sein. La SCD1 aurait comme role de fournir des acides gras insatures pour la fabrication de nouvelles membranes lors de la croissance des cellules cancereuses. Nos resultats demontrent une nette augmentation de la SCD1 dans des cellules provenant du cancer du sein sous influence d'oestrogenes. Le but de la presente etude est de demontrer l'implication de la SCD1 dans le cancer du sein, et son importance pour la croissance tumorale hormono-dependante. Notre strategie de recherche vise d'abord a elucider les mecanismes cellulaires par lesquels la SCD1 exercerait ces fonctions, par la suite l'effet d'une diminution de cette enzyme sur l'evolution  tumorale oestrogene-dependante. Notre etude pourrait pointer la SCD1 comme cible therapeutique, ou bien l'une des proteines cellulaires qui serait sous son emprise capable d'induire une reponse  favorable au traitement. Une telle decouverte permettra de cibler une population a recepteur d'oestrogene positive du cancer du sein a l'heure de la medecine personnalisee.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular epidemiology and gonorrhea transmission dynamics: Implications for prevention and control
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOSTATISTICS; DISEASE TRANSMISSION; EPIDEMIOLOGY; GONORRHEA; INFECTIOUS DISEASE; MODELLING; SEXUAL NETWORKS; SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTION; SOCIAL NETWORK ANALYSIS; STI
Abstract-Résumé: Gonorrhea infection poses a significant public health threat and is the second most common sexually transmitted infection (STI) both internationally and in Canada. In 2009 Saskatchewan had the highest gonorrhea rate of any province, and well over double the rate in many other provinces.  Gonorrhea and other STIs are not uniformly distributed across sexually active populations. Rather, transmission patterns reflect sexual networks and inter-relationships within defined groups of people. Analysis of these networks can reveal key individuals or core groups responsible for sustaining infection within the network and indicate the best targets for intervention.  The objective of this research is to link molecular data (information about transmission of specific strains) and traditional epidemiological data (contact tracing, social network analysis) to develop a new approach that will improve understanding of gonorrhea transmission patterns in populations. Analysis of this information will reveal transmission patterns, significant risk factors for transmission, and effectiveness of current and potential strategies for prevention and treatment.  Molecular and epidemiological data from China has already been collected and analysis is underway. Molecular data from Saskatchewan also exists; the next phase of the project involves collecting the epidemiological data for Saskatchewan. The existence of two datasets allows for comparison of the techniques developed through this research to determine their applicability on a global scale. The high rate of gonorrhea and rapid rise of other sexually transmitted diseases-including HIV-in Saskatchewan highlights the importance of understanding transmission dynamics and using this information to develop better prevention and treatment protocols in the province, the country, and internationally.

TitreApplicationTitle: Translating Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging to the Clinic: Robust, Simple, and Quantitative Measurement of Brain Physiology
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD OXYGENATION LEVEL DEPENDENT FUNCTIONAL MRI (BOLD FMRI); FMRI CALIBRATION; NEUROIMAGING; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; QUANTITATIVE FMRI
Abstract-Résumé: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is considered by many physicians as one of the most important innovations in medicine over the last 25 years. An MRI technique known as BOLD functional MRI (fMRI) has been an invaluable tool for cognitive neuroscience due to its ability to localize brain activity. With BOLD, which stands for blood oxygenation level dependent, contrast arises from a complex series of physiological events involving changes in neuronal activity, brain metabolism, blood flow, and blood volume. By calibrating the BOLD signal prior to scanning the patient, these hemodynamic and metabolic changes in the brain can be separately measured. However, current calibration techniques require complex gas inhalation experiments during scanning and can be uncomfortable for subjects.  The proposed research seeks to bring quantitative fMRI into the clinical context by developing a novel gas-free BOLD calibration technique that would dramatically simplify the process. The technique is based on measuring a fundamental MRI parameter that is dependent on the concentration of deoxyhemoglobin in the brain. It will be developed by scanning healthy, young adults. In addition to this, a computer model of cerebral vasculature will be developed to simulate fMRI signals produced under varying physiological states. This model will provide a testbed in which new calibration techniques can be developed before having to apply them to humans, therefore saving time and money.  The broad goal of this work is to take fMRI from simply addressing where activations are taking place using BOLD to making quantitative fMRI clinically viable for addressing how much activations are affecting physiological parameters. Achieving this has the potential to significantly improve the assessment of diseases that alter brain physiology, such as stroke and Alzheimer's disease. By making BOLD calibration simple, robust, and safe, this project is a critical step towards making this goal a reality.

TitreApplicationTitle: Social modeling in pediatric pain
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDREN; EXPERIMENTAL METHODS; FAMILY FACTORS; HEALTH BEHAVIOURS; PAIN RESPONSES; PEDIATRIC PAIN; SEX AND GENDER; SOCIAL MODELING
Abstract-Résumé: Families provide an important context in which pediatric pain should be understood, and previous research has shown that how parents react to pain can have an influence on how their children react to and experience pain. How children learn from their parent's modeling of pain behaviours may be influenced by the sex of the child and parent; however, the majority of pediatric pain research on parent-child interactions has only focused on mothers.   The proposed study will examine the impact of watching a parent's reaction to pain on children's own pain experience. Two hundred and forty parent-child pairs (50% fathers) will each complete the cold pressor task (CPT), which is a safe and commonly used method of inducing mild to moderate levels of pain in the lab. Children will first watch their parent complete the CPT, and will then complete the CPT themselves. Parents will be randomly assigned to display a natural, exaggerated, or minimized pain expression during the CPT. The pain experience of the parent and child will be measured with self-reports of pain intensity, pain threshold and tolerance, as well as coding of their facial expressions. Analysis will examine whether the child's pain behaviour and reports of pain are influenced by the parent's behaviours pain behaviour, and whether this differs based on the sex of the parent and child.   This research will help increase our understanding of the role of fathers in pediatric pain, which has been understudied to date. The results of this study will also contribute to explanations of how pain behaviours can be learned through social modeling by children from their parents, which will have clinical implications for family-based interventions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health perceptions of obese individuals and the impact of public health messaging
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE; CRITICAL MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; EATING DISORDERS; ETHNOGRAPHY; HEALTH PERCEPTIONS; MESSAGING; OBESITY; PUBLIC HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence of obesity in Canada has increased over the last 25 years. Nearly one quarter of Canadians (24.1%) are obese. As obesity is associated with health conditions including diabetes, hypertension, heart disease, and certain cancers, it has negative effects on individuals' health and health care costs. However, less discussed than the negative effects on health and resulting burden on the health care system, is the widespread discrimination faced by obese people in their relationships, workplaces, and the healthcare system. The majority of public health messaging encourages weight loss and focuses on the negative effects of excess weight. Unfortunately, weight loss can be difficult to achieve and maintain, due to environmental, social, biological, and genetic factors. However, there is evidence that improvements in health outcomes are possible with increased physical activity and healthier eating habits, without accompanying weight loss. Some studies have even shown that being slightly overweight may be beneficial in reducing risk of mortality. Despite this research, public health messaging continues to focus on excess weight as being necessarily unhealthy. While obesity is a serious health concern, messages that focus exclusively on obesity as problematic may contribute to weight discrimination and be disempowering to obese individuals, rather than motivational. For my study, I will investigate how people who identify as overweight, obese, or as eating disorder sufferers describe their health, what they prioritize in regard to their health and wellbeing, and how this affects and is affected by their experiences, particularly in regard to their interactions with medical professionals and in encountering messaging from public health and mass media. This research has the potential to develop public health messaging that will incorporate what Canadians view as essential to their health and well-being and inspire pro-active and empowering health behaviours.

TitreApplicationTitle: The suppression of DNA mismatch repair by the oncoprotein NPM-ALK.
Keywords-MotsClés: DNA MISMATCH REPAIR; IMMUNOBLOTTING; IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; LYMPHOMA; ONCOGENIC TYROSINE KINASE; POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATION; PROTEIN FUNCTION; SITE-DIRECTED MUTAGENESIS; TISSUE CULTURE; TUMORIGENESIS
Abstract-Résumé: There are many mechanisms known to contribute to cancer formation, one of which is related to a group of proteins called tyrosine kinases. In normal cells, tyrosine kinases are known to play key roles in regulating many important cellular functions. In some cancer cells, tyrosine kinases are over-active, thereby altering a wide range of cellular processes and often leading to uncontrolled cell growth and tumor formation. Our research group has been studying a cancer-forming tyrosine kinase called NPM-ALK for the past 9 years. Recently, we discovered for the first time that NPM-ALK can induce a cellular abnormality called genetic instability by interfering with a critical cellular function known as DNA mismatch repair. DNA mismatch repair normally functions to safeguard the integrity of our genes and protect them from potentially harmful mutations. Genetic instability is often a key feature seen in many types of cancer. The main purpose of this study is to investigate this novel cancer promoting mechanism and to further our understanding of how tyrosine kinases, when aberrantly over-active, can alter the capacity for the cell to undergo successful DNA mismatch repair. In the future, we aim to develop new therapeutic approaches based on the new information derived from this study.

TitreApplicationTitle: The effects of autophagy knockdown in breast cancer cells using in vivo xenograft models
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTOPHAGY; BREAST CANCER; CHEMOTHERAPY; DRUG RESISTANCE; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; XENOGRAFT MODEL
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer continues to be the most commonly diagnosed cancer and one of the leading causes of cancer death in women in Canada, as well as worldwide. Breast cancer is not a single disease; it is made up of several subtypes that have distinct molecular characteristics and clinical outcomes. In our project we study one of these subtypes, triple-negative breast cancer that is more commonly diagnosed in younger women. It is the most aggressive form of breast cancer with extremely poor prognosis.  For triple-negative breast cancer, chemotherapy remains the main therapeutic option. However, tumors that initially respond to chemotherapy often eventually develop resistance. Previous studies have shown that in response to stress (such as chemotherapy or radiation therapy) cancer cells activate a process called autophagy ("self-eating"). Autophagy helps cancer cells survive stressing conditions, and therefore is considered to be one of the mechanisms of drug resistance. In our study we are using cell lines and mice models to find out whether by blocking autophagy in triple-negative breast cancer cells we can enhance therapeutic response and overcome treatment resistance. We are aiming to propose a new strategy in the treatment of triple-negative breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of the bHLH transcription factor family in planarian neural differentiation and brain development
Keywords-MotsClés: C. ELEGANS; DEVELOPMENTAL GUIDANCE QUEUES; GUIDED MEMBRANE EXTENSION; MEMBRANE STRUCTURE; MUSCLE ARMS; PROTEIN LOCALIZATION; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Cell guidance events are key in the development of multicellular organisms. In higher animals with complex tissue and body structures, the ability for cells to extend processes that are guided to very specific targets is vital. Mutations in pathways responsible for such guidance events can result in tissue malformation and thus in disease. Our lab is focused on determining how cell membranes undergo guided extension. We study this process using the animal model Caenorhabiditis elegans, a free living roundworm (nematode). C. elegans has proven to be a powerful model for this phenomenon because it has guidance mechanisms that are conserved across many species such as in humans. The question we ask is how are cells able to restructure their membrane and produce extrusions that are guided towards specific targets. Nematode muscles extend processes (known as muscle arms) towards neurons, which can be exploited to discover how this guided membrane extension occurs. Recent discoveries in the our lab have determined a novel guidance signal known as MADD-4. MADD-4 is secreted by neurons in the worm which attract muscle arms towards them, to allow communication between the neuron and muscle. MADD-4 has orthologues in mammals, which suggests that MADD-4 may play a guidance role in other organisms. We currently know that MADD-4 attracts muscle arms, but we do not know exactly what membrane structural changes must occur before, throughout, and after a guidance event. To address this issue, I will be using confocal microscopy to image this process in real time, which will allow us to demonstrate how proteins localize over time, and in what manner the muscle arms grow. Additionally I will be culturing C. elegans muscle cells which will allow us to manipulate and observe the guidance process at the cellular level. Using both in vivo and in vitro techniques will allow us to get a deeper understanding of membrane guidance, which may shed some light on various developmental diseases.

Abstract-Résumé: Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma or DIPG are a type of brainstem tumour that affects young children on average around the ages of 6 or 7. Is is the number one cause of brain tumour related death in children with most patients not surviving longer than 12 months. This goal of this project is to look at the differences and similarities between proteins found in DIPG and other brain cancers found in children in order to develop treatment targets that would be beneficial for children with DIPG.

TitreApplicationTitle: Incidence and prognosis of post-traumatic headache (PTH)
Keywords-MotsClés: EPIDEMIOLOGY; HEAD INJURY; INCIDENCE; POPULATION ANALYSIS; POST-TRAUMATIC HEADACHE; PROGNOSIS; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW; TRAFFIC INJURY; WHIPLASH
Abstract-Résumé: Traffic injuries are a common cause of pain and disability in society.  More than half of those injured suffer from post-traumatic headache (PTH).  Despite aggressive treatment, PTH can remain debilitating and thus costly among adults who are working and caring for their families.  There is currently very little research on PTH after traffic injury, resulting in a diminished capacity to make informed decisions about effective patient care and policy.    To improve patient management, there is a critical need to investigate the burden of PTH in society, in addition to examining its course, outcome and likelihood of recovery.  The objectives of this research are to (1) systematically review and synthesize the scientific literature to address the incidence, course, and prognosis of PTH; (2) analyze the incidence, course, and prognosis of PTH from a large population-based study of traffic injuries from the province of Saskatchewan; (3) conduct a secondary analysis of the course and prognosis of PTH from the University Health Network - Whiplash Intervention Trial, Ontario; and (4) analyze the incidence, course, and prognosis of PTH from a large Swedish cohort of traffic injuries (formed at the Karolinska Institute).  This work will bring together experts from Scandinavia and Canada to advance our understanding of PTH after traffic collisions and identify the state of the scientific literature, including the critical knowledge gaps. Results form this work will inform future patient-centred research, practice and policy.  This involves the delivery of high quality, cost-effective health care that ultimately leads to better health outcomes for the patient.

TitreApplicationTitle: Complete Genome Sequence Based Genetic Analysis of Monozygotic Twins Discordant for Schizophrenia and Their Families
Keywords-MotsClés: GENOME SEQUENCING; GENOMIC VARIATION; MONOZYGOTIC TWINS; SCHIZOPHRENIA; TWIN DISCORDANCE
Abstract-Résumé: Recent results suggest that human genomes show much more variation between one another than was once assumed. No two individuals, including identical twins who begin life as a single entity, are genetically identical. This proposal seeks to first assess the number of DNA sequence differences each individual has as compared to what is understood to be the consensus human sequence. This will allow for greater understanding of the amount of genetic variation in human populations. In addition, this proposal seeks to identify differences between identical twins at the DNA sequence level through the comparison of their complete genome sequences. This study will also include one pair of parents in the analysis in order to determine the source of the identified changes; that is, whether the changes were inherited from the parents or whether they arose spontaneously. The twins in this study will be unique, as in each twin pair, one twin will have been diagnosed with schizophrenia while the other twin is not affected with the disease.  The experimental design will therefore also allow for the potential to identify genetic changes that may contribute to the occurrence of schizophrenia. The latter has implications for the treatment of schizophrenia, a debilitating illness that affects greater than 1% of the population worldwide and poses a major health and social burden to our society.

TitreApplicationTitle: Systematic identification of resistance mechanisms to HER2-targeted therapies in breast cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: COMBINATION THERAPY; HER2-POSITIVE BREAST CANCER; HER2-TARGETED THERAPY; LAPATINIB; LENTIVIRAL SHRNA SCREEN; THERAPEUTIC RESISTANCE; TRASTUZUMAB; XENOGRAPH
Abstract-Résumé: Approximately 15-20% of breast cancer patients are diagnosed with human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2 (HER2) amplification or overexpression and are at a greater risk for disease progression and poor clinical outcome. HER2, therefore, represents an attracted target for pharmacological intervention. At present, there are two HER2-targeted therapies approved for the treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer including trastuzumab (a therapeutic antibody) and lapatinib (a small molecule inhibitor). These HER2-targeted therapies have shown clinical activity alone or in combination with chemotherapy, and clinical trials are underway to explore the combination of trastuzumab and lapatinib together. However, many patients would relapse during the course of treatment, suggesting the existence of intrinsic or acquired resistance to these two HER2-targeted therapies. In my research study, I will try to identify the resistance mechanisms to trastuzumab and lapatinib via genome-wide lentiviral shRNA screens. The resistance-conferring genes identified from trastuzumab and lapatinib screens will be analyzed to find if any common resistance-conferring pathways exist. If successful, I will further investigate the efficacy of therapeutically targeting these pathways along with trastuzumab and/or lapatinib. My proposed research study has the potential to provide a genome-wide identification of resistance mechanisms to the two currently approved HER2-targeted therapies. The insights gained from my study may be applied to guide the development of novel treatment combination to treat HER2-positive breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Elucidating the Tim-3 Signaling Pathway to Identify Therapeutic Targets to Restore Immune Functioning in Progressive HIV Patients
Keywords-MotsClés: CD8 T-CELL EXHAUSTION; GALECTIN-9; HIV; IMMUNE CELL SIGNALLING; IMMUNOLOGY; THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION; TIM-3
Abstract-Résumé: While the use of Highly Active Anti-Retroviral Therapies (HAART) are effective at controlling viral replication in HIV-1 infected individuals, a treatment to completely eradicate HIV-1 infected cells remains undeveloped. Natural immune processes in the body can clear HIV-infected cells, through the CD8 cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) response, but is defeated by a process called exhaustion where the CTL response is diminished. This exhaustion is characterized by a biomarker called T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3 (Tim-3), which resides on the surface of CD8 T-cells. Interaction of this molecule with its binding partner, Galectin-9 (Gal-9), results in a signaling pathway which ultimately disables the CD8 T-cell and leads to exhaustion. Our studies have shown that disrupting the Tim-3 and Gal-9 interaction helps rescue this CTL response. Thus, the goal of this project is to determine this signaling pathway, establish how these CD8 T-cells cease to be effective and disrupt this pathway to rescue immune function. Biochemical and molecular biology techniques will be used to isolate Tim-3 and study the interactions with its binding partners in the cell. Once characterized, these Tim-3 binding partners will be knocked-down to prevent their expression and disrupt the Tim-3 signaling pathway, which is hypothesized to rescue the CTL response, in a manner similar to the disruption of the Tim3-Gal-9 interaction. This would allow the immune system to battle the HIV-1 infection naturally. Thus, characterizing this pathway may lead to therapeutic targets for restoring CTL responses in HIV patients and the design of new interventions, which, in combination with HAART, could potentially cure those infected with HIV-1.

TitreApplicationTitle: A Lifestyle Intervention to Improve Body Composition in Overweight and Obese Children
Keywords-MotsClés: BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS; BODY COMPOSITION; BONE DENSITY; CALCIUM; CHILDREN; DAIRY; DUAL ENERGY X-RAY ABSORPTIOMETRY; NUTRITION; OBESITY; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY
Abstract-Résumé: Although genetics and environment are well founded etiological factors that may cause child obesity, research typically focuses on the modifiable factors: diet and physical activity.  Canadian surveys reveal that children are not eating according to Canada's Food Guide, particularly milk products, and are physically inactive.  Despite readily available Government resources aimed at reducing obesity, childhood obesity rates have not declined.  Experts suggest that prevention/treatment programs must start at preschool age.  Programs using age-appropriate tools specifically targeted at families with school age children are lacking, as are the data showing the effects of these programs on healthy development of body and bone composition.  The proposed study will seek to fill this significant omission in childhood obesity research by examining the impact of using readily available Canadian reference tools in a randomized controlled trial (RCT) designed as a family-centered lifestyle intervention.  This RCT consists of 3 groups (1 control, 1 standard intervention, 1 intensive intervention).  In brief, 150 overweight/ obese children 6 to 8.5 y old will be followed for one year. The two intervention groups will immediately participate in six interventions sessions.  The control group will be monitored and will receive counseling at the end of the study.   Each session is individualized to address eating and activity behaviors and to set goals within the context of what is realistic.  Children randomized to the intensive group will be encouraged to consume the recommended amount of dairy servings for 9 y old (4 servings/ day versus standard 2 servings per day) to better support muscle and bone health.  This study will not only help the participating families, but also offer public health agencies and health care professionals current insight to the specific counseling techniques required to assist families in their pursuit of healthy lifestyle choices.

TitreApplicationTitle: Perception de la douleur d'autrui chez les professionnels de la santé: Implication pour l'intervention.
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNTITION; DOULEUR; EVALUATION DE LA DOULEUR; IMAGERIE CEREBRALE FONCTIONNELLE; INTERACTION SOCIALE; INTERVENTION EN SANTE; NEUROSCIENCES SOCIALES; REGULATION EMOTIONELLE
Abstract-Résumé: L'exposition reguliere a la douleur d'autrui vecue par les professionnels de la sante est associee a une tendance a sous-estimer la douleur des patients par rapport a l'evaluation faite par les patients eux-memes ou par des participants ne travaillant pas dans le milieu de la sante. Des etudes d'imagerie cerebrale demontrent que ces cliniciens presentent, lorsque compares a la population generale, moins d'activite dans les regions associees a la perception des aspects affectifs de la douleur d'autrui, mais davantage d'activite dans les regions associees au controle de sa reaction emotionnelle face a une expression de douleur. Ces resultats pourraient en partie expliquer le soulagement souvent inadequat de la douleur. Pourtant, aucune etude n'a etabli de lien entre le degre d'exposition a la douleur d'autrui, les changements cerebraux associes a cette exposition et le traitement des patients en douleur. Ce projet vise a etudier l'influence de l'exposition reguliere a la douleur d'autrui sur les mecanismes neurophysiologiques et les comportements d'aide associes a la perception de la douleur chez l'autre, et ce, dans le contexte de l'intervention en sante. Pour se faire, des cliniciens ainsi que des participants controles participeront a une serie d'etudes comportementales et en neuroimagerie fonctionnelle les placant en contexte d'evaluation et de traitement de patients en douleur. Les comportements d'aide face a la douleur des patients rencontres lors de ces mises en situation et la reponse cerebrale face a cette douleur seront compares pour evaluer les differences neurophysiologiques et comportementales dues a l'exposition reguliere a la douleur chez les professionnels de la sante. Ces connaissances pourront servir de base pour developper des interventions et des formations visant a sensibiliser  et les intervenants du milieu de la sante sur les consequences de l'exposition reguliere a la douleur et leurs effets possibles sur leur pratique.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of inflammation in the pathophysiology of intrauterine growth restriction and pre-eclampsia
Keywords-MotsClés: DOPPLER ULTRASOUND; HAEMOSTASIS; HEMODYNAMICS; INFLAMMATION; INTRAUTERINE GROWTH RESTRICTION; INTRAVITAL MICROSCOPY; PATHOPHYSIOLGY; PRE-ECLAMPSIA; PREGNANCY; RADIOTELEMETRY
Abstract-Résumé: Many women develop diseases of pregnancy, which can harm both mother and baby. Babies who are born too small are referred to as growth restricted. These babies are at an increased risk of suffering from diabetes and heart disease in their adult lives.  Some growth-restricted babies are born to mothers who develop a severe disease of pregnancy called pre-eclampsia. Women with pre-eclampsia develop dangerously high blood pressure that can lead to death. These women are also at risk of developing heart disease later in life. There are no effective treatments for these conditions.  We propose that increased inflammation during pregnancy causes growth restricted babies and pre-eclampsia. We believe that when blood flow to the developing baby is too little, the baby can't grow properly. The placenta is the organ responsible for nourishing the baby with mother's blood. We believe that the placenta does not develop properly if there is too much inflammation.  This can result in reduced blood going to the placenta. Inflammation can damage the placenta, causing it to release substances that can harm the mother's blood vessels. Damaged blood vessels occur in pre-eclampsia.  By injecting pregnant rats with a bacterial substance that causes inflammation, we will test if inflammation decreases placental blood flow. We will compare the placentas and babies from these rats with those of healthy rats who were not injected with the inflammatory substance. Using modern tools, we will look at blood flow in the placenta. We will determine if inflammation damages placental blood vessels and whether blood clots form, which could cut off blood flow to the baby. We will measure blood pressure in the rats to see if it increases. Using treatments that prevent inflammation we will see if we can prevent growth restriction and pre-eclampsia. If research can prevent or treat these diseases, it may be possible to prevent diseases like diabetes and heart disease later in life.

TitreApplicationTitle: Age, sympathetic activation, and the brain-heart connection
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; CARDIAC CONTRACTILITY; CORTICAL AUTONOMIC NETWORK; FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; ISOMETRIC EXERCISE; MUSCLE SYMPATHETIC NERVE ACTIVITY; SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM
Abstract-Résumé: The autonomic nervous system plays a critical role in regulating functions of the heart and blood vessels and specific regions in the brain are also involved in this control. There are two branches of the autonomic nervous system: parasympathetic, which serves to decrease heart rate, and sympathetic, which increases heart rate. With increasing age, parasympathetic activity decreases, while sympathetic increases, resulting in an altered balance of the two branches that is associated with cardiovascular disease. Previous research has not examined how brain regions involved in control of heart rate are different in older adults, with higher sympathetic activity, than in younger adults. This series of projects will first verify that sympathetic outflow to the heart and potentially more peripheral areas of the body are higher in older adults both at rest and during hand grip exercise. Hand grip exercise will be used to increase sympathetic activity in older adults even further beyond baseline levels. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) will be used to examine how brain regions involved in heart rate control are different in young and older adults during sympathetic activation that is stimulated by the hand grip exercise. The results are expected to provide important information regarding the impact of aging on cardiovascular health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Foreign-born status, physical mobility and the built environment: The experience of urban dwelling older adults
Keywords-MotsClés: CANADIAN COMMUNITY HEALTH SURVEY; COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; EVALUATION RESEARCH; FOREIGN-BORN STATUS; MULTI-METHODS; OLDER ADULTS; PHYSICAL MOBILITY
Abstract-Résumé: The Canadian population is aging, and among older adults, limited mobility predicts death and is a risk factor for disability, social exclusion and poor quality of life. Mobility is the physical ability of humans to work or move themselves within their communities. As mobility promotes independence of older adults, is also essential to understand how the built environment (BE) influences their health, mobility and wellbeing. The built environment is the combination of individual elements of towns and cities where people work, live and play (e.g. land use, density and connectivity on the macro-scale and sidewalks, benches and lighting on the micro-scale). Older Canadians are more ethnically diverse than the general population, and immigrants comprise 28% of the seniors population. Recent international literature suggests that some foreign-born older adults are at a higher risk for limited mobility. My study seeks to: 1) describe how foreign-born status and the BE influence the mobility of urban dwelling older adults and, 2) develop, implement and evaluate a program (e.g. walking or bus buddy group) that supports the mobility of foreign-born older adults, in partnership with South Vancouver Neighbourhood House. My study consists of 3 parts: i) analysis of data from the Canadian Community Health Survey (CCHS), ii) interviews with foreign-born older adults and iii) an evaluation of a community-based mobility intervention. Participants will be selected from neighbourhoods that either support or inhibit mobility.

TitreApplicationTitle: High-throughput sequencing approach to identify bipolar disorder genes
Keywords-MotsClés: AFFECTIVE DISORDERS; BIPOLAR DISORDER; GENE EXPRESSION; GENOMICS; HUMAN GENETICS; LITHIUM; MENTAL HEALTH; PSYCHIATRY; SEQUENCING
Abstract-Résumé: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a common mental health problem that affects 1-2% of the population.  The most effective treatment is Lithium, with results in 50-70 % of patients, but this drug's mechanism of action is not understood. There is strong evidence to suggest that BD can be inherited, given that one of the highest BD risk factors is having an affected first-degree relative. This implies that BD risk is transmitted through the genetic material. Thus, scientists have been looking for genes that cause BD when they malfunction due to mutations, with little success thus far. This is likely because (1) BD is actually an umbrella term for closely related psychiatric conditions that are difficult to differentiate in the clinic, and (2) alterations in individual sets of genes are responsible in each patient.  My research will identify genetic alterations that lead to increased risk of BD. I will do this by addressing the two problems mentioned above. Firstly, I will focus on families with many affected members who have responded well to Lithium treatment. This helps to define a sub-group of patients who have the same form of the illness. Secondly, I will find patient-specific mutations by probing all the genetic material at once. To achieve this I will use high-throughput sequencing, a novel technique that provides information about all of a person's genetic material in a matter of days, and identify all the individual's genetic alterations. By comparing the complete genetic profiles of BD patients and healthy individuals, I will identify the set of inherited mutations that cause the disease in each patient.  This work will lead to an enhanced patient-specific understanding of BD, particularly as regards treatment response. Consequently, my results will lead to the development of better ways to diagnose and treat this devastating illness. Given the social and economic burden of BD, investigating individual predisposition will have an enormous social impact.

TitreApplicationTitle: Transcranial magnetic stimulation may potentially enhance spatial learning
Keywords-MotsClés: GLOBAL POSITIONING SYSTEMS; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; RESPONSE LEARNING; SPATIAL LEARNING; SPATIAL MEMORY; VIRTUAL NAVIGATION STRATEGIES; VIRTUAL REALITY
Abstract-Résumé: Much of how we navigate depends on how well we know our environment. Global Positioning System (GPS) devices facilitate navigation by directing us to a destination, thereby eliminating the need to have prior knowledge of our environment and use our sense of direction. Indeed, when we navigate using a GPS, we no longer pay attention to the environmental landmarks that surround us, such as buildings and shops. Being aware of landmarks is the hallmark of spatial learning, as it allows us to form a cognitive, or mental, map of our environment. Spatial learning is mediated by the hippocampus, a brain region that is also responsible for the formation of episodic memories (memories of events). Therefore, we hypothesize that GPS navigation reduces or eliminates spatial learning, and by doing so, decreases hippocampal function and grey matter.  We will test two groups of healthy young adults: regular GPS users and control participants with no GPS experience. We will assess their spatial learning by testing them on three virtual navigation paradigms, in which they will have to learn the location of landmarks and objects in various environments. We will examine their brain function and grey matter while they perform a virtual navigation task in a magnetic resonance imaging scanner.       We expect regular GPS users to show poorer spatial learning than non-GPS users in the three virtual navigation tasks. In addition, we anticipate that GPS users will have reduced brain activity and grey matter in the hippocampus compared to non-GPS users.  Low hippocampal grey matter is a cause for concern because it is a risk factor for cognitive deficits as well as neurological and psychiatric disorders (e.g. Alzheimer's disease). If using a GPS hinders spatial learning and the hippocampus, then we may devise new ways of using the GPS that will engage spatial learning and promote healthy cognition and aging.

Keywords-MotsClés: ABC TRANSPORTERS; FLUORESENCE SPECTROSCOPY; KATP CHANNELS; NMR SPECTROSCOPY; NUCLEOTIDE BINDING DOMAIS; PHOSPHORYLATION; PROTEIN DYNAMICS; PROTEIN STRUCTURE; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; SULFONYLUREA RECEPTORS
Abstract-Résumé: Healthy hearts require specific levels of potassium to function properly. The amount of potassium that enters heart cells is controlled by a protein, SUR2A. Problems with this protein are responsible for a number of cardiovascular disorders, such as heart attacks and cardiac disease.  We will use a technique very similar to medical MRI to obtain a three-dimensional picture of healthy and disease SUR2A proteins. These experiments will also provide information as to how the three-dimensional shape of SUR2A changes with time, which is important for understanding protein function.  We will also focus on the regions of SUR2A which are the sites of disease causing mutations.  These regions are known as nucleotide binding domains (NBDs) and help to control whether the protein allows or prevents potassium from entering the cells.  These studies promise to enhance our understanding of how SUR2A mutations lead to cardiovascular disorders. This very specific and molecular-level knowledge will help to design new drugs and treatments to help improve the quality of life for Canadians with cardiac diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'impact de l'entraînement des fonctions exécutives sur la plasticité cérébrale des personnes âgées hypertendues.
Keywords-MotsClés: ENTRAINEMENT COGNITIF; FONCTIONS EXECUTIVES; HYPERTENSION ARTERIELLE; IMAGERIE OPTIQUE; NEUROPSYCHOLOGIE DU VIEILLISSEMENT; VIEILLISSEMENT COGNITIF
Abstract-Résumé: L'hypertension arterielle est une maladie silencieuse qui touche pres de la moitie des personnes agees de 65 ans et plus au Canada et qui, en plus de produire des effets deleteres sur le systeme cardiovasculaire, est associee a un risque plus eleve de developper une maladie neurodegenerative telle que la maladie d'Alzheimer. Cette categorie de maladies constitue la premiere cause d'invalidite et d'institutionnalisation chez les aines, ce qui exerce un poids significatif sur le systeme de sante au Canada. Des recherches anterieures ont demontre que certaines fonctions avancees du cerveau, comme la capacite d'alterner entre plusieurs taches differentes, de planifier et d'organiser efficacement l'information ou encore de resoudre des problemes sont particulierement touchees par l'hypertension. Cela serait cause par des alterations de certaines regions specifiques du cerveau qui sont responsables de l'efficacite de ces processus mentaux. La premiere partie du projet de recherche vise a mieux comprendre la nature des atteintes du cerveau provoquees par l'hypertension, grace a une technique d'imagerie cerebrale. La comprehension des effets de l'hypertension sur le cerveau s'avere essentielle pour bien orienter les strategies d'intervention. La seconde partie du projet a pour objectif de verifier s'il est possible de renverser ou de ralentir les deficits observes chez les personnes agees souffrant d'hypertension par le biais d'un programme de stimulation des fonctions intellectuelles. La demonstration de l'efficacite d'un tel programme pourrait permettre de developper de nouvelles methodes d'intervention afin de preserver le bon fonctionnement intellectuel des personnes agees qui presentent de l'hypertension arterielle, et ainsi contribuer a maintenir leur bien-etre et leur autonomie.

TitreApplicationTitle: MicroRNAs as modulators of lung cancer targeted therapy and novel predictors of drug response
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CHEMOTHERAPY RESPONSE; GENE EXPRESSION; GENETICS; LUNG CANCER; MICRORNA; PATHWAY ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide. This is largely due to the typical late stage of diagnosis and a lack of effective treatment options. The ability to predict which drugs will be most effective for individual lung cancer patients would greatly improve overall survival. This study aims to identify such predictive biomarkers by investigating the hypotheses that short RNA molecules called microRNAs (miRNAs) are deregulated in accordance with drug resistance and sensitivity, and therefore can be used to predict treatment outcome. miRNAs are major regulators of gene expression, and have a well established role in a variety of cancer types including lung cancer, although  the role of miRNAs in lung cancer drug response is largely unknown. By comparing cases that responded and did not respond to specific drugs, this study aims to identify miRNAs that are associated with drug resistance and sensitivity. Further, this study aims to identify which genes and biochemical pathways are regulated by these resistance- and sensitivity-associated miRNAs to gain knowledge about the mechanisms of drug response. The pathways identified here could be targeted to improve drug response; therefore, the final aim of this study is to use this knowledge of drug response-associated miRNA pathway regulation in order to design new, more effective drug regimens. Ideally, existing FDA approved drugs will be used in combination with the drug of interest to improve treatment response. This work will directly impact the health of Canadians by identifying novel predictors of drug response to direct current treatment options to those most likely to respond. It will also generate much needed insight into the biology governing drug response that may be used for the development of new drug combinations to improve treatment efficacy and patient survival.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigation into the Viridans Group Streptococci within Adult Cystic Fibrosis Patients
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE; BACTERIAL PATHOGENESIS; CYSTIC FIBROSIS; MICROBIOLOGY; PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA; STREPTOCOCCI; SYNERGENS; TRANSPOSON MUTAGENESIS; VIRULENCE
Abstract-Résumé: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a genetic disease that affects over 4,000 Canadians with 1 of every 25 healthy people carrying the diseased gene. The disease results in thick mucus building up in the lower lungs, an area that is otherwise free of bacteria in healthy individuals, but results in long-term infections for people with CF. The average age for people with CF is 46.7 with no cure to date. Despite the fact that CF is caused by a mutated gene, 90% of people die as a result of these chronic bacterial infections. Traditionally, only specific bacteria have been studied but recently it has been shown that otherwise ignored bacteria are playing a role in CF disease progression. These bacteria come from the group of bacteria known as streptococci. The streptococci are carried in healthy individuals in the upper respiratory tract and are thought not to normally cause disease. However, it is our hypothesis, based upon recent studies, that these streptococci are contributing to CF disease progression. One idea is they may be causing disease by acting as pathogens, such as is the case with the streptococci that cause strep throat or flesh-eating disease. Another theory is that they are contributing to antibiotic resistance seen in CF patients, as the streptococci can easily become resistant to drugs such as penicillin. The final idea is that the streptococci are interacting with other bacteria in the CF lung to make the pathogens even more virulent or dangerous. One of these bacteria, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, is well-known to cause infections in CF patients and some recent studies have shown certain streptococci make P. aeruginosa even more pathogenic than if it were alone, otherwise known as a virulent synergistic relationship. By studying the role of the streptococci, which are extremely abundant in the CF lung, we can better understand disease progression and target therapy towards appropriate microbes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Modeling the interactions of Vaccinia virus in the blood to achieve efficient systemic delivery
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIBODIES; COMPLEMENT SYSTEM; INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY; ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES; SYSTEMIC DELIVERY; VACCINIA VIRUS
Abstract-Résumé: Systemic delivery of oncolytic viruses is the ideal mode of treatment for metastatic disease because metastatic beds can be dispersed or their extent undiscovered. There are however many barriers to the systemic delivery of oncolytic Vaccinia virus that are presented by the innate and acquired immune systems. Most notably, complement and neutralizing antibody, the latter of which is specifically present in the demographic of patients vaccinated against Smallpox, act together to neutralize the virus and induce activation of the immune system. We have identified that complement and antibody in human blood together can neutralize up to 99% of the virus in vitro. The importance of these clearance mechanisms is then amplified when patients are treated with multiple doses and the amount of antibody produced significantly increases. Additionally, we have discovered that the virus partitioned preferentially to the cellular compartment over the plasma, as demonstrated in vitro as well as in blood samples from patients treated intravenously with oncolytic Vaccinia virus as part of a clinical trial. We have identified that the virus preferentially associates with B cells and phagocytic cells such as neutrophils and monocytes, however the red blood cell compartment also represents an important reservoir of virus due to its size. We are currently evaluating the mouse as a surrogate model for the delivery of oncolytic Vaccinia virus to tumours in the face of all the important clearance mechanisms. Through modeling the interactions between the virus and blood components both in vitro, in vivo, and in samples from previous and upcoming clinical trials, we will identify the interactions that are most important in lowering the effective dose of delivery, and undertake the corollary questions; which mechanisms can we manipulate in order to abrogate neutralization, and which ones can we capitalize on to increase delivery.

TitreApplicationTitle: Phospholemman and transport efficiency of Na/K ATPase - implications for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
Keywords-MotsClés: BASAL METABOLIC RATE; HIGH FAT DIET; N3 POLYUNSATURATED FATS; NA/K ATPASE ACTIVITY; NA/K ATPASE TRANSPORT EFFICIENCY; OBESITY; PHOSPHOLEMMAN; POTASSIUM UPTAKE; SODIUM EXTRUSION; WEIGHT MANAGEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: We are currently in the midst of a worldwide obesity pandemic. In Canada, obesity cases have been rising steadily and have been associated with other diseases, such as type II diabetes and hypertension. Obesity is a result of an imbalance on the energetic scale where energy in (caloric intake) is more than energy out. Energy expenditure is a result of a combination of physical activity, energy used to digest, store, and burn food after a meal, and energy used to keep the body's vital organs working. The latter is known as basal metabolic rate (BMR), and importantly a low BMR is a risk factor for obesity. Promoting metabolic inefficiency can increase BMR representing a potential treatment/prevention strategy for obesity. Muscle contraction and relaxation are energy-dependent processes that are partly regulated by sodium ions (Na+) and potassium ions (K+). Specifically, after contraction, Na+ and K+ are required to be replaced to their resting compartments, a process that requires energy and is carried out by specialized Na+/K+ pumps. Thus, Na+ and K+ cycling efficiency in muscle may have significant effects on metabolic rate and susceptibility to obesity. Furthermore, it has been suggested that a protein called phospholemman can reduce the cycling efficiency of Na+/K+ pumps, making the muscle metabolically inefficient. Therefore, the present study proposes to analyze the possibility that phospholemman- mediated Na+ and K+ cycling inefficiency can serve as a possible treatment/prevention mechanism for obesity.

TitreApplicationTitle: AMPK: Mediating the Metabolic Switch In Warburg Metabolism
Keywords-MotsClés: AMP-KINASE; GC/MS; GLYCOLYSIS; LKB1; METABOLISM; METFORMIN; NMR; TCA CYCLE; TUMORS; WESTERN BLOTTING
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer is a disease where cells lose their normal brakes on growth. In order to maintain unregulated cellular growth, cancer cells must be able to control how they acquire and process nutrients such as glucose (sugar) to make energy. One hallmark of many cancer cells is that they increase their nutrient intake and energy production to meet their increased metabolic demands. Thus, many cancers feature distinctly different metabolic activities than healthy cells. These growing tumors must also learn how to survive under suboptimal conditions when oxygen and nutrient supply is scarce. What remains to be seen is why cancer cells feature this distinct metabolism, how important it is to the life of cancer cells, and what is responsible for causing these differences in cancer cell metabolism? By understanding this last point we may find new and unique ways to treat cancer. Our research focuses on a major regulator of energy generation in cancer cells, namely the AMP-activated kinase (AMPK). We have found that AMPK enables cells to switch between breaking down sugars and burning fats to create energy. By doing so, AMPK helps cells to increase their nutrient intake, and to survive periods of low nutrient availability. Through our research, we are trying to understand how AMPK functions to control cancer cell growth. By examining the metabolic changes in cancer cells, we hope to better understand how cancers develop, and hope to identify new ways of treating cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: The effect of female sex hormones on regulating susceptibility and permissivity to HIV-1 infection in primary genital epithelial cells.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIVIRAL PATHWAYS; CELL CULTURE; EPITHELIAL CELLS; FEMALE GENITAL TRACT; FEMALE SEX HORMONES; HIV-1; POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION; VIRAL INFECTION; VIRAL REPLICATION
Abstract-Résumé: The face of the HIV/AIDS epidemic is changing. At the end of 2009 it was estimated that out of the 34 million adults worldwide living with HIV/AIDS, more than half were women. Approximately 40% of annual HIV infections occur through the female genital tract (FGT) via exposure to virus-containing semen. Genital epithelial cells (GECs) are the first cells to encounter HIV following sexual transmission. These cells line the genital tract and act as a biological barrier against infections. The relative contribution of GEC infection to HIV-1 transmission in the genital tract remains poorly understood. Furthermore, the FGT is under the influence of a number of factors, most notably sex hormones. Human clinical studies suggest that female sex hormones, owing to the menstrual cycle, hormonal contraceptives or pregnancy, may regulate susceptibility to HIV; however the mechanism by which this occurs in the genital tract is poorly understood. To address this problem, female GECs will be exposed to physiological concentrations of estrogen, progesterone or synthetic hormonal contraceptives and subsequently infected with HIV-1. We will measure entry and replication of HIV within GECs, as well as other intermediary steps in the HIV infection cycle in order to comprehensively describe how sex hormones regulate GEC susceptibility to HIV infection. Furthermore, we will also be measuring whether specific antiviral pathways are affected by female sex hormones in order to determine whether hormones facilitate or suppress GEC susceptibility to HIV-1 by regulating antiviral pathways. These results will provide useful information regarding the early stages of HIV infection in the FGT, which remains a highly controversial, poorly understood, yet important area of HIV-1 research. These results will also have considerable effect on public health measures regarding women's health, as it may provide new information regarding the safety of hormonal contraceptives that are currently in use.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effet d'un entraînement en résistance et d'une supplémentation en protéines sur la capacité fonctionnelle chez des femmes post-ménopausées dynapéniques et non-dynapéniques.
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTIVITE PHYSIQUE; AUTONOMIE; CAPACITE FONCTIONNELLE; COMPOSITION CORPORELLE; DYNAPENIE; FEMMES POST-MENOPAUSEES; FORCE MUSCULAIRE; PROTEINES; QUALITE DE VIE; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Le Canada vivre sous peu une periode de vieillissement de la population sans precedent. Or le vieillissement normal, et plus specifiquement la menopause se caracterise par une perte de masse musculaire et de force musculaire. Ces changements corporels sont associes a une augmentation du risque de chutes, a une diminution de l'autonomie et de la capacite fonctionnelle. La force musculaire aurait une impact important sur les capacites fonctionnelles. Les couts de sante associes a cette periode de perte d'autonomie et de mobilite sont estimes entre 9000 et 30 000$ par annee. Ainsi, il est crucial de trouver des facons de prevenir la perte d'autonomie associee au vieillissement et d'augmenter le qualite de vie des personnes agees en ameliorant les capacites fonctionnelles des femmes post-menopausee. La pratique d'activite physique est une intervention preventive et non-pharmacologique a envisager. Les personnes agees actives ont un risque plus faible de perte d'autonomie. Un entrainement en musculation permet une augmentation de la force de l'equilibre et de la posture ce qui par le fait meme permet d'ameliorer ou de maintenir les capacites fonctionnelles, la mobilite et donc l'autonomie. Une autre alternative a envisager est la prise d'un supplement en proteines. En effet, un supplement en proteine permettrait de prevenir la perte de masse et de force musculaire. Ainsi nous souhaitons verifier si un entrainement en resistance mixte de 16 semaines combine avec la prise ou non d'un supplement en proteine permet d'ameliorer la composition corporelle et la capacite fonctionnelle chez des femmes post-menopausees. Notre programme consistera en un entrainement supervise par un kinesiologue de 16 semaines (1h15, 3x/sem) compose d'exercice sur appareil pour chaque groupe musculaire important (a 80% du 1RM) combine a des exercices de posture et d'equilibre. Le supplement en proteine correspondra a une dose de 50 gr/jour.

TitreApplicationTitle: Pilot evaluation of an integrated knowledge translation intervention to improve symptom management in cancer patients.
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER CARE; GUIDELINES; INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY; INTERPROFESSIONAL TEAM; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; NURSING EDUCATION; PALLIATIVE CARE; PILOT CLUSTER RANDOMIZED TRIAL; SYMPTOM MANAGEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Forty percent of Canadians will receive a diagnosis of cancer in their lifetime. Many cancer patients still experience symptoms, despite the fact that guidelines exist to help nurses and other health care team members manage them.  These guidelines, from Cancer Care Ontario and the Registered Nurses Association of Ontario, are available to access via mobile devices.  This project will evaluate an intervention to promote the use of the guidelines for the management of pain, shortness of breath and confusion.  It will also show if it is possible to do a larger randomized control trial study in a similar way.  The study will take place on hospital oncology units, and involve student nurses, their clinical teachers, and all health care providers.  On one unit, student nurses, teachers and staff will be taught about guidelines that exist. They will also be shown how to use mobile devices to access the guidelines, and do practice exercises.  On the other units, teaching will only inform staff and students about the guidelines.  To evaluate whether the use of the guidelines on mobile devices is making a difference, pain, shortness of breath and confusion ratings will be measured once before the teaching is done, and then six and twelve weeks after.  Patient charts will also be reviewed to see if care was provided that was in line with the guideline recommendations.  Lastly, nursing students, teachers and members of the health care team will be asked how often they used the guidelines and to describe if use of the guidelines was feasible and helpful in practice.

TitreApplicationTitle: Une évaluation de l'efficacité clinique de la thérapie de couple axée sur l'émotion pour le traitement de la dépression post-partum
Keywords-MotsClés: COUPLES; DEPRESSION POST-PARTUM; ESSAI CLINIQUE; ESSAI RANDOMISE (RCT); INTERVENTION DE COUPLE; MATERNITE; THEORIE DE L'ATTACHEMENT; THERAPIE DE COUPLE AXEE SUR L'EMOTION (EFT)
Abstract-Résumé: La depression post-partum est une des complications les plus courantes de la grossesse. Non seulement la depression post-partum a des consequences negatives pour la femme affectee, mais elle peut nuire a la formation de liens affectifs entre la mere et son enfant, et causer des problemes de developpement cognitif et socio-emotionnel de l'enfant. En plus, la depression chez la mere augmente le risque que le pere developpe un probleme de sante mentale dans la periode postnatale. La depression post-partum a donc un impact negatif sur la sante de toute la famille.  Les problemes de couple sont un facteur de risque important pour le developpement de la depression post-partum. Beaucoup de meres qui sont deprimees apres la naissance de leur enfant vivent de la detresse dans leur couple. Lorsqu'un couple est en detresse, cela diminue le montant de soutien disponible a chacun des partenaires, a un moment ou ils en ont le plus de besoin. La therapie de couple axee sur l'emotion (Emotionally Focused Therapy--EFT) est un traitement prometteur pour la depression post-partum accompagnee d'une detresse dans le couple. L'EFT aide le couple a former un attachement securisant en aidant chacun a reconnaitre et a repondre aux besoins de base d'intimite et d'affection de l'autre. Plusieurs etudes ont trouve que l'EFT est efficace pour traiter de nombreux problemes, incluant la depression.  Ce projet de recherche va etre le premier a evaluer l'efficacite de l'EFT pour le traitement de la depression post-partum. Il s'agira d'une etude multicentre. Des patientes francophones et anglophones dans la region d'Ottawa qui vivent une depression post-partum et de la detresse dans leur couple seront invitees a participer a l'etude avec leurs conjoints et a recevoir 16 semaines d'EFT d'experts de l'EFT du Ottawa Couple and Family Institute. Il est predit que les couples qui recevront l'EFT rapporteront moins de detresse dans leur couple et moins de symptomes depressifs.

TitreApplicationTitle: The association between traffic-related air pollution, childhood allergic rhinitis and genetic variability
Keywords-MotsClés: AIR POLLUTION; ALLERGIC RHINITIS; ASTHMA; BIRTH COHORT; GENE-ENVIRONMENT INTERACTION; INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATIONS; MULTIPLE REGRESSION MODELLING; OXIDATIVE STRESS; SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISMS; TRAFFIC
Abstract-Résumé: Environmental factors, such as air pollution and environmental tobacco smoke, are increasingly linked to the onset and exacerbation of respiratory diseases. In particular, a growing number of studies have identified traffic-related air pollution (TRAP) as  contributing to the onset of childhood allergic rhinitis, although the results are not always consistent. In fact, the question still remains as to why TRAP increases the risk of allergic disease development and exacerbates symptoms only in certain susceptible subgroups. One prominent hypothesis is that TRAP may interact with certain genes involved in the defense mechanism of the body to toxins (principally, pathways for metabolism of oxidative species), thereby decreasing or increasing the risk of developing allergic rhinitis. However, it remains unclear which genes are most influential and how these genes interact with the environment to modify their effect.   This project aims to improve our understanding of whether TRAP affects the onset of childhood allergic rhinitis and how the genetic makeup of an individual can influence this association. We will utilize a unique international collaboration in which we will assimilate information on air pollution, genetics, lifestyle, and disease previously collected by studies in Canada, England, The Netherlands, Germany and Sweden. These data will be strategically combined and used to determine whether children who live in urban areas with high traffic density are more likely to develop allergic rhinitis than those who do not. Finally, we will investigate whether individuals with specific genetic compositions are more susceptible to the effects of TRAP.  The results of this study will yield insight as to how early-life environmental factors can affect the development of respiratory diseases during childhood, especially among genetically susceptible individuals.

TitreApplicationTitle: Aging with HIV/AIDS: How Older People Living with HIV Experience Health and Social Services
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; COMMUNITY BASED RESEARCH; GENDER; HEALTH SERVICES; HIV-AIDS; HOUSING; MENTAL HEALTH; QUALITATIVE RESEARCH; SOCIAL SERVICES
Abstract-Résumé: There is compelling evidence supporting the need for innovative health research to address the particular needs of older people living with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). People over age 50 embody a growing historical shift for people living with HIV/AIDS (PHAs). HIV is now considered a complex chronic illness. PHAs are living longer thanks to effective antiretroviral therapies. The goals of this project are to describe how older PHAs experience health and social services in Ontario, and to identify service gaps for this population. Following ethical approval, I will convene a Community Advisory Board (CAB) of older PHAs and service providers to identify priority areas to pursue. Using themes developed in these community consultations, I will refine a literature review and create a thematic interview guide to be used to conduct confidential in-depth interviews with 30 to 40 PHAs aged 50 and over. I will interview women and men of different backgrounds so that diverse groups are represented. Participants will be recruited primarily through local AIDS service organizations in Toronto, Hamilton and Ottawa. I will use qualitative strategies to identify, organize and code interview data. Members of the CAB will help interpret findings of the study and identify relevance and implications for service provision. This research will generate knowledge that will foreseeably assist in improving services that older PHAs need to remain healthy. Findings will be shared within the community through timely interactive workshops, publications, and other community-driven initiatives.

TitreApplicationTitle: Exploring the impact of community-based initiatives on dietary intakes and traditional and market food security in First Nation populations of the Mushkegowuk Territory
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL; COMMUNITY-DRIVEN; DIABETES; FOOD SECURITY; NUTRITION; OBESITY; PARTICIPATORY; TRADITIONAL FOOD; VEGETABLES & FRUIT; WEB-BASED
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence of overweight and obesity in Canada has risen steadily over the past 25 years, and continues to rise. Canadian Aboriginal populations face overweight and obesity rates far greater than the general population. Dietary intake is a potentially modifiable contributor to excess body weight; however, research on the dietary intakes of on-reserve Aboriginal people in Canada is scarce. Health improvement strategies are needed to improve the current situation.  The objective of this research is to evaluate the current nutrition environment and utilize a participatory, community-driven approach to reduce the incidence and prevalence of overweight, obesity, and diabetes in the communities of the Mushkegowuk Territory, on the Western coast of James Bay. This will first involve the evaluation of the current nutrition environment in these communities following the implementation of the Nutrition North subsidy program, which is hypothesized to have remained poor. It will then include the implementation and evaluation of sustainable community-driven strategies to improve the accessibility and affordability of healthy foods, namely vegetables and fruit and traditional game meats, through harvest sharing and community garden projects. As cost and availability are major barriers to healthy eating in these communities, it is hypothesized that these strategies will improve dietary intakes and community cohesion through harvest sharing. Data collection methods will include a validated web-based questionnaire (24-hour recall, food frequency questionnaire) to assess dietary intakes at baseline and post-program.  Focus group methodology will be used in the formative stages, as well as for program evaluation.  This research will contribute to the paucity of data on the dietary intakes of on-reserve Aboriginal people in Canada and aims to improve these intakes using sustainable, innovative, community-driven approaches.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of the Molecular Events that Cause a Novel Neisseria gonorrhoeae- derived Factor to Stimulate HIV Expression
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; HIV/AIDS; IMMUNOLOGY; MICROARRAY; MICROBIOLOGY; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; RNA INTERFERENCE; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; T CELLS; VIROLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Despite the inefficiency of HIV transmission during sexual intercourse, an estimated 2.7 million people become newly infected with HIV every year. Consequently, there is great interest in identifying factors that increase HIV transmission. Co-infection of HIV with other sexually transmitted infections, such as Neisseria gonorrhoeae, play a key role in increasing the risk of viral transmission. In this regard, recent work in our lab has led to the discovery of a previously uncharacterized N. gonorrhoeae derived molecule that potently increases HIV expression. This so called Neisseria-specific HIV-inducing factor (NSIF) likely plays a critical role in the pronounced increase in viral shedding that is observed in co-infected individuals, and may also affect susceptibility upon exposure to HIV. We hypothesize that NSIF represents a new signal that increases HIV expression by an undefined mechanism. To elucidate this mechanism, I first created reporter cell lines that will allow me to quantify the change in HIV gene expression we observe in response to NSIF. I now plan to use RNA interference (RNAi), a process through which any gene of interest can be repressed, to reveal genes essential for NSIF-mediated HIV expression.  Loss-of-function screens will be performed on both a genome-wide scale, and in an 'arrayed format' on individual host transcription factors with the potential to effect HIV expression in T cells. Identified genes will be vigorously characterized in my reporter cell lines, and validated in primary human T cells using wild-type HIV. This project will, therefore, allow us to understand how N. gonorrhoeae drives HIV expression and provide new insights into the relationship between these two common and devastating sexually transmitted infections. The genetic screens outlined above also provide the exciting potential to reveal new pathways that control HIV replication, and may thereby identify new targets for therapeutic agents to combat this deadly virus.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving the Health of Aboriginal Children through the Inclusion of Indigenous Knowledge and Perspectives in Early Intervention Therapy
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; ABORIGINAL INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN; COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH; COMMUNITY-BASED EARLY INTERVENTION THERAPY; COMMUNITY-BASED RESEARCH; CRITICAL INQUIRY; EARLY CHILDHOOD HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENT; HEALTH INEQUITIES; HEALTH PROMOTION; QUALITATIVE METHODOLOGIES
Abstract-Résumé: The purpose of this research is to generate knowledge that will improve the health, development and quality of life of Aboriginal children (0-5 yrs) who have developmental delays/disabilities.  Aboriginal children represent the fastest growing segment of the population and experience significant health inequities. Early intervention therapy programs provided by occupational therapists (OTs), physiotherapists (PTs) and speech language pathologists (SLPs) have been shown to be highly beneficial for young children in the wider Canadian population. Aboriginal perspectives are largely absent in EIT research and literature, and Aboriginal early childhood care and development (ECCD) leaders have called for programs to be culturally safe and informed by Aboriginal and community knowledge and perspectives. Provincial government, Aboriginal ECCD and EIT stakeholders are questioning (a) why EIT programs are consistently severely under-utilized by Aboriginal families, and (b) how services can be more culturally safe, and responsive towards the strengths and needs of this population. This exploratory, qualitative study will be inclusive of CIHR Guidelines for Health Research Involving Aboriginal People. In-depth interviews, participant observations and document analyses will be used to generate knowledge from multiple perspectives to inform (a) EIT practices and policies that are more culturally safe and responsive to the strengths and needs of Aboriginal children and families, and (b) recommendations for policy and decision-makers. Knowledge translation will be integrated throughout the research process in partnership with all stakeholders.
