TitreApplicationTitle: Elucidating the Mechanisms by which Mutations in Histone Modifying Genes Contribute to Lymphomagenesis
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CANCER; CHIP-SEQ; DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION; EPIGENOMICS; GENOMICS; HISTONE MARKS; RNA-SEQ; STATISTICS; THERAPEUTIC TARGETS
Abstract-Résumé: Lymphomas are aggressive cancers of the immune system. Non-Hodgkin Lymphomas (NHL), specifically Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), have a post-treatment survival rate of <50%.  Histones are the proteins that provide DNA with structure and allow it to be tightly packaged. Histone modifiers control the accessibility of transcriptional machinery to the DNA. As such, they play a crucial role in the regulation of transcription of their target genes. Recent studies have reported a large number of mutations in genes encoding for histone modifiers in NHL. However, how they contribute to the development of cancer is unclear.  The goal of my project is to understand how each of these mutations contributes to the development of NHL. I hypothesize that mutant histone modifiers target genes that control cell growth and proliferation. Alternatively, the mutations could foster self-renewal and prevent differentiation. My objectives are to 1) identify and characterize targets of mutant histone modifiers; 2) determine patterns of histone marks that are associated with the mutations; 3) examine if multiple mutations work together to promote cancer development. I will be developing and applying computational techniques to analyze high-throughput sequencing data from clinical DLBCL samples, and a range of mouse models and cell lines with a knock-in of the mutation of interest.  Elucidating the mechanisms by which mutant histone modifiers contribute to cancer initiation and progression will help us better understand and predict how normal and diseased cells regulate their epigenomes. Our findings may uncover other druggable epigenetic factors that may lead to the development of novel therapies to impede their tumorigenic activities. Ultimately, we expect that our findings will result in more specific epigenetic therapeutic strategies for NHL patients, and offer the possibility of a better survival rate for this disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification and Characterization of New MicroRNA Biomarkers in Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Stem Cells: Clinical Applications and Pathogenic Significance
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER STEM CELL; CHRONIC MYELOID LEUKEMIA; COLONY FORMING CELL ASSAY; ENGRAFTMENT IN MICE; FLUORESCENCE-ACTIVATED CELL SORTING; HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS; MICRORNA; PROGENITOR CELL ASSAY; RETROVIRAL TRANSDUCTION; STEM CELL ASSAY
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a form of blood cancer, characterized by increased growth of white blood cells in the bone marrow and the accumulation of these cells in the blood.  Its annual incidence is 1-2 per 100,000 people, and represents about 15-20% of all cases of adult leukemia in Western populations. CML displays a distinct mutation, the fusion of BCR-ABL gene, which causes ABL gene to be overly active. The recent introduction of imatinib mesylate (IM) medication has improved the treatment of CML by inhibiting ABL activity, but early relapses and the emergence of IM-resistant disease are an increasing problem. Currently, there are no effective molecular tests to predict patients' response to IM therapy. Also, growing evidence indicates that IM is not effective in eliminating leukemic stem cells, with disease returning after a period of apparent effect. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop novel therapeutic strategies for treatment of CML. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small molecules that are able to regulate gene expression and have been found highly deregulated in many tumors, such as breast and prostate cancers. Previously, we have created miRNA expression profile comparing CML stem cells with normal blood stem cells, and found 30 abnormally expressed miRNAs. In this project I propose to identify and characterize miRNA biomarkers in CML stem cells. I will first validate these 30 miRNA expression in patient samples from IM-responders vs. IM-nonresponders to identify most significantly changed miRNAs.  I will then compare patient samples before and after three-month treatment of nilotinib, a new ABL inhibitor that has recently approved as first-line therapy.  This would allow identification of new biomarkers to predict patients' response to nilotinib for clinical use.  In addition, I will characterize the roles of these miRNA biomarkers in CML stem cells, which could lead to development of novel therapies specifically targeting CML stem cells.

TitreApplicationTitle: Visual cortical basis of spatial suppression and its senescence
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; GABA; IN VIVO RECORDING; INACTIVATION; MICROELECTORDE; MIDDLE TEMPORAL AREA; MOTION PERCEPTION; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; SPATIAL SUPPRESSION; VISION
Abstract-Résumé: The relationship between neuronal response and our perception is of profound importance to health sciences, since aging has dramatic effects on neuronal responses that lead to perceptual deficits. The primate visual nervous system is ideal to study this relationship. It benefits from easily defined visual stimuli, approachable and well understood anatomical circuitry, and the possibility to train animals for perceptual behavioural tasks. In recent years, psychologists made the interesting and counter-intuitive observation that humans have more difficulty to perceive motion direction as the stimuli get larger. This "spatial suppression" effect is correlated to the neuronal response of the middle temporal (MT) visual area. MT responses are selective for motion stimuli direction, and more importantly, they are "surround suppressed", i.e. larger stimuli activate inhibitory surround that suppresses the responses. However, a causal relationship between MT neuronal response and spatial suppression has not been established. This spatial suppression phenomenon also gives a unique opportunity to investigate human aging, since old adults have different ability to perceive motion stimuli direction from young adults. Given the many deficits that come with old age, this opens a small and precise window to assess the deterioration of inhibitory processes with aging. Our research will use novel pharmacological approach to establish causality. We hypothesize that antagonizing MT inhibitory surround will improve the perception of larger motion stimuli direction in primates and strengthening MT surround will reverse the deficits in old animals. The results of this research will elucidate the relationship between neuronal response and perception, and how aging can affect these fundamental processes. This is especially important for the rapidly aging population in Canada and worldwide. We hope this direction of research will lead to future treatments for age-related visual impairments.

TitreApplicationTitle: Simultaneous intracoronary structural imaging and flow measurements to assess vulnerable plaques in human patients
Keywords-MotsClés: CATHETERS; DOPPLER; FLOW MEASUREMENTS; OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (OCT); OPTICAL DIAGNOSTICS; PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION (PCI)
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease is a leading cause of death in Canada and it is expected to become increasingly important with our aging population and the trend in obesity. While it is generally accepted that the blockage of blood vessels by fatty deposits, called plaques, ultimately lead to heart disease, there is currently no reliable clinical diagnostic tool to assess plaques, even after a heart attack. Optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) is a novel, FDA-approved clinical tool that has shown promise in the assessment of plaques. This optical imaging technology allows a virtual biopsy to be performed in patients in the catheterization lab and provides important structural information on the plaque, thereby enabling risk assessment.  My project will focus on two key aspects:     1. Simplifying the existing clinical system for use by physicians    2. Developing a method for simultaneous blood flow measurements  Since OFDI uses a unique contrast mechanism that is unknown to most physicians, I plan to first simplify the user interface by developing a real-time visualization framework. This is particularly important as the tool is currently being deployed to multiple centers worldwide for clinical investigation. To achieve this goal, I will use computational acceleration and image processing techniques to speed up the reconstruction of the raw data into a 3-D blood vessel representation and to allow the detection of vulnerable plaques using computer-assisted methods. To better assess the severity of heart disease and plaque stability, I will also develop a new method for simultaneous flow measurements inside the blood vessels. In many patients with vulnerable plaques, another heart attack, stroke, or other serious complications often ensue after the first attack, eventually leading to disability or death. By integrating both structural and flow imaging, we aim to reliably identify this group of high-risk patients, which would significantly improve patient outcome.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular characterization of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in prostate cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER STEM CELLS; CD151; CELLSEARCH SYSTEM; CIRCULATING TUMOR CELLS; EPITHELIAL-MESENCHYMAL TRANSITION (EMT); FLOW CYTOMETRY; FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION; MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION; PROSTATE CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Prostate cancer is a leading cause of cancer incidence and death in Canadian men. The majority of deaths caused by prostate cancer do not occur as a result of the primary prostate tumor, but rather from the spread of cancer cells to other vital organs. This process is known as metastasis, and the tumors formed in other organs are called metastases. Treatment of metastatic disease is difficult because metastases are hard to detect and often resistant to therapy. Prostate cancer cells use the bloodstream to travel through the body and these cells are called circulating tumor cells (CTCs). CTCs are very rare and require sensitive equipment to detect and count them accurately. Our lab has 1 of only 3 clinical instruments (called the CellSearch system) in Canada capable of doing this. We hypothesize that investigation of the molecular characteristics of these CTCs may provide important information about how a patient's disease will develop and/or respond to treatment.  The overall goal of the proposed studies is to use a combination of cell culture systems, animal model systems, and prostate cancer patient samples to test this hypothesis. We believe that CTCs could be used as a non-invasive, "real-time" biopsy to determine if/how a patients' disease is progressing and which treatment to use. Ultimately, this research could enhance our understanding of the biology of prostate cancer and improve clinical treatment of this deadly disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms of Neuropeptide Y, Y2 receptor-mediated anxiogenesis in the Basolateral Amygdala
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY; BASOLATERAL AMYGDALA; DEPRESSION; EGFP; ELECTROPHYSIOLGY; INTERNEURONS; NPY; POST TRAUMATIC STRESS DISSORDER; STRESS
Abstract-Résumé: Stress although unpleasant, is both necessary and adaptive. Prolonged stress however, is not adaptive, and can result in a variety of anxiety related disorders, such as Post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). An important factor determining an individual's susceptibility to stress related disorders is the peptide chemical messenger Neuropeptide Y (NPY). NPY is an important naturally occurring anti-anxiety compound, exerting much of its effects on the Basolateral amygdala (BLA) a brain area important in regulating emotions. NPY likely produces its anti-stress effects by decreasing output signaling from BLA pyramidal cells. Several lines of evidence suggest that the anti-anxiety actions of NPY are mediated by the Y1 receptor, while the Y2 receptor mediates pro-anxiety effects. This project focuses on the mechanisms within the BLA by which Y2 receptors may induce anxiety. Published data indicates that Y1 receptors act to inhibit BLA pyramidal neurons directly while; preliminary data indicates Y2 receptors act on interneurons sending inhibitory signals to pyramidal cells. The specific aim of this project will be to investigate the role Y2 receptors play in regulating the complex activity of BLA interneurons. This will be investigated using BLA containing rodent brain slices; with some experiments using mice expressing green fluorescent protein (GFP) labeled interneurons. The whole cell patch clamp technique will be used to directly measure electrical properties of BLA neurons while; targeted GFP expression will allow identification of specific BLA interneurons. By applying drugs that selectively activate or block Y1 or Y2 receptors we will measure electrical changes in patched cells when Y1 or Y2 receptors are selectively targeted. Through these investigations we hope to further understand the subtleties of NPY's anti-anxiety and pro-anxiety mechanisms. This in turn will provide novel targets for drugs potentially useful for treating anxiety related illness such as PSTD.

TitreApplicationTitle: Stress-reducing effects of palatable foods during adolescence: Behavioural and neurochemical correlates and implications for obesity.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY; DEPRESSION; GLUCOCORTICOIDS; JUVENILE STRESS; LEPTIN; METABOLIC SYNDROME; OBESITY; PALATABLE FOOD
Abstract-Résumé: The current obesity 'epidemic' in the developed world is a major health concern. A particularly worrisome trend is the increased prevalence of obesity in young people. Although the reasons for increasing obesity rates remain unclear, the parallel increase in perceived stress begs the question of the role of stress in overeating and weight gain. Stress changes the way we eat resulting in a shift in food choices away from healthy foods to more fatty, energy dense 'comfort' foods. Youth are particularly vulnerable to the effects of stress making this an ideal time window to examine the relationship between stress and eating. Recent research showed that rats exposed to stressors shortly after birth displayed increased anxiety later in life as they developed into adults. Interestingly, these effects were blunted or absent if rats were allowed to eat comfort food after stress exposure and weaning from their mother's milk. Although this suggests potential beneficial effects of comfort food from a psychological perspective, this high fat/carbohydrate diet, combined with stress also resulted in signs of metabolic syndrome and obesity. The current proposal aims to explore the effects of a stressful environment during adolescence by focusing on potential chemical processes that are altered in the brain that might contribute to increased comfort food consumption, and how these foods may reduce signs of stress. In particular, experiments will focus on the role of two chemical messengers in this process: Cortisol a chemical involved in our body's response to stress; and leptin a chemical which is involved in appetite and how our bodies process fat. We will also look at sex differences as females seem more prone to comfort eating. It is hoped that these studies will help us understand why we might choose to eat comfort food during times of stress and how it makes us feel better. Ultimately this research may point to new interventions for the prevention and treatment of obesity.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Emerging Challenge of Urban Malaria in Sub-Saharan Africa: an Inquiry of Malaria-Urbanization Dynamics
Keywords-MotsClés: COST-EFFECTIVENESS; EPIDEMIOLOGY; GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS (GIS); LONGITUDINAL; MALARIA; MATHEMATICAL MODELING; POPULATION HEALTH; POPULATION HEALTH INTERVENTIONS; URBAN HEALTH; URBANIZATION
Abstract-Résumé: Africa is the fastest urbanizing continent in the world and its urban population is expected to double between 2000 and 2030. More than 60% of these urban citizens, however, inhabit areas of informal settlements characterized by poor housing, lack of sanitation, and deficient drainage of surface water. Such conditions are potentially conducive to malaria transmission. In fact, the incidence of malaria has risen dramatically in urban centers of sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) in recent decades. The emerging challenge of urban malaria in SSA calls for integrated multi-sectored prevention and control strategies but current understanding of the malaria-urbanization dynamics is limited. The proposed research thus aims to: i) investigate the unique contribution and interactions, of individuals, neighborhoods, communities, health systems, and environmental determinants of urban malaria, ii) review the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of current approaches to malaria control, and iii) build a detailed predictive model of urban malaria that will serve to rationalize, prioritize, and optimize sustainable and cost-effective control strategies to reduce disease burden. Epidemiological data from large longitudinal studies in Dar es Salaam (Tanzania; N=64,537) and Accra (Ghana; N=15,000) will be analyzed, as well as high-resolution satellite imagery. Knowledge, attitudes, and practices surveys will be conducted and relevant data on control methods collected. The effect of new promising prevention and control methods will be modeled and their cost-effectiveness assessed. Findings are expected to inform program managers and local health authorities on the best practices to mitigate this preventable crisis by translating relevant knowledge into policy and practice. This study will provide much needed scope on the potential consequences of fast and unplanned urbanization on vector-borne diseases epidemiology in SSA, and on malaria in particular.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of personalized vaccines targeting tumour-specific mutations
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; CANCER GENETICS; CANCER IMMUNOLOGY; GENOMICS; INTERDISCIPLINARY ONCOLOGY; NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING; PERSONALIZED MEDICINE; VACCINES
Abstract-Résumé: A hallmark of cancer is the accumulation of DNA mutations that allow cancer cells to grow and multiply.  Recent technological advances in genetic sequencing have dramatically lowered the cost of identifying these mutations so we can now identify all mutations in a patient's tumour.  Studies to date indicate that human tumours contain tens to thousands of mutations, the vast majority of which are unique to individual patients.  The next major challenge is to develop clinically feasible, cost-effective strategies to therapeutically target the complex mutational landscape of human cancer. The immune system recognizes and destroys cells that are abnormal due to infection or mutation.  However, in the case of cancer, the immune system seems to ignore many mutations with the result that tumours are able to grow.  I hypothesize we can use vaccines to fully activate the immune system to recognize mutations and destroy tumours. To test this idea, we used next generation sequencing to identify mutations present in an experimental set of five different mouse breast tumours.  After we validate the mutations, we will develop vaccines made of small segments of proteins that mimic the mutations. To test whether these vaccines can induce a therapeutic effect, we will implant tumour cells containing the relevant mutations into mice. Once tumours are well established, we will vaccinate mice and measure the level of immune system activation. We expect vaccination to elicit a potent immune response that leads to tumour regression. If successful, this project will pave the road to the use of personalized vaccines to treat cancer. As the cost of sequencing an entire human genome approaches the $1000 mark, it will become feasible to routinely subject patients' tumours to genomic sequencing.  The mutations identified by sequencing could then be used to design personalized vaccines that trigger the patient's immune system to recognize and destroy cancer cells throughout the body.

TitreApplicationTitle: Diagnostic des besoins de prévention des comportements sexuels à risque et de promotion de comportements sexuels sains et responsables chez les jeunes Québécois et Québécoises âgé(e)s de 15 à 24 ans menant à la conception d'un jeu vidéo éducatif basé sur des données probantes
Keywords-MotsClés: DONNEES PROBANTES; DETERMINANTS DE LA SANTE; ENQUETE; FACTEURS DE PROTECTION; FACTEURS DE RISQUE; INTERVENTION CIBLEE (INTERVERNTION MAPPING); JEU VIDEO EDUCATIFS; EDUCATION A LA SEXUALITE
Abstract-Résumé: Les taux associes aux ITS et a la grossesse non planifiee chez les jeunes de 15 a 24 ans au Quebec inquietent et suggerent un relachement des pratiques sexuelles securitaires, tout comme des lacunes en matiere d'education a la sexualite. D'autres realites emergentes soulevent tout autant les inquietudes des intervenants et des parents, comme l'usage des medias sociaux et la presence d'activites sociales sexualisees. Toutefois, les donnees recentes et locales sont rarissimes au regard de ces enjeux et ne permettent aucune generalisation a l'ensemble de cette population. Si quelques enquetes rassemblent des donnees sur les comportements sexuels, elles se limitent pour la plupart a des items sur l'age lors de la premiere relation sexuelle, l'utilisation du condom et de la contraception et le nombre de partenaires. Pourtant, selon la definition proposee dans les Lignes directrices canadiennes pour l'education en matiere de sante sexuelle, la sante sexuelle surpasse cette dimension preventive et se definit comme « un etat de bien-etre physique, emotionnel, mental et social relie a la sexualite [et] ne saurait se reduire a l'absence de maladies, de dysfonctions ou d'infirmites ». Ainsi, ce manque au niveau des donnees probantes ne permet pas de comprendre les multiples dimensions de la realite sexuelle et actuelle de ces jeunes, ce qui est portant necessaire a l'elaboration de strategies d'intervention prioritaires et efficaces. Dans cette optique, le present projet vise, d'une part, a rendre accessible un diagnostic de la sante sexuelle globale des jeunes de 15 a 24 ans par le biais d'une etude provinciale representative, et d'autre part, a concevoir un jeu video educatif base sur ces donnees locales et actuelles. En effet, l'usage du jeu video semble une voie des plus prometteuses en matiere d'education a la sexualite, notamment car il s'agit d'un medium accessible et apprecie de la population ciblee, en plus de permettre un apprentissage differencie et experientiel.

Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death in Western societies. Cardiovascular risk factors include diabetes, smoking, obesity and lack of exercise. It is not known exactly how these risk factors promote the development of cardiovascular disease. We have recently found a role for the protein Glycogen Synthase Kinase (GSK)-3 during the development of cardiovascular disease. I will expand this research by investigating the role of GSK3 in specific tissues. Further, I will analyze the role of different forms of the GSK3 protein, specifically the alpha form and the beta form. This research may identify novel therapeutic targets to halt or reverse the progression of cardiovascular disease.

Keywords-MotsClés: BIOCHEMISTRY; BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING MODELS; BONE MARROW TRANSPLANTATION; CHEMOTHERAPY; ENDOTHELIAL CELLS; HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS; MICROSCOPY; PROTEIN EXPRESSION; RADIATION
Abstract-Résumé: Bone marrow transplantation (BMT) is used to treat different disorders and cancers. During a BMT, patients undergo chemotherapy and radiation in order to destroy the existing bone marrow. Stem cells are then injected with the goal of replacing the bone marrow that was destroyed. The success of a BMT is directly related to whether the injected stem cells make it to the bone marrow. In order for bone marrow to be restored, stem cells must migrate through cells lining the blood vessels (endothelial cells; ECs). Exactly how stem cells migrate and attach to ECs is not well understood, but is important to determine in order to improve the success rate of BMTs. This study will examine the role of the surface protein coating of the ECs in stem cell migration and attachment. Disruption of this surface protein coating is believed to occur with chemotherapy and radiation. Three dimensional cell culture models will be used to study the attachment of stem cells to ECs under blood flow conditions. We will then examine how removing the surface layer of the ECs affects migration and adherence of stem cells in the models. The data will help understand the BMT and improve the BMT success.

Keywords-MotsClés: ESSENTIAL METABOLITE CROSSFEEDING; GAME THEORY; GUT MICROBIOME; METABOLITE EXCRETION; MICROBIAL AGGREGATION; MICROBIAL CONSORTIA; MULTIPLEXED AUTOMATED GENOME ENGINEERING; MUTUALISM; QUORUM SENSING CIRCUITS; SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: It has been shown that diseases such as Crohn's, obesity, and infections are associated with disequilibrium of the human-associated microbiota. Current antibiotic and probiotic treatments have resulted in short term transient responses. The ability to robustly redirect the human microflora into a more beneficial state would be hugely beneficial. Metabolic cooperativity between strains in microbial communities enhances stable co-existence of different organisms. However, the evolution of cooperativity is a puzzling phenomenon under Darwinian evolution of survival of the fittest. The proposed work aims to investigate the evolution of cooperative and competitive interactions of engineered ecosystems and develop basic design strategies for novel synthetic ecosystem based therapeutics. I wish to determine the effectiveness of using forward genetics, quantitative models, and synthetic biology to combine directed reciprocation, autoaggregation, and metabolically enhanced cooperation to allow for the construction of robust and evolvable microbial synergies towards the development of artificial ecosystems that can compete in natural environments.

TitreApplicationTitle: Développement de nouvelles immunothérapies ciblant les Toll-like receptors (TLRs) pour traiter la maladie d'Alzheimer
Keywords-MotsClés: AMYLOID BETA; CYTOMETRIE DE FLUX; HYBRIDATION IN SITU; IMMUNOHISTOCHIMIE; MALADIE D'ALZHEIMER; MICROGLIE; MICROSCOPIE ET IMAGERIE; MODELES ANIMAUX TRANSGENIQUES; NEUROIMMUNOLOGIE; TOLL-LIKE RECEPTORS
Abstract-Résumé: La maladie d'Alzheimer est la plus frequente cause de demence chez l'humain, est actuellement incurable et son incidence est appelee a augmenter considerablement avec le vieillissement de la population. Cette pathologie est caracterisee par l'accumulation excessive d'Amyloid-beta (ABeta) dans le cerveau, ce qui causerait des deficits cognitifs tels des troubles de memoire. Plusieurs etudes ont rapportees que les microglies, principales cellules immunitaires du cerveau, sont mobilisees autour des depots d'ABeta. Ces cellules sont capables d'eliminer l'ABeta et d'ainsi ralentir la progression de la maladie. Consequemment, stimuler l'efficacite de ce processus immunitaire s'avere une avenue therapeutique puissante et prometteuse. Plusieurs etudes ont demontre l'importance de l'activation de recepteurs appeles TLRs dans l'elimination de l'ABeta par ces cellules. Nous croyons donc que l'administration de molecules capables de stimuler ces recepteurs pourrait retarder ou prevenir l'apparition des symptomes de la maladie d'Alzheimer. L'objectif de ce projet de recherche sera donc d'etudier differentes molecules ciblant ces recepteurs TLRs afin de selectionner celles qui sont les plus efficaces et securitaires en vue d'une therapie chez l'humain.  Nous evaluerons donc l'efficacite de ces molecules sur des souris transgeniques qui developpent les symptomes de la maladie d'Alzheimer. En plus d'analyser en details les mecanismes d'action des substances les plus prometteuses, nous determinerons aussi le mode d'administration et la dose ideale afin de maximiser les effets benefiques et la securite du traitement. En resume, ce projet de recherche permettra d'identifier des molecules ayant un reel potentiel therapeutique pour entreprendre des etudes cliniques afin de traiter cette maladie devastatrice.

TitreApplicationTitle: Barriers to depression screening in medical settings: Examining cumulative false-positive rates and possible solutions in rheumatology, oncology, and cardiovascular care settings.
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CUMULATIVE FALSE-POSITIVES; DEPRESSION; RHEUMATOLOGY; ROUTINE SCREENING
Abstract-Résumé: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common and disabling condition. Routine screening for depression is one proposed solution to improve depression care and has been recommended in specialty medical settings. To be successful, a screening program must use a questionnaire that can identify a large number of depressed patients and rule-out non-depressed patients, as well as engage newly identified patients into treatments that work. Without effective procedures for identifying and treating depression, costs and potential harms from screening are not justified. One issue with screening programs is that a large portion of screened individuals who are identified as depressed do not have clinical depression. Existing studies have only estimated this problem at a single patient visit, but not the extent of the problem over time as patients are screened repeatedly. A cumulative estimate is important as it would inform assessments of the cost of screening, as well as the potential for harms that may occur, for example, if treatment is provided to patients who do not benefit. In the proposed study, we will use large datasets from 3 specialty care medical settings (1) to assess the rates at which patients in a routine screening program are identified as depressed when they are not depressed and (2) to test whether a screening strategy that focuses only on severe or persistent MDD will improve the effectiveness of routine screening programs. The study will examine data from patients with a rheumatic disease, cardiovascular disease, and cancer. The results of this study will be important to improve the likelihood that screening can be implemented in health care settings to benefit patients.

Keywords-MotsClés: CELLULAR REPROGRAMMING; CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPIATION; ECTOPIC GENE EXPRESSION; GENE EXPRESSION ARRAY; HEMATOPOIETIC PROGENITOR CELLS; HUMAN DERMAL FIBROBLASTS; HUMAN-MOUSE XENOGRAFT ASSAYS
Abstract-Résumé: Previous work from our lab has demonstrated that human skin cells can be directly converted into cells of the blood system.  This effort was accomplished by turning on a normally silent gene in skin cells, Oct-4, and then cultivating the skin in a bath of blood specific growth factors.  During the conversion process a set of blood specific genes were up-regulated and are thought to be the drivers of the change in fate from skin to blood.  Here I propose to test the ability of these blood specific genes to both augment, and replace Oct-4 during skin to blood conversion.  I hope to illuminate the distinct molecular events which take place during this process in order to enhance skin to blood conversion and bring it closer to translation from bench to bedside.

TitreApplicationTitle: Body composition, nutrition and rehabilitation in elderly patients admitted to the intensive care unit
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; BODY COMPOSITION; COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY; CRITICAL CARE; METABOLISM; NUTRITION; REHABILITATION; SARCOPENIA
Abstract-Résumé: Elderly patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) experience worse clinical outcomes such as higher mortality rates and longer hospital length of stays (LOS) compared to non-elderly patients. Patients surviving ICU and hospital stay often experience malnutrition and loss of muscle mass. Both of these factors are associated with increased risk of developing infections and other clinical complications, higher mortality and morbidity, and declines in physical abilities. This represents a significant economic burden to our health care system.  My PhD research aims to characterize and evaluate critically ill elderly patients and develop the foundational work for future nutrition and rehabilitative interventions. Currently, there is no research that has investigated the specific changes in body composition (i.e. fat and muscle depots) at ICU admission and during hospitalization in critically ill elderly patients. Examining body composition is important because it relates to nutritional status and functional debility. I will thoroughly characterize skeletal muscle and fat mass in injured, elderly patients at ICU admission, and I will relate these measurements with nutritional status, physical function, mortality, length of hospital stay, and infection rates. This will build the base for my further objectives, which include the evaluation of the changes that develop in body composition, nutritional status, functional status and metabolic parameters during ICU and hospital length of stay. These changes will then be compared to clinical outcomes.  This research will lay the foundation for the development of specific nutrition and rehabilitation interventions that aim to improve functional recovery in the injured elderly.  The long-term goal of this research is to improve clinical outcomes and reduce mortality rates in the critically ill elderly.  Ultimately, this will reduce the health care costs associated with hospitalization of the elderly.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluating Syndromic Surveillance in Public Health Practice: Detecting Waterborne Disease Outbreaks
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOSTATISTICS; DISEASE SURVEILLANCE; GASTROINTESTINAL DISEASES; GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS; INFECTIOUS DISEASE
Abstract-Résumé: Large waterborne disease outbreaks occur regularly in Canada and other countries, resulting in considerable morbidity, mortality, and cost. Public health surveillance is critical to detect outbreaks when water treatment fails. If outbreaks are detected rapidly, interventions, such as boil-water advisories, are available to quickly and effectively limit the human and economic impacts. Traditional public health surveillance systems, however, frequently fail to detect waterborne disease outbreaks. For example, in the E.coli outbreak in Walkerton, 2000 and the Cryptosporidiosis in North Battleford, 2001, existing surveillance systems failed with tragic consequences - thousands of infections, multiple deaths, and enormous economic cost. Syndromic surveillance may address limitations of traditional surveillance by using novel data sources (e.g., emergency department records) and information technology to detect disease cases rapidly and identify outbreaks early in their course. We propose to evaluate empirically the effect of adding syndromic surveillance to existing public health surveillance systems in Canada on the detection and management of waterborne enteric disease outbreaks. We will investigate a variety of types of outbreaks based on population characteristics (e.g., immune-compromised status) and outbreak characteristics (e.g., severity of contamination). We will build and evaluate a model to simulate waterborne outbreaks of gastrointestinal disease (Cryptosporidium, Campylobacter) in Montreal, Quebec, by generating healthcare utilization and laboratory testing data that would result from an outbreak.  The model will be parameterized to simulate infection, the progression of the disease, and the subsequent utilization of healthcare services. We hypothesize that the addition of syndromic surveillance will improve the accuracy and timeliness of outbreak detection and decrease morbidity, mortality, and cost.

TitreApplicationTitle: The impact of health warning labels on smokeless tobacco packages in India and Bangladesh
Keywords-MotsClés: BETWEEN-SUBJECTS DESIGN; EXPERIMENTAL STUDY; FEAR APPEALS; HEALTH WARNING LABELS; LOW AND MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES; PERCEPTIONS OF RISK; POPULATION HEALTH; REGRESSION ANALYSES; SMOKELESS TOBACCO
Abstract-Résumé: Tobacco use remains the leading preventable cause of death. Much of the global burden of tobacco use is concentrated in low and middle income countries (LMICs), such as India and Bangladesh, which collectively have more than 300 million tobacco users. Smokeless tobacco use is disproportionately concentrated in these countries and unlike most other countries, smokeless tobacco accounts for a greater proportion of tobacco use than smoked forms such as cigarettes. Knowledge of the health risks of smokeless tobacco remains low, to the extent that it continues to be used for medicinal purposes in some communities.   Health warnings on tobacco packages are among the most cost-effective interventions to reduce tobacco use at the population level. There is an urgent need for evidence to guide the effective design of smokeless tobacco health warnings and their implementation in the face of industry legal challenges. However, both research and labelling practices are considerably more advanced for cigarettes compared to smokeless tobacco, and it is unclear how contextual factors, such as lower literacy rates and cultural differences in perceptions of disease and imagery, may affect the impact of pictorial health warnings for smokeless tobacco products.  The study will examine 1) the effeciveness of individual health warnings for each of the five leading health effects of smokeless tobacco (oral cancer, mouth disease, heart disease, addiction, and death), 2) the effectiveness of different health effects (e.g., oral cancer vs. heart disease), and 3) the effectiveness of pictorial "themes" (e.g., graphic vs. symbolic imagery) in India and Bangladesh. The study will also determine whether the effectiveness of labels varies by gender, age, and education. This research has the potential to address a key evidence gap in tobacco labelling and will provide regulators with a set of empirically tested health warnings and the evidence to support their implementation.

TitreApplicationTitle: What are the rules that regulate maturation of AMPA receptor only synapses?
Keywords-MotsClés: DEVELOPMENTAL NEUROBIOLOGY; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GLUTAMATERGIC SYSTEM; NEUROSCIENCE; PHARMACOLOGY; RETINA; SYNAPSE MATURATION; SYNAPTIC PHYSIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Communication between the cells of the brain, neurons, is essential for proper functioning the nervous system. This communication takes place at specialized junctions, synapses, through a process called synaptic transmission. In synaptic transmission, the presynaptic cell communicates to the postsynaptic partner by releasing chemicals called neurotransmitters, which bind to target proteins in the postsynaptic cell. Neurons encode information through changing the strength of this transmission.  The strength of transmission is adjusted dynamically, and is thought to underlie many biological functions like developmental formation of sensory organs, learning and memory and disease states.   Understanding how neurons control this process through changing the strength of neurotransmission is critical for unraveling brain functioning and diseases associated with it. To alter the synaptic strength, the presynaptic neuron can change its efficiency of release, or the postsynaptic cell can change its sensitivity to the release. In most of the cases, both partners, pre and post cells are affected. In order to elucidate the mechanisms underlying this change, we are using a simple sensory organ, the retina.   The retina is located in the back of the eye and is the sensory organ for vision. In the retina, communication between the rod bipolar cell- AII amacrine cell is essential for night vision. Malfunctioning of this synapse is associated with night vision impairments in melanoma-associated retinopathy and congenital stationary night blindness. In order to understand mechanisms that regulate the synaptic strength of this synapse, we deprive animals from light from birth on. We compare the activity in pre-and postsynaptic cells in dark reared retina to the retinas of animals that are raised in normal cyclic light cycle. By studying the differences we hope to understand the mechanisms that regulate the strength of neurotransmission and are defective in disease state.

TitreApplicationTitle: Innovative Prognostic Testing of Comatose Patients Using FMRI
Keywords-MotsClés: COMA; CONSCIOUSNESS; FUNCTIONAL MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; PROGNOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: After an acute brain injury, an individual can enter a comatose state. Since a coma is not permanent, questions arise about how to predict outcome or the chances of functional recovery. Clinically, predicting outcomes for comatose patients is limited and focuses only on prediction of poor outcomes as this leads to consideration of the withdrawal of life sustaining therapies. Since current clinical tools do not examine predictions of positive outcomes, there is no way to assess the chances of functional recovery in comatose patients. Recent advancements in neuroimaging techniques, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), have shown potential in predicting favorable outcomes in unconsciousness. The aim of the current study is to investigate brain activity of comatose patients using fMRI and correlate those brain activations to outcome 3 months following the brain injury with hopes fMRI may become a new tool for prognosis and management of patients in coma.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of integrin-linked kinase in oligodendrocyte development.
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL ADHESION MOLECULES; CELLULAR DEVELOPMENT; ENZYME PURIFICATION; INTEGRIN-LINKED KINASE; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; MYELINATION; NEURON; OLIGODENDROCYTE; PRIMARY CELL CULTURE; PROTEIN EXPRESSION
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple Sclerosis is a neurological disease causing physical and mental deficits in many Canadians. Much research is underway to understand this disease, and to develop new drugs that may halt or even reverse disease progression. The symptoms of Multiple Sclerosis may be attributed to the loss of function of brain cells, in particular, neurons. Neurons are brain cells which transfer information to other parts of our body. They transfer information by means of tiny wires, making electrical connections with other neurons. Just as electrical wires in our homes require insulation, neuron connections require insulation for proper information transfer. Oligodendrocytes are the cell type which provides insulation for neuron connections. They wrap the connections with an insulating layer of fatty material, allowing efficient communication between neurons. In order for oligodendrocytes to wrap neuron connections effectively, they require certain proteins to be functioning in the cell. It is believed that a family of proteins called the Integrins plays an important role in the wrapping of the neuron connections by oligodendrocytes. Recently, a protein called Integrin-Linked Kinase or ILK has been shown to interact with certain integrins and perhaps influence the development of oligodendrocytes. My project involves growing oligodendrocytes in Petri dishes and using various means to delete the ILK protein in these cells. Then, I look at how these ILK-deficient cells differ in their development when compared to normal oligodendrocytes. I also grow neurons and oligodendrocytes together in Petri dishes, to determine if ILK is important in oligodendrocyte wrapping of neuron connections. My research is not only important for the basic understanding of oligodendrocyte biology, but also highly beneficial to the understanding of Multiple Sclerosis. My research may lead to the identification of new drug targets aimed at treating neurological diseases such as Multiple Sclerosis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Botsha Buphelo: An exploration of medical circumcision for HIV prevention among adolescent boys in Soweto, South Africa
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENTS; CIRCUMCISION; HIV PREVENTION; SOUTH AFRICA
Abstract-Résumé: Studying attitudes towards male circumcision has a scientific, social and ethical rationale. Male circumcision is a scientifically tested and proven HIV prevention method and when properly facilitated can help reduce population risk (Mills 2008). In order to ensure that the roll-out of circumcision is successful, it important to understand what motivates or inhibits young men to participate. The aims of this project are to contribute new knowledge regarding an important and neglected population by exploring beliefs and attitudes towards circumcision among adolescent boys coming-of-age in an HIV endemic community.

TitreApplicationTitle: Bioinformatics integration of different genomic data to predict and understand resistance to FOLFOX and anti-VEGF treatment in the context of metastatic colorectal cancer.
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; BIOSTATISTICS; DATA INTEGRATION; DRUG RESISTANCE; GENOMICS; METASTATIC COLORECTAL CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: Since President Nixon signed the National Cancer Act in 1971 our understanding of cancer has increased tremendously. Unfortunately, cancer still remains the most devastating disease faced by Canadians. Great hopes are now placed on a new generation of extremely efficient drugs designated to target specific types of cancer. Although highly efficient, their cost is prohibitive, easily exceeding $25K for even short treatments. Moreover, only a subset of patients respond positively to such treatments. The community currently lacks any form of biomarker to accurately predict who will and will not respond.  Within Q-CROC, a Quebec-wide effort to understand cancer resistance to treatment, our goal is to develop a clinical test that will stratify cancer patients into responder and non-responder classes. This test is built from samples of cancer patients prior to any treatment using a number of new technologies like microarrays and next generation sequencing. This PhD project is focused on the application of bioinformatics and biostatistics to identify a set of genes that jointly predict whether a patient will respond or not to specific compounds. The genes within the predictor will be subjected to extensive analysis, in order to understand better the underlying cancer biology that distinguish between responders and non-responders. An accurate gene set predictor in this setting would reduce the number of patients suffering needlessly from anti-cancer drugs that are ineffective for their personal genome, and reduce the cost of health care.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dynamics of SHIP localization and site-specific phosphorylation in B lymphocytes
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTOIMMUNE DISORDERS; B LYMPHOCYTE FUNCTION; CELL CULTURE; CONFOCAL MICROSCOPY; IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; LIVE-CELL IMAGING; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PROTEIN COMPLEXES; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION; SURFACE PLASMON RESONANCE
Abstract-Résumé: B cells are immune cells best known for their role in producing immunoglobulins for specific defense against pathogens and abnormal self-cells. Like most cell types, B cell responses are controlled by integration of signals from the extracellular environment which are read by receptors on the cell surface. These signals are propagated inside the cell by signaling pathways that culminate in a particular cellular response. Some of these signals promote cell activation while others inhibit. The ability of our cells to balance these opposing signals appropriately in order to generate effective immune responses while avoiding tissue damage and autoimmunity is key to maintaining health. This project examines an important regulatory circuit in B cells that involves the lipid phosphatase SHIP, a regulator of an intracellular signaling pathway called the PI3-kinase pathway. SHIP negatively regulates B cell responses including cell proliferation and antibody production. SHIP and its associated inhibitory receptor are known to play a protective role in autoimmune diseases, leukemias, and allergic diseases. Given this important role and the fact that small-molecule activators of SHIP are now available, SHIP is emerging as a promising therapeutic target. This project aims to gain an understanding of how key signaling proteins influence SHIP activity and how the biochemical state of SHIP with respect to sub-cellular localization and post-translational modifications defines the functions of this protein. Dynamic spatio-temporal localization of SHIP and its regulators will be studied using cutting-edge live-cell imaging techniques. Post-translational modifications will be studied by Western Blotting and mass spectrometry. SHIP activity will be assessed by enzyme activity assays as well as by studying functional outcomes of structural changes. The results of these studies will provide crucial insight into how and when manipulation of SHIP activity might have a therapeutic benefit.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification des caractéristiques prédictives de l'utilisation d'une approche centrée sur le patient dans un contexte de douleur chronique
Keywords-MotsClés: APPROCHE CENTREE SUR LE PATIENT; DEVIS DESCRIPTIF CORRELATIONNEL; DOULEUR; DETRESSE PSYCHOLOGIQUE; DEVELOPPEMENT DE VIDEOS STANDARDISEES; EMPATHIE; PROFESSIONNELS DE LA SANTE; SERVICES DE LA SANTE; SOINS; EVALUATION DE LA DOULEUR
Abstract-Résumé: PROBLEMATIQUE La douleur chronique est une cause commune d'incapacite majeure et de pertes economiques, touchant environ 30 % de la population canadienne. Cette clientele suscite peu d'interet chez les cliniciens et il n'existe pas de traitement curatif pour plusieurs de ces patients. Il est suggere qu'une approche personnalisee et centree sur le patient entraine des resultats optimaux dans le traitement de la douleur chronique. Malheureusement, une telle approche est peu utilisee et peu de chercheurs en ont etudie les caracteristiques. La litterature nous permet de cerner certaines variables qui peuvent avoir un role a jouer dans le choix du type d'approche, dont l'empathie et la detresse psychologique. Le but de mon projet est d'etudier, dans un contexte de douleur chronique, la relation entre le type d'approche utilisee par les cliniciens avec leurs niveaux d'empathie et de detresse psychologique. METHODOLOGIE Je recruterai 10 medecins, 10 infirmieres et 10 physiotherapeutes, d'ages et de genres differents et uvrant dans divers contextes cliniques. Chaque clinicien participera a une seance dans nos laboratoires ou il visionnera trois videos prealablement concues, ou un patient reel decrira son experience de douleur. Le clinicien expliquera la prise en charge qu'il offrirait a chaque patient. A la suite de ses explications, le type d'approche utilisee et l'empathie seront evalues a l'aide de grilles prealablement concues et de questionnaires. La detresse psychologique sera aussi mesuree a l'aide d'un questionnaire. RETOMBEES En determinant les caracteristiques reliees a une approche personnalisee centree sur le patient, il sera possible de mieux outiller les cliniciens. Nous pourrons envisager des ateliers de formation, dans le but ultime d'ameliorer la prise en charge de personnes atteintes de douleur chronique afin d'en diminuer les couts et les consequences negatives sur le patient lui-meme, sa famille, son reseau social et le systeme de sante.

TitreApplicationTitle: Prédiction de la sécrétion de cortisol chez l'enfant : contribution relative des facteurs prénataux et postnataux.
Keywords-MotsClés: CONSOMMATION PRENATALE D'ALCOOL; CONSOMMATION PRENATALE DE DROGUES; CORTISOL; REGULATION EMOTIONNELLE; SENSIBILITE MATERNELLE; STRESS PRENATAL
Abstract-Résumé: Le cortisol est un glucocorticoide secrete par l'axe hypothalamo-pituitaire-surrenal (HPS) et sa concentration dans l'organisme augmente en reponse a un evenement stressant. Puisque des secretions atypiques de cortisol ont ete associees a l'agressivite et a des problemes internalises, plusieurs auteurs se sont interesses a la secretion de cortisol chez l'enfant, notamment en lien avec les facteurs prenataux. Les etudes suggerent une association entre les facteurs prenataux (consommation d'alcool ou de drogues, stress prenatal) et la secretion de cortisol chez l'enfant. Par contre, presque toutes ces etudes ne tiennent pas compte des facteurs postnataux, notamment la sensibilite maternelle, le principal marqueur de l'environnement postnatal en debut de vie et qui a egalement ete associee a la secretion de cortisol chez l'enfant. Le present projet de recherche propose donc d'examiner la prediction de la secretion de cortisol chez l'enfant a l'interieur d'un devis longitudinal incluant a la fois des variables prenatales et postnatales. Environ 150 meres seront recrutees et suivies pendant la grossesse et ce, jusqu'a ce que leur enfant soit age de 15 mois. Cette etude permettra de verifier la contribution relative des facteurs prenataux et postnataux dans la secretion de cortisol chez l'enfant. Puisque la secretion de cortisol est associee a plusieurs enjeux et pathologies, une meilleure comprehension des facteurs qui y sont associes s'inscrit dans une approche visant a comprendre l'interaction entre divers elements contribuant a la sante des populations. Les donnees issues de cette etude permettront de mieux cibler les interventions visant a favoriser le developpement de l'enfant et ainsi non seulement ameliorer la sante des enfants, mais egalement prevenir des difficultes de sante mentale a plus long terme.

Keywords-MotsClés: ADOPTIVE TRANSFER; DENDRITIC CELLS; EXPERIMENTAL AUTOIMMUNE ENCEPHALOMYELITIS; INTERFERON-B; MOUSE MODEL; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; T CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: The main objective of these proposed studies is to interrogate the role of IFN-B in regulating the development of cells that react against the central nervous system. Using a mouse model of MS, we have shown that mice lacking IFN-B exhibit increased clinical scores as well as earlier onset and more severe disease, than mice that are wildtype for IFN-B. IFN-B null mice have increased numbers of autoreactive cells in their brains and spinal cords during EAE. This suggests that IFN-B may regulate the activation and trafficking of cells during disease. We will use techniques to determine how activated these cells are and we will monitor their location during the time of disease. This will determine how IFN-B affects the activation of these cells as well as their location as the disease progresses.

TitreApplicationTitle: Comparison of Three One-Session Cognitive-Behavioural Treatments for Generalized Anxiety Disorder
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY DISORDERS; BRIEF THERAPY; CHRONIC WORRY; CLINICAL OUTCOME STUDY; COGNITIVE-BEHAVIOURAL THERAPY; COMORBID DISORDERS; GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER; MECHANISMS OF CHANGE; MEDICAL PRACTITIONERS; PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH
Abstract-Résumé: For one in every twenty Canadians, worrying can be a distressing experience. Individuals who worry excessively regularly seek help from family physicians and other health care practitioners to investigate common anxiety symptoms that might be misinterpreted as medical conditions. If practitioners could reduce their worrying by using a brief intervention, this would result in significant cost savings for the health care system. Currently, practitioners treat individuals who worry excessively with medication or brief counselling, but there has been no research that examines the effectiveness of brief therapy for excessive worrying. The present study will examine the effectiveness of three one-session interventions, by utilizing techniques from three effective 12-week psychotherapies. Approximately 90 individuals who identify as chronic worriers will be recruited. Participants will complete measures of excessive worrying, symptoms of related issues, and treatment credibility and implementation questionnaires. Half of the participants will then be entered into treatment, while the other half of participants will first undergo a 5-week waitlist period before entering treatment. For treatment, participants will be given information on chronic worrying and have one of the treatment strategies explained to them. Participants will then complete questionnaires each week to track changes in symptoms, treatment credibility, and implementation for four weeks, followed by a meeting with the researcher in the fifth week where the measures will be completed a final time. Participants will complete a follow-up questionnaire 4 months after the end of treatment. This study will advance this area by attempting to translate the treatments of chronic worrying from 12-week treatments to brief interventions. This study is a first step in the creation of new options for the treatment of excessive worrying by practitioners, which may improve the cost-effectiveness of the health care system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Rho-Associated Protein Kinase as a Therapeutic Target in Osteoarthritis
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; CARTILAGE; CHONDROCYTE BIOLOGY; JOINT PHYSIOLOGY/PATHOLOGY; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; OSTEOARTHRITIS; TRANSGENIC ANIMALS
Abstract-Résumé: Debilitating joint pain strikes 1 in 10 Canadians who are afflicted with osteoarthritis (OA). Current treatment options are limited to pain reduction, and in extreme cases joint replacement. The underlying cause of OA remains untreated and poorly understood. Development of OA is associated with cartilage degeneration and changes to underlying bone. Our lab has shown that OA is promoted in cartilage in vitro through transforming growth factor alpha (TGFa) and its mediator Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) through increased production of catabolic factors that break down cartilage. Blocking ROCK with a pharmaceutical inhibitor decreases the hallmark OA markers in tissue culture experiments. This leads us to hypothesize that inhibition of ROCK in vivo in animal models of OA may protect against cartilage degeneration. This would suggest that ROCK is a viable therapeutic agent for the treatment of human OA. OA will be induced surgically in rats, and treatment using a clinically available ROCK inhibitor will commence at various time points and concentrations. The resulting effects of ROCK inhibition are then assessed histologically and through various biomarkers found in blood and urine. ROCK function will also be assessed in human cartilage tissue obtained from routine orthopedic procedures. These samples will be cultured ex vivo with ROCK inhibitor, and hallmark OA markers will be analyzed. Transgenic mice models will also be utilized to further evaluate the ROCK pathway in primary OA. We expect that ROCK inhibition will decrease markers of cartilage degeneration in each case. Exploration of the ROCK pathway in cartilage will further increase our understanding of the molecular events that occur in OA, and how we may successfully intervene. This study will confirm the viability of ROCK inhibition as a therapeutic target in OA. Drugs targeting ROCK are already clinically available for other diseases, and can be easily adapted for use as a disease-modifying OA drug.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effectiveness of Fast muscle Activation and Stepping Training (FAST) on Balance and Mobility post-stroke.
Keywords-MotsClés: BALANCE; CLINICAL TRIAL; MOTOR UNIT; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; NEUROPLASTICITY; STROKE
Abstract-Résumé: Regaining independence in standing and walking is of utmost importance for patients recovering from stroke. Walking balance requires muscles in the legs and trunk to contract quickly if people lose their balance. Even though exercise is the main form of treatment used by physiotherapists in stroke rehabilitation, the ability of exercise to promote recovery of muscles after stroke is not known. This study will examine the effects of a novel retraining protocol that focusses on speed of muscle contraction to develop the fast bursts of muscle activation necessary for normal walking and standing balance. Given that keeping one's balance requires fast muscle activity, rehabilitation after stroke should focus on speed of movement. The purpose of this study is to determine whether Fast muscle Activation and Stepping Training, or FAST, exercises will improve walking balance in individuals after stroke more than usual care. Sixty patients who have been recently discharged from in-patient stroke rehabilitation will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: FAST exercises or usual care. Both groups will receive two treatments per week for six weeks with a physiotherapist at the out-patient physical therapy department of one of two local hospitals. The FAST exercises will include fast squats and stepping in standing. The usual care group will include strengthening and range of motion exercises, but no speed work. Walking balance and cortical excitability will be tested before, immediately after, and one month after therapy using clinical and laboratory measurements including assessment of walking, balance confidence, brain activation, muscle electrical activity, and the amount of body sway during standing. If FAST exercises are effective, walking balance will be better than in the usual care group. This study will examine whether these specific exercises could be used by physiotherapists to improve walking balance after stroke.

TitreApplicationTitle: A study of how predictive analytics is being applied by health leaders around the globe to make decisions about the future.
Keywords-MotsClés: CASE STUDY; GROUNDED THEORY; HEALTH ANALYTICS; INTERVIEWS; OBSERVATION; PREDICTIVE DECISION MAKING; QUALITATIVE RESEARCH; SURVEY
Abstract-Résumé: Historically, health leader decision making has focused on explaining past actions instead of predicting how to respond to future events. As a result of greater access to comprehensive electronic health data, and the development of sophisticated decision support technologies, the health sector is now in a position to more actively engage in predictive decision making. The purpose of this case study is to investigate where and how health leaders (i.e., early adopters) are applying predictive analytics to make better decisions. Data collection and analysis will focus on answering four questions: 1) how are analytics being applied in the health industry, 2) what are the characteristics of health organizations that apply analytics to make predictive decisions, 3) what benefits have been realized from predictive decision making in the health industry, and 4) what are the critical enablers to becoming an analytic health organization. A key component of this study will be the development of a framework that other health leaders could benefit from in their decision making processes as they perform various roles. Examples of these roles include the following: nations managing population health and pandemics, providers delivering wellness services and managing disease, governments conducting planning and setting policy, administrators managing operations, payers and donors determining how to distribute funding, and private corporations developing health innovations. Predictive analytics has been applied extensively in actuarial science, insurance, financial services, and the retail industry for the last decade. However, little research has been conducted on its application to the health sector. This research study will explore the relevance of predictive analytics to the health industry and contribute to advancing global health decision making through the development of a framework/theory that could be leveraged by health leaders during their decision making.

TitreApplicationTitle: La pratique infirmière en GMF : Vers une meilleure connaissance de son apport dans le suivi des patients atteints de maladies chroniques.
Keywords-MotsClés: ENQUETE; ETUDE DE CAS; GROUPE DE MEDECINE DE FAMILLE; MALADIES CHRONIQUES; PRATIQUE EXEMPLAIRE; PRATIQUE INFIRMIERE; SOINS DE PREMIERE LIGNE; SUIVI INFIRMIER
Abstract-Résumé: Au Quebec, l'arrivee des infirmieres uvrant au sein des Groupe de Medecine de Famille (GMF) a incite les ordres professionnels et les autorites gouvernementales a emettre des recommandations sur les activites que ces infirmieres peuvent exercer. Celles-ci peuvent maintenant assurer le suivi des patients atteints de maladies chroniques en collaboration avec le medecin traitant. Malgre cela, il existe actuellement des ecarts entre ce qui est propose dans la litterature et ce qui est pratique en GMF. La mise en evidence plus approfondie des roles que peuvent exercer les infirmieres permettrait demettre des recommandations pour une utilisation optimale de leurs competences dans le suivi des patients atteints de maladies chroniques(MC).  Ce projet a pour objectifs de decrire les roles de l'infirmiere GMF lors du suivi des patients atteints de MC. Plus precisement, il desire decrire les elements contextuels determinants de ces roles et comment ceux-ci s'inserent dans la collaboration infirmiere-medecin. II vise egalement a dresser un portrait de ces roles pour l'ensemble du Quebec. Pour ce faire, sept GMF de la province de Quebec seront analyses. Les acteurs principaux : infirmieres, medecins et patients seront rencontres et questionnes lors d'entrevues. De l'observation sera egalement faite dans les GMF et les dossiers-patients des participants a l'etude seront revises. Suite aux entrevus, un questionnaire electronique sera elabore. Ce questionnaire sera distribue par Internet a l'ensemble des infirmieres et medecins-responsables des GMF du Quebec.  Les resultats de cette etude permettront de rapporter les differents roles infirmiers en GMF lors du suivi de patients atteints de MC et ce, pour l'ensemble des GMF quebecois. Un fois ces roles rapportes, des recommandations seront emises afin de modifier la pratique des infirmieres GMF. Celles-ci seront alors en mesure d'assurer un meilleur suivi optimisant ainsi la sante et la qualite de vie des patients atteints de MC.

TitreApplicationTitle: Signification de la santé et du prendre soin pour des utilisateurs de drogue par injection rejoints par des services publics de santé à Montréal.
Keywords-MotsClés: ETHNOGRAPHIE; FACTEURS DE RISQUE; HISTOIRE DE VIE; PRENDRE SOIN; PROMOTION DE LA SANTE; SANTE MENTALE; SIGNIFICATION DE LA SANTE; TOXICOMANIE; UTILISATEURS DE DROGUES PAR INJECTION; VULNERABILITE SOCIALE
Abstract-Résumé: La signification de la sante et du prendre soin passent par un prisme de representations et de ressources collectives pour se maintenir en vie et en sante ainsi que des valeurs normatives du groupe d'appartenance. Puisque la sante est un etat complet de bien-etre physique, mental et social, et non seulement une absence de maladie ou d'infirmite (OMS,1946), l'objectif general de cette recherche est de jeter un eclairage sur la signification que se font des utilisateurs de drogue par injection (UDI) de la sante et du prendre soin ainsi que des mesures qu'elles favorisent pour leur permettre de mieux prendre soin d'eux-memes. Une meilleure comprehension du sens donne a la sante et au prendre soin par les UDI nourrira des reflexions interprofessionnelles, inter-etablissements et intersectorielles et permettra de mieux orienter les soins et services pour les UDI qui s'articulent aux frontieres de la  marginalite sociale. Ces resultats vont favoriser des subventions futures pour ameliorer les programmes de soin aux UDI et former les professionnels de la sante et intervenants uvrant aupres d'eux. Les resultats influenceront et guideront la pratique des infirmieres qui pratiquent avec des UDI dans differents milieux : salles d'urgence, cliniques communautaires, centres de readaptation en dependance, milieu carceral, etc., ainsi que de divers autres professionnels qui cotoient les UDI. Les connaissances qui emergeront  de cette etude devraient permettre d'offrir une meilleure reponse sociale, equitable et adaptee pour cette clientele hautement vulnerabilisee au regard de la promotion de la sante et du prendre soin.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving the Generation of Pancreatic Beta cells from Pancreatic Multipotent Precursors for the Treatment of T1D
Keywords-MotsClés: CALCIUM IMAGING; DEVELOPMENT; DIABETES MELLITUS; ELECTRON MICROSCOPY; IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY; MICROARRAY; PANCREATIC BETA CELLS; PROTEOMIC ANALYSIS; QUANTITATIVE PCR; STEM CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: Type I Diabetes (T1D) results from an autoimmune attack on pancreatic beta cells causing insulin deficiency. Treatment for T1D currently involves restricted diet, blood monitoring and multiple daily injections of insulin to regulate blood sugar levels. Improvements in pancreatic beta cell transplantation has introduced new options for T1D treatment, but problems remain; low tissue availability, cell loss during isolation, allorejection and the need for chronic immunosuppression. The potential to generate beta cells from stem cells offers a large source of insulin producing cells for transplant. The proposed studies will define the current capacity of beta cell differentiation protocols, and generate strategies to improve the differentiation and expansion of adult stem cells into beta cells. Both of these steps are required before stem cell-derived beta cells represent a viable treatment for T1D.

TitreApplicationTitle: Modulation of central respiratory networks by ATP: the role of astrocytes and ectonucleotidases
Keywords-MotsClés: CALCIUM IMAGING; GLIOTRANSMISSION; NEUROMODULATION; NEUROSCIENCE; OPTOGENETICS; PURINERGIC SIGNALING; RESPIRATORY DISEASE; RHYTHM GENERATION; WHOLE-CELL RECORDING
Abstract-Résumé: The rhythm generator underlying breathing is located in the preBotzinger Complex (preBotC) of the brainstem. The activity of this network of neurons is controlled via reflexes to maintain blood oxygen and carbon dioxide levels. ATP (adenosine triphosphate) plays an important role as a signaling molecule in these reflexes. During periods of low oxygen, an initial increase in breathing is followed by a secondary depression. In the preBotC, low oxygen causes a delayed release of ATP, which, acting through purinergic receptors weakens the secondary depression. Glial cells in the brain are important for providing metabolic support to neurons. Recently, however, it has become recognized that glial cells are also important participants in brain signaling. Past work strongly suggests that this ATP excitation is mediated by glial cells in the brain. I will explore the role of glial cells and the process by which they release transmitters to influence neuron activity with respect to breathing. To do this, I will implement 'optogenetics', which will allow us to use light to specifically stimulate glial cells, and electrophysiological methods to determine effects on breathing. My research will also examine the importance of ectonucleotidases, a diverse family of enzymes that degrade ATP in the preBotC. The distribution of these enzymes is critical because they have different endproducts. Some enzymes degrade ATP into ADP (adenosine diphosphate), which is excitatory like ATP. Others degrade ATP to ADO (adenosine) which inhibits breathing. I hope to advance understanding of mechanisms by which astrocytes use ATP to modulate inspiratory network activity, and the importance of ectonucleotidases in determining ATP responses. Given the diversity of ATP receptors and ectonucleotidases in the brain and the emerging role of glial cells in signaling, defining these basic mechanisms will provide insight into the role of the ATP signaling system and glial cells in modulating breathing.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of fetal and maternal expression of placental growth factor in the regulation of placentation adaptations leading to preeclampsia.
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR; DEVELOPMENT; HYPERTENSION; LYMPHOCYTES; NATURAL KILLER CELLS; PLACENTAL GROWTH FACTOR; PLACENTATION; PREECLAMPSIA; PREGNANCY; TROPHOBLASTS
Abstract-Résumé: Preeclampsia (PE) is a multifactorial gestational disorder characterized by pathologically elevated maternal blood pressure and proteinuria.  PE occurs in approximately 5-10% of all human pregnancies and is one of the leading causes of fetal morbidity and mortality in the developed world. Currently the precise cause of PE is unknown and there is no cure; the only effective treatment is induction of labour and delivery of the placenta. Although the specific causes of PE are unknown, the expression of the angiogenic signalling molecule placental growth factor (PGF) has been shown to be necessary for normal placentation changes during pregnancy. Furthermore, antagonism of PGF by soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFLT1) or S-endoglin has been shown to induce PE-like lesions. Recent evidence has shown that circulating plasma PGF levels decrease significantly immediately prior to the onset of PE in humans, while circulating sFLT1 levels increase significantly during the same timeframe. Interestingly, PGF is expressed by both fetal trophoblasts and maternal uterine natural killer (uNK) cells during pregnancy. However, it has never been established which source of PGF is responsible for directing normal placentation changes during pregnancy. Additionally, the pattern of PGF expression during mouse pregnancy has not been determined, and thus it is unknown if the changes in PGF expression which occur over course of pregnancy in humans are mirrored in mice. Furthermore, an effective animal model for studying the fetal and maternal contributions to PGF expression and normal placentation has never been established. In this study, we propose to determine the precise profile of plasma PGF levels throughout the course of mouse pregnancy in wild-type and alypmhoid mice lacking uNK cells. In addition, through embryo transfer experiments, we propose to determine the exact contributions of fetal and maternal-derived PGF in regulating placentation changes leading to PE.

TitreApplicationTitle: Role of Sonic Hedgehog in bladder cancer and bladder cancer stem cells
Keywords-MotsClés: BLADDER CANCER; CANCER PROGRESSION; CHEMOTHERAPEUTICS; CYCLOPAMINE; GLI 1; GLI 2; SMO INHIBITOR; SONIC HEDGEHOG; STEM CELL; TUMOUR
Abstract-Résumé: Bladder cancer is the fourth most common male cancer. Approximately 70% of bladder cancers are non-muscle invasive at initial diagnosis but up to 80% of patients with superficial bladder cancer will develop recurrent tumours, of which 20-30% progress into more aggressive and potentially lethal tumours. Current treatment with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) has shown significant benefits to prevent progression compared to chemotherapeutics but may be associated with significant side effects and high-risk patients ultimately require cystectomy within 15 years. Therefore,new therapies for early-stage high-risk bladder cancer are clearly required to prevent both recurrence and progression. There is growing evidence that many solid tumours of various origins may arise through differentiation from cancer stem cells (CSCs). Although CSCs account for approximately 10% of total tumour cells, they have the ability to replenish all tumour cell types, establish new tumours at distant sites and evade conventional drug therapies. We propose to look at the Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) pathway which we have shown can slow cancer growth and increase sensitivity to chemotherapies. Firstly, we will create cultured cell lines from patient's healthy and cancer tissues and identify the stem cells within. Secondly we will isolate these cells and analyze the gene expression and protein changes that occur in cancer cells. Thirdly, we will interfere with the SHH pathway and examine the effect on stem cell growth in combination with chemotherapy. We expect that the SSH pathway is important to CSCs and that it is a potential target for new therapies. This study will be the first to examine SHH in bladder cancer stem cells.

TitreApplicationTitle: A retrospective study of complications following total joint arthroplasty: relationship to rheumatoid arthritis versus osteoarthritis.
Keywords-MotsClés: ARTHRITIS; ARTHROPLASTY; OSTEOARTHRITIS; OUTCOMES; RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS
Abstract-Résumé: Total joint replacement surgery (TJR) is the mainstay of treatment for end-stage arthritis of the hip or knee. Overall, results of this surgery are good to excellent, with proven benefits in terms of improvement in pain, function and quality of life in patients with osteoarthritis (OA). However, the findings of these studies may not reflect the situation for the ~13% of Canadians receiving TJR who have rheumatoid arthritis (RA). RA is the most common inflammatory arthritis, affecting 1-2% of Canadians, and is distinct from OA in terms of etio-pathogenesis and medical management. Previous studies examining TJR outcomes that have considered type of arthritis as a predictor have been limited by lack of clarity surrounding the definition of RA, pooling of various inflammatory arthritides in the RA group, lack of adjustment for important covariates (age, gender, and co-morbidity). The present study will use health insurance databases to examine surgical outcomes after TJR in patients with RA and OA. We will compare rates of complications between groups, including rates of repeat surgery within two years, infection, fracture and death. The study will also examine predictors of TJR outcomes in the RA group. Lack of strong evidence for risks and benefits of TJR in the people with RA impedes informed patient-physician treatment decision making, both in primary care and orthopaedics. The present study will produce high-level evidence that will fill this knowledge gap.
