TitreApplicationTitle: Étude des profils de biomarqueurs plaquettaires chez des individus avec Syndrome du X fragile avant et après traitement à la lovastatine; relation avec la réponse cognitive.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYSE PROTEIQUE; ANALYSE QUANTITATIVE; BIOMARQUEURS; CORRELATION PHENOTYPIQUE; FMRP; GENETIQUE CLINIQUE; MODELES PLAQUETTAIRES; SYNDROME DU X FRAGILE; VOIES DE SIGNALISATION; ETUDES CLINIQUES
Abstract-Résumé: Le syndrome du X fragile est la premiere cause de deficience intellectuelle hereditaire et est souvent accompagne de problemes comportementaux et affectifs (troubles autistiques et troubles de l'humeur, entre autres). Depuis quelques annees, nous comprenons mieux les bases de cette maladie et, consequemment, des medicaments sont actuellement testes afin de verifier s'ils peuvent ameliorer le comportement des individus affliges et ainsi alleger le fardeau familial. Pour notre equipe de recherche, la lovastatine, un medicament approuve par Sante Canada il y a plus de 20 ans et utilise pour traiter a long terme l'hypercholesterolemie, pourrait s'averer un traitement a la fois abordable, securitaire et efficace du syndrome du X fragile. Nous avons donc initie une etude clinique a court terme avec ce medicament chez 16 individus affectes par ce syndrome. Toutefois, comme c'est le cas pour plusieurs autres traitements, une reponse cliniquement significative n'est pas toujours observee chez les individus. L'objectif de ce projet de recherche consiste en la decouverte de proteines facilement mesurables dans le sang qui nous permettront d'identifier au prealable les individus etant le plus susceptibles de repondre positivement au traitement propose. Pour realiser ce projet, des echantillons de sang seront preleves avant et apres le traitement a la lovastatine. De nombreuses proteines sanguines seront ainsi mesurees avant et apres ledit traitement chez tous les individus pour verifier s'il existe une correlation entre l'abondance relative de ces proteines et l'amelioration du comportement, et ce, afin d'identifier laquelle ou lesquelles temoignent d'une reponse favorable au traitement. A long terme, ce projet vise a mesurer les proteines d'interet avant de debuter un eventuel traitement afin d'optimiser la reponse clinique et d'eviter d'exposer inutilement les individus a un traitement qui serait pour eux inefficace et qui pourrait leur causer des effets secondaires.

Keywords-MotsClés: ADIPOSITE; BIOSTATISTIQUES; DIABETE GESTATIONNEL; GENETIQUE; LEPTINE; EPIGENETIQUE
Abstract-Résumé: Le diabete de grossesse predispose les enfants a un risque augmente d'obesite et de diabete plus tard dans leur vie. Les phenomenes biologiques qui expliquent ce lien restent encore obscurs, mais des etudes suggerent que les taux de glucose eleves de la mere auraient un impact sur des « marques » qui influencent de tres pres l'expression des genes. Ces « marques epigenetiques » induites par l'exposition au diabete de grossesse ont ete observees tout pres de genes impliques dans la regulation de l'appetit et du poids, tel que la leptine. Notre etude nous aidera a eclaircir si les marques epigenetiques pres du gene de la leptine font partie des phenomenes biologiques qui expliquent le lien entre le diabete de grossesse et le risque d'obesite chez les enfants.

Keywords-MotsClés: CELLULES SOUCHES; CYTOMETRIE DE FLUX; DIFFERENCIATION CELLULAIRE; IMMUNOBIOLOGIE; IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE; INVOLUTION THYMIQUE; PROLIFERATION CELLULAIRE; THYMUS; TRANSCRIPTOMIQUE; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Le thymus est un organe tres important pour le systeme immunitaire. Il est responsable de la maturation des lymphocytes T, cellules ayant un role central dans la regulation des reponses immunitaires. Le thymus est l'organe qui vieillit le plus rapidement chez l'humain : il commence a s'atrophier des l'age d'un an. Cette degenerescence provoque une diminution graduelle de la production des lymphocytes T, menant a un affaiblissement de nos defenses naturelles contre les infections et les cancers. Par ailleurs, plusieurs facteurs peuvent venir accelerer l'atrophie thymique, comme les infections, la grossesse et les traitements de chimiotherapie. Ainsi, bien qu'elle soit meconnue, l'atrophie thymique est la maladie immunitaire la plus repandue. C'est pourquoi il est essentiel de mieux comprendre comment le thymus se developpe et comment il vieillit. Ceci pourrait nous permettre de trouver des traitements qui renverseront sa degenerescence ou encore de recreer un thymus fonctionnel a partir des cellules souches d'un individu.

TitreApplicationTitle: Deciphering Protein Quality Control Pathways Targeting Cytosolic Proteins for Proteasome Degradation
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOCHEMISTRY; CELL BIOLOGY; MASS SPECTROMETRY; MICROSCOPY; NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES; PROTEASOME; PROTEIN HOMEOSTASIS; PROTEIN QUALITY CONTROL; UBIQUITIN; YEAST GENETICS
Abstract-Résumé: Proteins are essential components of the cell that participate to all aspect of cell life (e.g., enzymatic activity, structural component, maintenance and duplication of the genetic material, communication with other cells). After synthesis, proteins are assembled (i.e., folded) to their native state and surveillance pathways ensure that aberrant proteins (i.e., misfolded or damaged) are repaired or eliminated from the cell. Failure to eliminate aberrant proteins is associated to aging and numerous neurodegenerative proteopathies like Parkinson's disease. In order to better understand how the cell recognizes aberrant proteins and targets them for degradation, we will study several protein quality control pathways that employ so-called ubiquitin ligases. Ubiquitin ligases are enzymes that mediate a modification (i.e., ubiquitination) on aberrant proteins that is then recognized by the proteasome, a large cellular machinery, that degrades proteins. More specifically, we will investigate how these ubiquitin ligases recognize misfolded proteins. An exciting prospect is that modification of the protein quality control pathways (e.g., using drugs) could increase the degradation of aberrant proteins, thereby reducing their accumulation in the cell, improving cell survival, and stopping the progression of neurodegenerative diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effects of Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) on drug disposition and CYP450 activities; a special look at extra-hepatic metabolism.
Keywords-MotsClés: CYTOCHROMES P450; DRUG ANALYSIS; DRUG METABOLISM; LC-MS/MS; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; PHARMACOGENETICS; PHARMACOKINETICS; PHENOTYPE; TYPE 2 DIABETES
Abstract-Résumé: Drug-related morbidity (side-effects) is an important public health concern affecting both clinical outcomes and healthcare costs. Patients with type-2 diabetes (T2D) represent a particular interest in practice because of the large number of patients afflicted by this disease and because of the number of drugs required to treat the hyperglycaemia status and prevent cardiovascular comorbidities. On average, patients with T2D may take upto 8-10 drugs per day. Consequently, significant drug-drug interactions and large intra- and inter-individual variability are observed for the same dose of drugs administered to T2D patients. We propose to evaluate the contribution of the major system involved in drug elimination (CYP450 drug-metabolizing enzymes) with special attention to the role of disease state, focusing on T2D. Another important factor taken into consideration throughout our project is the determination of drug concentrations not only in plasma but more specifically in tissues, i.e., at the vicinity of drug action sites. The aim of this project is to study in depth two factors pertaining to intersubject variability in drug action in specific patient subpopulations: 1) the influence of T2D and its comorbidities on drug metabolism and 2) drug metabolism in extra-hepatic tissues. The acquired knowledge will contribute to reducing drug inefficacy and toxicities by better adjusting drug dose or selecting more appropriate drugs.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular Determinants of Cell Death in the Heart
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIAC MYOCYTES; CELL CULTURE; CELL DEATH; GENE EXPRESSION; HYPOXIA; MITOCHONDRIA
Abstract-Résumé: A delicate balance exists between cell growth and cell death. In the context of the adult myocardium inappropriate or inordinate cell loss through an apoptotic process may profoundly influence cardiac structure and/or function given the limited and meager ability of the heart for repair after injury. The ability to prevent or modulate inappropriate cardiac cell death would be of significant therapeutic value in maintaining cardiac function after injury. These studies will provide new information and advance our current understanding regarding the mechanisms that govern cell death in the heart. The long-term goals of these studies are directed towards understanding the mechanisms that underlie aberrant apoptosis in hypertrophic and failing hearts. This will lead to the development of new more effective treatments for patients with heart disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Leukocyte-Trophoblast Mediated Utero-Placental Vascular Remodeling
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGENESIS; CELL/EXPLANT CULTURE; CHEMOKINE BIOLOGY; PLACENTAL DEVELOPMENT/PATHOLOGY; PREECLAMPSIA / INTRAUTERINE GROWTH RESTRICTION; REPRODUCTIVE IMMUNOLOGY; UTERO-PLACENTAL VASCULAR REMODELLING
Abstract-Résumé: Two major disorders of pregnancy, Preeclampsia (PE) and poor fetal growth (IUGR) both result in an increased risk of death or disability for mum and baby. Both are thought to originate in early pregnancy during development of the placenta (afterbirth). At this time cells from the placenta called trophoblasts invade the lining of the womb (decidua) and dramatically remodel the vessels. This is essential to provide the baby with a sufficient supply of oxygen and nutrients. This process is defective in both PE and IUGR.  How trophoblasts remodel the vessel is not well understood. We have evidence that the mother's white blood cells (WBC) play an important role in vessel remodeling. We will investigate how WBC and trophoblasts act to remodel vessels in early pregnancy, and how this goes wrong in PE. We have developed a model of vessel remodeling, by culturing small pieces of placenta and decidua together, and see vessel remodeling identical to that seen in actual pregnancy. We will use this model to determine the exact events and factors involved in vessel remodeling, focussing on the role of the WBC. We will study a family of proteins called chemokines that are involved in WBC function. We will investigate whether there are differences in WBC or proteins expressed in PE. We have unparalleled access to early pregnancy tissues from normal and PE pregnancies. Our novel model allows us to study the very early processes involved in vessel remodeling. We have shown for the first time that specialized WBC enter the vessel wall, and may be responsible for the remodeling and recruitment of trophoblasts. We suggest that the failed remodeling in PE may be due to abnormal WBC function that may harm trophoblasts. This research will greatly increase our understanding of the roles of WBC in vessel remodeling and how this is defective in PE and IUGR.

TitreApplicationTitle: Binder of SPerm (BSP) genes and proteins: Role of human and mouse BSP proteins in sperm function and fertilization
Keywords-MotsClés: FERTILIZATION; GAMETE BIOLOGY (SPERM); MALE INFERTILITY; MALE REPRODUCTIVE TRACT; REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY; SEMINAL PLASMA PROTEINS; SPERM CAPACITATION; SPERM-EGG INTERACTION
Abstract-Résumé: Infertility is now defined by World Health Organization (WHO) as a "reproductive disease" that affects about 15% couples in the human population.   Approximately 50% of all cases can be traced to either partner.  Regardless of whether it is male or female infertility, affected couples suffer from enormous emotional and psychological distress and it can constitute a major life crisis in the social context. Many unknown cases of infertility have a genetic or molecular basis. The understanding of the molecular genetics of male infertility is just beginning, new genes are being discovered and molecular diagnostic approaches are being developed. This will greatly help diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to treat human infertility. The goal of the current investigation is to understand the molecular basis of male infertility which could provide a rationale basis for novel approaches in the treatments of male infertility.

TitreApplicationTitle: The long-term effects of dietary sodium restriction on clinical outcomes in patients with heart failure. SODIUM-HF (Study of Dietary Intervention Under 100 MMOL in Heart Failure)
Keywords-MotsClés: HEART FAILURE; QUALITY OF LIFE; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; SODIUM
Abstract-Résumé: Heart failure remains one of the most common, disabling, expensive and fatal medical conditions worldwide. In Canada, it is present in about 1/100 to 2/100 Canadians, and despite important improvements with medications, the number of deaths from heart failure continues to be high. Given that heart failure is a condition resulting in water and salt retention, it is generally thought that reducing dietary salt would help patients. Importantly, one of every 5 emergency room visits of patients with heart failure is linked to extra salt in the diet.  This study is conducted to find out if a low sodium diet (1500 mg/day sodium), compared with a moderate sodium diet (2300 mg/day sodium), reduces the chance that patients with heart failure will be admitted to the hospital, need to go to the emergency department, or live longer.  This is a clinical trial. This research will take place in 15 centers across Canada and will involved 1000 patients. Patients are expected to attend clinical visits over a period of 12 months to help them achieve and stay at the correct amount of salt in the diet.  Prior studies have tested if a lower salt diet improves how people feel or if they were hospitalized for heart failure. However, these trials were small and had short follow-up and so are unable to provide enough information to change practice and recommend to all patients with heart failure. Our trial is large enough to see if this will be good for most patients, and long enough to see if this makes a difference in clinical outcomes such needing to be hospitalized, visit the emergency department or die.

TitreApplicationTitle: Structural and Functional Correlates of Neuroplastic Change Associated with Stroke Recovery and Learning
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN; DIFFUSION TENSOR IMAGING; HUMAN; LEARNING; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; MYELIN; NEUROPLASTICITY; STROKE; WHITE MATTER
Abstract-Résumé: The main goal of this research is to understand whether the white matter of the brain is changed by experience. Further, we will examine which is the key driver of recovery of arm function after stroke: changes in the structure of the brain or changes in how brain regions interact with one another. Together, these data will advance our understanding of how neural systems support recovery from stroke. We have developed a new MRI technique that allows us to assess the health of a brain structure called myelin. This structure is important as it allows information to travel down nerves faster; the more myelin the quicker the signal can be conducted. Because we are among one of a few centers in the world who have this capability we will be the first to consider whether changes in myelin content care related to the amount of use of the paretic arm after stroke.  Perhaps more importantly, we will also test whether or not movement training can increase myelin in the brain in both people with stroke and healthy controls. If movement training does increase myelin in the brain, we will have identified an important new target for rehabilitation interventions. Taken together, the results of this study will provide crucial information for the advancement of stroke rehabilitation strategies that may improve quality of life for Canadians with stroke.

Keywords-MotsClés: COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY; DNA MOTIFS; GENOMICS; REPETITIVE ELEMENTS; RETROVIRUSES; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: One of the largest classes of proteins in the human genome - encompassing ~700 of the ~22,000 known human protein-coding genes - is the C2H2 zinc fingers.  These proteins are primarily believed to bind to specific DNA sequences and thereby regulate the expression, accessibility, and topology of the genome.  Most, however, are simply uncharacterized.   We propose to study the functions of proteins in the C2H2 class by exploring what sequences they bind, whether they bind DNA, RNA, or protein, and how the amino-acid sequence of the C2H2 zinc finger proteins relates to their biochemical and genetic functions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Fatty Acid Reference Ranges
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE; DISEASE ASSOCIATION; EPIDEMIOLOGY; ETHNIC DIFFERENCES; FATTY ACIDS; HEALTHY ADULTS; REFERENCE RANGES; SEX DIFFERENCES (BIOLOGICAL)
Abstract-Résumé: There is tremendous interest in understanding the relationship between blood levels of fatty acids and health. While different types of fats are commonly measured in the doctors office such as blood cholesterol and triglycerides, which are used as measures of health status, it is not yet feasible to evaluate individual fatty acids.  Measurement of blood fatty acids is widely reported in research, however the interpretability of human studies remains poor due to the lack of clinically useful reference ranges. This significant gap underscores a major challenge in the translation of the basic science of fatty acid research into clinical practice. Reference ranges for individual fatty acids would make it possible to establish healthy targets and evaluate whether certain levels of fatty acids are associated with deficiency or increased chronic disease risk. Thus, the central gap that the proposed study will address is the development of fatty acid reference ranges in healthy adult Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Control of cardiomyocyte proliferation by Mdm2 and p53.
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL CYCLE; HEART FAILURE; METABOLISM; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENES
Abstract-Résumé: Heart failure (HF) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Canada. Quality of life and prognosis for this group of patients remains poor with more than $1 billion of Canada's annual health budget being spent on this patient population. There are currently no means available which directly target the disease process itself.  As such, it is exceedingly important to consider novel approaches that allow discovery of alternate treatment strategies for the treatment of HF. In adults, cardiomyocytes (CM) cannot divide and thus are unable to restore heart function in patients with HF. We feel that this area of research is both of critical clinical importance and of great scientific merit. Our interest in identifying factors which regulate cardiac tissue homeostasis, including the multiplication of CM could provide the failing heart with the potential to "repair" itself. The anti-cancer factor p53 is the most frequent inactivated gene in human cancers. The activity of p53 is inhibited by Mdm2 which marks p53 for destruction in the cell. In response to stress, p53 either stops cellular division or triggers cell death. Thus, tight control of p53 through Mdm2 is pivotal in order to maintain the protective effects of p53 in normal cells within the body. We reason that an explanation for the absence of any significant CM proliferation lies, at least in part, in the Mdm2/p53 complex. This assumption is based on recent observations that p53 can also regulate basic physiological processes in cells under normal conditions, e.g. regulation of sugar metabolism, energy supply and protection against harmful oxidants. Thus, we hypothesize that Mdm2/p53 is a key regulator of cardiac tissue homeostasis. Our grant proposal will investigate whether genetic inactivation of the Mdm2 and p53 could trigger(1) CM proliferation in the heart of adult mice, (2)cardiac hypertrophy and (3) metabolic transformation.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Pain Summation in the Prediction of Poor Rehabilitation Outcomes in Individuals with Whiplash Injuries.
Keywords-MotsClés: DISABILITY; PAIN; PSYCHOSOCIAL; REHABILITATION; WHIPLASH
Abstract-Résumé: Individuals who have sustained whiplash injuries differ in how they respond to physical activity. For some individuals, repeated physical activity or exercise will lead to reductions in pain. For others, repeated physical activity or exercise will lead to increases in pain. Research from our laboratory has shown that, in response to repeated low level physical activity, approximately 30% of individuals with whiplash injuries will show an increase in pain of 80% or greater. We refer to this phenomenon as repetition-induced activity-related summation of pain, or RISP. It is possible that individuals who show elevated RISP may not benefit from traditional physical rehabilitation interventions for whiplash injuries. In the proposed program of research, we wish to examine whether susceptibility to RISP will predict who will, and who will not, benefit from physical rehabilitation. A better understanding of why some individuals experience an increase in pain in response to activity might lead to the development of more effective interventions for individuals who have sustained whiplash injuries.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of the host microbiota in opportunistic infection in cystic fibrosis (CF) and lung transplantation.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIMIROBIAL STEWARDSHIP; BACTERIAL COLONIZATION; BACTERIOTHERAPY; IMMUNOLOGY; INFECTION; LUNG PHYSIOLOGY; LUNG TRANSPLANTATION; MICROBIOME; OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTION; REJECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Cystic Fibrosis (CF) is the most common fatal inherited disease of those of European descent.  Many of those with CF progress to require lung transplantation, but the rate of progression of disease, the need for lung transplantation, and predictors of complications such as opportunistic infections are not wholly explained by the genetic composition of the host and traditional environmental factors.  The CF lung is colonized by diverse microbes, including bacteria, fungi and viruses, collectively referred to as the 'microbiota'.  Although not all of these microbes are pathogenic, they may profoundly affect the progression of disease, susceptibility to infection and prognosis after lung transplantation.  As part of a large collaborative group, my goal is to evaluate the lung microbiota and identify changes associated with specific disease states, opportunistic infections and rates of disease progression, with the goal of identifying novel prognostic indicators and therapeutic targets.

TitreApplicationTitle: Silencing Stat3 signaling in multiple myeloma: identifying potent small molecule inhibitors of Stat3
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTI-CANCER DRUGS; MOLECULAR RECOGNITION; MOLECULAR THERAPEUTICS; MULTIPLE MYELOMA; SRC HOMOLOGY 2 DOMAINS; STAT3 PROTEIN
Abstract-Résumé: Chemotherapy treatments rely heavily upon toxic drugs, which, although effective, are highly toxic and result in significant side effects, immensely reducing a cancer patient's quality of life. Frequent resistance to these toxic agents also develops, further compounding the problem. The Stat3 protein pathway confers resistance to cancer cell death in multiple myeloma(MM) tumor cells by preventing cell death and promoting cell survival. This project aims to develop novel drugs that specifically disrupt the formation of Stat3:Stat3 cancer-promoting protein complexes and prevent Stat3 gene expression programs. Through the suppression of Stat3 protein, our agents aim to kill MM tumor cells and sensitize tumors to traditional chemotherapies, thereby reducing effective dosages and lowering toxicity. Our Stat3 inhibitors will significantly reduce the side effects associated with conventional chemotherapy as either stand-alone agents or in combinatorial adjuvant therapeutic regime.

TitreApplicationTitle: Action of the CCR4-NOT complex in mammalian gene silencing networks
Keywords-MotsClés: DISEASE; GENE EXPRESSION; MICRORNA; POST-TRANSCRIPTIONAL CONTROL; RNA STABILITY; TRANSLATION
Abstract-Résumé: The CCR4-NOT complex is a type of cellular machinery that controls the activity of genetic material (messenger RNA), which in turn serves as the template for the synthesis of proteins in mammals.  The CCR4-NOT complex helps regulate such biological processes as fat metabolism, germ cell development and many others.  Moreover, its ability to regulate messenger RNAs is often disregulated in cancers and other diseases.  We are studying how the CCR4-NOT complex is recruited to specific messenger RNAs, and how, once recruited, it shuts down protein synthesis and brings about messenger RNA degradation.  Understanding these fundamental mechanisms of how the CCR4-NOT complex functions will allow us to design new molecular diagnostics for screening diseases and potentially target these diseases through novel therapeutic avenues.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluating a small change approach to preventing long term weight gain in overweight and obese adults
Keywords-MotsClés: DISEASE PREVENTION; LIFESTYLE; OBESITY
Abstract-Résumé: There is little evidence that the rise in obesity observed in recent decades is slowing.  Few would argue that it is the environment rather than individual biology that is driving the rapid increase in obesity regardless of age, gender or race.  Accordingly, while it is clear that most adults can adopt significant changes in physical activity and diet behavior and achieve substantial weight loss short-tern, forces within the environment make it difficult to sustain dramatic changes in behaviour long-term and thus sustained weight loss, if not weight gain (rebound), is the result.  Recently it has been suggested that a strategy of preventing weight gain may be more feasible than a strategy of weight reduction for the entire population and that prevention of weight gain could be achieved in most adults through a small-changes approach to diet and physical activity.  Specifically, a 100 kilocalorie change in any combination of increased energy expenditure and decreased energy intake could prevent weight gain in most adults.   Although initial evidence suggests that the adoption of small changes in lifestyle behaviors can prevent weight gain over a few months, whether adopting small changes in diet and physical activity can be adopted and sustained for several years in unknown. We will perform a study designed to test the effectiveness of a small-changes approach in diet and physical activity to prevent weight gain long-term (3 years) in overweight and obese adults.  Our approach will incorporate established behavior change techniques and proven methods for constructing health messages to encourage ongoing goal setting, planning, and monitoring of healthy lifestyle behavior. It is hoped that the findings of our study will provide a practical option for overweight and obese persons to adopt healthy behaviors long term and prevent weight gain.

TitreApplicationTitle: Integrated Systems and Team Working for Children with Disabilities: An Institutional Ethnography of Health Professional Practice in the Special Education Context
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDHOOD DISABILITY; INSTITUTIONAL ETHNOGRAPHY; INTEGRATED SYSTEMS AND SERVICES; INTERPROFESSIONAL COLLABORATION; MEDICAL COMMUNICATION; QUALITATIVE METHODS; SPECIAL EDUCATION
Abstract-Résumé: Children with disabilities or chronic health conditions have health care needs beyond clinics and hospitals. They often require health-related support at school in order to develop and learn. In order for health care needs to be met effectively and efficiently at school, clinical professionals must interact with school systems. Currently, this interaction is problematic. Clinical professionals tend to use documents to communicate with school-based professionals, or communicate through parents/caregivers. Thus, families are often caught in the middle, managing two different systems that are not well integrated. Children with disabilities or chronic health conditions thus fall through cracks as parents and professionals negotiate interprofessional and intersystem challenges. This research will reveal more about how people currently work through these challenges, by interviewing parents and professionals, observing school support team meetings, and reviewing documents from practitioners and policy-makers. Revealing what is currently done - both the problematic and the creative solutions - is an important step toward identifying opportunities for policy-level change and realization of school-based health support for children with disabilities.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of GABAergic Circuit Formation.
Keywords-MotsClés: CULTURE; DEVELOPEMENT; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GABA; INNERVATION FIELD; LIVE IMAGING; NEUROTROPHIC FACTORS; PLASTICITY; SIGLE CELL GENETICS; SYNAPSE
Abstract-Résumé: GABAergic neurons, a particular subset of brain cells, powerfully control the function of brain circuits. Many common neurological disorders, including schizophrenia and epilepsy, are thought to be partially consequence of defects in the development of GABAergic neurons. In particular, such disorders seem to be associated with defects in the way this subset of neurons connects and communicates with other neurons, via specialized loci called synapses. Because of the complexity of brain circuitry, it has been so far very difficult to understand how GABAergic neurons form synapses and how disturbances in this process may lead to altered cognitive functions. The experiments we propose will use modern live imaging and gene manipulations techniques to dissect the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the formation and plasticity of GABAergic synapses. This approach will shed light on the factors regulating the formation of GABAergic synapses in the normal brain and on the pathological process leading to their disturbance. Such understanding is the first necessary step towards the development of new targeted therapeutic approaches.

TitreApplicationTitle: Adeno-associated virus gene replacement in fragile X syndrome
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTISM; CELL SIGNALING; CEREBELLUM; EPILEPSY; G-PROTEIN COUPLED RECEPTOR; GLUTAMATE; MENTAL DISABILITY; MOUSE MODEL; NEURODEVELOPMENT; PURKINJE
Abstract-Résumé: Fragile X syndrome (FXS), a neurodevelopmental disorder and a syndromic form of autism, is the most common inherited cause of mental retardation.  In addition to varying degrees of mental retardation, persons with FXS display hyperactivity, social anxiety, autistic characteristics, and seizures (Hampson et al., 2012).  Our laboratory uses an excellent animal model of this human mental disorder called the FXS knockout mouse.  This mutant mouse is abnormal in that the protein product of the missing gene, called "Fragile X Mental Retardation Protein (FMRP)" is missing in these mice, as it is in humans with FXS.  We hypothesize that the documented impairments in the behaviour of FXS knockout mice are caused by the lack of FMRP in certain brain regions, and that reintroduction of this missing protein into the brain of the FXS mouse using a viral vector encoding the missing gene, will restore at least some of these functions.  This therapeutic strategy is termed virally-mediated gene therapy.  The goal is to create an appropriate expression vector, inject it into the brain of the FXS mouse, and subsequently determine if restoration of anatomical, cellular, and behavioural impairments has occurred.  The experimental strategies and methods that we will develop in this project are potentially applicable to not only persons with FXS, but also to other neurological disorders where a key brain protein is missing, reduced or abnormal.  Examples include other autistic syndromes such as Rett and Angelman syndrome, lysosomal storage diseases such as adrenoleukodystrophy, and possibly some neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease, Huntington's diseases, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Control of cell morphogenesis by PIP signaling
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVANCED MICROSCOPY TECHNIQUES; CELL BIOLOGY; CELL MORPHOGENESIS; CELL POLARITY; CHROMATIN ORGANIZATION; CYTOKINESIS; DROSOPHILA MOLECULAR GENETICS; MALE FERTILITY; PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL PHOSPHATES; SPERMATOGENESIS
Abstract-Résumé: Our bodies are made of many different types of cells, with various shapes and functions. For example, male germ cells that will become sperm undergo dramatic cell shape changes. They become very long and thin, with compact heads at one end and whip-like tails at the other. Together, these features allow the sperm to swim towards and fertilize an egg. Failures in cell shape changes can lead to the production of defective sperm, resulting in infertility. To understand how cells change shape, we are studying male germ cells in the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster). This allows us to take advantage of powerful genetic techniques and well-characterized stages of sperm development available in the fly. Using this system, we discovered that lipid molecules called PIPs are important for cell shape changes. Male flies with mutations in the proteins that control formation of PIPs can't form normal sperm and are sterile. The main goal of our research is to understand how these proteins regulate changes in cell shape. To do this, we will use advanced microscopy and molecular genetic techniques. Since human sperm and fly sperm form in a similar way, our discoveries may ultimately translate into novel ways to treat human male infertility.

TitreApplicationTitle: Engineering DNA-nanosystems for tumor targeting
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMEDICAL ENGINERING; BREAST CANCER; DNA ASSEMBLY; NANOTECHNOLOGY; TARGETING
Abstract-Résumé: The survival of patients with breast cancer improves dramatically when they are diagnosed early.  One of the biggest challenges in diagnosing or treating cancer is to be able to delivery enough of a small molecule diagnostic or therapeutic agent to the timor.  Recently, it has been demonstrated that the size, shape, and surface chemistry of a delivery system can influence how much of the agent is delivered into a tumor.  In my previous CIHR funded grant, we identified specific design parameters for building the optimal delivery vehicle to target tumors.  In this renewal application, we propose to use DNA to build these optimal nanoparticle-delivery systems, consisting  of a combination of DNA, synthetic polymer polyethylene glycol, and gold nanoparticles to engineer nanosystems of different sizes (20 to 150 nm), shapes (rod, cube, triangles, and oval), and aspect ratios.  We will then test the targeting or delivery efficiency in cells, tissues, and in whole animals of each design.  Using these biological models, we will be able to identify the optimal design and test how much of an improvement in diagnostic sensitivity.  The outcome of this important study is the development of new nanotechnology-based delivery vehicles for diagnosing and treating cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Les personnes cliniquement obèses souffrent-elles davantage de la douleur sociale induite par le rejet?
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNITION SOCIALE; CONFORMISME; CYBERBALL; DOULEUR SOCIALE; EMPATHIE; IMAGERIE PAR RESONANCE MAGNETIQUE FONCTIONNELLE; OBESITE; REJET
Abstract-Résumé: L'obesite est une condition medicale en forte croissance et est associee a plusieurs problemes de sante. Notamment, les personnes obeses seraient plus sensibles a la douleur physique. De plus, du a la stigmatisation a l'egard de l'obesite, cette population semble plus susceptible de vivre une douleur «sociale», douleur ressentie suite a la perte de liens sociaux, a la menace de ces liens, ou encore a la devalorisation de sa valeur sociale. Toutefois, aucune etude n'a investigue la douleur sociale chez cette population. Par ailleurs, un recoupement entre les regions cerebrales associees a la douleur physique et celles associees a la douleur sociale a ete mis en evidence. Celui-ci a d'importantes implications. Par exemple, la sensibilite accrue a la douleur physique des personnes obeses pourrait parallelement accroitre leurs chances de souffrir de douleur sociale. Cela met en lumiere le risque accru de cette population de souffrir de douleur sociale et souligne la pertinence d'etudier la question. L'objectif de la presente etude est donc de determiner si les personnes obeses ressentent plus de douleur sociale suite au rejet que les personnes ayant un poids sante. Pour ce faire, les participants seront amenes a jouer a un jeu virtuel qui simulera le rejet social, et nous nous interesserons a la douleur sociale subsequente. Nous croyons que les personnes obeses manifesteront une douleur sociale plus elevee que les participants ayant un poids sante. Enfin, les resultats de la presente etude permettront de mieux comprendre le phenomene de la douleur sociale suite au rejet chez les personnes obeses et conduiront a des pistes d'interventions pertinentes. De plus, du au recoupement douleur physique/douleur sociale, il est possible que ces interventions diminuent du meme coup les deux types de douleur, ayant ainsi un impact considerable sur la qualite de vie.

L'alternative a la cesarienne lors d'une seconde grossesse, l'accouchement vaginal apres la cesarienne (AVAC), est associee a moins de complication pour la mere et le bebe. TitreApplicationTitle: Évaluation d'un programme de gestion du stress et de l'anxiété pour les étudiants en médecine
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETE; BIEN-ETRE; PREVENTION; SANTE MENTALE; STRESS; ETUDIANTS EN MEDECINE
Abstract-Résumé: Au Quebec, un etudiant en medecine sur 20 considere son stress comme ingerable. Ce stress decoulerait du surplus de travail, de la competition et de l'exposition a la souffrance humaine. Le stress eleve peut entrainer une augmentation de l'anxiete, des troubles du sommeil et une diminution du bien-etre psychologique. A la fin de leur formation, 48 % de ces etudiants rapportent etre anxieux comparativement a 4% en premiere annee d'etude. Au moment de leur graduation, 52 % de ces etudiants rapportaient des difficultes a s'endormir. La detresse psychologique de ces etudiants engendre plusieurs consequences graves telles qu'un declin de la pratique empathique et du professionnalisme. Des traitements psychologiques preventifs realises aux Etats-Unis ont montre leur efficacite pour reduire l'anxiete et le stress chez les etudiants en medecine. Jusqu'a maintenant, au Quebec, aucune intervention validee empiriquement et mesuree avec des outils standardises n'a ete developpee dans le but de reduire le stress et l'anxiete chez ces etudiants. Ce projet evaluera l'impact d'une intervention de gestion du stress sur le niveau de stress, d'anxiete, d'insomnie et de bien-etre psychologique d'etudiants en medecine a l'Universite Laval. Avant de mettre sur pied l'intervention de gestion du stress, les barrieres et les preferences, des etudiants en medecine de l'Universite Laval ont ete explorees a l'aide de groupes de discussion. Les resultats montrent que les etudiants sont interesses a participer a une intervention de gestion du stress. Cette etude sera la premiere a evaluer de facon rigoureuse, sur un echantillon aussi grand, une intervention structuree offerte dans le cadre d'un cours obligatoire. Une intervention introduite dans un cours obligatoire permettra de rejoindre les individus vivant de la detresse qui ne se seraient pas inscrits de facon volontaire. Si l'intervention s'avere efficace, elle pourrait etre implantee dans d'autres facultes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Determinants of the progression and outcome of organic mitral regurgitation
Keywords-MotsClés: DOPPLER ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY; MAXIMAL EFFORT CAPACITY; ORGANIC MITRAL REGURGITATION; PROGRESSION OF MITRAL REGURGITATION
Abstract-Résumé: The heart is composed of four cavities: two auricles and two ventricles, left and right. The left side is the pump of the heart, sending the blood to the tissues. Between the cavities, there are valves, that open and close according to the time of the cardiac cycle. Those valves enable the blood to go in one way only. They are, usually, hermetic. The mitral valve is the one between the left auricle and the left ventricle. In multiple cases, this valve leaks. This regurgitation can be mild, moderate or severe, evaluated by Doppler echocardiography. It can evolve, more or less quickly, but we don't know the determinants of this evolution. When the regurgitation becomes severe and causes symptoms (an exaggerate breathlessness) or increases the left ventricle volume (increase the probability of sudden death or heart failure), a cardiac surgery should be done to repair or replace the valve.  But the exact time to do an optimal surgery is not well established. If we wait too long, the operatory mortality and the probability that the heart doesn't recuperate (leading to heart failure) are increased. A surgery done on a person that doesn't need it is not good either.  This study will analyse the metabolic profile of the patient and if it influences the progression of the disease. Thus, the patient's follow-up will be more adapted. Also, we suspect that the severity or at least the regurgitant volume can be modified (increased or decreased) by exercise. Therefore, daily activity can have an impact on the regurgitation and modify the time before there is a major impact on the heart. So, we will evaluate (by doing effort tests) how the dynamic modification of the mitral regurgitation has an influence on the progression and on the outcome (surgery or death). With these results, we will be able to do a better evaluation of the risks related to the disease and permit an appropriate treatment, follow-up and have a good timing for the surgery.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effets d'un entraînement supramaximal de six semaines sur le débit sanguin cérébral, l'autorégulation cérébrale et la prévalence de symptômes orthostatiques
Keywords-MotsClés: APTITUDE AEROBIE; AUTOREGULATION CEREBRALE; CYCLISME; DOPPLER TRANSCRANIEN; DEBIT SANGUIN CEREBRAL; ENTRAINEMENT PAR INTERVALLES; ENTRAINEMENT SUPRAMAXIMAL; OXYGENATION CEREBRALE; PHYSIOLOGIE CEREBROVASCULAIRE; SYMPTOMES ORTHOSTATIQUES
Abstract-Résumé: Il est bien etabli dans la litterature que l'entrainement aerobie est associe a des effets benefiques sur plusieurs fonctions du corps humain. Cependant, seules des etudes transversales, comparant des individus inactifs et des individus actifs, ainsi que des etudes chez l'animal ont observe des changements importants du debit sanguin cerebral lie a l'entrainement aerobie. En effet, l'entrainement aerobie est associe a une augmentation du debit sanguin cerebral, ce qui serait associe a une diminution de l'incidence d'accidents vasculaires cerebraux et d'autres maladies cerebrovasculaires, d'Alzheimer et de demence. Toutefois, dans les etudes longitudinales, les augmentations du debit sanguin cerebral sont beaucoup plus subtiles, voire inexistantes. Dans la presente etude, nous utiliserons plus specifiquement un entrainement supramaximal mene jusqu'a epuisement et evaluerons ses effets sur le debit sanguin cerebral.   De plus, les athletes ont une prevalence plus elevee de symptomes orthostatiques, tels que des etourdissements, des nausees et des pertes de conscience lors de changements brusques de leur pression arterielle, comme lors de changements de position rapides. Cela pourrait etre explique par un delai de la reponse d'autoregulation cerebrale dynamique chez ces individus, c'est-a-dire un delai dans la reponse de vasoconstriction ou de vasodilatation des vaisseaux sanguins du cerveau en reponse a des changements rapides de pression arterielle. Cependant, nous ignorons si un entrainement intense peut aggraver ce phenomene chez des individus deja entraines. C'est ce que la presente etude examinera.

TitreApplicationTitle: Le rétromère : une nouvelle cible des kinases Src dans le transport endosomal lors du remodelage cellulaire
Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSE ET CANCER; FACTEURS TUMORICIDES; INVASION TUMORALE; MUTAGENESE; ONCOGENES; ORGANELLES; POLARISATION DU CYTOSQUELETTE; SIGNALISATION CELLULAIRE; TRANSFORMATION CELLULAIRE; TRANSPORT ENDOSOMAL
Abstract-Résumé: Le cancer est une maladie genetique au niveau cellulaire qui se developpe suivant l'acquisition par les cellules tumorales de nouvelles proprietes leur permettant de se multiplier sans restriction. Il est dirige par des mutations qui activent des oncogenes poussant les cellules a se diviser et a envahir l'organisme, combinees a des mutations dans les genes suppresseurs de tumeur qui limitent l'activite normale des oncogenes. Ensemble, ils determinent le devenir cellulaire en controlant les voies de signalisation qui dirigent l'expression des genes. Les avancees recentes ont permis de cibler la destruction des cellules cancereuses en inhibant les oncogenes dans les tumeurs humaines. Bien que cette strategie therapeutique soit efficace et plus selective, les succes semblent transitoires du au developpement d'une resistance cellulaire. Les cellules cancereuses semblent acquerir de nouvelles anomalies dans les voies de signalisation controlees par l'oncogeme cible, restaurant le benefice apporte par la mutation initiale. Le defi actuel est d'acquerir une comprehension fine des dysfonctionnements dans les reseaux de signalisation des oncogenes associes aux tumeurs, afin de developper des strategies basees sur une combinaison d'agents qui agiraient a differents niveaux pour contrecarrer ces oncogenes. Ce projet de recherche vise une connaissance approfondie des voies de signalisation reprogrammees par l'oncogene Src dans les tumeurs. Nous etudions le mode d'action de proteines virales qui s'accaparent les fonctions cellulaires de cet oncogene, soit pour transformer les cellules et creer un contexte tumoral, ou pour induire selectivement la mort des cellules cancereuses. Ces etudes pourraient avoir un impact sur notre comprehension des dysfonctionnements responsables de l'apparition des metastases qui est la principale cause de morbidite des cancers humains.

TitreApplicationTitle: Rôle du CD103 dans la régulation de l'inflammation pulmonaire.
Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHME; CD103; CELLULES DENDRITIQUES; CYTOMETRIE DE FLUX; INFLAMMATION; LYMPHOCYTES T REGULATEURS; POUDRE D'ACARIEN; SOURIS TRANSGENIQUES; TRANSFERTS ADOPTIFS; EPITHELIUM PULMONAIRE
Abstract-Résumé: La reponse immune est essentielle a la survie. En effet, la precision et l'efficacite du systeme immunitaire est la cle de maints mecanismes de protection, dont le combat contre les infections et la reparation des blessures, et ce, plus particulierement la ou les surfaces sont en contact direct avec des pathogenes, comme dans le poumon. Cependant, le controle de l'intensite et de la duree de la reponse inflammatoire sont deux autres aspects importants pour le maintien de la sante pulmonaire. En effet, une perte du controle des mecanismes de defense peut mener a d'irreparables dommages et a l'alteration des fonctions pulmonaires. Dans le cas de plusieurs maladies pulmonaires inflammatoires, comme l'asthme, l'intensite et la chronicite de l'inflammation sont responsables de la plupart des symptomes. Les mecanismes regulant la reponse inflammatoire et les etapes menant a la chronicite de la maladie ont ete le sujet de plusieurs recherches dans le domaine de l'inflammation. Meme si ces etudes ont mene a l'elaboration de plusieurs voies therapeutiques, la majorite de ces therapies visent a bloquer la reponse inflammatoire, ce qui mene souvent a des effets secondaires et a une resistance contre leur efficacite, d'ou l'interet de trouver de nouvelles voies therapeutiques. Nous croyons que les therapies visant les molecules participant au controle de la reponse inflammatoire pulmonaire auraient un avantage par rapport aux therapies actuelles. Toutefois, les mecanismes exacts impliques dans la regulation de l'inflammation pulmonaire ne sont pas bien compris. Recemment, notre laboratoire a observe que l'asthme est augmente chez des souris ayant une ablation du gene de l'intregrine alpha-E CD103. Ainsi, en utilisant un modele d'asthme chez la souris, des souris transgeniques et des etudes in vitro, nous esperons elucider le role de cette molecule dans le developpement de l'inflammation pulmonaire et d'evaluer son potentiel en tant que cible therapeutique potentielle.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'état dépressif à l'adolescence et le rôle de l'abus sexuel à l'enfance comme prédicteurs du risque de s'impliquer dans une aventure sans lendemain chez les garçons et les filles et les conséquences d'un tel comportement.
Keywords-MotsClés: ABUS SEXUELS; ADOLESCENCE; AVENTURE SANS LENDEMAIN; ESTIME DE SOI; GENRE; RISQUE SUICIDAIRE; SANTE MENTALE; SEXUALITE; ETAT DEPRESSIF
Abstract-Résumé: Ce projet vise a determiner le role de l'etat depressif a l'adolescence dans l'implication dans des aventures sans lendemain (ASL), soit comme predicteur ou consequence, ainsi que l'influence du genre dans cette relation. Pour ce faire, l'echantillon de plus de 8000 adolescents quebecois de 14 a 18 ans de l'enquete longitudinale Parcours Amoureux des Jeunes sera etudie. Les variables sont l'ASL, les symptomes depressifs (detresse psychologique, risque suicidaire) et l'estime de soi, et seront mesurees en trois fois afin de distinguer l'impact, a court et a moyen terme, des ASL sur la sante psychologique des jeunes. De plus, le devis longitudinal permettra de savoir si un effet cumulatif des ASL s'exerce sur les symptomes depressifs et l'estime de soi. Puisqu'un vecu d'agression sexuelle a l'enfance, plus frequent chez les filles, pourrait contribuer a la relation entre l'etat depressif et les ASL, cette co-variable sera egalement analysee selon le genre. Ce projet est d'autant plus pertinent qu'il s'interesse aux aspects de sante longtemps negliges dans l'etude des activites sexuelles sans engagement amoureux fort presentes a l'adolescence. De plus, il est primordial d'etudier les facteurs predisposant a l'ASL et ses consequences au plan de la sante mentale et sexuelle, car les consequences de ces activites ont rarement ete etudiees chez les adolescents, et que les impacts de la depression sont considerables. Ce projet concourra aussi a une meilleure comprehension d'une des nombreuses retombees d'une victimisation sexuelle a l'enfance. Finalement, il alimentera les debats sociaux et les programmes d'education sexuelle en proposant un discours nuance sur les consequences des ASL tout en distinguant des trajectoires de vulnerabilite (Grello et al., 2003).

TitreApplicationTitle: Qualités psychométriques de la version canadienne-française du Geriatric Anxiety Inventory
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETE; AINES; GERIATRIC ANXIETY INVENTORY; OUTILS D'EVALUATION ANXIETE GERIATRIQUE; POPULATION AGEE; TROUBLE D'ANXIETE GERIATRIQUE; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Les troubles anxieux s'averent tres prevalents chez la population agee, notamment le trouble d'anxiete generalisee (TAG) dont les taux de prevalence atteignent 7.3% (Wolitzky-Taylor, Castriotta, Lenze, Stanley, & Craske, 2010). Le TAG est un trouble persistant, severe et est caracterise par de l'anxiete et des inquietudes excessives, multiples, chroniques et incontrolables generant d'importantes consequences. Malgre ceci, la plupart des personnes agees atteintes ne sont ni identifiees ni traitees. Afin de pallier au manque d'outils de depistage efficaces et adaptes a la population agee, Pachana et al. (2007) ont elabore le Geriatric Anxiety Inventory (GAI), un outil specifiquement developpe pour evaluer la severite des symptomes anxieux chez les aines. Le GAI presente d'excellentes proprietes justifiant son utilisation, tout comme une version breve de 5 enonces, le GAI Short Form (Byrne & Pachana, 2011). Le GAI jouit d'une notoriete internationale, il a ete traduit en plusieurs langues dont le francais (GAI-CF), mais n'a pas ete valide aupres d'une population francophone. L'objectif principal est donc d'etudier les qualites psychometriques des versions longue et breve du GAI-CF afin de justifier son utilisation chez la population agee francophone. Un second objectif est de documenter les relations entre le score au GAI-CF et diverses caracteristiques sociodemographiques et cliniques des participants. Les 350 participants ages d'au moins 65 ans seront recrutes dans des clubs sociaux et de loisirs, un centre de jour, une clinique medicale et des residences pour aines. Disposer d'un instrument d'evaluation de l'anxiete specifique aux personnes agees est une necessite pour l'intervention en milieu francophone, car les troubles anxieux sont repandus dans la population agee qui augmente. Avec le GAI-CF valide, les cliniciens disposeront d'un instrument permettant de depister les aines anxieux et de documenter de facon fiable, valide et rapide les symptomes anxieux.

TitreApplicationTitle: Interactions between Pbp1/ATXN2 and repetitive DNA in cellular lifespan control
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; ATAXIA; ATAXIN 2; CALORIE RESTRICTION; CHROMATIN; LONG INTERGENIC NON-CODING RNA (LINCRNA); RESVERATROL; RIBOSOMAL RNA GENES (RDNA); RNA-DNA HYBRIDS; SIRTUINS
Abstract-Résumé: Why do we age, how does it promote disease, and can we control aging? Our bodies are built from millions of living entities called cells. Each cell has a copy of our DNA, which is arranged in thousands of units called genes. The cell often needs multiple copies of particular genes to survive. In fact, more than half of human DNA is repetitive. However, repeats create problems. Every time a cell divides, it makes a second copy of its DNA. Major errors can occur as cells copy DNA repeats. For example, repeated genes can get mixed up uncontrollably between the two DNA copies being prepared for cell division. This leads to the gain/loss of DNA creating so many errors that cells eventually fail to copy DNA and divide. But cells have processes that protect repetitive DNA. We previously found that cells stabilize repetitive DNA by anchoring it to internal cellular structures, much like people literally standing on each others' shoulders in a human tower benefit from holding on to a nearby post. In addition, longevity proteins called sirtuins stabilize repeated DNA by compacting it into tight structures. This would be analogous to people sitting on each others' shoulders in the human tower. This research group has new data indicating that a protein present in yeast and humans stabilizes DNA repeats via a new process similar to that of a police officer ensuring that observers of the human tower do not try to sabotage it. This research will reveal how this protein achieves its policing role to protect repeated DNA and maintain yeast/human cellular lifespan. Mutations in this protein are linked to the neurological diseases ataxia and also ALS.  These diseases disrupt the brain, body movement control, and eventually life. This research will test contributions of DNA repeat instability to disease and point to therapeutic avenues. All in all, this project may allow us to counteract cellular aging and prevent/cure its related diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: A comprehensive genotype-phenotype map of a eukaryotic complexome
Keywords-MotsClés: CELLULAR ROBUSTNESS AND CANCER; GENETICS; GENOMICS; GENOTYPE-PHENOTYPE MAP; PROTEIN COMPLEX; PROTEIN DEGRADATION; PROTEIN REGULATION; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; SYSTEMS BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: The development of personalized medicine requires being able to predict which mutations will or will not affect a phenotype of interest and to understand how these effects take place. We can address this challenge by studying model organisms and measuring what the effects of a large number of mutations are and learning from them what are the mechanisms by which mutations affect the function of the cell. We are developing tools that allow dissecting cellular networks by systematically perturbing them at the genetic level in order to understand the molecular bases of their robustness and sensitivity to mutations.  Our approach combines the use of large-scale genetics to introduce mutations into protein interaction networks and the use of systems biology to measure how these mutations affect the network at the structural level. Our approach will allow to better understand how and why some mutations are tolerated by the cell while others are not and lead to diseases such as cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanism of the retinoblastoma/DRM complex in gene regulation.
Keywords-MotsClés: C. ELEGANS; CHROMATIN IMMUNOPRECIPITATION; CHROMATIN REGULATION; EPIGENETICS; GENE EXPRESSION PROFILING; HISTONE MODIFICATION; MICROARRAY; MODEL ORGANISM; TRANSGENE EXPRESSION
Abstract-Résumé: Understanding how genes are regulated is essential for designing therapeutic approaches to many diseases, including cancer. A major control point for gene regulation is transcription, which takes place in the context of chromatin (DNA packaged with proteins).  Chromatin regulators control gene expression by altering chromatin structure.  A chromatin protein of particular interest is the retinoblastoma (Rb) tumor suppressor protein, which functions in a complex called DRM. The Rb pathway is mutated in most human cancers, but its mechanism is not well-understood. My aim is to use C. elegans as a model to better understand the mechanism of Rb/DRM. Chromatin alterations mediated by Rb/DRM, DNA sequence requirements for its function, and how it co-operates with another complex called TIP60 will be investigated. Since Rb is evolutionarily conserved, this work will be highly relevant for understanding Rb/DRM function and developing therapies to treat human disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Genetic and functional analysis of a mouse model of pediatric obesity
Keywords-MotsClés: MOLECULAR GENETICS; OBESITY; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Problems with the control of food intake are thought to contribute to the growing obesity epidemic in Canada and worldwide. The brain monitors and regulates how we acquire, store, and use energy from food. The brain gets signals from nerves that connect the brain to the intestines. Information also comes from substances in the bloodstream, made by organs such as the pancreas, the liver, and especially fat tissue. The hypothalamus, a small and ancient part of the brain, controls both food intake and energy output depending on these signals. We discovered a gene, called Magel2, which is most active in the hypothalamus. We made mice that are missing Magel2. These mice are less active and have more fat and less muscle compared to mice that have a normal Magel2 gene. The Magel2 protein is not made in people with a genetic disorder called Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS). People with PWS continue to eat even when their stomachs are full, and they usually become very obese. In this project, we will find out why the hypothalamus in the mice without Magel2 does not properly respond to energy cues. By researching how Magel2 works in the brain to prevent excessive appetite and weight gain, we will further understand how the brain normally controls short-term food intake and long term body weight.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Amino Acid Decarboxylases in the Bacterial Acid Stress Response: A structural and biochemical study
Keywords-MotsClés: ACID STRESS; ALARMONE; ATP-DEPENDENT PROTEASES; BACTERIAL URINARY TRACT INFECTION; LYSINE/CADAVERINE; MOLECULAR CHAPERONES; PROTEIN DENATURATION; RAVA; THE INDUCIBLE LYSINE DECARBOXYLASE; UROPATHOGENIC E. COLI
Abstract-Résumé: Seemingly small and vulnerable, bacteria possess an extraordinarily complicated set of stress response mechanisms that give them the ability and resilience to survive, or even thrive, in harsh conditions. Acid resistance in pathogenic bacteria is one important example of such an adaptation. These bacteria can colonize the intestines of their host organism, including humans, and cause infection. In the process, they inevitably have to pass through the gastric acid in the stomach, which serves as a natural antibiotic barrier. Bacteria that colonize the urinary tract also face acid stress where the pH ranges from 4.5 to 8. Yet, these organisms have systems that allow them to survive in these hostile acidic conditions. Therefore, understanding the complex regulatory mechanisms and pathways of the bacterial acid stress response is crucial to developing strategies for controlling bacterial infection. Our studies will concentrate on Escherichia coli, which is one of the most frequent causes of many common bacterial infections. Specifically, we aim to characterize the role of enzymes that are used by Escherichia coli to combat acid stress. These studies should help us better devise strategies to treat microbial infections by targeting the acid stress response pathway in these bacteria.

TitreApplicationTitle: Optimizing Signaling, Cells, and Host Environment in Matrix-based Cardiac Regenerative Therapy: Towards Pre-clinical Application
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL-BASED ANGIOGENESIS; CIRCULATING ANGIOGENIC CELLS; CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE; ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION; INTEGRIN-LINKED COMPLEXES
Abstract-Résumé: Coronary artery disease is the most important killer of Canadians. Therapies to regenerate the heart and blood vessels by using the patient's own adult stem cells have so far mostly failed in humans, despite success in animal models. Extensive work from the applicants suggest that this may due to the tissues of humans being more aged and diseased, yet how this ultimately affects organ recovery remains unverified with respect to cell therapy. In this research, we will explore, in small and large experimental models of coronary artery disease such as mice and pigs, whether this assertion is true, and thoroughly examine how this occurs and can be circumvented. We will investigate the use of tissue engineered materials to improve the condition of the host tissue, and to deliver and enhance the retention of transplanted cells in the diseased tissue. We anticipate that by improving the regenerating environment and the number and function of transplanted cells, our novel tissue engineering strategies will eventually make humans more responsive to stem cell therapies. Indeed, in current scenario our proposal is an important bench-to-bedside endeavor to make this very promising form of treatment towards preclinical relevance, while ensuring its safety.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigation of functional switch to regulatory Natural Killer cells during infection
Keywords-MotsClés: CELLULAR IMMUNOLOGY; CYTOKINE; IMMUNE REGULATION; INNATE IMMUNITY; MOLECULAR GENETICS; MOUSE MODEL; NATURAL KILLER CELL; NK RECEPTOR; VIRAL IMMUNITY; VIRUS INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Natural killer cells (NK cells) are a type of lymphocyte (white blood cell) and a component of our innate immune system. NK cell dysfunction results in increased sensitivity to viral infection, suggesting that NK cells are necessary to elicit an optimal immune response to viral infection. Although the immune responses evoked during viral infection are critical for combating infection, they often cause collateral damage to the host when not appropriately controlled. As such, NK cells, in addition to their anti-microbial role against virus infections, can regulate the immune response by releasing anti-inflammatory molecules. The current project is focused on characterizing novel NK cell regulatory functions during sustained viral infection. NK cells are at the forefront of immunology, and the results of this investigation will help us to modulate excessive immune reactions, thereby providing new insights for therapeutic intervention during chronic infections.

TitreApplicationTitle: Determinants of health among young people in Canada: the role of health promoting families
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENTS; CHILDREN; DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; EPIDEMIOLOGY; FAMILY; HOLISTIC INDICATORS OF HEALTH; PROSOCIAL BEHAVIOUR; QUALITATIVE METHODS; QUANTITATIVE METHODS; RISK-TAKING BEHAVIOUR
Abstract-Résumé: Characteristics of families are among the most important determinants of health in populations of young people.  Some basic family-related factors (e.g., how often families eat meals together, whether there is positive adult-child communication, and how families are organized) relate strongly to many important child health outcomes.  Using a novel, holistic approach to child health, we wish to examine how such family factors potentially influence composite health outcomes, which include physical, social, emotional and spiritual factors.  The study will, efficiently, involve in-depth quantitative analyses of existing health survey data collected as part of the Health Behaviour in School-Aged Children Study.  It will also involve complimentary qualitative analyses of the experiences and perceptions of groups of young adolescents from across Canada.  Knowledge translation will be an important element throughout each phase of this study.  Knowledge products will include traditional scientific manuscripts, as well as a series of lay resources containing accessible and practical ideas to assist Canadian families (in all their rich diversity) in creating home environments that are optimal to nurturing a holistic experience of health in children and adolescents.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development and Validation of Clinical Prediction Rules for Bleeding for Patients on Anticoagulation Therapy for Venous Thromboembolism
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTICOAGULATION; BLEEDING; BLOOD; COAGULATION FACTORS; EPIDEMIOLOGY; VENOUS THROMBOSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Blood thinners prevent the formation of new clots in patients who have developed deep vein blood clots or clots that have traveled to the lungs. However, major bleeding associated with their use is a problem, as it will cause death in 12% of cases. Some patients need to be treated with blood thinners longer than 3 months and doctors must decide if they are candidates to continue treatment. This decision depend on balancing the chances between having a major bleed and developing a new clot. So, it is critical to know which patients are more likely to develop major bleeding events with long term blood thinners. This will enable proper treatment decisions. Currently, doctors are unable to predict the chances of bleeding with blood thinners. Some of the rules that have been developed are not well validated and not precise. We have initiated a study to develop a new rule that will determine the chances of bleeding in patients taking blood thinners longer than 3 months. Also, we are planning to determine if the previous rules are useful and precise. Our study will also include the study of inherited factors that may increase the chances of bleeding. The study is partially done but funding has been exhausted. To complete the study we need to enrol 600 more patients and complete 2 further years of observation to develop this rule and therefore supplementary funding is necessary. The development of a well validated and precise rule of bleeding could be useful to the 600,000 Canadians that receive blood thinners on an annual basis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluating the effectiveness of organized breast assessment among women screened in the Ontario Breast Screening Program
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST ASSESSMENT CENTRE; BREAST CANCER; BREAST SCREENING; PROGNOSTIC FEATURES; SURVIVAL; TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: To ensure the benefits of having a screening mammogram (breast x-ray), women with an abnormal test must have a timely diagnosis. Long delays between an abnormal mammogram can lead to increased patient stress and poor outcomes. A number of follow-up diagnostic tests such as an additional mammogram, ultrasound or biopsy are required after an abnormal screening mammogram to confirm whether breast cancer is present. The Ontario Breast Screening Program (OBSP) has offered coordinated diagnostic services at its Hamilton screening centre since 1991 and the OBSP began to offer this to women screened in other regions through established Breast Assessment Centres (BAC) in 1998. Dr. Chiarelli's team is planning to collect data from a large group of women 50 to 69 years of age who were screened at the OBSP between 2001 and 2010 and diagnosed with breast cancer. One group will have had further diagnostic tests after an abnormal mammogram through a BAC and the other group outside a BAC. This study will evaluate whether women diagnosed in a BAC that coordinates follow-up tests after an abnormal mammogram have shorter wait times to diagnosis and treatment and are less likely to have a subsequent breast cancer diagnosis and live longer. The results of our study should provide useful data to identify which women are most at risk for delays in diagnosis and treatment and would benefit from having coordinated diagnostic tests. This study has the potential to provide evidence that will make a difference in the survival of women with breast cancer in Canada and could change practice and ensure appropriate directing of resources. Given breast cancer is the leading cancer for women, any improvement in survival for those managed through BACs would be very significant.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms mediating adverse outcomes in Placental Malaria
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVERSE PREGNANCY OUTCOMES; C5A; COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION; LOW BIRTH WEIGHT; MALARIA; PLACENTAL MALARIA; PRETERM BIRTH; STILLBIRTH
Abstract-Résumé: Pregnant women are at great risk of malaria infection that can have life-threatening consequences for both mother and infant. There is an incomplete understanding of the pathways mediating poor birth outcomes in malaria during pregnancy. Our lab has shown that malaria is associated with dysregulated development of the placental vasculature and generated novel evidence of its association with excessive activation of the complement system. With this project we propose to examine the mechanisms and causality of the implicated pathways in a model of malaria in pregnancy and the possible application of therapies already available for other conditions. This will be translated into potential new predictors of women at risk and new targets for intervention that are safe to use in pregnant women.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessing Time-Varying Drug Exposures in the Canadian Co-infection Cohort: Methodological Tools to Address Missing Data and Measurement Error
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOSTATISTICS; CAUSAL INFERENCE; EPIDEMIOLOGY; HEPATITIS C; HIV; METHODOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Epidemiologic studies typically aim to estimate the true (causal) effect of an exposure such as medication or treatment on outcome, and cohort studies are often seen as an ideal way to investigate a range of outcomes - particularly time-to-event outcomes - due to the prospective nature of the follow-up. However, methodological challenges can arise in cohort studies where participants are recruited after disease onset, and so participants may have been exposed to risk factors of interest prior to cohort entry. It is also sometimes the case that affected individuals who experience an outcome of interest such as death may not survive long enough to enter the cohort, and that the time of cohort entry is not a clinically meaningful time origin. Furthermore, it is often the case that exposures of interest are not randomized, but rather their receipt is controlled by cohort participants and therefore the exposure level may be confounded by participant characteristics such as general level of health, socioeconomic status, and lifestyle or behavioural choices. Hence estimates from analyses of the response modeled as a function of received treatment based on the observed data only are often prone to bias.   Our projects are aimed at developing new methodological tools that will simultaneously address the three challenges noted above, thereby eliminating bias due to (i) cohort entry after both disease onset and after receipt of the exposure of interest, (ii) the non-random nature of the exposure, and (iii) measurement error so as to study questions of treatment and behavioural risk factors in an HIV-Hepatitis C co-infected population. In particular, we will investigate the effects of anti-retroviral treatment interruptions, illegal drug use, and alcohol consumption on liver fibrosis and end-stage liver disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: Contested Intervention: The History of MMR Immunization in Canada, 1963-2013
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; ALTERNATIVE MEDICINE; COMMUNICATION; EPIDEMICS; HEALTH POLICY; HEALTH SERVICES; HISTORY OF MEDICINE; IMMIGRATION; IMMUNIZATION; MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: At the 10th Canadian Immunization Conference in Vancouver in December 2012, delegates and keynote speakers highlighted childhood immunization against diseases such as measles, mumps and rubella as one of the most important preventive measures that have contributed nationally and internationally to human health. But they noted that immunization rates are declining and that parents are voicing their concerns about the number of vaccines their infants are receiving. The purpose of this research is to examine the discourses and rhetoric which mainstream and alternative health professionals and the public in Ontario and Quebec use regarding childhood vaccination and to determine which changing social, economic and political factors have influenced support, resistance or hesitancy about individual and mass immunization. Drawing on a wide array of documentary sources including new media such as the internet, blogs and tweets, this project will provide policy makers and front line health care personnel with new ways to discuss immunization with concerned parents.

TitreApplicationTitle: Analyzing temporal and geographical variations in computed tomography (CT) supply, demand and utilization in Saskatchewan to identify opportunities to improve efficiency and access
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION; RESOURCE UTILIZATION; RURAL ACCESS
Abstract-Résumé: Computed tomography (CT) is a medical imaging modality that helps diagnose many conditions by producing images of soft tissue and bone. Demand for CT exams is increasing in Canada. Due to lengthy wait times, it was a wait time reduction priority area for the First Ministers in 2004. Furthermore, CT facilities have high costs and require highly skilled technologists. In Saskatchewan, waiting times for imaging vary across the province - from 43 days to 2 days in Saskatoon and Lloydminster respectively at the 90th percentile for moderately acute CT patients. Therefore, it is important to lower the cost per CT exam, decrease wait times, and balance the demand on each CT facility. This research will evaluate variations in CT imaging utilization in Saskatchewan and provide recommendations for improvement. The analysis will evaluate three aspects: the current situation for CT utilization,  focus on accessibility in rural and remote populations, and recommend strategies to improve CT efficiency and access. Data will be obtained from Statistics Canada, Regional Health Authorities, CT clinics, and Ministry of Health in Saskatchewan.  Baseline statistics will be calculated for CT resource utilization rates, wait times and report turnaround times, and patient travel patterns. Statistical modeling will compare different patient populations and geographic regions. To reduce travel times, improvement opportunities will be modeled to find the best CT facility locations for access equity, new locations, and long term planning. The goal is to aid decision makers in creating effective policies in the placement of CT facilities to increase access to rural and remote populations and balance demand across different facilities. More efficient use of existing resources reduces the cost per CT exam and can delay the need for additional facilities. The modeling in this research can also be extended to the location planning of other health care facilities and resources.

TitreApplicationTitle: Defining the Molecular Basis of Invariant Natural Killer T Cell Autoreactivity In Vitro and In Vivo
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTO-REACTIVE; AUTOIMMUNITY; AVIDITY; CD1D; CDR3; INKT CELL; MOUSE; TCR; THYMIC SELECTION
Abstract-Résumé: We would like to study immune cells that cause autoimmunity.  Autoimmunity is a condition where immune cells are attacking the body's healthy cells. Unfortunately, autoimmunity can lead to serious medical conditions such as multiple sclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and type 1 diabetes. Normally, the body has mechanisms to prevent the production of these harmful cells and to suppress these self-damaging immune cells even if they are produced.  In healthy individuals, a type of white blood cell, known as the "invariant Natural Killer T" (iNKT) cell, has an important role in the immune system. An organ called the thymus filters out harmful iNKT cells that have the ability to attack healthy cells. Beneficial iNKT cells, which only attack tissues infected with pathogens or cancer cells, are allowed to pass through the thymus and enter the blood stream. Therefore, the thymus is important in selecting beneficial iNKT cells.  We would like to know more about the role of iNKT cells in autoimmunity. To do so, we need to compare both beneficial and harmful iNKT cells. We can collect beneficial iNKT cells from the blood. But we need to artificially produce harmful iNKT cells, since they are removed and cannot be found in blood. Our group has already succeeded in artificially producing harmful human iNKT cells in the laboratory.    In this proposal, we will extend the study into mice by artificially producing harmful mouse iNKT cells. It is important to perform the experiments in mice because we must observe the roles of these harmful cells in a living organism. With this proposed project, we will be able to uncover critical information on how iNKT cells cause autoimmunity and establish directions for developing new treatments for autoimmune diseases.
