TitreApplicationTitle: Mass spectrometry proteomic analysis of PTPN12 to elucidate its phosphatase role in tumor suppression and cell signalling
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL LINES AND TUMORIGENICITY ASSAY; MASS SPECTROMETRY PROTEOMICS; TISSUE CULTURE; TRIPLE NEGATIVE BREAST CANCER
Abstract-Résumé: PTPN12 is a phosphatase protein can cause cells to become tumorigenic when it is not working properly. It is found to be defective in patients with triple negative breast cancer, a type of breast cancer disease that is not easily identified by specific biomarkers and affects 20% of breast cancer patients. In addition, this particular breast cancer is highly aggressive and resistant to treatment. Better understanding of PTPN12 and its function in cellular biology will allow elucidation on how normal cells become cancerous. This project will focus primarily on triple negative breast cancer but the information gleaned from the research could very well apply to other cancers as well. One method to determine how PTPN12 functions in cellular biology is to see what other proteins it affects and interacts with. To do this, we apply a new technique called BioID that fused our protein of interest with a biotin ligase. This protein essentially allows neighbouring proteins of PTPN12 to be covalently linked with a biotin molecule. This physical linkage allows the proteins, which are those that interact with PTPN12, to be isolated and from the cell using streptavidin, which binds to biotin molecules with extremely high affinity. The purified proteins are then subjected to mass spectrometry analysis to identify them. This method allows the discovery of new, unknown proteins that were not reported to interact with PTPN12. Early results show that this method identifies known protein interactors from an established purification method that the Gingras developed and identified new ones as well. These new proteins will be experimented on to determine their roles in tumor suppression and metastasis.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of PGC-1a Signaling in Retinal Astrocytes
Keywords-MotsClés: ASTROCYTES; CELL CULTURE; GLAUCOMA; OXIDATIVE AND METABOLIC STRESS; RETINAL DEGENERATION; SIRNA KNOCKDOWN; TRANSFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Glaucoma is the second leading cause of blindness worldwide. It is caused by the death of neurons in the eye called retinal ganglion cells. There is no cure for this disease at the present and because there are many contributing risk factors, the effect of available treatments is inconsistent. I will examine cells called astrocytes that support the retinal ganglion cells in metabolism and structure. Specifically, I will focus on a molecule in astrocytes called PGC-1a, which has been shown to confer protection for neurons. I will determine whether changing its activity in astrocytes will improve cell survival. If the role of PGC-1a can be established, it can potentially become a therapeutic target for the treatment of glaucoma.

TitreApplicationTitle: Use of double negative regulatory T cell to induce tolerogenic dendritic cells and CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells to develop donor-specific transplantation tolerance.
Keywords-MotsClés: COSTIMULATORY MOLECULE; DENDRITIC CELL; ELISA; FLOW CYTOMETRY; MIXED LYMPHOCYTE REACTION; REGULATORY T CELL; TOLERANCE INDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Transplantation can save lives of people suffering from end-stage organ failure.  Current therapy involves injection of immunosuppressive drugs to transplant recipients to prevent destruction of donated organs by recipients' immune system through a process called graft-rejection.  However, immunosuppressive drugs make patients become susceptible to microbial infection and cancer development.  To improve the lives of transplant patients while preventing graft-rejection, tolerance induction is an active area of research.  Tolerance is a safety system built-in immune system of healthy individuals to prevent unwanted immune reaction against specific antigens, such as self-antigens.  There are different regulatory cell types involved in tolerance induction, such as Foxp3+ T regulatory cell and tolerogenic dendritic cell and double-negative T cell (DN T cell).  In animal model, DN T cell, Foxp3+ T regulatory cells, and tolerogenic dendritic cells, develop long-term tolerance against donor graft, in absence of any immunosuppressive drugs given.  Injection of DN T cell into graft-recipient mice increases Foxp3+ T regulatory cell number and induces long-term graft tolerance.  However, the exact relationship between Foxp3+ T regulatory cell and DN T cell remains elusive.  Treating mature dendritic cells with DN T cell downregulated expression of costimulatory molecules, which is a characteristic of tolerogenic dendritic cells.  However, the identity of DN T cell treated dendritic cell has not been investigated.  The goal of this project is to characterize DN T cell treated dendritic cells and to determine whether the latter is responsible for DN T cell mediated induction of Foxp3+ T regulatory cells.  Findings from this project lead to a therapy that involves different regulatory cell types that work in synergistic manner to induce tolerance against donated organ more effectively.

TitreApplicationTitle: Comparing the nutritional content of foods and beverages marketed to children and adults, respectively in Canada.
Keywords-MotsClés: FOOD AND BEVERAGE MARKETING TO CHILDREN; MEASURING PARENTAL ATTITUDES TOWARD MARKETING TO CHILDREN; NUTRITIONAL CONTENT OF CHILDREN'S FOODS
Abstract-Résumé: Childhood obesity is growing quickly in Canada, leading to serious health issues like heart disease and type II diabetes, and high costs to the Canadian healthcare system. There is a common belief that foods and drinks marketed to children are less healthy than similar adult foods. Food marketing affects children's food choices and requests for food to their parents, leading Canadian nutrition experts to suggest the government should ban the marketing of unhealthy foods to children. However, in Canada, there has never been a detailed look into how healthy children's foods actually are. I believe that foods directed at children are less healthy than similar products for adults, and that the marketing of children's products affects what parents buy for their children. To determine if children's foods are less healthy than similar adult products, I will classify all of the products in a database of Canadian food packages as being marketed to either children or adults, and compare their characteristics, including the number of calories, and amounts of fat, sugar, salt, and other nutrients to see if there are differences between products for children and adults. I will also play a major role in updating this food label database with new products in 2013, and examine patterns in food marketing to children over time.  Finally, to see how food marketing to children influences parents' purchase patterns, I will conduct a survey on parents' attitudes about food marketing to children and their food purchasing habits. By looking at how healthy children's foods are and how parents are influenced by food marketing to children, my research will provide data to help develop Canadian policies to promote healthy weights for children. Looking at patterns over time in children's foods will show whether a ban on the marketing unhealthy foods to children would be an appropriate strategy to prevent childhood obesity in Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms Underlying Noonan Syndrome Cardiac Defects with RAF1 Mutations
Keywords-MotsClés: DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Noonan Syndrome (NS) is a common developmental disorder that affects about one in every 1000 to 2500 children, with symptoms such as cardiac defects, facial dysmorphia and short stature. It is linked to defects in different components of the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway, due to overactivation of proteins regulating growth and development. Notably, not all NS mutations are associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), which is a leading cause of sudden death in young people. Approximately 3%-5% patients carry germline (inherited) mutations in the RAF1 gene, which encodes a kinase protein that participates in signal transduction via phosphorylation. Unlike many other NS mutations, patients with RAF1 mutations that confer increased kinase activity are highly (~95%) likely to develop HCM, similarly as observed in mouse models. Thus, RAF1 mutants present a great opportunity to elucidate the cellular and molecular basis underlying NS cardiac defects and its role in the pathogenesis of HCM. My research is aimed (1) to determine the cell type(s) in which RAF1 mutants act to promote NS cardiac phenotypes in transgenic mouse models; and (2) to identify actionable downstream targets for the development of therapy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Health Communication Strategies for Social Change
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL HEALTH; HISTORICAL ANALYSIS; MENTAL HEALTH; OUTCOME EVALUATION; PROGRAM EVALUATION; QUALITATIVE RESEARCH; SURVEYS AND INTERVIEWS; TRAUMA
Abstract-Résumé: The Canadian Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC), established June 1, 2008 with a five-year mandate, allows Indian Residential School survivors the opportunity to testify about their experiences in Residential Schools as a means to heal from trauma. The Canadian TRC exposes several questions, which have yet to be explored in the context of previous TRCs internationally. There is a great need to investigate whether individuals find the TRC an effective means of personal healing from the trauma associated with Indian Residential Schools and whether participation in this program improves mental health outcomes on a population level for residential school survivors. As part of my Masters of Public Health, I propose to undertake an outcomes evaluation study that utilizes qualitative techniques. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with IRS survivors who testified at the TRC National Events to gauge the self-reported level of healing as a result of testifying and whether the participants experienced any unanticipated adverse psychological impacts.  A control group of IRS survivors who did not participate in the TRC will be used to validate the results. I hypothesize that while testimony sharing is a valuable endeavor to improve mental health and personal healing, the process is associated with significant psychological risks that should be addressed by providing better support for those who testify. By determining the effectiveness of this national program, I hope to provide the first evidence in Canada of whether the TRC model of testimony sharing is a successful population-level public health approach to improving mental health of populations who have undergone mass trauma.

TitreApplicationTitle: A comparison of practice patterns and outcomes of pediatric trauma managed at adult versus pediatric trauma centers: a multi-center comparison and analysis
Keywords-MotsClés: PEDIATRIC TRAUMA; QUALITY OF CARE INDICATORS; QUALITY OF CARE RESEARCH; RETROSPECTIVE COHORT ANALYSIS; TRAUMA REGISTRY
Abstract-Résumé: Pediatric trauma is the leading cause of death in North America. Children are triaged to either pediatric or adult trauma centers depending on many factors, including severity of injury and proximity to nearest center. Despite national guidelines, significant differences in the way in which injured children are treated exist, depending on whether they are treated at adult versus pediatric designated trauma centers. An understanding of these differences is crucial toward quality of care improvement. For instance, injuries to the spleen provide one relevant example of significant variation in care between adult and pediatric trauma centers. Most children with traumatic splenic injury are treated without an operation, as this is the standard of care. However, higher operative rates and death have been shown in children treated at adult versus pediatric trauma centers, suggesting there is lack of pediatric expertise and education in adult centers. These are important differences to examine, as related outcomes and healthcare costs are significant.  Using the American College of Surgery trauma registry, which collects data from numerous trauma centers across the United States and Canada, we plan to look at patterns of care amongst injured children and see if these patterns differ between adult and pediatric centers. We also plan to look at outcomes such a death to better understand which centers are performing well and what best practices are.  By examining these patterns of care and any differences, we can determine where quality of care initiatives need to be aimed. This would improve outcomes and reduce related overutilization of resources, ensuring that the population is better cared for and healthcare costs are reduced. In addition, the American College of Surgeons is the body that creates policy for trauma care across the United States; hence we will be in a unique postion to truly effect change in the United States and Canada.

Abstract-Résumé: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a highly aggressive cancer that affects young children. There is no cure or effective treatment for JMML, which has an average survival rate of less than 20% past three years of diagnosis. A hallmark feature that defines and underlies JMML is the inordinately increased ability of leukemic cells to grow in the presence of granulocyte macrophage-colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF), a substance produced by cells to promote cell proliferation, via an unknown mechanism.  This proposal aims to provide insightful mechanistic understanding of how GM-CSF causes this increased growth potential of leukemic cells that is responsible for the pathogenesis of JMML.  Ultimately, I hope that the findings in this research endeavor will contribute towards the development of better cancer therapeutics for the management of children with JMML.

TitreApplicationTitle: Maximizing the Efficacy of Antimicrobial Agents through Conjugation with a Peptide Based Delivery System
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIBIOTICS; BACTERIA; BACTERIAL RESISTANCE; CELLULAR COMPARTMENTALIZATION; DRUG CONJUGATES; DRUG DEVELOPMENT; MITOCHONDRIAL PENETRATING PEPTIDES; TRIMETHOPRIM
Abstract-Résumé: The development of new drugs and antibiotics is a long and expensive process, traditionally involving the synthesis of number of assorted chemical compounds followed by large arrays of biological tests.  This process is economically inefficient and can often take hundreds of millions of dollars and decades of time, making the development of new antibiotics an arduous process.  In light of the recent rise of multiple drug resistant bacterial strains, it is clear that pharmaceutical development of antibacterial agents must become more efficient in order to effectively defend against new and stronger infectious agents.  Here, we describe the synthesis of a chemical tag which can be used to aid the development of new antibiotics. This chemical tag has the unique property of directing the attached drugs more efficiently into bacteria while simultaneously preventing toxicity against human cells by trapping the compound in compartments within the cell unaffected by the drug. Our research has the potential to rapidly generate a number of new pharmaceutical agents by increasing the pharmaceutical potential of drugs which were previously found to be just under the cutoff of clinical effectiveness.  In addition, continued use of our tag to boost future drugs which nearly meet pharmaceutical standards promises to increase the proportion new drugs which can make it market, an important consideration in the increasingly regulated and stringent drug market.

Keywords-MotsClés: BEHAVIOURAL PHARMACOLOGY; EPIGENETICS; G9A/GLP; MOUSE BEHAVIOURAL TESTING; PRECLINICAL TESTING
Abstract-Résumé: Psychiatric disorders are characterized by symptoms such as depression (a state of low mood)and psychosis (a loss of contact with reality). Current medications have numerous side-effects and are not effective in treating a large number of patients. Thus there is a great need for new and better treatments for these symptoms. Possible targets for new drugs include molecules that surround the DNA strand and affect gene expression (the way DNA exerts its effect on the cellular and organismal levels). These molecules are part of what is called the epigenome, and the study of these molecules is called epigenetics. We wish to test the efficacy of a new class of drugs, epigenetic drugs on their ability to reduce depression and psychosis in rodent models. If these new drugs are effective in correcting behavioual abnormalities in these rodent models, they have a much higher chance of also being effective as drugs for treating related symptoms in humans. These experiments are just a first step in the drug development process, and will require more experiments and investigations before clinical trials in humans can be performed. It is hoped that these experiments will help in the development of a new therapeutic agent(s) for the treatment of diseases such as depression and schizophrenia.

TitreApplicationTitle: Determining the Effect of Fructose on Glycemic Control and Insulin Sensitivity in Humans Using Meta-Analytical Tools
Keywords-MotsClés: DIABETES; FRUCTOSE; META-ANALYSIS; OBESITY
Abstract-Résumé: Diabetes associations have taken a harm-reduction approach to fructose recommendations discouraging the consumption of high intakes of dietary fructose, a simple sugar found naturally in fruits and vegetables and as a sweetener in processed foods. Their concerns relate to fructose's putative ability to elevate blood fats and cholesterol, known to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. However, the American Diabetes Association has also acknowledged that fructose has been found to improve blood glucose control in clinical trials of people with type-2 diabetes - the only organization to do so. In a previous systematic review and meta-analysis of relevant trials, we found that fructose exchange for another carbohydrate led to clinically significant improvements in blood glucose control in individuals with diabetes. No previous meta-analysis has been conducted to determine fructose's effect in healthy individuals. To improve the evidence on which nutrition recommendations for dietary fructose are based, I propose to expand our analysis to investigate the effect of fructose on glycemic control and insulin sensitivity in healthy individuals. I will be undertaking a systematic synthesis of data taken from all available clinical studies in humans and pooling it together in order to explore differences of different forms, doses and durations of exposure to dietary fructose. The findings generated from my project will help improve the health of consumers through informing recommendations for the general public and will improve evidence-based guidelines on which clinical decisions are made.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effect of Nuts on Cancer and Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors in Type 2 Diabetes
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; NUTRITION; OXIDATIVE STRESS; TREE NUTS; TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS
Abstract-Résumé: The number of people with diabetes is expected to double in the next 20 years.  With diabetes comes the fear of its related health problems. People with type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at more than twice the risk of heart disease and many cancers than people without diabetes.  Heart disease and cancer are two major causes of disease and death in the world.  Each year, over 1 million Canadians are affected by heart disease, costing the healthcare system over $20 billion.  Similarly, cancer costs over $17 billion yearly. Prostate and breast cancer kill over 4,000 men and 5,000 women, respectively. The World Health Organization suggests diet is a key factor in the prevention of both heart disease and cancer. Yet, there is little advice on the best foods to eat to reduce the risk of these diseases in people with T2D. Despite reported health benefits of nuts, people continue to worry that eating nuts will lead to weight gain due to their high fat content. However, nuts contain healthy fats along with other nutrients that may be good for your health. In our study, over 100 participants ate one of 3 diets for 12 weeks. These 3 diets were equal in calories and included: full-dose nuts, half-dose nuts, or a healthy muffin. Body weight and food intake were measured throughout the study.  Participants gave blood samples before and after eating the diet for 12 weeks.  These samples will be used to test prostate and breast cancer cell growth and amount of oxidative stress. Oxidative stress is damage to body cells that can lead to disease, such as heart disease. These tests will assess the effect of nuts on cancer and heart disease risk. Use of specific, yet simple, dietary advice, such as eating nuts, can have a large local and global impact on the prevention of these diseases.  We believe results from this study will provide health professionals with evidence to inform advice given to people with T2D with regard to nut intake to help reduce their cancer and heart disease risk.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identifying novel genetic variants in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder using whole exome sequencing
Keywords-MotsClés: EXTENDED PEDIGREES; LINKAGE MAPPING; OBSESSIVE-COMPULSIVE DISORDER; SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE POLYMORPHISM; WHOLE EXOME SEQUENCING
Abstract-Résumé: Obsessive-compulsive disorder is an anxiety disorder in which people have unwanted and repeated thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviours (compulsions). OCD is common (1 to 3% of people will develop it in their lifetime, disabling (among the ten most disabling medical conditions worldwide), and starts early in life (most often before the age of 18). Evidence from family and twin studies, has pointed to a large genetic contribution to the disorder, especially when symptoms begin in childhood. We hope to find genetic variants associated with OCD by studying families with many affected individuals, where a genetic cause is most likely implicated. By sequencing the DNA of distantly related family members with OCD we will increase our chances of finding genetic changes that are important in causing OCD. Since we expect related individuals to share many genetic changes, we will "filter" our data in order to identify those shared changes that are most likely to be relevant to OCD. For example, we will focus on chromosomal regions that are "linked" to the disorder in the family, and target changes expected to damage proteins. Genes that we identify as being altered in affected family members will then be screened in a much larger population of OCD cases in order to identify more people affected by same the genetic variation. Identification of genetic variants will lead to the identification of biological pathways leading to disease. Ultimately, analyzing DNA sequence variation will allow us to study which patients are genetically most likely to respond to existing treatments, and will lead to the identification of new targets for drug development. This will not only be an important contribution to the current body of knowledge in OCD and genetics, but will also be of significance for the families affected by these genetic variants.

TitreApplicationTitle: Use and effect of anesthesia provider performance feedback via integrated hospital data systems on learning and quality improvement: a comparative case series
Keywords-MotsClés: ANESTHESIOLOGY; COMPARATIVE CASE STUDY; ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS; PATIENT SAFETY; PERFORMANCE FEEDBACK; PERIOPERATIVE MEDICINE; QUALITATIVE STUDY; QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: With the increased use and availability of electronic health records, information on patient care and health outcomes is collected and stored on an ongoing basis.  This data, with all identifying information removed, can be analyzed to provide useful insights into health care quality.  It can help to define best practices and identify deficiencies and can be used as the basis for health care quality improvement projects.  This comparative case study will look at groups of anesthesiologists that have embraced using real performance data as the basis of their quality improvement efforts.  The time of surgery is associated with risks for patients including death and a reduction in quality of life.  Improvements in this area have the potential to alleviate significant human suffering so it is important to understand how physicians use data to monitor their performance and create a culture of continuous improvement, learning and patient safety.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of the microbiota in enteric infectious diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: DIARRHEA; ENTERIC DISEASE; INFECTIOUS COLITIS; INFLAMMATION; METABOLOMICS; MICROBIOTA; PATHOGENIC E. COLI; SALMONELLA; TYPE III SECRETION; VIRULENCE
Abstract-Résumé: The intestinal (digestive) tract is filled with vast numbers of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses and other microbes.  Collectively, these microbes are called the 'intestinal microbiota'.  We have known about their presence for centuries, but we are only beginning to realize the large role they play in health and disease.  Our laboratory has developed animal infection models using pathogenic bacteria that can cause diseases in humans, including those that cause food poisoning (called Salmonella and pathogenic E. coli, such as E. coli O157). Importantly, we demonstrated that the intestinal microbiota can alter the outcome of a disease caused by these pathogens: i.e. whether one gets sick or not.  But determining how they impact on disease occurrence and outcomes is a key question, and this is the main focus of this application.  We have begun to identify small molecules, either made by the microbiota or by the intestine in response to their presence, that affect the molecular machinery the microbe needs to cause disease. We will further study these molecules and how they interact with pathogenic bacteria, and determine their role in animal infection models.   By understanding how the intestinal microbiota interact with Salmonella and pathogenic E. coli, we will ultimately be able to block these and other pathogenic microbes that cause much disease worldwide.

TitreApplicationTitle: Overcoming therapeutic resistance in lymphoma
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER GENETICS; LYMPHOMA; SEQUENCING; THERAPEUTIC RESISTANCE; TUMOUR MICRO-ENVIRONMENT
Abstract-Résumé: One in 30 Canadians develops lymphoma and only half of these patients will be cured by chemotherapy. Those who do not respond to therapy have few alternative options - new drugs are needed to treat these patients. We have discovered that mutations in a gene called FAS are present in 20% of patients whose lymphomas are resistant to chemotherapy. We show that mutations in FAS can cause resistance to chemotherapy in mice but not in cultured cells in dishes, leading us to believe that the immune system, present in mice but not in cultured cells, plays a role in killing lymphoma cells after exposure to chemotherapy.  The aims of this research are to confirm that FAS mutations cause resistance to chemo-therapy lymphoma backgrounds, to better understand the role of the immune response after chemotherapy, and to find novel ways to treat lymphomas carrying FAS mutations.   We will determine if FAS mutations cause resistance to conventional chemotherapy in a lymphoma mouse model allows for different genetic backgrounds that closely mimics aggressive human lymphomas. We will transplant mice with lymphomas with or without mutated FAS and test whether this mutation induces resistance to the conventional chemotherapy that is given to human patients with lymphoma.  We will further study mutated FAS looking at it in context of a healthy versus deficient immune systems and using these models to determine which components of the immune system are important for killing the FAS mutant lymphoma cells. Finally, we will find ways to kill lymphomas carrying FAS mutations. First, by identifying survival signals that keep them alive to be used as targets for future therapies, and second, by using our mouse model to test existing therapies to determine which drugs could be used to treat patients with FAS mutant lymphomas.  This research should lead to improved therapy for patients with aggressive FAS mutant lymphomas.

TitreApplicationTitle: A comparison of cognitive-behavioral couple therapy and lidocaine in the treatment of provoked vestibulodynia: A randomized clinical trial
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC PAIN; COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL THERAPY; COUPLE THERAPY; DYSPAREUNIA; RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL; SEXUAL FUNCTION; TOPICAL LIDOCAINE; TREATMENT OUTCOME; VULVODYNIA; WOMEN'S SEXUAL HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic pain problems involving the female reproductive system are major health concerns for all women. Poorly understood, they entail great personal and financial cost. One such condition is vulvodynia, or chronic unexplained vulvar pain, which has a prevalence of 16%. Despite its negative impact on psychosexual and relationship satisfaction, there is little research examining empirically-tested treatments for afflicted couples. The proposed research builds on findings from our work focusing on the impact of relational factors on vulvodynia, and our previous research evaluating the efficacy of group cognitive-behavioral therapy for this problem. This two-centre randomized clinical trial aims to assess the efficacy of a novel, 12-week targeted couple therapy (CBCT) for women with vulvodynia in comparison to one of the most commonly prescribed first-line medical interventions, topical lidocaine. Primary research question: Is there a significant difference between the two treatments on women's pain during intercourse post-treatment? Based on our previous work and existing literature, we hypothesize that CBCT will yield significantly greater pain reduction post-treatment than lidocaine. Secondary research questions will assess for significant differences between the two treatments post-treatment and at 6-month follow-up on multidimensional aspects of pain using the McGill Pain Questionnaire, women and partners' sexuality (sexual function and satisfaction), psychological adjustment (anxiety, depression, catastrophizing, self-efficacy, attributions, and quality of life), relationship factors (partner responses and dyadic adjustment), and self-reported improvement and treatment satisfaction. We hypothesize that CBCT will show significantly greater improvements on all outcome measures compared to lidocaine. Results of this study will improve the health and quality of life of patients with vulvodynia by rigorously testing the efficacy of a novel couples treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Reassessment of Anti-Platelet therapy using InDividualized Strategies - Modifying Acute CoroNary Syndrome Algorithms based on Genetic and Demographic Evaluation: The RAPID-MANAGE Pilot study
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTI-PLATELET THERAPY; CYP2C19; PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION; PERSONALIZED THERAPY; PHARMACOGENOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: In patients with heart attacks, the treatment of choice is to restore blood flow with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) (use of stents (metal meshes) to open blockages).  After PCI, the standard drug treatment includes aspirin and clopidogrel.  These medications block full function of the platelet cells, which are responsible for clotting.  Despite their use, patients after PCI are at risk for heart attacks, sudden clotting of stents or death.  A major contributor may be resistance to clopidogrel.  New more potent drugs, which can overcome the resistance, are now available; however, they come with an increase chance of severe bleeding and costs.  An ideal solution would be to identify at-risk patients and selectively treat them with more potent drugs, while lower-risk patients continue with clopidogrel.  This type of strategy (personalized strategy) would decrease heart attacks and death (compared to clopidogrel), while also preventing bleeding complications (compared to treating all patients with the new drugs).               Of resistant patients, many carry genes (inherited units) that prevent proper absorption of clopidogrel.   Our group has recently developed and tested a new bedside genetic test, which identifies carriers of at-risk genes.  However, this technique alone does not identify all at-risk patients.  Consequently, we have now devised a novel tool, which combines genetics with patient characteristics to identify high-risk patients.  The proposed study combines this new tool into a strategy for personalized treatment.  Patients with heart attacks who undergo PCI will be randomly assigned to 1 of 3 strategies: a) new personalized strategy, b) ticagrelor strategy (stronger approved drug) or c) clopidogrel strategy (previous standard drug).  The function of the platelet cells will be measured at 1 month to determine potential benefits.  Evaluation of this new personalized strategy is important for improving patient outcomes after PCI.

TitreApplicationTitle: Endothelial transdifferentiation
Keywords-MotsClés: CONDITIONAL GENE-TARGETED MOUSE MODELS; ENDOTHELIAL TRANSDIFFERENTIATION; HEART DEVELOPMENT; NOTCH; TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS
Abstract-Résumé: The cells that line the interior of the heart and blood vessels are called endothelial cells. These cells are necessary for the heart to form key structures that divide the heart into four chambers, such as the heart valves. Heart defects are the most common congenital anomaly seen in newborns, and heart valve surgery is the commonest type of heart surgery performed in the adult. A key process in the formation of the heart valves and the walls that divide the four chambers of the heart is the formation and differentiation of embryonic tissue (called cardiac cushion), which partitions the heart into atria and ventricles, and a left and a right side. During this process the endothelial cells that line the interior of the heart change into a different type of cell that support the heart valves. This process is called endothelial-to-mesenchymal transdifferentiation (EMT). At the same time during development of an embryo, a specialized subset of endothelial cells lining the large blood vessel exiting the heart called the aorta change into cells that eventually form the blood that circulates in our body. This process is called endothelial-to-hematopoietic (blood cell) transdifferentiation (EHT). This grant is designed to identify the gene networks that are responsible for transforming the same cell type into different types of cells. In particular, we are attempting to gain a deeper understanding of how heart valves develop. We hope that a better understanding of these processes will provide direction for genetic diagnosis, prevention, and potentially tissue engineering efforts to create artificial heart valves.

TitreApplicationTitle: Vulnerability and Health - Global and Local
Keywords-MotsClés: ETHICS; GLOBAL JUSTICE; HEALTH; SOCIAL JUSTICE; VULNERABILITY
Abstract-Résumé: Vulnerability is a concern of both medical and bio ethics and, increasingly, of public health ethics and a central concern of global justice.  However, the concept of vulnerability, what it is and why it is morally salient is under-theorized in moral and political philosophy. The motivation for this research is to employ a typology of morally problematic vulnerability and to assess it in specific health-related contexts of vulnerability.  For the purposes of this project, we propose to examine the domestic and international context of health and global inequalities by means of four case studies. The findings of this research will yield two results: first, our results can be used to highlight the heuristic value of the concept of vulnerability in social and global justice theories; second, they can be used by policy makers and other health practitioners when designing ways to address the challenges vulnerability poses in health contexts.

TitreApplicationTitle: Multi-Functional Polymer-Amplified Radioimmunotherapy of Trastuzumab (Herceptin)-Resistant Breast Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; EPIDERMAL GROWTH FACTOR RECEPTOR; HER2; INDIUM-111; INSULIN GROWTH FACTOR RECEPTOR-1; LUTETIUM-177; METAL-CHELATING POLYMERS; RADIOIMMUNOTHERAPY
Abstract-Résumé: This project aims to develop a new radiation treatment for breast cancer that is resistant to trastuzumab (Herceptin). The introduction of Herceptin for treatment of HER2-positive breast cancer has been a major advance. However, only 1 in 2 patients respond to this treatment and almost all patients who initially respond to Herceptin develop resistance within a year. In the proposed project, a team of scientists will combine their unique expertise to design new treatments for overcoming Herceptin-resistance. These treatments will be composed of antibodies that recognize proteins on breast cancer cells linked to polymers that incorporate multiple binding sites for radioisotopes that increase their potency for killing tumour cells. The polymers will also include a function that delivers the radiation directly to the nucleus or DNA of tumour cells to further increase their effectiveness. The radioisotopes to be used emit short range radiation that kills only single tumour cells thus minimizing normal tissue toxicity or longer range radiation that can kill many cells within a tumour. These new treatments will first be tested for killing breast cancer cells in culture, then their ability to localize in breast cancer tumours in mice will be examined. Finally, the treatments will be tested for their effectiveness and toxicity in mice with human breast cancer tumours that are resistant to Herceptin. Through a collaboration with a clinical trials group in Ontario, the team plans to advance these new treatments to patients with breast cancer in the future if the results of the research are promising.

TitreApplicationTitle: Epigenetic regulation of bladder response to obstruction
Keywords-MotsClés: BLADDER; DNA METHYLATION; EPIGENETICS; MECHANOTRANSDUCTION; PCR ARRAY; PYROSEQUENCING; SIGNALLING; SMOOTH MUSCLE; UROLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: The urinary bladder is prone to wide-spread dysfunction resulting from anatomic or functional obstruction. This results in repeated urinary infection, incontinence, kidney damage, and severely degrades quality of life. The medical and societal costs of this condition exceed $67 billion annually in the U.S. with Canadian estimates roughly 10% of this cost. Very often, the bladder tissue and function changes do not return to normal despite removing the inciting obstruction. The widespread nature of this problem in humans, and its irreversibility when modelled in the bladder of animals or bladder muscle cells strongly suggests that this is a response to an ongoing change in the disease-induced cellular environment. Our objective is to find new therapy that may prevent or reverse this otherwise permenant bladder muscle disease.  We are testing the possibility that chemical changes to DNA, termed epigenetic changes, which can also be permanent and inherited, are an underlying mechanism in this disease. This research will use a system we developed to grow rodent bladders in test-tubes (that we can manipulate without the extraneous complexities of the living animal), along with bladder muscle cells, and live animal models of persistent bladder obstruction. Using these approaches, we will assess bladder organ, cell, and animal responses to available inhibitors of the principle epigenetic machinery, (the DNA methylation enzymes), as well as determine the role of existing and new molecular pathways that may be  epigenetically regulating this disease. Completion of this project is anticipated to reveal pathways to new drug therapy for this chronic condition.

TitreApplicationTitle: High frequency oscillations and seizure initiation in temporal lobe epilepsy
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; EPILEPTIC DISORDERS; HIGH FREQUENCY OSCILLATIONS; SEIZURES; TEMPORAL LOBE EPILEPSY
Abstract-Résumé: Seizures are unpredictable events during which the brain activity changes into a pathological state that is associated to abnormal behavior and, often, to impairment or loss of consciousness. Many antiepileptic drugs are available but seizures are poorly controlled in approx. one third of patients thus producing a socioeconomic impact as great as that of stroke or Parkinson. It is therefore crucial to understand the mechanisms involved in seizure initiation to develop more effective, mechanism-targeted therapeutic interventions. The objective of my studies is to identify how a seizure begins. To this end, I will use an established animal model of temporal lobe epilepsy in which we have discovered that progression to seizure activity is characterized in the EEG by increased occurrence of two specific types of high frequency oscillations, termed ripples and fast ripples. Since ripples and fast ripples may reflect the activation of distinctive neuronal networks we postulate that transition to seizures rests on two main mechanisms that will be firmly identified. We expect our future studies to clarify some of the contradictory findings regarding seizure initiation thus leading to specific pharmacological treatments.

TitreApplicationTitle: Approach and avoidance interpersonal goals in women with vulvodynia and their partners: A daily experience study
Keywords-MotsClés: DAILY EXPERIENCE METHODOLOGY; DYADIC METHODS; GOALS; MOTIVATION; PAIN; PROVOKED VESTIBULODYNIA; SEXUAL FUNCTION; SEXUAL SATISFACTION; VULVODYNIA
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic pain problems of the reproductive system are frequently misdiagnosed or ignored, resulting in a great personal and financial cost to women and society. One prevalent (16%) condition is vulvodynia, or chronic unexplained vulvar pain. Vulvodynia negatively affects all aspects of women's sexuality, and the quality of life and romantic relationships of women and their partners. Despite the interpersonal nature of this condition, studies examining relationship factors are lacking. The current proposal builds on our prior research on the influence of romantic relationships in vulvodynia as well as past studies on the important role of goals in chronic pain. Over 80% of women with vulvodynia continue to have intercourse, possibly because of interpersonal goals such as wanting to promote intimacy (i.e., approach goals) or to avoid a partner's disappointment (i.e., avoidance goals). The proposed two-centre, two-month daily diary study examines the role of women's own and their partner's sexual goals on her pain during intercourse and the psychological and sexual adjustment of both members of the couple. We expect that on days when women or their partners pursue sex for approach goals, women will report lower pain, and women and partners will report better sexual and psychological functioning, whereas on days when women or their partners pursue sex for avoidance goals, women will report greater pain and both will report lower sexual and psychological functioning. We also expect that higher approach goals will lead people to attend more to positive cues during sex, which will lead to less pain and better sexual and psychological functioning, whereas higher avoidance goals will lead people to attend more to negative cues during sex, which will lead to poorer functioning. Results may improve the health and quality of life of women with vulvodynia by suggesting that psychological interventions focus on increasing approach and decreasing avoidance sexual goals.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of a three-tiered, standardized process to assess senior drivers
Keywords-MotsClés: DRIVING; DRIVING SIMULATOR; EVALUATION; OLDER ADULTS; ROC CURVE
Abstract-Résumé: As the Canadian population continues to age, there are more and more older adult drivers on the roadways. Aging can cause health problems, such as memory or vision problems, that can impact safe driving. This does not mean that older adults with these types of concerns should have their drivers' licenses taken away; many seniors are safe drivers. Further, driving helps many seniors remain independent and mobile. However, to ensure the well being of older adults while at the same time maintaining public safety, we need to find a way to assess the driving abilities of senior drivers to figure out those who are safe, those who require more support or retraining, and those individuals who should no longer be on the road. For our study we will interview senior drivers in Thunder Bay and Ottawa. First, participants will complete a number of memory, vision and mobility tests. Then they will complete an assessment on a driving simulator. Finally they will do an on-road driving test with a driving instructor. The information that we collect will help us figure out the best way for health care professionals to assess senior drivers in a fair and equitable manner, ensuring they are not deprived of the driving privilege unfairly. This may have a profound effect on their quality of life by promoting independence.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cortical GABAerigc regulation of cognition, and its relevance to schizophrenia
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; COGNITION; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GABA; PREFRONTAL CORTEX; SCHIZOPHRENIA
Abstract-Résumé: The idea of schizophrenia typically conjures up images of people who hear voices, see visions and have delusional beliefs. However, clinicians have long recognized that cognitive dysfunction is actually one of the most fundamental and debilitating aspects of the disorder.  Numerous brain abnormalities are believed to underlie these symptoms. Among these, studies of the brains of schizophrenic subjects have identified dysfunction of a brain chemical termed GABA as potentially being a major cause of the cognitive symptoms. GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain that is important for filtering out extraneous information and helps to synchronize the activity of groups of neurons in the frontal lobes (also referred to as the prefrontal cortex).  In schizophrenia, GABA transmission appears to be reduced, resulting in a hyperactive or 'noisy' cortex that may impair attention and other cognitive functions that are regulated by the frontal lobes.  However, our understanding of exactly how prefrontal cortical GABA may regulate these different aspects of cognition is sparse.  Our proposed experiments are designed to thoroughly investigate how GABA transmission within the prefrontal cortex regulates a variety of cognitive functions known to be impaired in schizophrenia, using rats as a model system.  Other studies will investigate how a noisy cortex may interfere with information processing in other subcortical regions.  These studies will provide important new insight into how hyperactivity within the frontal lobes may be an underlying cause of the cognitive abnormalities present in schizophrenia. In turn, this information may facilitate the development of novel drug therapies intended to alleviate these cognitive deficits.

TitreApplicationTitle: Genetic Determinants of Congenital Hypothyroidism
Keywords-MotsClés: BIRTH DEFECTS; CHILD HEALTH; CLINICALLY DRIVEN EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; CONGENITAL HYPOTHYROIDISM; DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY; GENETICS; PEDIATRICS
Abstract-Résumé: Thyroid hormones play a crucial role in child development. In infants, too little thyroid hormone (hypothyroidism) is deleterious, especially for brain development, and untreated hypothyroidism in infancy leads to irreversible intellectual disability. To avoid this, newborn screening programs have been implemented to diagnose hypothyroidism early. Congenital hypothyroidism is most often due to a thyroid that has not developed in the correct location (thyroid ectopy) and does not produce enough hormones. In the most severe cases, there is complete absence of the thyroid (athyreosis). The reason why the thyroid gland does not attain its proper place in the neck is largely unknown. Therefore, it is important to better understand this disease, to diagnose it early and to optimize treatment. Early detection by taking a few drops of blood from the heel of the newborn, even before discharge from the hospital, allows most affected children to attain their full intellectual potential, with one tablet of thyroid hormone daily. However, developmental delay may still occur in some severely affected children. A loss of 10 points of intelligence quotient has a major impact for the affected individual and for society. We estimate a global economic benefit of 1 to 1.3 Million $ per year (in Canada) for each IQ point gained in patients suffering from severe congenital hypothyroidism, i.e. thyroid ectopy and athyreosis. However, nearly 40 years after implementation of routine screening, the cause of congenital hypothyroidism remains largely unknown. The goal of the present proposal is to discover the mechanisms underlying abnormal thyroid gland development and possible markers predicting loss of intellectual potential so as to provide prompt remedial help to children needing it. A video explaining our research goal is available on YouTube (www.youtube.com/watch?v=bSvycG-PKls)

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving neurological outcome of intensive care by bedside monitoring of cerebral perfusion
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOMEDICAL OPTICS; CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW; CEREBRAL ISCHEMIA; NEAR INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY; NEUROMONITORING; PERFUSION IMAGING; SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE
Abstract-Résumé: Despite only making up 2% of the body's weight, the brain consumes 20% of the body's energy.  Because of this high energy demand, the brain is extremely vulnerable to damage caused by reduced blood flow (i.e. ischemia).  This vulnerability is a foremost concern for patients with acute brain injury, such as stroke or brain bleed (hemorrhage), who are undergoing intensive care.  These patients have a elevated risk of additional brain injury due to complications during intensive care that impede the flow of blood to the brain.  Unfortunately, there is current no reliable technology suitable for detecting brain ischemia at the patient's bedside.  Real-time detection would enable the intensive-care team the opportunity to take prompt measures to restore blood flow, as it is well known that in terms of preventing ischemic brain injury: "time is brain."  Our research team is developing a portable, safe, light-based technology for measuring brain blood flow in the intensive care unit.  The goals of this work are to expand the capabilities of our optical method to provide continuous flow measurements - critical for determining the duration of ischemia - and to begin studies involving intensive care patients in order to test the clinical feasibility of the technology.  If successful, this research would help improve patient outcome by reducing the incidence of this debilitating complication.

TitreApplicationTitle: Adaptive Mechanisms of Locomotion after Contusive Spinal Lesions in Cats
Keywords-MotsClés: ELECTROMYOGRAPHY; INTRATHECAL INJECTIONS; LOCOMOTION; LOCOMOTOR TRAINING; NEUROIMAGING; NEUROPHARMACOLOGY; PARALYSIS; SPINAL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; SPINAL LESIONS; SPINAL REFLEXES
Abstract-Résumé: We have previously shown that cats can recover the ability to walk with the hindlimbs 2-3 weeks after a complete surgical spinal cord injury (SCI) performed at the last Thoracic spinal segment. This confirms that there exists a complex spinal circuitry capable of generating the locomotor pattern without descending brain inputs. Furthermore, during the last CIHR grant (2008-2013), we have studied the capacity of cats to walk after partial unilateral hemisection. The major finding was that cats recovered hindlimb locomotion largely through changes induced in the spinal cord (SC) below the lesion indicating its important capacity to change after lesions (neuroplasticity). We also investigated the role of locomotor training and found that it improved significantly the quality of locomotion as well as the ability to walk immediately after a complete second spinalization (instead of 2-3wks). These results have prompted us to investigate, in the present proposal, the locomotor capacity of cats after performing a more clinically relevant SC lesion using an impactor to compress the SC and damage incompletely both sides of the SC as is most often the case in humans. We will establish the kinematic and reflex changes occurring during a period of 3 weeks after the compression. In different groups of cats, we will investigate the role of important neurotransmitters such as noradrenaline and serotonin by injecting agonists or antagonists of these systems on the SC.  At the end of each protocol, cats will be submitted to a terminal experiment during which we will investigate changes in the intrinsic spinal circuitry. We believe that this project has a significant clinical impact since there is virtually no kinematic nor pharmacological studies in cats with contusive lesions and this is needed to establish an appropriate pharmacotherapy in humans with SCI.

TitreApplicationTitle: Advanced MRI methods for early detection and characterization of placental dysfunction and the monitoring of therapy
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTOREGULATION; BIOPHYSICAL MODELLING; BLOOD FLOW; BLOOD OXYGENATION MEASUREMENT; FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; MOUSE MODELS; OXYGEN THERAPY; PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION; PREGNANCY
Abstract-Résumé: A healthy placenta is essential to a healthy pregnancy. Placental dysfunction affects over 3.3% of all Canadian pregnancies each year (>17,000 cases/year). Inadequate supply of oxygen and nutrients through the placenta to the fetus reduces growth and places the fetus at risk of brain injury or stillbirth from asphyxia. Early delivery of the fetus is currently the primary therapy for severe placental dysfunction, yet there is significant risk that this action leads to severe brain injury. It is therefore essential to develop new therapies that address placental dysfunction during pregnancy as an alternative to early delivery, and to develop non-invasive techniques to monitor the response of the fetus to treatment.  Maternal breathing of oxygen enriched gas mixtures has the potential to be used both diagnostically in assessing abnormal pregnancy and therapeutically to support the at-risk fetus as an alternative to premature delivery. The goal of this proposal is to develop advanced imaging technologies to evaluate placental/fetal health in at-risk pregnancies and their response to maternal breathing of supplementary oxygen. Our proposal is to develop this technology initially in experimental mice that model placental dysfunction, and then make corresponding imaging measurements in women with at-risk and normal pregnancies.  For this, we will leverage the ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technologies that we have developed for characterization of placental and fetal blood flow and blood oxygenation. In healthy pregnancies, these two measures will be used to establish the normal pattern for blood flow and oxygen delivery. In at-risk pregnancies, we will use these technologies to measure changes in fetal blood flow and oxygen levels before and after maternal oxygen enrichment.  Guided by our data from the mice, these measures will allows us to determine whether the fetus has the potential to benefit from therapeutic oxygen delivery to the mother.

TitreApplicationTitle: Manipulating the RIG-I signaling pathway to inhibit influenza virus infection
Keywords-MotsClés: 5'PPP RNA; ADJUVANT; ANTI-VIRAL INNATE IMMUNITY; CELL-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSES; FLOW CYTOMETRY; INFLUENZA VIRUS; INTERFERONS; MICROARRAY; RIG-I SIGNALING; VIRUS-LIKE PARTICLES
Abstract-Résumé: Influenza virus epidemics represent a major public health problem that affects up to 500 million people every year, with children and the elderly being the higher risk population. Past influenza outbreak - 1918, 1957, and 1968 - caused millions of fatalities, with the most severe epidemic in 1918-1919 which killed an estimated 40 million people worldwide. Although it is not possible to predict when the next pandemic might occur, that it will occur is almost certain. Influenza virus infection is controlled in large part by the host antiviral immune response. Our research, as well as the work of many other scientists throughout the world over the past decade, has identified key elements of the immune system that sense and respond to incoming virus infection. More specifically, the cellular receptor RIG-I specifically detects small molecules of viral RNA. The goal of this project is to dissect immune response triggered by RIG-I during Influenza infection and use small molecules of RNA that mimic the viral RNA to defend against infection. We also want to examine the potential of using these small RNA molecules in combination with influenza vaccines to enhance their efficacy. Understanding these virus-host interactions will provide important insights concerning Influenza infection and disease. We believe that this study will contribute to the development of novel strategies for antiviral therapy.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessment of Metoprolol in the Prevention of Vasovagal Syncope in Aging Subjects (POST5)
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; BETA BLOCKER; HYPOTENSION; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; SYNCOPE; VASOVAGAL
Abstract-Résumé: Fainting affects about 50% of Canadians, is the cause of 1-2% of emergency room visits, and probably causes $250 million in health care spending each year. Frequent fainting causes a poor quality of life, and problems at work, at home, and while driving. The most common cause is reflex fainting. This occurs in people of all ages, and while many people only faint once or twice there are hundreds of thousand of Canadians who faint many times, and often more than once a year. Reflex fainting is due to abrupt drops in blood pressure and often drops in heart rate, and these reduce blood flow to the brain enough to make people lose consciousness. There is no known medical treatment for frequent fainting. One possible treatment would be to prevent the reflex that causes the drop in blood pressure. A drug called metoprolol might do this, but only in people over age 40. The evidence for this comes from earlier studies but is pretty weak, and in this study we will test whether metoprolol prevents moderate to severe reflex fainting. We will study 248 patients who have fainted recently, have reflex fainting, and are at high risk of fainting again. They will enroll in a randomized clinical trial. Consenting patients will be assigned randomly to receive either metoprolol or a dummy pill called a placebo, and we will follow them for 1 year. We then will compare the number of people who faint in those taking metoprolol compared to placebo. We will also compare the frequency of fainting, quality of life, and health costs, in each arm of the study. This study will have centres in Canada, the United States, Europe and South America. It is the only study of its kind and it will be pivotal.

TitreApplicationTitle: Deciphering the role of TRK-fused gene (TFG) in antiviral innate immunity
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIVIRAL ASSAYS; ANTIVIRAL RESPONSE; ANTIVIRAL THERAPIES; CELL SIGNALING; INNATE IMMUNITY; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY TECHNIQUES; TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR; TRK-FUSED GENE; TYPE I INTERFERONS PRODUCTION; VIRAL INFECTION
Abstract-Résumé: Viruses are cellular parasites that can only replicate within a suitable host cell; they mainly depend on certain cellular mechanisms for their replication.  Thereby, interfering with viral replication in a specific manner, i.e. without inflicting damage to the host, with a pharmacological agent becomes problematic. However, a better characterization of innate immunity determinants could transform antiviral treatments by introducing a broad-spectrum therapeutic arsenal to enhance and optimize the normal antiviral response of the host.  The invasion of a host cell by a virus triggers a series of immune responses occurring as a result of an interaction between viral components and surveillance mechanisms of the host. These host-infectious agents interaction usually leads to the production of certain cytokines which eventually disrupt viral replication and dissemination. Interestingly, a protein called TRAF3 has shown to be important in the development of such antiviral response. Although, the precise method by which TRAF3 reacts in such conditions remains elusive. However, the identification by our laboratory of TRK-fused gene (TFG), a protein involved in secretory pathways, as a new partner of TRAF3 could propose new insights about the mechanism underlying the antiviral response.  Thus, the aim of my project is to decipher the role of TFG in the innate antiviral response. The central hypothesis of my project is that TFG is a new TRAF3 partner whose capacity to regulate the secretory pathways allows it to control the antiviral response. Thus, we will characterize the interaction between TFG and TRAF3 and the role of TFG in the innate antiviral immune system. Then, we will establish the link between TFG antiviral influence, its interaction with the secretory pathway as well as with other known members of the antiviral response.  This research program aims to identify and characterize new effectors that could be targeted for future antiviral therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Changements cérébraux dans l'apnée obstructive du sommeil associée au trouble cognitif léger.
Keywords-MotsClés: APNEE OBSTRUCTIVE DU SOMMEIL; DEMENCE; IMAGERIE PAR RESONANCE MAGNETIQUE; NEUROIMAGERIE; NEUROPSYCHOLOGIE; NEUROSCIENCES; TOMOGRAPHIE PAR EMISSION MONOPHOTONIQUE; TROUBLE COGNITIF LEGER; TROUBLES COGNITIFS; TROUBLES DU SOMMEIL
Abstract-Résumé: L'apnee obstructive du sommeil est un probleme de sante majeur qui touche environ 20% des personnes agees. Les arrets respiratoires en sommeil dans cette maladie sont associes avec une fatigue et des problemes cognitifs comme l'attention au cours de la journee. On observe aussi une perte de la matiere grise du cerveau et une diminution du flot sanguin dans certaines parties du cerveau. Les problemes cognitifs dans l'apnee du sommeil peuvent etre assez severes pour atteindre les criteres diagnostic dun trouble appele le trouble cognitif leger. Celui-ci peut mener a la demence et correspond a une diminution des capacites cognitives plus grande que celle attendue lors du vieillissement normal. Le trouble cognitif leger, en plus de partager plusieurs facteurs de risque avec l'apnee obstructive du sommeil, se presente aussi avec une perte de matiere grise du cerveau et une diminution du flot sanguin dans certaines parties du cerveau. La presence d'apnee obstructive du sommeil non traitee pourrait expliquee en partie les problemes cognitifs chez les patients diagnostiques avec un trouble cognitif leger. Un traitement efficace de l'apnee du sommeil pourrait donc diminuer ou empecher la progression du trouble cognitif leger vers la demence. Ce projet vise a evaluer si des patients ayant de l'apnee obstructive du sommeil associe avec un trouble cognitif leger presentent une plus grande perte de la matiere grise et une diminution plus marquee du flot sanguin que les personnes avec un trouble cognitif leger seulement. Des techniques de neuroimagerie seront utilisees pour faire cette evaluation. C'est la premiere etude qui s'interesse a la presence et aux effets de l'apnee obstructive du sommeil dans le trouble cognitif leger. Celle-ci nous permettra une meilleure comprehension des processus impliques dans l'apnee du sommeil et dans le trouble cognitif leger, deux maladies ayant des consequences importantes dans notre systeme de sante.

TitreApplicationTitle: Do physiological stress responses contribute to metabolic dysfunction?
Keywords-MotsClés: AGE DIFFERENCES; METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION; PHYSIOLOGICAL REACTIVITY; PROSPECTIVE; SEX DIFFERENCES; STRESS
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide, killing an estimated 17 million people every year. The yearly economic burden of cardiovascular disease is approximately 22.2 billion dollars in Canada alone. Metabolic abnormalities incur significant risk for cardiovascular illnesses, particularly coronary artery disease. One out of 5 Canadians is affected by the metabolic syndrome (MS) over the lifespan. MS consists of at least three of the following five factors: central adiposity, high blood pressure, elevated triglycerides, increased fasting blood glucose, and low levels of high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol. Psychological factors may contribute to MS via heightened or prolonged physiological responses to stress. Our objective is to examine the concurrent and prospective relations between a global index of metabolic dysfunction (MD) and stress responses, as well as the moderating effect of age and/or sex on these associations.  MD is defined as the number of MS parameters for which participants are in the higher quartile (lower for HDL) for their sex. A sample of 193 healthy working men and women were exposed to four stressor tasks while blood pressure, heart rate, and heart rate variability measures were obtained. Five-minute recovery periods followed each stressor. Residual change scores for stress reactivity (stress-baseline) and recovery (recovery-baseline) were used to control for baseline values. Three years later, MD was reassessed in 136 participants. Analyses will involve hierarchical linear regressions. This project will elucidate the importance of physiological stress responses to the development or progression of metabolic dysfunction, as well as highlight any sex and/or age differences in this regard.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification précoce des prédicteurs socio-cognitifs de d'adhésion dans l'hémophilie sévère
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER INFANTILE; DYADES PARENT-ENFANT; DETRESSE; LEUCEMIE; STRESS POST-TRAUMATIQUE; SYMPTOMES POST-TRAUMATIQUES; TRAUMATISME; EVOLUTION DES MALADIES
Abstract-Résumé: Le diagnostic d'un cancer infantile est un evenement potentiellement traumatique a la fois pour les parents et pour l'enfant.  Certaines etudes soutiennent qu'il existerait un lien entre la detresse vecue par les parents suite au cancer de leur enfant et la detresse ressentie par l'enfant lui-meme. Specifiquement, notre etude vise a clarifier les caracteristiques du lien entre le stress post-traumatique des parents d'enfants survivants de leucemie lymphoblastique aigue et celui des survivants eux-memes et a determiner si les symptomes exprimes par l'un et l'autre s'apparentent.  Nous voulons egalement determiner les facteurs susceptibles de moduler cette proximite emotionnelle.  Par exemple, des facteurs tels que les attitudes parentales, le sexe du parent et de l'enfant, l'age du parent et de l'enfant au moment du diagnostic, le temps ecoule depuis le diagnostic, l'intensite du traitement et le nombre de recidives pourraient agir comme moderateurs sur le lien entre la detresse des parents et celle des enfants survivants. Une meilleure comprehension de cette proximite emotionnelle et des moderateurs impliques permettrait d'integrer des mesures plus adequates de detection des survivants de cancer infantile qui sont le plus a risque de detresse emotionnelle.  Cela permettrait egalement d'etablir,  dans les milieux hospitaliers specialises, des plans de prevention et de traitement plus efficaces et plus adaptes des traumatismes relies a la situation particuliere cancer infantile.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude de l'effet de la privation de sommeil sur le protocole diagnostique, la somnolence et les anomalies électrophysiologiques à l'éveil chez les somnambules.
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYSE SPECTRALE; DIAGNOSTIC; PHYSIOPATHOLOGIE; POLYSOMNOGRAPHIE; SOMNAMBULISME; SOMNOLENCE; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGIE
Abstract-Résumé: Malgre presque 5 decennies d'investigations sur les troubles du sommeil, relativement peu de choses sont connues a propos du somnambulisme (SM). De plus, et contrairement a la plupart des autres troubles du sommeil, le SM est encore diagnostique principalement ou exclusivement sur la base de l'histoire clinique des patients. Cette parasomnie est un des plus frequents et dramatiques exemples des troubles du sommeil et est beaucoup plus commun chez les adultes (approximativement 3-4%) que ce qui est generalement accepte. Le SM est aussi associe avec un potentiel considerable de blessures et les patients consultent souvent suite a une histoire de comportements dommageables ou agressifs pendant le sommeil.  Diagnostiquer le SM avec des instruments objectifs tels que le polysomnographe est souvent difficile etant donne que les episodes surviennent rarement dans le laboratoire de sommeil. L'objectif principal de ce projet de these est d'etablir un protocole robuste pour le diagnostic en laboratoire du somnambulisme et de mieux documenter les anomalies comportementales et electrophysiologiques pendant l'eveil chez les somnambules adultes.  Ce projet s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un programme de recherche sur la physiopathologie du somnambulisme subventionne pour 5 ans par les IRSC.

TitreApplicationTitle: CXCR7, Negative Regulator Of Leukemia Bone Marrow Homing
Keywords-MotsClés: CHEMOKINE RECEPTORS; CHEMOTHERAPY RELAPSE IN LEUKAEMIA; CXCL12; CXCR4; CXCR7; RISK EVALUATION
Abstract-Résumé: Leukemia is the most spread cancer among Canadian children. Though its treatment shows a high initial success rate, relapsing after chemotherapy is frequent. Some leukemic cells residing in bone marrow niches are responsible for this relapse. This process of bone marrow homing of leukemia cells is dictated by a receptor CXCR4. We hypothesize here that CXCR7, a different chemokine receptor, regulates CXCR4 when they are co-expressed on leukemia cells. As CXCR7 and CXCR4 together are involved in chemotaxis, their levels of expression would be a predictor of the homing of leukemia cells and the risk of relapse after chemotherapy. The mechanism by which this effect is achieved remains to be determined. The project set out to investigate the following specific aims: to evaluate the chemotactic comportment dependence on the expression of the two receptors, and to decipher the mechanism of CXCR4 regulation by CXCR7. The results of our study will open new avenues for the future development of innovative treatment approaches. First, pharmacologic targeting of CXCR7 may increase its negative impact on CXCR4 in homing. Second, the ratio of CXCR4 and CXCR7 expression by ALLs patients may reveal predictive for bone marrow homing and the risk of relapse. This risk prediction may allow doctors to individually adjust doses of chemotherapy accordingly. This would be an indispensable perspective for the treatment of ALL, where toxic side effects and overtreatment are clearly an issue.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'effet des contaminants environnementaux sur le circuit cérébral de la peur: L'Imagerie par raisonnance magnétique fonctionelle (IRMf) chez les jeunes Inuits du Nunavik
Keywords-MotsClés: CIRCUIT DE LA PEUR; CONDITIONNEMENT DE PEUR ET EXTINCTION; DIMORPHISME SEXUEL; HORMONES DE STRESS; MEMOIRE EMOTIONNELLE; SOMMEIL PARADOXAL; SSPT SOUS CLINIQUE; SYNDROME DU STRESS POST-TRAUMATIQUE; SYSTEME DE NEURO-IMAGERIE TEMP; TROUBLE DU CAUCHEMAR IDIOPATIQUE
Abstract-Résumé: Le syndrome de stress post-traumatique (SSPT) est un trouble d'anxiete declenche par l'exposition a un evenement traumatique. Sa prevalence dans la population canadienne est eleve (9.2%) et les couts lies aux soins medicaux et aux pertes de productivite qu'il engendre sont considerables. Les patients souffrant du SSPT revivent leur traumatisme sous forme de cauchemars et souffrent de deficits cognitifs, en particulier dans l'apprentissage et dans l'extinction de la peur. Tres peu connu et pourtant fort repandu, le trouble des cauchemars idiopathiques (TCM) ressemble a bien des egards au SSPT. Cette similitude souleve donc la possibilite importante que le TCM est une forme sous-clinique du SSPT et un facteur de risque pouvant predire et eventuellement prevenir le SSPT. Des preuves suggerent que le SSPT est un dysfonctionnement induit par une suractivation du circuit mnesique de la peur. La consolidation qui sous-tend ces souvenirs traumatiques s'effectue pendant le sommeil paradoxal. Le premier objectif est donc de proposer un modele qui prend en compte a la fois les cauchemars du SSPT et du TCM pour refleter ce dysfonctionnement sous-jacent, plus severe dans le SSPT. Les composants neuronaux de ce modele comprennent: 1) une augmentation de l'activite de l'amygdale qui produit la sur-consolidation des souvenirs de peur; 2) une mediation inefficace par les regions pre-frontales qui mene a l'echec de l'extinction des souvenirs de peur; 3) un deficit dans les regions hippocampiques qui regule l'evaluation des contextes dangereux et securitaires 4) une difference entre les sexes concernant la lateralite hemispherique. Le deuxieme objectif important de cette recherche est d'utiliser une nouvelle generation de systeme de neuro-imagerie TEMP (tomographie d'emission monophotonique) a haute resolution pour decouvrir des preuves de ces elements dysfonctionnels dans les circuits neuronaux du SSPT et du TCM.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanisms underlying long-term synaptic plasticity and memory formation
Keywords-MotsClés: ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; FIELD POTENTIALS; MRNA GRANULES; NEUROBIOLOGY OF MEMORY; PATCH CLAMPING; REGULATION OF TRANSLATION; RNA BINDING PROTEINS; SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY
Abstract-Résumé: To form new memories, our brain relies on its ability to change the strength of connections between cells creating a unique pattern of activity encoding information that we can remember. A way in which the brain can reinforce or weaken the communication between neurons, or brain cells, is to quickly produce new and specific proteins very close to the point of connection - a phenomenon we call protein synthesis dependent synaptic plasticity. This synthesis needs to be tightly regulated for neurons to function normally. In fact, emerging evidence is revealing that a dysfunctional regulation of this protein synthesis plays an important role in various neuropsychiatric diseases such as autism and schizophrenia. Yet, we still know very little about the mechanisms that govern these biochemical changes. Thus, our research thus aims to uncover the underlying molecular basis of memory and proposes a fundamentally new paradigm of translation control. This will have critical implications for developing new drug therapies for a variety of neuropsychiatric diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Accessibility and costs of healthcare for refugee claimants following changes to the Interim Federal Health Program
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESS TO HEALTH CARE; ADMINISTRATIVE DATA ANALYSIS; COSTS OF HEALTH CARE; CRITICAL INCIDENT ANALYSIS; ETHICS; HEALTH POLICIES; INTEGRATED KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; INTERIM FEDERAL HEALTH PROGRAM; MIXED-METHOD DESIGN; REFUGEE CLAIMANT
Abstract-Résumé: Access to healthcare is a key factor in refugee health. On June 30, 2012, the federal government drastically reduced the scope of the Interim Federal Health Program (IFH), that previously covered medical services and medications for all refugee claimants and resettled refugees. Persons who are partially uninsured, as is now the case for refugee claimants, often delay medical consultation. Such delays may lead to worsening health conditions that require more costly interventions than providing timely primary care, and might also lead to increased critical incidents, morbidity and mortality.  The main objective of this research project is to assess the impact of the June 2012 changes to the IFH program on refugee claimants' access to healthcare and the potential effects on their health, as well as on the cost of providing care to this population. A knowledge transfer strategy aimed at improving healthcare delivery to this population will subsequently be implemented.  The study will be conducted in hospitals and primary care clinics of Toronto and Montreal where the majority of the approximately 100,000 refugee claimants live. It will have two components: First, a mixed-method quantitative and qualitative analysis will document the impact of IFH changes on costs, use of services and potential health consequences and identify the systemic factors impeding access to healthcare and their contribution to adverse outcomes. Second, healthcare providers' perceptions and practices regarding refugee claimants' access to healthcare will be assessed through an online survey and focus groups.   The integrated knowledge translation strategy will help to inform knowledge, attitudes and practices of health professionals and administrative staff and to formulate policy recommendations that will be submitted to decision-makers in the federal and provincial governments as well as in healthcare institutions.

Keywords-MotsClés: ABCA1; ATHEROSCLEROSIS; CHOLESTEROL; CYTOKINE; GENE REGULATION; INFLAMMATION; LIPID RAFT; MACROPHAGE
Abstract-Résumé: ABCA1 has tow major functions: one is to promote cholesterol removal and thus make HDL (good cholesterol), another one is to control inflammation. We propose that both these functions is originated from cell surface where ABCA1 is making the cell wall more flexible. This makes cholesterol removal easier and also helps cells to fight inflammation.
