TitreApplicationTitle: Genetic models of Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumours
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER GENETICS; CHROMATIN MODIFIERS; DAXX; EPIGENETICS; MDM2; P53
Abstract-Résumé: Recent advances have highlighted that cancer represents a collection of diseases, differing not only in the location or organ of disease but the fundamental makeup of the tumours.  To advance treatment options and approaches, a better understanding of the underlying causes of disease is essential.  DNA and genome-based sequencing studies have revealed a number of differences between normal and tumour cells, and from this we can draw associations about how cancers arise.  It is, however, essential to test these associations in a laboratory and experimental setting in order to be able to identify the changes that actually drive cancers to develop, as these will provide the best opportunities to develop novel drugs or therapies.  One recent sequencing study of the second most common type of pancreatic cancer, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (PNETs), revealed a number of new players in these cancers.  Specifically, 43% of patients showed mutations in either DAXX or ATRX.  Interestingly, this was the first report to suggest a role for DAXX in cancer. DAXX and ATRX work to together to help maintain DNA integrity.  As it is well established that a loss of DNA integrity can contribute to cancer development, our work aims to test the hypothesis that DAXX loss is an important for the formation of a subset of PNETs.  To address this, we aim to develop a mouse model for PNETs through the specific loss of DAXX in the pancreas.  We will also study how other changes common in cancers contribute to the development of PNETs in this model.  Not only will our models of PNETs teach us a great deal about how these cancers arise, they will also provide a tool in which we can start to study what treatment options are most effective for these tumours, having a direct role in advancing patient care.  Combined, through this work and a better understanding of the key changes that drive these cancers we aim to advance diagnosis and treatments options for patients with PNETs.

TitreApplicationTitle: Determination of Angiotensin Type 1 Receptor Structure in Complex with Beta-arrestins and Ligands
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOTENSIN TYPE 1 RECEPTOR; ANTAGONIST; BETA-ARRESTIN; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES; DRUG DISCOVERY; LOSARTAN; PROTEIN COMPLEX; RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN SYSTEM; TRV120027; X-RAY CRYSTAL STRUCTURE
Abstract-Résumé: The entire world lives in an era of communication driven by the recent rise of electronic technologies. Indeed, nearly everyone has a cell phone or a computer and is able to join friends, family or mate in an instant through any internet connection gaining time and efficacy on every aspects of our life. The human body has similar devices that communicate with each other to automatically take decisions in order to fulfill our fundamental needs. For example, everyone has to maintain a stable level of blood pressure. Analogous to a covered pot accumulating pressure on a hot stove, eventually if nothing is done, the cover will be displaced and the pot content will spill. For humans, high blood pressure level will do similar effect. To control blood pressure, the body has to send a message to the appropriate body device, the blood vessels, that will trigger the wanted effect. But similarly to a cell phone, a message will be received only if the antenna on the vessel works properly. These antennas are called message receptors or just receptors and are also implicated in other type of fundamental needs than blood pressure control. As any devices, sometimes it does not work properly and need to be fixed. This is important as in the case of blood pressure control, it can lead to lethal diseases.  It is only recently that the exact 3-dimensional plan of the first body receptor has been found. Our research aim at determining the 3-dimensional plan of the receptor that control blood pressure. We think that finding the plan of that receptor will allow us to find a way to design better strategies to fix it when it is broken and save lives.

TitreApplicationTitle: Memory Dysfunction in Schizophrenia and Parkinson's Disease: Investigating the Role of Dopamine using Pharmacological FMRI
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNITIVE TESTS; D-AMPHETAMINE; DOPAMINE; FMRI; HUMANS; MEDICATION; MEMORY; PARKINSON'S DISEASE; PHARMACOLOGY; SCHIZOPHRENIA
Abstract-Résumé: Memory dysfunction is a major factor that impairs the quality of life for individuals suffering from a broad set of conditions, ranging from schizophrenia to healthy aging. To date, research has focused on how memory dysfunction relates to permanent structural changes in the brain. But emerging findings from animal research show that a neurotransmitter called dopamine, which is dysfunctional in many conditions that result in memory disorders, plays a crucial role in regulating how the brain forms memories. This opens the possibility that some clinical memory deficits may be chemical in nature and, thus, more treatable than previously believed. The proposed project uses a combination of cutting edge pharmacological and brain imaging techniques to assess how dopamine influences memory in the healthy and diseased human brain. The project aims to uncover (1) whether pharmacological manipulations of dopamine influence memory formation in humans, (2) the neural mechanisms underlying this modulation, (3) the extent to which memory deficits are caused by dopaminergic dysfunction in two disorders which are characterized by dopamine imbalance, schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease, and (4) how dopaminergic medications used to treat schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease influence the aspects of memory that are dopamine-modulated. The results of this project will provide new insights into the physiological basis of memory deficits and can be used to identify the specific aspects of memory which are most likely to be treatable with pharmacological intervention along with the aspects of memory which are least affected by dopaminergic dysfunction and on which patients with schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease can learn to rely.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Sequential Response of Innate Lymphoid Cells Governs the Switch from Inflammation to Tissue Repair During Influenza A Virus Infection
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOPTIVE TRANSFER; CYTOKINES; FLOW CYTOMETRY; INFLAMMATION; INFLUENZA; INNATE IMMUNITY; INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS; MOUSE MODEL; TISSUE REPAIR
Abstract-Résumé: Infection with influenza A viruses (IAV) causes inflammation in the lungs of infected individuals that is essential to clear the infection but that can also have detrimental effects if not well controlled. The restoration of lung tissue and return to homeostasis are critical to maintain efficient pulmonary function. Cells that contribute to inflammation are well characterized, however little is known about the ones that mediate lung repair. Furthermore, the mechanisms that govern the balance between inflammation and return to homeostasis are poorly understood. Innate lymphoid cells (ILC) represent an emerging population of cells that were recently identified and that can have a double-edged character, either by promoting a beneficial immune response or by causing detrimental immunopathological effects during IAV infection. However, the precise populations responsible for these phenomena are not well characterized and the mechanisms by which ILC are activated upon infection unknown. Here, we hypothesize that ILC populations act sequentially to promote inflammation, early upon infection and lung repair, at later stages. To test this, mice will be infected with IAV, and the ILC populations will be monitored daily. This will allow us to identify when ILC that promote inflammation or tissue repair accumulate in the lungs. Transfer experiments of these cells to mice at different time points post-infection will be performed to confirm the sequential effect of different ILC. Finally, ILC will be isolated from naive mice and stimulated in vitro to determine which stimulus is important for their activation and how they respond to it. There is a fine balance between inflammation, its resolution, and tissue repair. ILC can have both beneficial and detrimental effects in the lungs.  A better understanding of ILC populations during IAV infection will provide new insights on the regulation of lung inflammation and could provide new therapeutics avenues.

TitreApplicationTitle: Novel mechanisms to control lung inflammation by clearance of air pollutants via lung cells
Keywords-MotsClés: AIR POLLUTANT; ALVEOLAR MACROPHAGE; APOPTOSIS; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; LUNG EPITHELIAL CELL; LUNG INFLAMMATION; PARTICULATE MATTER; PHAGOCYTOSIS; SCAVENGER RECEPTOR; STATIN
Abstract-Résumé: The inhalation of toxic environmental particles (either cigarette smoke or air pollutants) is a worldwide public health problem. Epidemiological studies have shown that exposure to these articulate matter (particles smaller than 10 µm or PM10), are associated with lung and cardiovascular disease. Exposure to ambient PM causes lung inflammation and retention of these particles in the lung is thought to perpetuate lung tissue inflammatory responses, contributing to the development and exacerbation of chronic lung diseases such as asthma and COPD. We have made the novel observation that 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase inhibitors (statins) suppress the PM-induced lung inflammatory response in vivo, which is thought to be due to their anti-inflammatory or pleiotropic effects. We postulate that one of the potential mechanisms of how statins reduce lung inflammation could be through the processing and clearance of PM in the lung. We hypothesize that statins enhance the processing of PM in the lung and promote their removal from lung tissues to regional lymph nodes, thereby reducing both the local (lung) and systemic inflammatory responses induced by air pollution exposure. The main goal of my studies will be to determine the mechanisms how PM are processed by different lung cells, focusing on lung macrophages and how treatment with statins impact these properties. We will also determine the impact of statins on the pro-inflammatory mediators produced by lung cells that phagocytose PM and the downstream effect on the local (lung) and systemic inflammatory responses. These studies will involve an array of in vitro and in vivo studies, using our well established rabbit model of urban PM exposure. We expect these studies will reveal novel pathways that can be targeted in the future with therapies to prevent the respiratory and cardiovascular adverse health effects in high-risk individuals expose to a polluted environment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Child Health in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: The Effect of Social Policies
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILD HEALTH; GLOBAL HEALTH; INTERNATIONAL HEALTH; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH; SOCIAL POLICIES; SOCIOECONOMIC INEQUALITIES
Abstract-Résumé: There is a growing body of evidence demonstrating a social gradient in children's health outcomes within countries: children belonging to higher socioeconomic status (SES) households are in better health compared to their lower SES counterparts. While the current literature has highlighted the importance of SES on child health, there are a limited number of cross-national studies on socioeconomic inequalities in child health outcomes. Moreover, although extant work has demonstrated the impact of social conditions (e.g. lack of education) on health and health equity, evidence on how changes in social policies could be used to improve equity in child health are sparse. Thus, the proposed study aims to address this gap in the literature by assessing the causes of socioeconomic inequalities in two main indicators of children's health, low birth weight (LBW, less than 2.5 kg) and infant mortality (IM), across low-and-middle-income countries (LMICs). In the first stage, we will use information derived from more than 80 LMIC countries to measure and identify factors associated with socioeconomic inequalities in LBW and IM. The second step of this study will focus on the causes of socioeconomic inequalities in ill health. We will assess the effects of social policies (e.g. educational policies and labour market policies) in LMICs on the determinants (e.g. teenage pregnancy, risky birth interval, mother's education and etc.) and levels of socioeconomic inequalities in LBW and IM. The monitoring of socioeconomic inequalities in child health has an important role in gauging progress toward the commitments made by decision makers to reduce inequalities in health. Identifying the factors explaining such inequalities is also essential to implementing effective policies to redress these inequalities. This study, which empirically investigates the effects of social policies on child health, will also help to identify policy levers for improving child health and health equity.

TitreApplicationTitle: The potential of new MRI biomarkers to increase accuracy and cost-effectiveness in osteoarthritis research and care: analysis of longitudinal data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
Keywords-MotsClés: EPIDEMIOLOGY; HIP; IMAGING; KNEE; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; OSTEOARTHRITIS; OUTCOME MEASUREMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Imagine if the trigger for treating heart disease were a heart attack, for treating high blood pressure, a stroke, or for osteoporosis, a fracture. Fortunately, tests exist (e.g., cholesterol, blood pressure, bone density x-ray) that detect disease before symptoms appear, so the devastating outcomes can be prevented. Unfortunately, the same approach doesn't apply to osteoarthritis (OA), the most common arthritis worldwide and leading cause of disability in Canada. The prevalence of OA is projected to double by 2020, due to increases in obesity, sports trauma and longevity.   Detecting OA early is key. Currently x-ray is the most widely used test but is not strongly linked with pain and doesn't show early OA - a critical period for treatment. Conversely MRI is related to pain and shows early disease, but is expensive due to the time to interpret images, and is largely subjective. This has resulted in small research samples with limited power to show important changes, and a sometimes confusing array of information for physicians.  New MRI software has been developed and pilot-tested that provides readings that are semi-automated (rapid) and objective, leading to faster, cheaper, and more accurate diagnosis. However they have not been fully tested in large datasets - a necessary step before widespread research and clinical use.  This research will compare new MRI measures to conventional MRI, testing them for the ability to correlate with a patient's pain and function, identify early disease and progression, and reduce reading times.   Significance: This work will immediately benefit researchers with improved and earlier diagnosis at lower costs leading to larger, more powerful studies. This will strengthen prevention efforts and lead to earlier interventions to prevent disability. It will benefit physicians through development of a single diagnostic score for knee OA (similar to the bone density score for osteoporosis) leading to earlier and better treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: Promoting children's mental health: The effects of a parenting program
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDREN MENTAL HEALTH; PARENTING EDUCATION; PRIMARY PREVENTION; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL DESIGN
Abstract-Résumé: Raising children is an important yet challenging responsibility. While research confirms that parents have a vast impact on their children's adjustment, it has also shown that, to promote children's mental health, parenting must be (1) warm (vs. harsh), (2) structuring (vs. permissive) and (3) autonomy-supportive (vs. controlling). Unfortunately, knowing how to provide all of these key "ingredients" is not always second nature for parents. In addition, available parenting resources are sometimes contradictory, abstract, and rarely target all three key parenting components. Providing the general population with concrete and complete parenting education is essential in improving families' daily lives and in fostering children's mental health. The goal of our research project is to evaluate the impact of a parenting program (i.e., How-to program; Faber and Mazlish, 1980) which aims to teach the three main components of optimal parenting (i.e., warmth, structure, and autonomy support). In a recent study, we offered the program to 93 parents (11 groups). Results from this first study provide support for the efficacy of the program in fostering optimal parenting and in improving children's mental health. The next step is to assess the impact of the How-to parenting program more rigorously. Our goal is to compare participating parents and their children to families on a wait list, who will attend the program at a later time. We also plan to obtain teachers' reports of children's adjustment, to gain a more objective evaluation of children's mental health. Finally, assessments will also take place 6 and 12 months following group participation, to examine whether the program's benefits are maintained over time.  Appropriately evaluating the impact of this promising parenting program is a crucial step toward helping parents foster their children's mental health, thereby contributing to our nation's quality of life.

TitreApplicationTitle: Establishing an International Multiple Sclerosis Falls Prevention Research Network and Trial Protocol
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCIDENTAL FALLS; COLLABORATIVE NETWORK; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; PREVENTION; REHABILITATION; SELF-MANAGEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic and often progressive disease of the central nervous system that causes a wide range of variable and disabling symptoms. Canada has some of the highest rates of MS in the world. People with MS must find ways to manage the functional consequences of MS.  One commonly experienced consequence is an accidental fall.  Falls are experienced by up to 60% of people with MS.  Approximately half of these falls result in an injury requiring medical attention.  Reduced activity, fear of falling, and social isolation are other common outcomes of falls.  Despite the efforts of several individual research teams around the world, success in reducing the number, severity and consequences of falls experienced by people with MS has been limited.  Many teams are engaged in overlapping or complementary studies rather than working in a coordinated way that could accelerate progress.  International collaboration and partnership will enable us to pool our unique areas of expertise to produce evidence about the best ways to reduce falls frequency, severity and consequences for people with MS.  Our collective capacity will be greater than that of any individual team working alone.   Therefore, the purpose of this proposed project is to establish an International MS Fall Prevention Research Network whose members will collaboratively develop research protocols to advance knowledge on falls and falls prevention among people with MS.  A CIHR Planning Grant would provide support for an inaugural meeting for this Network, during which a sustainable infrastructure will be developed, collaborative partnerships built, and a research protocol for a MS falls prevention intervention trial designed.  By working together, our long term goal is to develop and disseminate clinically relevant knowledge that will reduce the frequency, severity and functional consequences of falls experienced by people with MS, in Canada and worldwide.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Biliary Atresia Registry Planning Meeting
Keywords-MotsClés: BILIARY ATRESIA; BILIARY ATRESIA REGISTRY; EVIDENCE BASED RESEARCH; HEPATO-PORTOENTEROSTOMY; NEONATAL CHOLESTASIS; PEDIATRIC LIVER DISEASE; PEDIATRIC LIVER TRANSPLANT
Abstract-Résumé: Biliary atresia is the most important pediatric liver disease. While a rare condition (1:19,000 live births in Canada), biliary atresia is the leading cause of liver failure in the pediatric population and the most common reason why children require a liver transplant.  Early disease recognition and treatment, in the first months of life, is key for optimal survival and best outcomes. Yet previous research in Canada has identified delayed referral, untimely intervention and a lack of standardization of care as problematic. There is need for a national collaborative approach to BA health care delivery, education and research so as to improve the outcomes for the 300-400 affected Canadian children.   This application is to support a one day planning meeting that will bring together an expert team of pediatric liver specialists and pediatric surgeons from every pediatric university hospital center across Canada as well as citizens who have a vested interest in biliary atresia including family members of affected children and other volunteer organizations, to finalize the plans for and implement a Canadian biliary atresia registry (CBAR). The overall goal of CBAR is to generate evidence-based data to optimize standards of BA care in Canada and improve outcomes, and to provide a national collaborative platform for biliary atresia research, education and knowledge translation.

TitreApplicationTitle: Safe to Play: A longitudinal research program to establish best practice in the prevention, early diagnosis and management of sport-related concussion in youth ice hockey players
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDREN; CONCUSSION; INJURY; PREVENTION; SPORT; YOUTH
Abstract-Résumé: Over half a million Canadian youth are registered in ice hockey leagues, and 10-20% of them get a concussion each year. The long-term effects of concussion and the best way to treat it are still unknown, especially in youth. This is a frightening thought for parents, doctors, and athletes. We want to find out: (1) how to stop youth ice hockey players from sustaining a  concussion by understanding the risk factors for concussion; (2) if they get a concussion, how to identify and manage it as soon as possible; and (3) if they get a concussion, how to make sure that they recover fully and prevent re-injury. In this project we will follow 1040 ice hockey players starting in Pee Wee (ages 11-12 years) from Calgary, Alberta, for five years. We will collect information on hockey participation and concussions sustained. Each year the players will undergo baseline assessment including physical, psychological, and functional tests. If players sustain a concussion during the five years of the study, they will be referred to a study sport medicine doctor immediately, and undergo the same testing that they do each year at baseline as well as other tests that monitor the symptoms specific to concussion. This project will help us understand how to reduce the risk of concussion and prolonged symptoms associated with concussion in youth who play ice hockey.  This research will inform best practice to improve the short- and long-term health and quality of life of youth who have suffered concussion.

TitreApplicationTitle: Generating innovation through the use of common data: Improving the diagnosis and treatment of pediatric and adolescent mild traumatic brain injury in Canada.
Keywords-MotsClés: CONCUSSION; DATA MANAGEMENT; EMERGENCY MEDICINE; HEALTH SERVICES; IMAGING; MILD TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY; OUTCOME; PEDIATRICS; REHABILITATION
Abstract-Résumé: The incidence of pediatric traumatic brain injury (TBI) in North America is alarmingly high; studies suggest that mild TBI (mTBI) make up 70-80% of all cases reported. Of particular concern is that not only do many post-concussive symptoms, which manifest as cognitive, physical and behavioural deficits, persist for a subset of patients, but there is very little consensus among clinicians and researchers on how to diagnose and treat mTBI. Furthermore, there is a dearth of research examining the long-lasting effects of sustaining multiple mTBIs. One factor that contributes to this lack of consensus is that many clinicians and researchers use different tools or methods to collect data, thus making comparisons across sites challenging. Given this, we have assembled a team of nationally and internationally distinguished clinician scientists, researchers, and knowledge users from across Canada, whose innovative research programs and clinical initiatives have had a significant impact on the field of pediatric mTBI. We propose to create a comprehensive, flexible and sustainable data management system that will serve to significantly advance clinical care via amalgamated and accessible research evidence. The goal of this mTBI Team Grant is to create a culture of national collaboration, data collection and rapid clinical uptake of innovation in discovery. Our overall goal is to enhance our ability to conduct multi-centre research and provide evidence-based care across Canada that will assist in diagnoses and treatment of pediatric mTBI.

TitreApplicationTitle: Predicting Persistent Postconcussive Problems in Pediatrics (5P)
Keywords-MotsClés: CLINICAL PREDICTION RULE; CONCUSSION; EMERGENCY; EPIDEMIOLOGY; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PEDIATRIC; PERSISTENT POSTCONCUSSIVE SYMPTOMS; TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY
Abstract-Résumé: Concussion, a mild traumatic injury common in children and adolescents, is a complex pathophysiological process affecting the brain.  The lay press is inundated with reports of tragic consequences of concussion, and children are not immune.  Persistent postconcussive symptoms (PCS) is defined as the persistence of somatic, cognitive, physical, psychological or behavioural changes lasting more than one month following injury.  PCS significantly impacts children and their family's quality of life through school absenteeism, depressed mood and loss of activities.  Validated, easy-to-use prognosticators do not exist for clinicians to identify children at highest risk for PCS.  As a result, physicians cannot accurately inform children and parents if they should expect longer symptoms, nor initiate pharmacotherapy or other management to reduce the occurrence or severity of PCS.  The objective of our research is to derive and validate a clinical prediction rule for the development of PCS in children and adolescents presenting to the emergency department (ED) following acute head injury.  We have 3 specific aims: (1) determine PCS prevalence at one-month follow-up in children aged 5-17 who sustain a concussion, (2) derive a rule to predict PCS from variables in the history and physical examination, and (3) assess the accuracy, reliability and acceptability of the prediction rule in a subsequent cohort.  Using a prospective, multicentre study across 10 large Canadian pediatric EDs, we will recruit the largest prospective epidemiological cohort of children with concussions in the literature.  This work will provide rigorous evidence to determine PCS prevalence in children and its impact on quality of life.  The results of this study will enable clinicians to identify children at highest risk for PCS, optimize treatment and provide families with realistic anticipatory guidance, and establish a strong and vital evidence base to advance concussion research.

TitreApplicationTitle: "NeuroCare" as Innovation in Intervention: A Neurophysiological Approach to Determine Readiness for Return to Activity
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENTS; INJURY MANAGEMENT; MILD TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY; NEUROIMAGING; NEUROPHYSIOLOGY; OUTCOME; REHABILITATION; RETURN TO ACTIVITY; SPORTS-RELATED CONCUSSION
Abstract-Résumé: To date, there are major gaps in our knowledge about how to best manage the physical and cognitive demands associated with returning adolescents to activity following mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI). Returning to activities prior to the brain healing from its injury may result in delayed recovery or the increased risk for more serious brain injury. One approach to further inform when the brain and body are ready to reengage in activity may be monitoring neurophysiological parameters, or how the brain and related nervous tissues have recovered after a mTBI (are they operating they way that they should). Heart rate variability (HRV) is a non-invasive measurement of neurophysiological function that when used with adolescents with mTBI may provide insight into when the brain and body are ready to return to activity. The initial objective of this project is to develop the NeuroCare approach which involves combining HRV with other clinical measures typically used to assess recovery from mTBI in children and youth.  In the second phase of the project, smart phone technology required to deliver NeuroCare will be developed in collaboration with end users.  The usefulness of this technology to help with clinical decision making will be determined in Phase 3.  Ultimately this project aims to create a wearable device (NeuroCare) that can let children and youth, their parents and treating clinicians know when it is safe for them to take part in activities and when it is better to continue to rest their brain and body. The techniques proposed in this project are feasible, accessible and have high potential to be used in clinical practice. The ultimate goal is that this innovative approach will optimize clinical decision-making, educate health care professionals and improve the health outcomes for adolescents recovering from mTBI across Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: A Novel Class of Drug Treatment Against Chronic Constipation in Spinal Cord-Injured People
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTONOMIC FUNCTION; BOWEL PROBLEMS; CONSTIPATION; DRUG TREATMENT; SPINAL CORD INJURY
Abstract-Résumé: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating condition leading to immediate and irreversible paralysis below injury level. Patients with SCI suffer also from severe health problems including bladder and bowel dysfunctions. Although, some approaches or devices are currently used to treat occasional constipation in the general population, those same approaches are generally considered as inefficient or unsafe when chronically used against chronic constipation. We obtained evidence suggesting that some unsuspected classes of molecules could be used to trigger episodes of defecation in SCI patients. We propose experiments that will enable the selection of the best molecule(s)among them. This may pave the way to a novel class of pills specifically designed to safely and efficiently treat chronic constipation in SCI patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: WaSH and Health: A Different Dialogue - Changing Evidence and Evidence for Change in Rural Communities
Keywords-MotsClés: ABORIGINAL; DRINKING WATER; EVIDENCE AND EVIDENCE BASE; EXPERIENTIAL EXCHANGE; GAPS AND OPPORTUNITIES; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION AND MOBILIZATION; MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH; PARTICIPATORY; SANITATION; TRANS-SECTORAL; TRANSDISCIPLINARY; TRANSNATIONAL
Abstract-Résumé: In 2010, the United Nations declared access to water and sanitation a human right. Despite this declaration, 780 million people remain without access to improved sources of drinking water, with 653 million of them living in rural areas; and 2.5 billion are still without improved sanitation. WaSH (water supply, sanitation and hygiene) problems are especially acute in low and middle income countries (LMICs), which often lack the financial, human, and infrastructure resources to deal with the problems of providing enough drinking water of sufficient quality and appropriate sanitation/wastewater treatment alternatives. WaSH access has direct impacts on health. Poor water and sanitation can lead to several common health problems in vulnerable populations that can be life threatening and/or chronically debilitating. In high income countries (HICs), rural communities often experience parallel difficulties. In 2008 more than 1700 boil water advisories were in effect across Canada and as of December 31st, 2012 there were 117 First Nation communities under a Drinking Water Advisory. Moreover, Aboriginal populations are reported to have lower life expectancy and higher disease burdens than the general Canadian population. There is a need, both in Canada and globally, to address the problem of inadequate WaSH in rural, remote and otherwise marginalized communities to improve health and well-being. These complex problems require a concerted trans-sectoral and transnational response, employing integrated transdisciplinary approaches. The proposed event will bring together water and health experts from S.E. Asia, Africa and Canada to explore a different and transformative approach to integrating research, policy and practice as it applies to the WaSH crisis. The ultimate goal of the event is to develop a network of researchers, practitioners and policy makers to address what has become a "wicked" problem.

TitreApplicationTitle: Prognostic gene signature for stage I lung adenocarcinoma
Keywords-MotsClés: COMMERCIALIZATION STRATEGY; GENE EXPRESSION; INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY PROTECTION; LUNG CANCER; MARKET; NON-TUMOR LUNG TISSUES; PATENT; PROGNOSIS; QPCR; SOCIO-ECONOMIC BENEFITS
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths and is associated with a poor prognosis. Surgery remains the first line of treatment for a low stage non-small cell carcinoma (NSCLC). However, a significant percentage of these patients with low stage disease will eventually die after a relapse of their cancer. Prognostic factors for selecting patients for adjuvant chemotherapy following resection of a NSCLC is an urgent and unmet medical need. We aim at identifying prognostic gene expression signatures to predict relapse-free and overall survival. The original discovery made in this project was achieved using data from an ongoing genomic research program on lung diseases. Briefly, confirmed cases of NSCLC underwent lung resection at the Institut universitaire de cardiologie et de pneumologie de Quebec. A non-tumor lung sample from each patient was harvested and analyzed using a whole-genome gene expression array. Clinical endpoints were also obtained including follow-up time, disease-free interval and survival. Analyses were carried out to identify genes that correlated with survival. A panel of genes was found to stratify patients in the high- or low-risk groups. A quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) assay was developed for near-term clinical application. The goal of this project is to validate this new qPCR test in an independent set of samples. Ultimately, we aim to have a new genetic test that will guide adjuvant chemotherapy following lung resection for patients with a low stage NSCLC and implement this test in standard clinical care. The genetic test will be developed into a marketable application to optimize the management and treatment of patients with lung cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Canadian Guidelines for Determining Medical Fitness to Operate Motor Vehicles
Keywords-MotsClés: AGREE GUIDELINES; KNOWLEDGE SYNTHESIS; MEDICAL PRACTICE GUIDELINES; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Background- The Canadian Medical Association's CMA Driver's Guide-  Determining Medical Fitness to Operate Motor Vehicles was published in its 8th edition in December 2012.  The publication is a document used by physicians across Canada to guide decision-making about assessing the impact of patients' medical conditions and treatments on driving abilities, advising patients of the risks, and reporting to transportation authorities.  The publication however has some significant limitations related to lack of strictness in gathering information, input from key parties, external review and procedure for updating.   Aim- The purpose of the present grant is to bring together the authors of the guidelines, as well as stakeholders from physician and government transportation groups, with a goal of planning to substantially strengthen upcoming editions of the CMA Driver's Guide.  Research Plan- Four teleconferences and a two-day meeting in Ottawa will be held with the authors of the Canadian guidelines and representatives of the Canadian Medical Association, the Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators / Transport Canada as well as international collaborators.  The purpose of these teleconferences and meeting is to develop a clear action plan that addresses the limitations of the current CMA Driver's Guide.  Specifically a plan will be made to form working groups, review current knowledge, foster collaboration between physicians and transportation authorities, and develop a procedure to update the driving guidelines over time.  Outcomes- By the end of the planning grant, working groups will be in place, collaborations between physicians and transportation authorities will be established, and reports related to the quality of the existing guidelines and a plan for improving the next edition of the Driver's Guide will be prepared.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cells lines for screening GPCR/Nav signaling compound
Keywords-MotsClés: DRUG SCREENING; GPCR ARRESTIN MEDIATED SIGNALING; VOLTAGE GATED SODIUM CHANNELS
Abstract-Résumé: The focus of research covered in this Proof Of Principal - Phase I application is the generation and validation of new cellular models that will be used for drug discovery. These new transgenic cell lines will be the cornerstones for the further development and commercialization of rapid screenning protocols of chemical libraries (hundreds of thousand compounds). We previously discovered that the physical association of a dopamine receptor with a membrane channel having specificity to sodium ions shift all the signaling output of the receptor toward molecules that have been shown to be targeted by mood stabilizers, and thus important for behaviors regulation. To date, this cellular model is unique, and will be usefull for identification and selection of new highly selective molecules with minimal unwanted side effects for the treatment of depression, dipolar disorder and schyzophrenia. We are now interested in the development of other cellular models expressing different membrane receptors and sodium channels. Seven different cell lines will be develop, each one containing a receptor specific to neurotransmitters dopamine or serotonin along with one of the three ionic channels studied, all specific to sodium ions. These cell lines will be first tested for confirmation of the signaling mechanism modulation. Our second objective will be to validate the use of these cellular models with technologies that allowed a researcher to quickly conduct millions of chemical, genetic or pharmacological tests, named high throughput screening (HTS). Two HTS technologies were selected, the AlphaScreen SureFire will allow us to easily monitored the receptor activity, thus confirming or not the shift of the signaling output of the receptor. The second technology is the Bioluminescence Energy Transfer (BRET) will allow the possibility to identify new compounds that disturb the physical interaction between the receptor and the channel.

Keywords-MotsClés: MULTIDRUG RESISTANCE; PLATINUM DRUG; REFRACTORY BREAST CANCER ON CHEST WALL; THERMOSENSITIVE LIPOSOME
Abstract-Résumé: Recurrent breast cancer on chest wall is a difficult to treat disease with no standard of care. This disease occurs in 5-45% of women after mastectomy, and is often bleeding, painful, unsightly, and tedious to attend. It also creates tremendous mental distress of having visible disease, affecting the patients' quality of life. Surgical removal is seldom possible, and radiation and chemotherapy alone are usually not effective with failure rates between 30% and 55%. Enhancing local control of the chest wall tumors increases patient's survival if no distant spreads, and improves patients' quality of life. Dr. Li is developing a drug delivery technology using heat at the fever range (39-42°C) to guide and focus the dose of an anticancer drug in tumors, thereby enhancing the treatment and reducing the side effects of chemotherapy. This technology is particularly useful for locally advanced diseases, and is expected to enhance the treatment of refractory breast cancer at the chest wall.

Keywords-MotsClés: APPLICABILITY; GUIDELINE DEVELOPMENT; HEALTH EQUITY; LOW AND MIDDLE INCOME COUNTRIES; REPORTING GUIDELINES; RESEARCH METHODOLOGY; SYSTEMATIC REVIEWS
Abstract-Résumé: Systematic reviews are the pillars for synthesizing current knowledge and guiding new research. Reporting guidelines improve the impact of research by providing a specific framework of recommended items to report in order to ensure transparency and completeness of reporting. These allow readers to fully evaluate the quality of the review and make better judgments on the applicability of research findings. PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta Analyses)is the current gold standard of systematic review reporting. We have developed an equity extension of PRISMA, called PRISMA-E 2012, using explicit consensus methods with international stakeholder input. Wide dissemination and uptake of these reporting guidelines is paramount for ensuring the effects on health equity are considered and reported in both primary studies and in systematic reviews. This dissemination proposal aims to reach key stakeholders to facilitate wider implementation of PRISMA-E 2012 to journal editors, systematic review authors, peer reviewers, and commissioners of systematic reviews.

Abstract-Résumé: The main purpose of this workshop is to identify, in concert with provincial service providers, decision-makers, government and community representatives, concrete and practical solutions to optimize the mental health care services delivered to TBI patients presenting mental health issues. 1)Present our research findings about services currently available for persons with TBI and having mental health problems (i.e. perceptions about the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats of the current provincial health care system in Quebec); 2)Inform participants about existing but limited evidence-based knowledge on TBI and mental health issues based on the literature, while taking into account clinicians' expertise and consumer experiences; 3)Develop an interdisciplinary and multi-sectorial network, strategies and an action plan to optimize health service delivery in the province for persons with a TBI and mental health issues; 4)Create the first provincial network of all persons interested in TBI and mental health issues in order to build collaborative capacity for future endeavors.

TitreApplicationTitle: Prediction of successful sperm retrieval in patients with non-obstructive azoospermia using a panel of protein biomarkers measured in seminal plasma
Keywords-MotsClés: AZOOSPERMIA; BIOMARKERS; COMMERICALIZATION; INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY; MALE INFERTILITY; MULTIPLE-REACTION-MONITORING ASSAY; OBSTRUCTION; PROTEOMICS; SEMEN; TESTICULAR FAILURE
Abstract-Résumé: Close to 15% of men with infertility have no sperm in the semen due to testicular failure (the men may have no sperm production or may produce small amounts of sperm). Close to 50% of these men may have a small amount of sperm being produced within the testis. Until recently, these men had no hope of having biologically related children. With the revolution in technology, we now are able to extract sperm from the testis (this is an extensive micro-surgical procedure which may take hours to perform) in approximately 50% of the men with testicular failure, and subsequently use the sperm in an in vitro fertilization program to produce a pregnancy. Literally thousands of these procedures have been performed worldwide.   The goal of this project is to identify markers in the semen which will determine, without needing surgery, which of these men with testicular failure have sperm within the testis. We have identified a total of 18 proteins in the semen which are markers to differentiate sperm production from non-sperm production for men with testicular failure. We now propose to test these 18 proteins in the semen of a total of 210 men with normal fertility and testicular failure to find the most accurate markers for sperm production. Each one of the men with testicular failure has had surgery to confirm that he either does or does not produce sperm. We will then choose 2-3 markers (selected from the 18) which best identifies sperm, to be used for the commercial test.   An accurate, non-invasive marker for sperm production would allow us to predict which men with testicular failure are producing sperm. This should reduce the need for surgery and increase the yield if the surgery is performed. As can be seen from the numbers of men with infertility, there is the potential for a high demand for this type of test.

TitreApplicationTitle: Initiating a national quality agenda in hepato-pancreato-biliary surgery: How should we improve the processes of surgical care?
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER SURGERY; COLORECTAL DISEASE; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; LIVER DISEASE; PANCREATIC DISEASE; QUALITY IMPROVEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer is responsible for over 75,000 deaths annually. Liver and pancreatic cancers are among those with the worst prognosis. Surgery is the best treatment option, but hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) surgery is complex, with significant potential for perioperative morbidity and mortality. Complications following surgery have a negative impact on quality of life and survival. Quality improvement (QI) may be achieved by optimizing the processes involved in care delivery. A variety of surgical process improvement tools (SPITs) have been developed, but none are currently in routine clinical use. The aim of this project is to disseminate emerging knowledge in surgical QI to initiate a Canadian quality agenda in the area of HPB cancer surgery.We propose a knowledge exchange workshop that will: 1. Disseminate our research findings in the area of SPITs; 2. Solicit input to establish priority areas that should be targeted for QI; 3. Initiate a national quality agenda in HPB surgery.  Knowledge end users involved in HPB surgery and QI from across Canada will be invited to participate in a nominal group workshop. The agenda will include a presentation/review of the results of our research on SPITs, including a clinical pathway tool, as well as group identification and ranking of key concepts/ themes/tools that should be included in a quality agenda. Participants will deliberate on new knowledge presented and rank priority areas that should be addressed in a national quality agenda according to relevance, feasibility and impact. Data will be collected with a ranking questionnaire and themes will be extracted through qualitative analysis. A post-workshop survey will be used to consolidate results and share outcomes. Knowledge exchange will occur between researchers and participants during the workshop. We will use the recommendations generated at the workshop to establish a national quality agenda for HPB surgery and to guide the development of future QI interventions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Bringing Stillbirth Out of the Shadows: Workshop/Meeting for Bereaved Parents
Keywords-MotsClés: BEREAVEMENT CARE; FAMILIES; HEALTH PROFESSIONALS; PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH; QUALITATIVE; STILLBIRTH
Abstract-Résumé: Despite 2.6 million stillbirths worldwide each year and rising local rates in British Columbia, stillbirth remains a stigmatized entity and a neglected public health issue.  Furthermore, the associated grief of those families affected is disenfranchised. As global health institutions and professional organizations start to prioritize the reduction of stigma around stillbirth and ensure the availability of bereavement care, Canada must also make strides in this direction.  The lack of attention to stillbirth in Canada has left health providers serving bereaved families with limited local research to guide their practice. Furthermore, while initiatives to support families affected by pregnancy and infant loss exist in some Canadian cities, these efforts remain localized and without a specific focus on stillbirth.  Following the example of parent groups in other countries who have been successful in effecting comprehensive change in stillbirth research and bereavement care, Still Life Canada: Stillbirth and Neonatal Death Education, Research and Support Society (SLC), founded by a group of bereaved families, is committed to improving support for those affected by stillbirth in Canada not only through education, but also through promoting stillbirth research. Therefore, in collaboration with SLC, a workshop/meeting is planned that will create a safe place for bereaved parents to gather, support each other, share stories, and prioritize common themes with the research team and frontline health care professionals.  The outcomes of this gathering will be used to guide bereavement programs, education of providers, policy and future research.  Although the workshop/meeting will initially focus on attendees from British Columbia, the findings will be disseminated not just provincially, but also to interested and invested stakeholders nationally at a subsequent meeting with health care professionals, educators, researchers, policy makers and community groups.

TitreApplicationTitle: Intravesical Docetaxel Formulation for the Treatment of Ta/T1 Stage Bladder Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: ADVANCED FORMULATION; ANTICANCER DRUGS; BLADDER CANCER; DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS; HYPERBRANCHED POLYMERS; INTRAVESICAL CHEMOTHERAPY; MUCOADHESION; NANOPARTICLES; SAFETY AND TOXICOLOGY; TISSUE PENETRATION AND DISTRIBUTION
Abstract-Résumé: Bladder cancer is the seventh most common cancer worldwide, the fourth most prevalent cancer in Canada in men, twelfth in women, and has an overall mortality rate of 20 percent. It has the highest lifetime treatment cost per patient of any cancer and yet despite the drivers of cost, high mortality and morbidity, no new therapies have emerged in the past few decades with numerous clinical trials showing no improvement over mitomycin C and Bacillus Calmette Guerin (BCG), the current standard of care.  Microtubules are one of the most successful targets in cancer therapy and the recent phase I trial of intravesical docetaxel for the treatment of nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer, refractory to BCG, has shown this to be a promising agent. However, conventional formulations are maintained in the bladder for only two hours and drug exposure rarely lasts beyond the first voiding of urine, resulting in low drug uptake into bladder tissues. There is a clear unmet need for formulations that improve the residence time and penetration of intravesical agents.  We have developed a novel polymeric drug delivery platform for the intravesical delivery of docetaxel employing Hyperbranched Polyglycerol (HPG) drug delivery technology. It has demonstrated superior efficacy in proof of concept studies over the commercial Taxotere formulation and provides enhanced drug retention and tissue penetration characteristics in in vivo and ex vivo studies.  The aim of this project is to complete early stage preclinical development of a novel therapy for bladder cancer enabling our funding partner, CDRD Ventures Inc. (CVI) to create a private company to move the technology towards clinical studies. A Canadian spinoff company translating UBC and CDRD IP will improve the health of Canadians and others worldwide, while bringing further international recognition and investment to both Canadian innovation and the Canadian biotechnology industry.

Prior to this invention it was possible to place an implant in the intramedullary (interior) part of straight long bones such as the femur and tibia but not into curved bones. As countries with large populations (e.g. China) experience economic growth and vehicles on their roads increase in speed and size, the incidence of these fractures and the ability to afford surgical treatment will grow. Older people with these injuries are often treated non-operatively but can have complications related to hospitalization and bed rest. TitreApplicationTitle: Device for recanalization of peripheral and coronary arteries
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC TOTAL OCCLUSION; GUIDEWIRES; PERCUTANEOUS INTERVENTION; RECANALIZATION; SHOCK WAVES
Abstract-Résumé: The project aims at performing validations of a novel method used to recanalize obstructed peripheral and coronary arteries such as chronic total occlusions (CTOs). This project is directed at a first demonstration of the efficacy, safety and clinical applicability of the method. The project will involve a team of engineers from the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Universite de Sherbrooke (UdeS) and cardiologists from the Sherbrooke University Hospital (CHUS) and the Montreal Heart Institute (ICM).  The proposed system offers a radically different solution to the problem of crossing chronic total occlusions as it offers a new energy source for crossing occlusions, namely high-amplitude mechanical waves such a shock waves, which have been shown to be safe and effective in other medical contexts such as urology and orthopaedics. As well, with the proposed system the energy deposition device is the wire itself, which can be engineered to have similar physical and mechanical properties as existing guidewires, and not some bulky catheter that is difficult to maneuver to the occlusion.

TitreApplicationTitle: 2013 Canadian Cancer Research Conference
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER RESEARCH; COMMUNITY FORUM; CONFERENCE; WORKSHOPS
Abstract-Résumé: The 2013 Canadian Cancer Research Conference (CCRC) will be held November 3-6 in Toronto. Hosted by the Canadian Cancer Research Alliance (CCRA), an alliance of 33 research funding agencies, the CCRC is unique in Canada as it is the only national conference devoted to the entire spectrum of cancer research, spanning basic discovery research to palliation, policy, and health economics research. Attended by researchers, practitioners, and policy makers, a key goal of the conference is to showcase research that may have an impact on or influence other research areas, providers, and policy makers. Moreover, by exposing researchers to the views of policy makers and the process of adoption of research into practice, research itself can be affected. Building on the success of the first CCRC held in 2011, the 2013 conference program has been expanded to include an embedded program on developing careers in cancer research as well as a new opportunity to present late-breaking research, in addition to a rich scientific program of 8 plenary sessions, 20 symposia, and 600 poster presentations. To complement the scientific agenda, there will be a "Community Forum" designed to showcase selected areas of cancer research to a lay audience. This will also provide an opportunity for researchers and the general public to informally interact as part of the structure of the Forum. The CCRC is funded through a combination of registration fees (40%) and contributions (60%) from CCRA member organizations and other organizations engaged in cancer research, cancer care, and control. We are anticipating approximately 1,200 registrants at the CCRC. With this funding application we are requesting $25,000 to support the CCRC. These funds, representing about 4% of the total conference budget, will be directed to speakers' travel and accommodation and support of scientific program planning activities.

TitreApplicationTitle: Uniting Autism, Aging and Disability Researchers: A Discussion of the Methodological and Clinical Issues in the Development of a Screening Tool to Detect Autism in Later Life
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTISM; MEASUREMENT; OLDER ADULTS; QUESTIONNAIRES; RELIABILITY; VALIDITY
Abstract-Résumé: Autism is a lifelong condition, despite the fact that it is most often associated with childhood. However, there is very little research examining older adults, aged 50 and over, with an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). There is currently no tested measure to identify ASDs among older adults, but yet there is a need for one. Research suggests that referrals for ASD assessments in adulthood are in fact occurring. They are often the result of individuals experiencing a pattern of difficulties in relationships and employment, or a result of parents or relatives of recently diagnosed children, self-referring. Studies also suggest that adults with an ASD may have either gone undiagnosed in childhood, or were misdiagnosed, due to the difficulty in identifying ASDs from other disorders. The first step needed to establish a research agenda in this new area of research, is to be able to identify ASDs in older adults. We propose a 1 ½ day meeting at McMaster Innovation Park, Hamilton, ON, on November 14th to 15th, 2013 to address the following objectives: 1) to create a networking opportunity that brings together researchers from a range of disciplines, settings, and countries, to discuss for the first time, the issues related to aging with an Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); 2) to identify, discuss, and resolve key research and clinical issues related to the development and testing of a screening tool for ASDs in later life and; 3) to understand our current knowledge on Autism and aging through brief presentations from meeting participants from each of Canada, the Unites States, and the UK, and to discuss an action plan to move a research agenda on Autism and aging forward.

TitreApplicationTitle: New dual-mode antiviral agents for the treatment of hepatitis C virus infection
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIVIRAL AGENTS; HEPATITIS C VIRUS; INNATE IMMUNITY; TREATMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Hepatitis C virus (HCV), leads to chronic infections in people resulting in serious and permanent liver damage.  Late stage disease due to this devastating virus is the leading cause of liver transplantation in North America.  The disease afflicts 180 million people worldwide, including 1-2 % of the North American population.  There is no vaccine or immunotherapy currently available for the treatment of HCV infection.  A combination of pegylated alpha-interferon, ribavirin and protease inhibitor is being used to treat HCV infected patients, but this treatment is not adequate, only works in a fraction of patients, and has serious side effects associated with it.  Therefore, there is a tremendous need to develop new therapeutic approaches against this dreadful virus.  The focus of this research project is to study new treatment for hepatitis C virus.  In our studies, we have identified promising agents which work on virus specific targets and host defense mechanisms and are non-toxic. In the proposed project, we will investigate their detailed antiviral properties using cell culture and mouse models and perform important preclinical studies.  This project will advance our technology and the development of new drug candidates for the treatment of HCV patients worldwide.

TitreApplicationTitle: 7th International Biocuration Conference (Biocuration 2014). Bridging disciplines: bioinformatics and medical informatics to advance clinical research.

Abstract-Résumé: With the explosion of scientific data generated by the life science research community, databases have become the standard way of managing and processing large amounts of information. Biocuration is essential in examining how raw data from genome sequencing, gene and protein expression profiling projects can be used to generate knowledge about gene and protein function and structure, molecular evolution, drug targets and disease mechanisms. The International Society of Biocuration (ISB) and the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research (OICR) are hosting 7th International Biocuration Conference (Biocuration 2014) in Toronto, on April 6-9, 2014. The overarching goal of the Biocuration 2014 Conference is to connect biocuration groups worldwide that collect all manner of biological information pertaining to microorganisms, animals and humans, with researchers and clinicians studying human disease such as cancer, cardiovascular disease and diabetes. The conference is designed to maximize interactions, and to provide a dynamic environment for the exchange of ideas, results, and to create new collaborations. The conference will include three plenary talks featuring established scientists within the biocuration community and lead projects that relying upon curated data types. Amongst the sessions and workshops, will be time devoted to finding synergies between bioinformatics and medical informatics, which will promote knowledge translation, and the dissemination and integration of biological and clinical research data. These areas are critical for the development of a robust and engaged group of biocurators that will take on the next generation of challenges in biological and clinical research.

TitreApplicationTitle: Chimeric Oncolytic Virus for Brain Cancer Treatment
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOTHERAPEUTICS; BRAIN CANCER; CANCER THERAPY; COMMERCIALIZATION; MANUFACTURING; ONCOLYTIC VIRUS; PROCESS DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Effective brain cancer therapies remain a critically unmet need in human healthcare.  Advances in surgical, radiation and chemotherapeutic treatments have done little to change patients' outcomes in the past 30 years.  Clearly, new approaches are needed if we are to control these diseases.  Many groups worldwide have been exploring the use of viruses that can selectively replicate in and kill tumour cells without harming normal cells; these so called "Oncolytic Viruses" (OV) have shown some remarkable results in late stage clinical trials.  Despite this clinical success most OVs are inherently neurotoxic and are not safe to use with brain cancer.  Recently, we have discovered a new OV variant (a Chimeric Maraba virus) that is non-neurotoxic when injected directly into the brain of mice and that is also effective in a rodent model of brain cancer in vivo and human glioblastoma tumour cells in vitro.  A current impediment to further clinical development of this virus therapy is a lack of safety/toxicity data in non-human primates (NHP).  The work proposed in this grant is primarily directed at clearing this road block by testing a small scale manufactured lot of Chimeric Maraba virus in a preliminary NHP safety study.  A secondary goal of the grant is to expand the Intellectual Property protection to other similar but novel Chimeric Maraba candidates.  Our overarching goal with this proposal is to de-risk this platform sufficiently to engage a partner for further clinical development.  If successful in these studies and in partnering as described, we expect to conduct the necessary pre-clinical testing and initiate clinical trials within 3 years.

TitreApplicationTitle: HealtheSteps: Strategies to Engage Rural Canadian Men in Chronic Disease Prevention and Management Programs
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT; COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT; EXERCISE; HEALTHY EATING; KNOWLEDGE BROKER; MENS HEALTH; QUALITATIVE METHODS
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic disease (CD) is a growing epidemic in Canada. Canadian men, especially those living in rural/remote regions, are at risk for a number of lifestyle-related CDs including type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, heart disease, stroke and some forms of cancer. CDs share many risk factors including overweight, physical inactivity, unhealthy diet, and smoking. Poor health outcomes suggest that Canadian men continue to fall short in adopting healthy lifestyles that could prevent CD. There are also alarming discrepancies in CD burden by geography, whereby rural residence increases the risk of developing CD and results in poorer outcomes. The HealtheSteps community-based program of research and knowledge translation offers lifestyle prescriptions (exercise, healthy eating), coaching, and technology supports to help Canadians become more physically active, eat better, and improve their health. Our research shows that those at risk for type 2 diabetes who take part in the HealtheSteps program increase their step counts, lose weight, lower their blood pressure and cholesterol, and improve their overall sense of well-being. As we implement the HealtheSteps program in community settings, we observe that more than 90% of participants are women, and our community partners report challenges engaging men in group and individual health programs. Our preliminary research scan identified a dearth of studies that focus on men's involvement in chronic disease prevention and management (CDPM) initiatives. There are a few examples of successful men's health initiatives such as the Shed Project in Australia and the 40+ Men's Health Initiative in Finland. Popular campaigns such as Movember show promise in improving awareness of men's health, but there is still a gap in shifting from awareness to action. A better understanding of what would support men's participation in CDPM programs will lead to the implementation of novel, sustainable strategies to improve the health of Canadian men.

TitreApplicationTitle: Integrated Surgical Lighting and Navigation System
Keywords-MotsClés: CADAVERIC STUDY; MEDICAL IMAGING; SPINAL SURGERY; SURGICAL NAVIGATION; SYSTEM INTEGRATION; TOPOLOGY; TREATMENT PLANNING; VERTEBRAL BODY
Abstract-Résumé: In North America, approximately 60-80 % of the population suffers from back pain at some stage of their lives. For a significant number of patients suffering from back pain, even basic daily activities become impossible and spinal surgery (involving implanted screws or other hardware placement) may become necessary.    However, surgery carries its own risks such as misplaced screws leading to a wide array of complications.  Surgical navigation has the potential to reduce these risks through accurate guidance. Existing commercial surgical navigation systems have the ability to provide the underlying structure of a vertebra, but is only used by 10% of spine surgeons. However, present technologies require the attachment of reference frames which suffer from (a) lengthy set-up, (b) error from movement of reference frame, (c) error from spine movement between preoperative imaging and patient positioning for surgery. Our solution uses continuous intraoperative optical imaging with a specialized lighting scheme and redundant camera systems to accurately guide the placement of orthopedic implants and to track the motion of surgical targets, without the use of cumbersome reference frames. The innovative technology developed in this proposal will also limit exposure to harmful radiation on both the patient and the health care team.  The low-cost high-performance design principles in this project will likely generate production models suitable for export to both developed world and developing countries (the latter currently has no readily available access to advanced surgical navigation platforms).     Finally, from the health care system perspective in the long run, deploying a low-cost real-time surgical navigation system for spinal procedures will potentially provide cost-savings by decreasing surgical time, complication rate, and revision surgeries, which undoubtedly will benefit individual patients in Canada and worldwide.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Programme de bourses postdoctorales Banting CRSNG/CRSH
TitreApplicationTitle: Synthesis of Novel Core/Active-Shell Lanthanide-Doped Upconverting Nanoparticles and their Application in Thermal Imaging for Cancer Diagnosis and Therapeutics
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIMICROBIAL PEPTIDES; CANCER; CATIONIC PEPTIDES; CELLULAR MEMBRANES; COMPUTER SIMULATIONS; DRUG DELIVERY; LIPIDS; MEMBRANE PORES; SIRNA
Abstract-Résumé: The overriding objective of this proposal is to develop a multifunctional nanoparticle (MNP) capable of delivering a diagnostic and therapeutic modality for cancer therapy. In particular, we will focus on the temperature dependent multiphoton excited luminescence for imaging, nanothermometry and phototherapy. In this project, we will synthesize and study the temperature-dependent spectroscopic properties of various multiphoton excited nanoparticles including semiconductor quantum dots, metal nanoparticles, and dielectric lanthanide-doped nanoparticles. We will also explore hybrid systems composed of two more types of nanomaterials with core/shell architecture. Our objective is to obtain a deep understanding of the temperature-dependent luminescence mechanisms of the different nanoparticles to understand their behavior when incorporated into biological systems. Moreover, our plan is to determine the most suitable system for different diagnostic and therapeutic applications (intracellular imaging, thermal imaging, photoheating, nanothermometry, etc.) and subsequently incorporate them into a single nanoplatform to provide diagnostic information and deliver a therapeutic modality. This single platform would be able to heat its local environment while simultaneously relay temperature information, for applications in photothermal cancer treatment. If successful, this project can have significant long-term social implication, particularly in the targeted treatment of cancer. The development of novel imaging probes to locate disease sites and perform site-specific localized therapy, thus minimizing side effects on neighboring tissues or organs, can relieve the suffering of many Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Attosecond Control in Buckminsterfullerene (C60): Towards Attosecond Transistors
Keywords-MotsClés: ATTOSECOND CHEMISTRY; ATTOSECOND DYNAMICS; ATTOSECOND SCIENCE; FEMTOSECOND CHEMISTRY; FULLERENES; LASERS; MOLECULAR DYNAMICS; NANOTECHNOLOGY; ULTRAFAST ELECTRONICS; ULTRAFAST PHOTONICS
Abstract-Résumé: The development of today's telecommunications is based on increasing the speed at which information is transmitted. Recent progress in ultrafast optics shows how femtosecond (fs=1E-15 s.) laser sources are capable of controlling electronic processes with unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution approaching the angstrom (=0.1 nanometer)-attosecond (as=0.001 fs). Indeed, these significant advancements in laser-matter interaction demonstrate that an electronic current is launched in a single atom or molecule following the removal of one electron, a process called ionization. The main properties of the induced ultrafast electron-hole current --oscillation frequency, amplitude and phase-- are controlled by both (1) the electronic structure of the atomic or molecular system interrogated and (2) the properties of the ionizing laser field such as its wavelength and intensity. This original combination is analogous to the conventional transistor controlling charge currents in electronics. Here, however, the alternative current (AC) operates at a extremely high frequency approaching the peta- (1E+15) or even the exahertz (1E+18 Hz), surpassing by many orders of magnitude terahertz (1E+12 Hz) bit rates in state of the art fiber optics optoelectronic devices. In this postdoctoral project, the expertise of the fellow candidate in attosecond laser spectroscopy (Ph. D.) will be combined with cutting edge attosecond technology, recently developed by the host institution (Max-Planck-Institut fur Quantenoptik), to characterize femtosecond electron-hole currents in small molecules. These experiments will be extended to larger molecules, such as buckminsterfullerene (C60), mounted on a chip or thin films, where attosecond nanometer-size surface and volume electron oscillations will be explored. We project integrating and using these currents in real circuits, thereby, pushing the frontiers of laser-matter interaction and developing the emerging field of attosecond electronics.

TitreApplicationTitle: Loop Quantum Gravity and Spinfoam models, a quantum description of space-time?
Keywords-MotsClés: COSMOLOGICAL CONSTANT; DISCRETE GRAVITY; LOOP QUANTUM GRAVITY; NON-COMMUTATIVE GEOMETRY; QUANTUM GRAVITY; QUANTUM GROUP; SEMI-CLASSICAL LIMIT; SPINFOAM MODEL; SPINORS; TENSOR OPERATORS
Abstract-Résumé: Quantum gravity is the quest for a consistent framework describing general relativity and quantum mechanics. My research project aims to understand better the quantum gravity regime as described by the loop quantum gravity (LQG) and spinfoam (SF) frameworks. These frameworks are based on the use of two different quantization techniques applied to general relativity with a zero cosmological constant. The LQG framework arises from the canonical quantization scheme whereas SF models are constructed using the path integral quantization. Both approaches have encountered significant successes. For example, it was shown that there is a notion of quantum of space. More explicitly, the geometric operators such as the area or the volume operators have a discrete spectrum. SF models are promising candidates to describe the transition amplitude between different quantum state of space encoding the notion of quantum space-time. These approaches have also weak points. For instance, LQG and SF models are supposed to be two equivalent ways to describe the quantum gravity regime. However it is not clear how to relate the two approaches and to show properly this equivalence. Also, we know from measurements that there is a non-zero cosmological constant, so a proper physical LQG theory should be constructed to take this into account. My research program presents a number of projects aiming at solving these issues by using a combination of innovative mathematical techniques and physical insights. Once one has in hand a mathematically consistent quantum gravity theory, one has to check explicitly that this theory allows recovering general relativity plus some quantum corrections when we go to the semi-classical regime. This physical consistency analysis is very important. To achieve this, one needs to propose phenomena involving quantum gravitational effects that hopefully can be experimentally verified. I intend to explore this difficult question in the SF models frameworks.

TitreApplicationTitle: Approximation algorithms for quantum problems
Keywords-MotsClés: APPROXIMATION ALGORITHMS; ALGORITHMS AND COMPLEXITY; COMPUTER SCIENCE; HARDNESS OF APPROXIMATION; LOCAL HAMILTONIAN PROBLEM; QUANTUM COMPUTING; QUANTUM CONSTRAINT SATISFACTION; QUANTUM ENTANGLEMENT; QUANTUM MERLIN ARTHUR (QMA)
Abstract-Résumé: The world around us as we perceive it is governed by what are known as the laws of classical mechanics. Yet, if we peer down into tiny systems such as atoms, protons, and electrons, the physical rules which apply change - the world at this level is governed by the laws of quantum mechanics. One of the major challenges for physicists around the world is to study and understand the workings of this tiny world. However, quantum systems are so complex that accomplishing this task in a precise fashion for certain problems is strongly believed to be infeasible with computing devices. Unfortunately, such problems are moreover extremely important, as they are tied to our very understanding of the quantum world around us, and as such, these problems have attempted to be solved for decades by the physics community. In this project, we propose a novel approach to tackling such significant, but difficult quantum problems. Our method is to adopt beautiful tools from theoretical computer science known as approximation algorithms. As suggested by its name, an approximation algorithm allows one to solve a difficult problem only approximately (as opposed to precisely); however, in exchange for giving up this small amount of precision, an approximate solution to the problem can now be computed very quickly. By bringing such tools over to the realm of quantum physics, we are hence proposing an entirely new paradigm for studying very difficult quantum problems, which to date have no exact solutions. As a result, this project promises to bring together the fields of theoretical computer science and quantum physics, while having a significant impact on both.

TitreApplicationTitle: Directly-printable quantum-tuned nanoparticle solar cells
Keywords-MotsClés: ALTERNATIVE ENERGY; NANOTECHNOLOGY,; PHOTONICS; PHOTOVOLTAICS
Abstract-Résumé: In recent years there has been a growing need to develop new manufacturing approaches for the fabrication of photovoltaic devices in order to make them cheaper while simultaneously improving in the power conversion efficiency. Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) are semiconductors only a few nanometres in size that can be used to harvest the entire solar spectrum - including both visible and invisible wavelengths - and convert it into electricity. Unlike current slow and expensive semiconductor processing, CQD films can be fabricated simply, quickly and at low cost from an ink-like solution. Solution-processed CQD solar cells are cost-effective to manufacture and offer the potential for high conversion efficiency (>10%). Here I propose to develop fabrication strategies of CQD films by modifying the surface of the CQDs while in solution in order to enhance photovoltaic performance. The selection of surface passivant, or ligand, and the control of its coverage over each individual CQD enable manipulation of the electrical and optical properties of the final solid-state CQD film. This proposal aims to determine the optimal materials and processing conditions for solution-phase ligand exchanges as well as to identify the benefits and limitations of such a method as a manufacturing approach in CQD solar cell engineering. Importantly, the simple and direct solution phase processing that yields short-ligand passivated CQD films of high optoelectronic quality is expected to open the door to high efficiency CQD photovoltaic devices. More importantly, this research is expected to pave the way for solar cells that can be fabricated on flexible substrates of any size with roll-to-roll processing in the same way newspapers are rapidly printed in mass quantities. The combination of high efficiency and low cost of solution-processed CQD solar cells compared to traditional silicon photovoltaics makes this technology transformative for the Canadian and international energy markets.
