TitreApplicationTitle: Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy and the Risk of Subsequent Cardiovascular Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOGENIC SHOCK; CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOMES; HEALTH OUTCOMES RESEARCH; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION; POPULATION-BASED STUDY
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiogenic shock in patients with acute myocardial infarction accounts for 50-80% of in-hospital deaths.  Current treatment recommendations support the urgent use of revascularization procedures (including percutaneous coronary intervention and coronary artery bypass graft surgery).  Although these recommendations have resulted in lower rates of death, overall rates remain high mainly in patients presenting to hospitals without revascularization facilities.  Inter-hospital transfers present a challenge since many primary care hospitals are not able to effectively stabilize these patients.  However, previous studies have found that transfer patients have similar rates of death compared to patients directly admitted to hospitals with revascularization facilities.  These studies may have however been biased since the majority of transfer patients were younger and presented with less severe disease states.  Given the limitations of previous studies, we propose to examine the trends in treatment and outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock in a real-world setting.  We will use two Quebec databases that include information on hospital admissions and physician and drug claims.  The study population will include all patients admitted with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock from January 1st, 1999 to December 31st, 2009.  Follow-up data will be collected for a minimum of 1 year.  We will use this data to compare in-hospital and long-term outcomes and use of devices, procedures, and medications in patients presenting to hospitals with revascularization facilities versus patients presenting to hospitals without revascularization facilities.

TitreApplicationTitle: Housing and Health-Related Trajectories among Homeless Women Struggling with Mental Illness and Addictions: A Trauma-Informed Perspective
Keywords-MotsClés: CUMULATIVE ABUSE; GENDER AND HEALTH; HOMELESSNESS; HOUSING FIRST; LATENT CLASS ANALYSIS; MENTAL HEALTH AND ADDICTIONS; RECOVERY; TRAUMA; VIOLENCE
Abstract-Résumé: Homeless women with mental illness are a highly vulnerable population struggling with poverty, violence and trauma, and are often disengaged from the current system of care. The realities of homeless women's lives present multiple barriers to the access and uptake of essential services, which can compound health risks and compromise health and mental health outcomes. This is important, as the number of homeless women has increased more than men in the last ten years in Vancouver. This research will explore the impact of violence and trauma among a cohort of homeless women with mental illness. The research will draw from data collected at the Vancouver site of the At Home/Chez Soi National Research Demonstration project - a randomised controlled trial investigating mental health and homelessness over two years, funded by the Mental Health Commission of Canada. Early findings indicate high rates of post-traumatic stress (40%) and partner violence (65%) among the women, and significantly greater incidents of sexual violence and violent victimization. Many women have attributed these experiences as directly related to becoming homeless. Utilising the statistical method of latent cluster analysis, this project will identify patterns of cumulative violence, trauma and abuse among participants, and link to trajectories of homeless women's service utilisation, residential stability and health-related outcomes. It is expected that women with more extensive and severe histories of violence and trauma will be less engaged with essential health care services and supports, resulting in compromised housing, health and mental health outcomes. Given the magnitude of the preventable health and social costs of homelessness, this research will generate gender-specific evidence to inform Canadian housing and health-related policy and address inequities in health among a highly disadvantaged, and currently underserved, group of women.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of sleep-wake circuitry in enabling cognitive flexibility via tuning of cortical signalling variability
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNITIVE FLEXIBILITY; IN-VIVO ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; MICRODIALYSIS; MONOAMINERGIC NEUROTRANSMISSION; SLEEP-WAKE STATE; STATE SPACE ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Quality of life for all human beings depends in part on our natural ability to adjust our behaviour in response to ongoing changes in our environment. This ability is termed cognitive flexibility and its mechanism is poorly understood. A lack of cognitive flexibility is associated with reduced activity in brain systems that are known to promote wakefulness and prevent sleep. Reduced activity in these systems is very common, occurring naturally every evening (i.e., drowsiness) as well as chronically in patients who experience a progressive loss of these systems (eg., Parkinson's disease). This research tests the idea that these brain systems induce and optimize signalling variability in a region of the brain that is important for cognitive flexibility - the prefrontal cortex - thereby permitting flexible adaptation of behaviour. This research also tests whether or not breakdowns in this mechanism are responsible for the loss of cognitive flexibility that accompanies Parkinson's disease and drowsiness. To test these questions, we will use mice that are genetically designed to be missing major parts of the wake producing and sleep preventing systems. In these mice we will measure whole-brain electrical activity as well as activity specifically in the prefrontal cortex. We will identify if changes in brain activity patterns in genetically altered mice missing sleep-wake system components are predictive of lost cognitive flexibility. We will determine if lost cognitive flexibility can be 'cured' by restoring levels of brain chemicals specifically in prefrontal cortex by delivering drugs locally into this region. Identifying the brain regions, chemicals, and activity patterns that allow for flexibility of behaviour is required to develop therapies that restore lost flexibility in patients with neurodegenerative conditions and for shift-workers who need to remain awake and alert during periods of the day when brain systems promoting wakefulness become less active.

TitreApplicationTitle: Promoting Equity in Parental Antenatal Decision Making Support
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTENATAL DIAGNOSIS; COMMUNICATION; CONGENITAL HEART DISEASE; DECISION MAKING; EQUITY; HEALTH CARE RELATIONSHIPS; PARENTAL EXPERIENCE; PREGNANCY AND CHILDBIRTH; QUALITATIVE METHODOLOGIES; SHARED DECISION MAKING
Abstract-Résumé: An antenatal diagnosis of a complex congenital heart defect (CHD), the most common structural congenital malformation, can have crippling effects on the psychological well-being of parents, undermining the future health of parents and child. Emerging research indicates parents who choose to end a pregnancy or pursue complex neonatal treatments following antenatal diagnosis of CHD often face significant mental health concerns. Improving communication and parental decision making support is the most important action health care providers (HCPs) can take to ensure quality and equitable care during this emotionally difficult time. Contextual factors such as an emphasis on efficiency and biomedical concerns in HCP-parent interactions may limit communication and contribute to parental distress and inadequate support. Moreover, HCP-parent interactions that focus on pregnancy or complex treatment options may obscure the broad range of experiences and decisions parents face. In addition, socioeconomic, gender and other differences between HCPs and parents can influence parents' decision making to align with what HCPs view as in the parents' best interests without a detailed discussion of the family's preferences or beliefs. This study seeks to understand the complex communication and decision making dynamics involved when parents receive an antenatal diagnosis of complex CHD in order to improve parental participation, ease parents' distress, and foster equity in decision support. The study will involve a qualitative analysis of in-depth interviews with parents and HCPs, observation of HCP-parent interactions, and review of organizational data. Parents from diverse backgrounds will be recruited including those who continue or end their pregnancy following antenatal diagnosis of CHD. Research findings have the potential to promote equity in decision making support, develop explicit tools for practice, guide clinical training programs, and inform healthcare system policies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Contrôle spectral de la stimulation lumineuse permettant l'ajustement de l'horloge circadienne des policiers patrouilleurs de nuit.
Keywords-MotsClés: CYCLE CIRCADIENS; MELATONINE; PHOTOBIOLOGIE; SANTE ET SECURITE AU TRAVAIL; SOMMEIL; TRAVAIL DE NUIT; VIGILANCE; ELECTROENCEPHALOGRAPHIE A L'EVEIL
Abstract-Résumé: Les troubles du sommeil et la fatigue au travail sont les principaux problemes evoques par les travailleurs de nuit. Le travail de nuit impose a l'organisme un horaire qui va a l'encontre du mecanisme habituel de son horloge biologique. En effet, celle-ci predispose l'humain a etre actif le jour et inactif la nuit. L'horloge biologique etant tres influencee par la lumiere, une solution serait d'inverser le cycle lumiere-obscurite du travailleur. Il est aussi connu que c'est la lumiere bleue qui a le plus d'impact sur l'horloge biologique. Il serait donc interessant d'enrichir de lumiere bleue l'environnement du travailleur de nuit pendant son quart de travail et de couper cette lumiere bleue pendant le jour. Cependant, l'exposition a une illumination de forte intensite la nuit est difficile a appliquer, surtout pour la conduite d'un vehicule motorise. Neanmoins, notre laboratoire a recemment demontre que la lumiere bleue pulsee, malgre sa plus faible intensite lumineuse, est plus efficace sur l'horloge biologique qu'une lumiere forte continue. La lumiere bleue pulsee pourrait alors etre une strategie pour l'adaptation au travail de nuit, tout en etant plus propice a utiliser dans un vehicule. Nous avons egalement valide l'efficacite de lunettes a lentilles orangees a bloquer la lumiere bleue. Nous souhaitons donc tester ce systeme d'illumination couple avec le port des lunettes orangees sur des policiers patrouilleurs de nuit. Les policiers seront exposes a la lumiere bleue pendant leur quart de nuit et porteront les lunettes orangees le jour. Nous prendrons des mesures sur leur horloge biologique avant et apres notre intervention. Nous mesurerons aussi la vigilance et les temps de reaction pendant leur travail et leur sommeil sera enregistre grace a un petit appareil porte au poignet. Ce projet a pour  objectifs d'ameliorer la vigilance/le sommeil et l'adaptation au travail de nuit, ce qui, en somme augmenterait sensiblement la qualite de vie de ces travailleurs.

Keywords-MotsClés: CELL ACTIVATION; CELL TRANSPLANTATION; REGENERATION; RETINAL STEM CELLS
Abstract-Résumé: There are many causes of blindness, and this proposed research offers a solution to the variety of diseases which result in the inability to see.  Blindness may be inherited as in the case of retinitis pigmentosa which affects 1 in 3,500 people worldwide.  Injury leading to retinal detachment is a significant cause of blindness, where complete functional recovery after surgery is often not the case.  Furthermore, diseases such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is currently the leading cause of irreversible blindness, affecting 1 in 20 people over 60 years old.  In all these cases, the main cell type affected is called photoreceptors, which are light detectors that transfer visual information to the brain.  Retinal stem cells have been found to exist in the adult eye, but are not activated even in response to injury.  However, they do possess the ability to give rise to all retinal cell types, including photoreceptors, and therefore may have the potential to treat blindness in humans.  The proposed project will investigate two strategies for retinal regeneration: endogenous stimulation and exogenous transplantation.  Specifically, it will be determined what mechanisms are in place that is keeping human adult retinal stem cells (aRSCs) in a non-activated state.  Once these signals are identified, it will be investigated how to block the signalling in the eye, thereby allowing for the activation of aRSCs and regeneration of the retina.  In parallel, the production of retinal stem cell progeny such as photoreceptors will be optimized so that they can be transplanted and integrated into the eye effectively.

TitreApplicationTitle: An All-in-One Approach to Image and Treat Brain Tumors using Multifunctional Gadolinium Texaphyrin Shell Microbubbles
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN CANCER; CONTRAST AGENTS; IMAGING; RADIOSENSITIZER; THERAPY
Abstract-Résumé: The delivery of imaging and therapy drugs to brain tumors is often limited by the presence of the blood brain barrier, which prevents the diffusion of molecules from the blood into the brain tissue. Small pores can be formed in the blood brain barrier for a short period of time, thereby allowing the passage of molecules to the brain tissue before the pore reseals. Gadolinium texaphyrin has been demonstrated to be both an MRI contrast agent and radiosensitizer for radiation therapy and is non-toxic to humans. This project focuses on the development of gadolinium texaphyrin shell microbubbles to first cross the blood brain barrier by forming pores in blood vessels using ultrasound, and then reach the tumor region to enhance imaging and improve radiation therapy, delivering gadolinium texaphyrin in large quantities. This approach is aimed to develop a new method for treating early stage brain tumors.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of a cell permeable peptide inhibiting the phosphorylation of the Gab proteins in VEGF-induced angiogenic responses in vitro and in vivo
Keywords-MotsClés: ANGIOGENESIS; ANIMAL STUDIES; CANCER; ENDOTHELIAL CELLS; GAB PROTEINS; INHIBITORY PEPTIDE
Abstract-Résumé: Angiogenesis, a process by which new blood vessels are formed, is associated with multiple pathologies and occupies a growing place in cancer research. For tumors, the recruitment and formation of new blood vessels in their vicinity is essential for providing nutriments and oxygen supplies allowing their growth and survival. Moreover, these new tumor-associated blood vessels are ill-structured and highly leaky allowing cell dissemination and the formation of metastases, which is the deadliest process of cancer. Thus, the block of angiogenesis is required to stop tumor growth and dispersal. Our laboratory has identified Gab proteins has important promoters of angiogenesis and, consequently, as an interesting target. The objective of this project is to characterize a novel peptidic inhibitor of Gab proteins and evaluate its efficiency at blocking angiogenesis and tumor growth in cellular and mouse models. This innovative approach will allow the study of a new and potentially important therapeutic target for cancer treatment.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of a novel chemerin receptor, G protein-coupled receptor-1 (GPR1) on adipose tissue function in obesity and inflammation.
Keywords-MotsClés: ADIPOKINE; ADIPOSE FUNCTION; CHEMERIN; CMKLR1; G PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTOR; GLUCOSE HOMEOSTASIS; GPR1; OBESITY; PHARMACOLOGY; SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Currently, almost 60% of Canadian adults are obese or overweight. Obesity puts individuals at increased risk for a number of severe diseases such as type 2 diabetes, heart disease, chronic inflammation, and cancer. It is unclear what role extra fat tissue plays in the development of these diseases and few therapeutic strategies exist for reducing the risk of their development. Researchers now believe that hormone-like proteins called adipokines, which are secreted from fat tissue, become dysregulated in obesity and may underlie disease development. Chemerin is an adipokine that is released into the blood by fat cells and is important in controlling fat development, and regulating energy metabolism in tissues outside of fat. Chemerin exerts its functions by binding to two receptors, CMKLR1 and GPR1. My aim is to determine the changes that occur within fat cells when chemerin binds to these receptors so that we can better understand how chemerin influences the health of fat tissue and overall metabolism. To do this I will determine the levels and signaling of these receptors in the variety of different cells that make up adipose tissue. My research will also examine what happens to adipose tissue, growth, and metabolism in the absence of GPR1 receptors. In the long term, these findings will improve our understanding of how fat cells use chemerin to communicate with other cells  of the body and how this communication affects the health of fat tissue. Understanding the signals within chemerin responsive cells will help identify possible new drug targets for treating obesity and disorders related to obesity such as type 2 diabetes, inflammation, and heart disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Role of Vitamin K and Matrix Gla Protein in the Development of Vascular Calcification in Experimental Chronic Kidney Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE; HYPERTENSION; PULSE WAVE VELOCITY; VASCULAR CALCIFICATION; VASCULAR DYSFUNCTION
Abstract-Résumé: Over 20 million people in North America (including 2 million Canadians) have chronic kidney disease. These individuals die from heart and blood vessel diseases more often than they need dialysis. This is due to hardening of the arteries caused by calcium deposits inside the blood vessel walls which is known as vascular calcification (VC). The calcium deposits damage the vessels, causing them to lose flexibility. This makes them unable to respond to the changing demands of the body. This will eventually lead to heart disease and death. The protein matrix Gla protein (MGP) is a potent inhibitor of VC. Vitamin K is a co-factor in the activation MGP and therefore adequate vitamin K stores are essential to inhibit calcification of the arteries. Population studies have shown that CKD patients develop more severe VC at a much younger age than the rest of the population. To date, the role of vitamin K and MGP have not yet been evaluated in an animal model of CKD. Our laboratory hypothesizes that vitamin K supplementation will slow the progression of CKD-induced VC and the associated changes in vascular properties. Warfarin is an anti-coagulation drug that is used widely in patients, including those with CKD, to prevent thrombosis. It acts by inhibiting vitamin K. Our laboratory hypothesizes that administration of therapeutic doses of warfarin will increase the progression of CKD-induced VC and the associated changes in vascular properties. Discovering the role of vitamin K and MGP carboxylation status in a CKD model will give us a further understanding of VC in CKD patients. This will allow for the development of better treatment for these patients, and a decrease in the morbidity and mortality as well as an increase in their quality of life.

TitreApplicationTitle: The DEPRESsion Screening Data (DEPRESSD) Registry: Using Individual Patient Data Meta-analysis to Generate Valid Estimates of Diagnostic Accuracy
Keywords-MotsClés: ASSESSMENT; DEPRESSION; INDIVIDUAL PATIENT DATA; MENTAL HEALTH; META-ANALYSIS; SCREENING
Abstract-Résumé: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a chronic, disabling condition and it is present in 10-20% of patients with chronic diseases. Routine depression screening has been recommended as a way to improve depression management. However, existing studies have not found that depression screening improves depression outcomes. For depression screening to be successful, depression screening tools must be able to accurately distinguish between patients with and without MDD. Typically, patients who score above a cutoff score on a screening tool are considered likely cases of MDD, whereas those below the cutoff are considered unlikely cases of MDD. Several studies have been conducted to attempt to ascertain optimal cutoff scores that maximize the ability to accurately diagnose MDD across different screening tools. However, these studies have important limitations. For example, many studies are limited by small sample sizes and do not produce precise estimates of diagnostic accuracy. As a result, different studies often generate different optimal cutoff scores for the same screening tool. Furthermore, the information published in studies often varies, making information synthesis across these studies tricky. In order to overcome these problems, Dr. Thombs, has developed a large depression screening data registry to conduct individual patient data (IPD) meta-analyses. IPD meta-analysis involves obtaining original patient data from existing studies and synthesizing the data to obtain unbiased, precise estimates of diagnostic accuracy across all possible cutoff scores. For my doctoral project, I will have access to this registry, which will also allow me to analyze factors that may influence accuracy, such age, sex, and diagnosis. Creating the registry and conducting IPD meta-analyses is a step towards better understanding whether depression screening is an effective approach for improving depression management and, if so, will help to identify the best screening tools to use.

TitreApplicationTitle: BRCA2 and Thymidylate Synthase (TS) in Anti-Cancer Therapy
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTISENSE TECHNOLOGY; BRCA2; FLOW CYTOMETRY; SIRNA; THYMIDYLATE SYNTHASE
Abstract-Résumé: Individuals with BRCA2 mutations are at an increased risk of breast, ovarian, and other cancers because they have a defect in their cells' ability to repair DNA. However, published evidence (for example, references 1 and 2) indicate that patients with mutated BRCA2 respond better to conventional cancer therapy, including drugs which target thymidylate synthase (TS), an enzyme important in DNA synthesis and repair. Cancer cells deficient in DNA repair accumulate mutations at a greater rate than their repair-proficient counterparts, and tend to be more prone to death as a result of those accumulated mutations. The objective of the proposed studies is to determine whether use of antisense or siRNA drugs to reduce or eliminate BRCA2 in human cancer cells will reduce their ability to survive in culture and when grown in host animals; a particular focus will be combination therapy with antisense/siRNA knockdown of TS and simultaneous treatment with anticancer drugs that damage DNA. The biochemical, molecular and immunological mechanisms behind this phenomenon will be explored in order to accelerate the development of this promising and novel therapeutic avenue.  1. A.R. Venkitaraman. Targeting the molecular defect in BRCA-deficient tumors for cancer therapy. Cancer Cell. 2009 Aug 4;16(2):89-90.  2. P.M. Vencken et al. Chemosensitivity and outcome of BRCA1- and BRCA2-associated ovarian cancer patients after first-line chemotherapy compared with sporadic ovarian cancer patients. Ann Oncol. 2011 Jun;22(6):1346-52.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification of the unstable atherosclerotic plaque: from bench to clinical practice
Keywords-MotsClés: ATHEROSCLEROSIS; BIOMEDICAL TECHNOLOGY; CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE; CHOLESTEROL EFFLUX CAPACITY; DIGITAL IMAGE ANALYSIS; GENE EXPRESSION ANALYSIS; MICRO RNA; STROKE; ULTRASOUND IMAGING
Abstract-Résumé: Fatty plaques are build-ups of fat that block arteries. Pieces of fatty plaques in the arteries that feed the brain (carotid arteries) can break off and cause strokes. Strokes cause thousands of deaths each year. So it is important to find out early when the plaques become dangerous and about to break off. However, we only know with certainty if a plaque is dangerous once it is removed surgically and checked under a microscope, or if it already caused a stroke. Many people do not know that they have dangerous plaques ready to cause a stroke! We are interested in examining plaques in the carotid arteries that can cause strokes. New technology is available to us. Using an ultrasound picture of the plaque, a new computer program can tell us if the plaque is dangerous. But this program is new, so we need to confirm that it is useful against something that is well known. What a dangerous plaque looks like on the microscope after it is removed surgically is well known. In this study, we will include people with plaques in their carotid arteries who are about to have surgery to remove their plaques. We will take ultrasound pictures of their plaques before the surgery. We will then run our computer program on the pictures. We will also examine the plaque on the microscope to see how dangerous it looks. Next, we will compare the findings of the microscope and the findings of the computer program, and identify those that match. We will also do a new cholesterol test and see if it is related to the dangerous plaques. This study will find how a dangerous plaque looks on ultrasound, so we will be able to recognize a dangerous plaque on ultrasound when we see it again in people. We will use this new computer program in the future to find out early if a plaque is dangerous and may cause a stroke. This way we will be able to treat patients who have dangerous plaques earlier and more aggressively, to prevent strokes from happening and save lives.

TitreApplicationTitle: Assessing depression treatment in primary care
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE MANAGEMENT; DEPRESSION; ELECTRONIC MEDICAL RECORDS; PATIENT EXPERIENCE OF CARE; PATIENT OUTCOME; PATTERNS OF CARE; PRESCRIBING PRACTICES; PRIMARY HEALTH CARE; REFERRAL PATTERNS; SURVEILLANCE DATA
Abstract-Résumé: One of the most prevalent chronic conditions affecting Canadians today is depression--a debilitating illness that severely impairs cognitive, emotional and social functioning. It costs the Canadian economy $14.4 billion annually in treatment costs and work productivity losses, and causes substantial human suffering that results in family dysfunction and increased mortality risk. Currently, most patients diagnosed with depression seek help and treatment exclusively in primary care, either through family physicians or nurse practitioners. Yet, we know little about the type, duration and outcome of treatments commonly prescribed in the primary health care setting. This PhD research will address this gap in knowledge by investigating how electronic medical records (EMR) can be used to monitor the prevalence of depression; examining the type and range of services commonly prescribed to individuals identified as having depression; and, studying gender differences in treatments and services provided to patients diagnosed with depression. Data for this project will be obtained from the Canadian Primary Care Sentinel Surveillance Network--a Public Health Agency of Canada-funded network tasked to build a chronic illness data library based on EMRs maintained by participating family physicians across Canada. The results of this project will inform and enhance the planning and delivery of depression treatment in the Canadian primary care setting.

TitreApplicationTitle: PilM of the Bacterial Type IV Pill: a Tantalizing Therapeutic Target
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIRETROVIRALS; BIOCHEMISTRY; DRUG RESISTANCE; ENZYMOLOGY; EPIDEMIOLOGY; HIV CURE; HIV/AIDS; HOST-RESTRICTION FACTORS; MOLECULAR GENETICS; VIROLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Regarding current HIV therapy, optimal drug combinations are not always predictable, so causes of treatment failure must be critically evaluated to ensure patient and public health.  Within the past year, a new combination of drugs underwent trials in patients, including the new reverse transcriptase inhibitor, rilpivirine.  Drug resistance causing treatment failure was a serious issue, and the most common cause of drug resistance was simply two mutations termed E138K and M184I.  In previous studies, the M184I mutation was considered to be beneficial; it decreases fidelity and fitness, and the range of cells that HIV can infect.  However, results from our cell-free reverse transcriptase assays hint that the E138K mutation may subvert the beneficial qualities of M184I containing virus, which may yield a more transmittable, virulent, and broadly drug resistant virus.  We propose to assess and compare the fidelity and fitness of E138K and M184I containing viruses to gauge the public health threat this mutational combination may pose.  The unique qualities of the E138K mutation may enable it to preferentially infect the very cells HIV uses to hide during anti-HIV therapy; therefore, we also propose to assess the cell types that virus with E138K can infect.  This work is of immediate clinical relevance, and may be an important step towards curing HIV.

TitreApplicationTitle: Fast Biophotonic Simulations for Clinical Applications
Keywords-MotsClés: AGILE COMPUTING; BIOLUMINESCENCE IMAGING; BIOPHOTONICS; CUSTOM COMPUTING; HEAD AND NECK CANCERS; LIGHT PROPAGATION IN TURBID MEDIA; MONTE CARLO MODELLING; PHOTODYNAMIC THERAPY
Abstract-Résumé: Many novel therapeutic, diagnostic, and research techniques use light. Therapeutic applications depend on producing a desired light distribution within a target tissue, while diagnostics and imaging ascertain the properties and geometry of the volume from which light is transmitted or emitted. The success of all these applications depends critically on the ability to simulate light propagation quickly and accurately. Required computation time is the limiting factor in many cases. This project aims to improve by a factor of 10x or more the speed of such simulations without sacrificing accuracy, an improvement which will render many significant treatment and imaging techniques clinically practical. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) using light-activated drugs to treat cancer is a prime therapeutic example. The procedure's specificity depends on delivering an adequate light dose to cancerous cells while avoiding overexposure of surrounding healthy tissue. Since living tissue scatters light strongly, many millions or billions of photon paths must be simulated to produce an accurate result when planning treatment which is very time-consuming. The demands are compounded by the need to run potentially hundreds of simulations to arrive at an optimized plan. In cases of deep-seated tumours, these requirements limit the clinical utility of PDT. For a diagnostic example, bioluminescence imaging (BLI) is a promising research tool in which cells of interest in animal models are genetically modified to emit light. The growth and spread of the marked cells can then be observed inexpensively and non-invasively via the resulting light distribution on the animal's skin. However, it is necessary to estimate a cell configuration, simulate, and adjust many times to discover the anatomical structure that caused a given image. Success would enable PDT for a broader range of cancers clinically, make BLI more practical for research, and accelerate many other important applications.

TitreApplicationTitle: Treating retinal degeneration with stem cells - a multifaceted approach
Keywords-MotsClés: ELECTRORETINOGRAPHY (ERG); HUMAN EMBRYONIC STEM CELLS (HESCS); LIPOSOMAL GENE THERAPY; MESENCHYMAL STEM CELLS (MSCS); OPTICAL COHERENCE TAMOGRAPHY (OCT); OPTOKINETIC TRACKING (OKT); PHOTORECEPTOR PRECURSOR CELLS (PPCS); RETINAL DEGENERATION; STEM-CELL BASED RETINAL THERAPUTICS; SUBRETINAL INJECTION OF PPCS AND MSCS
Abstract-Résumé: Retinal degenerative diseases can be devastating, as they can take away one's primary ability to interact with the world around them. The most common of these diseases is age-related macular degeneration (AMD), which affects nearly 600,000 Canadians and over 14 million people worldwide, with these figures continuing to rise given our aging population and increasing life-spans. Though remarkable progress has been made in the treatment of 'wet' AMD, the other 'dry' form, which accounts for over 90% of all AMD, has no effective treatment and there is little-to-no understanding of its underlying cause. In many retinal degenerative diseases, photoreceptors atrophy and then die off, while the neighboring network of neurons that mediate the passage of visual signals to the brain remain largely intact. In light of this, scientists have attempted to use stem cells to regenerate these photoreceptors, as stem cells have the unique ability to differentiate into any desired cell type when treated with the correct growth factors. Unfortunately, preclinical trials using stem-cell derived photoreceptor precursor cells (PPCs) to regenerate the retina have resulted in too few cells staying at the desired site in the retina, and those that remain rarely integrate - form connections with downstream neurons. The problem is that PPCs are dispersing from where they are needed most, and the majority of those that remain fail to live long enough to form synapses. To address this, I propose to utilize novel materials that gel once inside the eye as a vehicle for PPCs, thereby retaining them at the site of injection. I also propose to harness the neuroprotective effects of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) by co-injecting them with PPCs, which should increase PPC survival, while the addition of synapse-promoting factors should lead to greater integration. My research will help lead to an effective therapy that restores the sight of the many Canadians suffering from advance retinal degeneration.

TitreApplicationTitle: Enhancement of health care delivery through knowledge translation at both physician and patient levels to improve chronic disease outcomes
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC DISEASE; EVALUATION RESEARCH; HEALTH INFORMATION TECHNOLOGIES; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; PATIENT DECISION-MAKING; PHYSICIAN DECISION-MAKING; PRIMARY ADHERENCE; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL; SHARED DECISION-MAKING
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic diseases are very common, and can cause a great deal of illness and premature deaths. Chronic disease outcomes can be improved by adopting health behaviors, such as taking appropriate medication. However, studies have shown that approximately one out of four prescriptions to manage a chronic diseases are never filled at a pharmacy.  We expect that people who know more about their chronic disease and treatment options, and who have taken the time to consider what is important to them, will be better prepared to discuss treatment options with their physician. Furthermore, we expect that these patients who take an active role in treatment decisions will be more likely to follow the agreed upon treatment plan, and as a result, reduce side effects, emergency department and hospital visits, while improving their chronic disease outcomes and overall quality of life.  This study aims to improve health care delivery by offering decision support tools for both patients and physicians in an effort to involve patients in the decision process to ultimately make better treatment decisions. The first part of the study will develop the decision making tools based on patient and physician recommendations for presentation and content. The decision making tools will feature a new generation of information that will show patient-specific information about risks and benefits for available medications, while encouraging patients to consider personal preferences to make good decisions about treatment. The second part of the study will examine whether use of the decision support tools is successful in increasing the number of people who follow their treatment plan by filling their prescription at the pharmacy. If the study confirms that people are, in fact, more likely to follow their treatment plan, then we can expect an improvement in their chronic disease outcomes, and overall quality of life.

TitreApplicationTitle: Metabolic Flexibility in Obese Youth: Exercise as a Screening Test and a Treatment
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDHOOD OBESITY; DIABETES MELLITUS; ENERGY METABOLISM; PEDIATRIC EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: With the rise in childhood obesity, type 2 diabetes, a condition that was once diagnosed in mainly adults, is now occurring earlier in children. As a result, there is increased interest in prevention and intervention strategies to reduce metabolic complications related to obesity, especially in children. Understanding how the muscle burns certain fuels during exercise is important because impaired energy metabolism is often associated with type 2 diabetes. In obese adults who are at risk for developing type 2 diabetes, energy cannot be taken up into the muscle to be burned as efficiently. This leads to excess energy being stored in other places in the body, contributing to potential health complications. Exercise therapy is one method to improve the ability of muscle to burn more energy and reduce health risks in obese adults. However, much less is known about energy metabolism and the benefits of exercise training in obese children.   The proposed research will assess how obese children use energy during exercise and provide the potential to develop an early screening test to identify children that are at an increased risk for developing type 2 diabetes. Earlier identification will be beneficial for reducing metabolic complications, especially in children that may require more aggressive therapy. In a subgroup of children with impaired energy metabolism, we will also examine the effect of short-term exercise training to improve the capacity of the muscle to burn energy, which has not been investigated in children before. If effective, this proposed study will provide the ability to improve childhood obesity treatment and help explain why some obese children are at a greater risk for developing type 2 diabetes than others.

TitreApplicationTitle: Characterization of the oncogenic potential of the mevalonate (MVA) pathway
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER METABOLISM; HMG-COA REDUCTASE; INITIATING ONCOGENE; MEVALONATE PATHWAY; TRANSGENIC MOUSE
Abstract-Résumé: The mevalonate (MVA) pathway is highly regulated in normal cells to provide essential end-products for cell growth and survival, such as cholesterol. Our lab has recently shown that dysregulation of the MVA pathway can contribute to cancer etiology. Moreover, inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR), the rate limiting enzyme of the MVA pathway, can selectively induce apoptosis in a subset of cancer cells (statin-sensitive tumour cells). However, the oncogenic activity of the MVA pathway in vivo, as well as the oncogenic determinants within the MVA pathway, remains to be characterized. To this end, we will develop a mouse model to evaluate the activity of HMGCR as a cooperating oncogene with K-Ras in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In addition, we will employ our cell cuture transformation systems to further determine the oncogenic activity of specific MVA pathway components, such as enzymes involved in the production of Acetyl CoA, enzymatic intermediates downstream of MVA, and the primary transcription factors regulating lipid biosynthesis.

TitreApplicationTitle: New mechanisms driving non-small cell lung cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: LUNG CANCER BIOLOGY; MECHANISMS OF TUMOURIGENESIS; NON CODING RNA; PSEUDOGENES
Abstract-Résumé: Lung cancer is a deadly disease with a 5 year survival rate of less than 15%. The most common cause of lung cancer are mutations of cancer promoting genes, however the root cause of approximately 50% of lung cancer remains unknown. With recent advances in sequencing technology, we can now investigate previously unexplored areas of the tumour DNA, specifically the many overlooked genes that do not encode proteins called non-coding RNA genes. While several non-coding RNA's (ncRNAs) have been recently implicated in lung cancer development, the function of the vast majority of these ncRNAs remain unexplored. The objective of this study is to identify ncRNAs differentially produced in cancerous lung tissue and to determine how they affect cancer driving biological pathways. ncRNAs with aberrant levels will be identified by comparing tumour and matched normal lung tissue. To investigate the role of ncRNAs in tumour biology several assays will be performed on lung cancer cell models. Finally the presence and the levels of ncRNAs of interest will be assessed in blood samples from lung cancer patients comparing to healthy individuals, in order to evaluate its use as diagnostic and prognostic biomarker. Significance: Large scale analysis of ncRNA has not been done in lung cancer, providing an opportunity to learn much about ncRNAs in lung tumour biology. This analysis will lead to the discovery of new and alternative mechanisms of lung cancer development providing potential targets for designing therapy as well as for developing biomarkers for early detection and diagnostic strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étiologie dimensionnelle génétique et neuropsychologique des difficultés en lecture et du trouble déficitaire de l'attention avec ou sans hyperactivité (TDAH)
Keywords-MotsClés: DIFFICULTES DE LECTURE; ENDOPHENOTYPE; FONCTIONS COGNITIVES; GENETIQUE COMPORTEMENTALE; TROUBLE DEFICITAIRE DE L'ATTENTION AVEC HYPERACTIVITE; VARIABLES NEUROPSYCHOLOGIQUES
Abstract-Résumé: La dyslexie et le trouble deficitaire de l'attention avec ou sans hyperactivite (TDAH) sont tres heritables a l'enfance. La dyslexie se traduit par des retards du decodage des mots et le TDAH par de l'inattention, de l'hyperactivite et de l'impulsivite. Les deux se presentent souvent ensemble : environ la moitie ayant un TDAH ont des difficultes en lecture et vice-versa. Cette cooccurrence s'explique par des origines genetiques et neuropsychologiques communes. L'objectif est de mieux comprendre la source de cette cooccurrence en examinant les associations entre les difficultes en lecture et les composantes du TDAH et en evaluant des deficits cognitifs susceptibles de renseigner sur les atteintes en cause. De plus, les etudes portent souvent sur des enfants en clinique, ce qui ne permet pas d'etudier les mecanismes a la base. La dyslexie et le TDAH sont consideres comme des manifestations extremes sur une distribution continue, ce qui permet de tenir compte de ceux avec un niveau sous-clinique. L'etude sera effectuee aupres d'une population de jumeaux suivie depuis la naissance. En genetique comportementale, il s'agira de verifier les associations entre les difficultes en lecture et les composantes du TDAH au primaire. Cet objectif permettra de voir si l'une des composantes du TDAH (inattention et hyperactivite) est davantage associee aux composantes de lecture (decodage de mots et comprehension de lecture) et si ces liens s'expliquent par la genetique ou l'environnement. Ensuite, il sera possible d'evaluer les deficits cognitifs partages avec les difficultes en lecture et le TDAH et ceux uniques a l'une ou l'autre de ces problematiques. Ce sera la premiere etude genetiquement informative a ce sujet chez des enfants canadiens. Elle permettra d'augmenter les connaissances sur cette cooccurrence, de faire de la detection precoce chez les enfants ayant des symptomes et d'adapter les interventions pour minimiser l'impact sur le developpement de ces troubles a l'enfance.

TitreApplicationTitle: Epigenetics of neural tube defects
Keywords-MotsClés: DNA METHYLATION; EPIGENETICS; FETAL TISSUES; FOLATE TRANSPORT & METABOLISM; ILLUMINA DNA METHYLATION MICROARRAYS; MATERNAL ENVIRONMENT; NEURAL TUBE DEFECTS; PLACENTA; PYROSEQUENCING; REPETITIVE ELEMENTS
Abstract-Résumé: Neural tube defects (NTDs) such as spina bifida and anencephaly, are a group of abnormalities affecting the spinal cord and brain in developing babies, often resulting in loss during pregnancy. Children who do survive suffer disability and need a lot of support from their family and the health care system. NTDs develop during the first month of pregnancy - a time when the growing baby is extremely sensitive to its environment. Because it has been shown that folate decreases the risk for NTDs, women trying to become pregnant are told to take this vitamin and it has been added to all grain products in Canada. Even with these changes, 75 babies with an NTD are reported in every 100,000 births in Canada. This suggests that there may be other causes of NTDs.   It is known that the environment can affect human health through impact on our genes. For example, cells use folate from the diet to add chemical structures to DNA and these changes can turn genes on and off. The placenta is the connection between the mother and baby and controls the developing baby's environment. My research project will look at whether a problem in the placenta decreases the amount of folate that the baby gets from its mother and then changes which genes are on or off in babies that develop NTDs. I will ask three questions:  1) Is there a difference in the chemical structures added to DNA between brain tissues from normal and NTD babies?   2) Is there a difference in the chemical structures added to DNA between placenta from normal and NTD babies?   3) Do the placenta from NTD babies function in the same way as placenta from healthy babies?  This research is important because it may lead to a better understanding of the causes of NTDs. This knowledge could be used to help prevent some NTD-affected pregnancies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigation of the role of microglial activation in cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease using a novel PET radiotracer
Keywords-MotsClés: COGNITION; MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION; NEUROINFLAMMATION; PARKINSON'S DISEASE; PET IMAGING
Abstract-Résumé: Increased microglial activation plays an important role in the diffuse brain changes associated with neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease (PD). Microglial activation is present in the post-mortem brains of PD in the regions associated with cognition. Microglial activation also precedes neuronal degeneration in animal models of PD. These observations suggest that quantification of microglial activation in vivo may serve as a new biomarker for early detection of cognitive impairment in PD. Previous neuroimaging studies using Positron Emission Tomography (PET) supported diffuse microglial activation including in the brain regions relevant to cognition. However, these studies did not include PD patients with cognitive impairment. Also the limitations of the PET radiotracer and analysis method warrant further studies. Therefore, I will measure microglial activation in PD patients with cognitive impairment using a PET radiotracer that our group has developed to overcome the limitations of the previous radiotracer, and investigate the relationships (1) between microglial activation and cognitive impairment as well as (2) between microglial activation and other neuroimaging data. PD is the second most common neurodegenerative illness, affecting more than 100,000 Canadians. Cognitive impairment is common in PD, and is considered to be one of the important risk factors for developing dementia: At least 80% of PD patients will develop dementia after 10 years of having the disease. My proposed study will provide in vivo the first reliable evidence of increased microglial activation using a novel PET radiotracer in PD patients with cognitive impairment, and demonstrate the relationships between microglial activation and cognitive impairment as well as other neuroimaging data. It will be used as a new biomarker for early detection of cognitive impairment, which will help to further confirm the relationships between microglial activation, MCI and development of dementia.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dissecting regulatory circuitry governing fungal drug tolerance composed of Hsp90, calcineurin, Cas5 and protein kinase C signaling
Keywords-MotsClés: CANDIDA ALBICANS; CELLULAR SIGNALLING; FUNGAL DRUG RESISTANCE; MOLECULAR CHAPERONE
Abstract-Résumé: Candida albicans is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen that can cause severe, life-threatening bloodstream and deep organ infections in the growing population of immunocompromised individuals, with associated mortality rates approaching 40%. Although antifungal drugs are routinely used to treat Candida infections, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by the drug tolerance of fungal pathogens. The molecular chaperone heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) stabilizes diverse client proteins, and is a key modulator of drug tolerance in C. albicans. Recent studies suggest that Hsp90 stimulates responses to drug-induced cell wall stress through its client protein calcineurin and the cell wall integrity pathway mediated by protein kinase Pkc1. The goal of my research is to elucidate the Hsp90-dependent regulatory circuitry that controls tolerance to the echinocandins, which target the fungal cell wall and are the only new class of antifungal to reach the clinic in decades. My initial research suggests that Pkc1 is a client protein of Hsp90, and identifies a novel target downstream of both Pkc1 and calcineurin with a key role in drug tolerance, the transcription factor Cas5. My results suggest that although Pkc1 and calcineurin play a role in regulating CAS5 gene expression, the expression of CAS5 alone is not sufficient to confer tolerance to the echinocandin caspofungin, leading to my current hypothesis that Pkc1 and calcineurin may post-translationally modify Cas5 protein to enable it to function in concert with other transcription factors such as Crz1 and Rlm1. My future research will elucidate the mechanism(s) by which the Hsp90 clients Pkc1 and calcineurin control tolerance to caspofungin in C. albicans via Cas5. My work suggests novel cellular circuitry through which Hsp90 regulates drug tolerance and implicates Cas5, a fungal-specific protein downstream of Pkc1 and calcineurin, as a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of life-threatening fungal diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Whole Genome and Transcriptome Analysis of Thyroid Cancers
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; BIOSTATISTICS; DE-NOVO ASSEMBLY; DETECTION OF NOVEL SOMATIC MUTATIONS; DIAGNOASTIC; NEXT GENERATION SEQUENCING; PROGNOSTIC AND PREDICTIVE MARKER IDENTIFICATION; SOFTWARE ENGINEERING; THYROID CANCERS; TISSUE MICROARRAY ANALYSIS; WHOLE GENOME AND TRANSCRIPTOME ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: An estimated 4% to 7% of the population will develop a clinically significant thyroid tumor during their lifetime. In many cases, diagnosis results from standard techniques are inconclusive and so a large proportion of individuals undergo surgery as a diagnostic procedure for cancer. The suspicious mass, however, is found to be malignant in only 20% of all cases. Several studies have evaluated malignant and benign thyroid lesions in order to identify molecular markers that allow for accurate diagnosis; none have proved sensitive and specific enough for clinical use. The underlying mechanisms that cause thyroid malignant and benign tumors are still poorly understood and hence the need for a more comprehensive analysis.  The emergence of the massively parallel "next-generation" sequencing technologies has made possible the thorough examination of tumors on the level of DNA and as a result the identification of most of the mutations in tumor samples. Several individuals' genomes and tumor samples have been sequenced for a small fraction of the cost of sequencing the first human genome. We have undertaken a complete sequence analysis of thyroid cancers in order to characterize, for the first time, the underlying molecular mechanism of this disease. Utilizing these technologies, we have sequenced the genetic material of dissected tumors in addition to normal tissues, such as blood, from the same patients. This will allow us to identify the novel mutations that have given rise to the disease in each individual patient. Systematic comparison between the tumors allows commonly mutated genes in thyroid cancers to be identified. Such analysis will help in determining the molecular changes causing the disease, identifying more sensitive diagnostics as well as the proteins and pathways important for therapeutic interventions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Decision-making Across the Adult Lifespan in the Context of Breast Cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: BREAST CANCER; DECISION-MAKING; DISTRESS; GENDER; GROUNDED THEORY; LIFESPAN; ONCOLOGY; PATIENT-ORIENTED; PSYCHOSOCIAL; QUALITATIVE
Abstract-Résumé: Breast cancer is the most diagnosed cancer among women worldwide.  The diagnosis brings a range of physical, psychological and social distresses which differ for women depending on their age. This distress is significant when decision-making is crucial to cancer care and distress may impact decision-making. Current cancer decision-making supports are derived from decision-making theory that assumes patients make clinically rational decisions. Yet literature shows that women with breast cancer do not consistently make treatment decisions as expected and the reasons are unclear. It is unknown what influences decision-making for women with breast cancer and whether there are differences among women based on their age. This study is built upon a pilot study and it seeks to explore the real-world experience of making decisions in cancer. The primary purpose of this qualitative study is to explore decision-making for women with invasive breast cancer. Specific objectives include comparing decision-making for young, middle-aged and older women as well as describing how psychological and social factors influence decision-making. Participants are women diagnosed with invasive breast cancer in the past 12 months. To determine the influence of age on decision-making three age groups will be compared: pre-menopausal, peri-menopausal, and post-menopausal women. Multiple data sources will be collected including demographic surveys, open-ended interviews, and field notes. Constant comparative analysis will explain how women of differing ages make decisions in breast cancer and what influences their decision-making. Findings from this study will provide a patient perspective regarding treatment decision-making and will inform how to best support women of all ages in breast cancer decision-making. Ultimately, this research will contribute to improving patient care for women of all ages with breast cancer.

TitreApplicationTitle: Disorders of Sleep and Wakefulness among Ontario workers with Traumatic Brain Injury: Prevalence and Impact.
Keywords-MotsClés: ALERTNESS; DEPRESSION; DISABILITY; FATIGUE; INSOMNIA; OUTCOME; SLEEP; SLEEPINESS; TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY; WORKERS
Abstract-Résumé: Workers with Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) are at high risk for sleep disturbances, which may occur as a result of direct and indirect trauma to the brain, damage to the hypothalamus/neurotransmitters interfering with sleep-wake cycle, and pain subsequent to damage to the neck/back. Once sleep problems develop, they contribute to the workers' impairment by causing additional confusion, frustration, and depression. Little is known about the role of sleep dysfunction in formation of disability post-TBI. This study aims to draw upon hundreds of Ontario workers who experience persisting symptoms after a work-related TBI.  The main complaint in this population is fatigue, which may arise from medical, psychiatric and behavioural lifestyle changes. In many patients, fatigue presents as an excessive daytime sleepiness or difficulty maintaining alertness throughout the day, resulting in reduced performance. Accurate diagnosis is important, not only because of the negative impact of fatigue, excessive sleepiness or impaired alertness and their underlying causes on the person's health and performance, but also because they are treatable. This research will provide a better understanding of the role of sleep dysfunction in the etiology of fatigue, excessive sleepiness and impaired alertness after TBI which deprives workers of the potential for recovery and leads to disability after mild to moderate brain injury. Results will also highlight gender differences in sleep functioning and will inform clinical practice, health and labour policy on importance of assessing sleep post-TBI.

TitreApplicationTitle: Regulation of human hematopoietic cells with rapid in vivo repopulating activity
Keywords-MotsClés: BONE MARROW; CELL CULTURE; CELL HOMING; CORD BLOOD; FLOW CYTOMETRY; GROWTH FACTORS; HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS; HEMATOPOIETIC TRANSPLANTATION; MYELOPOIESIS; NOD/SCID-IL-2R¿C-/- (NSG) MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Bone marrow contains "stem" cells that can restore normal blood cell production in patients transplanted with these cells. This procedure now allows patients with certain leukemias and non-malignant blood diseases to be cured. However, many cannot benefit from this type of therapy because the numbers of cells available are insufficient. The procedure would also become much safer and cheaper if it were possible to expand the cells that produce new blood cells very rapidly after the transplant is performed. Over the past few years, tissue culture conditions have been developed that appear useful at first glance, but subsequent studies showed these cultured cells no longer work properly when transplanted. I have confirmed this finding and shown it develops very quickly (within a day). These findings are important clinically as they indicate that additional methods are required to make these cells clinically useful.   The goal of my project is to better understand the mechanism that activates the engrafting defect these cultured cells acquire, and identify new agents that can prevent or reverse the problem. My preliminary experiments indicate that certain unidentified proteins can achieve this result. I will now use several strategies to determine what these are and how they work. This will include looking for changes in the molecules known to be involved in the normal engrafting ability of these cells. A second approach is to screen for genes that are key to the defect and small molecules that have the desired corrective effect. Candidates thus identified will finally be tested in a model in which human cells are transplanted into mice that are genetically immunodeficient. The results will provide a significant contribution to our understanding of why cultured cells perform poorly in patients and how this situation can be corrected with clinically useful agents, leading to improved outcomes in patients whose prognosis relies on a transplant.

TitreApplicationTitle: The NLRP3 inflammasome: understanding the mechanism of burn-induced hypermetabolism
Keywords-MotsClés: CATECHOLAMINES; GLIBENCLAMIDE; HYPERMETABOLISM; IMMUNOLOGY; METABOLISM; NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME; PROPRANOLOL; SEVERE-BURN; STRESS-INDUCED DIABETES; TWO-HIT RODENT MODEL
Abstract-Résumé: Severe burn injury is a catastrophic event that forces a victim to succumb to a life long battle of recovering both physically and psychologically. Overactive metabolic response is a well-established hallmark of severe burns, which includes insulin resistance, elevated glucose and fat breakdown, and collectively can lead to multiple organ failure and death. The mechanism for this sequence of events is not well understood, however recent studies of stress-induced diabetes have brought into question the role of the immune complex, NLRP inflammasomes.    The NLR family is an assembly of structures that control cellular surveillance of invading pathogens and have been implicated in various medical conditions including gout, type II diabetes, and obesity. The most attention of these is the NLRP3 inflammasome. Using fat tissue from patients with severe burns, our preliminary data suggests that there is increased activity of NLRP3. However, the mechanism explaining how cellular monitoring develops into liver over-reactivity and dysfunction is not well understood.    The present project aims to: establish whether the NLRP3 inflammasome is the most relevant contributor to burn-induced hypermetabolism, determine whether blocking the inflammasome results in improved metabolic regulation and show that blocking other aspects of burn-induced metabolic over- activity will modulate inflammasome function. Using a rodent model of burn-induced metabolic damage and experimental techniques that measure immunological and metabolic parameters, the proposed study will construct a mechanistic understanding of inflammasome activity resulting in consequential organ damage.    Collectively, this project will provide a deeper understanding of the relationship between inflammasome activity and metabolic response during the progression of severe burn injury and may translate to clinical treatments targeting this immune factor, ultimately leading to improved survival.

TitreApplicationTitle: The association between a history of severe mental illness and the early detection, diagnosis, treatment and survivorship of cancer
Keywords-MotsClés: ADMINISTRATIVE DATA; CANCER CARE CONTINUUM; CANCER DIAGNOSIS; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; MENTAL HEALTH CARE; PRIMARY CARE; SEVERE MENTAL ILLNESS
Abstract-Résumé: Individuals with a severe mental illness will live significantly shorter than the general population. Studies have demonstrated that the majority of increased mortality is not explained by the mental illness itself, but by a greater burden and worse outcomes of co-existing illnesses such as heart disease and diabetes. Little research has been done to understand if a history of a severe mental illness negatively impacts cancer outcomes. For example, individuals with a severe mental illness may be at increased risk for delay to cancer diagnosis and worse stage at diagnosis, both of which are associated with worse survival from cancer. Using national and provincial data, we plan to study the journey of a patient with a severe mental illness through the cancer system, including interactions with primary care; from screening to diagnosis to follow-up care and compare the journey and outcomes with an unexposed (no history of mental illness) general population cohort. Identifying differences in stage at diagnosis, survival and treatment of cancer in the severely mentally ill would uncover a previously unknown gap in primary care and cancer care. Through this work, we hope to identify potential areas of intervention to improve the integration of mental health and primary and cancer care both before and after a cancer has been diagnosed, and improve the prognosis of cancer for this vulnerable population.

TitreApplicationTitle: Contrôle moteur postural et atrophie des muscles multifides en lombalgie chronique : rééducation conventionnelle et neurostimulation périphérique
Keywords-MotsClés: CONTROLE SENSORIMOTEUR LOMBOPELVIEN; EXCITABILITE CORTICOSPINALE; INTERVENTION/READAPTATION; LOMBALGIE CHONIQUE; MUSCLES LOMBOPELVIENS; PHYSIOTHERAPIE; PLASTICITE CEREBRALE; RECHERCHE CLINIQUE; TMS SIMPLES & REPETITIVES; ELECTROMYOGRAPHIE
Abstract-Résumé: Au Quebec, la douleur lombaire representait, entre 2003 et 2006, 59% des affections vertebrales indemnisees chez les travailleurs. 2-3% des lombalgies (douleur au bas du dos) persistent, et induisent la majorite des couts relies aux soins de sante. La forte prevalence de la lombalgie est associee a des recidives de douleur lombaire dans les mois et annees suivants un premier episode douloureux. Ces recidives seraient imputables a un changement de la musculature du tronc et a la perturbation des patrons moteurs essentiels au controle de la colonne vertebrale. Le retour de ce controle semble essentiel pour diminuer la douleur et eviter les recidives. Le muscle multifides, important stabilisateur de la colonne vertebrale, est perturbe (diminution de sa grosseur et de son controle). Il est implique dans le controle de la colonne lombaire dans tous les mouvements du tronc. En lombalgie, son activation est perturbee lors de la marche et des mouvements des membres. On peut l'expliquer par un changement de l'organisation du cerveau chez les lombalgiques. L'entrainement du muscle permet de normaliser l'organisation du cerveau et les patrons moteurs. Dans le projet, il s'agit d'utiliser une nouvelle technologie, les stimulations magnetiques repetitives au-dessus des multifides et les combiner a des exercices qui activent les multifides. Cette technologie a ete montree efficace pour diminuer la douleur et ameliorer le controle des muscles. Il serait possible de produire des changements rapides et de longue duree au niveau de la grosseur et du controle des multifides grace a cette combinaison (stimulations/exercices) de deux semaines. Le retour d'un meilleur controle permettrait de briser le cycle de la douleur en diminuant les micro-traumas entretenus par le manque de controle de la colonne. L'utilisation des stimulations magnetiques comme adjuvant a la physiotherapie pourrait devenir une avenue interessante pour traiter une population refractaire aux soins actuels.

TitreApplicationTitle: The interaction of H2S and PGC-1alpha on hepatic gluconeogenesis in diabetes
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC HYPERGLYCEMIA; GLUCONEOGENESIS; GLUCOSE HOMEOSTASIS; HYDROGEN SULPHIDE; INSULIN-RESISTANCE; MITOCHONDRIAL BIOGENESIS; PGC-1ALPHA; STREPTOZOTOCIN PLUS HIGH FAT DIET-INDUCED TYPE 2 DIABETES
Abstract-Résumé: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes is increasing at an alarming rate among Canadians. Chronic hyperglycemia is the leading cause of diabetes-related complications. The major metabolic defect that contributes to hyperglycemia is uncontrolled glucose production (gluconeogenesis) from the insulin-resistant liver. Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) is produced in liver cells via cystathionine gamma-lyase (CSE). Abnormal metabolism of H2S and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma coactivator (PGC)-1alpha are major pathogenic factors for diabetes development.  Indeed, our CSE knockout (CSE-KO) mice exhibited a delayed onset of diabetic status and a reduced rate of gluconeogenesis.  We also discovered a significant reduction in the expression level of PGC-1alpha in the CSE-KO mice, which was up-regulated by NaHS treatments. It is intriguing how H2S up-regulates PGC-1alpha and what are the functional consequences of this interaction on hepatic glucose production. We hypothesize that the CSE/H2S system stimulates hepatic gluconeogenesis through the induction of PGC-1alpha by up-regulating the cAMP signaling pathway. As such, our objectives are to determine the signaling mechanism of H2S-induced PGC-1alpha up-regulation; to examine PGC-1alpha dependency of H2S-induced glucose production; and to investigate therapeutic approaches to correct H2S-induced over-stimulated hepatic glucose production. To achieve our goals, we will perform a series of in vitro and in vivo gluconeogenic experiments and induce type 2 diabetes in the CSE-KO and wild-type mice. Thereafter, the rate of gluconeogenesis and the development of diabetes will be determined and compared. We will also examine whether PPG, a CSE inhibitor, can reverse H2S-related diabetes development. Our study will unmask a novel approach to treat diabetes by highlighting the importance of targeting the overproduction of H2S to prevent its induction of PGC-1alpha in order to normalize an otherwise enhanced gluconeogenic system.

Keywords-MotsClés: CORTICOMETRIE; IRM DE DIFFUSION; MALADIE DE PARKINSON; MALADIE NEURODEGENERATIVE; MORPHOMETRIE VOXEL PAR VOXEL; NEUROIMAGERIE; TROUBLE COMPORTEMENTAL EN SOMMEIL PARADOXAL; EPAISSEUR CORTICALE
Abstract-Résumé: Le trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal est une maladie qui se caracterise par des comportements involontaires souvent violents pendant le sommeil. Ces comportements sont fortement associes au contenu du reve et perturbent le sommeil. De plus, ils peuvent provoquer chez le patient ou son partenaire de lit des blessures graves. Nous avons observe qu'un grand nombre de patients avec un trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal developpent une maladie neurodegenerative (comme la maladie de Parkinson) apres quelques annees. Ainsi, le but de la presente recherche vise a identifier les regions du cerveau qui sont impliquees dans la transition d'un trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal vers une maladie neurodegenerative. Une telle avancee permettrait de mettre sur pied des traitements afin de retarder ou de prevenir l'apparition de maladies neurodegeneratives chez les patients diagnostiques d'un trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal.

TitreApplicationTitle: Preparing Parents to be Present During Induction for Pediatric Surgery: Evaluating a Preparation Intervention
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY; COMMUNICATION; HEALTH BEHAVIOURAL RESEARCH; PAIN; PARENTAL PRESENCE; PEDIATRIC ANESTHESIA; PEDIATRIC SURGERY; PEDIATRICS; PERI-OPERATIVE PREPARATION
Abstract-Résumé: Surgery is identified as one of the most painful experiences, for thousands of children in Canada who are admitted to hospital each year. Research suggests that children's anxiety about induction prior to surgery is related to the amount of pain they experience and the amount of analgesics they use after surgery. Children's anxiety prior to surgery can be managed with sedative pre-medication but some children find administration of the medication stressful and in some cases the medication can cause negative reactions (e.g., agitation).  Consequently, research on non-pharmacological ways of managing children's anxiety is needed. Parental presence during anesthesia is one such way to help children manage their anxiety. However, research suggests that parents' own anxiety may be detrimental to their child during anesthesia induction. Therefore, parents who are going to be present need to be carefully selected and be prepared about how to help their child cope in order for their presence to be helpful.  The present study will compare children whose parents have received a family-centered preparation to be present during induction with children whose parents receive basic preparation on sterile procedures required to be present during induction on measures of anxiety, pain, analgesic use and time required to recover from the surgery in hospital.  It is expected that children whose parents receive a family-centered preparation before being present during induction will have lower anxiety before surgery and less pain and analgesic use after surgery and will be discharged sooner than children whose parents received a more general preparation about sterile procedures.

Abstract-Résumé: Suicide is the 9th leading cause of mortality in Canada, accounting for 1.6% of total deaths. Identifying and targeting risk factors for suicide is an important goal in preventing suicide. Although the primary risk factor for suicide ideation and completed suicide is mental illness, chronic medical illness is also a significant risk factor. Individuals with chronic medical illness are on average 1.6 times more at risk of dying by suicide than the general population, even after accounting for any mental disorders these patients may have in addition to the physical illness. The reasons for this are poorly understood. Assessing suicide risk in patients with chronic medical illness remains a problem because currently short questionnaires are used, whose validity is not established. Beyond total statistics on mortality and risk little is known about why patients with chronic physical illness may or may not think of killing themselves. The proposed project will evaluate suicide risk in a chronic progressive rheumatic illness, scleroderma. Nothing is known about suicide risk in scleroderma beyond the initial rate of suicide ideation reported by a study I conducted as part of my master's thesis. The project will be carried out in the framework of Canadian Scleroderma Research Group, a pan-Canadian network of rheumatologists and researchers in scleroderma. Patients with scleroderma will be administered validated questionnaires to assess suicide risk, and analyses will be performed to report association between suicide ideation and physical and psychological variables in this disease. In addition, a qualitative study will be conducted, in which selected patients will participate in one-on-one interviews about their thoughts of death and how they relate to suicide risk. The results of these studies will help understand the reasons why patients with scleroderma think about death and suicide and will carry the field forward in understanding suicide risk in medical illness

TitreApplicationTitle: Birth after a previous caesarean section: Health communication strategies to enhance decision making
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDBIRTH; HEALTH SERVICES; INFORMED CHOICE; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; MATERNITY CARE; QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWING; RESEARCH INTERVIEWING
Abstract-Résumé: Across Canada, caesarean section (CS) rates have exceeded optimal levels, exposing mothers to increased morbidity. As CS delivery costs significantly more than vaginal delivery, the increase in CS also creates strain on health care system funding and resources. In British Columbia, 83.4% of women with a previous CS undergo a repeat CS. Best evidence indicates, however, that most women with a previous CS are good candidates for a vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) and 70% who try have successful VBACs. In this context, we have a limited understanding of why women and their care providers choose elective repeat CS and what information they use in making decisions for mode of delivery. Understanding women's health information needs is essential to educate women on the risks and benefits of VBAC and repeat CS, enhance women's self-confidence around vaginal birth, and to support women to make informed, shared decisions for mode of delivery. This study builds on existing initiatives to optimize the caesarean rate in British Columbia and aims to 1) explore multiparous women and care providers' decision-making for mode of delivery after a previous CS; and 2) identify communication strategies that improve health literacy around CS and VBAC and enhance women's informed choice for mode of delivery. Using qualitative research methods, I will interview mothers and maternity care providers to explore their decision-making and communication around mode of delivery. Integrated knowledge translation with key stakeholders in provincial maternity services will enhance the relevance of the recommendations and their application to existing quality improvement initiatives to optimize the CS rate. Best practices in mode of delivery can decrease the rate of elective CS, thereby reducing health risks to mothers and infants and accruing significant health care system savings.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification of mediators implicated in the progression of ovarian cancer to the peritoneum
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER PROGRESSION; MASS SPECTROMETRY; METASTASIS; OVARIAN CANCER MICROENVIRONMENT; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: Not only is ovarian cancer (OvCa) the deadliest gynecological malignancy among women in Canada, it is probably the most poorly understood. Rather than remaining confined to the ovary, OvCa often spreads to local regions in the abdominal cavity, which is covered by a membranous layer called the peritoneum that is composed of mesothelial cells. It is commonly assumed that the initial step in achieving this is for the cancer cells to first attach to mesothelial cells, followed by the subsequent invasion by cancer cells. Both processes of attaching and invading are not well-defined, as several mediators and mechanisms may be involved. As a result, there is a need to investigate the underlying mechanisms of ovarian cancer progression, as well as determine how and why the cancer spreads so quickly. Thus, the ultimate goal of this proposal to determine which molecules play a role in the adhesion of cancer cells to mesothelial cells, and the mechanisms they employ. To investigate this, ovarian cancer and mesothelial cells will be grown either separately or together, and the media that these cultures are grown in will be collected. This media will contain hundreds of proteins that the cancer or mesothelial cells secrete. We believe that when cancer and mesothelial cells are cultured together, different proteins will be secreted than when they are grown alone. After determining which factors become up-regulated during the contact of these two cell types, the next step will be to assess their presence in clinical samples and determine their functional role. The research proposed here will further our knowledge about how ovarian cancer develops into a more advanced disease, and will add to our current understanding about the initial events that typically occur before the cancer becomes too difficult to treat. Therefore, this research has the potential of discovering new therapeutic targets for the treatment of OvCa.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Sandwich Synapse: A Novel Trans-glial Inter-neuronal Signaling Mechanism
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL DISSOCIATION; CHEMICAL TRANSMISSION; DORSAL ROOT GANGLION; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GLIOTRANSMISSION; GLUTAMATERGIC; NMDA; PURINERGIC; SATELLITE GLIAL CELL; VOLTAGE-GATED CALCIUM CHANNEL
Abstract-Résumé: Calcium-dependent neurotransmitter release at chemical synapses facilitates communication between presynaptic neurons and their targets cells by activating postsynaptic receptors. Non-neuronal glial cells are closely associated with chemical synapses throughout the nervous system and their supportive roles in various synaptic processes are relatively well characterized. In the past, it was believed that glial cells were not involved in neurotransmission; however, pioneering work at the neuromuscular junction and recent reports have demonstrated that glia are active participants at synapses. Glial cells can receive signals from presynaptic neurons and respond by releasing transmitters, leading to the tripartite synapse model. Our laboratory has recently expanded this concept with observations of a novel form of transmission between neighbouring neurons in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) through an intervening satellite glial cell (SGC) functioning in series, at which we term a Sandwich Synapse (SS). A subset of DRG neurons are closely-apposed and separated solely by a SGC membrane to form a functional trimer. Stimulation of one DRG neuron evokes a response in both itself and its passive partner, a phenomenon we refer to as SS transmission. Using imaging, pharmacological and electrophysiological techniques we have elucidated several of the mechanisms involved in SS transmission and infer that ATP secretion from the neuron induces a glial calcium response and release of glutamate to activate postsynaptic receptors. We are currently investigating the mechanism of glutamate release from the SGC that enables neuronal communication. We will also test the prediction that SS transmission occurs between neighbouring neurons in other parts of the nervous system. This discovery would transform our understanding of neural processing. The DRG SS itself could have implications for sensory processing, both in normal and defective situations.
