TitreApplicationTitle: Development of a cytotoxic T-lymphocyte based cell-to-cell therapeutic delivery system
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOPTIVE CELL THERAPY; EXPERIMENTAL THERAPEUTICS; FUSION PROTEINS; GENETIC ENGINEERING; GRANZYMES; RNA INTERFERENCE; SYNTHETIC BIOLOGY; T LYMPHOCYTES
Abstract-Résumé: One of the main issues with all pharmaceutical therapy is unwanted side effects. Not only are these adverse effects extremely unpleasant and even at times life threatening, but concerns over adverse outcomes often limit the utility of a given therapeutic. These adverse affects are typically caused by a combination of poor specificity and inappropriate distribution. Specificity is an issue when a drug acts not only on its target, but also at other sites. Distribution is an issue either when a harmful drug accumulates in sensitive regions of the body, for example the brain, or conversely when a beneficial drug cannot access an important region. The aim of this project is to develop a human T-cell based system that can deliver a therapeutic molecule to only the diseased tissue and cells.  Cytotoxic T-cells are a part of the human immune system that kill tumor or virally infected cells. T-cells have three characteristics that make them suitable for this project: (i) they have T-cell receptors that are specific for a matching small molecule on a given cell surface, enabling very precise targeting; (ii) they have a unique secretion pathway that delivers molecules from the T-cell to the target cell, without letting any molecules diffuse to other, non-target cells; and (iii) they are known to distribute throughout the body, ensuring access to all necessary tissue.  These properties are already exploited in the field of adoptive cell therapy. T-cells that have been extracted from a patient are given a specificity for a tumor or virally infected cell, replicated (both in a laboratory), and then re- administered to the same patient, whereupon they kill tumor or virally infected cells. I am engineering T-cells so that rather than only killing a cell, they may be used to deliver any type of molecule: one that may be either detrimental to the cell (if it needs to be eliminated, as in cancer) or therapeutic to the cell (if it needs to be healed, as in autoimmune disorders).

Keywords-MotsClés: ENV GPS CONFORMATIONAL CHANGES; GP120-GP41 INTERACTIONS; HIV; ISOTHERMAL CALORIMETRY; SURFACE PLASMON RESONANCE; TRANSMITTED/FOUNDER VIRUS; VIRAL REPLICATION
Abstract-Résumé: The first cases of infection with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) in Canada were reported over 25 years ago. Notwithstanding all the efforts to prevent new infections, it is estimated that 65,000 Canadians are living with HIV/AIDS and thousands are newly infected every year. While there has been significant progress in clinical treatment of HIV-1 and in understanding its relation with the human immune system, there are still no effective vaccines or therapies that eradicate the virus. Our project aims to better characterize how the virus can infect new individuals, what is called the transmission event. In most cases of transmission, only one viral particle is able to establish the infection. We will look specifically at those transmitted viruses compared with the large amount of non-transmitted in order to identify if there are any differences that could help promote the transmission event. If there are, those differences could be exploited for clinical intervention. These characterization studies are essential in order to establish the theoretical basis needed for the design of novel, next-generation anti-HIV-1 entry inhibitors, vaccine and microbicides that will specifically target the transmission event.

TitreApplicationTitle: Spatial epidemiology of child and youth injury in Canada
Keywords-MotsClés: EPIDEMIOLOGY; GIS; HEALTH; HEALTH GEOGRAPHY; INJURY; PUBLIC HEALTH; TRAUMA
Abstract-Résumé: Centering on the social and environmental determinants of childhood injury, this study will examine both the geographical distribution of major traumas within the Canadian child and youth population, and the effectiveness of Canadian pediatric trauma systems. Approximately 25,000 Canadian children are hospitalized each year as a result of unintentional injuries.  Of these, approximately 400 will die.  The rate of injury and death amongst Canadian Aboriginal youth is even higher.  While the cost of these injuries is significant - estimated at 5.1$ billion annually - to date, very few studies have focused on the effectiveness of Canadian pediatric trauma systems. This project aims to address these issues and identify gaps in the delivery of pediatric trauma care by  mapping the hotspots for child and youth injury within Canada, identifying disadvantaged populations and high risk injury mechanisms and patterns, determining the types of injury requiring high level care, and exploring the barriers that impede access to appropriate care.  Results from this project, together with those from a larger CIHR-funded project (the CIHR Team in Child and Youth Injury Prevention which forms part of the larger STAIR project), will provide decision makers with the ability to allocate and reallocate resources to appropriate groups based on evidence. The results will be provided to users via a web based dashboard which will enable users to interact and analyze the data using a graphic user interface.     In summary, this project will analyze Canadian pediatric traumas in terms of the severity of injury, the identification of at risk populations and the provision of appropriate treatment. In so doing, the intention is to optimize the provision of care and delivery of services to target populations and to help direct scarce prevention-related public health resources so as to have the greatest impact on reducing pediatric injuries in Canada.

Keywords-MotsClés: APOPTOSE; CANCER OVARIEN; CHIMIORESISTANCE; CIBLE THERAPEUTIQUE; CISPLATINE; LENTIVIRUS; OESTROGENE; PAR-4; XENOGREFFES; ELECTROPHORESE
Abstract-Résumé: Le cancer ovarien est le 5e cancer causant le plus grand nombre de deces chez la femme et la principale cause de mortalite au Canada des cancers gynecologiques. Ce haut taux de deces est en partie cause par l'inefficacite des traitements actuels, du au stade avance auquel ce cancer est detecte. L'incapacite des traitements chimiotherapeutiques a ces stades avances de progression a pour consequence qu'une majorite des cancers ovariens sont designes comme etant resistants a la chimiotherapie. Afin  de contrer cette problematique, de nouvelles cibles therapeutiques doivent etre etudiees. Prostate Apoptosis Response-4 (PAR-4) est une des cibles therapeutique potentielle pour combattre le cancer ovarien. En effet, cette proteine possede une caracteristique unique lui permettant d'induire la mort d'une maniere selective chez les cellules cancereuses, sans detruire les cellules saines. Le niveau d'expression de cette proteine est regule par differents moyens tels une regulation negative par l'estrogene ou la presence d'une portion clivee de PAR-4 presente seulement chez les cellules sensibles a la chimiotherapie. Les objectifs sont de determiner si la surexpression du fragment clive de PAR-4 sensibilise les cellules resistantes aux traitements chimiotherapeutiques par l'induction des mecanismes de mort cellulaire et d'explorer l'hypothese que l'inhibition des estrogenes pourrait etre un mecanisme de reactivation de l'expression et/ou activite de PAR-4. L'etude de cette nouvelle cible permettra la mise au point de traitements alternatifs viables contre le cancer de l'ovaire en selectionnant specifiquement les cellules cancereuses, et en sensibilisant les cellules cancereuses aux traitements chimiotherapeutiques. Ainsi, ces recherches vont permettre d'ameliorer la sante des femmes atteintes du cancer de l'ovaire. Ces resultats pourront ainsi ouvrir de nouvelles possibilites de traitements contre les cancers feminins.

TitreApplicationTitle: Reducing the Transgenerational Transmission of Depression: Testing the HPA Programming Hypothesis.
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILD COPING; CHILD EMOTION AND BEHAVIOR PROBLEMS; CORTISOL; DEPRESSION; DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; EMOTION REGULATION; HPA AXIS; NEUROBIOLOGY; PARENTING STYLE
Abstract-Résumé: Background: Over 10% of Canadian women experience depression in the early years of their child's life (Public Health Agency of Canada, 2012). These children have elevated risk for physical and mental health problems (e.g. Murray et al., 2003). A potential mechanism accounting for this risk is the abnormal hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) activity, shown by atypical cortisol levels, in depressed women and their children. The HPA programming hypothesis states that the HPA axis is programmed early in life, and is influenced by maternal HPA activity and psychological (e.g. depressed) states.  Objectives: 1) Delineate how maternal depression and maternal HPA activity influences child HPA activity across development; 2) determine how children's HPA activity, in association with other child features (i.e. emotion regulation), explains children's emotion and behavior difficulties.   Method: The sample will be drawn from the CIHR-funded Maternal Adversity, Vulnerability and Neurodevelopment (MAVAN) project, which is an ongoing study of 150 depressed and 100 healthy control mother-child dyads, assessed prenatally and thereafter. Mother-child dyads have already participated in 5 stressful tasks across development, during which cortisol was sampled. Dyads will return for a follow-up visit-children are now approximately 7 years old. During this visit, dyads will participate in a stressful task and cortisol will be collected. Maternal depression and child emotion and behavior problems will be assessed using an interview and self-report measures. During all study visits children's emotion regulation strategies will be coded.   Implications: This study will elucidate longitudinal effects of maternal depression on child HPA activity and emotion regulation ability. This research will be informative for determining sensitive periods of HPA programming, which can be applied to interventions for at-risk children, to decrease the transgenerational transmission of depression.

TitreApplicationTitle: Improving Functional Engraftment of Beta-cells Within Micro-tissue Units that Randomly Assemble into a Vascularized Pancreatic Organoid
Keywords-MotsClés: ALTERNATIVELY ACTIVATED MACROPHAGES; ENDOTHELIAL CELLS; ENGRAFTMENT; MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS; TISSUE ENGINEERING; TRANSPLANTATION; TYPE 1 DIABETES MELLITUS; VASCULARIZATION
Abstract-Résumé: Type 1 diabetes is a prevalent disease resulting from the destruction of insulin-producing beta-cells in the pancreas. Transplantation of insulin-secreting cells offers a promising therapy for patients, but is hampered by the survival and long-term function of cells once transplanted. The goal of my project is to improve survival and function of beta-cells by delivering them within small (micrometer scale) collagen gels, surrounded by two vascular cell types. I hypothesize that this mode of delivery will lead to the formation of a densely vascularized graft that provides an oxygenated environment to support cell survival, and by recruiting beneficial immune cell types. In my first aim, a microfluidic device will be used to fabricate small cell-embedded collagen gels. Subsequently, cell-embedded micro-tissues will be implanted in immune-altered drug-induced diabetic mice to assess vessel formation in the implant and blood glucose levels over time. Finally, interactions between vascular cells, pancreatic beta-cells and an immune cell type will be investigated. Completion of this project will lead to a better understanding of cell factors important in graft survival and function, as well as the development of a tissue engineering strategy that can potentially benefit diabetic patients.

TitreApplicationTitle: Impact of Age and Vascular Disease on Sympathetic Nervous System Discharge Patterns
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTION POTENTIAL DISCHARGE PATTERNS; AGING; CARDIAC REHABILITATION; EXERCISE TRAINING; MICRONEUROGRAPHY; REFLEX CARDIOVASCULAR CONTROL; SYMPATHETIC DYSREGULATION; SYMPATHETIC NERVE OUTFLOW; SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM; VASCULAR DISEASE
Abstract-Résumé: Increasing age and vascular disease (i.e., coronary artery disease; CAD) are associated with altered sympathetic nervous system (SNS) outflow patterns that have deleterious consequences for health and survival. There exists a lack of knowledge and mechanistic understanding of age- and vascular disease-related sympathetic dysregulation. As such, this research will evaluate critically the impact of age and vascular disease on SNS outflow patterns, and investigate whether exercise training can reverse and/or alter this dysregulation. This research will make use of a novel analytical model developed in our laboratory that offers a new intricate scale of extraction and quantification of SNS discharge patterns. This approach will represent the first exploration into a comprehensive analysis of SNS outflow patterns, and how these are affected by aging, vascular disease, and exercise training. In study one, direct measures of muscle sympathetic nerve activity via microneurography will be collected in young healthy controls, older individuals, and CAD patients at baseline and during autonomic challenge maneuvers to assess the impact of age and vascular disease on sympathetic outflow. In study two, older participants and CAD patients will be re-tested after 6- and 12-months of aerobic and resistance exercise training (older participants) or exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation (CAD patients) to determine whether an exercise intervention can reverse and/or alter dysregulation in SNS discharge patterns. As such, the knowledge to be learned will provide invaluable information for the creation of more effective health care strategies designed to mitigate the consequences of SNS dysregulation associated with aging and vascular disease. Exercise training may be key in reversing and/or altering sympathetic dysregulation in these populations, and as such, the proposed research will offer important knowledge for health and survival, health care, and clinical practice.

TitreApplicationTitle: Retour post-isolement en milieu psychiatrique : implantation et évaluation d'une intervention en soins aigus.
Keywords-MotsClés: GESTION DE L'AGRESSIVITE; MESURES DE CONTROLE; METHODES MIXTES; PRATIQUE REFLEXIVE; RETOUR POSTISOLEMENT; SANTE MENTALE
Abstract-Résumé: En sante mentale, les infirmieres sont souvent confrontees au comportement agressif des patients. Dans ce contexte, l'isolement du patient est une intervention de dernier recours parfois utilisee pour y faire face. Afin de diminuer les mises en isolement, plusieurs interventions ont ete proposees, dont un retour avec l'equipe et le patient sur son isolement, sans avoir toutefois fait l'objet d'une evaluation. Le projet vise a adapter, implanter et evaluer une intervention, le retour post-isolement, dans le but d'ameliorer l'experience du patient et des infirmieres en trouvant des moyens alternatifs a la mise en isolement. Ce projet permettra d'ameliorer la pratique infirmiere concernant la gestion de l'agressivite ainsi que l'experience d'hospitalisation des personnes souffrant de maladie mentale presentant des episodes d'agressivite.

TitreApplicationTitle: Motivational Interviewing to Enhance Weight-Loss among Obese Hypertensive Patients: A Stepped-Care Random Controlled Trial
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD PRESSURE; HYPERTENSION; MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING; RANDOM CONTROLLED TRIAL; STEPPED-CARE; WEIGHT LOSS
Abstract-Résumé: Elevated blood pressure and obesity remain two of the greatest health and economic issues facing the world. In 2010, Statistics Canada reported that 17.1% of Canadians over the age of 12 reported high blood pressure and 18.3% of Canadians over the age of 18 reported being obese. Obesity is a risk factor for hypertension, heart disease, and diabetes. While weight loss can effectively lower blood pressure, many hypertensive adults prescribed lifestyle change fail to lose weight and maintain blood pressure control. We will test whether motivational interviewing - a style of counseling that explores the positive and negative aspects of a behavior and motivates change by empowering people to overcome barriers to treatment and take an active role in their own health - improves weight loss among obese hypertensive patients. A group of obese hypertensive patients will be given usual care (e.g., emphasize gradual weight loss, progressive increase in exercise, and education). A second group of obese hypertensive patients will have their usual care stepped up to include motivational interviewing if they fail to meet their weight loss goals at each check-up. Usual care or motivational interviewing sessions will be given at baseline, 1-month, 2-months, and 3-months. Body weight and blood pressure will be measured at each office visit (baseline, 1-month, 2-months, 3-months, 4-months, and at a 2-month follow up). In addition to this, patients will keep track of their physical activity using a daily exercise journal. We believe that participants given motivational interviewing will demonstrate greater weight loss, more physical activity, and better blood pressure control.  This project has the potential to change the way health-care providers motivate hypertensive patients to lose weight.  Implemented broadly, this technique may drastically reduce the risk of uncontrolled hypertension, and heart disease.

TitreApplicationTitle: The role of transcription factor 7-like 2 (TCF7L2) in hepatic glucose production: Implications to type 2 diabetes mellitus
Keywords-MotsClés: CELL CULTURE STUDIES; DIABETES; GENE EXPRESSION ASSAYS; GLUCONEOGENESIS; INSULIN; KNOCKDOWN STUDIES; LIVER; TCF7L2; TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODELS; WNT
Abstract-Résumé: According to the Canadian Diabetes Association, more than 9 million Canadians are currently living with diabetes or prediabetes, of which the majority have type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D). Recent human genomic studies have identified that small DNA "mutations" in the gene called "TCF7L2" often lead to higher risk of T2D. TCF7L2 plays an important role in our cells by carrying out the final steps of a cellular pathway called the "WNT signaling pathway". However, the mechanism by which "mutations" in TCF7L2 can confer susceptibility to T2D is currently poorly understood. Recent human and mouse studies have suggested that TCF7L2 may be important for the normal production of glucose in the liver which primarily occurs during fasting to provide energy for the body. During feeding, on the other hand, insulin is released by the body to reduce glucose production in the liver in order to prevent blood sugar levels from rising to toxic levels. Abnormally elevated glucose production in the liver is detrimental to health as it leads to high blood sugar levels and diabetes. In my studies thus far, I identified that TCF7L2 and the WNT signaling pathway contribute to the reduction in glucose production in the liver in response to insulin, using both experimental animals and cell culture techniques. Based on my results, I will investigate in more detail how TCF7L2 and WNT carry out this function in the liver using both a transgenic animal model in which TCF7L2 is only deficient in the liver as well as advanced cell culture techniques. The proposed work for my PhD project will lead to new important insights into how TCF7L2 is involved in glucose production, metabolism, and the risk of T2D. Enhanced understanding of the role of TCF7L2 in the liver from my study will contribute to the development of new strategies for the prevention and treatment of diabetes in millions of Canadians in the future.

TitreApplicationTitle: Reassessing the effect of mode of delivery after previous Caesarean on maternal and infant health: An innovative application of robust causal inference models
Keywords-MotsClés: CAESAREAN DELIVERY; CAUSAL INFERENCE; EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTH POLICY; GEOGRAPHIC VARIATION; INSTRUMENTAL VARIABLE ANALYSIS; MEDICAL DECISION MAKING; NATURAL EXPERIMENTS; PERINATAL EPIDEMIOLOGY; VAGINAL BIRTH AFTER PREVIOUS CAESAREAN; WOMEN'S HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Introduction: Despite guidelines supporting vaginal birth after previous Caesarean in low-risk pregnancies, most pregnant women with a previous C-section will undergo a repeat C-section. This disparity between guidelines and practice indicates a lack of consensus regarding best practice. Indeed, no randomized controlled trial of this question has been undertaken and observational studies may suffer from confounding bias. There is an urgent need for more concrete evidence to guide best practices and to identify nonclinical drivers of mode of delivery.  Research Objectives: i) To identify non-clinical drivers of mode of delivery after previous C-section across Canada and over time, and ii) To use an innovative approach to identify the causal effect of mode of delivery on maternal and infant health outcomes in women with previous C-sections.  Methods: Two separate studies will be undertaken to address each of the identified objectives. In the first study, I will use multi-level models to examine differences in clinical (e.g., maternal risk factors) and non-clinical (e.g., physician remuneration schemes) factors that impact C-section rates to illustrate how such rates vary across the provinces and have changed over time. In the second study, I will use a technique that isolates the causal effect of mode of delivery after previous Caesarean on maternal and infant health. This method offers many benefits over traditional designs when there is a high risk for producing confounded effect estimates.  Relevance: Caesarean section is one of the two most performed surgical procedures on Canadian women. The potential of unwarranted Caesareans may put women at unnecessary risk for associated adverse outcomes and greatly increases healthcare expenditures. This study will be the first to apply an innovative causal approach to examine which mode of delivery results in more favourable birth outcomes and will be used to inform best practice guidelines.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding experiences of obesity and weight loss strategies of menopausal women from contrasting social environments
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPORTEMENTS DE SANTE; INEGALITES SOCIALES DE SANTE; MENOPAUSE; OBESITE; PERTE DE POIDS; VIEILLISSEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Considering significant health risks related to obesity, it is crucial to study the socio-cultural mechanisms that lead to obesity and weight loss amongst various socio-economomic status groups. In women, midlife is strongly characterized by weight gain and increased health risks related to metabolic changes associated to menopause. Therefore prioritizing obese postmenopausal women is particularly relevant regarding this issue. To our knowledge, no social class analysis has focused on the susceptibilities of obese aging women to follow a weight-loss program. This research proposal focuses on disposition to loose weight of clinically obese postmenopausal women from contrasting social classes. The aims of this study are: 1) To identify the norms and values of clinically obese postmenopausal women of diverse socioeconomic background with regards to the ways of treating and caring for the body and to outline the socio-cultural processes which incline (or not) these individuals to pursue a weight loss strategies 2) To develop a theoretical and empirically-grounded account of the discursive and embodied effects of health and obesity discourses on obese aging women, 3) to understand how obese women are interpellated by dominant and/or alternative discourses on obesity. From a practical standpoint, this project will: A) develop knowledge that will assist health professionals in their contextualized interventions to improve obese women's health and weight management; B) inform those programs and policies that are intended to promote their participation in physical activity and other health practices; and C) provide information to help develop interventions that will better serve the goal of obese women's increased health and well-being.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Experience of Hard to Reach Families in Accessing and Engaging in Pediatric Rehabilitation Services
Keywords-MotsClés: ACCESS-ENGAGEMENT; GROUNDED THEORY; PRESCHOOL; QUALITATIVE STUDY; REHABILITATION; SERVICE DELIVERY
Abstract-Résumé: Pediatric rehabilitation services (physical, occupational, and speech-language therapy) help children with disabilities to learn new skills and to participate actively and successfully at home, at school and in the community. Within Ontario over 60,000 families are accessing rehabilitation services through the 20 children's treatment centres of the OCARS network. We know that many families who use these services have improved social inclusion, mental health and well-being. Therefore, it is a concern that not all children and families have equal access to these publicly funded rehabilitation services and some families do not engage in the services that have been offered. Families who do not use the services for which they are eligible are often labelled "hard to reach families". There are no estimates of the number of "hard to reach families"; however the importance of this issue has been recognized within education, health, and social service research. This literature typically reflects service providers' perspectives of "hard to reach families", however a shift is required to the family's perspective in studying "hard to access services". The proposed study will investigate the concepts of both "hard to reach families" and "hard to access services" from the perspective of parents of children with disabilities. Using a semi-structured interview, parents will be asked about their experience of accessing and engaging in therapy services at KidsAbility, an OACRS Children's Treatment Centre. Interviews will be recorded and reviewed to identify key themes and inform recommendations to improve the accessibility of pediatric rehabilitation services within Ontario. These recommendations will be published and presented through the OACRS annual conference and best practice workgroup to promote social inclusion and improved health for children with disabilities and their families. TitreApplicationTitle: Génétique, acides gras oméga-3 et facteurs de risque des maladies cardiovasculaires
Keywords-MotsClés: ACIDES GRAS POLYINSATURES OMEGA-3; GENES IMPLIQUES DANS LE METABOLISME DES LIPIDES; HAPLOTYPES; PHASE VERSION 2.1; POLYMORPHISMES NUCLEOTIDIQUES; QUESTIONNAIRE DE FREQUENCE ALIMENTAIRE; TAQMAN; VARIABILITE INTERINDIVIDUELLE
Abstract-Résumé: Les maladies du coeur et les accidents cerebraux vasculaires representent deux des trois principales causes de deces au Canada. La consommation d'acides gras polyinsatures (AGPI) omega-3 (n-3) a ete associee a un risque moindre de maladies cardiovasculaires (MCV). Les politiques de sante publiques actuelles assument que chaque individu reagit de facon similaire a une recommandation nutritionnelle. Toutefois, suite a un traitement nutritionnel, il existe une importante variabilite interindividuelle faisant en sorte que certains individus seront consideres comme «hypo repondeurs» et d'autres «hyper repondeurs». Des facteurs genetiques peuvent partiellement expliquer ces dissemblances. L'objectif du present projet est de mieux comprendre la variabilite de la reponse interindividuelle des facteurs de risque lipidiques des MCV suite a une supplementation en AGPI n-3. La nutrigenomique, soit l'etude de la genetique et de l'alimentation, a le potentiel de modifier les lignes directrices en nutrition. Toutefois, avant d'y parvenir les mecanismes responsables de la variabilite interindividuelle devront etre entierement elucides. Jusqu'a maintenant quelques etudes se sont penchees sur l'effet de polymorphismes (SNPs) et les facteurs de risque de MCV. Toutefois, ces analyses n'observaient qu'un seul gene ou quelques genes a la fois. En considerant plusieurs genes simultanement, ce projet permettra d'approfondir globalement notre comprehension des effets d'interaction gene-diete specifiquement en lien avec la prise d'une supplementation en AGPI n-3 d'origine marine et la modification des facteurs de risque lipidiques des MCV. Cela permettra d'identifier les individus a haut risque de MCV qui par leur predisposition genetique pourraient beneficier davantage d'une supplementation en AGPI n-3 d'origine marine. Ultimement, grace a ces connaissances nous pourrons contribuer a prevenir les MCV.

TitreApplicationTitle: Promoting Neural Regeneration and Functional Recovery after Chronic and Severe Spinal Cord Injury
Keywords-MotsClés: AXONAL REGENERATION; CELL TRANSPLANTATION; COMPLETE TRANSECTION; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GENE THERAPY; MOTOR TESTING; MTOR; PTEN; SCHWANN CELL; SPINAL CORD INJURY
Abstract-Résumé: Though spinal cord injury (SCI) affects an estimated 42,000 Canadians, no treatment options aimed at reversing symptoms of this devastating disease exist. This is especially the case for patients suffering from complete injuries, which result in full paralysis and loss of sensory function below the site of injury. The cause of these dysfunctions is primarily the loss of projecting axons carrying electric signals. In other words, the inability of nerve cells to regenerate after injury permanently interrupts communication between the brain and the rest of the body. Transplantation of cells into the injured cord to coax tissue growth and activating intrinsic growth of cells that remain intact but damaged represent two strategies that could promote regeneration and functional recovery after SCI.  Previous work in our lab has shown that transplantation of skin-precursor derived Schwann Cells, a type of helper cell that promotes regeneration, promotes recovery when transplanted a week after injury. We have also demonstrated that inhibition of an enzyme called phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) can activate axonal growth after SCI in a supraspinal system of axons important for motor function. By combining these two therapies, we can potentially promote synergistic regeneration and recovery after severe injury.   In this study, we will assess the potential of this combination therapy to promote recovery after severe and chronic SCI. By assessing this therapy in a complete transection rodent model of injury, we can provide proof of principal that the therapy translates to a population of SCI patients who need treatments that reverse symptoms the most. By assessing this therapy at the chronic stage of injury, we can provide proof of principal that the therapy could reverse symptoms well after the injury itself has actually occurred. This work aims at preclinically validating a potential treatment as an important step forward in the cure for paralysis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Marqueurs neuropsychologiques et en SPECT du développement de maladies neurodégénératives dans le trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal
Keywords-MotsClés: DEMENCE A CORPS DE LEWY; MALADIE DE PARKINSON; MALADIES NEURODEGENERATIVES; MARQUEURS EN SPECT; MARQUEURS NEUROPSYCHOLOGIQUES; TROUBLE COGNITIF LEGER; TROUBLE COMPORTEMENTAL EN SOMMEIL PARADOXAL
Abstract-Résumé: Le trouble comportemental en sommeil paradoxal est un trouble de sommeil qui se caracterise par des comportements anormaux et souvent violents au cours du sommeil paradoxal. Les patients souffrant de ce trouble presentent des perturbations des fonctions cognitives et du flot sanguin cerebral regional similaires a ceux retrouves chez les patients ayant la maladie de Parkinson ou la demence a corps de Lewy. Ainsi, ces anomalies observees dans le TCSP pourraient representer un signe precoce du developpement d'une maladie neurodegenerative. Le but de cette etude vise a identifier des signes discrets de neurodegeneration et de marqueurs precoces de maladies neurodegeneratives dans le TCSP. Plus precisement, nous cherchons a detecter des anomalies dans les fonctions cognitives et dans le flot sanguin cerebral dans le TCSP, en utilisant une evaluation neuropsychologique complete et une technique specifique d'imagerie par resonance magnetique fonctionnelle nommee tomographie d'emission monophotonique. Nous effectuons un suivi longitudinal des patients TCSP, ce qui permet la comparaison de leurs evaluations sur plusieurs annees, pour determiner si l'evaluation initiale permet la prediction du developpement futur de la MP ou de la DCL. Ce projet de recherche s'avere tres important pour l'avancement des connaissances sur le developpement des maladies neurodegeneratives. En effet, il sera possible d'etablir un portrait clinique des patients plus a  risque de developper la MP ou la DCL en identifiant certains marqueurs SPECT et neuropsychologiques. Si nous pouvons preciser le profil evolutif des sujets avec TCSP, nous pourrons alors verifier si des traitements de neuroprotection presentement en developpement peuvent prevenir ou retarder l'apparition d'une maladie neurodegenerative chez ces sujets.

TitreApplicationTitle: Social anxiety from disfigurement due to medical illness: From assessment to intervention
Keywords-MotsClés: ACQUIRED DISFIGUREMENT FROM MEDICAL ILLNESS; BODY IMAGE AND APPEARANCE DISTRESS; HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE; INTERVENTION DEVELOPMENT AND PILOT TESTING; PATIENT-ORIENTED RESEARCH; PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES; PSYCHOMETRIC ASSESSMENT; QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS; SCLERODERMA; SOCIAL ANXIETY
Abstract-Résumé: Disfigurement from medical illness has been linked to mental health problems, and interventions addressing these problems focus on reducing discomfort in social situations. No studies, however, have looked at how common it is for people with disfigurement from illness or injury to experience clinical levels of anxiety in social situations. Systemic sclerosis (SSc), or scleroderma, is a rare, chronic illness that frequently leads to visible appearance changes and extensive skin disfigurement. People with SSc rate appearance changes as one of the most significant stressors of having the illness. The goal of the proposed project is to determine how often people with SSc experience clinical levels of anxiety in social situations, to examine what factors are associated with these feelings, and to develop and pilot test an online intervention to help them manage distress related to their body image concerns, including anxiety in social situations. The project will involve interviewing people with SSc to better understand their experiences of living with a visibly different appearance, as well as collecting information from these individuals through questionnaires that ask about discomfort in social settings. Using the information collected by these means, I will outline and pilot test an online intervention to reduce the distress, anxiety, and discomfort that people with SSc feel related to their appearance. This project is the first time such issues have been examined among people with disfigurement from a medical illness, and it constitutes an important step towards increasing public awareness as well as improving the mental health of these individuals. The developmental work proposed here will serve as a significant foundation for future large-scale trials, and towards broad dissemination of the intervention, with the goal to reach as many Canadians with SSc as possible who may be experiencing anxiety or distress about their physical appearance.

TitreApplicationTitle: Design of a novel mutant human coagulation protein as a new anticoagulant drug, and as a tool for investigating the activity and regulation key enzymes in blood coagulation.
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD COAGULATION PROTEINS; ENZYME KINETICS; HEPARINS AND OTHER ANTICOAGULANTS ( BLOOD THINNERS); VENOUS AND ARTERIAL THROMBOEMBOLISM
Abstract-Résumé: Heart attacks and strokes, the number one cause of death and disability in Canada, are often caused by defective blood clotting in the human body. This research project aims to translate discoveries made on the scientific bench to the bedside, by figuring out the way blood clots are controlled in the body in order to identify novel therapeutic strategies. In the past several years, numerous new anti-clotting drugs have entered the market worldwide for the treatment of strokes that target the blood clotting system. Unfortunately, given the biological nature of these new agents, readily accessible and effective antidotes and unavailable. This creates a major barrier to the widespread use of these easy to administer lifesaving drugs because for some patients, these drugs can cause life-threatening bleeding. These at-risk patients would need an antidote to quickly reverse their anticoagulation. Our laboratory has engineered a new molecule for which we have pilot data on a novel way to use this molecule to measure the action of the critical parts of the blood clotting system called tenase and prothrombinase. Because this part of the system is also the target for these new drugs, a clearer understanding of how they work aid in the development of an effective antidote for the new anti-clotting agents. Because our molecule also directly targets the tenase and prothrombinase systems, this new molecule or versions of it has the potential to become a new drug anti-clotting therapy for the treatment of heart attacks and stroke.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identification of GATA4 regulatory mechanisms associated with heart development and disease
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIAC DEVELOPMENT; GENE REGULATION; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY; MUTAGENESIS; POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS; PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS; PROTEOMICS
Abstract-Résumé: Abnormalities associated with the cardiac protein GATA4 are linked to congenital heart diseases such as septal or valvular defects, the single largest class of human birth defect. In Canada, approximately 1 in 100 children each year are born with these cardiac abnormalities, ranging from small holes that do not impede significantly on heart function to life threatening deformities that affect the heart's ability to pump oxygen and nutrients around the body. GATA4, originally identified by the Nemer lab, has proven to be a key player in cardiac form and function and multiple laboratories have demonstrated that minor modifications (mutations) to its structure can lead to various forms of congenital heart disease. However, it is unclear how these mutations lead to disease. Our working hypothesis is that normal function of GATA4 requires the interaction with other proteins, some of which are disrupted when GATA4 is mutated. Likewise, we hypothesize that these mutations could also alter the post-translational modification of GATA4, a critical cellular mechanism to control protein function. For my doctoral research, I will identify GATA4 protein interacting partners and post-translational modification sites in cardiac cells and the effect of GATA4 mutations on these interactions. The information garnered from this project will be of particular value to the community as it will provide knowledge on the genetic basis of cardiac disease which can be used to create new and effective treatments for those born with congenital heart diseases.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dissecting Mechanisms of Echinocandin Tolerance and Resistance in the Fungal Pathogen Candida albicans
Keywords-MotsClés: ANTIFUNGALS; CANDIDA ALBICANS; DRUG RESISTANCE; DRUG TOLERANCE; ECHINOCANDINS; FUNGAL PATHOGENS; GENE EXPRESSION; GENOMICS; HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY PROFILING; HEAT SHOCK PROTEIN 90 (HSP90)
Abstract-Résumé: Candida albicans is the leading cause of fungal infection in humans, and is capable of causing lethal bloodstream infections in immunocompromised individuals, including patients with HIV and those undergoing chemotherapy. There are a very limited number of antifungal drug classes available for treatment of these infections that do not have toxic side effects to the patient. The echinocandins are the only new class of antifungals to reach the clinic in decades, and function by causing loss of fungal cell wall integrity, thus killing the cell. C. albicans has developed resistance to these drugs and therefore there is a pressing need for new strategies to block resistance and improve the efficacy of the few antifungals available. The main mechanism of resistance to the echinocandins is mutations in the drug target; however, additional mechanisms remain to be determined. The goal of my project is to identify new mechanisms of echinocandin resistance, and to develop therapeutic strategies to reduce this resistance. As a pilot, I have screened a library of C. albicans gene deletion mutants to look for genes that are involved in the response to the echinocandins. I propose to perform this screen on a large scale, using a larger gene deletion library, and to delete the relevant genes in an echinocandin-resistant strain of C. albicans to see if resistance is reduced. In order to develop new therapeutic strategies to reduce this resistance, I have initially screened a library of drug compounds for those that are able to improve the efficacy of the echinocandins against a resistant strain of C. albicans. I have identified 19 such compounds, and propose to screen further drug libraries. Future investigations will involve testing toxicity to mammalian cells, and determining the modes of action of these compounds. My project is poised to identify new mechanisms involved in echinocandin resistance and has broad therapeutic potential.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding the beneficial role of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) for normalizing intestinal lipoprotein metabolism during insulin resistance
Keywords-MotsClés: APOB48; CHYLOMICRON; DYSLIPIDEMIA; EXENDIN-4; GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1; INTRACEREBROVENTRICULAR INJECTION; POSTPRANDIAL LIPOPROTEIN; SMALL INTESTINE; SYRIAN GOLDEN HAMSTER MODEL; TYPE 2 DIABETES
Abstract-Résumé: Type 2 diabetes has been labelled a world-wide epidemic, with 285 million individuals currently affected; a number that is expected to reach 439 million by the year 2030. Though this condition is known for causing high blood sugar levels, abnormalities in blood lipoproteins are what ultimately account for two thirds of patient deaths. Lipoproteins are carriers of fats in the blood and their accumulation in type 2 diabetes leads to the clogging of blood vessels and damage to the heart. This emphasizes our need to understand of how lipoprotein production is regulated in the body, in order to create therapies that will provide patients with the best long-term prospects. The small intestine is an important contributor to lipoprotein production. After a meal has been consumed, fat from the ingested food is absorbed by the intestine and packaged into lipoproteins called chylomicrons, which then travel in the bloodstream. Recently, a hormone called glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) has shown promise in its ability to reduce chylomicron production in the diabetic state. However, the way in which this occurs remains unknown. My research aims to determine which processes involved in chylomicron production are modulated by GLP-1. I also aim to understand whether this hormone acts directly on small intestine cells, or whether it activates nerve signals that regulate intestinal function. Our findings would give insight into how the production of chylomicrons can be controlled by hormone therapy, and which molecular targets are affected. Such data could potentially yield a new approach to preventing heart disease-related complications in type 2 diabetic patients where GLP-1 production is defective, ultimately improving patient health and survival.

TitreApplicationTitle: Underlying Neurobiological and Cognitive Mechanisms of Disability in Social Anxiety and Schizophrenia
Keywords-MotsClés: EEG; EYE-TRACKING; SCHIZOPHRENIA; SOCIAL ANXIETY; SOCIAL FUNCTIONING; THREAT PROCESSING
Abstract-Résumé: In Canada, the burden of mental illness is more than 1.5 times that of all cancers. Social anxiety disorder and schizophrenia are among the most debilitating illnesses worldwide and place a substantial financial burden on the Canadian health care system. Perhaps surprisingly, these two disorders often co-occur and share remarkable similarities. Both are characterized by social avoidance, maladaptive thought patterns, irrational fears, and enhanced processing of threatening stimuli. Both conditions also share similar genes, neurochemistry, and abnormal brain activity. My research aims to investigate the neurobiological and cognitive mechanisms that account for enhanced threat response in social anxiety and paranoia. Identification of novel biomarkers that explain this overlap in pathology can lead to more effective treatments. Participants in this study will complete measures of threat sensitivity, using electroencephalograph (EEG) and eye-tracking technology to tap brain mechanisms involved in threat processing, as well as measures of coping strategies, flexible thinking, and social skills. My research project can help identify specific cognitive and neural mechanisms that will help explain differences in the manifestation of symptoms in these two disorders. The results of this study will provide a fuller understanding of the mechanisms that relate to everyday behaviour, as it is the underlying brain mechanisms and presenting clinical features, not simply diagnosis, that act as a barrier to functional recovery in Canadians with mental health problems. Identifying underlying mechanisms of illness will improve knowledge about the treatment of chronic mental disorders. The promotion and dissemination of evidence-based research can aid future endeavours in the prevention and treatment of mental illness, ultimately increasing the health of Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Reducing symptom distress in long-term survivors of colorectal cancer: A Symptom Management Intervention
Keywords-MotsClés: COLORECTAL CANCER; GENDER; LONG-TERM OUTCOMES; PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS; QUALITY OF LIFE; SYMPTOM MANGEMENT; SYMPTOM SEVERITY
Abstract-Résumé: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the fourth most common type of cancer and second most common cause of cancer-related deaths for both men and women in Canada. Although treatments have improved survival, they can cause lasting side effects, such as bowel dysfunction, sexual dysfunction, fatigue, and worse quality of life (QOL). Data are surprisingly lacking on the long-term physical and psychological symptoms, symptom management problems, and their associated distress after treatment for CRC. Although symptom management programs have been developed for other cancers, none exist for long-term CRC survivors. Therefore, this project makes a novel contribution to the survivorship care planning of this population by examining symptom severity and symptom management problems in long-term CRC survivors and designing and implementing a symptom management intervention.

TitreApplicationTitle: Psychological Adjustment Over Time in Couples Facing Multiple Sclerosis: Predictors and Moderators
Keywords-MotsClés: DEPRESSION; DISABILITY; HEALTH ANXIETY; INTERPERSONAL RELATIONSHIPS; MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS; PHYSICAL SYMPTOMS; PSYCHOSOCIAL ADJUSTMENT; RELATIONSHIP DYNAMICS; RELATIONSHIP SATISFACTION
Abstract-Résumé: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) is a prevalent chronic illness characterized by a range of physical symptoms. Depression, health anxiety (fear of illness and intrusive health-related thoughts), and relationship distress are common psychological outcomes reported by both MS patients and their partners. Although evidence has suggested that physical symptoms predict worse psychological adjustment, little is known about protective factors. The present study examines whether physical symptoms predict depression, health anxiety, and relationship distress over 12 months in MS couples, and how relationship dynamics buffer or exacerbate these associations. 120 couples will be recruited through existing partnerships with St. Michael's Hospital MS Clinic and the MS Society of Canada. Participants will each complete an online survey at baseline, six-months, and one year follow-up that assesses physical symptoms (fatigue, pain, cognitive impairment, and disability), positive and negative relationship dynamics (communication, social support, constraints from one's partner on illness-related communication, and hostile conflict), and psychological outcomes (depression, health anxiety, and relationship adjustment). It is expected that greater physical symptoms will predict greater depression, health anxiety, and relationship distress over time. It is also predicted that positive relationship dynamics will buffer the effect of greater symptoms on worse outcomes, while negative dynamics will exacerbate it. The high rate of negative outcomes in MS couples calls for a greater understanding of predictors and moderators. The present study will add to the current literature by identifying temporally valid predictors of couples' psychological outcomes. Additionally, identifying positive and negative relationship dynamics that protect couples from the negative effects of physical symptoms, or exacerbate their detrimental impact, will inform psychological interventions.

TitreApplicationTitle: Physical activity in pregnancy in relation with child's growth from birth to two years of age
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIO-RESPIRATORY FITNESS; EXERCISE PHYSIOLOGY; MUSCULAR FITNESS; NEONATES; OBESITY; PERINATALITY; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY INTERVENTION; POST-NATAL GROWTH; PREGNANCY
Abstract-Résumé: With the current obesity pandemic, it is crucial to identify non-optimal environment during pregnancy and design interventions that can prevent its effect in order to enhance mother's and infant's well being. Physical activity can influence maternal nutrition, body mass index and weight gain during pregnancy, all contributors to infant birth weight. The effects of maternal exercise during pregnancy on infant birth weight may also be different according to maternal obesity and fitness level at the time of pregnancy.  Moreover, the effects of maternal exercise during pregnancy on infant body composition and weight at birth are still quite unknown. Thus, this study aims at verifying whether physical activity and maternal fitness during pregnancy can influence infant birth weight and growth. First, we will investigate the influence of physical activity before and during pregnancy on infant body composition (weight, length, and fat mass at birth, 3 months and 2 years old) in a large cohort of pregnant women. Secondly, we will document the relationship between maternal fitness, a sensitive marker of exercise training, and newborn percentage of lean and fat mass. Finally, we will evaluate if the participation in an exercise program during the 2nd trimester of pregnancy reinforces healthy life habits later in pregnancy in a group of obese women, who are at increased risk of complications during pregnancy. Effects of exercise on maternal fitness and newborn's anthropometry at birth will be also evaluated. These studies will contribute towards determining if physical activity in pregnancy is beneficial to both mother and child, and ultimately, if it has the potential to reduce the incidence of obesity in infancy.

Abstract-Résumé: L'obesite et le diabete de type 2 ont des proportions epidemiques. La Vitamine A (acide retinoique-AR) est un nutriment bioactif. Nos etudes sur animaux montrent que l'AR induit une normalisation glycemique et une diminution de l'obesite. C'est une importante contribution a la  connaissance de l'action de l'AR dans le foie, gras et muscles, via la transcription des genes du metabolisme des retinoides, energetique, l'oxydation des acides gras et la resistance a l'insuline. Ceci identifie des nouveaux effets antidiabetiques et peut conduire a des remedes anti-obesite et antidiabetiques issus des retinoides. L'administration orale et l'absorption gastro-intestinale peuvent reduire les couts des traitements.         L'originalite de notre equipe (seule dans l'Est Canadien qui aborde l'obesite et le diabete par l'implication des retinoides dans plusieurs voies metaboliques d'interet preventif et therapeutique) fait que la plus recente revue de litterature de specialite publie par Biochimica Biophysica Acta (Bonet, Ribot, Palou et al. Universite des Iles-Baleares, Spain, 2012) nous classifie parmi les 12 equipes au monde ayant genere des donnees probantes dans ce domaine. La prestigieuse revue pharmaceutique britannique Lead-Discovery a classifie notre projet parmi «les recherches les plus prometteuses avec grand potentiel pour rapidement aboutir au developpement d'un nouveaux medicament efficace » donc « de tres grand interet pour l'industrie pharmaceutique». Les retombees de valeur de nos recherches -(cliniques, sante publique et communautaire, nutrition et industries alimentaires)- sont facilement transferables a la societe par les collaborations du CRCHUM. Obtenir un remede antidiabetique, novateur et peu dispendieux au Canada en premiere mondiale, aura un echo international important.

TitreApplicationTitle: Do alpha 5 GABA-A receptors contribute to memory impairment after traumatic brain injury?
Keywords-MotsClés: BRAIN INJURY; ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY; GABA SUBTYPE A RECEPTORS; INFLAMMATION; TONIC CURRENT
Abstract-Résumé: Each year, approximately 1.7 million North Americans sustain a traumatic brain injury with an estimated 90,000 people experiencing long-term disability as a result. Memory deficits are among the most common and enduring impairments following traumatic brain injury. Unfortunately, the molecular mechanisms underlying the condition remain elusive and there is no effective treatment strategy to improve memory performance.   Previous studies showed that the hippocampus, a brain region that plays a key role in learning and memory, is particularly vulnerable to brain injury. Damage to brain cells, or neurons, in this brain region is often credited with the onset of memory deficits following injury. However, even in the absence of severe damage to neurons, traumatic brain injury is still associated with persistent memory impairments. These impairments could arise as a result of disruption in the normal activity, or neurotransmission, of surviving neurons. Therefore, understanding the effect of brain injury on neurotransmission could help explain and ultimately treat the memory impairments associated with traumatic brain injury.  Our laboratory was the first to identify a specific group of 'memory blocking' receptors, which are highly expressed in the hippocampus. Drugs that activate these receptors cause memory impairment while drugs that block these receptors can improve memory performance. In this study we propose that brain injury could increase the activity of these 'memory blocking' receptors thereby causing memory deficits. Furthermore, we suggest that selectively blocking these receptors after traumatic brain injury may improve memory.  Therefore this study will provide insights into the mechanism by which memory impairment may occur following mild to moderate brain injury and identify a possible treatment strategy for the condition. We also anticipate that our results could provide the foundation for future clinical trials.

TitreApplicationTitle: Understanding Recent Trends in Chlamydia in Ontario Using Applied Epidemiology and Mathematical Modeling
Keywords-MotsClés: CHLAMYDIA TRACHOMATIS; EPIDEMIOLOGY; HEALTH ECONOMICS; MATHEMATICAL MODELING; PUBLIC HEALTH; SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS
Abstract-Résumé: Chlamydia is a sexually transmitted infection and is the most common infectious disease in Canada. Although most people infected with Chlamydia have no or mild symptoms, if untreated, it can cause pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) in women, a condition that is associated with infertility, ectopic (tubal) pregnancy, and chronic pelvic pain. A screening test can be used to identify and treat individuals who are infected with Chlamydia but have no symptoms. Canada has expanded screening programs over the past 20 years, with the aim of decreasing the number of Chlamydia infections. However, the opposite effect has been observed; Chlamydia infections continue to increase in the population. The goal of the current project is try to understand why Chlamydia infections are not decreasing, even though we are finding and treating more cases. We think that this increase is to be expected, because we are screening and testing more people who don't have symptoms. To test this idea, we are working with public health units in Ontario to look at trends in the number of Chlamydia cases, the number of screening tests they are performing, and the number of PID cases that are occurring. If we are finding and treating more cases in people who would otherwise go on to develop PID, we would expect to see a decrease in the number of PID cases reported over time. We will use statistical methods to test this hypothesis. We will use these results to construct mathematical models, which are simplified representations of how Chlamydia is spread in a population. These models will help us to understand why we are observing an increase in Chlamydia cases over time, and will let us test, in a simulated environment, how different strategies for controlling Chlamydia might alter disease patterns in the future. Using these models, we can also assess how much we expect these different strategies to cost, since health care decision-making occurs in the context of limited resources.

TitreApplicationTitle: Evaluating the use of isometric handgrip exercise as a stimulus for long-term blood pressure reductions: is there a causal link to heat shock proteins and/or the autonomic nervous system?
Keywords-MotsClés: BLOOD PRESSURE CONTROL; EXERCISE; HYPERTENSION; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; LIFESTYLE INTERVENTION; PREDICTION
Abstract-Résumé: There is a strong relationship between increasing blood pressure (BP) and declining cardiovascular health. This is particularly true in post-menopausal women due to the lost vascular protection of estrogen. Securing control over resting BP is of the utmost importance. This control can be accomplished with regular exercise, such as isometric handgrip exercise (IHG). The use of IHG to produce desirable BP responses in post-menopausal women is an understudied technique. Our research team has shown a link between long-term reductions in resting BP following eight weeks of exercise training and an acute vascular response called post exercise hypotension (PEH).  PEH is a short lasting drop in BP that consistently follows a single exercise bout. It is important to investigate both the long-term effect of IHG on resting BP and the short-term effect of IHG on PEH.   In order to fully understand IHG as an exercise protocol we must understand the vascular mechanisms it works through. Extracellular heat shock proteins are one potential mechanism. The proposed research will examine: in a population of post-menopausal women using IHG as an exercise stimulus (1) Do acute BP responses (PEH) correlate with long term BP reductions? (2) What is the mechanistic role of eHSP in both acute and long term BP control? (3) Is the exercise induced release of eHSPs mediated through the basal autonomic nervous system (ANS) excitability?  Post-menopausal women with slightly elevated resting BP will be recruited for study participation. Both short-term and long-term physiological responses will be examined following the IHG exercise stimulus.  The evaluation of vascular responses following IHG in post-menopausal women must occur if we want to develop alternative strategies for optimal vascular health. This information will be valuable to women and clinical staff alike, as we aim to better the cardiovascular health of the aging population.

TitreApplicationTitle: Étude des mécanismes d'induction de la réponse immunitaire par des nanoparticules adjuvantes

Abstract-Résumé: Les nanoparticules du PapMV sont connues comme etant un adjuvant pouvant etre utilise dans des preparations vaccinales. Ces particules contiennent un stimulateur du systeme immunitaire qui leur confere des proprietes d'adjuvant vaccinal. Cependant, le mecanisme impliquant la reconnaissance des particules par le systeme immunitaire reste encore inconnu. Le projet presente a pour but d'elucider ce mecanisme. L'etude de ce contact est essentielle a la comprehension et a l'amelioration des capacites d'adjuvant des nanoparticules du PapMV. Une meilleure reconnaissance signifie que les nanoparticules seront plus efficaces et auront un plus grand potentiel d'adjuvant. Ainsi, la dose necessaire afin d'obtenir une reponse immune maximale sera fortement diminuee. Les nanoparticules du PapMV pourront ainsi etre utilisees a moindre cout pour bonifier un vaccin.

TitreApplicationTitle: Examining the role of physical activity in improving cancer-related outcomes in shift workers
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOLOGICAL; BREAST CANCER; INTERVENTION; LIFESTYLE; OCCUPATIONAL; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY; PREVENTION; QUALITY OF LIFE; SHIFT WORK; SLEEP HYGIENE
Abstract-Résumé: Shiftwork with circadian disruption has been classified as a Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans) carcinogen and has been linked with increased breast cancer incidence. The biological mechanisms for this link to breast cancer are not yet completely understood, however, disruptions in sleep and associated changes in biological markers which may impact breast cancer development, have been implicated. To date there is little intervention research that has been conducted in the area of shiftwork and breast cancer. Project 1 will evaluate the relationship between physical activity and biological markers of breast cancer risk, as well as investigate the barriers to and preferences of physical activity participation in this population. This information will be used to guide Project 2, a physical activity intervention in female night shift workers at high risk for breast cancer. The aim of this study is to improve aerobic capacity, and reduce biological markers of breast cancer risk.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cancer screening knowledge and decision-making among transgender populations
Keywords-MotsClés: AND CANCER HEALTH; GENDER; KNOWLEDGE MOBILITY; SEXUALITY; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH DECISION-MAKING; TRANSGENDER HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: Research and literature in the area of transgender health consistently reports that this population experiences numerous barriers in accessing health care generally, and cancer care specifically, resulting in treatment avoidance. In order to address population health disparities, effective health care provision needs to be informed by research that directly concerns transgender people's health care knowledge and decision-making. This research project will address a growing gap in health literature regarding transgender people's cancer screening experiences by directly assessing a diverse group of transgender people's knowledge of cancer health and how gender identity impacts decision-making regarding health care generally, and specifically, screening for breast, gynecological, and prostate cancers. Results of this study will be of benefit to understanding the impacts of gender identity on cancer health, as well as yielding transferable knowledge that will contribute to the provision of culturally competent and effective cancer screening protocols for transgender people and the quality of cancer care for all Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Est-il possible de dissocier une émotion musicale d'une émotion vocale?
Keywords-MotsClés: ANALYSE DE PATRONS MULTI-VOXELS; CONECTIVITE; EMOTION; IMAGERIE (IRMF); IMAGERIE (MEG); MUSIQUE; NEUROCOGNITION; PERCEPTION; PROCESSUS COGNITIFS; VOIX
Abstract-Résumé: Pourquoi la musique nous emeut-elle? Une des possibilites pour expliquer ce phenomene est que les emotions musicales utilisent les zones cerebrales, qui se sont developpees pour percevoir les emotions vocales (tres utiles pour interagir en societe). Ce projet de recherche tentera de determiner comment notre cerveau percoit les emotions liees a la musique et determinera si ce traitement est different de celui utilise pour percevoir les emotions vocales. La realisation de ce projet requiert plusieurs etapes. Dans un premier temps, des courts extraits musicaux neutres et d'autres exprimant la peur, la joie, la tristesse ont enregistre de maniere a etre tres comparables aux Voix Affectives Montrealaises (deja enregistrees). Par la suite, nous ferons entendre ces extraits musicaux et vocaux a des participants lors d'experiences dans deux types d'appareils d'imagerie differents. Une premiere tache sera realisee dans un scanner d'imagerie par resonance magnetique pour identifier les regions activees lors de l'ecoute de ces deux types de sons. Une fois ces regions identifiees l'experience sera repetee en magnetoencephalographie (MEG) pour determiner comment ces regions communiquent entre elles. En combinant ces sons et ces deux techniques d'imagerie, nous pourrons comparer la maniere dont les emotions musicales et vocales sont traitees par notre cerveau. Il y a plusieurs manieres d'explorer comment notre cerveau fonctionne et une d'entre elles est par le systeme auditif. Cette etude pourra non seulement nous aider a comprendre le fonctionnement du systeme auditif et la maniere dont notre cerveau percoit et analyse les emotions, mais apportera aussi des connaissances anatomiques plus precises sur ces systemes qui pourront etre utilises par les neuropsychologues et les neurochirurgiens. De maniere plus generale, ces etudes apporteront aussi un soutien aux programmes de traitement utilisant la musique comme outils de readaptation ou de relaxation.

TitreApplicationTitle: Implication of CNK in the regulation of RAS/MAPK pathway
Keywords-MotsClés: CANCER; KSR; PROTEIN INTERACTION; RAF; RAS/MAPK; SIGNALISATION
Abstract-Résumé: Cancer is currently the main cause of mortality in Canada and around 500 people die of it every day. Even with prevention and scientific progress, there is still a severe lack of effective therapeutics to cure cancer. Relapse occurs well too often with more aggressive and frequently metastasized tumours that become resistant to initial treatments. Our laboratory focuses mainly on the RAS/MAPK pathway, whose dysregulation is observed in a third of all human cancers. This pathway comprises enzymes that interact with each other to transmit proliferation signals within the cells. Activating mutations in the small GTPase RAS and the kinase RAF are the most prevalent mutations that cause overactivation of the RAS/MAPK pathway in cancer cells. Components of the RAS/MAPK pathway are highly conserved through evolution, from simple organisms such worms and flies to mammals. Our laboratory takes advantage of the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster to study this pathway because of the availability of powerful biological tools and the greater simplicity of its genome compared to mammals. Two key proteins required for the RAS/MAPK pathway have been discovered in Drosophila, namely, KSR (Kinase suppressor of RAS) and CNK (Connector eNhancer of KSR). These proteins have the ability to bridge together the central components of the RAS/MAPK pathway, which are known as RAS, RAF, MEK and MAPK. The goal of my project is to delineate at a molecular level the specific impact that CNK impinges on the RAS/MAPK pathway. Given that these proteins are also fund in mammalian cells, this work will contribute to our understanding of the RAS/MAPK pathway and thereby should lead to the development of better anticancer therapeutic agents

TitreApplicationTitle: Design and evaluation of a maneuverable, inflatable, cannulated device to facilitate long bone fracture reduction
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOENGINEERING; DRIVABLE WIRE; FLUOROSCOPIC GUIDANCE; FRACTURE RECONSTRUCTION; FRACTURE REDUCTION; IMPLANT DESIGN; INTRAMEDULLARY NAILING PREPARATION; MECHANICAL TESTING; ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY; PRESSURIZATION
Abstract-Résumé: Fixing broken bones first requires reconstructing the fractured pieces before the permanent hardware can be attached to stabilize the bone. In fixing the femur (thigh bone), fractures are most commonly treated with a long nail placed surgically down the centre of the bone. Alignment of the fractured fragments is generally accomplished manually to allow an initial wire to be placed down the canal before the nail is inserted. However, current methods of fracture reduction remain technically challenging and are often time consuming extending the patient's time in the operating room. The objective of the proposed research is to design and evaluate a novel device that facilitates the initial reduction of fractured long bones. The design will allow navigation of the device through malaligned fracture fragments. The performance of the device (prototype) will be tested in its ability to reconstruct fractured femurs using a jig that enables simulation of consistent fracture displacement and compared to the standard fracture reduction technique. Performance will also be evaluated based on the time, radiation exposure and forces required to realign each fracture, as well as ease of use, potential user challenges and overall surgeon satisfaction. Overall, fracture reduction should be facilitated by the drivable nature of this new device. The potential for reducing operative times with this device may translate into both improved outcomes and reduced health care costs for fracture reconstruction of the femur and other bones.

TitreApplicationTitle: Globalization of the Food and Agricultural Economies: The Impact of International Trade Policy on Canadian Food Security
Keywords-MotsClés: FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL TRADE; FOOD SECURITY INITIATIVES; FOOD SECURITY POLICY; GLOBALIZATION; INTERNATIONAL TRADE AND INVESTMENT AGREEMENTS; POLICY ANALYSIS; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH
Abstract-Résumé: The World Food Summit defined food security as existing "when all people, at all times, have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food to meet their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy lifestyle." Despite the fact that enough food is produced globally to feed everyone in the world, an estimated 925 million people live with chronic hunger. In Canada, 851,014 citizens accessed a food bank monthly in 2011, the second highest level of use on record. With the increasing integration of world economies there has been rapid growth in the number of regional, bilateral and multilateral trade and investment agreements involving food and agriculture, which has had broad consequences for food security. The capacity of the state to manage public health policy is increasingly challenged by trade and investment treaties that are shrinking the policy space within which food security initiatives can be developed and implemented. This study will conduct a policy analysis to examine how international agricultural trade and investment agreements ratified by the Canadian government, or under consideration and publicly available for review, will influence the success of national food security policies. It will also examine the role of trade and investment agreements in the development and sustainability of local and national food security initiatives and the role of food security actors in trade policy. While numerous examinations have been conducted on the influence of trade on food security in developing nations, to date the body of work studying how global food trade has impacted food security in Canada has been negligible. Understanding the implications of trade policy on government capacity to enact socially responsible public health policy, such as food security, will be essential as we continue down the path of an increasingly globalized economy.

TitreApplicationTitle: L'activation des intentions comme intervention visant à promouvoir la saine alimentation chez des femmes enceintes à risque de diabète gestationnel
Keywords-MotsClés: ACTIVATION DES INTENTIONS; DIABETE GESTATIONNEL; ESSAI CLINIQUE ALEATOIRE; PROMOTION DE LA SANTE; PREVENTION; QUESTIONNAIRE; RECHERCHE QUALITATIVE; RECHERCHE QUANTITATIVE; SAINE ALIMENTATION; SANTE MATERNELLE
Abstract-Résumé: Au Canada, la prevalence du diabete de grossesse (DG) chez la population non autochtone est de 3,7%. Le DG peut avoir de graves consequences pour la femme enceinte et le foetus (e.g., diabete de type 2, macrosomie foetale). Des etudes recentes indiquent que l'utilisation d'interventions de type activation des intentions est efficace pour promouvoir la saine alimentation chez la population generale. L'activation des intentions est un type d'intervention psychosociale qui implique la completion d'un questionnaire comportant une liste de situations problematiques de type si (e.g., Si je suis presse...) et de solutions de type alors (...alors je vais utiliser des legumes surgeles deja appretes). A notre connaissance, une intervention de ce type n'a jamais ete testee chez des femmes enceintes a risque de developper du DG.  L'objectif de l'etude est d'evaluer  l'efficacite d'une intervention de type activation des intentions chez cette population. Un total de 128 femmes enceintes a risque de developper du DG seront reparties au hasard entre le groupe experimental et le groupe controle. L'intervention se fera a l'aide d'un questionnaire qui sera distribue par les medecins du Centre hospitalier universitaire de Quebec (CHUQ) qui effectuent des suivis de grossesse. La consommation de fruits et legumes sera evaluee au debut de l'intervention et a chaque visite medicale par un questionnaire valide. Des affiches seront posees dans les salles d'attente et les medecins de famille, gynecologues et obstetriciens du CHUQ seront contactes pour les informer du projet. Ce projet permettra de verifier si l'activation des intentions est une bonne strategie pour promouvoir la consommation de fruits et legumes chez les femmes enceintes a risque de developper du DG. Si tel est le cas, elle pourrait etre implantee a plus grande echelle et diminuer les risques de complications chez les femmes a risque de developper du DG, ce qui serait benefique a la fois pour la mere et l'enfant.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development and Evaluation of an Interpretation Modification Program for Enhancing Treatment of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)
Keywords-MotsClés: ANXIETY DISORDERS TREATMENT; COGNITIVE BIAS; COGNITIVE-BEHAVIOURAL THERAPY; INTERPRETATION MODIFICATION TRAINING; PSYCHOPATHOLOGY; TREATMENT ACCESSIBILITY
Abstract-Résumé: Effective Cognitive-Behavioural treatment (CBT) protocols have been developed for Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), however research demonstrates that 30% of affected individuals do not fully benefit from treatment. Furthermore, many affected individuals do not seek treatment or do not have access to treatment and as a result, experience continued impairment in functioning and significant distress in their daily lives. As such, for my PhD research I plan to develop and evaluate the utility of an innovative treatment tool to decrease threat interpretation biases that are prevalent among individuals with GAD. Given the compelling support for the use of a computerized Interpretation Modification Program (IMP) in the treatment of Social Anxiety Disorder, I am very optimistic about the use of such a program for GAD. The computerized IMP is unique in that it targets more automatic information processing styles related to both a benign bias and a threat bias. Furthermore, the program takes approximately 10 minutes to complete and therefore has the potential to become a widely accessed and rapidly completed treatment tool to enhance current Cognitive-Behavioural Treatment protocols. In an effort to make the program as effective in treatment as possible, an additional objective of my research is to investigate whether or not anxious individuals benefit more from an individualized IMP (targeting specific domains of worry indicated by the client) compared to a generalized IMP (targeting all 10 domains of worry, commonly cited in the literature on GAD). This research will not only have important implications for targets of treatments, it also has the potential to result in establishing an easily administered and widely used therapy tool in treating generalized anxiety.

TitreApplicationTitle: Baseline Emotion Regulatory Capacity and Dialectical Behaviour Therapy Skills Training in Borderline Personality Disorder: A Multi-Method Investigation
Keywords-MotsClés: BORDERLINE PERSONALITY DISORDER; DIALECTICAL BEHAVIOUR THERAPY; EMOTION REGULATION; PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGY; SELF-INJURY; SUICIDE
Abstract-Résumé: Suicide and self-injury are serious issues in Canada, and rates of suicidal behaviours are disproportionately high in Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). BPD involves instability of self-image, relationships, emotions, behaviour, and cognitions. There is clear need to effectively treat, and reduce the suicidal behaviours, in BPD. Individuals with BPD display difficulties with emotion regulation, and suicidal or self-injurious behaviour in BPD is conceptualized as an attempt to regulate emotions. Effective treatments for BPD such as Dialectical Behaviour Therapy (DBT) focus on increasing healthy emotion regulation. However, these therapies are long (i.e., at least one year) and labour-intensive (i.e., involve both individual and group therapy components). Canadians would thus benefit from research examining the individual characteristics that render those with BPD as more or less likely to benefit from a shortened, group-therapy only version of DBT (i.e., 20-week DBT skills groups). The proposed study will collaborate with an ongoing study at the Centre for Addictions and Mental Health (CAMH) assessing the effectiveness of a 20-week DBT skills group (as an adjunct to treatment as usual) compared to a waitlist control in the treatment of chronically suicidal and non-suicidal self-injurious behaviours in BPD individuals. The proposed study will examine whether baseline difficulties with emotion regulation (i.e., decreased ability to change or regulate emotional responses as indicated by self-report and bodily changes in an experimental task) predict the reduction of suicidal and self-injurious behaviours in BPD individuals in a 20-week DBT skills group. The findings in the proposed study will indicate if baseline difficulties with emotion regulation can be used to select effective and efficient treatments for some individuals with BPD, thereby reducing the burden of long and labour-intensive treatments for patients, health care providers, and Canadian taxpayers.
