TitreApplicationTitle: Investigating the use of biclustering to identify blood mRNA biomarkers to monitor the efficacy and safety of pharmacological and nutritional compounds targeting MetS.
Keywords-MotsClés: BICLUSTERING; BIOMARKER DISCOVERY; COMPUTATIONAL STATISTICS; GENE EXPRESSION; METABOLIC SYNDROME; MICROARRAY; NUTRIGENOMICS; PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONONUCLEAR CELLS; RESVERATROL; ROSIGLITAZONE
Abstract-Résumé: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a common condition characterized by insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and abdominal obesity. Individuals with MetS have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes. Recent reports estimate that one in five Canadian adults have MetS, highlighting its prevalence in the general population. It is widely accepted that lifestyle modifications such as changing one's diet and exercise habits can be used to prevent MetS. The problem is that most people adopt these new lifestyle habits initially, but quickly revert back to their old "bad" habits. Thus, many people turn to pharmacological and nutritional compounds to help prevent and/or treat MetS. While traditional blood markers (e.g., glucose, free fatty acids) are used in clinical practice to monitor the effects of these compounds, these markers often miss important side effects that can have serious implications on a person's health. This is not surprising given that many pharmacological and nutritional compounds will affect tissues throughout the body. Because people are understandably reluctant to provide tissue samples, alternate screening methods are required. This research proposal will develop a new statistical approach to identify tissue-specific markers that can be measured in blood. This work will use tissue samples from a previous study using obese rats. This proposed work is important for a number of reasons. First, we will obtain a better understanding of how pharmacological and nutritional compounds influence the body. Second, we will develop a powerful new method that identifies blood markers that can reflect tissue function. Finding these new markers will help to better understand how compounds used to prevent and/or treat MetS affect the various tissues in our body, as well as lead to the possible development of new clinical tools that can be used to better monitor the development of side effects.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular underpinnings of how paternal prenatal exposure to environmentally-relevant organochlorines compromises health of future generations: A possible mechanism for health discrepancies between Northern Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal Canadians
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOINFORMATICS; ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS; EPIGENETIC; NORTHERN ABORIGINAL CANADIANS; ORIGINS OF DISEASE; PATERNAL HEALTH; PLACENTA; REDUCED REPRESENTATION BISULFITE SEQUENCING; RNA-SEQ; TRANSGENERATIONAL TRANSMISSION
Abstract-Résumé: Society is concerned about the impact of environmental contaminants on human health. Numerous highly publicized reports of deformities, disease and infertility have been attributed, at least in part, to environmental contaminants. Many contaminants work their way up the food chain, as is the case for organochlorines in Canada's Far North. Northern Aboriginal populations have a significantly higher body burden of environmental contaminants, which may contribute to the major health disparity compared to non-aboriginal Canadians. Moreover, the "developmental origins of adult disease" model has been proposed to explain how exposure of the developing foetus to environmental stressors while still in the womb predisposes it to dysfunction later in life. Although maternal exposures can affect child health and development, our recent disturbing findings indicate that the effects of environmental exposures can be transmitted to future generations via the father. These results shatter current public dogma that paternal health is inconsequential to child health. Our objective is to use our proven rat model to determine the molecular underpinnings of how contaminants of the Northern food chain perturb the development and health of the next and subsequent generations in a paternally-mediated manner. Our central hypothesis is that prenatal exposure of the F1 male offspring to environmentally-relevant organochlorines induces epimutations in his sperm's DNA that increase birth defects and health problems in his F2 offspring. These sperm epimutations are transgenerationally-transmitted though the father's sperm, thereby inducing health problems in future  generations. Together with our preliminary observations, our anticipated results will provide insight into many of the health concerns in the Far North, including high rates of preterm birth, stillbirth, infant mortality and poorer health of Inuit children and adults relative to non-Aboriginal Canadians.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effects of public policies on medical end-of-life practices: a systematic review
Keywords-MotsClés: ASSISTED SUICIDE; ETHICS; EUTHANASIA; HEALTH POLICY; HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Recent legal and political developements have put end-of-life policies at the forefront of Canadian debates. Comparative international studies could inform public deliberations, but making sense of international evidence is difficult because of inconsistent definitions and contextual health system differences.   This systematic review will address the following questions:  1) What are the effects of public policies on changes in medical end-of-life practices; 2) What is known of the effects of policies on different patient groups; 3) How do differences in context between countries influence the effects of policies?   We will search three electronic databases to identify studies comparing medical practices between countries with different policies, or within a single country before-and-after a change in policy. We developed a classification of medical end-of-life practices that distinguishes practices with different international legal status. We will compare the frequency of medical practices in countries with different public policies, or within countries before-and-after a change in policy. We will analyze variations in practices among different patient groups, and among countries with different contextual characteristics.   Reserch objectives  were established in collaboration with key organizations in Canada. Four deliberation meetings in two Canadian provinces will be conducted with policymakers, health professionals, and citizens to discuss the interpretation of findings and its implications for the canadian context. Communication of results will use publicly-accessible publications and plateforms. Our team brings together international experts in medicine, ethics, law, health policy, community psychology, social science, and systematic review methods. This systematic review has the potential to support better informed democratic deliberation on end-of-life policies in Canada.

TitreApplicationTitle: Early life determinants of obesity and metabolic compromise
Keywords-MotsClés: DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMMING; HIGH FAT DIET; INFLAMMATION; MATERNAL OBESITY; MICROBIOME; PLACENTA
Abstract-Résumé: Maternal obesity is the primary risk factor for childhood obesity and metabolic compromise, perpetuating a feed forward cycle of chronic disease risk for future generations. In this proposal we ask, how is it that exposure to an obesogenic environment in utero gives rise to children that are destined to become obese and what are the signalling pathways? Obesity is associated with chronic low-grade inflammation, which has been implicated in many chronic diseases such as diabetes. Obesity is associated with significant changes in gut permeability; it alters the gut microbiome and gut-derived bacterial components cause inflammation in metabolic tissues. We hypothesise that similarly, during obesity/high fat diet in pregnancy maternal gut-derived bacterial components could cause placental inflammation modifying placental and/or fetal development, predisposing offspring to obesity and chronic disease. In the proposed study, we will investigate how shifts in the pregnant gut microbiome affect maternal adaptation to pregnancy and how these microbial shifts impact placental and fetal development. We will determine if a shift in the pregnant microbiome is associated with alterations in maternal intestinal permeability and structure, promoting the translocation of maternally-derived bacteria to the placenta and/or the fetus thus promoting an pro-inflammatory in utero environment. This will further substantiate the role of the maternal gut microbiome and inflammation in the programming of childhood obesity and risk of chronic disease. Identification of underlying mechanisms relating early life events to long-term disease risk will inform new strategies in optimizing maternal and childhood health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Exposition aux perturbateurs endocriniens contenus dans les produits d'usage courant et effets sur la santé reproductive. Une revue systématique.

Abstract-Résumé: De nombreuses substances chimiques entrent dans la composition des produits d'usage courant(Cosmetiques, jouets, pesticides, produits de nettoyage, etc.). Du nombre, un type de substance souleve a la fois un enjeu majeur de sante publique et un defi de taille aux chercheurs et aux gestionnaires travaillant sur les effets sur la sante des substances chimiques. L'exposition quotidienne et a de faibles doses aux perturbateurs endocriniens aurait pour consequence d'affecter profondement les mecanismes de fonctionnement du systeme hormonal chez l'humain. Les effets potentiels pour la sante de la population canadienne commencent a peine a etre compris, mais posent deja des problematiques majeures pour la sante reproductive (anomalies du systeme reproducteur, dereglement des mecanismes lies au genre et aux hormones sexuelles, fertilite, etc.). A l'heure ou les jeunes filles et les jeunes garcons ayant possiblement ete le plus exposes des leur conception a ces substances relativement nouvelles arrivent en age de procreer, des travaux scientifiques ont ete realises dans un ensemble de domaines (toxicologie, biologie, medecine, etc.) sans avoir ete synthetises et rendus accessibles, et les gestionnaires de la sante publique et les medecins demeurent peu outilles pour detecter des problematiques qui pourraient etre associees aux perturbateurs endocriniens et suggerer des moyens pour diminuer l'exposition a ces substances. Ce projet d'analyse et de revue systematique des connaissances, mene par une equipe de chercheurs provenant de diverses disciplines vise ainsi a consolider les donnees pertinentes afin d'en faire beneficier les principaux types d'intervenants susceptibles de contribuer a diminuer l'exposition de la population canadienne a ces substances, notamment par le biais de politiques gouvernementales et d'outils destines aux praticiens.

TitreApplicationTitle: A systematic review of managerial leadership for research use in nursing and allied healthcare professions
Keywords-MotsClés: HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH; IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; LEADERSHIP; MANAGEMENT; NARRATIVE SYNTHESIS; RESEARCH USE; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Nurses and allied healthcare professionals (physio, occupational, speech and nutrition therapists) form the bulk of the clinical healthcare workforce and play a central role in health service delivery.  There is potential to improve the quality of health care if these professionals routinely use research evidence to guide their clinical practice.  However, the use of research evidence remains unpredictable and inconsistent.  Leadership is consistently described in implementation research and theory as critical to enhancing research use by nurses and allied healthcare professionals.  However, this important literature has not yet been synthesized and lack of clarity exists about what constitutes effective leadership for research use, or what kinds of interventions effectively develop leadership for the purpose of enabling and enhancing research use in clinical practice.  In this systematic literature review, we propose to synthesize the evidence on leadership behaviours amongst front line and senior managers that are associated with research evidence by nurses and allied healthcare professionals, and then determine the effectiveness of interventions that promote these behaviours.  With the engagement of knowledge users in leadership and practice, we will synthesize the research from a broad range of disciplines in order to understand key elements of leadership and how to develop leadership for the purpose of enhancing research use in clinical practice.   This integration of knowledge will be critically important to policy makers, organizational leaders and healthcare managers to design effective interventions and create sound organizational strategies to improve the delivery of evidence based healthcare for improved patient outcomes.

TitreApplicationTitle: Talking with children and families about weight-related issues: A scoping review of best practices
Keywords-MotsClés: COMMUNICATION; SCOPING REVIEW; WEIGHT DISCUSSIONS; WEIGHT MANAGEMENT
Abstract-Résumé: Canada is in a public health 'crisis' with up to a third of children considered to be overweight or obese. Obesity in childhood has been linked with a range of potentially life-threatening conditions and greater chances of being bullied and excluded. Healthcare professionals are in an ideal position to talk to children and their families about healthy weight management as they grow up, and to help them establish the foundations for a lifetime of good health. However, a number of problems have been reported by healthcare professionals, including a lack of training, time pressures, and worries that they will upset the family or trigger an eating disorder in the child by communicating in the wrong way. Furthermore, there are no guidelines around how healthcare professionals can effectively and sensitively talk about weight and obesity with children and families. The intent of this scoping review is to gather and summarize information from a range of sources to capture what is known about this topic. The scoping review will use an established sequence of steps to search, select and summarize previous research and other relevant information to understand how conversations about weight and obesity can be conducted in the best possible way (called 'best practices'). Parents and healthcare professionals working in child weight management will be involved throughout the entire review process. We will also talk to children/youth and other experts to discuss their views on what we find and how they think we can best communicate these findings to different audiences. This might include children, parents, healthcare professionals and those who write guidelines about clinical practice. The outcomes of this process will be a better understanding of what evidence exists on this topic, guidance on how healthcare professionals might best talk with children and families, and the identification of where more research needs to be done.

TitreApplicationTitle: Aging baby boomers: An investigation of the health prospects of Canada's largest demographic and the impact their health needs will have on society and the economy
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; BABY BOOMERS; GERIATRICS; HEALTH CARE SERVICES; INTERACTIVE DATA; LONG TERM CARE; MULTIMEDIA; NEWS ARTICLES; POPULATION HEALTH; VIDEO INTERVIEWS
Abstract-Résumé: I am investigating the long term health needs of the baby boomer population in Canada. As boomers age, it is important for them to understand the health risks they face. By presenting boomers with information about health risks and preventative measures they can take to improve their health, they can make choices that will contribute to healthy aging. Ensuring this population remains healthy for as long as possible can have many positive gains for not only their individual lives and their families, but also for the health care system and economy.  From the societal perspective, with such a large portion of the population at risk of needing serious medical care in the coming years, understanding the impact that will have on the health care system and economy is necessary for long term planning. If families need flexibility at work to take days off to care for elderly parents or if more funding is needed in the health care system, those changes should be considered in the near future. The findings of my research will be presented as an online multimedia project featuring articles, video and interactive data.

TitreApplicationTitle: Epigenetic effects of early life antibiotics on genes relevant for metabolic disease and immune tolerance
Keywords-MotsClés: DIABETES; EPIGENETICS; MICROBIOTA; NEONATAL ANTIBIOTIC EXPOSURE; OBESITY; PANCREAS; PIG MODEL; T-CELL DEVELOPMENT
Abstract-Résumé: A large proportion of Canadian infants are exposed to antibiotics in early life. Although critical for treating some bacterial infections, antibiotic exposure during the early developmental period is associated with an increased risk of obesity later in life. There is an abundant population of microbes colonizing the gut that play an important role in shaping human development. Antibiotic exposure alters the composition and diversity of these microbes; when this occurs in early life it may be an important driver of immunologic and metabolic diseases later in life, including inflammatory bowel disease, asthma, diabetes and obesity. Because the effect of antibiotics on longterm obesity outcome are only seen when administered in the early life we believe that a programming effect, in the form of epigenetic modifications, is responsible. Epigenetic modifications are alterations to the DNA that change the expression of genes without changing the underlying DNA sequence. In some regions, nearly a third of children receive antibiotics in the first 6 months of life, therefore it is critical that we gain an understanding of the impacts of this environmental exposure on long-term chronic disease. The contribution of neonatal antibiotics and resulting changes in the microbiome to diabetes and obesity later in life has not been experimentally tested. We will use the piglet as a model for the human infant to identify how postnatal antibiotic exposure  influences immune and pancreas development that program an infant for an increased risk of obesity and insulin resistance later in life.

TitreApplicationTitle: Investigating the Cell Type-Specific Regulatory Role of Ethanol on MeCP2 Expression
Keywords-MotsClés: ALCOHOL EXPOSURE AND WITHDRAWAL; BRAIN CELLS; BRAIN DEVELOPMENT; DNA METHYLATION; EPIGENETIC CONTROL; FASD; GENE EXPRESSION; GENE REGULATION; MECP2 GENE
Abstract-Résumé: An environmental factor that causes chronic compromised brain function is maternal alcohol exposure. Prenatal alcohol exposure leads to Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD). FASD refers to neurological disorders that affect 1-3% of live born children and is associated with intellectual disabilities, facial-growth abnormalities and impaired brain function. FASD is the most preventable and life-long brain disease in the Western world, with an estimated annual cost of 5.3 billion CAD for health services and activity loss in Canada. In mice FASD models, MeCP2 protein levels are reduced in the brain of offspring. Precise expression levels of MeCP2 are highly critical for normal brain development and function. Currently, FASD has no cure or prevention, underscoring an urgent need for innovative therapeutic and preventive strategies. This application is a collaborative and new initiative designed to understand the compromised gene expression program of brain cells affected in FASD.   The highest MeCP2 levels are detected in brain, but how this is controlled is unclear. In brain, MeCP2 levels are highest in neurons compared to cells that support neurons (e.g. astrocytes). Currently, the biological reasons of such high levels of MeCP2 in neurons are unknown. This is an important scientific question that has not been previously addressed. We reported the first generation of preclinical human MeCP2 gene therapy viruses as well as the cell type-specific MeCP2 expression in the developing and adult brain. As a team with expertise in brain development and disease, combined with control of gene expression expertise in another discipline (cancer research), we propose a collaborative multidisciplinary project to study the molecular mechanisms that regulate MeCP2 expression in brain cells. The outcome will be beneficial for future preventive and therapeutic strategies for FASD as a chronic life-long disease with no cure that is caused by an environmental factor.

TitreApplicationTitle: Effective Psychosocial Interventions for Autism: Synthesis and Knowledge Translation
Keywords-MotsClés: AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER; META-ANALYSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) affect around one per cent of children and have a devastating impact in the intellectual, daily living, and  social functioning of these individuals. Various psychosocial approaches to treatment attempt to palliate the symptoms of autism but the lack of unbiased syntheses on the main comprehensive psychosocial interventions for ASD makes it difficult for health decision makers, professionals, and parents to support the interventions that show potentially greater promise. In the current project we have selected the two models of intervention that have generated more research over the years as the target of a thorough evaluation of clinical effectiveness. The general purpose of the present study is twofold: (a) to provide a synthesis of the evidence in support of major psychosocial approaches to intervention using state-of-the-art methods for the evaluation of scientific evidence; and (b) engage our knowledge users in each step of the research as part of a comprehensive knowledge translation process. Our knowledge users and collaborators include the clinical directors of two major regional service providers for people with ASD and a high-rank representative of the Government of Manitoba. They have expressed a strong interest in using the results of the current project as the basis for the development of evidence-informed services and policies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Do sugar-sweetened beverages cause adverse health outcomes in adults? A systematic review
Keywords-MotsClés: ADULT; CANCER; CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CHRONIC DISEASE; DIABETES; METABOLIC SYNDROME; OBESITY; SUGAR-SWEETENED BEVERAGE; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes are examples of chronic diseases that impose significant morbidity and mortality worldwide.  Most chronic diseases are associated with underlying preventable risk factors, such as elevated blood pressure, high blood glucose or glucose intolerance, high lipid levels, physical inactivity, excessive sedentary behaviors, overweight and obesity, and tobacco use. Some researchers propose that sugar-sweetened beverages are significant sources of calories and recent attention has been given to their contribution in the development of chronic diseases.   In parallel with media attention regarding sugar-sweetened beverages, the scientific literature has been rapidly accumulating as of late. Systematic reviews of the evidence are important in order to collect and assess the relevant evidence to answer health questions. Such systematic reviews exist in this area but mainly evaluate individual outcomes (for example, cardiovascular disease), have important issues with their methods, and may now be out-of-date. To address those concerns, we will conduct a systematic review to assess whether consuming sugar-sweetened beverages causes adverse health outcomes in adults. This review will be of interest to the general public, healthcare professionals, and policy makers.

TitreApplicationTitle: Repeat and Co-Infection of Sexually Transmitted Infections, Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Hepatitis C: A Systematic Review
Keywords-MotsClés: HEPATITIS C; HIV; REPEAT AND CO-INFECTION; SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS; SURVEILLANCE; SYNDEMIC
Abstract-Résumé: Individuals who engage in activities that put them at risk for acquiring a sexually transmitted infectiion are known to get repeatedly infected over time.  They are also prone to being infected with more that one organism at a time.  This can result in more serious sexual health consequences such as infertility or rapid progression of HIV.  The methods that public health surveillance officers and researchers report rates of repeat infections or co-infections differs greatly making it difficult for juridictions to compare trends.  We would like to conduct a thorough and systematic review of the medical literature to examine different ways that repeat and co-infections are defined, how they are measured, and how the data are analyzed and reported.  From this we would like to produce recommendations about how repeat and co-infections and be reported in a standardized way.  In addition, we would like to review the literature and provide pooled rates of repeat and co-infections in the general population as well as in populations engaging in high risk activities.  We believe this research is important to inform how prevention strategies should be rolled out in Canada and beyond.

TitreApplicationTitle: Children and youth engagment with nature and their health: A scoping review of interventions
Keywords-MotsClés: CHILDREN AND YOUTH; HEALTH PROMOTION; MULTIDISCIPLINARY; NATURAL OUTDOOR PLACES; NATURE; PUBLIC HEALTH; SCOPING REVIEW; SOCIO-ECOLOGICAL
Abstract-Résumé: Obesity, mental and behavioural disorders are especially concerning for Canadian children and youth and all have the potential to negatively impact long-term health. There is a growing interest among researchers, decision-makers, public health professionals, ecologists and the education sector on the use of natural outdoor places as a means of improving health outcomes across a range of issues including obesity, physical activity, mental health and social connectedness and pro-environmental behaviours. A scoping review is needed to map the literature on population and individual level interventions targeted to children and youth. The review will generate results that will be highly pertinent to our knowledge users as well as to the broader community and organizations around the world. It will allow us to compare interventions and to describe the positive and negative outcomes and absence of outcomes for interventions. It will also help to identify where sufficient evidence exists so that action plans and future policy recommendations can be made about interventions to engage children and youth with nature for health purposes. Gaps and contradictions in evidence will also be identified along with areas where further knowledge synthesis is needed and where more primary research is warranted

TitreApplicationTitle: Pathways for scaling up complex public health interventions: A participatory realist synthesis
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPLEX INTERVENTIONS; DISSEMINATION AND IMPLEMENTATION; INTEGRATED KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; POPULATION HEALTH; REALIST REVIEW; SCALING UP; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Even though many new products, programs and policies are developed to improve public health, their full potential is often not realized since they are only implemented on a small scale. Increasing their coverage and access is referred to as 'scaling up' and is one of the biggest challenges in public health, especially scaling up a coordinated set of interventions that operate at multiple levels in a system. The Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) is tackling this challenge through two funding programs. The Innovation Strategy funds projects that focus on healthy weights and mental health and is currently planning a scaling up phase. A new funding program is seeking to support partnerships that will promote healthy living and prevent chronic disease, with a goal to scale up effective practices.  PHAC is seeking advice on the process of scaling up, including questions like: how successful scaling up of coordinated sets of public health interventions unfolds; how scaling up starts, continues, and stops; how to support scaling up efforts; and barriers to successful scaling up and how these are overcome. This project will provide information and insights to answer these questions on scaling up public health interventions. It will complete a systematic review using a realist approach that looks at relationships between context, mechanisms for change, and population health outcomes. The review includes information from published and grey literature, theory and expert opinion on how scaling up may be accomplished successfully. The review process engages researchers, international experts, knowledge users and practitioners experienced in scaling up. It includes four phases over 12 months: (1) refining research questions, (2) retrieving information, (3) synthesizing information, and (4) interpreting information. Findings and strategies to apply them will be shared with PHAC and other organizations through a workshop and webinar at the end of the project.

TitreApplicationTitle: Comprehensive analysis of IL1R1 and IL1R2 genes in asthma considering smoking status
Keywords-MotsClés: ASTHMA; ATOPY; BRONCHIAL EPITHELIAL CELLS; EPIGENETICS; EXPRESSION; GENETICS; IL1R1; IL1R2; IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY; PROTEIN LEVELS
Abstract-Résumé: Asthma is a chronic respiratory disease which afflicts patients of all ages, causes significant morbidity and mortality and generates substantial costs to our society. Although the exact causes remain largely undefined, we know that genetic and environmental factors are important in development and symptoms of asthma. After huge efforts deployed to identify asthma genes, including Genome-wide associations studies, it is clearly apparent that the focus must be on 1) the integration of the environment in the refining of analyses for studies where genetic, clinical and exposition data are available, and 2) the development of experimental models (cellular, animal and/or analytic taking into account environmental factors) to better understand the role of the associated genes in asthma pathophysiology. In this context and based on previous encouraging genetics, epigenetics and expression data, the present catalyst focus on IL1R1 and IL1R2 genes and take into account tobacco smoking as environmental factor. Indeed, tobacco smoking is recognised to deteriorate lung function and increase the severity in asthma. In addition, tobacco exposure is well documented to have a large collection of epigenetic targets including proinflammatory cytokines. Our project provides a unique and valuable opportunity to decipher the impact of the IL1R1 and IL1R2 genes in asthma considering smoking status as environmental factor. The results will help to design future functional studies on these genes to ultimately develop new therapies.

TitreApplicationTitle: A review of the role of aging in return to work and stay at work
Keywords-MotsClés: AGING; BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL; HEALTH; JOB LOCK IN; KNOWLEDGE SYNTHESIS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; RETIREMENT; RETURN TO WORK; WORK; WORK DISABILITY PREVENTION
Abstract-Résumé: The health of workers is increasingly in the public eye. It has always played a key role in the Canadian economy but attention is growing, because of an aging workforce. Aging workers need to stay employed. A number of reviews show the benefits of work participation and the importance of good work to health and well being. However, negative impacts of aging on work are also reported. For example, aging workers are more likely to experience a variety of chronic diseases like COPD, heart disease, cancer or diabetes, putting these workers at an increased risk for leaving work, or having trouble maintaining work due to the challenges related to their medical conditions. However, older workers are also more likely to return to work following an injury. The established consensus of work being a positive experience for individuals has encouraged clinicians and policy-makers to focus on improving work participation through preventing an early end to work, that is, before the standard retirement age, and encouraging return to work. Research to date has been unable to untangle these interacting and concurrent trends. It is unclear to what extent these factors have been examined in understanding the return to work of aging injured workers and reasons for staying at work in those at increased risk for involuntary retirement due to for instance chronic conditions. For this reason, we propose to synthesize the literature on return to work in older workers to identify factors that would help these workers to maintain employment, avoid re-injuries and successfully return to work. By doing this, researchers can identify gaps in the literature, evaluate the success of existing interventions and propose new areas of focus. Moreover, what we find will help those active in work disability prevention to apply the summarized evidence that is often generated by different academic research disciplines and, as a result, difficult to understand for stakeholders.

TitreApplicationTitle: Self-Formulated Conditional Plans for Changing Health Behaviour: A Systematic Review
Keywords-MotsClés: CONDITIONAL PLANS; CONSUMERS; HEALTH-RELATED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE; HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: The health of individuals is strongly determined by their health-related behaviours and those of healthcare professionals. This has resulted in considerable interest in knowledge translation. Strategies to improve knowledge translation often require health consumers and healthcare professionals to change their behaviour. Most people intend to change an aspect of their health-related behaviours at some point in time, whether it is to quit smoking by health consumers, or to follow best practice guidelines by healthcare professionals. For some people, these health intentions can and are translated into successful behaviour. However, for many more, intentions never result in the targeted behaviour. Conditional Plans are proposed as one approach to help individuals realize their health intentions.  Conditional Plans comprise statements that specify specific cues and the behaviour(s) that one will undertake to realize their intentions. The behaviour will occur in response to the cues. With Conditional Plans, individuals are able to form a mental image of when, where, and how they will perform the intended behaviour. Conditional Plans can either be provided to an individual (e.g., as an instruction) or can be self-formulated (i.e., the individual participates in developing his or her own plan). In the proposed systematic review, we are focusing on self-formulated Conditional Plans.   While Conditional Plans are widely used to promote behaviour change, there is a lack of synthesized evidence summarizing their effectiveness in changing health-related behaviours of health consumers and healthcare professionals. A synthesis of this evidence  will result in a better understanding of how to translate health intentions into behaviour for health consumers and healthcare professionals. Conditional Plans, if effective, are a simple low-cost intervention that can be widely implemented to improve health outcomes and healthcare for Canadians.

Keywords-MotsClés: CORRELATED EXPOSURES; CORRELATED OUTCOMES; DOSE -  RESPONSE; META-ANALYSIS; MULTIVARIATE META-ANALYSIS; ROBUST META-ANALYSIS; STATISTICAL METHODOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: "Meta-analyses", or pooled averages, are used to summarize the effects of a variety of health care interventions or treatments on different health outcomes.  Often, the same intervention may have effects on multiple outcomes, and when this is the case, special statistical methods are required to come up with correct estimates of the effects of the treatment on each outcome.  The goals of this project are 1) a) to identify existing methods for estimating the effect of an intervention on multiple outcomes, and test how well these methods work using computer simulations; b) to summarize available methods for dealing with many levels of treatment intensity measured or applied within the same summary project, and test how well these methods work using computer simulations; and 2) to identify the optimal method to summarize the results of many studies when a small number of these studies show extremely large or atypical effects.

TitreApplicationTitle: Mechanical environment - gene interactions in chronic musculoskeletal diseases
Keywords-MotsClés: BONE; CARTILAGE; DEGENERATIVE DISC DISEASE; ENVIRONMENT - GENE INTERACTIONS; EPIGENETICS; GENETICS; INTERVERTEBRAL DISC; MECHANOTRANSDUCTION; OSTEOARTHRITIS; OSTEOPOROSIS
Abstract-Résumé: Our goal is to assemble a new group of researchers from different disciplines to investigate the effects of mechanical stimuli - such as exercise, physical activity and vibration - on bone and joint health.    Chronic musculoskeletal diseases, such as osteoporosis, degenerative disc disease and osteoarthritis, are caused by many factors including genetics and environmental influences.  One of the most widely accepted environmental influences on the skeletal system is mechanical loading. Interestingly, either excessive or insufficient physical activity can lead to loss of bone and joint function.  Vibration is now being used as a therapy to strengthen bones; however, our preliminary findings suggest that it may have negative effects on spine health and may lead to osteoarthritis.    We will use mice that have been modified genetically to explore interactions between vibration and a particular gene that is thought to play a key role in responses to mechanical loading. This gene is often mutated in humans, which may explain why individuals respond differently to exercise and physical activity.    Our long-term goal is to establish an efficient system for studying interactions between the mechanical environment and other critical genes. We can then apply this information to the development of new approaches to prevent and treat common, chronic diseases of bones and joints - osteoporosis, degenerative disc disease and osteoarthritis.

TitreApplicationTitle: Early-Life Environment and Chronic Allergic Disease: Leveraging a Prospective Study to Discover the Epigenetic Signatures
Keywords-MotsClés: AIR POLLUTION; ALLERGY; BIRTH COHORT; CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT; DENDRITIC CELLS; EARLY LIFE EXPOSURES; ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH; EPIGENETICS
Abstract-Résumé: This project seeks to examine the effects of early-life exposures on allergic disease in a group of 350 children that we have been following since before birth. At age 2 we will measure outdoor traffic-related air pollution and indoor levels of environmental chemicals at the homes of the children. At the same time we will collect blood samples. We propose to investigate a mechanism called epigenetics as a mediator of gene-environment interactions. Epigenetic modifications are changes that affect gene expression that do not involve changes in the DNA code. Epigenetic modifications are highly dependent on both environment and cell type. We propose to look at epigenetics in dendritic cells, a specific cell type that lies at the interface between the individual and the environment. Dendritic cells encounter both pollutants and potential allergens and influence the immune response. We will test the hypothesis that distinct epigenetic patterns, potentially induced by the environment, are associated with health outcomes and the development of allergies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Molecular mechanism of a gene-stress interaction on obesity
Keywords-MotsClés: CHRONIC MILD STRESS; DIABESITY; GENE-STRESS INTERACTION; MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Genetic factors play a strong role in determining an individual's risk of obesity and diabetes. However, these factors alone do not account for the rapidly increasing prevalence of these diseases. Interactions between genetic risk factors and environmental and lifestyle factors are driving the obesity epidemic. Using mouse models we recently identified two genes associated with increased risk of developing obesity and diabetes (diabesity). During this process, we found that stress had a significant impact on the magnitude of these genetic differences. Stress is  known to affect food intake and body weight, but it is unknown how changing these two genes can make some individuals more susceptible to the effects of stress on body weight. The goal of the proposed studies is to determine how stress interacts with these genes to affect obesity and diabetes risk. We will study mice with and without the genetic variants increasing risk of diabesity. Half will be subjected to ongoing mild stress, while the rest will remain unstressed. We will examine how these genes and stress combine to affect food intake, body weight and pre-diabetes. We will determine if stress directly affects these two genes and how changing these genes modifies the effects of stress on obesity, food intake and diabetes. The studies will involve detailed analysis of specific parts of the brain and the specific molecular pathways that mediate the effects of stress and control food intake. Knowledge gained from these studies can be used to identify individuals at greater risk from a stressful lifestyle and those who may benefit more from stress reduction. Previous obesity drugs acted on pathways by which stress alters food intake but had side effects. Increasing our understanding how these genes and stress combine to affect obesity, as in these studies, is important for developing new safer ways of treating obesity.

TitreApplicationTitle: Deciphering the pathways associated with tissue destruction in celiac disease
Keywords-MotsClés: CELIAC DISEASE; GENES-ENVIRONMENT INTERACTIONS; GENETIC SUSCEPTIBILITY; LOSS OF ORAL TOLERANCE; MOUSE MODELS OF CELIAC DISEASE; VILLOUS ATROPHY IN CELIAC DISEASE
Abstract-Résumé: Celiac disease (CD) is a complex intestinal inflammatory disorder induced by dietary gluten, which development is controlled by a combination of environmental and genetic risk factors. CD is highly prevalent in North America with around 1% of the Canadian population affected by the disease. The classical pathological changes of CD in the small bowel encompass an increased number of intraepithelial lymphocytes, the presence of autoantibodies, and a destruction of the lining of the small intestine (called villous atrophy). The only effective treatment currently available for CD is a lifelong gluten free diet (GFD), yet persistent symptoms and intestinal tissue damage are commonplace among celiac patients that adhere to a GFD. Thus, there is an urgent need for non-dietary therapies that improve patient health and alleviate the social and personal constraints associated with following a GFD.  The development of new therapies has however proven challenging because of our incomplete understanding of the mechanisms underlying CD pathogenesis (particularly the factors leading to villous atrophy) and the lack of a suitable mouse model of CD. We have recently developed a series of humanized mice that recapitulate all the main features observed in CD patients, including the development of villous atrophy in response to gluten ingestion. These newly developed mouse models are likely to revolutionize research in CD by allowing to study the complex innate and adaptive immune mechanisms leading to villous atrophy and to test novel therapies. Here, we propose to use a systems biology approach that will capitalize on the use of these innovative mouse models together with human samples to identify genes and pathways that contribute to the development of villous atrophy in active CD patients. In addition, our work may lead to the validation of a long-awaited physiopathologically relevant murine model of CD that is indispensable to implement novel therapeutic strategies.

TitreApplicationTitle: Identifying pollutant-sensitive DNA methylation marks associated with a global measure of thrombosis risk: a proof-of-concept study
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES; EPIGENETICS; EWAS; GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY; GWAS; HEMOSTATIC PROTEINS; METALOMIC PROFILES; METHYLATION; QUANTITATIVE TRAITS; VENOUS THROMBOEMBOLISM
Abstract-Résumé: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) - a blood clot in the vein - affects nearly 64,000 Canadians each year. In nearly 10% of cases, people will die suddenly or before they are diagnosed.  These deaths are preventable since the condition can be treated if caught early.  We know that exposure to metal pollutants (e.g. mercury, lead, zinc) is associated with VTE and other cardiovascular diseases.  We also know that VTE may be caused by a combination of lifestyle, environmental and genetic factors.  Although researchers have had some success finding genes and environmental factors involved in the condition, people at risk of VTE are still not well managed and overall understanding of the disease remains poor.  So far, explorations of the genetics of VTE have only looked for variations in the sequence of DNA molecules.  New studies, however, can look at not just the order of molecules, but at how DNA molecules are packed, which affects the way they work.  These newer studies are called 'epigenetic' studies, 'epi' meaning 'above'.  Like DNA sequence, epigenetic marks may be passed from parent to child.  But unlike DNA sequence, which is fixed from the moment you are conceived, epigenetics can be changed by your lifestyle or environment, and so make great treatment targets.  Our study will be the first to look at how epigenetics, genetics, and metal pollutants interact to cause VTE.  Using data from different cities known for significant exposure to industrial pollution (in Canada, Mexico and France), including both families and unrelated people with and without VTE, we will combine new epigenetic analyses with traditional genetic data, as well as measurements of metal pollutant levels in people's blood.  A better understanding of how epigenetics, genetics, and environment work together to cause VTE is vital to prevent, diagnose, and treat this potentially devastating disorder, and may also provide insight into other cardiovascular conditions, such as heart attack and stroke.

TitreApplicationTitle: Toward a Patient Information Aid in Primary Health Care: What are the Outcomes Associated with the Use of Online Consumer Health Information? A Participatory Systematic Mixed Studies Review.
Keywords-MotsClés: CONSUMER HEALTH INFORMATION; INFOMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY; INTEGRATED KNOWLDGE TRANSLATION; MIXED METHODS RESEARCH; PARTICIPATORY RESEARCH; PATIENT CENTERED CARE; PRIMARY HEALTH CARE; SYSTEMATIC MIXED STUDIES REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Our ultimate goal is to facilitate the patients' use of online consumer health information in community-based primary health care, thereby promoting better patient health outcomes. To achieve this goal, we propose to review the literature, which will help us to design an innovative Patient Information Aid. There are aids for specific decisions, but no comprehensive aid for helping patients to find and use relevant understandable general information. Patients routinely seek health information on the Internet. The use of information found on the Internet may improve patients' self-care, and control on their health; it can also improve patient engagement in their own health, care, and treatment. However, little is known about the outcomes of using online consumer health information in primary health care.  Our specific objectives are to list types of patient information use and types of patient health outcomes, and to identify conditions associated to outcomes. To achieve these objectives, a participatory review of the literature will be conducted by a multidisciplinary team of researchers, and Knowledge User partners (representatives of patients and information providers). Our review will consist of four stages: identification of potentially relevant references; selection of relevant full-text documents; quality appraisal of included research studies; and synthesis of study results. Eligible documents will include original qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods studies on the use of online consumer health information in primary health care. We will combine a qualitative and quantitative synthesis.  The proposed review will be the first to synthesize knowledge on this topic. Findings will lead to design a Patient Information Aid that will be implemented by our partners and other knowledge users to help patients finding and using information, and collect their feedback to improve information products.

TitreApplicationTitle: Ancillary testing for diagnosis of brain death: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Keywords-MotsClés: ANCILLARY TESTING; BRAIN DEATH; CRITICAL CARE; DETERMINATION OF DEATH; KNOWLEDGE SYNTHESIS; ORGAN DONATION; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW; TRANSPLANTATION
Abstract-Résumé: Organ transplantation is for many patients with terminal heart, lung, liver and kidney disease the only hope for survival. In 2011, 4660 patients were on the waiting list for transplantation in Canada and 285 died waiting for an organ. For the purpose of organ donation, organs can be obtained from living donors, harvested after cardiac death (DCD) or after neurological death diagnosis (NDD). Organs harvested after NDD represent the principal source of organ transplanted in Canada and in 2011, 466 patients with NDD procured a total of 1518 organs for transplantation. The only source for hearts, pancreas and intestine transplantation come from NDD organ donors. As such, it is of uttermost importance to accurately identify potential patients in a state of neurological death and to proceed in a humane, accurate, timely and cost-effective manner to NDD. Neurological death, also called brain death, is the condition a patient has an irreversible loss of consciousness and of the functions of the brain required to stay alive such as breathing. Physicians rely on a very extensive physical examination and tests at the bedside to diagnose this condition. Situations however happen where the physician can't diagnose brain death at the bedside because of certain medications or facial trauma, for example. He then has to use additional tests called "ancillary tests" to help diagnose this condition. We will conduct a knowledge synthesis of the available literature about the use of ancillary tests for diagnosis of brain death. This work will provide clinicians with an up to date and reliable appraisal of all the current literature to help them make the best decisions regarding the use of these tests for diagnosis of brain death. It will help policy-makers implement evidence based clinical guidelines about the use of these tests and it will provide solid foundation for researchers in areas where data is inconclusive to further study the determination of brain death using these tests

TitreApplicationTitle: Individual recovery expectations and prognosis of low back pain: Synthesis and implementation of prognostic factor evidence
Keywords-MotsClés: DISABILITY; EXPECTATIONS; KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION; LOW BACK PAIN; PSYCHOLOGY; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Low back pain is one of the most costly and disabling conditions worldwide. Researchers have not identified a specific cause for most cases and although many treatments are available, none have shown strong effectiveness for all people. A new area of research that may be useful in this situation is to investigate characteristics of people and their environment that are related to increased disability. Recent studies have suggested people who think that they are going to do poorly (i.e. poor recovery expectations), in fact, do experience more disability with their low back pain, however study results have differed. Further understanding about recovery expectations and its relationship to outcome can help inform management of low back pain, relevant to service and healthcare providers.  In this project we will explore the relationship between individual recovery expectations and outcome in adults experiencing low back pain. We will use a systematic review of the research literature to identify all relevant studies that have been published, and will combine and compare information from them to draw conclusions. Since this is a new area of research, we will also explore the best ways to conduct this type of research synthesis, including different literature search strategies and testing a way to assess the quality of studies included in the review. Throughout the project we will communicate with low back pain healthcare providers to help us to better understand and deliver appropriate messages about our findings. The knowledge from this review will help understand the relationship between recovery expectations and low back pain outcomes. These results will be useful to plan strategies for managing adults with low back pain. Related methodological work will inform future prognostic factor systematic reviews and extend the benefits of well conducted evidence syntheses.

TitreApplicationTitle: A scoping review of training and clinical models for invasive bedside procedures performed by internists
Keywords-MotsClés: ASSESSMENT METRICS; CLINICAL PRACTICE MODELS; COMPETENCY-BASED TRAINING; INTERNAL MEDICINE; INVASIVE BEDSIDE PROCEDURES; MAINTENANCE OF COMPETENCE; PATIENT OUTCOMES; PROCEDURAL QUALITY; SCOPING REVIEW; TRAINING MODELS
Abstract-Résumé: Up to 40% of patients in Canadian acute care hospitals are admitted to a medical ward. Many will require an invasive bedside procedure for diagnosis or treatment. Procedural complications are a leading cause of avoidable harm and disability in many countries including Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. Some research evidence suggests that one way to decrease procedural complications is to improve how we teach procedures to medical trainees and how we assess their competence in performing these procedures. Certifying bodies such as the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (RCPSC) and the American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) govern physician training and certification. Both bodies list invasive procedures as 'core competencies' for licensed internal medicine physicians. These organizations do not, however, have specific guidelines for how to ensure trainees are competent or how to assess that physicians have maintained their competence. Also unclear is how best to measure the quality and safety of bedside procedural performance. One reason for the lack of specific guidelines for physicians' procedural competence is that the literature is large and dispersed, with inconsistent findings. For certifying bodies to confidently set guidelines for procedural training, the existing research must be synthesized in a concise and usable format.  The proposed scoping review will synthesize the literature and update knowledge users on the existing evidence related to teaching of procedural skills, performing these procedures in clinical practice, and assessing physicians' competence in performing procedures. The aim is to provide clear guidance for how to teach and assess competence in these skills so that future physicians will have the necessary expertise to provide safe and effective patient care for Canadians who require procedures.

TitreApplicationTitle: The Efficacy and Safety of Smoking Cessation Interventions in Patients with Cardiovascular Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
Keywords-MotsClés: CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE; CORONARY HEART DISEASE; HIERARCHICAL BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS; META-ANALYSIS; PERIPHERAL VASCULAR DISEASE; RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS; SMOKING CESSATION; SMOKING CESSATION AID; SMOKING CESSATION INTERVENTION; SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
Abstract-Résumé: Heart disease and smoking are 2 leading causes of death in Canada. A smoker who also has heart disease is at especially high risk for major problems such as heart attacks. These problems are also expensive and place a burden on our healthcare system. However, quitting smoking is not easy. Even after a heart attack, 2 out of 3 patients who are motivated to quit start smoking again within 1 year. Treatments such as counseling and medication (for example, the nicotine patch, nicotine gum, bupropion, or varenicline) can help people quit smoking. However, what we know about smoking cessation in the general population is not necessarily the same for people with heart disease. Smoking cessation therapies are usually tested in younger, healthier smokers, who have smoked for fewer years and may be less addicted than people with heart disease. Our objective is to learn how many smokers with heart disease are able to stay quit long term using each of the available therapies. We also want to know if certain therapies are better than others, in terms of how safe and effective they are in this population. We will search databases to find clinical trials of smoking cessation therapies in people with heart disease. These trials will have randomized patients to receive either a smoking cessation therapy or a control treatment. We will then take the information from each study and pool it with information from other studies looking at the same therapy. This way, we can better estimate the number of people who are able to quite smoking long term. We will then compare each therapy, to identify the therapy(ies) which are most effective for people with heart disease. Safety information will also be pooled and compared. We will then provide clear recommendations about these treatments to physicians, policy makers, and millions of Canadian smokers. Our conclusions could help individual smokers quit more easily, and reduce the overall burden of smoking on the healthcare system.

TitreApplicationTitle: Hepatitis B virus X protein activates NF-kB pathway by promoting nuclear localization of Rel protein p65 in liver cells.
Keywords-MotsClés: HEPATITIS B VIRUS X PROTEIN; HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA; NFKB PATHWAY
Abstract-Résumé: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections results in approximately one million deaths per year caused by liver diseases.  Many studies have shown that HBV X (HBx) protein is important for viral replication, subversion of host cell processes, such as nuclear factor kappa B (NF-kB) pathway, and development of liver cancer.  Interestingly, there is strong evidence that NF-kB factors may promote oncogenesis.   The molecular mechanisms with which HBx may cause liver cancer, however, remains poorly understood.  This study will undoubtedly contribute to further our knowledge on how HBV and its protein, HBx, cause liver diseases. Investigating the relationship between HBx and NF-kB pathway can reveal important targets for novel therapeutics designed to inhibit viral replication and prevent development of HBV-associated liver diseases. Given the importance of both HBx and NF-kB in HBV infections, the potential benefits of this study is enormous.

TitreApplicationTitle: Emotional Intelligence in Adolescents with Autism Spectrum Disorders
Keywords-MotsClés: ADOLESCENTS; AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS; EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE; SOCIAL EXPERIENCES
Abstract-Résumé: People with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) struggle with social situations. When they fail to fit in, they may feel poorly about themselves and this influences their overall personal health. Emotional intelligence (EI) is related to our social experiences and as a result, it could be used to explain why individuals with ASD struggle in social situations. EI includes whether we can label emotions, understand them, and control them. There are two types of EI: ability and trait. Ability EI is related to how we reason about emotions while trait EI is related to personal characteristics that foster appropriate social interactions. Despite its promising implications for improving social skills, research about EI in youth with ASD is limited (aside from work from our research group). Moreover, existing social skills programs for individuals with ASD fail to produce consistent or lasting improvements in social skill performance. To understand how ability and trait EI relate to the social experiences of teens with ASD, I will collect information from teens with and without ASD, their parents, and their teachers to understand how typically developing adolescents compare to adolescents with ASDs in their characteristics and skills for emotional interactions. More precisely, I will evaluate how they perceive, use, understand, and manage emotions and how that relates to their self-reported social stress and interpersonal skills. Parents and teachers will also be asked to provide information in order to obtain a different perspective of the adolescents' social skills and adaptability. Pinpointing the differences in EI between people with and without ASD will clarify the relationship between social and emotional skills, and generate novel, yet critical information relevant to intervening with ASDs. In addition, understanding this relationship will inform programming to improve the academic and social outcomes of persons with ASD as well as their personal health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Formate Metabolism in vivo
Keywords-MotsClés: FOLATE; FORMATE; ONE-CARBON METABOLISM; RIBOFLAVIN; VITAMIN B12
Abstract-Résumé: Formate, the smallest organic acid, is an important yet often overlooked piece of the one-carbon metabolism puzzle. Its name comes from the Latin formica indicating its origins from ants, from whom it was first isolated some 300 years ago. Despite formate's humble discovery, research in the past 60 years or so has unraveled some of the importance of this metabolite. In the 1950's it was demonstrated that formate is essential for forming the purine rings of adenine and guanine; these are building blocks for our genetic material. More recently it has been shown in our lab that altered plasma levels of formate may be indicative of different B-vitamin deficiencies. These results indicate that together with homocysteine, circulating formate levels may be a useful diagnostic tool to differentiate between different vitamin deficiencies in a clinical setting. My future work in the lab will explore the origins of our body's formate pool and examine how this pool can be affected by deficiencies of Vitamin B12, folate, or Vitamin B2 (riboflavin). While determination of the origins of formate in the body is key to the understanding of formate metabolism, so is knowing formate's destination. We also hope to examine formate's potential to be used as a source of one carbon groups for reactions in the body that synthesize a variety of different compounds, including some amino acids, the precursors of protein, and creatine.

TitreApplicationTitle: How does gender influence the mental health of refugees in St. John's? A qualitative study.
Keywords-MotsClés: CULTURE AND MENTAL HEALTH; GENDER DIFFERENCES; HEALTH PROMOTION; MENTAL HEALTH; MENTAL WELLBEING; QUALITATIVE METHODS; REFUGEE HEALTH; SETTLEMENT PROCESS
Abstract-Résumé: Canada provides refuge to thousands of people each year; in order to become positive contributors to society, refugees must become well settled and be in good physical and mental health. However, refugees experience many risks to their mental health, such as trauma in their home country, the stress of moving to a new country and leaving loved ones behind, as well as the difficulties of settling into a new context. Past research has found that refugee men and women experience these stresses differently, so mental health services need to take gender into account when working with refugees. In the city of St. John's, Newfoundland, there are no mental health services that cater to the city's refugee residents. This research project will use interviews to learn about refugee men and women's experiences of mental health in St. John's, with the goal of understanding how mental health services can best serve refugees in the city. As such, the results of this research project can improve mental health services for refugees in St. John's, helping them reach their full potential.

TitreApplicationTitle: Cellular and molecular mechanisms implicated in the metabolism and actions of endocannabinoids and other arachidonic acid-derived lipid mediators in leukocytes.
Keywords-MotsClés: BIOACTIVE LIPID; CELL BIOLOGY; EICOSANOID; ENDOCANNBINOID; INFLAMMATION; LC-MS/MS; LIPIDOMIC; MACROPHAGE; NEUTROPHIL
Abstract-Résumé: Although cannabis has been used in medicine for centuries, nobody clearly understands how it exerts its effects in humans. Cannabis does much more than increasing appetite: it also decreases pain and inflammation. However, our understanding of how cannabis prevents inflammation is very limited. Over the last decade, two lipids that mimic the effects of cannabis were found in the human body. Because of that, they have been termed endocannabinoids. Endocannabinoids contain a lipid named arachidonic acid, which can be transformed into several other lipids that worsen diseases such as arthritis and asthma. Among these lipids are the prostaglandins and the leukotrienes. Our preliminary data indicate that white blood cell behavior is modulated by endocannabinoids. Our current hypothesis is that some endocannabinoids are more involved in the beginning of inflammation while others are involved during the resolution of inflammation. To prove this, we will characterize how and when our white blood cells make endocannabinoids and how the different endocannabinoids promote or block inflammation.  Our long term objective is to develop a therapy promoting the anti-inflammatory effects of endocannabinoids  to promote the resolution of inflammation. We believe this can be achieved with a compound that would prevent their transformation into arachidonic acid. This would certainly   increase the quality of life of many Canadians suffering from chronic inflammatory diseases such as rheumathoid arthritis

Keywords-MotsClés: ARTERIAL BLOOD PRESSURE; CARDIAC FUNCTION; EXERCISE TRAINING - VOLUNTARY WHEEL; HYPERTENSION; PREECLAMPSIA; RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN SYSTEM; TELEMETRY; TRANSGENIC MICE
Abstract-Résumé: Preeclampsia is a pregnancy-associated disease where women develop high blood pressure and protein urine. It is the leading cause of mother and foetus mortality and morbidity. In addition, children born to preeclamptic mothers have a higher risk of high blood pressure as adults and women who have had preeclampsia are more at risk of developing several cardiovascular diseases. However, we have yet to identify its specific cause as well as methods for early detection and prevention. Women who have high-blood pressure are more at risk of developing preeclampsia. Because of the difficulties imposed by this human disease, animal models of preeclampsia have been developed although there are very few who develop the disease spontaneously. We have discovered a new mouse model which has the same symptoms as women who suffer from high blood pressure and go on to develop preeclampsia when they become pregnant. In addition, we have recently produced data that suggest new molecules that could be implicated in this disease. As such, we wish to further investigate these elements and determine if they may be used as therapeutic targets using our animal model which would have important clinical impact as there is no effective treatment for this disease a part from early delivery.

Keywords-MotsClés: FUNCTIONAL ELECTRICAL STIMULATOR; MUSCLE FATIGUE; NEUROPROSTHEES
Abstract-Résumé: People with spinal cord injury have impaired movements of their arms and/or legs, due to paralyzed muscles. However, when we externally stimulate those muscles using electrical stimulation, muscles can be made to contract to generate different limb movements and physical activities such as walking, standing, and grasping. People with spinal cord injury can also use electrical muscle stimulation to train muscles and maintain muscle strength, which will in turn prevent other complications such as pressure sores, low-impact fractures, and deep vein thrombosis from occurring. Thus, rehabilitation using electrical muscle stimulation is very advantageous for this patient population. However, one aspect that often limits the use of electrical stimulation is the rapid onset of muscle fatigue. One can potentially explain the muscle fatigue following electrical stimulation by the fact that electrical stimulation contracts muscle fibers simultaneously and that electrical stimulation is unable to contract all the fibers within the muscle. We have proposed a new stimulation method that would activate most of the muscle fibers in a regulated cyclic pattern, and showed the effectiveness in our previous CIHR project for leg muscles. In this novel method, special electrodes and a stimulator are used to distribute the stimulation centre over a larger area of skin. In the current project, first, we will design a small electrical circuit with which one can use this method in actual therapy. Secondly, we will test the new method in muscle strength exercise. Thirdly, we will test the new method for arm muscles. We expect that we will translate our new method to a simple form that can be easily used in therapies. The tool may later be commercialized.

Abstract-Résumé: Bone injuries are costly, challenging and common clinical problems which present an important health care issue as 5-10% of all fractures have delayed or impaired fracture healing.  However, our current understanding of fracture healing at the molecular and cellular level is limited. Yet such knowledge is critical to advance treatment options to optimize bone repair and remodeling.  While it is known that inflammatory cells are important for fracture healing, the interplay of the immune system and bone repair remains unclear.  This emerging field of osteoimmunology requires further study to identify and characterize the gene targets that regulate bone formation to develop new approaches to predictably improve fracture healing.  The proposed research will identify and characterize the relevant immunological cell types and key signaling pathways that direct fracture repair through bone forming cells.  The outcomes of this research will advance our knowledge of the fracture repair process as modulated through the immune system which is currently lacking and provide insight into the possible therapeutic targets. This will ultimately provide better treatment strategies for impaired fracture healing and improve overall bone health to promote earlier restoration of mobility and independence.

TitreApplicationTitle: TryCYCLE (Critical Care Cycling to Improve Lower Extremity Strength): A Single-Center, Prospective Pilot Study of the Safety and Feasibility of Early Rehabilitation using Cycle Ergometry in Mechanically Ventilated Patients
Keywords-MotsClés: ADULTS; CRITICAL CARE; CYCLE ERGOMETRY; MECHANICAL VENTILATION; MOBILITY; OUTCOME MEASURES; PHYSICAL ACTIVITY; PROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY; REHABILITATION
Abstract-Résumé: Patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) are the sickest in hospital, and need advanced life-support. Survivors of critical illness are very vulnerable to weakness and disability. Up to 1 in 4 have severe leg weakness impairing their quality of life for as long as 5 years after ICU discharge. In-bed cycling employs special equipment that attaches to a patient's hospital bed, allowing them gentle leg exercise while in the ICU. We will offer patients in-bed cycling while they are needing a breathing machine, to help them recover from weakness as fast as possible. Before doing a larger trial testing if in-bed cycling reduces disability, data on safety (Is it safe?) and feasibility (Can we do it?) are needed.  Objective: To study the safety and feasibility of in-bed leg cycling in critically ill patients who need breathing machines.  Methods: Adult patients admitted to the ICU who need a breathing machine and are expected to survive their ICU stay are eligible. Specially trained physiotherapists will provide patients with 30 minutes of in-bed cycling each day while they are in the ICU.  Outcomes: We will study (1)Safety: the heart rate and breathing patterns of patients doing in-bed cycling, while carefully monitoring for safety. (2)Feasibility: whether patients can cycle on most days of their ICU stay, whether patients and their families agree to be a part of the study, and whether we can assess patients' strength in the ICU and at hospital discharge.    Relevance: As the Canadian population ages, the demand for breathing machines during acute illness will increase dramatically. Effective methods of physiotherapy are needed for critically ill patients to minimize muscle weakness, speed recovery, and improve quality of life. This pilot study is the first of several future larger studies about in-bed cycling in the ICU. This program of research will help patients needing life support to regain their strength and recover as fast as possible from critical illness.

TitreApplicationTitle: Safety Evaluation of Natural Health Products
Keywords-MotsClés: EFAVRENZ; GINKGO BILOBA; HERBAL MEDICINES; NATURAL HEALTH PRODUCT; QUERCETIN; VITAMIN D; VITAMIN D RECEPTOR
Abstract-Résumé: The use of natural health products/herbal products has increased substantially over the years in North America, including Canada.  However, there is relatively little scientific information available as to how they work or whether they are safe to consume.  We have obtained preliminary data indicating that Ginkgo biloba extract and and quercetin (which is a dietary supplement) have the ability to increase the activity of vitamin D.  Therefore, in the proposed research project, experiments were designed to: 1) characterize the effects of the combination of Ginkgo biloba extract and vitamin D and those of the combination of quercetin and vitamin D on the action of a receptor known as vitamin D receptor; 2) assess how this combination interacts with the vitamin D receptor; and 3)determine whether these combinations increase the breakdown of a drug known as efavirenz, which is used by HIV patients to treat their infection. The proposed experiments will be performed in cell culture, including human hepatocyte.  Our novel studies will provide information on the safety assessment of natural health products (i.e. Ginkgo biloba, quercetin, and vitamin D) that are consumed commonly by Canadian and others in the world.

TitreApplicationTitle: Dietary Creatine Supplementation as a treatment of Fatty Liver Disease
Keywords-MotsClés: ANIMAL MODELS; CELL CULTURE; CREATINE; DIETARY SUPPLMENTATION; HIGH FAT DIET; LIPID METABOLISM; LIVER; METABOLIC DISORDERS; METABOLIC FLUX; MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
Abstract-Résumé: Creatine, a naturally occurring substance, is made in our bodies but can be obtained from the food supply. The major dietary sources of creatine are meat and dairy products. We have made the novel discovery that creatine supplementation reduces the amount of fat in the liver of rodents fed a high fat diet. This finding suggests that creatine may be a treatment for fatty liver diseases. Current data suggest that 20-30% of Canadians have fatty liver diseases which, if left untreated, would represent a significant stress on the health care system. In this proposal, we will determine the mechanism by which creatine prevents fat accumulation in the liver. To accomplish this goal we will use liver cells and various mouse models.  The results of this proposal will determine the efficacy of feeding creatine, an inexpensive, safe natural health product, in the treatment of fatty liver diseases. It will provide the experimental evidence to support future clinical trials to treat this serious obesity related disease.

Keywords-MotsClés: 14:3:3 PROTEIN; CANCER STEM CELLS; EPITHELIAL-MESENCHYMAL TRANSITION; HIPPO PATHWAY; INTEGRIN LINKED KINASE; METASTASIS; RICTOR; TARGETED CANCER THERAPEUTICS; TGF-BETA; WNT SIGNALING
Abstract-Résumé: We have been investigating the molecular basis of a fundamental process called "Epithelial to Mesenchymal Transition" ( EMT), which converts normal and cancer cells into highly migratory and invasive cells, leading to the spread of tumor cells from the primary tumor to distant organs, a process called metastasis. EMT has now been shown to represent a very imoportant process for tumor dissemination, including the dissemination of "cancer stem cells", a subpopulation of cells that sustain tumor growth, and are resistant to chemotherapy and radiation. Targeting this process is therefore essential for effective therapy of cancer. We have been studying a protein called Integrin Linked Kinase (ILK), which we and others have shown to play an essential role in the EMT process. The ILK protein has now been established to be overexpressed in many types of human cancers, with high levels predicting poor patient prognosis. We have determined that ILK modulates several cellular signaling mechanisms involved in EMT. In this application we propose to extend our findings over the last 4 years to precisely determine how ILK controls these mechanisms in the process of EMT as well tumor cell proliferation, key contributors of aggressive tumor behavior. We have developed several cell based and mouse model systems to determine the role of ILK in controling other key cellular signaling pathways known to contribute to oncogenesis. This in depth understanding will allow us to develop more precise therapeutic approaches that will target not only ILK but its associated protein complexes and pathways for the treatmment of advanced cancer.
