Abstract-Résumé: This grant application proposes to bring together the initial members of the Nova Scotia Strategy for Patient Oriented Research Network for Primary and Integrated Health Care Innovations (NS-PIHCI). If funded, NS-PIHCI will provide Nova Scotia the opportunity for research, policy, clinical leaders and stakeholders to collaborate in a new research team with the intent to design new ways of providing health services to people with complex health care needs. NS-PIHCI will develop its capacity to become a member of CIHRs National SPOR Network, allowing Nova Scotians to benefit from participation and learning in cross-provincial research and applied changes in health care across the country. The research funding will be used to set the priorities NS-PHICI should work on and determine who best should do this work. These innovative ways will see health services working better together, be better coordinated, be focussed in the community and include not only better health care delivery but be connected to ways to prevent the diseases leading to complex care needs. The funding will allow Nova Scotia's research, policy, and clinical leaders to engage health care organizations, citizens and other stakeholders in the development of the network and how it will work together. The initial members have extensive experience collaborating, and the NS-PIHCI will allow important decision makers in government, research and health care providers to formally coordinate their program, policy and research efforts to deliver innovative and cost-effective solutions to improve healthcare for this group of Nova Scotians, while learning from and informing healthcare across Canada.

By involving end-users and other key stakeholders in engagement and research activities, better knowledge transfer and application (sharing and use of results of research) will be possible. In this first year of activities, we will identify and gather key stakeholders in Quebec who will identify existing resources and priority areas for action in subsequent years. Abstract-Résumé: The Ontario government is committed to a process in which evidence will drive health system transformation and funding of new programs.  We propose to build on that commitment and on the rich resources for health innovation and research in Ontario through the development of a provincial network for Better Access and Care for Complex Needs (BEACCON). BEACCON will foster a new alliance between research, policy and practice in order to create a dynamic and responsive learning network that develops, evaluates and scales up new approaches to the delivery of integrated and cost-effective services across and beyond sectors of health care.  BEACCON will create a provincial leadership council committed to evidence-informed transformation to more cost-effective and integrated health care working with Innovation Development, Evaluation and Scale-up (IDEAS) teams of researchers, providers, patients and policy makers focused on children, adults and older people.  The IDEAS teams will be supported by an innovation incubator that will work with health professionals, patients and families to develop, refine, pilot test and scale up new ideas for providing care and improving health.

TitreApplicationTitle: Manitoba SPOR Network in Primary and Integrated Health Care Innovations-Development Funds Proposal
Keywords-MotsClés: CARE INTEGRATION; HIGH NEEDS POPULATIONS; MULTI-SECTORAL; PATIENT-ORIENTED; PRIMARY CARE
Abstract-Résumé: This proposal describes the first step in developing a research network as part of the CIHR SPOR initiative: 'Network in Primary and Integrated Health Care Innovations'. The Manitoba SPOR Network (MSN) is designed to conduct research and implement new practices to help individuals with high and complex care needs through their lifespan. The MSN will work with other research networks across Canada, in a combined effort, to deliver research for individuals, across all age groups (from children to older adults), but focusing on those with the greatest use of the system.  The MSN will have three leaders, one having extensive experience in bridging groups to help change the health system (Thomson), one delivering primary care and collaborating with front line physicians (Buchel), and a leading primary healthcare and health services researcher (Katz). In addition, the MSN has strong links to four of the Community Based Primary HealthCare Innovation Teams funded by CIHR with one of the teams being led by Dr Katz.    The planned MSN membership will have many clinicians, policy makers, researchers who represent different clinical and research specialties, government departments, health regions, and community organizations. The MSN initial membership has expertise in many areas including: health services research, and policy innovation; healthcare delivery across the primary care spectrum; and public health and government policy and relations. The MSN will be embedded within the George and Fay Yee Centre for Healthcare Innovation which houses the CIHR funded SPOR SUPPORT Unit. The Manitoba SUPPORT Unit has several services that the MSN will use during its creation. The MSN will develop a governance structure that includes many groups working together including patients, which will provide the opportunity to work toward goals with significant and sustained impact on the health of the population.

Abstract-Résumé: The purpose of this Network grant is to develop a collaborative network of researchers, physicians, community members, and policy-makers that will focus on generating new evidence in primary and integrated health care effectiveness, efficiency and access across the care spectrum.   The Saskatchewan team includes individuals from across the province including researchers, physicians, and policy makers who will work together to improve the health equity, more specifically in indigenous and rural areas, with a focus on prevention, and how to better provide services to patients across their life spans (early childhood to older adults). The Saskatchewan team hopes to focus on specific signature initiatives that are very strong in this province. The value of having a Saskatchewan Network (if successful) will allow researchers in various different areas to come together to focus on integrating primary heath care and social determinants across urban and rural areas, indigenous peoples, as well as provincial and national components. Through our collaboration with not only researchers, but also physicians and policy-makers this will allow the network to identify specific issues facing individuals in Saskatchewan regarding their primary care. This Network LOI comes at an opportune time given the ambitious and far-reaching systemic changes underway in Saskatchewan health care system (e.g. Lean Initiative, Primary Health Care reform).

TitreApplicationTitle: Developing the BC SPOR Network: A Consultative Process
Keywords-MotsClés: COMPLEX CARE NEEDS; HORIZONTAL INTEGRATION; PRIMARY HEALTH CARE; SPOR NETWORK; VERTICAL INTEGRATION
Abstract-Résumé: Through a confluence of factors, BC is ready to begin a new phase in transforming its health care system. The goal with the BC SPOR Network is to enable innovation and support government, health authorities, and health professions in introducing innovation to improve the delivery of BC's health care services. Our preliminary vision for this is that it will enable the 1) achievement of optimal health outcomes for residents of BC, particularly for those with complex care needs across the life course and 2) greater efficiency of the health care system by bringing together knowledge users (KUs), patients and researchers so they can learn from each other, collectively generate new knowledge, and chart a common future.  We share a common commitment to quality, clearly articulated by the US Institute of Medicine in its classic report Crossing the Quality Chasm. This report defined eight dimensions of quality, all of which are relevant to our work; care should be accessible, person-centred, safe, effective, efficient, equitable, coordinated, and population health oriented. Specific objectives of the BC SPOR Network are:   a) Development of systems and processes to measure health outcomes;  b) Knowledge Generation through Observation (Descriptive work) and Experimentation (Intervention work); c) Knowledge Translation and Exchange; and d) Development and implementation of processes for the spread of integrated health service delivery  We will use a provincial consultative process that includes deliberative dialogues and small group consultations. At the end of the Network development process, researchers, knowledge users, patients and communities will have outlined priority actions and areas for a BC SPOR Network in primary and integrated health care innovations.

TitreApplicationTitle: Development of a Northern-Based SPOR Network in  Primary and Integrated Health Care Innovations
Keywords-MotsClés: NETWORK; NORTHWEST TERRITORIES; PRIMARY HEALTH CARE
Abstract-Résumé: Health care in Canada's North faces considerable challenges with its remote and widely dispersed population, harsh environmental conditions, and thinly deployed health professionals. Despite per capita expenditures that are among the highest in the world, health outcomes continue to lag behind the rest of Canada, and health disparities between the Aboriginal and non-aboriginal population within the North continue to persist. While improving the health of northerners requires addressing underlying social determinants, transforming the health care system holds promise in the short and medium term. The evidence required to inform a northern-focused and relevant transformation, however, remains to be generated.  The establishment of a SPOR Network in Primary and Integrated Health Care Innovations is timely. Its intention to include the northern territories fills a capacity gap that has long been recognized by northern governments and communities. The Institute for Circumpolar Health Research (ICHR) and its partners in the territorial governments, regional health authorities, Indigenous organizations, and academic research institutions will consolidate and further develop a northern-based network and apply for membership in the national Network.

NomDuProgrammeFR: Chaires d'excellence en recherche du Canada
TitreApplicationTitle: Canada Excellence Research Chair in Personalized Pain Medicine
Abstract-Résumé: Chronic pain is a global public health problem of enormous social and economic impact. One in five Canadians  more than 6 million people - suffers from chronic pain. Their annual health care costs are estimated at over $10 billion, more than cancer, heart disease and HIV combined. The most common forms of chronic pain are osteoarthritis, cancer, migraine and back pain, whose prevalence increases with age, reaching 50% in the over 65s. The latter will be one quarter of the Canadian population in less than 20 years and chronic pain will severely impair their quality of life and place pressures on those upon whom they depend. Current treatments for chronic pain are unsatisfactory and existing analgesics are often not effective because the underlying genetic mechanisms are poorly understood. The research program of this CERC will focus on the genetic mechanisms of pain, searching for targets for chronic pain therapies and the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. These are currently the top priorities of increasing numbers of research and health organizations as well as of the pharmaceutical industry. The projects will focus on the identification of molecular mediators of chronic pain states using genome-wide genotyping and sequencing of DNA and RNA and evaluating these variables in populations of chronic pain patients. Identified targets will be validated through molecular and cellular techniques and through gene targeting, animal behavior and, ultimately, clinical trials. The Chair will also lead efforts to expand our current training programs in personalized pain medicine. The CERC candidate will join a team at McGill University with a 40-year tradition of excellence in pain research. The CERC will foster a qualitative change by breaking new ground in human pain genetics to ensure that McGill and Canada remain among the worlds leading centers of excellence in pain research for years to come.
